jobs.title: Project Manager / Assessment Researcher
jobs.body:
## **Job Description: Project Manager / Assessment Researcher**

**Program:** Iraq Higher Education AI Workforce Readiness Program

**Location:** Baghdad, Iraq (full-time, in-person)  
**Duration:** 12 months

### About Development Gateway

[Development Gateway: An IREX Venture (DG)](https://developmentgateway.org/) is an international non-profit organization with approximately 80 team members based in more than 15 countries worldwide. By leveraging the combination of programmatic and IT developer capacity and skills within DG, over the last 20 years we have *researched* data ecosystems, *built* digital tools to support those data ecosystems, and *advised* on data strategy and digital transformation to strengthen decision-making, transparency, and service delivery.

### **Position Summary**

The Project Manager / Assessment Researcher will serve as the senior in-country lead for Development Gateway (DG) on the Iraq Higher Education AI Workforce Readiness Program, a 12-month program implemented with IREX in coordination with institutional partners in Iraq. Based in Baghdad, the Project Manager will manage delivery of Development Gateway's workstreams while leading the research that establishes a baseline of AI readiness across Iraqi higher education institutions (HEIs).

This is a role for a professional who is comfortable working on strategic questions and on technical detail. The Project Manager will manage the program workplan, budget, and reporting; lead the AI ecosystem mapping, the virtual university survey, and stakeholder interviews; and turn the findings into a visual baseline report and individual university factsheets. The role will also guide the design of the in-person AI workforce convening and the AI readiness roadmaps, and will advise program leadership on political, institutional, and technical risks as they emerge.

The Project Manager will build and maintain relationships with Iraq government institutions, university leaders, U.S. technology firms, and the funder, and will guide and mentor the AI Technical Specialist and other technical colleagues so that their work stays complementary and linked to program goals. The role reports to DG's program leadership and works daily with the IREX Iraq team and a distributed DG team.

### **Key Responsibilities**

#### **Project Management and Delivery**

- Lead day-to-day management of DG's activities under the program in Iraq, ensuring timelines, deliverables, and budgets are met.
- Develop, maintain, and update work plans, MEL plan, activity trackers, and budgets in coordination with IREX and DG colleagues, and adjust direction as new priorities or contextual realities emerge.
- Ensure accurate and timely programmatic reporting to IREX, DG, and the funder, coordinating inputs across the team and partners, in English and Arabic as required.

#### **AI Readiness Assessment and Research**

- Lead the AI ecosystem mapping and rapid diagnostic of priority government institutions, private sector partners, and universities, in close partnership with the AI Technical Specialist and IREX counterparts and with support from the Deputy Director of Programs, adapting the AI readiness methodology developed by IREX and DG to the Iraqi context.
- Manage the virtual AI readiness assessment, including survey adaptation, the virtual orientation workshop, and participant support, with a target of at least 40 institutions across federal Iraq and the Kurdistan Region.
- Conduct 20 to 30 interviews with Ministry officials, university leaders, U.S. technology firm representatives, and other stakeholders, and review relevant policies, strategies, and grey literature.
- Analyze the data, including regional comparisons for the Southern and Western provinces and the Kurdistan Region, and produce a highly visual baseline report and 2-page factsheets for each participating university.

#### **Strategic Advisory**

- Maintain a view across all program workstreams, identify emerging political, institutional, and technical risks early, and propose practical solutions and adjustments to program leadership.
- Provide analytical input to and quality review of external-facing knowledge products, including the baseline report, factsheets, briefs, and roadmaps.
- Promote and support strategic and business development opportunities for DG in Iraq as required.

#### **Stakeholder Convening and Partnership Building**

- Lead engagement with government partners and university leadership to align the program with national AI and higher education priorities, working in close coordination with IREX and the funder.
- Guide the planning of the in-person Private Sector and Iraqi AI Workforce Convening, facilitate working sessions, and steer discussions toward concrete use cases, skill needs, and partnership commitments with U.S. and Iraqi employers.
- Guide the development and virtual validation of AI readiness roadmaps for selected universities, and represent DG at external events and in meetings with partners.
- Mentor and guide the AI Technical Specialist and other technical colleagues, and contribute to a collaborative working culture across DG and IREX teams in Baghdad.

### **Qualifications**

#### **Required Qualifications**

- **Education:** Bachelor's degree in public policy, education, information systems, a STEM field, or a related discipline.
- 7+ years of experience working in complex, multi-stakeholder environments, with a track record of managing project delivery and high-level institutional relationships, preferably on donor-funded programs.
- Demonstrable experience building strategic relationships with government stakeholders in Iraq, ideally in higher education, alongside subject-matter experience in higher education, digital policy, or workforce development.
- Experience designing and conducting applied research and assessments, including surveys, key informant interviews, and document review, and analyzing mixed-methods data.
- Experience guiding, mentoring, or coordinating technical staff and consultants across teams and organizations.
- **Language:** Professional fluency in written and spoken Arabic and English, with strong communication and diplomacy skills.
- **Work authorization:** Must have existing work authorization in Iraq.

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

- Master's degree in education, public policy, or a technology-related discipline.
- Demonstrable experience in AI policy or AI in education, including familiarity with national AI strategy developments in Iraq.
- Experience with U.S. Government-funded awards and with consortium-based programs involving several implementing partners.
- Experience organizing workshops, conferences, or convenings that include private sector participants.

Position Details

This is a full-time embedded in the IREX office in Iraq. The expected annual compensation range is **USD $42,000-$45,000**, depending on relevant experience. The position is for the duration of the project, which is 12 months.

DG will review applications on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Interviews are expected to begin in early November.

jobs.body:
**Contract length:** 4–6 months, with a possible paid 6-month extension based on performance and budget availability

**Hours:** flexible,  
20-40 hours per week, during CET core working hours (Monday to Friday)

**Location:** Amsterdam or Lyon (to be confirmed) Hybrid arrangement: office-based with some remote flexibility

**Travel:** none, except relocating to Amsterdam or Lyon

**Reporting to:** Language Access and Engagement Specialist

Erasmus+ supports traineeships (work placements, internships) abroad at any workplace for students currently enrolled in higher education institutions in Program Countries at short-cycle Bachelor and Master level as well as for doctoral candidates. These opportunities are also open to recent graduates.

Erasmus+ traineeships are open to any student enrolled in a higher education institution holding an Erasmus+ Charter for Higher Education.

The traineeship must be relevant for the degree-related learning and personal development needs and, wherever possible, be integrated in the study program.

A traineeship can take place at any organization located anywhere in the world (with the exception of EU institutions, bodies and agencies).

CLEAR Global (previously known as Translators Without Borders) is an equal-opportunity employer, committed to having a diverse team where individuals of all backgrounds collaborate and learn from one another. We believe we can be most effective with diverse experience and expertise in our team. We recruit on merit, actively seek diverse applicant pools and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, marital or parental status, or sexual orientation, and welcome all types of diversity.

Within CLEAR Global, the Influence & Language Justice (I&LJ) team sits at the intersection of language access and movement building. The team currently leads the integration of Tarjimly into CLEAR Global, bringing together two large and active communities of language volunteers and professionals around a shared language justice mission. Our work spans community engagement, advocacy, and operational support for language access initiatives across humanitarian contexts. As an intern on this team, you will be embedded in day-to-day activities that are both community-facing and behind the scenes, contributing to work that has a real impact on how people access information in their own language.

**The role**

Assist the Community team in engaging a volunteer community of over 200,000 language professionals, coordinate collaboration among volunteers, ensure healthy growth of the volunteer community, as well as timely and effective communication.

**Responsibilities**

- Maintain effective communication with community members, ensuring they remain engaged and have a clear understanding of expectations
- Assist with outreach to new community members, both strategically and in response to crisis
- Support in the planning, logistics and management of community engagement events and activities
- Support in the recruitment of community members for in-CLEAR Global roles and their training and preparation for these
- Support in the monitoring and development of community member dialogue within digital platforms
- Support CLEAR Global teams in identifying opportunities for community member involvement within workflows and activities
- Support the development of role descriptions, coordination structures and processes for community member engagement initiatives
- Support community members in their experience with CLEAR Global, and ensuring that various community programs and processes run efficiently
- Carry out administrative tasks, data entry and data collection
- Handle other community management tasks as assigned
- Other duties as required

Please note that these roles and responsibilities are approximate and may change over time.

**Qualifications**

- Eligible for the Erasmus+ traineeship
- Fluent in spoken and written English; knowledge of other languages an advantage
- Strong communication skills, with particular awareness of intercultural contexts
- Previous experience in translation and/or interpreting (internships and volunteering are considered valid experiences) an advantage
- Previous experience working with non-profit organizations an advantage
- Familiarity with technology (with a special focus on translation and/or data entry tools) a plus

**Requirements**

This internship position is very dynamic. The right person is an energetic team player and an individual who agrees with CLEAR Global´s basic beliefs and values and who can work productively in a remote setting, while interacting regularly with the international team.

- Self-starter and able to work independently
- Strong organizational skills
- Analytical thinker able to transform ideas into tangible actions
- Understands that communication in the right language is key to improved humanitarian response
- Team player, collaborative, adaptable and self-motivated
- Interested in acquiring translation and community management experience
- Able to adapt to new technologies and learn new skills quickly
- Has enthusiasm for humanitarian work
- Reliable and flexible and has the ability to uphold the Core Values of the organization
- Able to work during CET core hours

**About CLEAR Global**

CLEAR Global exists to help people get vital information, and be heard, whatever language they speak. We believe that everyone has the right to give and receive information in a language and format they understand. We work with nonprofit partners and a global community of language professionals to build local language translation capacity, and raise awareness of language barriers. Our network of over 200,000 community members translate millions of words of life-saving and life-changing information a year.

**Core values**

CLEAR Global employees and volunteers are people who believe passionately about the value of this work and take personal responsibility for achieving the mission. CLEAR Global’s mission and organizational spirit embody the core values established in its strategic framework:

- Excellence: As the leading voice for communicating humanitarian information in the right language, CLEAR Global is a leader in the translation industry and in the non-profit sector.
- Integrity: CLEAR Global believes that every person, whether it’s the people who we serve, our volunteers or our staff, has value, deserves respect and has inherent dignity.
- Empowerment: CLEAR Global believes in using language to empower people around the world to control their own development and destiny.
- Innovation: CLEAR Global recognizes and celebrates the power of innovation to address humanitarian and crisis issues around the world.
- Sustainability: CLEAR Global recognizes that meeting our mission necessitates establishment and maintenance of a solid financial and organizational infrastructure.
- Tolerance: Our staff and volunteers are highly knowledgeable and skilled; value each other, our partner and our recipients; create a supportive work environment; and, conduct themselves professionally at all times.

*CLEAR Global may re-advertise the vacancy, cancel the recruitment, offer an appointment with a modified job description or for a different duration at its discretion.*

**Background/IRC Summary:**

The Syria crisis is often described as the worst humanitarian catastrophe since the end of the Cold War. Today, 13.4 million people in Syria - more than half of the country's population - are in need of humanitarian assistance with needs increasingly being exacerbated by economic decline. Of these, 6.8 million are refugees and asylum-seekers who have fled the country. This is no short-term humanitarian episode. The devastating human consequences to huge numbers of people will endure for decades. The destruction of relationships, communities, livelihoods, homes and infrastructure will take years to repair.

IRC is offering a robust humanitarian response to the Syria crisis a rapidly expanding portfolio, supported by more than 1000+ staff in Syria Country Program. IRC is undertaking programs in Syria and the neighboring countries of Turkey, Iraq, Lebanon, and Jordan in the fields of health, child protection, early childhood development, education, women’s protection and empowerment, non-food items and food distribution, cash assistance, water and sanitation, protection and rule of law, and livelihood programming. Our work in these challenging settings gives rise to some of the most pressing issues facing contemporary humanitarian action, including questions of access, security, funding, and coordination.

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The IRC Economic Recovery and Development (ERD) team is implementing emergency relief and early recovery programs in Northeast Syria. These activities support short-term, basic need provision and longer-term development of marketable skills and productive assets. Within its livelihood portfolio, the IRC provides employment support services, including vocational training, financial literacy and transferable life skills classes, and apprenticeships with existing businesses to promote the development of marketable skills and on-the-job training. The IRC also supports the delivery of micro-grants to new and existing enterprises to continue and grow their economic activities, improve their business processes, and better manage the demands of the crisis. The ERD Information Management Officer will be responsible for maintaining the data and information management systems and acting as the data focal point for the program, as implemented directly or with partners.

**Responsibilities:**

**Generic Responsibilities:**

- Participate and support in all beneficiary selection for ERD programming based on provided criteria, including; Multipurpose Cash, Cash-for-Work, Vocational training and Apprenticeship, Micro-enterprise grant support, and Agriculture and Livestock projects; and review partner database.
- Provide insight and recommendations on improved selection techniques and criteria alongside the line supervisor.
- Generate Quick Response (QR) codes for IRC and (when required) partner cash delivery programs.
- Ensure that all program data collected include the minimum of information that is required for follow-up and conduction of the Post-Distribution/Delivery Monitoring (PDM) Assessments and end-line evaluations. E.g. beneficiary numbers.
- Support the formulation of the M&E Matrix and plans to address donor and IRC indicator

reporting requirements.

- Provide training and support field enumerators and partners on data capture, analysis, and use.
- Support data capture processes to ensure they are implemented according to plans and agreed standards.
- Provide analysis of information and data to address reporting requirements and internal
    
    learning.
- Assist in regular reporting for donors and internal reports.
- Support the draft of mobile/digital data collection surveys for the field teams and coordinate with the other colleagues.
- Maintain the program-specific portion of data collection, analysis, and warehousing platforms, so they are well organized and accessible and data privacy regulations.
- Systematically review datasets for deficiencies or errors based on data quality SOPs and accurately any possible incompatibilities.
- Develop and train in handling ERD’s information systems, platforms, and databases - including developing improved visualization and access to program data for program managers and project leads.
- Analysis of program outcomes and findings through timely and accurate data visualizations and insight for ad-hoc needs and project reflection meetings.
- Lead submission of accurate and timely 4/5W reports to relevant Clusters and other Working Groups.
- Support ERD Coordinator and Managers in providing ERD-specific reporting to the IRC’s Global Technical Unit.

**Program Implementation:**

- Support ERD team in the collection of employment, entrepreneurship and income data as required
- Support with beneficiary surveys, focus groups and other feedback mechanisms according to the approved monitoring and evaluation plan.
- Identify issues, problems and/or concerns affecting the program and present these to the ERD manager in a timely manner.
- Assist the implantation manager with the market assessments design and implementation to assess needs, skills, and identify gaps to recommend the types of training in line with market mapping.
- Build the capacity of ERD program and partners’ staff in relevant technical and management proficiencies, such as Washington Group Question sets, QR code generation and use, and registration form usage

**Communication:**

- Support timely information-sharing regarding IM challenges and needs.
- Conduct regular data review meetings with the partners.
- Attend relevant 4/5W meetings and training, as well as any other relevant reporting meetings held by Clusters and Working groups (i.e. Food Security and Livelihood Cluster, Early Recovery Cluster, Cash Working Group) and maintain close connections with their relevant IMOs.
- Work with ERD Technical Unit focal points to share learning on ERD data collection and usage and when needed support the roll out improved processes and technology.
- Collaborate with the M&E staff to support beneficiary registration and application process.
- Submit weekly/monthly/daily reports as defined by the ERD Manager and ERD coordinator.

**Staff Performance Management, Learning & Development**

- Hire, supervise, and build the capacity of team members in relevant technical and management competencies.
- Develop and implement remote management capacity-building approaches to build the strengths of the teams in Syria.
- Coach, train, supervise, and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting annual performance objectives, providing regular and timely positive and constructive performance feedback, and providing documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Approve and manage time, attendance, and leave requests to ensure adequate departmental coverage; ensure monthly, accurate timesheet submission and carry out probationary reviews.
- Hold high-quality meetings with each direct report on a regular and predictable basis, minimally on a monthly basis.
- Provide a measurable development plan including on-the-job learning with the aim of strengthening technical capacity, exchanging knowledge within the team and providing guidance on career paths.
- As required, identify staff performance issues and work with Human Resources to document and address these in accordance with the National Staff Employment Policies.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.
- Look for opportunities to support staff in their career growth, where appropriate. As part of the succession plan and nationalization goals, identify, train, and develop the capability and capacity of national staff to successfully transition roles and responsibilities, by the end of the assignment.

**Required Experience/qualification/Skills:**

- University degree in information management and systems, computer science, data science, business administration, marketing, economics or an academic degree in other fields alongside relevant experience in this field.
- at least 2-4 years of progressively responsible professional experience in information systems management, monitoring and evaluation, database development and management.
- Relevant experience with INGOs will be a plus.
- Statistics, data analysis, data-driven computation are all relevant areas of experience
- Knowledge about the Syrian context is a significant advantage.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- A commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values, and IRC Way – Professional Code of Conduct.
- Credible written, presentation, and verbal communication skills; ability to convey information effectively and solid experience providing training and staff development.
- Validated a sense of professional discretion, integrity, and ability to handle complex situations diplomatically and to effective resolution.
- Excellent management and interpersonal skills and a solid ability to promote harmonious/cohesive teamwork, in a cross-cultural context.
- Validated ability to plan long-term, organize priorities, and work under administrative and programmatic pressures with detail orientation and professional patience.
- Highly collaborative and resourceful; ability to establish positive working relationships with senior-level management and all other partners to maximize cooperation and productivity.
- Curiosity, a desire to continually learn and develop and a sense of humor is a must.
- Analytical ability in creating effective solutions to complex matters while adhering to labor laws and internal policies.

**Language/Travel:**

- Arabic & English are required
- Travel: 20% to field sites in ERD business locations in Al Raqaa and Aleppo as well as attending regional and global workshops and meetings.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to: ERD coordinator**

**The position directly supervises: currently no staff under his/her supervision.**

**Key Internal Contacts: ERD coordinator, Sr. ERD managers, ERD manager, ERD senior officers, center officer, SME Officer, Agro- officer, CFW officer, HR, Finance, supply chain, Access, and IT sectors.**

**Key External Contacts: HAO, market actors, and ERD's partners.**

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based and are currently located outside of your home country and possess over two years of international work experience, the Middle East Region has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, a return flight to post, a shipping allowance, temporary housing, and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols, and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENA, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

IRC is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful, and safe work environment where all persons are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability, and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.

jobs.title: Area Coordinator (national)
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.body:
**About Acted**

For the past 30 years, Acted has been working at the forefront of humanitarian action to save lives. Acted supports more than 27 million people in 43 countries, meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas, while pursuing a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental, and development actor.

**Job Purpose**

The ***Area Coordinator*** provides high-level strategic guidance, quality assurance, and humanitarian coordination for Acted activities within their designated geographic area. This role focuses on translating external field realities into actionable project strategies, driving critical thinking, and mentoring staff.

The Area Coordinator is responsible for representing Acted's interests with area local authorities, donors, beneficiary communities and other key stakeholders. This includes all external engagement on behalf of capital COO or PCs as well as management of MOUs, exploratory meetings with LA’s and other government officials, and donors.

The Area Coordinator is a member of the senior management team and works to ensure program quality and operational implementation, as well as growth where appropriate and feasible, and strong representation. The Area Coordinator collaborates with Project Coordinators ensuring that projects and programs address beneficiary needs and are implemented according to Acted's global strategy, donor guidelines, approved work plans and budgets. The Area Coordinator also oversees day-to-day operations and security in the respective areas.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

***DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES***

**I. Strategic Input & Critical Thinking**

- Act as the primary strategic representative for responsibility area at regional UN Cluster meetings, Humanitarian Hubs, and (I)NGO forums.
- Initiate and lead regular meetings and information exchanges with other international and local NGOs, external engagement with NGO platform, UN/OCHA, partner INGOs, partner NNGO/CSOs, operating in relevant geographic areas.
- Establish regular dialogue channels with local Ukrainian universities, think tanks, and local research institutes. Leverage academic and institutional data and research to refine organizational program design.

**1.1. Networking, positioning and general representation:**

- Participate in donor meetings at area level and communicate relevant information to the Country Director and other relevant staff;
- Establish, maintain and improve active and regular working relationships with other NGOs, UN agencies, clusters, working groups, consortia, etc. at area level ensuring maximum visibility of Acted
- Establish, maintain, and improve active and regular working relationships with local authorities and where necessary non-state actors and obtain required authorizations and buy-in for Acted's activities at area level
- Development and application of the Acted country strategy at area level and tie ins to Country strategy.
- Ensuring Acted representation and positive relationship building in the responsibility area including MOUs with hromadas/oblasts, + gaining traction in municipal space discussions.

**II. Strategic Debriefing & Local Authority Analyses**

2.1 Context analysis: Ensure Acted has an up-to-date understanding of the area's socio-economic situation, trends, needs and gaps, and who does what and where (eg using 4W, other sourced data).

2.2 Strategy Implementation: Take a lead role in implementing Acted's country program strategy in the area identifying strategic opportunities for expanding Acted's work in the area, and in particular:

1. Identify new opportunities and new sectors of intervention;
2. Consolidate and stabilize programming;
3. Review the geographic and thematic footprint;
4. Ensure activities are relevant and meeting area/beneficiary needs;
5. Identify Acted added value;
6. Ensure humanitarian principals are adhered to;
7. Contribute to identifying new donors, private sector partners, national and international NGOs, think tanks, academia, etc. to work with in the area based on complementarity and added value

**III. Program Quality, Internal Coordination, and Advocacy**

**3.1 Program Quality, Development, and growth:**

- Matrix Guidance: Provide operational and strategic guidance to Project Coordinators (and Managers as useful), ensuring project implementation aligns with overall country strategies and donor commitments.
- Operational Troubleshooting: Identify implementation bottlenecks across departments and facilitate collaborative, cross-functional problem-solving sessions to unblock field activities.
- Proposal Input: provide inputs for CNs, proposals, N/CEs with high-quality, evidence-based field analysis derived from local operations, *hromada* interactions, and external networks.

3.1.1. Proposal development:

1. Lead assessment(s) at area level to ensure proposals are relevant; create and contribute to concept notes using local knowledge
2. Support the Country Director and Project Development Department in proposal conceptualisation (problem statement, logframe) within the framework of the country, regional and global strategy
3. Contribute to budget design and ensure budget needs at area level have been taken into consideration

3.1.2 Project Implementation Tracking:

1. Supervise Project Managers/Officers in the area as needed, and provide support to project implementation through trouble shooting and eliminating blocking points
2. Monitor output achievement and cash burn rates to assist timely completion of projects through review of BFUs and project reports
3. Anticipate and mitigate risks ensuring operations in the area are compliant with Acted finance, logistics, administration/HR, transparency and security (FLATS) procedures
4. Ensure that relevant project information is up-to-date and available for reporting purposes
5. Ensure coordination and complementarity amongst projects within the area of intervention

3.1.3. Project Quality Control:

1. Ensure the application of a practical field-based MEAL system/plan for each project
2. Conduct frequent field visits to project sites to assess activities and ensure efficient use of resources
3. Advise Project Managers to adapt projects according to monitoring and evaluation findings
4. Ensure beneficiary feedback mechanisms are in place
5. Ensure capitalisation of best practices and lessons learnt for projects in the area of operations, and explore options to learn from other areas and teams.

3.1.4. Partner Management:

1. Identify potential local partners in the area based on an assessment of complementarity and added value
2. Provide support to partners in project implementation and ensure timely and qualitative implementation of projects by partners in line with Acted and donor requirements

**3.2. Internal Coordination & collaboration**

ACs will work collaboratively with internal department heads, project coordinators, and capital coordination to achieve mission results. They are an integral part of FLATS and SMT meetings and coordination.

3.2.1. Internal Coordination and Staff Management

1. Facilitate interdepartmental communication and information sharing for a positive working environment
2. Ensure implementation of Acted coordination mechanism at area level
3. Ensure that all staff in the area understand and are able to perform their roles and responsibilities related to area operations and link with the capital Head of Departments to discuss improvement initiatives
4. Promote team building, productivity and staff welfare
5. Mentor and support the team to build capacities, and improve efficiency and performance, and follow career management
6. Manage interpersonal conflicts among staff at area level

3.2.2. Finance Management:

1. Although budgets are generally held at Capital level, the AC should be able to advise on project budgets at area level to help PCs avoid under/over spending.
2. Collaborate with Finance teams and PCs to ensure accurate budget forecasting and efficient cash flow management; lead Area BFU preparation and maintenance.
3. Assist with timely and accurate area finance TITANIC reporting, as requested

3.2.3. Logistics & IT Management:

1. Ensure timely procurement and adherence to rules of origin and nationality at area level
2. Ensure quality supply management at area level
3. Ensure proper asset management at area level and enforce asset investment policy
4. Ensure proper stock management at area level
5. Ensure proper IT systems, data back-up and protection from malware at area level
6. Ensure sufficient and reliable means of communication at area level
7. Ensure fitting office and guesthouse space depending on size of team and availability of budget
8. Assist with timely and accurate area logistics TITANIC reporting

3.2.4. Administration and HR Management:

1. Ensure transparent and timely recruitment of national staff and contribute to international staff recruitment upon capital request
2. Proactively advise Head of Department managers and Country Coordination around adaptive staffing structures, tailored to area needs and funding parameters
3. Ensure regular performance appraisal and career management for staff at area level
4. Assist with timely and accurate area HR TITANIC reporting, as requested
5. Ensure timely and complete exit forms

3.2.5. Transparency/Compliance Management:

1. Minimize risk of fraud and corruption by ensuring adherence to Acted FLATS procedures
2. Ensure that staff is aware of Acted's transparency and whistle blowing policy
3. Ensure appropriate action from departments and teams for department and project documentation, and uploading onto Archive 2.0

3.2.6. Security Management:

1. Analyse the security context at area level and in close collaboration with the Country Security Manager contribute to defining, analysing and evaluating risks
2. Engage with relevant key stakeholders at area level to ensure access and support of interventions
3. Address security and safety risks by implementing standard operating procedures defined for the area
4. Ensure the offices and houses conform to recommended security, health and safety standards
5. Ensure all staff in the area adhere to security procedures
6. Ensure security incidents at area level are promptly reported to the capital

**3.3. Advocacy**

The AC should act as both a collector of information for processing and use in Acted country proposals/strategy, as well as being an area advocate in groups and collective NGO meetings to discuss and formalize issues, and to raise relevancies for Country Coordination to follow through with state bodies as needed.

3.3.1. Advocacy: Contribute to drafting issues papers, advocacy notes, press releases on relevant humanitarian and development issues in the area of operation.

3.3.2. Promotion of Acted network: Keep abreast with and contribute to Acted's global initiatives and global trends, in particular Impact (REACH), HQ initiatives (3Zero), and the Acted Humanitarian Network.

**IV. Key Performance Indicators**

- Number of (elected) positions in area-based clusters, working groups, coordination mechanisms
- Knowledge of strategic partners and key stakeholders in area including analysis, networking, stakeholder mapping, and administrative (governmental) relationships
- Number of localised partnerships in the area and improvements catalogued by AC and /or partnerships team
- Number of projects in the area and % change as compared to previous year
- Retention rate among international and national staff
- Regular and timely holding of internal coordination meetings and submission of reports to D/CD
- Proactive contributions to donor reports and concept notes for capital level
- % ineligible expenses incurred at area level and % change as compared to previous year
- % of projects in area with contractual targets/indicators met
- Number of complaints received from beneficiaries and % change as compared to previous year
- FLAT folders are complete and sent to capital office in a timely manner

jobs.title: Project officer, UZHF (Sohag) Re-advertisement
jobs.body:
**THE ORGANISATION**

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation/charity/non-profit that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

Scaling Up Economic Empowerment and Systemic Integration is a three-year project (July 2026 – June 2029) funded by the Ursula Zindel-Hilti Foundation (UZHF). The project aims to enhance the resilience and socioeconomic empowerment of vulnerable women and men within supportive and inclusive communities. The initiative focuses on strengthening collaboration between Plan International Egypt (PIE) and Ashoka Arab World (AAW) to achieve sustainable, community-driven impact. It engages social entrepreneurs, community leaders, and community-based organizations (CBOs) as key agents of change. The project will be implemented across four governorates: Assiut, Sohag, Beheira, and Damietta, targeting marginalized groups through integrated and inclusive economic empowerment interventions.

A total of 24 partner CBOs will be supported through comprehensive institutional capacity building, governance strengthening, and tailored technical assistance provided by PIE. In parallel, these CBOs will participate in social entrepreneurship training delivered by AAW, equipping them with innovative tools and approaches to design and implement effective, community-based solutions. Following the capacity-building phase, CBOs will be empowered to design, implement, and manage local initiatives, with continued technical guidance and financial support from both PIE and AAW.

At the community level, the project will directly target 1,600 beneficiaries, contributing to improved livelihoods and inclusive economic participation. The project is designed across 4 main outcomes:

Outcome 1: Strengthened capacities of community actors, and CBOs as key drivers of change within the targeted communities.

Outcome 2: Fostered influence and engagement of social entrepreneurs, youth emerging changemakers, and CBOs are across the targeted locations, as evidenced by the development and implementation of inclusive, community-based socioeconomic initiatives benefiting vulnerable women and youth.

Outcome 3 Enhanced resilience of 1,600 women, youth, and men across the targeted locations through expanded and equitable access to sustainable socio-economic opportunities, contributing to inclusive growth and long-term socioeconomic empowerment.

Outcome 4: Project’s best practices and lessons learnt were streamlined and disseminated among the project’s partners and participants to support women and youth entrepreneurs in establishing and scaling up their own businesses.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

You will support the implementation of the “Scaling Up Economic Empowerment and Systemic Integration” project. You will focus on supporting the coordination of capacity-building activities, partnerships, and community-based interventions aimed at strengthening the capacities of partner CBOs and enhancing livelihood opportunities for vulnerable groups, particularly girls and young women.  
You will work closely with Plan International Egypt teams, partner organizations, and local stakeholders, support the delivery of training and social entrepreneurship activities, follow-up on mentorship processes, and ensure effective coordination and communication among all partners. Further, you will support logistical and administrative arrangements to facilitate smooth implementation across targeted governorates.  
Also, you will contribute to monitoring project progress, documenting lessons learned, and promoting knowledge-sharing to support project scaling, replication, and sustainability.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Support and follow up on capacity‑building activities with partner CBOs.
- Conduct field visits to monitor progress, provide support, and identify challenges.
- Organize reflection sessions to gather feedback and document lessons learned.
- Coordinate with consultants and service providers for assessments and trainings.
- Support delivery of social entrepreneurship and livelihood programmes.
- Manage logistics and administration for project activities.
- Collect and analyze data and feedback to inform improvements.
- Contribute to monitoring and reporting, including inputs for donor communications.
- Plan International has a robust global policy for Safeguarding and PII policy for Preventing Sexual Harassment Exploitation and Abuse; and Gender Equality and Inclusion standards, ensuring staff and associates within your scope strictly comply with these principles and guidelines.
- You will be trusted to take on additional assignments within the scope of work as assigned by your supervisor on need basis.

**What we are looking for:**

- Someone who possess a bachelor degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies or similar field.
- You should have 3-5 years of experience with a proven record of success at a similar level preferably in an INGO sector.
- Someone experienced in working with government entities, civil society organizations on livelihoods, economic empowerment, or community development projects.
- Someon experienced in planning, conducting, and facilitating trainings/workshops.
- You should have strong understanding of the socio-economic and governance context in Egypt, particularly challenges faced by vulnerable and marginalized groups.
- You should demonstrate ability to coordinate, and deliver participatory training and learning programmes.
- Someone with proven skills in documentation, reporting, and analysis of lessons learned, good practices, and project outcomes.

**Please respond to the requirements of this role in your cover letter.**  
**Only applications in English language will be accepted.**

**Location: On site working and the role has work station is Sohag (Upper Egypt)**

**Reports to: Upper Egypt Area Manager**

**Job Grade: Hay Level 12**

**Vacancy advert closing Date: 26th October 2026**

**This vacancy is open to Egypt nationals only.**

Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.

We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.

We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.

Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.

A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Safeguarding Children and Young People policy. Plan International also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this scheme we will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**Disclaimer: Plan International is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate applicants on any basis. We also do not charge Job seekers any fees at any point of the recruitment process.**

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

You will be responsible for the design, planning and successful delivery of gender transformative projects and at every stage of the project management cycle in line with donor requirements and Plan International minimum standards and best practices. Also, you will lead the project team and be responsible for all the aspects of the project.

As a staff member of a child-centred international development and humanitarian organisation, you will commit to comply with Plan International’s standards and policies related to Safeguarding and PSHEA (Preventing Sexual Harassment, Exploitation and Abuse), gender equality, inclusion and diversity. All Plan International staff are expected to uphold the organisation's values and behaviours in every aspect of their work.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Contribute to the initiation of the project idea in line with the country strategy and identification of project potential local partner(s).
- Ensure projects are feasible by leading due diligence, shaping gender‑transformative scope with partners, analyzing risks and resource needs, managing pre‑startup activities, confirming partners, and embedding child safeguarding measures into design and budgets.
- Collaborate with partners to establish project governance structures, developing a detailed implementation plan covering risk, procurement, HR, monitoring, and budgets, and working with senior leadership and departments to launch the project both internally and externally.
- Lead project implementation by coordinating teams and resources, overseeing monitoring and evaluation with partners, managing risks, procurement, and finances, and ensuring timely reporting. Integrates gender‑transformative approaches and safeguarding measures to protect children and young people.
- The role ensures effective project monitoring and evaluation by establishing a data collection system aligned with partners, supporting future project design for the target population, and maintaining compliance with Plan International’s global data privacy policy.

jobs.title: Malawi Case Investigation Senior Coordinator
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## About the Role

Lead our case investigation team. We are seeking an expert to manage audit execution, drive fraud prevention, and improve internal controls. You'll own a critical role in safeguarding program integrity and supporting our mission for farmers.

## Responsibilities

- Lead and Develop the Team: Manage a team of 4–5 audit officers, conducting regular check-ins, performance reviews, and targeted professional development to keep morale and performance high.
- Oversee Audit Operations: Build the yearly risk-based audit plan, manage weekly team bandwidth, and prioritize urgent ad-hoc fraud or harassment investigation requests.
- Ensure High Quality: Conduct weekly quality checks on reports, shadow field investigations, and provide on-the-ground coaching to close delivery gaps.
- Drive Investigations & Controls: Safeguard the program by investigating staff and farmer fraud, client harassment, and "ghost farmers," while constantly tightening internal control frameworks.
- Collaborate & Troubleshoot: Partner with HR on cash recovery, support Global Legal teams on high-level investigations, and collaborate with Field Operations on anti-fraud campaigns.
- Manage Data & Reporting: Consolidate monthly audit reports for stakeholders, maintain country and global trackers, and populate the Global Client Protection Heatmap.
- Shape the Future Framework: Work hand-in-hand with the Business Operations Lead to transition the team from traditional repayment audits into a pure case investigation unit.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Degree: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Auditing, Accounting, or a related field.
- Experience: 2+ Proven track record in internal/external auditing, risk-based audit planning, and compliance monitoring.
- Technical Knowledge: Deep understanding of internal control frameworks and fraud investigation techniques.
- Data Skills: Basic to intermediate SQL skills and proficiency in at least one BI/visualization tool (e.g., Power BI, Superset).
- Soft Skills: Strong analytical thinking, rigorous attention to detail, and excellent team leadership abilities.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Zomba, Malawi

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Malawi.

## Application Deadline

01 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Technical Manager Medical (TMM) - Maiduguri Roving
jobs.body:
## **JOB PURPOSE:**

The incumbent will be responsible for the overall management, coordination, and monitoring of health programs including integrated primary health care, sexual and reproductive health (SRH), nutrition, and immunization services with a particular focus on improving polio vaccination coverage in hard-to-reach areas in Borno state. The role will provide technical guidance and support to field teams to strengthen program quality, improve data collection and analysis, and ensure the timely preparation of accurate reports.

The incumbent will also coordinate closely with the State Ministry of Health, particularly the Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) Department on immunization-related matters and other primary health care priorities.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- In collaboration with the Program Manager, Medical Coordinator, and relevant team members, support the planning, implementation and monitoring of medical activities in line with INTERSOS project plans, mission strategy, technical standards, and protocols.
- Contribute to annual planning processes, budget reviews, project proposal development, and donor reporting.
- Supervise Medical Activity Managers to promote a harmonized program approach and high-quality medical service delivery across all projects.
- Monitor the quality, progress and outcomes of medical activities, and promptly report analyses, implementation challenges, gaps, and emerging humanitarian health concerns to the Medical Coordinator and relevant coordination team members.
- In coordination with the Medical Coordinator, establish and maintain constructive working relationships with donors, local authorities, implementing partners, health actors, project stakeholders, and other organizations operating in target areas.
- Actively participate in relevant field-level and intersectoral coordination meetings, including Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) and other health-sector coordination platforms.
- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with the State Ministry of Health, particularly the EPI Department, and provide technical guidance and support to field medical teams to expand immunization coverage in hard-to-reach areas, in accordance with donor and State Ministry of Health guidelines.
- Coordinate, supervise, coach, support, and evaluate medical team members to strengthen staff capacity, improve the quality of medical project components, and ensure compliance with INTERSOS standards and procedures.
- In close coordination with the Human Resources Department, plan and oversee the recruitment, induction, training, performance management, professional development, and internal and external communication of medical staff to ensure appropriate staffing levels and competencies.
- Conduct regular monitoring visits to project locations to verify that activities are implemented in accordance with donor requirements, approved workplans, and INTERSOS quality standards.
- Review monthly Health Management Information System (HMIS) data to ensure accuracy, completeness, reliability, and consistency, and share key findings, project progress, and emerging challenges with senior management.
- Support the Medical Coordinator in planning and organizing health-awareness events, including World Polio Day and other relevant observance days, to raise awareness of polio and other vaccine-preventable diseases.
- Compile high-quality donor reports and ensure their timely submission to the Medical Coordinator and Grants Unit.

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Advanced university degree in medicine MBSS or other paramedical studies. Desirable specialization in Tropical Medicine or a master’s degree in public health

**Professional requirements:**

- Minimum 5 years relevant work experience as a senior managerial with any humanitarian organization in fragile and unstable environments
- Candidates with previous experience of managing polio immunization programs will be preferred
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)
- Demonstrate experience with different donors’ compliance and reporting.

**Personal requirements:**

- Leadership, people management and development
- Teamwork and cooperation
- Strategic vision
- Results and quality orientation
- Behavioural flexibility
- Understanding of humanitarian operations principles, standards and best practices
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles

**Languages**

- Proficiency in English (written and spoken)
- Knowledge and fluency in English and local languages (Hausa and Kanuri) will be an asset.

jobs.title: Field Pharmacist - Dikwa, Magumeri and Maiduguri (Roving)
jobs.body:
## **JOB PURPOSE:**

Under the guidance of the Project Manager and Pharmacy Officer, the field Pharmacist oversees pharmacy stock management in compliance with Good Storage and Distribution Practices (GSDP) across all INTERSOS health facilities and the regional pharmacy warehouse in their respective LGA. This encompasses the complete receiving, storing, and dispensing lifecycle for pharmaceuticals, consumables, medical materials, and equipment. Additionally, the pharmacist is responsible for providing patients with essential treatment precautions, usage instructions, and clinical recommendations.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Data Collection and Analysis:**

- Be able to provide at any given time reliable information on stock, consumption, use of medicines and health products for each project.
- Assist the pharmacist at central level in updating stock information when required
- Create/update the stock-cards of the drug/medical material/equipment received and other tools in a timely manner
- Ensure regular and appropriate use of the management document (inventory records, delivery notes, computer tools etc.) Update the global stock inventory
- Ensure the storage of the items according to good storage practices
- Compile, in collaboration with the medical doctor and PM, a stock transfer request to the central pharmacy
- Work closely with the medical department to check, in relation to epidemiological data, the status of stocks and the consumptions and assess the appropriateness of prescriptions.

**Supply Management:**

- Ensure order reception by veryifing and recording the quantity and quality of the drugs/medical materials/equipment received. Inform central pharmacy and supervisor in the event of non-compliance.
- Prepare order/supply request regarding the average monthly consumption, the stock level and supply delay in collaboration with the medical doctor.
- Validate the supply request with the Project manager and send the stock transfer request to the central pharmacy Update the global stock inventory.

**Stock Management:**

- Set up and maintain the pharmacy stock according to good storage practices (storage of drugs by categories, alphabetic order and expiry date…)
- Ensure that FEFO (first expired first out) is respected
- Implement and ensure the stock follow up by calculating the average monthly consumption and minimal stock level for the main items
- Implement stock management system for each item and update each stock card/follow up in a timely manner
- Ensure a physical inventory of the pharmacy and medical stock, including consumables and laboratory material on a monthly basis
- Inform the project manager in case of any missing/damaged/expired item
- Make sure that the main stock and the pharmacy are kept clean
- Organize effective destruction and quarantine of damaged items in collaboration with the Central pharmacist
- Ensure pharmacovigilance including the immediate report of any problem with the quality of a drug in accordance with INTERSOS pharmaceutical management procedures.

**Treatment Delivery:**

- Ensure all medical equipment is prepared for the day
- Deliver the treatment to the patient according to medical doctor prescription
- Explain the posology, and provide advice and precaution of use
- Prepare the drugs for the pharmacy on a weekly basis according to the needs

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree in pharmacy (BPharm.). Registration with Pharmacy Council of Nigeria and License.

**Professional requirements:**

- Essential previous experience of at least 4 years in similar or relevant positions.
- Strong knowledge of pharmacies and medical supply chain processes.
- Skilled in pharmaceutical care, supportive supervision and data reporting.
- High level computer literacy, especially excellent MS Excel / Word skills
- Desirable previous experience in pharmacy
- At least two years’ experience of working with any humanitarian organization in challenging environment.

**Personal requirements:**

- Results and quality orientation
- Teamwork and cooperation
- Behavioural flexibility
- Service orientation
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles

**Languages**

- Proficiency in English (written and spoken)
- Knowledge and fluency in English and local languages (Hausa and Kanuri) will be an asset.

jobs.title: Medical Activity Manager - Dikwa and Magumeri.
jobs.body:
## **JOB PURPOSE:**

The Medical Activity Manager is responsible for the overall management and implementation of health and nutrition programs at the LGA level, working in close coordination with relevant LGA health authorities. The incumbent conducts regular monitoring visits to health facilities, nutrition sites, and vaccination sites to ensure service quality and provide ongoing technical support to program teams. Additionally, they oversee monthly data collection from all supported facilities, analyze trends, prepare comprehensive monthly reports, and submit them to the Medical Technical Manager.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Provide technical support and guidance to doctors, nurses, midwives, vaccinators and clinical teams across health facilities to ensure high-quality care. Ensure all sites maintain up-to-date clinical protocols and guidelines in compliance with Ministry of Health standards.
- Conduct regular monitoring visits (at least weekly) to health facilities and outreach sites to verify that health service delivery aligns with organizational quality guidelines. Complete quality monitoring checklists, compile field trip reports, and submit them to the Medical Technical Manager.
- Collaborate closely with the Field Pharmacist to perform accurate forecasting of medicines and medical supplies, ensuring monthly consumption reports are prepared and submitted on time. Verify the continuous availability of essential medicines, vaccines, and a functional cold chain system.

- Supervise facility data focal points to ensure accurate data entry into morbidity registers and the timely preparation of monthly reports. Thoroughly review monthly consultation and consumption data for consistency and reliability prior to submission to the MEAL team.
- Ensure that all supported health facilities maintain robust medical emergency and preparedness plans alongside adequate stocks of essential medicines and supplies. Immediately investigate suspected disease outbreaks and report findings to the line manager without delay.
- Supervise the Community Health Supervisor and vaccinators to guarantee that micro-plans for fixed and outreach immunization sessions are effectively in place and implemented.

jobs.title: Midwife Activity Manager - Maiduguri (Roving).

## **JOB PURPOSE:**

The Midwifery Activity Manager is a senior-level healthcare management role responsible for overseeing, coordinating, and improving maternal and reproductive health services across multiple health facilities and Local Government Areas (LGAs). The position seamlessly integrates clinical oversight, team leadership, program monitoring, and administrative and logistical management to ensure the highest standards of patient care and operational efficiency.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Ensure that all midwives and MCH staff have standard job descriptions and perform their duties accordingly.
- Plan, organize, and ensure the implementation and supervision of maternal and child health interventions in all health facilities in respective LGAs based on national reproductive health policy guidelines.
- Participate in annual project planning and budgeting, and when needed, support the TMM and Medical Coordinator with new project proposals and strategic planning.
- Work closely with Medical Activity Managers to ensure that each health facility in target LGAs has maternal and reproductive health guidelines and protocols.
- Assist and collaborate with field doctors and nurses when required (normal or complicated deliveries, spontaneous vaginal deliveries, etc.) to complement existing human resources and contribute to the resolution of complicated cases and arrange timely referral to higher level health facilities.
- Ensure newborn babies are followed up correctly from delivery until discharge, and that all pregnant women and newborn children are referred to the Extended Program on Immunization (EPI).
- Plan and supervise associated HR processes (recruitment, training, performance evaluation, motivation, internal/external communication, etc.) in order to improve staff capabilities and ensure both the correct staffing size and required knowledge levels.

- Conduct monthly meetings with all MCH staff from all LGAs to provide everyone with a chance to share achievements and highlight challenges.

jobs.title: Nutrition Assistant - Maiduguri, Magumeri, Dikwa
jobs.body:
## **JOB PURPOSE:**

The incumbent will be responsible for the day-to-day management of activities at the Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) site. This includes requesting, receiving, and distributing nutrition supplies according to daily needs; maintaining accurate records of quantities received and utilized and compiling daily reports on stock movements and the number of malnourished children attending the OTP to receive treatment. The incumbent will also support the Medical Activity Manager in preparing technical weekly and monthly programme reports including key indicators such as total admissions, default rates, deaths, recovery rates, and other relevant OTP performance data.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Prepare weekly and monthly forecasts for nutrition supplies for the Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) based on the number of children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) enrolled in the programme.
- Prepare monthly supply requests and submit them to the relevant Medical Activity Manager for validation and approval. Follow up with the logistics team on shipment status to ensure supplies arrive before existing stock is depleted.
- Coordinate closely with warehouse staff to ensure nutrition supplies are dispatched to the assigned OTP site daily in accordance with approved requests.
- Verify that all nutrition supplies received at the OTP are within their expiry dates and suitable for distribution. Ensure that patients receive ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) with at least 14 days remaining before expiry.
- Work closely with OTP nurses to compile daily reports on programme performance including new admissions, total attendance, defaulters, recovery rates, deaths and other relevant indicators.
- Ensure that the quantity of RUTF distributed each day corresponds to the number of patients who attended the OTP and their prescribed ration.
- Collect empty RUTF sachets from caregivers for supplies issued 7–14 days earlier. Verify that the batch numbers on returned sachets correspond with the batch numbers of the RUTF distributed during the previous visit.
- Record all empty sachets collected in the daily reporting template. Immediately report any discrepancies, missing sachets, or inconsistencies in batch numbers to the Medical Activity Manager.
- Support the Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) focal person with daily reporting on the number of IYCF sessions conducted and other relevant programme information.
- At the end of each month, compile, finalize, and submit the OTP monthly report to the Medical Activity Manager for review and feedback.
- Ensure that all Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) develop weekly work plans outlining proposed outreach activities and conduct field visits in accordance with these pre-approved plans.
- Ensure that CNVs perform mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) screening for all children under 59 months of age and record the results daily in the approved reporting template.
- Compile nutrition data received from all CNVs on a daily basis and submit a consolidated monthly report to the Medical Activity Manager.
- Organize training sessions for CNVs on the community-based management of acute malnutrition and reporting requirements, in consultation with the line manager.
- Ensure that Community Health Volunteers and OTP staff maintain adequate stocks of Health Management Information System (HMIS) tools, including registers, tally sheets, OTP cards, and other required reporting materials.
- Assess monthly and annual requirements for HMIS tools and submit timely requests to the Medical Activity Manager to facilitate printing or procurement from the State Ministry of Health (SMOH), ensuring uninterrupted availability at OTP and community level.
- Any other responsibility assigned by the respective line manager.

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Diploma/Certificate in CHEW, bachelor’s degree preferred.
- Minimum 2 years’ professional experience as Nutrition Assistant and previous experience in other NGO’s

**Professional requirements:**

- At least 6 months of previous work experience in a data-management role in NGO
- Able to learn and use software used for recording

- Prior experience in an INGO is required.

jobs.title: Finance Manager
jobs.body:
TEAM PURPOSE: To ensure effective financial management and reporting within Syria programme

  
JOB PURPOSE: To manage and co-ordinate the effective and efficient implementation of financial support across the country office and in the programme. To advise on ‘best practice’ and ensure compliance, governance in all areas of financial management. Create a team than can respond innovatively and effectively and create an enabling environment to support effectively programme delivery.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES (Technical, Leadership, People and Resource management) Operational Financial Management and Internal Control:  
•Ensures that all Finance procedures are consistent with corporate and regional standards, are clearly defined and understood and are operated effectively throughout the programme.  
•Ensures effective, timely and accurate functioning and monitoring of the complete PeopleSoft financial systems (GL and OPAL), including maintaining the completeness and integrity of data within the system, generating necessary reports and authorising monthly data compilation in the system.  
•Contributes to the design of and oversee the preparation of regular (monthly/quarterly) management reports (QMRs) to meet the needs of programme managers within the programme and also meet the requirements for regular reporting set by the RC and Oxford, ensuring timeliness and accuracy.  
•Supports the CD, DCDS, and other programme staff, in the preparation of programme (PIP) and project budgets and manage the preparation of financial projections/forecasts on a regular basis.  
•Responsible for ensuring Bank Mandates and Delegation of Authorities updates.  
•Responsible in ensuring that all offices have enough funds for programme implementation  
•Responsible for ensuring that all transactions/finance reports have clear and complete audit trail both for internal and external audits  
  
Contribution to strategy development and implementation  
•Contributes to the development and implementation of the programme strategy in close collaboration with the Country Director and the Programme team.  
•Provides direct support to the Managers and the programme team on all matters of finance specifically budget preparation, monitoring, control and reporting with a view to ensuring good financial standards.  
  
Donor Finance Management:  
•Contributes to the development of proposals to donors.  
•Works with the funding team and the Donor Accountant to manage the preparation of financial reports to Donors according to set deadlines.  
•Responsible in ensuring complete audit trail from primary documentation to the accounting system for accurate and rapid donor reporting and general record keeping.  
•Responsible for ensuring proper donor contract management including systems requirements e.g. CRIMSON and RCB.

Budget, Financial Accounting and Reporting:  
•Verifies budgets prepared by finance officer and coordinator for accuracy and advises on design for optimum monitoring.  
•Responsible for ensuring the preparation of the Budget versus Actuals (BVA) and prepares analyses on a monthly basis or as and when required highlighting major variances for follow up and action by the CD, DCD and other stakeholders.  
•Responsible for ensuring accuracy and timely submission of month-ends and year-end reports including balance sheet reconciliations.  
•Responsible for the preparation and updating of annual budget (Global Budgets & Matrix) and forecast for the country programme.  
•Assesses performance of offices in complying with financial standards and ensures adequate internal controls are in place.  
•Responsible for ensuring all financial reports – month ends and year-end are complete and submitted to the CD for final approval.  
•Review and endorse the monthly payroll of all offices and signs/approves the payslip of Erbil office’s staff.  
•Final technical approval for cash flows, donor proposals and donor reports.  
  
Partners Financial Management  
•Lead in the Partners Financial Assessment in coordination with the Partnership Coordinator/Manager, HPC and Area Managers.  
•Ensure that Partnership Agreements are checked and reviewed in accordance to Oxfam and Donors requirements before CDs signing.  
•Ensure the Partners Financial Reports are checked and reviewed following Oxfam and Donors requirements  
•Responsible for ensuring that partners are monitored and capacitated as regards to financial management and other financial-related aspects of the partners project implementation.  
  
Team Management:  
•Leads, motivates and supports the Finance staff in direct line management to work effectively together in their jobs; provides close technical support to finance officers in the project offices
