jobs.title: Director of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning, VisionFund International
jobs.body:
VisionFund International is World Vision’s microfinance provider serving vulnerable clients through loans, savings, and insurance. We enable families to grow their livelihoods in hard to reach, rural locations in 28 countries so that caregivers can create secure futures for their children.

We believe in brighter futures for children; empowering families to create incomes and jobs; unlocking economic potential for communities to thrive.

Join VisionFund as we seek to end intergenerational poverty through microfinance.

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Director of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning, VFI**, you will lead the design and delivery of VisionFund’s measurement, evaluation, research, and learning function, ensuring the quality and credibility of evidence underpinning VisionFund’s impact claims. You will oversee the network monitoring architecture, client voice instruments, external research partnerships, internal impact evaluations, and capability building for impact staff across the MFI network.

You will also strengthen fundraising capabilities by leading MERL design for institutional, philanthropic, and blended-finance proposals from opportunity qualification through implementation. You will build joint measurement capability with World Vision and ensure measurement commitments are appropriately resourced and tracked.

You will own VisionFund’s monitoring and evaluation approach, including indicator architecture, data collection protocols, quality assurance, reporting cadence, and client voice methodologies. You will establish technical standards for impact measurement, provide assurance on their application, and ensure evidence is consistently used to inform decisions.

You will lead MERL design for funding proposals, advise on measurement-related go/no-go decisions, and ensure measurement requirements are credible, costed, and deliverable. You will build measurement capability with World Vision support and field offices and track commitments throughout implementation.

You will own and maintain VisionFund’s theory of change and manage the organisational research agenda, prioritising questions where stronger evidence can influence decisions. You will manage flagship academic research partnerships, commission and quality-assure third-party research, and strengthen the evidence base supporting child-level results and defensible impact claims. You will also contribute to sector methodology development through publications, technical working groups, and peer review.

You will design and deliver capability-building for impact measurement staff across the MFI network through technical curricula, coaching, methodological guidance, and tooling support. You will manage the measurement implications of network changes, including reporting close-out for exiting entities and maintaining the integrity of network-level aggregates across reporting periods.

You will lead the MERL team, including performance management, capability development, and succession planning, while fostering a Christ-centred, high-performing culture. You will establish routines that ensure evidence reaches and influences decision-making and will contribute to departmental and organisational strategy as a member of the Impact & Engagement senior leadership team.

**Requirements include:**

- Graduate-level degree in Economics, Development Economics, Statistics, Public Policy, Evaluation, or a related quantitative discipline, or demonstrably equivalent applied expertise
- Minimum 10 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role leading MERL, evaluation, research, or impact functions within a multinational NGO, development finance institution, inclusive finance organization, or similarly complex global organization.
- Demonstrated experience leading the design and implementation of measurement frameworks, evaluation methodologies, and impact-monitoring systems across multi-country or decentralized organizations.
- Minimum 5 years of experience designing and overseeing MERL components of institutional donor, foundation, climate-finance, or other externally funded proposals, including results frameworks, indicator selection, evaluation design, and budget development.
- Demonstrated experience serving as a technical counterpart to academic institutions, research organizations, consultants, or external evaluators, including commissioning, quality assurance, interpretation, and application of research findings.
- Proven experience strengthening technical capability and performance of geographically dispersed teams through coaching, training, curriculum development, and technical guidance.
- Experience influencing and maintaining quality standards across teams and stakeholders that are not under direct line management.
- Demonstrated experience leading organizational change, establishing, redesigning, or significantly strengthening a MERL, research, or evidence function.
- Evidence of external technical contribution through publications, conference presentations, participation in technical working groups, peer review, or other recognized sector contributions.
- Proven experience leading and developing diverse professional teams, including performance management, talent development, succession planning, and fostering high-performance cultures.
- Fluent in English. Working French or Spanish desirable.
- **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement: Home** based role with 20% travel

*For positions filled in the United States, the typical salary range for this role is $102,000 to $140,000 USD. Ranges are based on various factors, including the labor market, job type, job level, internal equity and budget. Exact salary offers will be determined by factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, experience and geographic location.*

jobs.title: Expression of Interest: Annual Resilience Measurement - SomReP
jobs.body:
**Terms of Reference for Annual Resilience Measurement**

**Programme Name: Somalia Resilience Programme (SomReP)**

**Target Locations:** 10 districts of SomReP target Districts

**Programme Goal:** Increase the resilience of chronically vulnerable Somali people, households, communities and systems to recurrent climatic shocks and other related risks in targeted pastoral, agro-pastoral and peri-urban livelihood zones by 2029

**Specific Objective:** Sustainably improve food security and livelihoods of Somali people, households, communities through effective risk management, protection of productive assets, improved governance of resilience structures, and promotion of innovations and evidence-based programming.

**Intermediary Outcomes:**

1. Improved capacity of households to implement disaster risk reduction and positive coping strategies to mitigate the immediate effect of exposure to shock;
2. Improved capacity of individuals, households and communities to adhere to positive development trajectories; despite exposures to shocks and utilize strategies designed to allow adaptation to rapid and slow on-set hazards;
3. Improved capacity of households to engage in strategies for sustainable livelihoods and economic growth to enhance food security and resilience;
4. governance structures at community, district and national levels are strengthened to enhance participation, transparency and accountability;
5. Programming, policy actions and decisions on resilience in Somalia informed on evidence-based resilience research, learning and innovation

**Key Partners:** ADRA, ACF, CARE, COOPI, DRC, Oxfam, Shaqodoon, and World Vision Somali (Consortium lead).

**Assessment Type:** Annual Resilience Measurement (ARM 2026)

**Target Locations:** 10 active SomReP districts (pastoral, agro-pastoral, peri-urban, and displacement settings). Badhan, Bossaso, Burao, Ceel Afweyne, Dollow, Eyl, Laas Caanood, Lughaya, Hargeisa and Salahley

**Start and End Date:** November 2026

**Anticipated Reporting Date:** December 2025 (Final Consolidated Report)

**1.0 Background**

1. **About SomReP**

Somali Resilience Programme (SomReP) is a consortium of seven international NGOs and one local NGO namely Action Against Hunger (AAH), the Adventist Development and Relief Agency International (ADRA), Cooperative Assistance for Relief Everywhere (CARE), Cooperazione Internazionale (COOPI), Danish Refugee Council (DRC), Oxfam, World Vision Somalia and Shaqodoon whose aim is to tackle the challenge of mitigating the effects of recurrent shocks and stressors and alleviating the chronic vulnerability that is common among pastoralists, agro-pastoralists, and peri-urban households across Somalia. The program was designed to address communities’ unique needs by building resilient livelihoods, a strategy founded on the lessons learned and best practices of the consortium members.

With support from DFAT, EU, SIDA, BMZ and SDC, SomReP has been implementing interventions with the aim of enhancing the resilience of vulnerable populations. To achieve this, SomReP programming supports resilience through:

1. Livelihoods & food security: HHs in targeted communities have improved access to productive livelihoods for enhanced food access and diversity;
2. Social Safety Nets: HHs in target communities have their livelihoods and assets protected during shocks and stressors through the establishment and strengthening of social safety nets, including the use of crisis modifier mechanisms such as Savings Group Schemes;
3. Natural resource management: Eco–system health improved through promotion of equitable and sustainable natural resource management;
4. Local governance capacity building: Communities, civil society and local institutions are better equipped with resilience strategies and response capacities to cope with recurrent shocks and stressors; and

The rationale behind the theory of change and impact pathways is that implementation of such interventions would eventually result in positive changes in well-being indicators which implicitly is indicative of enhanced adaptive, absorptive and transformative capacity. The program targets 45,350 households and is implemented in the districts of; Badhan, Bossaso, Burao, Ceel Afweyne, Dollow, Eyl, Laas Caanood, Lughaya, Hargeisa and Salahley,

At the beginning of all these projects, SomReP conducted baseline surveys to establish benchmark indicators. In addition, since 2016/17 SomReP has conducted annual resilience measurements to document impact of the SomReP programmes and assess the progress made annually on key outcomes and output indicators. This resilience measurement study will build on these studies to document the programme’s impact and assess the progress so far made on key outcomes and output indicators. SomReP would also want to take advantage of this assessment to establish whether the hypotheses and assumptions set to underpin SomReP Theory of Change and causal linkages between inputs and activities and outcomes and impacts were plausible and valid. The results of the assessment will be particularly important for SomReP not only to understand the impact of the project, test the theory of change underpinning the strategies and interventions delivered, but will also inform future strategic programming and project development. The 2025 round will be the fifth consecutive annual assessment and will generate nationally comparable data across 10 active districts where SomReP is currently operating.

The table below provides the core and outcomes indicators for SomReP: [https://wvi.box.com/s/l3dcl2kath9tjj2atu95e81k8ttpbher](https://wvi.box.com/s/l3dcl2kath9tjj2atu95e81k8ttpbher)

**2.0 Purpose and Scope of Annual Resilient Measurement**

**2.1 Annual Resilience Measurement**

The scope and focus of the ARM is to explore the outcomes and impact of the programme, in order to facilitate an understanding amongst the consortium programme staff and stakeholders of the extent to which the envisaged change has been realized. It will track progress against SomReP’s Theory of Change, identify resilience trajectories, and provide actionable evidence for adaptive management.

ARM 2026 will generate nationally representative data on resilience capacities, food security, livelihoods, and coping mechanisms across 10 districts using household surveys, KIIs with local leaders and government, and FGDs with women, youth, and marginalized groups.

**2.2. ARM 2026 Objectives:**

- Assess the relevance, and effectiveness of the program strategies and interventions in relation to the context and the programme strategic framework, documenting the lessons learnt and best practices to inform future adaptations of interventions typologies.
- Establish the extent to which the consortium has achieved its purpose and delivered on intended outputs, and whether the intended outcomes were met in relation to resilience programming
- Assess the impact of the programme with particular focus on establishing changes that have occurred as measured by resilience capacity indices (absorptive capacity index, adaptive capacity index and transformative capacity index ) and wellbeing indicators (provided for in SomReP master logical framework) for example food security and coping strategies indicators (i.e. HHS, FCS, rCSI), ownership of household and community productive assets (climate sensitive and non-climate sensitive assets), income and expenditures among others; and disaggregated to livelihood zones and other vulnerabilities.
- Assess the effectiveness and efficiency of programme interventions in strengthening the response capacity of various shocks and stresses including COVID-19 effects, Desert Locust, Conflict, drought, Floods etc.
- Employ a quasi-experimental design to compare households and communities directly targeted by SomReP interventions with non-targeted or indirectly exposed groups, thereby strengthening attribution of observed changes to program interventions.
- Compare findings with the last four rounds of ARM surveys (2021–2025) to analyze longitudinal trends in resilience trajectories, highlight persistent gaps, and identify lessons on what has worked or not worked in different livelihood and displacement contexts.

***Gender specific questions***

- Has there been an increase in women’s /girls’ access to health, education, information, training, or other services? How does this compare to men’s or boys’ access to these services? Did the program address women’s greatest needs for human capital?
- How has the program influenced women's access to resources and their ability to assert rights in comparison to men, and which barriers to women's economic empowerment were most effectively addressed?
- Were there any discernible disparities in benefits between men and women, and how effectively did the program incorporate women's perspectives in community-focused discussions?
- How have external conditions and power dynamics uniquely impacted women's and girls' experiences and opportunities?
- Based on the program's results, what essential changes are recommended to enhance gender equality in SomReP's next phase?

**3.0 Study Population, Scope and Methodology**

**3.1 Study Population and Sampling Frame**

The study population and sampling frame will comprise of 10 districts where the programme has been implemented targeting households, government line ministries focal points, local community committee leaders as well as the different community groups and leaders. The sampling frame will constitute target project beneficiaries, and community governance structures from the districts. The sample frame will further include strategic partners such as government departments who have been involved in coordinating the programme.

**3.2 Survey Design**

The study will use a cross sectional survey research design that incorporates both qualitative and quantitative data collection as well as analysis techniques. The consultant will be expected to propose an appropriate and detailed methodology for conducting this study including the appropriate design for the nested quasi-experimental component. This includes specifying the data collection methods, how to phase the implementation to ensure that there is rigorous data triangulation between the data collection methods, data collection tools corresponding to type of information to be collected and the target population, sample size for both qualitative and quantitative data together with the calculation formula used to arrive at such with all parameters defined. The qualitative data needs to indicate the key stakeholders to be involved in the key informant interviews as well as the focus group discussions. The consultant will further have to proposed the methodological approach (research design, sampling approach) for conduct tracer studies for TVET and VSLA participants.

The consultant will develop data collection tools that will need to be approved by the project M&E team. He/She will ensure that the survey tools designed will cover all outcome level indicators as well as add more questions to the questionnaire as appropriate.

The Project M&E team recommends that the consultant employs mobile data collection for quantitative data. The consultant will also be responsible for engaging and managing the team of data enumerators during the data collection period. The consultant will make use of SomReP data management platform for the quantitative data collection.

**4.0 Logistics**

The consultants will be responsible for their own logistics (i.e. transport and accommodation if necessary). The consultants will also be responsible for their own insurances, vaccinations, health, and security preparedness.

**5.0 Ethical and Technical Requirements**

The successful consultant will be responsible for ensuring that data collection and analysis approaches are designed to mitigate child protection risks and protect participants’ privacy and wellbeing by establishing and following credible ethical evaluation principles:

- The lead consultant shall ensure that all survey participants are fully informed of the objectives of the study, their right to decline participation, and their liberty to withdraw at any stage. Informed consent from beneficiaries is mandatory prior to commencing data collection. In addition, where applicable, and depending on the nature of the study, the consultant shall also seek approval from an Institutional Review Board (IRB) i.e. Somalia Bureau of Statistics or any other agencies.
- The lead consultant shall ensure that all research assistants are oriented on research ethics and child protection policy prior to commencement of data collection.
- The lead consultant shall ensure that each member of the research team adheres to research ethics and child protection policies.
- The lead consultant shall ensure that every piece of information collected is treated with all the confidentiality that it deserves.
- The lead consultant shall ensure that survey participants to be involved in the study are well informed of the objectives of the study and their consent is sought prior to starting data collection. Participants will be informed of their rights to decline participation in the study and that they will be at liberty to withdraw from the process if they wish to do so.

**6.0 Roles and Responsibilities of ARM Stakeholders: Consultant**

**Consultants' Scope of Work**

The study is to be conducted by a consultant with the below list of scope of work.

- Acquire all clearances and permissions necessary to collect data in all needed regions where the project will be implemented
- Preparation for the study: planning scope, engagement, logistics and schedule; documented in a clear inception plan together with the work plan including schedule for field work
- Develop inception report before actual roll out of the assessment detailing study methodology and appropriate/relevant data collection tools, sampling and workplan.
- Work closely with SomReP Head of Quality Assurance, M&E and Knowledge Management during the design of the methodology/ tools; agree on the tools that will be used.
- Incorporate feedback into tools and reports which will be given from the SomReP team.
- Adequately train and supervise enumerators/Research assistants across the locations during the data collection exercise.
- Undertake internal quality control procedures to ensure data collected is comprehensive, consistent and accurate
- Make visits to data collection sites and lead primary data collection and analysis
- Incorporate feedback from the project team and other stakeholders.
- Conduct Focus group discussions and Key informant interviews with sampled stakeholders including government, partner frontline staff, Consortium staff etc
- Conduct data analysis for the quantitative and qualitative data.
- Draft ARM 2025 Report with resilience indicator tables.
- Final Consolidated Report synthesizing findings across ARM, with cross-cutting lessons and recommendations.
- Submit a summary brief of the results (not more than 20 pages)
- Do a debriefing on preliminary findings. The result is expected to be shared with SIDA, DFAT, and other stakeholders, and the consultant needs to give due attention to the quality of the report.
- Approximately one-hour PowerPoint presentation of results and discussions to be presented in a stakeholder’s validation workshop.
- Cleaned survey data (in Excel and STATA compatible formats), transcripts of the FGDs, KIIs, photographs and ethical approval from Somali Bureau of Statistics or designated agency or bodies etc
- Infographics and factsheets outlining the Key Findings

**7.0 Required Skills, Experience and Competence**

SomReP is looking to engage the services of a qualified consultant in undertaking the ARM. We are looking for a consultant who has the following skills and expertise;

- In depth knowledge and experience of Somalia (especially the district of interest in this study) and its regions including government and community level service delivery structures.
- Masters degree in Social science, Agricultural Economics, Development studies, Public Health, Monitoring and evaluation and international studies, project planning and management and other related fields
- Has a minimum of 5 years of technically sound experiences in conducting livelihood projects evaluations or Resilience measurements
- Proven expertise in large-scale mixed-methods research and application of OECD-DAC evaluation criteria.
- Proven Experience in conducting Quasi-Experimental study design in fragile or similar contexts.
- Familiarity with the Technical Assistance to NGOs (TANGO) Resilience measurement framework.
- Familiarity with computation of resilience capacity, adaptive capacity, absorptive capacity and transformative capacity indices.
- Has at least 5 years of extensive experience in food security, resilience measurement, governance, displacement, WASH, and livelihood programming/resilience programming in fragile contexts
- Diverse team comprising personnel with the following skills and expertise: Resilience expert, M&E expert, statistician/data analyst, Gender expert, graphics designer etc.
- Demonstrated experience of working in donor-funded projects, EU, BMZ and SDC will be an added advantage
- Excellent analytical and communication skills
- Experience in writing impact evaluation reports and presenting this to diverse audience
- Ability to produce high quality work under tight timelines
- Experience working in Somalia

**8.0 Roles and Responsibilities of ARM Participants: World Vision Staff / SomReP / Partners**

- Ensure that the consultants adhere to research ethics and child protection policy
- Ensure quality assurance and provide technical oversight throughout the study implementation
- Provide the consultants with necessary documents as demanded by the consultant
- Review report and provide feedback to the consultants to ensure quality delivery and compliance to the study protocol
- Support community entry, mobilization, and contextual insights.
- Arrange key informant interviews and focus-group discussions as requested by the consultants.
- Review and approve operational approaches to be used by the consultants including the inception report
- Review the draft report and provide feedback to the consultants.
- Facilitate access and participate in the dissemination of findings.
- Approve the final reports contingent on the reports meeting the intended objectives and quality assurances

**9.0 Project Timeframe**

The assessment is expected to commence in November 2025 for approximately 30-45 days inclusive of data collection period and report review. The consultant is expected to provide a detailed schedule listing the different activities to be conducted and their time period.

**More Details to be provided in the full ToR upon Expression of Interest.**

**We hereby invite Expression of Interest from registered, approved and reputable consultants to provide above-named services to World Vision Somalia.**

jobs.title: Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment
jobs.body:
Terms of reference (TOR)

Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment

UGANDA & KENYA

· Project: Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP)

· Procuring Organisation: IsraAID

· Contract Type: Consultancy

· Contract Period: October 2026 to December 2026, 75 days (Phased implementation)

· Target Start Date: Tentatively 26/10/2026

· Application Deadline: 23/10/2026

· Submission Method: EMAIL – see 'how to apply'

BACKGROUND

IsraAID is an International Humanitarian Non-Governmental Organization founded in 2001 and headquartered in Israel. It supports people and communities affected by humanitarian crises, combining rapid emergency response with longer-term recovery, resilience, and preparedness. Over the years, IsraAID has worked in more than 60 countries, responding to disasters, displacement, epidemics, and other crises. Its mission is centered on partnering closely with local communities to provide urgent assistance while helping them rebuild and strengthen their resilience to future shocks.

IsraAID is implementing a project titled Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement in Uganda and in Kakuma Refugee Camp in Kenya. The programme intends to improve health outcomes and reduce morbidity and mortality associated with malnutrition in vulnerable communities participating in the Program. ICNMP is designed as a regional initiative that responds to acute and chronic nutrition needs across East Africa, beginning its phase zero in Q2 of 2026, and actual implementation in September 2026. Although the immediate program launch focuses on Uganda and the emergency phase in Kenya, early 2027 will see Kenya incorporating the full package while the broader intention is to establish a model that can later expand to South Sudan as funding becomes available. The regional framing is essential, as the scale of displacement, vulnerability, and recurring shocks across these countries requires harmonized technical standards, shared learning, and coordinated supply chain approaches. The program will expand decentralized nutrition services by placing screening, early identification, and treatment within spaces that families already use daily, including schools, Child-Friendly Spaces, transit points, and primary health facilities. To be able to achieve the intended outcomes, IsraAID seeks services of a consultant to conduct a baseline upon which project progress and successes will be measured.

This Terms of Reference (ToR) sets out the background, purpose, objectives, scope of work, expected deliverables, and management arrangements for the baseline study, and invites eligible firms to submit technical and financial proposals for consideration.

PURPOSE

This assignment aims at establishing both quantitative and qualitative baseline information on access to integrated nutrition services, nutrition and food security practices and programme systems to ensure that these are addressed by programme interventions to realise the intended overall goal. The baseline will also establish baseline information on several learning areas under the OECD criteria and the IsraAID Community Resilience framework (CRF). The baseline therefore aims at obtaining verified, disaggregated benchmark values for the programme indicators, enabling precise measurement of outcomes and impacts at endline (Year 2, 2028).

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The assignment will specifically

A. Assess the 3 programme outcome indicators

1\. Vulnerable communities — especially children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) — access integrated, quality nutrition services delivered through a multi-tier workforce (community and formal system) and functional multi-sectoral pathways.

2\. Caregivers and community structures adopt improved nutritional and food security practices that prevent and protect against malnutrition.

3\. Programme systems — accountability, information, governance and supply chain, inventory management systems, logistics & distribution modalities — are functional and progressively integrated into and owned by national, district and community structures.

B. Provide baseline information on the specified Community Resilience Framework (CRF) and OECD learning questions.

SCOPE

The baseline survey will be conducted in programme’s area of implementation, covering Nakivale Refugee Settlement and its surrounding host communities in Western Uganda and Turkana West Sub-County specifically targeting Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kalobeyei settlement and its surrounding host communities in Kenya. There are several credible data sources that will benefit the project including, among others, District Information Health System (DHIS 2),

Food Security and Nutrition Assessment reports (FSNA), Demographic Health Surveys, and Population Census reports. Primary baseline information will be obtained from, among others, health facilities, schools, households, children-friendly spaces, community structures and partners engaged in nutrition interventions

METHODOLOGY

IsraAID anticipates a mixed-methods baseline design combining quantitative and qualitative approaches, consistent with the evidence requirements set out in the MEAL Plan. The final design will be proposed by the Firm and refined collaboratively with IsraAID’s MEAL team.

The baseline study should be designed so that its instruments, sampling frame, and methodology can be replicated with fidelity at endline, enabling credible before and after comparison and contribution analysis.

ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS

The consultant will be expected to demonstrate how the assessment will be conducted in line with research ethics while protecting the human rights of the participants. It will also be the responsibility of the consultant to ensure strict adherence to IsraAID Safeguarding Policy. The consultant will also be responsible for ensuring that any persons hired, engaged, or consulted during the process are familiar with the policy and commit to abide by it during the delivery of the assignment.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE

This assignment will last approximately 75 days from the date of signing of the contract. The consultant will provide a detailed work plan with realistic timelines to the logical conclusion of the baseline survey. The following deliverables are expected from the consultant:

The baseline assessment will be undertaken by one consultant/firm. Fieldwork will be conducted sequentially, beginning in Uganda and subsequently moving to Kenya.

1\. Inception & Evaluation Design – Week 1

Key activities

· Desk review of programme proposal, Theory of Change, Logic Model and MEAL Plan.

· Inception meetings with IsraAID.

· Refine evaluation design, sampling strategy and evaluation matrix.

Deliverables

· Inception report.

· Refined methodology and sampling plan.

· Approved work plan and evaluation/indicator matrix.

2\. Tool Development, Piloting & Field Preparation – Weeks 2–3

Key activities

· Finalize quantitative and qualitative data collection tools aligned with Indicator Reference Sheets.

· Share tools with relevant teams and incorporate feedback.

· Pilot testing and tool refinement.

· Enumerator training/orientation and field preparation.

· Ethics/safeguarding clearance preparation.

Deliverables

· Approved final data collection tools and protocols.

· Pilot findings and revisions.

· Enumerator training/orientation completed.

· Ethics/safeguarding documentation.

3\. Data Collection – Uganda – Weeks 4–5

Key activities

· Deploy quantitative and qualitative surveys/interviews with agreed respondents in Uganda.

· Conduct ongoing field-level data quality assurance.

· Hold regular field debriefs with participating stakeholders.

· Complete Uganda fieldwork and initial data quality checks.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

Deliverables

· Uganda quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Uganda dataset.

3\. Transition & Data Collection – Kenya – Weeks 5–7

Key activities

· Close out any outstanding Uganda data collection activities.

· Uganda findings first draft submission

· Transition/travel from Uganda to Kenya.

· Conduct quantitative and qualitative data collection in Kenya.

· Maintain ongoing data quality assurance and stakeholder debriefs.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

· Complete Kenya fieldwork and initial data checks.

Deliverables

· Uganda fieldwork close-out and initial findings draft shared.

· Kenya quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Kenya dataset.

4\. Analysis & Validation – Weeks 7–9

Key activities

· Clean, code and analyze quantitative and qualitative data.

· Triangulate findings across methods and countries.

· Develop and populate indicator baseline values.

· Prepare and conduct validation workshop with IsraAID/programme stakeholders.

Deliverables

· Analyzed datasets.

· Populated indicator baseline table.

· Draft findings.

· Validation workshop summary.

5\. Reporting & Dissemination – Weeks 9–10

Key activities

· Incorporate feedback from IsraAID.

· Finalize evaluation/baseline report.

· Prepare executive summary/brief and presentation deck.

· Present findings to relevant stakeholders.

· Hand over final datasets, tools and supporting documentation.

Deliverables

· Final report in MS Word and PDF.

· Executive summary/brief.

· Presentation deck.

· Final clean datasets and tools.

Summary of Key Milestones

· Week 1: Inception phase completed

· Week 2 & 3: Tools finalised/piloted and field preparation completed

· Week 4 & 5: Uganda fieldwork completed

· Weeks 6 & 7: Kenya fieldwork completed and initial Uganda finding draft

· Weeks 8 & 9: Analysis and validation completed; draft report ready

· Week 10: Final report, presentation and data/tools handover completed

Note: The timeline is indicative and may be adjusted in consultation with IsraAID, provided the overall 10-week period and Uganda-to-Kenya sequencing are maintained. Analysis may overlap with final data cleaning. IsraAID will want to be provided access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected, to enable ongoing data quality checks and early identification of gaps or issues.

Summary of Key Baseline Deliverables

· Inception report by the consultant within one (1) week upon signing of the consultancy contract.

· Draft Baseline Survey report with clear findings in line with the aim and outcomes of the programme, conclusion, and recommendations for review.

· Final Baseline Survey report in electronic format (MS Word as well as PDF)

· Summary of the findings in (MS PowerPoint) to be used for subsequent dissemination.

· All raw data: transcripts from In-depth Interviews, Individual Surveys, FGDs and cleaned data set used for analysis and production of the final report in an acceptable electronic format shared on a rolling basis.

KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

IsraAID and the Programme Team

· Draw the contract and manage its implementation within the period.

· Coordinate the baseline study

· Share relevant documentation that are important for this assignment

· Introduction of the consultant and team to the relevant bodies within the study locations.

· Organize a validation meeting for the baseline findings.

· Review and approve the deliverables presented by the consultant.

Consultant

· Recruit, contract, remunerate, train, coordinate, and supervise data collectors, ensuring compliance with the agreed methodology, ethical standards, data quality requirements, and timelines.

· Lead consultancy assignment including data collection and analysis.

· Develop and review the data collection tools.

· Lead the development of the consultancy report and incorporate any feedback from IsraAID

· Ensure all deliverables of the assignment are accomplished and approved by IsraAID

· Present findings to the IsraAID team and relevant stakeholders for validation.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

IsraAID expects the successful consultant/firm to field a multidisciplinary team with a balance of quantitative, qualitative, and GESI expertise, complemented by strong in-country presence across ICNMP priority geographies where possible. The indicative team composition below is provided as guidance; consulting firms may propose an alternative structure provided all required competencies are demonstrated and justified.

· Team Leader / Baseline Study Lead: Advanced degree in public health, social sciences, statistics, international development, or related field; minimum 10 years’ experience leading baseline/endline evaluations for complex, multi-country development programs; demonstrated experience with forced displacement, refugee, or migration programming; strong track record managing mixed-methods research teams across multiple African countries. Excellent interpersonal and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with the IsraAID team.

· Quantitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in statistics, economics, or related field; expertise in survey design, sampling methodology, and quantitative data analysis (e.g., STATA, R, SPSS); experience with mobile data collection platforms (e.g., KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, ODK).

· Qualitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in social sciences; expertise in qualitative methods including KIIs, FGDs, and complexity-aware approaches (e.g., Outcome

· Data Management / MEL Support: Experience in data cleaning, database management, and dashboard/data visualization; familiarity with data protection standards applicable to work with protected persons.

GOVERNANCE AND REPORTING LINES

The consulting firm will report to IsraAID’s ICNMP MEAL Coordinator, who holds day-to-day responsibility for the MEAL leadership of the ICNMP programme, and will work closely with the ICNMP program teams in both Uganda and Kenya Country Offices on tool design, data quality assurance, analysis, and reporting. The ICNMP MEAL Coordinator retains overall accountability for the assignment and will review and approve the inception report and final baseline report.

PAYMENT PLAN

50% after the approval of the inception report, 50% after the approval of the final report.

APPLICATION PROCESS

Interested candidates should submit the following:

· Technical proposal outlining approach and methodology

· A financial proposal in US Dollars (USD), detailing all consultancy-related costs (operational, and logistical costs for conducting the assignment in Kenya and Uganda).

· CVs of the Lead Consultant and the entire team

· At least three relevant samples of previous similar work

· At least two (2) recommendation letters from recent clients for similar assignments.

· Copy of the company registration, Memorandum, and Articles of Association if a company/ firm is applying.

· Copy of tax compliance Certificate

· TIN Number

· VAT Number

· Any other relevant information supporting the application.

EVALUATION CRITERIA FOR SELECTION OF THE CONSULTANT/CONSULTING FIRM

Proposals from the interested bidders will be evaluated against the following criteria:

1\. Technical Approach & Understanding of the Assignment (30%): Understanding of the programme, evaluation objectives and scope; quality and appropriateness of the proposed methodology; sampling approach; quantitative and qualitative

methods; data analysis, triangulation and validation; and ethical/safeguarding considerations.

2\. Relevant Experience & Technical Capacity (25%): Demonstrated experience conducting baseline studies, evaluations or similar assignments, particularly in humanitarian, refugee, displacement and development contexts. Experience working with refugee and host communities in Uganda and/or Kenya will be an advantage. Qualifications and expertise of the proposed consultant/team will also be considered.

3\. Workplan, Fieldwork & Data Quality Approach (20%): Feasibility of the proposed workplan within the 10-week period; capacity to undertake fieldwork sequentially in Uganda and Kenya; approach to data quality assurance, data management, safeguarding and secure access to data on a rolling basis during data collection.

4\. Financial Proposal & Value for Money (25%): Completeness, clarity and reasonableness of the financial proposal, including professional fees and all logistical and operational costs required to conduct the assignment in Uganda and Kenya.

ANNEXES

1\. Program Document

2\. Program LogFrame

RESERVATION OF RIGHTS

Nothing contained in this RFP/TOR shall be construed as creating any obligation on the part of IsraAID to enter into a contract with any bidder. IsraAID reserves the unrestricted right to determine the evaluation criteria, request additional documentation, waive minor irregularities, seek clarifications, reject any or all proposals, and terminate the procurement process at its sole discretion and without prior notice.

  
Appendixes can be found here - [**public folder**](https://israaid-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/eoyoo_israaid_org/IgC0MsUIQfMjR5rArPJsF2AmAZsbCmAQ5eV4Ul5n7Gh-fS8)

jobs.title: Head of Support Services - Lebanon (Readvertised)
jobs.body:
**Who are we?**

DRC has been responding to various humanitarian crises in Lebanon since 2004, working with Palestinian, Iraqi and Syrian refugees. Since 2011, DRC has focused on responding to the Syrian refugee crisis in Lebanon and the resulting impact on Lebanese host community, and more recently the impact of the economic and financial crises as well as responding to the ongoing conflict. DRC Lebanon’s focus is to ensure that we are able to respond to critical emerging humanitarian needs whilst improving the living conditions of displacement-affected populations and contributing to the achievement of durable solutions. DRC is focusing its response in protection, economic recovery, shelter and site coordination and management, and humanitarian mine action across the country directly and through partners. DRC is also contributing to the broader humanitarian response through our Referral Information Management System (RIMS), utilised by 170 organisations.

**About the job**

The Head of Support Services (HoSS) is operationally and strategically responsible for Finance, Human Resources, Logistics and Procurement, Administration and/or IT. S/he oversees, develops and provides strategic direction to his/her support areas. This role has a country focus (Lebanon) and ensures compliance to DRC procedures and guidelines within the country. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides support and/or technical guidance to country operations while overseeing country activities.

With senior level management experience, you are expected to have demonstrable successful track record of organizational development and resource mobilization and play a leadership role in developing and implementing country-specific strategies as well as improving operational systems, processes, and policies in support of DRC’s mission and values.

**Previous experience in a Finance Manager/Director or similar role and/or a Finance-related qualification is highly recommended.**

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**Responsibilities:**

**Staff Management**

- Lead and manage the support managers (including people planning, performance, well-being and development) whilst providing dotted technical line support to wider country support team.
- Work to build the capacity of the operational support staff throughout the operation though frequent in-service training sessions, mentoring support and frequent visits to field offices.
- Role model and lead the wider country programme against DRC values, diversity and inclusion as well as code of conduct.

**Support Services Management**

- Responsible for the strategic development, management and implementation of the support operations as per DRC operational handbook. This includes developing and improving operational approaches, compliance and systems, and support the Country Director to build and deliver effective and sustainable interventions.
- Support the Country Director and the Senior Management Team in liaising with donors and authorities, especially as relates to issues of compliance, registration, and audit
- Ensure appropriate technical support is available to programs, in line with organizational priorities
- Provide strategic guidance to the HR/Admin department to develop and implement DRCs HR policy in Lebanon. This includes providing strategic guidance for all staff management, career & development recruitment and induction process as well as appropriate stress management and care for Expatriates and National Staff.
- Lead on DRC Lebanon annual master budgets and ensuring that monthly monitoring of expenditure informs management decision making.
- Lead on the effective implementation and adherence of organization and stakeholder financial regulations.
- Overseeing the operationalization of the contextual/localized finance handbook.
- Ensure the implementation of sustainable and robust supply chain and financial system for an efficient and effective support to all DRC programs and support services.
- Ensure an efficient ICT Operating environment is in place to meet operational needs.

**Operational Management**

- Responsible for maintaining and improving operational resource management in the mission, together with SMT, identifying both short term and long-term resource needs and translate these into objectives and priorities for future DRC projects in Lebanon
- Responsible for leading the development and update of the resource management component of the Country Strategy, ensuring the Support Services facilitate the delivery of the strategy in line with DRC global policies and strategy.
- Ensure that DRC retains and continually develops its operational capacity to provide rapid emergency response in particular within its procurement and HR systems
- Ensure that Lebanon operation complies to DRC Risk Management Framework, and operational Compliance Tools and processes are duly implemented. This includes development of a risk management plan for the country that identifies the major financial and operational risks and implement a mitigation strategy
- Regular review and improvements to Country SOPs to ensure the internal control environment strengthened as well as develop policies as required where gaps are noted.
- Supervision, audits and controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to DRC’s operational standards within support area. This also includes ensuring the timely implementation of DRC’s internal audit and external audit recommendations and contextualize HQ understanding of local challenges.
- Participate as a member of the SMT in drafting project proposals, and on the use of resources according to budgets and policies.
- Together with the Head of Programs, lead the mainstreaming of Project Cycle Management and partnership best practices throughout the organization.
- Contribute to the delivery of DRC Lebanon’s localisation strategy, development and oversight of partnerships and ensure Support Services are fit for purpose to support equitable partnerships and capacity exchange.
- Ensure that all administrative and legal-related systems are accurate and maintained, and that DRC Lebanon is legally compliant with Government of Lebanon directives and processes.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of DRC’s global development initiatives
- As and when required, substitute the Country Director when is requested as such (leaves, field visits, long meetings etc)

**DRC Dynamics ERP System**

- Ensure ERP functionality is properly used by relevant staff
- Apply reports and data analytics from DRC Dynamics to improve overall performance
- Act as heavy user for most of the Projects & Finance functionalities

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect the following:

*Required*

- Minimum 7 years’ experience in a similar role in an international NGO.
- 4 years’ experience in people management with proven leadership skills.
- Proven operational management experiences and capability, including in complex and emergency settings
- Proven significant financial, information and systems management experience as well as in procurement and tender processes
- Understanding and experience of institutional fundraising.
- Excellent communication, negotiation and problem-solving capacities; with the ability to work flexibly in a diverse team in a dynamic environment, fostering a positive working environment
- Strong capacity building, facilitation, and presentation skills with the ability to collaborate, network and negotiate in order to facilitate communication and support to staff, local partners, Governments, UN, donors & other NGOs without losing sight of the strategic objective
- Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple competing deliverables on varying timelines
- Experience working in an ERP system, including Supply Chain, Finance and HR systems
- Full professional proficiency in English and Arabic

*Desirable*

- Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple competing deliverables on varying timelines
- Experience working in an ERP system, including Supply Chain, Finance and HR systems

**Languages**

- Full professional proficiency in English
- Full professional proficiency in Arabic

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Education**

A Master’s Degree or advanced professional qualification in Finance, Business Administration, Logistics or HR

**We offer**

- Contract length: 1 year
- Band: Management - E1
- Designation of Duty Station: Beirut - Lebanon
- Start date: ASAP

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for **national and expatriate employees.**

  
**DRC as an employer**  
By working in DRC, you will be joining a global workforce of around 6000 employees in approximately 30 countries. We pride ourselves on our:

- Professionalism, impact & expertise
- Humanitarian approach & the work we do
- Purpose, meaningfulness & own contribution
- Culture, values & strong leadership
- Fair compensation & continuous development

  
  
DRC’s capacity to ensure the protection of and assistance to refugees, IDP’s and other persons of concern depends on the ability of our staff to uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. DRC conducts thorough and comprehensive background checks as part of the recruitment process.  
  
**If you have questions or are facing problems with the online application process, please visit** [**drc.ngo/jobsupport**](https://drc.ngo/jobsupport)**.**
