Quantitative comparison should be undertaken only where sufficiently comparable data are available and should not rely on blanket comparisons of overhead or transfer ratios.

Please find all further details, including requirements and timelines [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/13oOsb4q9-w501OB3uhzsJ2cSWjdejLp6/view)

jobs.title: WASH&Shelter/NFI _only national staff

jobs.body:
Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) is currently looking for **Shelter/WASH Manager** to support implementation of the projects.

General information:

- Organization: Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH), Warsaw-based international non-governmental organization with representation office in Ukraine
- Position: Shelter/WASH Manager
- Location: Kyiv with regular field visits
- Job terms: full-time
- Type of job: employment contract
- Starting date: ASAP
- Duration: 12 months (3 month of approbation period) with possibility for extension

*We encourage qualified candidates to apply as soon as it is possible as the applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.*

**About PAH:**

Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) is an international non-governmental organization providing humanitarian and development aid worldwide since 1992. So far, the interventions have been carried out in 46 different countries. By possessing long-standing expertise in the implementation of projects in WASH, FSL, Protection, as well as Nutrition and Education, PAH concentrates its global activities on ensuring sustainable development of regions suffering from consequences of armed conflicts, natural disasters, climate change and others humanitarian crises.

PAH has been present in Ukraine since August 2014 delivering humanitarian aid to the most vulnerable of the conflict-affected population. PAH provides assistance to internally displaced people, elderly, children and other vulnerable population groups. PAH is currently working in the sectors of FSL, protection, WASH and Shelter. For more information, please refer to: [Homepage - Polska Akcja Humanitarna](https://robota.ua/redirect?event_name=url_click&redir_token=eyJPcmlnaW5hbFVybCI6Imh0dHA6Ly93d3cucGFoLm9yZy5wbC8iLCJWYWNhbmN5SWQiOjEwMTY5MDcxfQ==)

**Key Duties and Responsibilities:**

**Programme Management and Technical Leadership**

- Lead the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of WASH and Shelter/NFI assistance programmes in line with humanitarian standards and PAH guidelines.
- Contribute WASH/Shelter-NFI technical expertise to multi-sector needs assessments (MSNAs) and lead sector-specific needs assessments when required, translating findings into clear, prioritised programme recommendations.
- Lead the technical design of concept notes, proposals and project modifications with WASH/Shelter-NFI component;
- Develop detailed work plans, budgets and procurement plans for WASH and Shelter/NFI interventions in close coordination with the logistics department, ensuring efficient and effective use of resources.
- Contribute to the development and revision of the Country Programme Strategy, ensuring WASH/Shelter-NFI priorities, geographic focus, localisation approach and emergency-to-recovery pathways are clearly and realistically reflected.

 **Partner Coordination and Technical Support**

- Serve as the WASH/Shelter-NFI technical focal point for implementing partners; review partner assessments, designs, bills of quantities, technical specifications, work plans, and narrative reporting.
- Provide timely technical guidance, coaching and capacity-strengthening support to partners on WASH/Shelter-NFI programming methodologies, resource management and reporting requirements.
- Oversee partner implementation of WASH/Shelter-NFI activities, ensuring compliance with sectoral technical and donor requirements; escalate material risks promptly and track corrective actions to closure.

 **Quality Assurance, Tools and Monitoring**

- Review technical assessments, designs, specifications, BoQs, tender technical documentation, samples/materials, construction or installation quality, and commissioning/handover documentation for direct and partner-led activities.
- Define and maintain a risk-based technical monitoring framework and tools for direct and partner-led WASH/Shelter-NFI activities, coordinating monitoring planning with Area Managers, Project Leads, Partnership and MEAL teams.
- Develop and institutionalise practical WASH/Shelter-NFI tools, checklists, SOPs and a standard project-file and document-management structure, in coordination with Programme, Logistics, MEAL, Grants and Partnership teams.
- Participate in project reviews, field monitoring, troubleshooting and lessons-learned processes; use monitoring data to inform programme adjustments, identify best practices and contribute to organisational learning.

 **Financial Management**

- Monitor budget expenditure, identify variances and take corrective action as necessary to ensure financial accountability and transparency.
- Provide continuous review of partners' financial and programmatic performance and implementation.
- **Reporting and Representation**
- Prepare timely and accurate reports for donors, government partners and other stakeholders, highlighting programme achievements, challenges and lessons learned.
- Represent PAH in relevant national WASH, Shelter/NFI and technical coordination forums and cluster meetings, advocating for the sector and sharing useful updates and opportunities internally.
- Identify and pursue documented strategic or technical engagement opportunities with clusters, authorities, other NGOs, technical institutions and prospective partners.

 **Team Management and Capacity Strengthening**

- Lead the WASH/Shelter-NFI team, including hiring and management of staff, performance reviews and goal-setting, and development of supportive relations with subordinates.
- Ensure direct reports have clear objectives, regular documented check-ins and timely feedback, coordinating constructively with Area Managers and other functions.
- Maintain a practical capacity-development approach for PAH WASH/Shelter-NFI staff and implementing partners, delivering targeted coaching or learning sessions based on identified performance gaps.
- Maintain an effective management flow for the function, including clear priorities, realistic work planning, a live work plan/action tracker, and concise monthly reporting to the Head of Programmes.

 **Shelter/WASH Manager will be selected based on the qualification requirements described below:**

- Higher professional education in the relevant field of study (master’s degree, specialist);
- Professional experience of more than 7 years;
- At least 3 years of work experience in international or local NGO;
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English (at least upper-intermediate level) and Ukrainian;
- Understanding of the context in Ukraine;
- Understanding of international humanitarian work;
- Good interpersonal skills;
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Google Apps;
- Good organizational skills and discretion with confidential information;
- Proven ability to handle challenging workload;
- Ability to work independently and proactively.

**What PAH offers:**

- Opportunity to gain experience in a professional and flexible international NGO, one of the largest organizations in Central and Eastern Europe.
- Work in a dynamic and motivated team.
- Voluntary medical insurance fully covered by the organization.
- Free English language courses and other opportunities for professional growth.
- Full social benefits package in accordance with Ukrainian legislation.
- Flexible work arrangements.
- Access to confidential psychological support sessions when needed.

**Equal Opportunities and Non-Discrimination**

Our organization adheres to the principles of equality, respect for human dignity, and non-discrimination in accordance with the legislation of Ukraine.

We do not tolerate discrimination based on age, sex, gender identity, marital status, pregnancy, parental status, disability, health condition, race, skin color, ethnic or national origin, citizenship, language, religion or other beliefs, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic.

All candidates are assessed solely on the basis of their professional competencies and alignment with the position requirements.

 **Employment of Persons with Disabilities**

The organization is open to employing persons with disabilities and ensures equal opportunities to participate in the recruitment process.

If needed, we are ready to:

If you require any accessibility accommodations to participate in the recruitment process, please indicate this in your cover letter.

**Code of Conduct**

PAH applies a strict zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment (SH), and any inaction in response to such misconduct by its personnel, partners, or stakeholders. The organization is committed to preventing harm, ensuring a safe and respectful environment, and taking timely and appropriate action when harm occurs.

**How to Apply**

jobs.title: Sign Language Interpreter Consultants invitation to join our preferred supplier list
jobs.body:
**Call for Expressions of Interest**

**Sign Language Interpreters invitation to join our preferred supplier list Tanzania**

**Location:** Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Candidates must have the legal right to provide consultancy services in the country where any assignment is delivered.

**Contract type:** Consultant/Consultancy

**About Sightsavers**

Sightsavers is an international development organisation working to prevent avoidable blindness, promote equality for people with disabilities and support inclusive development. Through the Mastercard Foundation Digital Futures Programme, Sightsavers is supporting young women and men with disabilities to access digital skills, entrepreneurship opportunities and pathways into dignified and fulfilling work.

We are therefore issuing an invitation to qualified sign language interpreters in Tanzania to join our preferred supplier list (PSL). Successful applicants who join our PSL as pre-qualified consultants/consultancies will be contacted for short-term and intermittent assignments as and when the work becomes available. Please know inclusion on our PSL does not guarantee work, a minimum number of assignments, or any minimum level of fees.

**Programme:** Mastercard Foundation Digital Futures Programme and other Sightsavers programme activities requiring sign language interpretation support.

**Scope of work**

Consultants/Consultancies on the PSL may be invited to provide professional sign language interpretation for meetings, workshops, training sessions, consultations, recruitment activities, webinars, field visits, partner meetings, community engagement activities or recorded content. Assignments may be delivered in person, remotely or through hybrid arrangements, depending on programme needs.

The interpreter will support effective two-way communication between sign language users and spoken-language users, helping to ensure all participants can engage equitably, safely and with dignity.

Key responsibilities include:

- Provide accurate, impartial and professional interpretation between the relevant signed and spoken languages.
- Prepare for assignments by reviewing agendas, slides, technical terminology, participant information and safeguarding or accessibility notes shared in advance.
- Maintain professional neutrality and avoid speaking on behalf of participants except where clarification is needed to support accurate interpretation.
- Work respectfully with Deaf participants, programme participants, colleagues, partners, facilitators, captioners, note-takers, co-interpreters or other accessibility support providers.
- Advise Sightsavers where additional interpretation or accessibility support may be required, including co-interpreters, Deaf interpreters, relay interpreters, captioning, breaks or rotation arrangements.
- Maintain strict confidentiality before, during and after the assignment.
- Raise any concerns relating to accessibility, interpretation quality, safeguarding, wellbeing, conduct, data protection or logistics promptly through the agreed Sightsavers route.
- Comply with Sightsavers’ safeguarding, confidentiality, data protection, code of conduct and professional behaviour expectations.

**Consultant/Consultancy expertise**

- Professional experience providing sign language interpretation in the relevant national sign language and spoken language.
- Strong understanding of Deaf culture, communication preferences and disability inclusion.
- Experience interpreting in professional, development, education, employment, health, community, safeguarding, research or programme settings.
- Can interpret accurately, impartially and confidentially in sensitive or technical contexts.
- Ability to prepare for assignments by reviewing background materials and clarifying terminology in advance.
- Understanding of professional boundaries, safeguarding responsibilities and appropriate conduct when working with children, adults at risk, programme participants or community members.
- Work respectfully with diverse participants, including young people with disabilities, women with disabilities, partners, community representatives and Sightsavers staff.
- Willingness to complete required due diligence checks, safeguarding briefings, references, right-to-work or eligibility checks and any assignment-specific onboarding requirements before starting work.

**Safeguarding and conduct**

Sightsavers is committed to safeguarding, equality, diversity and inclusion. Consultant engagement is conditional on satisfactory completion of relevant checks and agreement to comply with Sightsavers’ safeguarding standards, Code of Conduct for representatives, confidentiality and data protection requirements. Where assignments involve children, adults at risk, programme participants, community members, personal stories, sensitive data, images or field activity, additional safeguarding controls may apply.

Please read the full [ToR](https://sightsavershh.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/HRExternal/IQC81GxEGFWIRaz_hH6jNIlRAWkSXeticPX4-a77gzegBv0) that details a suggested scope of work, safeguarding requirements, payment terms, skills, confidentiality and intellectual property provisions. Selection for the roster does not guarantee work.

- Ensure proper implementation and respect of organization policies and guidelines, design or adapt relevant local policies, procedures and tools for optimized management of the mission financial resources
- Support HQ Administration department in preparing country’s yearly financial forecast of mission (staff, running, shared and indirect costs) and annual budget
- Support Head of mission/Country Representative in elaborating and consolidating the annual accounting of the mission and the report to the relevant authorities and donors
- Support external and internal audits
- Oversee banking relationships and signatory responsibilities delegated
- Monitor the overall financial management of the mission
- Is responsible for coordinating and ensuring effective treasury management for the smooth running of operations, while maintaining appropriate controls to mitigate security risks. Identify and promptly flag financial shortfalls or overspending in the mission's financial management and propose corrective measures.
- Ensure compliance with general accounting and project financial management principles, as well as with UPP's anti-fraud, anti-corruption and anti-terrorism policies and procedures.
- Provide training, orientation and tutoring for finance and logistics staff and partners where necessary and/or requested
- Assess and mitigate the financial risks on the mission, ensure that reliable internal control systems are in place, and financial ethics is respected
- Check that the administrative procedures related to taxes and payment of social security obligations are followed, and comply with established legal procedures in the country
- Monitor the payment of suppliers and staff salaries

**HR management**

- Together with the Senior Management Team (SMT) and the field managers, plan HR operational and budget needs, in order to efficiently ensure the required sizing and capabilities of the mission

- Support the Senior Management Team (SMT) and the field managers in detecting training needs according to operational requirements, in evaluating people’s performance and in implementing the associated action plans to improve people capabilities
- Is responsible for training and coaching all HR staff in the mission on the key Human Resources pillars, policies, procedures, and practices, as well as raising awareness among key management staff, including coordinators, on HR responsibilities, risks, and good practices

- Essential degree in Economics/Finances/HR management, Psychology, International Relations, Political Science. Master in HR Management desirable
- Essential 3 years’ experience in Finance and HR Management with at least 2 in HR managerial positions in humanitarian contexts with NGOs
- Excellent oral and written English essential
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)
- Experience of financial reporting and grant management with a range of external donors using Excel and administrative software
- Financial management skills and knowledge of finance systems and procedures
- Strategic vision
- Leadership

- People management
- Ability to work in multicultural environment
- Non-discriminatory attitude

**UPP requires criminal background check certificate (released max 3 months before the date of job offer) to confirm a job offer. However, UPP runs selections to deploy staff in emergency programs and time-lapse between job offer and field deployment is often very short. Thus, we kindly ask all candidates to get prepared on time and be able to submit their certificate promptly in case of success in the selection.**

Un Ponte Per is an International NGO committed to diversity and inclusion within its teams, in line with the principle of non-discrimination. UPP encourages all candidates irrespective of gender, religion and ethnicity including persons with disabilities to apply and become part of the organization.

***Ethical Conduct & Safeguarding***

*UPP takes a **zero-tolerance** approach to any form of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (SEAH), Child Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, and Physical/Emotional Harm, including online abuse, and is committed to recruiting only those suitable to work with children and the communities we serve. As a participant in the* [*Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS)*](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/)*, UPP systematically requests information from previous employers on any substantiated findings of SEAH or serious breaches of child safeguarding, reserves the right to contact any organisation a candidate has worked for, and requests data on investigations ongoing at the time of their departure. All posts are subject to vetting checks including criminal records disclosure and screening against anti-terrorism, anti-money-laundering, anti-corruption, and anti-fraud sanctions lists. Shortlisted candidates must provide a criminal background check certificate issued no more than three months before the job offer; candidates are encouraged to obtain this in advance as processing times vary. By submitting an application, candidates confirm their understanding of these procedures, authorise UPP to conduct all mandatory inquiries, declare that they have never committed or been subject to findings of SEAH or Child Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, or Physical/Emotional Harm. All selected candidates are expected to work in accordance with UPP's Code of Conduct and all PSEAH and Child Safeguarding policies. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.*

jobs.title: Protection Officer (PRoL)-Daraa
jobs.body:
**Background/IRC Summary:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview/Summary:** The Protection Officer (PRoL) is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day implementation and technical quality of integrated protection programming delivered through partner organizations in Daraa and other assigned locations. The position has a primary focus on Protection and Rule of Law (PRoL) interventions, including legal awareness, legal assistance, civil documentation support, housing, land and property (HLP) issues, referrals, and community-based protection activities, while also supporting the quality and effective implementation of Child Protection (CP) and Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE) interventions delivered by partners.

The Protection Officer serves as the primary technical focal point for partner field teams, providing ongoing coaching, mentoring, capacity building, and technical guidance to ensure services are delivered in accordance with IRC standards, donor requirements, and international protection principles. The role includes conducting regular field visits, monitoring service quality, verifying program data and documentation, identifying implementation gaps, and working collaboratively with partners to strengthen program performance and accountability.

The Protection Officer supports the establishment and strengthening of community-based protection mechanisms, promotes meaningful participation of affected populations, and ensures that vulnerable individuals are safely identified and referred to appropriate services. The position works closely with partner staff, community structures, and IRC technical teams to promote integrated protection outcomes, strengthen referral pathways, enhance service quality, and ensure that protection interventions effectively address the needs of women, girls, boys, men, and individuals with specific needs.

The position also contributes to strengthening partner capacity, quality assurance processes, project reporting, coordination with stakeholders, and continuous improvement of protection programming to ensure the effective and accountable delivery of services across all project locations.

**Major Responsibilities:** Major responsibilities of the **Community-based Protection Officer** (not exhaustive) are listed below:

- Lead the day-to-day technical support and oversight of Protection and Rule of Law (PRoL) activities implemented through partners, ensuring adherence to IRC technical standards, donor requirements, and international protection principles.
- Support partners in the implementation of legal awareness, legal information dissemination, HLP-related activities, civil documentation support, protection advocacy, and referral services.
- Provide technical guidance to partner staff on protection case management principles, safe identification, referrals, protection mainstreaming, confidentiality, and survivor-centered approaches.
- Support the implementation and quality assurance of Child Protection (CP) and Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE) activities delivered by partners, ensuring compliance with sector standards and quality benchmarks.
- Ensure that integrated protection approaches are applied across all project interventions and that protection risks are systematically identified and addressed.
- Accompany partner teams during field visits and service delivery activities to provide mentoring, coaching, and technical support.

**Community Protection Systems Strengthening & Sustainability**

- Assess partner capacity gaps and develop capacity-strengthening plans in coordination with relevant technical coordinators and managers.
- Deliver training, coaching, mentoring, and on-the-job capacity-building for partner staff on PRoL, CP, WPE, safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, referrals, and case management principles.
- Facilitate regular technical review meetings with partner teams to discuss challenges, lessons learned, and corrective actions.
- Support partners in developing action plans to improve service quality and ensure timely implementation of recommendations.
- Support sustainable capacity strengthening and knowledge transfer initiatives to enhance partners’ long-term ability to deliver quality protection services independently.

**Referral & Coordination Oversight**

1. Oversee referral pathways to ensure effectiveness, continuity, and proper coordination with partners and service providers.
2. Work closely with the partner to ensure gradual handover of responsibilities and knowledge transfer.

**Data Validation, Compliance & Reporting**

1. Verify beneficiary data and ensure its accuracy and reliability.
2. Manage documentation and achieving in line with donor requirements.
3. Prepare impact reports, closure reports, and ensure full compliance with donor regulations and requirements.

**Program Closure & Transition Planning**

1. Support final evaluations and lessons learned exercises.
2. Lead or contribute to closure planning, ensuring safe and structured transition of activities to partners or communities.
3. Ensuring protection mainstreaming is integrated across remaining program activities.
4. **General**

- Perform any other duties as required by program needs or as requested by the supervisor.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Protection Senior Manager.
- **Position directly supervises:** Protection field staff – local partner activities.
- **Indirect Reporting:** IP Coordinator.
- **Other Internal and/or external contacts:**
- ***Internal:*** Protection Officers, Health team, WPE, and CP teams, ERD team. IP senior managers, IP Coordinator.
- ***External:*** INGOs, local actors, and local authorities.

 **Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- A bachelor's degree in social work, international relations, human rights, community development, or any other university degree.

***Work Experience:***

- Proven experience 2-4 yearsin Protection, PRoL, legal assistance, civil documentation, case management, or related humanitarian programming.
- Experience working with NGOs and implementing programs through partner organizations.
- Experience in providing technical support, coaching, and capacity strengthening to staff and partners.
- Experience in field monitoring, quality assurance, reporting, and compliance with donor and organizational standards.
- Knowledge of Child Protection (CP), Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE), referral pathways, and protection principles.
- Strong understanding of the Syrian humanitarian context and commitment to protection, inclusion, and gender equality.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Strong management and organizational skills.
- Excellent time management skills and ability to meet deadlines.
- Strong communication, negotiation and persuasion skills
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team, as well as independently.
- Flexible and able to work in a dynamic and diverse environment.
- Experience in regular report writing.
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team, as well as independently.
- Flexible and able to work in a dynamic and diverse environment.
- Must be computer literate (Microsoft Word and Excel).

***Language Skills:***

- Arabic & English are required
- Travel: If requested

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based and are currently located outside of your home country and possess over two years of international work experience, the Middle East Region has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENA, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

IRC is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful and safe work environment where all persons are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.

jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of 30 September 2027.***

**Job Overview:**

The Program for Initial Resettlement Caseworker Assistant supports refugee and other ORR-eligible populations during their integration into the United States by assisting with service delivery, client support, documentation, transportation, and resource coordination. Working under the guidance of the Cash and Medical and Initial Resettlement Coordinator, the Caseworker Assistant helps ensure clients have access to essential services and resources while promoting self-sufficiency, stability, and successful community integration.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Assist in coordinating pre-arrival and post-arrival services to ensure clients receive essential support upon arrival.
- Support airport pickups, housing setup, food assistance, transportation arrangements, and community orientation activities.
- Assist clients with navigating community resources and accessing essential services.
- Conduct client intake and assessment activities to help identify household strengths, needs, and priorities.
- Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide referrals and follow up on service connections, appointments, and action items.
- Support the distribution of direct assistance and program-related resources according to organizational and funder requirements.
- Maintain regular communication with assigned clients to support progress toward established goals.
- Document client interactions, services provided, referrals, and outcomes accurately and timely.
- Enter and maintain client records in ETO and other required databases.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Associate degree in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years’ experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Experience providing customer service, case management support, or community outreach preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Will require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($18.45). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Deputy Country Director for Programme
Junior Project Assistant
jobs.body:
**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

**Organizational Context and Scope**

Under the direct supervision of the project manager and under the guidance of the Head of Unit for Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion (LMI) and under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission in the Country Office for Belgium and Luxembourg, the incumbent will assist the LMI team with the implementation of projects of the IOM Country Office. In addition to this, the incumbent will be expected to support some activities related to the development of new projects in the LMI Team.

**Responsibilities**

In particular, the incumbent will:

  
I. ASSIST WITH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECTS

1\. In close coordination with the LMI Head of Unit, assist the Project Management Teams with the implementation and follow-up on project activities. This includes supporting the team with research tasks, administrative tasks and the (logistical) organization of meetings and events.   
2\. Assist with the drafting/ formatting of reports; routine correspondence, type letters, reports and memoranda as well as IOM documents and forms related to IOM operational and administrative matters;   
3\. Assist the Project Management Team with the development of new projects and initiatives in the field of Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion. This includes assistance with the drafting/ formatting of concept notes and project proposals.   
4\. Assist in drafting/ formatting public information documents, website articles, press releases and information dissemination on IOM activities towards public and private stakeholders.   
5\. Any other tasks as may be required.

  
II- ASSIST WITH POLICY SUPPORT AND OUTREACH

6\. Assist in identifying possible partnerships with the private sector, civil society (NGOs, diaspora associations, etc.) and other stakeholders (such as the Belgian government and universities) in order to improve knowledge on migration initiatives and policies.   
7\. Assist with the drafting/ formatting of presentations and speeches related to integration for the LMI Head of Unit or the Chief of Mission.   
8\. Prepare for, participate in and follow-up on meetings/conferences on behalf of the organization.   
9\. Any other tasks as may be required.

**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

**•**  Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in economics, social science, migration studies or related field from an accredited academic institution with one year of relevant professional experience.   
OR   
• Completed High School degree with three years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

• Demonstrated first working experience or internship in the area of project management, or evaluation of projects;   
• Demonstrated first working experience or internship in the area of migrant integration or labour migration;   
• Strong organizational and time-management skills;   
• Ability to work independently;   
• Experience in liaison with non-governmental organizations, national, regional and international authorities and institutions is an advantage.

**Skills**

• Strong organizational and time-management skills;   
• Strong communication and diplomatic skills, applied in a professional environment;   
• Ability to work independently against tight deadlines.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Advanced knowledge of Dutch is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators Level 1

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

jobs.title: Director of Finance and Administration (national contract)
jobs.body:
Location: Jerusalem (frequent travels to the West Bank)  
Contract duration: 5 years (possibility of extension)  
Contract: national contract  
Reports to: LWF Representative in Jerusalem, technical supervision by the Head of World Service Finance and Support Functions (Geneva-based)  
Starting date: end of 2026 / beginning of 2027

***The Applicant must hold a Jerusalem ID.***

**Lutheran World Federation (LWF) World Service**  
LWF World Service is the humanitarian and development arm of the Lutheran World Federation. We are a widely recognized, international, faith-based organization working in more than 20 countries globally. We seek to bring people of all backgrounds together in the common quest for justice, peace, and reconciliation in an increasingly complex and fragmented world. A commitment to the human rights of every individual, regardless of their status, guides our work, actions, and operations. We are particularly known for our timely, compassionate, and professional humanitarian work, and for our field presence in hard-to-reach areas. Our work is people-centered and community-based. Above all, we work with the most vulnerable, and to claim and uphold their rights, we engage proactively with local government and community structures. For additional information, please see [LWF World Service.](https://worldservice.lutheranworld.org/)

LWF has been present in Jerusalem since 1950, serving Palestinians through healthcare, education, and humanitarian programs. Today, the Jerusalem program operates the Augusta Victoria Hospital (AVH), a leading referral hospital for Palestinians from the West Bank and Gaza, as well as vocational training centers in Jerusalem and Ramallah. In line with its humanitarian mandate, LWF is also expanding its emergency response and development programming. For additional information, please see [LWF Jerusalem.](https://lutheranworld.org/programs/lwf-jerusalem)

**Purpose**  
The Director of Finance and Administration is a senior level position and provides strategic leadership and oversight of all financial, administrative, procurement, logistics, and property management functions across LWF Jerusalem programs. This includes responsibility for the financial management of Augusta Victoria Hospital, vocational training centers, humanitarian and development projects, and any future program expansions, ensuring compliance, accountability, operational efficiency, and sound stewardship of resources. The position may assume the responsibilities and authority of the Representative during periods of absence, when designated by the LWF Representative, ensuring continuity of leadership, organizational oversight, and external representation as required.

**Required Qualifications**  
University degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Management, or a related field.  
A relevant postgraduate qualification or professional certification (e.g., CPA, CMA, ACCA, CIA) is an advantage.

**Knowledge and Experience**  
Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in finance, administration, operations, human resources, including senior leadership responsibility.  
Significant experience within an INGO, hospital or healthcare institution, humanitarian / development organization, or other complex mission driven organization.  
Leadership experience in finance, HR, procurement, administration, and operational support functions.  
Strong expertise in financial management, budgeting, reporting, risk management, and compliance.  
Knowledge of procurement, contract management, IFRS, and relevant legal and regulatory requirements.  
Proven ability to drive organizational effectiveness, change management, and process improvement.  
Strong people leadership, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills.  
Excellent strategic thinking, decision-making, communication, and problem-solving abilities.  
Experience managing complex operations, multiple priorities, and cross-functional teams in diverse environments.

**Language Skills**  
English and Arabic: fluency required  
Hebrew: working knowledge is a strong advantage

**LWF Core Skills**  
Analytical thinking - resource level\*  
Achieving results - advanced level  
Accountability - resource level  
Initiative - advanced level  
Leadership - resource level  
Working effectively with others - resource level

**LWF Functional Skills**  
Strategic thinking - resource level  
Resource Mobilization - advanced level  
Stakeholder Management - resource level  
Networking - advanced level  
People Management - resource level  
Innovation - advanced level

\*LWF 3 skills levels are: basis - advanced – resource

**Main duties**  
Direct Financial Accountability and Strategic Oversight for all LWF Jerusalem Program operations, including Augusta Victoria Hospital (AVH), the Vocational Training Centre (VTC), and Property Management.

**Financial Leadership and Management**  
Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the financial management of all LWF Jerusalem Program entities.  
Lead the annual budgeting process and ensure alignment of financial plans with organizational priorities and strategic objectives.  
Oversee financial performance, reviewing income, expenditure, and financial trends against approved budgets and targets.  
Review, analyze, and present monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports to senior management, offering recommendations for informed decision-making.  
Ensure effective cash flow management, financial sustainability, and the organization's ability to meet its financial obligations.  
Lead financial forecasting and scenario planning, identifying financial risks and opportunities and advising leadership accordingly.  
Direct and supervise the accounting, treasury, payroll, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and financial reporting functions, ensuring efficient and compliant operations.  
Ensure robust internal controls, financial systems, and accountability mechanisms are in place and function effectively.  
Develop, implement, and periodically review financial policies, procedures, and operational guidelines to ensure compliance with organizational requirements, donor regulations, and international standards.  
Provide leadership and capacity development to finance teams, fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.  
Serve as a strategic adviser to the Representative, Executive Leadership Team, and governing bodies on financial matters, resource allocation, and long-term financial planning.

**Advisory Boards and Management Reporting**  
Provide the LWF senior management team with clear financial information.  
Prepare financial reports for the Advisory Boards and the AVH Finance Committee meetings.  
Help leadership evaluate the financial implications of new programs or projects.

**Grants and Restricted Funding**  
Track grants and restricted funds.  
Ensure expenditures comply with grant agreements and donor restrictions.  
Oversee financial reports required by funders and monitor grant budgets and deadlines.

**Audit, Compliance, Internal Controls, and Risk Management**  
Lead coordination of external and internal financial audits and other assurance reviews.  
Ensure timely implementation and monitoring of audit recommendations.  
Maintain a robust internal control framework safeguarding organizational resources and assets.  
Ensure appropriate segregation of duties, authorization controls, bank reconciliations, procurement controls, and financial monitoring.  
Establish mechanisms for identifying, assessing, monitoring and mitigating financial and operational risks.  
Ensure compliance with applicable LWF policies, donor requirements, accounting standards.  
Ensure proper financial documentation and records are maintained.  
Ensure appropriate compliance with applicable labor laws, taxation, National Insurance, pension, employee benefits and other statutory requirements.  
Promote fraud-prevention, accountability and ethical resource-management practices.  
Ensure appropriate insurance coverage and risk-transfer arrangements for organizational assets and operations.  
Regularly advise senior management regarding material financial, compliance and operational risks.

**Administration, Procurement, Logistics & Property Maintenance**  
Provide strategic oversight of procurement, logistics, administration, property/facilities management and related support services.  
Ensure transparent, competitive and cost-effective procurement systems consistent with LWF and donor requirements.  
Oversee tendering, contracting, vendor management, and procurement planning.  
Oversee administrative systems, office/facility services, maintenance and related operational support.  
Promote environmentally responsible, efficient and sustainable use of organizational facilities and resources.  
Ensure appropriate records management and document retention systems.  
Develop, review and continuously improve administrative, procurement and operational policies and procedures.

**Human Resources and Organizational Development**  
Ensure appropriate oversight of payroll governance, personnel-related financial obligations, and workforce cost planning as part of the organization's overall financial management framework.

**Digital Transformation, Systems and Process Improvement**  
Lead modernization, digitalization and continuous improvement of Finance and Support Function processes.  
Promote integrated management-information systems and reliable data to support timely management decision-making.  
Identify opportunities to automate administrative and financial processes, reduce duplication and improve efficiency.  
Ensure appropriate controls, accountability and data governance are incorporated into digital processes.  
Promote organizational learning and appropriate adoption of emerging technologies.

**Leadership and People Management for the Finance Department**  
Provide leadership to the HR function when delegated by the LWF Representative.  
Establish clear objectives, responsibilities, performance standards and accountability mechanisms for supervised functions.  
Build management and technical capacity within Finance and promote succession planning and knowledge transfer.  
Ensure adequate staffing structures and appropriate segregation of duties within Finance and Support Functions.

jobs.title: Social Safeguard Assistant, Calabar
jobs.body:
About WCS

The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a U.S.-based non-profit, tax-exempt organisation established in 1895, dedicated to saving wildlife and wild places through science-driven solutions and conservation actions that benefit both nature and humanity. With over a century of experience, long-term commitments across diverse landscapes, operations in more than 60 countries, and a track record of supporting the establishment of over 150 protected areas worldwide, WCS has built unparalleled biological expertise, cultural understanding, and partnerships to ensure that vibrant wildlife and ecosystems thrive alongside local communities. By working directly with communities and organisations, WCS applies this knowledge to address species, habitat, and ecosystem management challenges that are critical to improving the quality of life for rural populations whose livelihoods depend on natural resources.

Since 2001, WCS has been at the forefront of conservation efforts in Nigeria, safeguarding critical wildlife habitats and species such as the Cross River gorilla, savannah and forest elephants, and other threatened fauna. Alongside biodiversity protection, WCS supports local livelihoods and improves access to water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services for surrounding communities, addressing development challenges while fostering conservation awareness. In Cross River State, WCS has provided support to strengthen the protection and management of Cross River National Park, Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary, and the Mbe Mountains Community Forest. In Bauchi State, WCS collaborates with the state government to provide technical expertise for the effective conservation and management of Yankari Game Reserve.

Our MISSION is to save wildlife and wild places worldwide through science, conservation action, education and inspiring people to value nature. Our VISION is a world where wildlife thrives in healthy lands and seas valued by societies that embrace and benefit from the diversity and integrity of life on earth. Our GOAL is to conserve the world’s largest wild places in 16 priority regions, home to more than 50% of the world’s biodiversity. Our VALUES are respect, accountability and transparency, innovation, diversity and inclusion, collaboration, and integrity.

WCS is committed to preventing and mitigating harm arising from its conservation and development programmes. Safeguarding helps ensure that activities respect the rights, dignity, safety and well-being of local communities, including people from diverse ethnic and cultural backgrounds and those who may face greater barriers or risks.

Effective field-level support is required to implement safeguarding measures, strengthen inclusive community engagement, operate the Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), monitor emerging risks and maintain reliable documentation across programme activities.

Job Summary

The purpose of this position is to provide practical field and administrative support to the Social Safeguards Manager across WCS programme areas in and around Cross River National Park, Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary and the Mbe Mountains. The Safeguards Assistant will support safeguards implementation, human rights and community engagement, GRM implementation, gender equality and social inclusion, conflict-sensitive engagement, field monitoring, training, data management and reporting.

The role will interact regularly with communities, local authorities, partners and WCS field teams. It will ensure that feedback and safeguarding concerns are accurately recorded, promptly reported and followed up through the appropriate channels. The Safeguards Assistant reports to and works under the direction of the Social Safeguards Manager. The role may collaborate with designated programme staff on specific assignments while remaining accountable to the Social Safeguards Manager.

**Major Responsibilities**

- Support the Social Safeguards Manager in applying WCS safeguards policies, procedures and agreed mitigation measures across programme activities.
- Participate in field visits, screening and monitoring to identify potential risks, concerns and implementation gaps relating to human rights, safety, inclusion and potential harm to communities.
- Record findings, agreed actions, responsible people and timelines; maintain accurate safeguards files; and support follow-up as directed by the Social Safeguards Manager.
- Promptly escalate safeguarding incidents and serious or urgent concerns to the Social Safeguards Manager through established channels.
- Support non-discriminatory community relationships, stakeholder consultations, sensitisation, and other engagement activities using respectful, accessible and culturally and ethnically sensitive approaches.
- Promote meaningful participation by women, young people, persons with disabilities, minority ethnic or cultural groups and others who may face barriers to participation.
- Support the Social Safeguards Manager with the implementation of the GRM in line with approved WCS procedures confidentially.
- Monitor and report emerging concerns, tensions, misunderstandings or conflicts that may affect communities or programme activities.
- Coordinate with safeguards, programme activities and community engagement teams; participate in relevant meetings; and support logistics for consultations, training and field visits.
- Track cases, agreed actions and response timelines, and support follow-up with complainants and relevant teams as directed by the Social Safeguards Manager
- Support the collection and documentation of relevant contextual information without acting beyond the responsibilities of the role
- Assist with the organisation and delivery of safeguards, human rights, GRM, gender equality and social inclusion training or awareness activities for staff, partners, community representatives and other stakeholders.
- Any other assigned task.

**Job Qualifications:**

- Bachelor's degree, Higher National Diploma or equivalent qualification in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Community Development, Sociology, Anthropology, Gender Studies, Human Rights, Environmental or Social Management, Rural Development or another relevant field.
- Relevant professional training in safeguarding, community engagement, gender, conflict management or GRM is an advantage.
- Previous experience through employment, internship, volunteering or community-based work in community engagement, development, conservation, social work or a related field is an advantage.
- Experience supporting community meetings, consultations, awareness activities, training or field data collection is desirable.
- Experience working in rural or remote environments with diverse ethnic or cultural groups, people with disabilities or people who may face barriers to participation is an advantage.
- Previous exposure to a GRM, complaints mechanism or community feedback system is desirable.
- Experience in conservation, natural resource management or development programmes is an advantage.

**Additional Requirements:**

- Good communication, listening, observation and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to engage respectfully with diverse communities and stakeholders and support meetings, consultations and awareness activities.
- Basic understanding of safeguarding, human rights, community engagement, gender equality, social inclusion, conflict sensitivity and GRM principles.
- Ability to identify, document and promptly report community concerns and emerging safeguarding risks.
- Ability to collect basic field data, maintain clear records and reports, and use Microsoft Word and Excel.
- Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately and maintain professional boundaries.
- Good organisational skills, attention to detail and ability to work effectively as part of a team.
- Willingness to learn, consistently follow WCS procedures and demonstrate integrity, professionalism and respect for others.
- Ability and willingness to work in remote and challenging environments and undertake regular field travel; a valid driving licence and practical driving experience is an advantage.

Language

- Fluency in English is required.
- Fluency or strong working knowledge of the relevant local language(s) is an advantage

jobs.title: Proposal Development Manager
jobs.body:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with a contract duration of one year with good prospects of extension.

The position is **home-based**, with the applicable national employment conditions and salary determined by the employee’s country of residence.

As Proposal Development Manager, you coordinate the development of high-quality, competitive funding proposals for selected strategic and financially significant opportunities. You ensure that proposals are responsive to identified needs, aligned with Welthungerhilfe’s strategy and country priorities, and fully compliant with donor requirements and internal quality standards.

As part of Welthungerhilfe’s Flexible Management Support (FMS) team, you provide proposal development expertise to Country Offices based on specific assignments and Terms of Reference. You are able to integrate quickly into existing teams and processes and provide effective support at short notice.

## Your responsibilities

- Coordinate the development and writing of high-quality concept notes and full project proposals in response to specific donor opportunities.
- Support and, where required, organize needs assessments and field-level analyses as a basis for project design, involving local partner organizations, other NGOs and relevant stakeholders.
- Facilitate needs- and impact-oriented project design in line with Welthungerhilfe’s strategy, relevant country strategies and donor priorities.
- Translate technical inputs, assessments and strategic priorities into coherent and compelling project concepts and proposals.
- Ensure that proposals are developed in accordance with relevant donor requirements, strategies and guidelines.
- Assess the feasibility and overall coherence of proposed interventions by critically reviewing assumptions, risks, implementation approaches and relevant contextual factors
- Coordinate the proposal development process and required contributions to ensure complete, high-quality proposals are submitted on time.

## Your profile

- A university degree in a relevant field or an equivalent combination of professional qualifications and relevant work experience.
- Demonstrated experience in coordinating proposal development processes, including managing inputs from technical experts, partners and other relevant stakeholders under tight deadlines.
- Strong experience in developing concept notes and full project proposals for institutional donors, including working with donor-specific requirements and guidelines.
- Sound knowledge of project design and proposal development, including needs assessments, intervention logic, feasibility and risk analysis.
- Technical expertise in at least one of Welthungerhilfe’s relevant thematic areas and the ability to quickly familiarize yourself with new country contexts and programmatic topics.
- Strong analytical, writing and coordination skills, with the ability to turn technical inputs and complex information into clear and compelling proposals.
- You recognize the growing value of data in proposal development and project design and are eager to strengthen your skills in incorporating data-informed approaches into your work.
- Excellent interpersonal and intercultural skills and the ability to work effectively with diverse teams, local partner organizations and other stakeholders across different country contexts.
- Excellent written and spoken English is required; a strong command of French is a great asset.

## What we offer

- Fair Compensation: A fair and equal remuneration based on a transparent salary scale.
- Work-Life Balance: Enjoy flexible working arrangements to support a balanced lifestyle.
- Modern & Agile Work Environment: Be part of a forward thinking organization that fully embraces digitalization and innovation across all areas.
- Personal & Professional Growth: Access diverse learning and development opportunities to advance your career.
- Team: Join our dedicated and diverse teams, where passion, expertise, and joy come together to create a better world.

In addition, Welthungerhilfe offers numerous other benefits, which are listed under [**Our benefits**](https://www.welthungerhilfe.org/benefits-for-employees-in-germany/).

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*
