- the chance to contribute to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices

***\* The post holder is expected to undertake regular travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina, in particular to Una-Sana Canton.***

***\*\* The post remains subject to continued project funding.***

jobs.title: Head, Information and Communication Technology Services (P.5)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
The Head of Information, Communication and Technology Services (ICTS) reports directly to the Chief of Central Support Services within the Administrative Division and provides strategic leadership for all ICTS activities in support of IMO’s programmes and long-term modernization objectives.

The role is responsible for developing and implementing IMO’s digital strategy, strengthening ICT governance, and ensuring that secure, reliable, and scalable technology services support business needs. This includes leading digital transformation, ERP integration, cloud adoption, cybersecurity maturity, and data-driven decision-making.

As the principal advisor to senior management on technology, digital services, data, enterprise architecture, and ICT operations, the Head of ICTS translates business priorities into practical technology solutions and maintains an information and technology architecture roadmap aligned with organizational goals.

The Head of ICTS leads the development, management, and enforcement of ICT policies, standards, frameworks, and guidance across IMO. The role also promotes continuous improvement, collaboration, service excellence, and innovation within the ICT function.

The Head of ICTS oversees information security operations, ensures appropriate controls are in place, and supports audit, investigation, and incident response activities by enabling secure access to required systems and data while maintaining confidentiality.

**Main Duties and Responsibilities**

**Strategic Planning:**

- Leads the formulation and implementation of the vision strategy, and roadmap for transforming ICT solutions, operations, and service delivery to achieve the organization’s goals, fostering digital transformation and prioritizing IMO initiatives.
- Drives the design and execution of a comprehensive digital modernization roadmap, embedding innovation, interoperability, and resilience into ICT operations.
- Leads the development and enforcement of data governance frameworks, including data quality standards, analytics capabilities, and business intelligence tools that support informed decision-making.
- Leads the digital enablement and operational alignment of ERP/SAP systems with IMO’s core processes, ensuring enterprise-wide integration, data coherence, and improved resource planning through modern ICT platforms.
- Acts as champion for emerging technologies that advances organisational agility and effectiveness, providing direction for innovation, awareness, and adoption of new digital tools and IT-enabled work practices that fosters and contributes to a continuous change management environment.
- Translates strategic and complex requirements of stakeholders and clients, into innovative, scalable, value driven ICT plans and solutions.
- Facilitates organization-wide alignment on the ICT and data strategy, related investment decisions, and ICT and security risk management based on strategic and data-driven insight.
- Establishes enterprise standards and metrics to measure, guide and communicate contribution of ICT and data services to optimizing internal operations and implementing secretariat mandates.
- Standardizes and modernizes approaches for the secure, continuous integration and continuous deployment of systems led and managed by the secretariat.

**Leadership:**

- Leads the ICTS section fostering a purpose-driven, client-oriented, and inclusive team culture that values excellence, innovation, and accountability to stakeholders and partners.
- Drives an inclusive, innovative, enabling and collaborative culture, that encourages diversity, job satisfaction, technical development, and individual well-being of the ICT section.
- Guides the organisation’s digital maturity and adoption planning through advocacy for continuous transformative solutions and change management.
- Ensure development, oversight and adherence to service delivery metrics, ensuring that large-scale transformational projects are delivered within established time, cost, and quality parameters.
- Acts as a visible and inspiring leader, promoting agile and client-focused system development and service delivery.
- Actively participates in, leads, or co-leads UN forums and clusters to advance the broader UN mandate and demonstrate effective IMO leadership in information and technology.

**Management:**

- Oversees the planning, resourcing and monitoring of annual work plan of activities for ICTS, ensuring efficient allocations of human and financial resources and technical expertise.
- Oversees the strategic management, integration, and optimization of the Organization’s enterprise platforms, ensuring their alignment with IMO’s operational needs and interagency standards
- Governance and management of ICT budget and oversees its implementation, ensuring balancing of strategic investment, operational need and financial transparency.
- Manages a complex and dynamic ICT environment, including high volumes of structured data exchanges with internal and external entities, as well as unstructured data related to content management.
- Oversees critical aspects of enterprise architecture and the development of a data services architecture.
- Oversees the enterprise-wide deployment, customization, and lifecycle management of ERP/SAP systems, ensuring their full integration with IMO’s core operational processes, financial management, and HR services.
- Provides strategic oversight to ensure optimal configuration, user adoption, and long-term system sustainability.
- Ensure coordination of the design and delivery requirements of ICT services to support onsite and offsite hybrid workshops, meetings, and conferences.
- Supervises the design and implementation of the Information Security Management Programme.
- Oversees the design and continuous strengthening of risk management and information security frameworks, promoting a risk-aware, compliant, and resilient ICT environment
- Ensures that the organization's business processes are supported by user-friendly, streamlined, and appropriately scaled technology solutions.
- Holds accountability for ICT’s IT systems, communication networks, and technologies, ensuring they are cost-effectively harmonized across the organization. In this regard, actively engages with other UN organizations to strive for system-wide coherence.

**Representation and Partnerships**

- Represents the secretariat in information technology at the international level and with its internal and external clients.
- Serves as a strategic and technical resource for Secretariat leadership in ICT-related intergovernmental processes
- Builds and nurtures partnerships with external entities, UN Agencies, and donor and government officials to exchange innovative approaches, best practices and service delivery metrics.
- Supports institutional efforts to build and develop integrated partnerships aligned with organisational goals and resource mobilisation strategies.

**Performs other job-related activities required to support the goals and objectives of the Secretariat.**

**Required Competencies**

1. Strategic leadership in ICT strategy, governance, and service delivery.  
    Expertise in hybrid infrastructure, enterprise systems, and cloud platforms (especially Microsoft Azure and M365).
2. In-depth knowledge of cybersecurity, data protection, and ISO frameworks (e.g., 27001, 27701, 20000, 9001).
3. Strong budget and procurement planning skills, including cost optimization and vendor management.
4. Proven ability to lead digital transformation projects, implement AI and automation tools, and improve service efficiency.
5. Excellent communication and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical audiences.
6. Strong organizational, planning, and risk management skills.
7. Ability to lead high-performing and diverse teams in a multicultural environment.  
    Commitment to continuous learning, innovation, and client satisfaction.

**Professional Experience**

A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in ICT management, including infrastructure, systems administration, cybersecurity, or enterprise application delivery.

At least 5 years of experience in a strategic leadership role managing ICT operations or teams.

Demonstrated experience leading major digital transformation or modernization projects.

Proven experience with hybrid cloud management (Azure), cybersecurity governance, and ISO implementation.

Experience in budget planning, procurement, and ICT governance frameworks.

Experience in UN system or intergovernmental organizations is desirable.

Experience in inter-agency collaboration or participation in UN/IGO digital governance initiatives is desirable.

**Education**

A Master's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related field is essential. A first level or university degree (Bachelor’s or equivalent) in these fields, combined with four additional years of qualifying professional experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced degree.

Relevant technical or management certifications would be an asset.

**Language Skills**

Proficiency in English (oral and written) is essential. Knowledge of another official UN language is an asset.

**Other Skills**

Advanced skills in Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Intune, Power Platform, and enterprise systems.  
Strong understanding of IT service management (ITIL), information security (ISO 27001, 27701), and project management (PRINCE2, PMP).

Experience with procurement systems (e.g SAP) , budgeting tools, and data analytics platforms (e.g., Power BI).

Familiarity with ServiceNow, GitHub, automation tools, and digital workplace solutions.

jobs.title: Technical Officer (P.3)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
Under the supervision of the Head of the Facilitation Section, the incumbent will participate in and contribute to the implementation of the Section's programme of work relating to facilitation, maritime digitalization, data harmonization, port administration and technical cooperation activities. The incumbent will be expected to undertake in the Maritime Safety Division, a broad range of responsibilities and to adapt to evolving organizational priorities, including the delivery of new projects and initiatives in response to emerging operational, technological, regulatory or strategic requirements of the Maritime Safety Division and the Organization.

**Main Duties and Responsibilities**

1. Provide secretariat support to the Facilitation Committee (FAL), the Expert Group on Data Harmonization (EGDH), and other related subsidiary bodies and working groups, as required including the preparation of briefs, notes, documents and reports, and the development and review of manuals, guidance and other publications.
2. Act as Secretary of the Expert Group on Data Harmonization (EGDH) coordinating and supporting its work, including the preparation of meeting documentation, reports, correspondence and follow-up actions.
3. Deal with maritime facilitation, maritime digitalization, port administration and port management issues, including the management, maintenance and development of GISIS modules, databases, information systems and data structures supporting the IMO Compendium on Facilitation and Electronic Business, Maritime Single Window (MSW) implementation and data harmonization activities, and provide technical advice and assistance to Member States, international organizations, port authorities and industry stakeholders, as appropriate.
4. Assist in the preparation for, serving and following-up of, meetings of Committees, Sub-Committees and other relevant bodies through the preparation of documents, briefs and reports; and assist in other meetings, as appropriate.
5. Act as Secretary of working, drafting or expert groups established by the Facilitation Committee, the Maritime Safety Committee or other relevant bodies.
6. Assist in the conduct of multidisciplinary projects, coordinating and supporting their implementation; and in other work of the Maritime Safety Division as may be assigned;
7. Prepare reports, publications, circulars and other documents and correspondence as assigned, including responses to queries on IMO instruments, facilitation matters, maritime digitalization, port administration and port management issues.
8. Support the delivery of technical cooperation and capacity-building activities related to maritime facilitation, maritime digitalization, port management, Maritime Single Window implementation and data harmonization, including the organization of, and participation in, seminars, workshops, training courses and missions, as required.
9. Carry out missions to Member States on specific assignments; represent the Organization at meetings, conferences, seminars and workshops; and prepare and deliver presentations, lectures and technical papers, as required.
10. Undertake such other duties connected to the work of the Maritime Safety Division as may be assigned.
11. Undertake such other duties connected with the work of the Organization as may be assigned.

**Required Competencies**

1. Ability to establish and maintain effective working relations with people in a cross-cultural environment.
2. High capacity for independent planning, organizational skills, ability to work under pressure whilst maintaining high quality work outputs.
3. Professionalism, confidentiality, initiative, integrity, tact and sound judgement.
4. Ability to communicate complex issues clearly both orally and in writing.

**Professional Experience**

A minimum of five years of progressively responsible professional experience in maritime transport, shipping, port management, data management, maritime facilitation or related fields is essential.

**Education**

University degree or equivalent in Maritime Transport, Shipping and Port Management, Logistics International Trade or data management.

**Language Skills**

Proficiency in English (written and oral). Working knowledge of other official language/s of the UN, will be an advantage.

**Other Skills**

Relevant professional experience in the maritime and port sector is essential. Advanced skills in MS Office applications. Thorough knowledge of relevant international conventions and other IMO instruments. Proven ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary and multi-national management team.

jobs.title: Chief, Central Support Services (D.1)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
Under the immediate supervision of the Director, Administrative Division, the incumbent leads and provides direction to the Office of Central Support Services which provides the following services to the Secretariat: information, communication and technology services, facilities management, procurement, asset management, publishing, catering, travel, diplomatic, and registry/mailroom and distribution.

**Main Duties and Responsibilities**

1. Plan, oversee and provide direction to the management of Central Support Services (CSS), including facilities management, procurement, asset management, publishing, catering, travel, diplomatic, UNLP and registry/mailroom and distribution.
2. Oversee and supervise the budget and financial management of expenses within CSS’s remit (Regular Budget, Headquarters Capital Fund, Trading Fund), including the approval of variable works requested by contractor under the total facilities management contract.
3. Develop and maintains up-to-date policies and procedures for CSS services.
4. Provide strategic, policy and budgetary advice to senior management on all CSS matters.
5. Recommend purchases of equipment and services aligned to CSS objectives.
6. Serve as Country Security Focal Point for the United Kingdom within the framework of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS).
7. Serve as the certifying officer for the request for the issuance of UNLP and documents related to diplomatic car and duty free goods privileges.
8. Serve as the focal point for the Organization for the United Nations Organizational Resilience Management System (ORMS).
9. Perform any other duties as may be requested.

Within delegated authority, the Chief, CSS, is responsible for the following:

**Facilities Management Services (FMS)**

- Oversee the organization’s FM activities and financial management of budget and expenses, including the approval of variable works requested by the contractor and reviewed by the Facilities Manager.
- Comply with the Organization’s obligations as a tenant: long-term planning of major works, in collaboration with Landlord (host Government) and appointed Managing Agent; protect the Organization’s interests on building-related matters and payment of rent and rates.
- Preventive and reactive maintenance of plant and equipment in the IMO HQ, ensuring the smooth running of all systems to provide a safe and healthy environment.
- Ensure security for IMO HQ, including liaison with the Parliamentary and Diplomatic Protection group of the Metropolitan Police.
- Provision of office cleaning and porterage services, building and motor vehicle insurance, utilities, waste removal/recycling services.
- Manage the relationship with tenants, including calculation of rent and service charges.
- Compile reports on the Secretariat’s greenhouse gas emissions for UN Environment’s Sustainable UN programme; work towards reducing the Secretariat’s carbon footprint.

Information, Communication and Technology Services (ICTS)

- Oversee the organization’s ICTS activities, including budget planning, financial management and budgetary and expense performance, and budget transfers.
- Review and approve or clear staff related matters: recruitment; overtime; extension of appointment; performance management, including functions, roles and responsibilities, if necessary.
- Review ICT related project proposals submitted by Head, ICTS for the approval by the Director, Administrative Division.
- Provide strategic leadership and organizational oversight of IMO’s ICT function,
- Represent IMO as member of the Management Committee of the International Computing Centre.

Procurement and Asset Management Services (PAMS)

- Oversee and manage the Organization’s procurement activities.
- Plan and manage procurement of all goods and services for the Organization, including for field offices and projects implemented on behalf of World Bank, EU and other donors, ensuring good value for money.
- Negotiate and conclude contracts for goods and services procured by the Organization; contracts management including monitoring and review of performance.
- Prepare recommendations to Committee on Contracts for high-value contracts.
- Provide advice and support to senior management and requisitioning officers on procurement policies and procedures.
- Compile reports on procurement statistics for UN Procurement Network.
- Review and update the Procurement Manual.
- Asset management, including gifts to the Organization.
- Oversee and manage the registry and general service functions for the Secretariat.
- Oversee the processing of Host Government-related entitlements and privileges.
- Ensure effective operation of office services, equipment and stores.
- Ensure effective operation of mail room, registry and pouch services.

Publishing Services (PUBS)

- Oversee and manage publishing services (funded by the Trading Fund) Monitor, review and update policies and strategies related to production (including digital production) and sales.
- Provide advice and support to the Secretariat (including senior management) on publishing policies and practice. Manage the publishing element of the Trading Fund budget, including revenue forecasting and long-range expenditure planning.

Catering Services (CATS)

- Oversee and manage the Organization’s in-house catering activities (funded by a Trading Fund).
- Manage the catering element of the Trading Fund budget, including revenue forecasting and long-range expenditure planning.

Travel and Diplomatic Services (TDS)

- Oversee and manage travel and diplomatic services for the Secretariat.
- Coordinate the provision of all official travel (including mission travel, entitlement travel, recruitment and repatriation travel, consultants’ travel.
- Liaison with and performance monitoring of travel agency.
- Review and update the Travel Manual, travel policies and administrative procedures against industry standards and best practices as adopted by Other UN agencies.
- Compile statistical reports on Secretariat travel.
- Oversee the administration for the issuance of UNLPs.

**Required Competencies**

1. Ability to negotiate and influence effectively to build consensus and achieve objectives.
2. Ability to formulate and implement strategic plans and objectives, and make decisions with a focus on impact on the Organization.
3. Excellent spoken, written and presentation skills, and ability to provide guidance and explain complex issues and positions to a variety of audiences.
4. Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, at all levels including in an international, cross-cultural context.
5. Strong leadership skills and experience in managing a diverse team of staff and budgetary resources.
6. Proven analytical and organizational skills with the ability to focus on outcomes and thorough implementation of activities.

**Professional Experience**

At least 15 years of responsible experience in the management of multi-disciplinary teams, including a minimum of 5 years’ experience at a senior or international level position, with line management capacity is essential. Experience in contract and financial management is essential.

**Education**

Advanced university degree in Business/ Public Administration, Management or other relevant fields is essential.

**Language Skills**

Proficiency in English (oral and written) is essential. Knowledge of another official language of the Organization would be an asset.

**Other Skills**

Demonstrated experience in managing several support service functions is essential. Proficiency in MS Office applications. Working knowledge in an ERP (e.g. SAP) will be an asset

jobs.title: Project Officer – MEAL, Ukraine (Europe and Asia)
source: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
jobs.body:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

The Europe and Asia Entity at DCAF works across Eastern Europe, the South Caucasus, Central Asia and other parts of Europe and Asia, providing policy advice, capacity-building, technical assistance and support to institutional reforms. Its work covers areas such as democratic oversight, accountability, integrity and anti-corruption, human rights, defence and security governance, and institutional resilience, working closely with governments, parliaments, security institutions, civil society and international partners. For our country office in Kyiv, Ukraine, we are looking for a highly-motivated and dynamic individual to be our next **Project Officer – MEAL (Europe and Asia).**

**Location: Kyiv, Ukraine**

**Starting date: As soon as possible**

**Work rate: 100%**

**Duration: 2-year fixed-term contract \***

**The role**

The Project Officer (MEAL) provides country-level capacity for Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL), while supporting activity-level financial tracking, reporting and programme administration for DCAF’s Ukraine programme. The position strengthens evidence-based programme management by ensuring that implementation progress, results and expenditure are consistently tracked against approved objectives, outputs and activities.

The main objective of the position is to support the effective implementation of DCAF’s MEAL framework across the Ukraine programme, with a particular focus on results-based management and programme performance. The position contributes to ensuring that implementation progress, results and, where relevant, financial delivery are effectively monitored and used to inform programme management, reporting and adaptation. It also supports the integration of MEAL considerations across programme activities and may contribute to programme and office administration as required.

Within the team structure, the Project Officer (MEAL) provides an important link between programme performance, financial implementation and administrative follow-up, enabling management to assess whether resources, activities and results remain aligned. The position works closely with the team in Kyiv and Geneva to ensure consistency with DCAF’s corporate MEAL, financial and donor-reporting requirements. The position reports to the Fund Manager in Geneva.

**Key areas of operation**

• Maintain and coordinate the programme MEAL framework, including the results framework, indicators, monitoring tools and reporting arrangements across the Ukraine programme.

• Monitor and analyse programme performance and results, collect relevant data and identify implementation trends, challenges and areas requiring management attention.

• Coordinate beneficiary feedback, lessons learned and other accountability processes, ensuring that findings are documented and reflected in programme adaptation and development.

• Contribute to donor reporting, programme reviews and evaluations by providing accurate performance, results and financial implementation data.

• Support programme and office administration, documentation and coordination, working closely with the Head of Country Office, Resource Manager and programme team to ensure efficient day-to-day implementation.

**Your experience**

• 3 to 5 years of relevant professional experience in MEAL, programme monitoring, administration or a related field, preferably within an international organisation or donor funded programme.

• Professional proficiency in Ukrainian and English, with the ability to communicate effectively with Ukrainian partners, colleagues and international teams.

• Demonstrated experience in monitoring and evaluation, results frameworks, indicator tracking, data collection and analysis, preferably in governance, development or security sector programmes.

• Strong analytical and organisational skills, with the ability to manage data and documentation, identify implementation issues, meet deadlines and translate monitoring findings into practical recommendations.

• Ukrainian citizenship at the time of application is a prerequisite.

**We offer**

• a rewarding, dynamic and meaningful work experience

• the chance to be part of a diverse team of collaborative, respectful, hardworking and values-driven people

• the chance to contribute to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

• the position is offered on the basis of an official employment contract, with all applicable taxes and statutory social security contributions paid by the employer in accordance with Ukrainian legislation.

• the expected net monthly salary (after applicable taxes and employee social security contributions) is EUR 1,600–1,800, depending on qualifications and relevant experience.

*\* The post remains subject to continued project funding.*

jobs.title: Head of Support Services
source: International Network For Aid Relief and Assistance
jobs.body:
**GENERAL INFORMATION**

Job Title : Head of Support Services

Location : Remote

Job Type: Full-time

Contract Duration : The contract is for an initial period of **one (1) year**, with the possibility of extension depending on the availability of funding and the continued need for the role.**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

Vision

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

Mission

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

Purpose

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Head of Support Services provides strategic leadership and oversight of INARA’s global finance and operational support systems across all country operations and legal entities. The role ensures strong financial management, compliance, internal controls, budgeting coherence, donor financial accountability, and organizational financial sustainability.

The post-holder serves as the central finance oversight function between Headquarters and Country Offices, ensuring that financial systems, reporting processes, fund management, and accounting practices operate in alignment with donor requirements, organizational policies, and applicable regulatory frameworks.

The role also supervises finance staff across country operations, supports organizational audits and compliance obligations, oversees financial systems optimization, and strengthens institutional financial management capacity across the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

Key responsibilities include and may not be limited to:

1. **Financial Planning and Budget Oversight**

The Head of Support Services leads organizational budgeting processes and ensures financial planning aligns with operational realities and strategic priorities.

Tasks:

- Review and consolidate annual organizational budgets and donor project budgets from all country operations
- Ensure consistency between programmatic plans, operational priorities, and financial forecasts
- Validate budget assumptions including exchange rates, inflation projections, staffing costs, and operational estimates
- Review cost allocations across grants, shared costs, and general organizational operations
- Support Country Offices and program teams in developing realistic and compliant donor budgets
- Ensure budget structures align with donor regulations and internal financial controls
- Monitor overall organizational financial sustainability and resource allocation

Key Competencies:

- Strong financial planning and budgeting expertise
- Advanced analytical and forecasting skills
- Understanding of donor budgeting requirements
- Strategic financial oversight capacity

1. **Fund Management and Financial Oversight**

The role oversees organizational fund management processes and ensures financial liquidity and accountability across all operations.

Tasks:

- Oversee inter-office fund transfers and HQ financial allocations
- Review and approve fund requests from Country Offices
- Monitor cash flow, liquidity, and financial reserve levels
- Monitor foreign exchange exposure and associated financial risks
- Ensure donor funds are utilized in accordance with approved budgets and restrictions
- Track organizational spending thresholds and authorization compliance
- Support the CEO on high-level financial decision-making and risk management

Key Competencies:

- Strong treasury and cash-flow management skills
- Financial risk management expertise
- Understanding of multi-country fund management
- Strong attention to accountability and financial control

1. **Expenditure Management and Internal Controls**

The Head of Support Services ensures organizational expenditures comply with internal policies, donor regulations, and approval frameworks.

Tasks:

- Review expenditures above approved authorization thresholds and submit to the CEO for final approval where required
- Review complex procurement packages including competitive bidding documentation and vendor justifications
- Ensure expenditures comply with donor restrictions and organizational policies
- Monitor implementation of internal control procedures across all country operations
- Identify and address financial control weaknesses and operational risks
- Ensure procurement and expenditure documentation is audit-ready and properly archived

Key Competencies:

- Strong internal control and compliance knowledge
- Procurement and donor compliance understanding
- Risk identification and mitigation skills
- Attention to detail and accountability

1. **Accounting, Reconciliation, and Financial Systems Oversight**

The role ensures the accuracy, integrity, and efficiency of organizational accounting systems and financial records.

Tasks:

- Oversee organizational accounting and bookkeeping processes across all country operations
- Ensure financial entries, reconciliations, and classifications are accurate and completed on time
- Review month-end and year-end closing processes
- Conduct periodic spot checks of financial records and supporting documentation
- Ensure bank reconciliations and petty cash reconciliations are completed accurately and on schedule
- Supervise organizational use of QuickBooks Online (QBO)
- Coordinate with system consultants on QBO structure optimization and reporting systems
- Maintain oversight of chart of accounts, donor classes, and financial coding structures

Key Competencies:

- Advanced accounting and bookkeeping knowledge
- Strong financial systems management skills
- QBO proficiency and oversight experience
- Strong reconciliation and audit trail management skills

1. **Financial Reporting and Donor Compliance**

The role oversees organizational financial reporting processes and ensures compliance with donor and regulatory requirements.

Tasks:

- Consolidate financial data from all country operations into organizational financial reports
- Review and validate donor financial reports prior to submission to the CEO and donors
- Ensure financial reports meet donor formatting, compliance, and deadline requirements
- Review budget versus actual (BvA) reports and variance explanations
- Provide structured feedback to Country Offices on reporting quality and compliance gaps
- Ensure consistency between programmatic implementation and financial reporting
- Support donor financial reviews and due diligence processes

Key Competencies:

- Strong donor financial reporting expertise
- Financial analysis and variance interpretation skills
- Understanding of humanitarian donor compliance frameworks
- Strong organizational and coordination skills

1. **Audit, Compliance, and Organizational Risk Management**

The Head of Support Services leads financial compliance and audit coordination processes across all INARA operations.

Tasks:

- Maintain and update financial policies, SOPs, and internal control frameworks
- Coordinate external audits including donor audits, IRS filings, and independent organizational audits
- Ensure implementation and follow-up of audit recommendations
- Oversee submission of IRS Form 990 and other compliance-related financial filings
- Support compliance across INARA’s legal entities and jurisdictions
- Identify organizational financial risks and recommend mitigation measures
- Ensure compliance with donor regulations, anti-fraud standards, and applicable legal requirements

Key Competencies:

- Strong audit and compliance management experience
- Knowledge of nonprofit regulatory frameworks
- Risk management and governance expertise
- Strong policy development and implementation skills

1. **Systems Strengthening and Capacity Building**

The role strengthens organizational financial systems and supports finance staff development across all operations.

Tasks:

- Supervise and support Country Finance Leads and finance staff across all country operations
- Conduct finance staff performance evaluations and capacity development planning
- Organize training workshops and refresher sessions on financial procedures and systems
- Identify inefficiencies within financial systems and recommend improvements
- Support automation and financial process optimization initiatives
- Strengthen organizational financial documentation and reporting systems
- Promote standardization of financial practices across all country operations

Key Competencies:

- Leadership and staff management skills
- Capacity building and mentoring experience
- Systems improvement and problem-solving skills
- Strong coordination and communication abilities

**Key working relationships**

- CEO: Primary line manager and final financial approval authority
- Country Directors: Coordination on budgets, expenditures, and operational finance oversight
- Country Finance Leads: Technical supervision and financial management oversight
- Partnerships & Development Department: Coordination on proposal budgets and donor financial reporting
- Program Teams: Budget planning and financial monitoring support
- Auditors and External Consultants: Compliance, audit, and systems coordination
- SMT: Strategic financial planning and organizational decision-making

**THE POST-HOLDER WILL BE EXPECTED TO DEMONSTRATE MEASURABLE PROGRESS AGAINST THE FOLLOWING WITHIN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS:**

The post-holder will be expected to demonstrate measurable progress against the following within the first six MONTHS:

- Reporting validation process fully established and adhered to across all active country operations
- Zero reports submitted to Partnerships & Development without completed quality review
- SMT action tracker operational and actively maintained, with no overdue items going unescalated
- Entity documentation archive created and populated for all INARA legal entities
- Coordination gaps between Country Offices, Finance, and Partnerships & Development visibly reduced
- Positive feedback from Country Directors, Finance, and the CEO on coordination quality and turnaround times

**Requirements & Qualifications**

**Qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or related field
- Professional accounting qualification preferred

**Experience**

- Minimum 7 years of progressive finance and operational management experience
- Experience in humanitarian or nonprofit sector finance management
- Experience managing multi-country financial operations
- Strong knowledge of donor compliance and nonprofit financial systems
- Experience with QuickBooks Online and financial reporting systems

**CONFIDENTIALITY AND SAFEGUARDING**

**Confidentiality**

As the position is involved in sensitive topics, he/she must observe absolute discretion within and outside the organization. Non-respect of this clause or any breach of responsibility may result in a written warning or immediate dismissal.

**Safeguarding**

INARA has zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, or harm to children and vulnerable adults. INARA employees must adhere strictly to safeguarding policies, maintain professional boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

**Location: Amsterdam, Barcelona, Brussels, Geneva, Paris** (the candidates must hold a valid work authorisation in one of these locations)

**Starting date**: 01st of January 2027

**Deadline to apply:** 20th of October 2026

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract.

**I. MSF INTERNATIONAL**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 28 associations and other offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information, and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**II. CONTEXT**

The role of Travel Administrator involves managing the travel arrangements for MSF International staff based in various MSF entities. The role replaces that of the Travel Referent for all staff travel, liaising with the finance and procurement departments, MSF partner sections, decentralized hubs, the Global Procurement Unit, as well as external suppliers such as the AMEX travel agency and accommodation providers.

**III. PURPOSE OF THE JOB**

The Travel Administrator is responsible for booking and coordinating travel arrangements for MSF International staff, ensuring that travel services are delivered accurately, efficiently and in compliance with the Travel Policy. The role provides operational and administrative support to travellers and contributes to the smooth delivery of travel services across MSF International.

**IV. ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**Coordinate travel bookings and related travel services for MSF International staff, ensuring compliance with the Travel Policy and operational requirements.**

- Review travel requests for completeness and compliance.
- Book flights, trains, buses, accommodation and related travel services.
- Ensure travel arrangements meet traveller and organisational needs.

**Provide travel administration and traveller support throughout the travel process.**

- Advise travellers on travel procedures and documentation requirements.
- Support visa and travel preparation processes.
- Respond to travel-related queries and provide accurate travel information.

**Contribute to efficient and sustainable travel management.**

- Identify travel options that balance cost, duration, comfort and environmental impact.
- Apply the most appropriate booking channels according to organisational requirements.
- Promote responsible travel practices among travellers.

**Maintain travel records and support travel monitoring and reporting.**

- Update and maintain travel-related data and records.
- Consolidate information required for travel reporting and monitoring.
- Escalate irregularities or non-compliance with the Travel Policy

**V. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY**

**Autonomy**

Works within established procedures and the Travel Policy, organising travel bookings and managing competing priorities while referring exceptional situations to the Travel Referent

**Complexity**

Operates in an international and multicultural environment, coordinating with multiple stakeholders while balancing operational, administrative, budgetary and data protection requirements.

**VI. SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE**

The incumbent is committed to contributing to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse, including those detailed in MSF’s Typologies of Abuse, and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.

**VII. REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Secondary education and relevant administrative training or equivalent professional experience.

Asset: Training in travel, tourism, business administration or a related field.

**Experience**

- Minimum 2 years' experience in travel administration, travel coordination, travel agency services or a similar role.
- Experience organising international travel arrangements.
- Experience working with multiple stakeholders and service providers.

Asset: Experience in an international and multicultural environment and/or the humanitarian sector.

**Knowledge**

- Knowledge of travel booking processes and travel administration.
- Understanding of international travel requirements, visas and travel documentation.
- Proficiency in travel booking systems, databases and standard IT applications.
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to prioritise workload and manage multiple requests.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills.

**Languages**

- Fluency in English; French is an advantage.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. MSF expects all staff to share this commitment and promote an environment where abuse and misconduct is not tolerated.**

**We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.**

**Note: All offers of employment will be subject to reference checks and to appropriate screening checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her/their understanding of these recruitment procedures.**
