El rol busca fortalecer los flujos de información, la coordinación y la disponibilidad de productos pertinentes para el contexto territorial, manteniendo alineación con los estándares, metodologías y herramientas definidos por 3iS y EVIDEM+.

La prestación de los servicios tendrá un enfoque principalmente local, sin perjuicio de la articulación con actores y espacios nacionales cuando sea necesario para la adecuada ejecución de los productos y servicios requeridos.

En el marco de la hoja de ruta nacional para la integración de la coordinación y la gestión de información en Colombia, considerando la descentralización de los Equipos Locales de Coordinación (ELC), el rol de los gestores de información en estos espacios de coordinación es fundamental para fortalecer la respuesta humanitaria territorial en relación con el Ciclo de Programación Humanitario (HPC). Estos ELC tienen liderazgos definidos que den cobertura a las tres dinámicas humanitarias de Colombia, a saber: conflicto armado, desastres y movilidad humana (migrantes y refugiados) y su nexus con la paz y el desarrollo. Al mismo tiempo, el enfoque de trabajo se hace bajo los principios humanitarios y en respuesta a los TdR de los ELC.

En ese sentido, se mantendrá un balance operativo que permita fomentar la coherencia, articulación y acción conjunta para atender de manera equitativa las responsabilidades vinculadas al Equipo Humanitario de País (EHP) y del Grupo Interagencial sobre Flujos Migratorios Mixtos (GIFMM), y el Sistema de Naciones Unidas (SNU), alineados con las prioridades nacionales y los diferentes planes de respuesta vigentes. Lo anterior, garantizando la continuidad de los productos, procesos y estándares comunes establecidos, evitando la duplicidad entre los mismos y garantizando la interoperabilidad y armonización donde sea posible.

**A. Actividades**

1. **Apoyo en la gestión de Información y coordinación de actores locales**

- Apoyar y brindar asistencia técnica sobre los procesos de gestión de información a líderes y socios de los Equipos Locales de Coordinación (ELC), según las funciones de información vinculadas de los Términos de referencia establecidos para los ELC. Estos incluirían de manera general participando en reuniones, elaborando y actualizando productos de situación /contexto humanitario, emergencias, nexus, respuesta y vacíos en los formatos establecidos, brindando acompañamiento y asistencia técnica a socios y requerimientos del ELC, de acuerdo con lineamientos, metodologías y SOP.
- Mantener actualizado el directorio/bases de datos de socios y actores clave del territorio.
- Articular con puntos focales de las organizaciones y contrapartes locales clave para asegurar el intercambio, cobertura, reporte y calidad de datos.
- Asegurar el cumplimiento metodológico sobre procesos comunes y lineamientos acordados/establecidos en el desarrollo de las funciones establecidas
    
    **2. Comunicación y Flujo de Información**
- Apoyar e informar regularmente a socios sobre contexto y análisis relevantes del territorio.
- Elaborar y compartir síntesis y trazabilidad de acuerdos, compromisos y responsables claros derivados de las reuniones (minutas).
- Apoyar en la elaboración de presentaciones u otros insumos acordados para reuniones ELC.
- Socializar y asegurar informar sobre los lineamientos acordados en el nivel nacional al nivel local para garantizar la implementación y entendimiento común.

**3. Análisis para la Toma de Decisiones**

- Solicitar, recolectar, consolidar, registrar y procesar información territorial como parte del monitoreo de la situación, intervenciones y capacidades locales en las herramientas y servicios comunes establecidos.
- Apoyar con el procesamiento y análisis integral de información cuantitativa y cualitativa del contexto territorial, primaria y/o secundaria, como parte del monitoreo del impacto y necesidades causadas por los tres conductores de crisis (conflicto armado, fenómenos naturales, variabilidad climática y movilidad humana) en los grupos poblacionales, vinculando todos los perfiles poblacionales afectados.
- Apoyar los análisis descriptivos sobre los hallazgos de evaluaciones de necesidades coordinadas realizadas en territorio, junto con los socios participantes de estas.
- Apoyar en el análisis de información integral,

**4. Fortalecimiento de Capacidades**

- Capacitar, informar y actualizar periódicamente a socios y contrapartes locales (instituciones, organizaciones locales y socios) sobre el uso y consulta de información en las herramientas, sistemas, plataformas y productos comunes clave y disponibles (ActivityInfo -5W-, Reliefweb, Monitor, tableros de control/dashboards, matrices, formularios Kobo -encuestas, evaluaciones-), además de procesos metodológicos y el flujo y reporte de información.
- Promover el enfoque de localización en la gestión de información mediante asistencia técnica y fortalecimiento de capacidades a organizaciones locales para la sostenibilidad de procesos.
- Participar en los grupos de trabajo de manejo de información como el GTMI (Grupo Temático de Manejo de Información), y otras sesiones de conocimientos incluso a nivel nacional.
    
    **5. Respuesta en Emergencias**
- Participar en misiones de terreno para la recolección de información y apoyar en las evaluaciones de necesidades coordinadas, multisectoriales, rápidas en contextos de emergencia, cuando sea posible.
- Implementar funciones técnicas definidas en los SOP para la elaboración de los productos de emergencias estandarizados y ad hoc, asegurando la caracterización/desagregación rápida, análisis de impacto, vacíos y respuesta.
- Apoyar con la recolección, sistematización de datos derivados de diferentes evaluaciones y/o estudios sectoriales para caracterizar perfiles, barreras de acceso y riesgos de protección con las herramientas, repositorios y formatos comunes definidos/acordados.
- Monitorear e incentivar el reporte de la respuesta por parte de las organizaciones en las herramientas comunes establecidas, garantizando la visibilidad y oportunidad del proceso.

**6. Elaboración de Productos Clave**

- Apoyar con la redacción y consolidación de informes estandarizados y comunes de emergencias, evaluaciones, Briefing departamentales, fichas, fact sheet, infografías y/o dashboard temáticos, entre otros acordados
- Consolidar productos analíticos sugeridos y útiles para incidencia y toma de decisiones de manera oportuna.
- Otros reportes solicitados desde el nivel nacional, que respondan a procesos del ciclo de programación humanitaria cuando sea necesario: relatorías, visualizaciones, consolidaciones departamentales, mapas, insumos para tableros o fichas comparativas.
- Apoyar con la elaboración de mapas, dashboards e infografías sugeridas, acordadas y de utilidad para el ELC.
- Garantizar la revisión, aportes, aprobación por los líderes y socios de los ELC, y posteriormente las publicaciones.

**7. Reporte y uso de sistemas/plataformas/herramientas**

- Alimentar y actualizar oportunamente los sistemas, plataformas y herramientas comunes para el monitoreo de situación y respuesta a emergencias como MONITOR, matriz de emergencia y capacidades de respuesta, 3W, ActivityInfo (5W), u otra herramienta que se defina, asegurando la desagregación de información en todos los campos, según los lineamientos, y evitando duplicidad de herramientas
- Asegurar carga de datos e informes los diferentes ejercicios de recolección en los repositorios habilitados.
- Asegurar la carga de documentos en Reliefweb, actualizaciones y personalización de la sección de los ELC en esta plataforma.

**8. Localización**

- Diseñar e implementar, en coordinación con el/la PM y otros actores relevantes, el plan de trabajo estratégico que permita el seguimiento a las actividades del proyecto, la articulación con socios y la entrega de productos de calidad en relación con las actividades de localización en el marco del consorcio EVIDEM+.
- Coordinar con equipos técnicos y socios implementadores la ejecución oportuna de las acciones previstas en el plan, asegurando alineación con las prioridades del proyecto y del consorcio EVIDEM+.
- Participar activamente en espacios de coordinación interinstitucional en especial a nivel local, representando la estrategia del proyecto y promoviendo su integración en mecanismos humanitarios existentes.
- Coordinar y/o asistir a reuniones estratégicas con socios humanitarios, clústers, sectores, ELCs, GIFMM locales y otros actores clave, velando por la coherencia técnica y metodológica del enfoque del proyecto.
- Participar en los espacios transversales de gestión del conocimiento y en las reuniones de equipo de 3iS y del consorcio EVIDEM.
- Asistir a encuentros presenciales y realizar misiones de terreno cuando sea requerido, para fortalecer la coordinación local y la implementación de actividades.
- Diseñar en conjunto con el/la coordinador/a de la estrategia de localización un esquema de selección de organizaciones beneficiarias de las capacitaciones y mentorías impartidas por 3iS en el marco de la estrategia de localización
- Realizar acompañamiento a las organizaciones nacionales y locales en la implementación de herramientas y estrategias de manejo de información en el marco de la estrategia de localización.
- Facilitar mecanismos de retroalimentación comunitaria para validar la pertinencia de las acciones y recoger insumos cualitativos para la mejora continua.
- Supervisar el cumplimiento de los compromisos establecidos con las organizaciones locales y comunitarias y apoyar al equipo en la resolución de situaciones críticas o sensibles.
- Elaborar insumos cualitativos y descripciones contextualizadas de los avances, retos y aprendizajes en el relacionamiento con las organizaciones locales y comunitarias.

**. Actividades transversales:**

- Elaborar el plan de trabajo y comunicar oportunamente sus avances, dificultades y retos al referente de este contrato.
- Atender los espacios presenciales del proyecto.
- Realizar misiones a terreno cuando se requiera su participación en el proyecto.
- Preparar reportes mensuales de avances.
- Garantizar la entrega puntual de los productos.
- Participar en los grupos transversales oportunamente.
- Contribuir con la estrategia de gestión de conocimiento de la organización y al fortalecimiento del conocimiento interno sobre uso de estadísticas e IA en gestión de datos.

## **CALIFICACIONES MÍNIMAS:**

**Educación**

Profesional con título universitario en estadística, matemáticas, ciencia de datos, economía o áreas afines. Estudios de postgrado o formación complementaria en ciencia de datos o a fines (Deseable)

**Experiencia**

Para ser elegible, la persona postulante deberá contar con al menos tres (3) años de experiencia comprobada en actividades similares a las descritas en los presentes Términos de Referencia, particularmente en gestión de información, análisis de datos, coordinación y asuntos humanitarios, en contextos de emergencias o respuesta humanitaria.

Se valorará experiencia en: Obtención, procesamiento y análisis de información primaria y secundaria; desarrollo de procesos analíticos y redacción de reportes técnicos e informativos ; Elaboración de productos de gestión de información, tales como actualizaciones rápidas, informes de situación, notas informativas, alertas humanitarias y análisis de riesgos; Operaciones humanitarias y coordinación humanitaria en terreno (deseable);Preparación de insumos analíticos o reportes para donantes y para visitas de alto nivel a operaciones humanitarias (deseable).

**Habilidades Técnicas**

- Experiencia en el manejo de sistemas de información y bases de datos, preferiblemente aplicados a contextos humanitarios.
- Competencias sólidas para el análisis e interpretación de información cuantitativa y cualitativa, con conocimiento de herramientas estadísticas como SPSS, SAS, STATA, R u otros paquetes relevantes.
- Conocimientos intermedios en Python, JavaScript o SQL, y conocimientos básicos de programación.
- Conocimiento y experiencia en el uso de herramientas y plataformas de visualización de datos, tales como Power BI, Tableau, Data Studio u otras herramientas similares.
- Conocimiento en el desarrollo y entrenamiento de agentes de inteligencia artificial, así como en la aplicación de tecnologías innovadoras para el análisis y gestión de información.
- Manejo avanzado de Microsoft Office, con especial énfasis en Microsoft Excel.
- Se valorará experiencia en el uso de plataformas y bases de datos humanitarias.
- Capacidad para trabajar bajo un enfoque orientado a resultados, mediante el cumplimiento de objetivos, estándares de calidad e indicadores de gestión.

**Idiomas**

Se requiere un dominio fluido del español (hablado y escrito), conocimientos intermedios del idioma inglés (deseable).

**Responsabilidad ante los beneficiarios**

Se espera que el personal respete los principios de rendición de cuentas a los beneficiarios de los programas de 3IS en línea con las normas internacionales, al tiempo que involucra activamente a las comunidades beneficiarias como socios iguales en el diseño, seguimiento y evaluación de los proyectos de 3IS.

## **PRINCIPIOS GUÍAS:**

Se espera que el personal respete la cultura local y las políticas, procedimientos y valores de 3IS en todo momento.

3IS tiene tolerancia cero con el acoso, la explotación y el abuso sexual, el rastreo humano, el abuso y la explotación infantil. Cualquier violación de estos principios y políticas será tratada como falta grave.

3IS es un empleador que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades independientemente de los antecedentes. 3IS puede llevar a cabo comprobaciones de referencias con otras organizaciones sobre asuntos relacionados con el acoso sexual, la explotación y el abuso.

***Fecha Límite 14 de octubre 2026: Declaración: La Evaluación de candidatos se realizará de forma continua y el puesto podría cubrirse antes de la fecha límite de solicitud.***

jobs.title: MMC Consultancy on Sudan Displacement Data Analysis and Report Writing
jobs.body:
## Who is the Danish Refugee Council?

Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international NGO and one of the few with a specific expertise in forced displacement. Active in 40 countries with 9,000 employees and supported by 7,500 volunteers, DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement affected people and communities. DRC works during displacement at all stages: In the acute crisis, in displacement, when settling and integrating in a new place, or upon return. DRC provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included into hosting societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence.

MMC is a knowledge centre engaged in data collection, research, analysis, and policy and programming on mixed migration. MMC has regional hubs hosted in Africa, Asia, Europe and Latin America, with a global team headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and based in several countries worldwide. MMC is a leading source for independent and high-quality data, research, analysis and expertise on mixed migration. MMC aims to increase understanding of mixed migration, to positively impact global and regional migration policies, to inform evidence-based protection responses for people on the move and to stimulate forward thinking in public and policy debates on mixed migration. MMC’s overarching focus is on human rights and protection for all people on the move. The MMC is part of and governed by the Danish Refugee Council. For more information on MMC visit our website ([http://www.mixedmigration.org/](http://www.mixedmigration.org/)).

## Purpose of the consultancy

MMC Eastern and Southern Africa, Egypt and Yemen, based in Nairobi, occupies a central place in producing regional research on mixed migration dynamics. In 2026, MMC has a project with UNHCR on the regional and routes-based displacement consequences of the war in Sudan. Three years into the war, displacement dynamics have become increasingly complex, regionalised, and multi-directional. Movements are no longer limited to neighbouring countries but extend across North Africa, the Sahel, the Mediterranean, and beyond, often through non-linear and stepwise pathways.

Existing analysis has highlighted several critical features:

- The vast majority of Sudanese remain close to Sudan, but a growing number engage in onward movement across routes.
- Movement decisions are shaped by shrinking protection space, limited access to services, and deteriorating conditions in countries of asylum, rather than predefined destination intentions.
- There is a need to better understand drivers of movement, protection risks, and decision-making processes over time, rather than focusing only on arrivals or flows.

Both UNHCR and MMC hold complementary datasets:

- UNHCR: protection monitoring (quantitative and qualitative), registration/profiling data, operational insights
- MMC: 4Mi primary data, qualitative interviews, route-level perspectives

This project proposes to move beyond parallel analysis toward a joint evidence-building exercise, combining UNHCR and MMC data to produce protection-sensitive, route-based insights. The joint analysis will lead to comprehensive report on the Regional and Routes-Based Displacement Dynamics linked to the War in Sudan. Key sections will include: 1) analysing the scale of displacement and mapping the various routes, 2) exploring onward movement intentions and decision-making, 3) mapping exposure and identifying the determinants of vulnerability to abuse and harm, 4) mapping assistance gaps and provision, and 5) analysing the scale of returns and return intentions.

Objective of the consultancy

MMC is looking for a consultant to take the lead in:

- Conducting quantitative and limited qualitative analysis, involving the bridging of datasets and methodologies to produce coherent, routes-based and protection-sensitive analysis
- Drafting a joint UNHCR–MMC report on Sudanese (and third-country national) movements across key routes following the outbreak of the war in Sudan
- Informing advocacy, programming, and donor engagement with an evidence-based narrative and presentation of the approach and key findings
- Developing a model of structured data collaboration that can be replicated for other contexts.

## Deliverables

The Consultant will contribute to the following task:

**Phase**

**Expected deliverables**

**Indicative description tasks**

**Maximum expected timeframe**

**Inception**

**1. Data analysis strategy and inception report**

Assess available MMC and UNHCR datasets and draft a plan / inception report for analysing the data, planning data visualisations, and structuring the report. Inception report should include draft sections for the introduction, background and methodology that will feature in the final report.

**5 days**

**Analysis**

**2. Findings presentation**

Full analysis of MMC and UNHCR data, in relation to all research questions; identification of initial findings and presentation to MMC and UNHCR for feedback.

**8 days**

**Writing**

**3. Full draft of report**

Produce full draft of report, following inception report and based on findings developed during the analysis phase. Share with MMC region and global teams and UNHCR for feedback.

**10 days**

**Finalisation**

**4. Final draft of report**

**5. PPT presentation**

**6. Short data analysis brief**

Produce a finalised version of the report, incorporating MMC and UNHCR feedback. Depending on the polished nature of the first draft, this may require more than one feedback round. The final report should be fully copy edited by the consultant and confirm to MMC’s editorial guidelines.

Prepare a powerpoint presentation on the paper’s analytical approach and key findings. The PPT should be framed to inform advocacy, programming, and donor engagement.

Prepare an internal two-page analysis brief on coordinating analysis of MMC-UNHCR data.

**7 days**

The Consultant will provide the completed tasks***by email and in word and powerpoint formats as indicated above.***

## Duration, timeline, and payment

The consultant will work 30 days between November 1st and December 27th, 2026.

DRC will make the first payment of 20% of the total costs upon signing of the contract, and the remaining amount upon satisfactory completion of the work.

## Proposed Composition of Team

- Senior displacement researcher, well versed in qualitative and quantitative data analysis
- Mapping and data visualization assistant, if not a part of the senior researcher’s skillset.
- Copy editor, if needed

## Eligibility, qualification, and experience required

### Essential:

- An advanced degree and post-graduate degree in the Social Sciences, International Development, Migration, Forced Displacement or Refugee Studies, or any other related area of study.
- At least five (5) years of experience in the above or any other related area of study within East Africa.
- Demonstrable experience on matters relating to regional displacement dynamics and migration routes.
- A strong and proven publication track record on migration or forced displacement issues
- Excellent research, analytical and reporting skills.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Prior experience with MMC is a plus.

jobs.title: Director of Program Development, Quality & Learning (PQL) - Port au Prince, Haiti
jobs.body:
**Location:** Port-au-Prince, Haiti

**Position Status:** Full-time, Regular

**Language:** Required language fluency in French

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) X **Level 3** ☐**Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

## **About Mercy Corps**

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within.

Now, and for the future.

## **Program/Department Summary**

Mercy Corps helps communities develop their own ideas to solve Haiti’s most daunting problems by using innovative approaches to bring Haitians new social and economic opportunities and to make their country more secure, productive and just. Established in January 2010, Mercy Corps Haiti has offices in Port-au-Prince, Jeremie, and Miragoane and more than 80 staff implementing programs in WASH, financial inclusion, economic development, agriculture, natural resource management and humanitarian response. Mercy Corps’ economic development work is guided by the principles of pro-poor development and demand driven strategies. Mercy Corps takes a progressive approach to development that leads communities and entrepreneurs from relief to sustainable livelihoods to resilience.

Mercy Corps Haiti is going through a transformational change at this moment. As a catalytic organization, our future impact will increasingly focus on **sustainability and transformative change,** supporting lasting improvements in the lives of the communities we serve. This ambition will be supported through several key drivers, including: evidence-based programming, learning generation to influence systems change, scaling impact through Mercy Corps and strategic partners, stronger knowledge management and impact measurement, expanded partnerships and alliances, greater commitment to gender equity and diversity and strategic advocacy and fundraising.

## **General Position Summary**

As a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT) in Haiti, the Director of Program Development, Quality and Learning (PQL) is responsible for driving cross-functional engagement in the development and delivery of Country Program Strategy, developing annual plans and reporting on results. S/he is responsible for ensuring development and delivery of high quality, evidence-based, innovative programs that contribute to Mercy Corps Global Strategy and Mercy Corps Haiti new strategic vision. The Director of PQL ensures that a robust monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) system is in place, that the country office engages in the collection and use of evidence and that this is shared across the global organization, and that reliable data is used for decision-making. One key aspect of the role is ensuring capability building, mentoring and coaching of the Program/Project Managers in order to support program quality in line with global standards and key performance indicators. As a senior leader in the country office s/he plays a representational role with the government, donors, partners, peer agencies, and others. The Director of PQL supports strategic positioning with donors and partners and leads on project design to ensure that the country office strategy can be delivered in line with Mercy Corps vision.

As one of the most senior staff in the Country Office, the Director of Program Development, Quality and Learning must demonstrate the qualities of agile leadership. This role plays a key role in defining and pursuing the strategic direction for Mercy Corps programs in Haiti, ensuring the relevance, coherence, safety and impact of our programs. It is essential that the Director of Program Development, Quality and Learning builds and maintains strong relationships across functions within the Country Program.

## **Essential Job Responsibilities**

**STRATEGY & VISION, PLANNING & REPORTING**

- Lead the development/updating of the analysis of the country context ensuring community, partners and other stakeholders’ participation as necessary.
- Lead the SLT to develop/update and drive forward the Country Program Strategy that is in line with the global strategy.
- Provide leadership on development of the Country Annual Implementation Plan, monitoring of progress against the plan, and completion of accurate, on-time Country Annual Report of outcomes and impact, aligned with the Global Results Framework.
- Facilitate the development and pursuit of thematic and cross-cutting strategic priorities in line with the Country Program Strategy, including gender equality, to guide current and future Mercy Corps programming and Humanitarian Principles.
- Support ownership and commitment to the Country Program Strategy by all staff and departments through clear communication, regular feedback on progress and engagement of all functions in updates.
- Participate in global discussions and working groups to represent country programs, in learning for a, in strategy design and policy development.
- Support change processes and roll out new ways of working to improve achievement of the Country Program Strategy.
- Drive Innovation and thought leadership at all levels in the CO (strategy, programme, project and individual levels).

**PROGRAM DESIGN & DEVELOPMENT**

- Lead strategic resource (financial, materials & human) mobilization drive and ensure the Country Program is always resourced to drive programme design and development.
- Work with CD and SMT to set funding targets and drive implementation at all levels ensuring the entire Country Program is committed to and aware of these contributions to these targets.
- In consultation with the Country Director and Members, ensure technical engagement with donors to pre-position and prepare for opportunities, and engage in strategic positioning work directly as appropriate.
- Lead the identification of new initiatives and opportunities that respond to identified needs and the country strategy, in coordination with the Country Director and Program Managers, as well as the Regional Program Director, headquarters-based Senior Program Officer, Technical Advisors and other relevant staff.
- Play a leading role in designing innovative projects/proposals, including:
    - Engaging with technical experts as needed to ensure high quality, evidence-based designs that draw on needs assessments, learning from past programs and program standards principles.
    - Ensuring partners are identified and appropriately engaged in program design, linking with Operations as need be for assessments, especially to strengthen gender sensitivity at design stage.
    - Ensuring proposal designs and their budgets include robust MEAL plans that are aligned with the Global Results Framework and build in critical learning questions.
    - Ensuring the project budget will enable the project to be delivered as designed.
    - Incorporating community participation into design, as relevant.

**PROGRAM QUALITY AND PROGRAM TECHNICAL EXCELLENCE**

- Ensure the Country Program delivers high quality, multi-sectoral programming in both development and humanitarian contexts (as appropriate).
- Monitor and advance technical and operational quality of programmes, including conducting regular field visits to provide feedback on quality benchmarks, soliciting inputs for design of new programs and collecting ideas for innovation.
- Monitor program Key Performance Indicators and, in partnership with other functions, take steps to improve the quality programming platform to meet agreed upon standards.
- Work closely with the Director of Operations to ensure procedures are followed throughout the project cycle and across the portfolio.
- Ensure Program/Project Managers proactively and regularly communicate planned requirements for program design, learning and implementation to relevant Country Program departments/functions.
- Oversee program startup and ongoing program management and administration of teams across various field locations.
- Ensure that program implementation is responsive to communities and partners and consistent with Mercy Corps’ relevant program guidelines, principles, values, quality standards and strategic plan.
- Ensure that beneficiaries are effectively targeted according to established and well-defined criteria and processes.
- Develop partners’ MoUs and contracts and ensure that partners are delivering in accordance with the agreements.
- Support the PMs and team in the development and ongoing refinement of implementation strategies.
- Integrate community approaches, gender sensitivity and capacity building into all activities as appropriate.
- Ensure program implementation is on time, target and budget, using effective M&E systems to reach desired impacts (adaptive management).
- Create and maintain systems ensuring effective and transparent use of financial resources for timely and informative reporting in line with donor and Mercy Corps policies and procedures.
- Conduct frequent field visits to all project sites for monitoring, quality control and program staff mentoring and coaching.
- Ensure that community feedback mechanisms are in place, functioning, and clearly communicated to staff and beneficiaries.
- Review all draft reports and ensure that reports are ready for submission to HQ on time.
- Lead and coach the Program/Project Managers to enable them to successfully deliver against the Country Program Strategy.
- Ensure effective working relationships with Mercy Corps global, Member and regional technical advisors, procuring technical support as needed to support program and advocacy efforts, including during Emergencies.
- Ensure that program technical experts engage in larger communities of practice within and external to Mercy Corps, to link with the most relevant and evidence-based approaches and conduct timely and useful review of project reports to support quality reporting for Members and donors.
- Ensure that the different technical sectors of the Country Program are coordinated, integrated and support each other to optimize programs and projects.

**DRIVING EVIDENCE, MEAL AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT**

- Work to develop a monitoring system that provides timely and accurate project results by embedding MEAL across program implementation. This requires ensuring effective collaboration across MEAL staff, Technical Specialists, Technical Advisors and program implementation teams to develop logframes, indicators, implementation plans, quality benchmarks, monitoring and evaluation frameworks and related tools.
- Lead programme quality improvements by monitoring and improving Programme KPI performance, including resourcing and conducting high-quality evaluations to demonstrate outcomes and impact and ensuring that accountability mechanisms are in place for all projects so that identified actions are resolved, with critical issues escalated to senior management.
- Ensure the research, evaluation and policy work of the Country Program contributes to generation of evidence for development and improvement of program quality, sound decision making and policy influencing internally and externally.
- Establish effective program learning and knowledge management systems to support adaptive programming and innovation that improves outcomes for children through service delivery, policy & advocacy and campaigns.

**STAFF MANAGEMENT, MENTORSHIP, AND DEVELOPMENT**

- Ensure appropriate staffing of Program Development and Quality team, and engagement of additional technical support when needed to deliver quality project design and delivery.
- Ensure that staff proactively build and maintain technical, managerial and leadership skills, , providing coaching opportunities when needed.
- Create and sustain a work environment of mutual respect where team members strive to achieve excellence.
- Promote accountability, communicate expectations and provide constructive feedback via regular performance reviews.
- Supervise, hire and orient new team members as necessary.
- Provide team members with information, tools and other resources to improve performance and reach objectives.
- Contribute to country team-building efforts, help team members identify problem-solving options and ensure the integration of all team members into relevant decision-making processes.
- Be comfortable and able to manage a team remotely and with limited travel based on the security situation.

**FINANCE & COMPLIANCE MANAGEMENT**

- Ensure compliance with donor and Mercy Corps regulations related to programming.
- Review BVAs with Finance and Program managers to identify any issues and undertake any necessary budget revisions.
- Ensure program close-out begins in a timely manner to minimize any significant under or overspends at the end of the grant (i.e. final variance for all grants should be within 5%).

**INFLUENCE, ADVOCACY & REPRESENTATION:**

- Guide functions and thematic tracks to identify advocacy issues and lead them at the national level.
- Ensure Mercy Corps is represented in the relevant networks.
- Develop and / or participate in various networks for opportunities to extend the program and defend interests.
- Ensure Program issues are subject to pressure and advocacy at national and other levels.
- Ensure programming models are demonstrated/documented and scaled up in line with strategic directions.
- Undertake an in-depth analysis of the powers and policies of the country's structures, systems and networks to identify opportunities for changes in law, policy, budget and behavior at the national level that will achieve the goals and objectives strategies set by the national office.
- Lead and manage the design and implementation of the influence strategy in coordination with staff and partners, taking an integrated approach to influence.
- Revise and update the advocacy strategy according to the evolution of the context.
- Ensure strong links with programs and monitoring, evaluation, research and learning (MERL) so that advocacy and policy approaches are evidence-based.
- Monitor and report on progress in influencing and its contribution to change, including to donors where appropriate.

## **Supervisory Responsibility**

Project Directors, Program Managers, CARM Manager, MEL Manager, Safeguarding Manager, Program Development & Knowledge Manager and other staff as needed.

## **Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Country Director  
**Works Directly With:** All program staff, both national and expatriate in Haiti; HQ-based program, operations, recruiting, human resources, finance, and technical support teams.

## **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

## **Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- BA/S or equivalent in international studies, social science, management, economics or other relevant fields. MA/S preferred.
- 7+ years of experience with European and US institutional and private donors, including proposal development.
- 5+ years overseas experience, including at least 3 years in a senior management position.
- Experience managing humanitarian relief and/or transitional programs in areas affected by insecurity and natural disasters.
- Previous experience working in Haiti or similar contexts strongly preferred.
- Proven track record in program design, proposal writing and development, and donor reporting.
- Be trained and knowledgeable in design, monitoring, and evaluation concepts and methodologies. M&E experience should include conducting assessments and surveys, program design using a logical framework approach, selecting indicators, implementing monitoring plans, coordinating evaluations and data analysis.
- Experience supervising international and national staff, starting up programs and working in difficult environments.
- Experience managing programs in relevant technical areas including Participatory Community Development, Livelihoods, Agriculture, Water and Sanitation, Economic Recovery, Women’s Empowerment and GBV programming, Peacebuilding, Civil Society Capacity Building and Youth.
- Knowledge of major donor requirements and compliance issues.
- Strong management skills with good understanding of relevant cross-cultural issues.
- Understanding of advocacy, policy, and government systems in the host country.
- Strong skills and proven experience in leading strategic planning, change management and program management processes, also from the knowledge and learning perspective.
- Strong skills and proven experience in new program development, project design and proposal writing with corporate, foundations and/or institutional donors.
- Skills in training, capability building, coaching, mentorship, problem solving, and project cycle management.
- High level of self-awareness and willingness to take feedback for growth and self-development.
- Proven experience as a team player and leader in an international organization.
- Demonstrated attention to detail, ability to follow procedures, meet deadlines and work independently and cooperatively with team members.
- History of working effectively with host country government, national and international NGO partners, and collaborating with other actors, including the private sector.
- Solid knowledge of and experience with security protocols is essential.
- **Fluency in written and oral French and English is required.**

## **Success Factors**

A successful candidate will be conscientious, with excellent judgment and will display an entrepreneurial spirit that is both creative and flexible. S/he will combine strong communication skills, creativity, initiative, participatory leadership and tactful decisiveness to assist in the development and implementation of Mercy Corps’ country strategy. Prioritizing, problem solving and simultaneous attention to detail and strategic vision are essential. The individual will be a strategic thinker able to bring ideas to implementation in growing program operations. They will have exceptional proposal development skills and an outstanding ability to design, implement and manage innovative programs that respond to current needs. An interest and ability to travel and work in remote environments, and awareness of and sensitivity to multi-cultural international development work and ability to train and facilitate dialogue among a diverse group of individuals with various skill sets and working styles is required. An even temperament and a good sense of humor are appreciated. Language proficiency in English/French is a must.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

Haiti is a country of 11 million people and is the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere. The country has been wracked by a series of major natural disasters since 2010 including earthquake, hurricanes, and drought. A new government is in place for the next five years which is anticipated to reduce instability, however occasional violent demonstrations and flare-ups in crime can occur. Haiti suffers from chronic high unemployment, severe environmental degradation, food insecurity, and health issues like cholera exacerbated by low levels of access to water and poor infrastructure. Nonetheless, Haiti also has great beauty including beaches and mountainous national parks. Its international airport provides daily flights to multiple destinations in the US, as well as access to DR, Canada, Paris, Cuba, Panama, Curacao, and other locations in the Caribbean.

The position is based in Port au Prince, which is estimated at around 2.5 million people. Although infrastructure is also poor in the capital, comfortable housing with water and electricity are readily available. There are many places to eat in all price ranges, as well as shops, and supermarkets which are comparable to a US supermarket. Self-drive is permitted, however driving can be challenging, and traffic is often very heavy. Housing is provided for this position.

Mercy Corps Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and Mercy Corps' policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

## **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

## **Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

jobs.title: Executive Support Specialist to the Country Director
source: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
jobs.body:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organizations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopens its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 14 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors. From 2026, the portfolio is planned to be expanded by several new projects.

**Your tasks**

- Supporting the planning and implementation of events and meetings including agendas, venues, logistics, participant coordination, materials and on‑site support.
- Coordinating and Managing the Country Directors, including itinery, bookings and travel applications and settlements in line with GIZ procedures
- Managing visa processes for the Country Director and visiting staff and consultants, ensuring timely applications, compliance with host‑country regulations and required documentation.
- Serving as the executive office point of contact, triaging incoming correspondence, preparing briefings, drafting communications and ensuring timely information flow to stakeholders.
- Maintaining accurate records and files (travel, events, visas, contracts, contacts) and prepare required reports for management.
- Contribute to continuous improvement of executive office workflows and tools, i.e. maintenance of mailing lists, documenting SOPs and integrating lessons learned from travel, events and visa cases

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- Education: Completed bachelor’s degree in business administration, office management, public administration or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
- Experience: three years of progressively responsible administrative experience, including coordination of calendars, travel arrangements and event logistics.
- Coordination and planning: Proven ability to manage multiple parallel tasks and deadlines, prioritize effecttively and deliver under time pressure with high attention to detail.
- Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills in English; ability to draft professional correspondence, briefs and meeting materials. German language skills are an advantage.
- Stakeholder management: Experience liaising with internal and external stakeholders (e.g. authorities, service providers, partners) in a professional and service‑oriented manner; high intercultural sensitivity and discretion.
- Digital skills: Confident use of MS Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and virtual collaboration tools; ability to work with internal filing/workflow systems and follow standard operating procedures.
- Compliance and process discipline: Demonstrated adherence to organizational policies, documentation standards and data protection; reliability and integrity in handling sensitive information.
- Personal competencies: Proactive, structured and solutions‑oriented working style; strong team player with a high sense of responsibility and confidentiality

Information Security Lead
jobs.body:
**Location:** Any MSF office within +/-3 hours CET

**Contract:** Fixed term at 100% position - The term of this assignment is intended to be for a period of two (2) years, nevertheless, the duration of the contract may be subject to the employment regulations and labor laws of the country where the selected candidate is based.

**Starting date:** 15th of November 2026

**Deadline to apply:** 18th of October 2026

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract.

**I. MSF INTERNATIONAL**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of origins, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects/programmes and initiatives as requested.

**II. POSITION BACKGROUND**

The Information Systems Management (ISM), one of the international platforms of MSF gathering all the Heads of IT/IS from key MSF entities, has been mandated by MSF’s executive governance body, the Full Excom, to lead the development of an international information systems management strategy seeking to optimise interoperability across MSF in priority areas. The ISM Platform is responsible for setting standards for IT/IS architecture and technology development and aims to promote targeted innovation in information technology/information systems (IT/IS).

Critical to this role, and in response to an increasingly complex cyber and global regulatory landscape, the ISM Platform spearheaded the development of a global information security policy framework back in 2020, which has continued to evolve.

In its strategic ambitions, the ISM Platform has committed to prioritising information security and incident resilience as a cross-cutting theme across all its initiatives. The role of the Information Security Lead is to develop an effective execution strategy and a programme to improve MSF’s overall information security posture and governance of information security in the movement.

**III. PLACE IN THE ORGANISATION**

The Information Security Lead will:

- Report hierarchically to the International Information Systems Coordinator (who chairs the ISM Platform), with functional oversight provided by the ISM Platform
- Work closely with the members of the ISM Platform, InfoSec focal points in each section, ISM InfoSec WG, MSF SITS (Shared IT Services) and other MSF stakeholders to ensure the information security initiatives, working group(s) and/or task force(s) created/sponsored/guided by the ISM are all aligned to the evolving needs of the organisation and the ISM’s strategic vision
- Work in collaboration with the ISM Coordination team to ensure a consistent approach to programme and project management within the ISM portfolio and Working Group (WG) initiatives

**IV. OBJECTIVES OF THE POSITION**

The Information Security Lead will lead the development of the roadmap for information security governance, risk & compliance in MSF under the guidance of the ISM platform and in close collaboration with the Info Sec WG. The Information Security Lead will provide strategic guidance, operational support, and incident response expertise across headquarters and field missions, balancing security requirements with the realities of medical and humanitarian operations.

The Information Security Lead will establish the governance mechanisms necessary to ensure better identification, monitoring and mitigation of information security risks in MSF. This role will recommend planning and allocation of infosec resources, and develop the necessary processes/frameworks to do so.

Specific Objectives

1. An effective global information security framework, strategy, and roadmap are in place to guide MSF’s short-, medium-, and long-term security priorities.
2. Priority information security risks are proactively managed through a shared and structured organisational approach.
3. Security incidents requiring intersectional coordination are responded to effectively, limiting impact and supporting resilience.
4. Technical information security decisions across MSF are informed by reliable expert guidance.
5. Sensitive information is managed securely and in line with relevant governance requirements.
6. Organisational information security awareness and capability are strengthened on an ongoing basis.
7. Emerging threats and external developments relevant to MSF are monitored and reflected in a stronger overall security posture.

**V. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Information Security Strategy and Governance

- Develop, implement, and maintain MSF’s information security strategy and roadmap
- Define and maintain information security policies, standards, and procedures
- Advise senior management on information security risks and mitigation options, including new resourcing and delivery models
- Support definition of mutualised approaches for selected information security capabilities across MSF (e.g. baseline policies/standards, security monitoring / SIEM-SOC options, incident coordination, third-party security assurance, etc.)
- Contribute to organisational risk management and governance processes

Risk Management

- Identify, assess, and prioritise information security risks in the movement
- Conduct and support information security risk assessments for existing and new initiatives
- Propose feasible mitigation measures
- Support the documentation and acceptance of residual risks

Incident Response and Crisis Management

- Lead responses to movement-wide information security incidents
- Support field missions and headquarters during high‑pressure or sensitive incidents
- Coordinate with relevant functions (IT, legal, communications, HR, security, etc.)
- Ensure post‑incident reviews and follow‑up actions are completed

Technical and Operational Security Oversight

- Advise on matters such as infrastructure, network, cloud, and endpoint security
- Advise on security matters such as identity & access management and remote working
- Ensure security requirements are integrated into system design, procurement, and third‑party arrangements

Data Protection, Ethics, and Safeguarding

- Advise on data classification, minimisation, retention, and secure sharing
- Work closely with data protection, legal, safeguarding, and other stakeholders
- Promote digital practices that minimise risks of harm to individuals and communities

Awareness and Capacity Building

- Develop and deliver information security awareness and training programs
- Build information security capacity among staff
- Translate complex security concepts into clear, practical guidance

Coordination and Representation

- Collaborate closely with all relevant functions
- Chair the ISM Information Security Working Group sessions
- Coordinate with external service providers and security experts
- Represent MSF in relevant information security and humanitarian forums
- Monitor emerging threats relevant to humanitarian and medical organisations

**VI. REQUIREMENTS**

**Education:**

- Minimum Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline (Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, etc.) or equivalent
- Certification as a security professional, e.g. Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) or Certified Information Security Auditor (CISA)

**Experience and skills:**

- Minimum 7 years’ experience in information security or security risk management.
- Strong expertise in cloud, network, and cybersecurity, including incident response, vulnerability management, DLP, IDS/IPS, and penetration testing.
- Good knowledge of security frameworks, risk management, and compliance requirements (e.g. NIST, ISO 27001, CIS, GDPR, PCI DSS).
- Experience developing security policies, standards, and enterprise solutions in complex, decentralised, and international environments.
- Knowledge of business continuity and disaster recovery.
- Strong leadership, communication, analytical, and cross-cultural collaboration skills, with high ethical standards and alignment with MSF values.

**Languages:**

- Fluent spoken and written English

**Other:**

- International travel may be required a few times a year
- Occasional availability outside normal working hours during incidents

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. MSF expects all staff to share this commitment and promote an environment where abuse and misconduct is not tolerated.**

**We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.**

**Note: All offers of employment will be subject to reference checks and to appropriate screening checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her/their understanding of these recruitment procedures.**

jobs.title: Comprehensive Mapping & Private Sector Analysis (CM&PSA) Consultant
jobs.body:
Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

Qatar’s Private Sector constitutes a central pillar of the national economy, contributing significantly to economic diversification, innovation, employment and social development.

For the International Organization for Migration (IOM), private sector engagement is increasingly strategic, particularly in advancing sustainable development outcomes, ethical labour practices, and responsible business conduct.

 However, there is currently no single, comprehensive and structured reference that provides a holistic understanding of the private sector landscape in Qatar. Existing information is fragmented, sector-specific, and limited in analytical depth, making it difficult to support evidence-based engagement and decision-making for government entities, UN agencies, and development actors seeking to engage effectively with the private sector.

This consultancy will address this gap by developing comprehensive private sector mapping and analysis, serving both as:

- A public-facing national reference document, and
- An internal strategic resource for IOM to inform engagement and partnership development.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

  
The consultant will work under Programmes in IOM Qatar Country Office.  
**Responsibilities**

**Category B Consultants: Tangible and miserable outputs of the work assignment**

The consultant will be responsible for carrying out the following:

**Private sector Mapping**

- Identify and profile major sector companies (large firms, SMEs, multinationals, family businesses, free zone entities, social enterprises)
- Analyze sectoral distribution and typologies across key industries

**Business Associations Analysis**

- Map chambers, councils, networks, and representative bodies
- Assess mandates, membership, and influence

**Corporate Practices and Policies**

- Document CSR, ESG, and sustainability practices
- Assess internal policies related to governance and social responsibility

**Regulatory Framework Analysis**

- Analyze laws and policies governing private sector operations, including:
    - Company registration and licensing 
        - Investment, labour, and governance regulations
        - ESG/CSR frameworks

**Strategic Engagement Component**

- Identify key engagement platforms, events, and communication channels.
- Map companies, business associations, and networks according to IOM engagement pillars (Impact, Income, Innovation).
- Assess organizational interests, capacities, influence, and alignment with IOM priorities.
- Identify and prioritize high-potential partners for strategic engagement, collaboration, sponsorship, technical cooperation, and resource mobilization.
- Develop practical engagement pathways and recommendations for outreach to priority stakeholders.

**Methodology**

The consultant will apply a mixed-method, multi-phase approach, including:

- Desk review of secondary data from official registries, business associations, and company disclosures
- Quantitative data collection through structured questionnaires
- Qualitative analysis of partnerships, engagement potential, and sector dynamics
- Data triangulation (minimum two sources per key data point)
- Use of standardized classification frameworks and data tools
- Stakeholder validation to verify findings

The methodology will follow five phases:

1. Desk review and longlisting
2. Private sector survey
3. Business association mapping
4. Regulatory framework analysis
5. Engagement strategy development

Particular emphasis will be placed on generating actionable findings and practical recommendations that support IOM’s partnership development strategy. The analytical framework will assess stakeholder’s relevance and potential contribution across the Impact, Income, and Innovation pillars, enabling prioritization of engagement opportunities for the Misson,

**Deliverables**

The Consultant will produce the following core deliverables (*on a 5-installment payment basis*):

1. Comprehensive Private Sector Mapping Report
2. Consolidated and searchable private sector database
3. Business associations and regulatory framework annex
4. Internal engagement and strategy annex
5. Executive summary (5-8 pages)

**Duration and Timeline**

Indicative timeline:

- Weeks 1-2: Inception and methodology design
- Weeks 3-5: Desk review and initial mapping
- Weeks 6-10: Stakeholder consultation, questionnaire and landscape mapping
- Weeks 11-14: Analysis and drafting outputs
- Weeks 11-16: Validation and finalization

Each phase will produce interim outputs to support ongoing engagement.

**Reporting and Coordination**

- The consultant will report directly to the designated IOM project manager
- Regular progress updates (weekly or bi-weekly) will be required
- Draft outputs will undergo internal review and validation
- Coordination with:
    - IOM 
        - Government stakeholders
            - Business associations and private sector actors

**Performance Indicators for the Evaluation of results**

The consultant will be evaluated based on:

- Timely delivery of agreed outputs
- Quality, accuracy, and completeness of data and analysis
- Adherence to methodology and data governance standards
- Responsiveness to feedback and stakeholder engagement
- Usability of deliverables for strategic and operational purposes

The consultant must ensure:

- Source transparency for all data collected
- Verification protocols (minimum two-source validation)
- Neutrality and non-endorsement of entities
- Data protection compliance, including informed consent where applicable
- No collection of sensitive or confidential data without authorization
- Screening and mitigation of reputational risks
- All outputs must comply with IOM data protection and ethical standards

## **Qualifications**

**Education:**

- Advanced Masters University degree in a related field

**Experience:**

- Minimum 7 years of relevant experience
- Proven experience in private sector analysis, market research, or economic mapping
- Experience in Qatar or the GCC region strongly preferred
- Familiarity with CSR, ESG, and sustainable business practices
- Experience working with international organizations is an asset

**Skills:**

- Strong analytical and research skills
- Experience in database development and data management
- Excellent report writing and communication skills

**Languages**

For this consultancy, Fluency in English (both oral and written is required) Fluency in Arabic will be considered an asset.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

jobs.title: Program Officer, Instructional Design
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.**

***This position has an end date of September, 29, 2027.***

**Job Overview**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Program Officer for Instructional Design for Switchboard, a project that provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at www.SwitchboardTA.org.

The Program Officer for Instructional Design will report to the Senior Program Officer for Instructional Design and will be responsible for delivering high-quality instructional design across Switchboard’s capacity-building initiatives, including online training, self-paced courses, communities of practice, and learning resources such as videos, information guides, toolkits, etc. This position is remote and may be located anywhere in the United States.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Instructional Design**

- Deliver high-quality instructional design across trainings and learning resources developed by Switchboard’s internal and external subject matter experts; provide guidance and review of instructional design across all materials including eLearning courses, instructor-led courses, webinars, and meetings
- Serve as Switchboard’s webinar and meeting producer
- Research and recommend innovative training and instructional design practices that Switchboard should incorporate
- Ensure that practitioner knowledge informs Switchboard’s trainings and learning resources
- Lead implementation of strategy for updating and/or maintaining previously developed Switchboard learning resources
- Champion a culture of learning and continuous improvement in Switchboard’s approach to instructional design; identify relevant professional development opportunities for Switchboard team

**Project Management and M&E**

- Contribute to needs assessment process to ensure instructional design best practices are incorporated into Switchboard’s annual workplan
- Analyze feedback and evaluation data from Switchboard’s TTA participants with a focus on instructional design improvements
- Provide input into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.
- Other duties as assigned*.*

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s Degree in instructional design, education, or other relevant field (or equivalent experience)
- Minimum four years of experience developing and implementing training, technical assistance, capacity-building, or education programs
- Experience developing and producing innovative virtual multimedia trainings, such as webinars, online courses, self-paced e-learning, etc.
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Familiarity with and commitment to data-driven, evidence-based programming
- Excellent written and oral communication skills, with evidence of ability to build capacity of staff at multiple levels
- Ability to effectively manage complex projects with strict timelines

**Preferred Experience & Skills:**

- Graduate degree in relevant field (or equivalent experience)
- Familiarity with relevant Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded programs
- Experience engaging with external subject matter experts and/or consultants

**Working Environment:** This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** ($80,000 - $85,000 - annually ). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits.
