jobs.title: First Nations Engagement and Partnership Adviser
jobs.body:
Job Brief:

This role is open to both international and PNG national candidates.

Position Description:

DT Global has been engaged by Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to manage the next phase of Australia’s investment in strengthening the delivery of law and justice services in Papua New Guinea for a 4-year period to December 2027.

APLJ seeks to contribute to PNG’s law and justice sector capacity to provide inclusive, safe, secure and accountable law and justice foundations for peaceful and prosperous communities, equitable economic development and private sector growth.

APLJ aligns with the Australia-PNG Development Partnership Plan (DPP) 2024–2029 and the Government of Papua New Guinea’s (GoPNG) law and justice sector goal of ‘building peaceful and prosperous communities together.’

APLJ will focus on three End of Program Outcomes (EOPOs):

EOPO 1 - Community Safety and Access to Justice at the Local Level: Communities in target locations, especially women, children, persons with disabilities, vulnerable people and those accused of sorcery, have improved access to selected justice and support services.

EOPO 2 - Law and Justice Services Supply: Responsible law and justice sector agencies increasingly provide selected inclusive, responsive, and accountable essential law and justice services in target locations.

EOPO 3 - Leadership, Coordination and Accountability: Responsible law and justice mechanisms demonstrate improved sectoral leadership and coordination of national and subnational law and justice services and improved sector integrity systems.

APLJ will have a strong focus on addressing gender equality, disability equity and social inclusion (GEDSI): this includes continued and strengthened attention to Gender Based Violence (GBV) and strengthened opportunities for women in leadership, as well as increased focus on the engagement of persons with a disability and other particularly marginalized populations.

The program will continue Australia’s support to law and justice development in Enga, Hela, Madang, Morobe, Southern Highlands, Western, West New Britain and the Autonomous Region of Bougainville (the National Capital District will be covered through support to national agencies).

Additionally, the DPP prioritises fostering partnerships and exchanges between First Nations communities in Australia and local communities in PNG, encouraging shared knowledge and collaboration.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

  
**The Role**

  
The First Nations Engagement and Partnership Adviser will undertake a targeted assessment of APLJ’s current engagement with Australian First Nations businesses, organisations and partners, with a focus on identifying practical opportunities to strengthen First Nations participation in APLJ procurement, programming and partnership activities.

The Adviser will review relevant procurement and supply chain data, program documentation, supplier information and existing engagement practices to establish a baseline of current First Nations participation, identify barriers and enabling factors, and assess areas where increased participation may be feasible and provide value to APLJ.

The Adviser will also develop a prioritised and actionable pipeline of procurement and partnership opportunities. This will include identifying relevant First Nations businesses and organisations, matching potential suppliers and partners to specific APLJ needs and opportunities, and recommending practical changes to procurement, market engagement and partnership practices.

The Adviser will also identify opportunities to support the Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan objective of fostering partnerships and exchanges between First Nations communities in Australia and communities and institutions in PNG. This may include identifying potential twinning or knowledge-exchange opportunities relevant to APLJ’s law and justice mandate, particularly where there is interest from PNG partners and potential for future engagement.

The Adviser will work closely with the APLJ team, DT Global’s First Nations Lead, procurement and corporate functions, and relevant technical teams to ensure findings are translated into practical actions that can be implemented during the remainder of the program.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position:

[https://tinyurl.com/3tbe7v6n](https://tinyurl.com/3tbe7v6n)

**About You**

· Relevant tertiary qualifications applicable to Law and Justice, International Development, or other relevant qualification

· In depth knowledge and understanding of First Nations engagement

· Demonstrated experience undertaking procurement, supply chain, market and organizational program reviews and assessment

· Experience engaging with First Nations organizations, businesses, communities or representative bodies with an understanding of culturally appropriate engagement approaches

· Experience working with government, NGO and CSO counterparts including technical advisers and other specialists critical to the program’s successful performance

· Experience in coordinating with multiple partners and harnessing and strengthening networks.

· Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to adapt

· Ability to work under pressure and at times meet multiple deadlines

· Ability to work independently and as part of a team

· Flexibility and adaptability to work with multiple stakeholders across diverse cultures

**This role is open to suitable qualified both International and PNG Nationals’ candidates.**

**Why join APLJ?**

**Provide program selling points, as an example:**  
*By joining APLJ, you will be part of an environment where you can collaborate with leading experts from diverse backgrounds, access development programs to achieve your career goals, and be challenged to take a global outlook.*

jobs.title: Agriculture Engineer - Project Officer
jobs.body:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job Location: Northwest Syria – Idleb or Aleppo**

**Job purpose:**

Under the supervision of the Project Manager, the Project Officer leads day-to-day implementation of the RISE Syria project (Resilient Irrigation for Smallholder Empowerment), funded by the Humanitarian Innovation Programme (HIP)/Innovation Norway. The Officer facilitates coordination and dialogue between the private sector partner and smallholder wheat farmers, ensures adherence to project timelines and objectives, and works closely with the MEAL team and consortium partners Engineers Without Borders Norway and Field Ready MENA to deliver a high-quality, accountable pilot and scale-up process.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**1. Farmer–Private Sector Dialogue and Coordination**

- Serve as the primary day-to-day liaison between the private sector partner and the 50 pilot smallholder wheat farmers in Southern Aleppo, ensuring clear, culturally appropriate two-way communication throughout Phase 2 and Phase 3.
- Organize and facilitate regular farmer–private sector dialogue sessions, joint field visits, and mentoring sessions aligned to the wheat production calendar.
- Support farmer registration, onboarding, and baseline data collection in coordination with the private sector partner and the MEAL team.
- Facilitate co-design sessions between farmers, technical experts, and the private sector partner on system installation, interface design, alarms, and workflow adaptations.
- Support resolution of operational misunderstandings or grievances between farmers and the private sector partner, escalating unresolved issues to the Project Manager.
- Track farmer feedback, adoption barriers, and satisfaction, feeding this information into MEAL processes and design pivot decisions.
- Maintain a log of all farmers–private sector interactions, agreements, and issues raised, for project accountability.

**2. Project Implementation, Planning and Partner Coordination**

- Support the Project Manager in translating the RISE Syria workplan into detailed weekly/monthly implementation plans for Phase 2 and Phase 3 activities.
- Coordinate with Engineers Without Borders Norway (EWB-N) and Field Ready MENA on technical inputs, site access, logistics, and field-level implementation requirements.
- Monitor progress of the staged pilot rollout (5 → 15 → 30 farms) against agreed milestones and flag delays or risks to the Project Manager.
- Support site verification processes (water access, soil conditions, farmer consent) in coordination with the private sector partner.
- Ensure project activities comply with HIP/Innovation Norway requirements, World Vision internal policies, and applicable national regulations.
- Provide regular field-based updates, progress reports, and technical recommendations to the Project Manager

**3. Monitoring, Evaluation Support**

- Work closely with the MEAL team to apply the Response Innovation Lab (RIL) MEAL Toolkit, including tracking pilot performance and farmer satisfaction.
- Support MEAL team in data collection for baseline, postimplementation monitoring (PIMs), and endline assessments related to farmer adoption, water-use efficiency, and irrigation decision-making.
- Contribute to maintaining the project's pivot diary, documenting design adaptations and their rationale based on farmer feedback.
- Support the establishment and ongoing functioning of community feedback and complaint mechanisms for pilot farmers.
- Ensure MEAL-related field data is accurately entered, verified, and shared with the MEAL team in a timely manner.

**4. Development Documentation, Case Study, and Internal WV Reporting**

- Contribute to development of the RISE Syria case study, including collecting farmer stories, field data, and photographic evidence structured around the RIL innovation methodology.
- Draft and compile internal World Vision reporting requirements (donor reports, internal updates, SharePoint documentation) related to the Project Officer's areas of responsibility.
- Support preparation of materials for dissemination events, learning briefs, and scale-up planning documentation.
- Maintain accurate, organized project records (photos, field evidence, farmer engagement logs) per donor (HIP/Innovation Norway) and WV documentation standards.

**5. Networking and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Coordinate with local authorities, community representatives, and relevant stakeholders in Southern Aleppo to support smooth pilot implementation.
- Participate in relevant food security, agriculture, or humanitarian innovation coordination forums as required.
- Represent World Vision professionally when engaging with the private sector partner, farmers, and other consortium partners.

**6. Child Protection and Safeguarding**

- Ensure all farmer engagement and field activities comply with World Vision's Child Protection Policy and safeguarding standards.
- Identify and report any child protection or safeguarding concerns arising during farmer dialogue, field visits, or private sector engagement activities.
- Promote awareness of Do No Harm principles among farmers, technicians, and private sector partners involved in the pilot
- Perform other duties as assigned by the Team Lead or Project Manager.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**

**Required Professional Experience:**

- Minimum 5 years of experience in agricultural project implementation, preferably within humanitarian innovation, private-sector engagement, or livelihoods programming. Solid knowledge of wheat production, irrigation systems, and climate-smart agriculture is required, along with demonstrated experience facilitating coordination and dialogue between private-sector actors and smallholder farming communities.

**Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor's degree in Agricultural Engineering, Civil Engineering, or another closely related field. Candidates without this specific degree but with extensive, demonstrable professional experience in agriculture and food security programming may also be considered.

**Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Excellent English and Arabic communication skills (both oral and written).
- Strong interpersonal and coordination skills, with a demonstrated ability to build trust and manage relationships between diverse stakeholders — particularly private-sector actors and smallholder farmers.
- Familiarity with private-sector engagement models, market-based approaches, or innovation piloting within humanitarian contexts.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
- Motivated to work in the humanitarian innovation field and grow professionally; eager and quick to learn.
- Familiar with core principles of Children's Rights, Child Protection, Participation, and Do No Harm.
- Knowledge of and adherence to the Child Protection, Red Cross and NGO Code of Conduct.
- Working knowledge of the logical framework approach and basic MEAL principles.

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

- The position requires 100% of the time to be field based.
- Position requires willingness and ability to continue functioning during a crisis, including during a World Vision response to a manmade or natural disaster.

**Language Requirements:**

- Fluent Arabic and working proficiency in English (spoken and written).

jobs.title: Peacebuilding Officer
jobs.body:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Location: Syria – Hassakeh**

**Job purpose:**

The Peacebuilding officer will be responsible for designing, implementing, and monitoring peace-building initiatives within WVSR. S/he will focus on promoting conflict resolution, social cohesion, and community resilience in post-conflict and conflict-prone areas. The Peacebuilding officer will work closely with community leaders, local organizations, governmental bodies, and international partners to develop and foster sustainable peace and development strategies. S/he will ensure that project objectives are met, resources are utilized effectively, and project activities are implemented in line with the project plan.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**1. Peacebuilding Program Management:**

- Develop and implement peacebuilding activities tailored to the local context, conflict dynamics, and identified community needs.
- Conduct conflict and context analyses to identify key conflict drivers, risks, stakeholders, and opportunities for peacebuilding.
- Facilitate dialogue, mediation, and other peacebuilding processes between relevant groups and communities.
- Ensure gender, diversity, inclusion, conflict sensitivity, and Do No Harm principles are integrated into project design and implementation

**2. Community Engagement and Participation:**

- Engage with communities and relevant stakeholders to understand their perspectives, priorities, concerns, and peacebuilding needs.
- Support the establishment and strengthening of community-based peacebuilding structures, committees, and networks.
- Promote meaningful participation of women, youth, and marginalized groups in peacebuilding activities and decision-making processes.
- Support community-led peacebuilding initiatives and activities that strengthen social cohesion and community resilience..

**3. Capacity Building and Technical Support:**

- Assess capacity-building needs of community committees, local leaders, stakeholders, and relevant partners.
- Develop and facilitate training, workshops, awareness sessions, and coaching on conflict resolution, dialogue, peacebuilding, social cohesion, and related topics.
- Provide technical guidance and ongoing support to community structures and stakeholders implementing peacebuilding initiatives.
- Support local institutions and community actors to strengthen their capacity to prevent and manage conflicts.

**4. Research, Context Analysis and Learning:**

- Conduct and regularly update conflict and context analyses relevant to project locations.
- Monitor emerging peacebuilding trends, conflict dynamics, risks, and opportunities in the operational context.
- Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and innovative approaches from peacebuilding interventions.
- Use evidence and learning to inform programme adaptation and future peacebuilding initiatives.

**5. Coordination, Advocacy and Networking:**

- Establish and maintain effective relationships with community leaders, local authorities, NGOs, UN agencies, civil society organizations, and other relevant stakeholders.
- Represent the organization in relevant peacebuilding coordination meetings, forums, workshops, and policy dialogues as required.
- Coordinate with relevant internal and external actors to strengthen complementarity and avoid duplication of peacebuilding interventions.
- Identify opportunities for collaboration, partnership, and joint peacebuilding initiatives

**6. Monitoring, Reporting and Documentation:**

- Develop and follow up on peacebuilding activity plans, workplans, and implementation schedules.
- Monitor peacebuilding activities to ensure quality, relevance, conflict sensitivity, and achievement of intended results.
- Prepare regular activity and progress reports, including challenges, achievements, lessons learned, and recommendations.
- Maintain comprehensive documentation of peacebuilding activities, participant data, training records, meeting minutes, success stories, and other relevant evidence.
- Support preparation of project proposals, budgets, donor reports, and other programme documentation as required.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**

**Required Professional Experience:**

- Previous experience in project support or project management.
- Experience in managing peace-building interventions.
- Proficiency in project management tools.
- Strong organizational and time management skills.
- Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
- Problem-solving and analytical abilities.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
- Familiarity with donor regulations, reporting, and compliance.
- A minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience in peace-building.

**Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Certificate in community / development background
- Results-oriented and meets dateline
- Ability to work independently.
- Results-oriented in performing official duties.

**Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in social sciences, psychology, law, or a relevant field.
- Good interpersonal skills and cross-cultural sensitivity
- Excellent English and Arabic communication skills (both oral and written)
- Good networking and partnership development skills

Communication, advocacy & facilitation skills

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

The position requires ability and willingness to travel to other WV project sites when needed

**Physical Requirements**:

- Ability to effectively coordinate with staff and key stakeholders ensure successfully program implementation.

**Language Requirements:**

- Arabic, English

jobs.title: Health Coordinator
jobs.body:
**CONTEXTE**

Le 15 mai 2026, la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a déclaré sa dix-septième épidémie d'Ebola après la confirmation de cas dans la province de l'Ituri. L'épidémie s'est depuis étendue à d'autres zones touchées et à risque, ce qui accroît la pression sur un système de santé déjà fragile. La réponse se déroule dans un contexte humanitaire complexe, marqué par les conflits, les déplacements de population, un accès limité aux services de santé et des lacunes persistantes en matière de prévention et de contrôle des infections (PCI), d'eau, hygiène et assainissement (EHA), de surveillance, de systèmes de référencement et de fournitures médicales essentielles. Ces difficultés augmentent le risque de transmission liée aux soins de santé et de perturbation des services de santé essentiels.

L'IRC a lancé une réponse intégrée à l'épidémie d'Ebola en collaboration avec le ministère de la Santé et les structures de réponse nationales, provinciales et de zone de santé concernées, notamment le COUSP, les Divisions provinciales de la santé (DPS), les équipes cadres des zones de santé (BCZ), les formations sanitaires et d'autres partenaires de la réponse. La réponse de l'IRC réunit les secteurs Santé, PCI/EHA, Communication sur les risques et engagement communautaire (CREC), Protection, et Santé mentale et soutien psychosocial (SMSPS). La réponse sanitaire vise à renforcer la capacité des formations sanitaires à détecter et référer en toute sécurité les cas suspects d'Ebola, à améliorer la PCI et la sécurité des patients, à renforcer la surveillance et les filières de référencement au niveau des formations sanitaires, et à soutenir la continuité en toute sécurité.

**APERÇU DU POSTE**

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) Santé assure le leadership technique global et la supervision programmatique de la réponse santé de l'IRC à la maladie à virus Ebola (MVE) en RDC. Rattaché(e) au Directeur adjoint des programmes (DDP) Ebola, le poste est chargé de veiller à ce que la réponse santé de l'IRC soit techniquement solide, opérationnellement réalisable, suivie par rapport aux résultats convenus, et alignée sur le ministère de la Santé (MoH), les structures nationales de réponse à la MVE et les normes de l'IRC.

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) Santé assure la direction technique de la programmation MVE au niveau des formations sanitaires, notamment la prévention et le contrôle des infections (PCI), le dépistage, le triage et l'isolement temporaire, la surveillance au niveau des formations sanitaires, la prévention de l'exposition professionnelle et la continuité en toute sécurité des services de santé essentiels. Le poste supervise directement les Responsables PCI seniors et assure la supervision technique, le mentorat et l'assurance qualité auprès des équipes PCI santé dans l'ensemble des sites de réponse. Le rôle travaille en étroite collaboration avec les équipes EHA, CREC et Protection afin de garantir une réponse intégrée et redevable.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS**

**Leadership technique et qualité des programmes**

- Assurer le leadership stratégique et technique global de la réponse santé MVE de l'IRC, en traduisant l'épidémiologie de l'épidémie, les priorités de la réponse et les données de terrain en priorités programmatiques claires et en orientations techniques.
- Veiller à ce que les interventions de santé soient mises en œuvre conformément aux protocoles du MoH, aux directives nationales de réponse à la MVE, aux engagements envers les bailleurs et aux normes techniques de l'IRC.
- Assurer la supervision technique des mesures de prévention et de réponse à la MVE au niveau des formations sanitaires, y compris le dépistage et le triage, l'isolement temporaire, la circulation des patients, les précautions standard et liées à la transmission, l'hygiène des mains, le nettoyage et la désinfection environnementaux, la gestion des déchets biomédicaux, l'utilisation des EPI et la prévention de l'exposition professionnelle.
- Veiller à ce que les formations sanitaires appuyées par l'IRC puissent identifier, isoler et référer en toute sécurité les cas suspects de MVE tout en maintenant un accès sûr aux services de santé essentiels et en réduisant les risques de transmission liée aux soins.
- Orienter l'élaboration, l'adaptation et l'application des protocoles techniques, procédures opérationnelles standard (POS), listes de contrôle, aide-mémoires, outils d'évaluation et démarches d'amélioration de la qualité pour la réponse MVE.
- Veiller à ce que les priorités programmatiques et l'appui aux formations sanitaires soient fondés sur les risques et réactifs à l'évolution de l'épidémiologie, aux risques au niveau des formations sanitaires, aux expositions du personnel soignant, aux tendances d'utilisation des services et aux lacunes identifiées en matière de PCI/EHA.
- Fournir une orientation technique lors d'incidents cliniques ou de PCI significatifs, veiller à une escalade et un suivi appropriés, et appuyer l'adaptation des programmes sur la base des enseignements tirés.

**Gestion des programmes, suivi et amélioration de la qualité**

- Superviser la mise en œuvre des programmes santé/MVE de l'IRC par rapport aux plans de travail approuvés, aux cadres de résultats, aux indicateurs de performance, aux plans de dépenses et aux engagements envers les bailleurs, en veillant à des mesures correctives rapides lorsque la mise en œuvre s'écarte des objectifs.
- Effectuer des visites de terrain et des revues techniques régulières afin d'évaluer la qualité des programmes, d'encadrer les équipes, de vérifier la mise en œuvre et de suivre les mesures correctives convenues.
- Travailler avec les équipes MEAL afin de garantir la mise en place et l'utilisation cohérente de systèmes de suivi, de bases de données, d'indicateurs et de processus de qualité des données appropriés dans l'ensemble de la réponse santé.
- Examiner et analyser les données programmatiques, les scores d'évaluation PCI, les données de surveillance et de dépistage, les tendances d'utilisation des services, les résultats de formation et de mentorat, les événements d'infection/exposition du personnel soignant et les informations sur les intrants, afin d'orienter les décisions et l'amélioration des programmes.
- Veiller à la production en temps voulu de mises à jour programmatiques, de rapports internes, de rapports aux bailleurs et de contributions techniques aux rapports de situation précis et de haute qualité, documentant clairement les réalisations, les lacunes, les risques, les mesures correctives et les priorités.

**Supervision, leadership et développement du personnel**

- Superviser directement les Responsables PCI seniors et les autres membres du personnel de santé senior assignés, en définissant des priorités claires, en évaluant la performance et en garantissant la redevabilité en matière de qualité et de mise en œuvre des programmes.
- Assurer une supervision technique, un coaching et un mentorat réguliers auprès des Responsables PCI seniors et garantir des normes et approches techniques cohérentes dans l'ensemble des sites de réponse.
- Diriger le recrutement des postes clés en santé/MVE en coordination avec le DDP, les RH et la direction de terrain.
- Identifier les lacunes de capacité et garantir une formation technique structurée, un mentorat et un développement professionnel pour les équipes santé.
- Veiller à ce que des mesures de devoir de diligence appropriées soient appliquées pour les équipes travaillant en contexte d'épidémie, y compris le respect des protocoles de sécurité du personnel, la prévention de l'exposition et le signalement des incidents

**Développement des activités, gestion des subventions et supervision budgétaire**

- Participer activement à l'élaboration des notes conceptuelles et des propositions de réponse à Ebola, en assurant le leadership technique pour l'analyse des besoins, la conception des programmes, les paquets d'activités, les indicateurs, les cibles, les approches de mise en œuvre et les notes techniques narratives.
- Travailler avec les équipes Subventions, Finance, Opérations, MEAL et techniques afin d'élaborer des budgets de proposition réalistes, des structures de dotation en personnel, des besoins en approvisionnement et des plans de mise en œuvre alignés sur la conception du programme.
- Superviser la composante santé de la mise en œuvre des subventions et assumer la responsabilité de la gestion du budget du programme, y compris l'examen régulier du budget par rapport aux dépenses réelles (BvA), des plans de dépenses, des taux de consommation budgétaire, des prévisions et des écarts identifiés.
- Veiller à ce que les équipes santé maintiennent des plans d'approvisionnement et des prévisions actualisés pour les EPI, les intrants PCI, les fournitures médicales, les équipements et autres intrants programmatiques, en lien avec les plans d'activités et de dépenses.
- Veiller à ce que la quantification soit fondée sur le type de formation sanitaire, le volume de services, le niveau de risque, les données de consommation et les plans programmatiques, avec une action précoce pour éviter les ruptures de stock ou une utilisation inappropriée.
- Contribuer aux réunions de revue des subventions, aux rapports aux bailleurs et à la clôture des programmes, en veillant à l'alignement des livrables techniques, des dépenses et des résultats programmatiques.

**Coordination et représentation**

- Représenter l'IRC dans les forums de coordination pertinents aux niveaux national, provincial et de zone de santé, y compris le Cluster Santé et les structures techniques de réponse à la MVE.
- Entretenir des relations de travail constructives avec le MoH, les DPS, les autorités des zones de santé, la direction des formations sanitaires, les agences des Nations Unies, les bailleurs, les ONG et les autres partenaires de la réponse.
- Renforcer la qualité des activités de PCI par une supervision formative régulière avec les DPS et les zones de santé.

**Partenariats**

- Servir de point focal technique santé de l'IRC pour les partenariats appuyant la réponse à la MVE en Ituri et au Nord-Kivu, en travaillant en collaboration avec les responsables techniques des partenaires.
- Contribuer à la planification technique conjointe, à la revue et à l'adaptation de la réponse, en veillant à ce que les activités santé de l'IRC soient complémentaires à celles des partenaires et alignées sur les priorités convenues de la réponse.
- Représenter l'IRC dans les discussions techniques pertinentes avec les partenaires et veiller à ce que les actions techniques convenues concernant l'IRC soient communiquées et suivies en interne.

**Sécurité, sauvegarde et redevabilité**

- Travailler avec le service Sécurité et la direction de terrain pour surveiller les risques affectant les équipes santé et la mise en œuvre des programmes, et veiller à ce que les incidents ou préoccupations soient signalés et traités rapidement.
- Promouvoir une programmation centrée sur les clients et redevable, y compris la sensibilisation et l'utilisation appropriée des mécanismes de retour d'information et de plainte dans les services appuyés.
- Intégrer l'analyse des risques de sauvegarde et les mesures d'atténuation des risques pertinentes dans la conception et la mise en œuvre des projets.
- Maintenir à jour une cartographie multisectorielle des services et une filière de référencement pour la réponse aux violences. (Ceci sert des objectifs programmatiques mais sous-tend également les procédures opérationnelles standard de l'IRC pour la réponse à tout préjudice lié à la sauvegarde.)

**PROFIL RECHERCHÉ**

- Professionnel(le) de santé ayant une solide formation en santé publique (un master en santé publique serait un atout).
- Au moins 3 à 5 ans d'expérience progressivement responsable dans la programmation santé humanitaire ou d'urgence, y compris la gestion de programmes de santé complexes et la supervision de personnel technique senior.
- Une expérience opérationnelle avérée dans la réponse à la maladie à virus Ebola, à une autre fièvre hémorragique virale, ou à une épidémie de maladie infectieuse comparable est fortement souhaitée.
- Compétences avérées en leadership, communication et facilitation.
- Expérience de la gestion d'équipes multidisciplinaires sur plusieurs sites de terrain, avec de solides compétences en coaching, gestion de la performance et résolution de problèmes.
- Maîtrise de Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint et des outils courants de suivi de programme.
- La maîtrise du français est requise, avec un bon niveau d'anglais ; la connaissance des langues locales pertinentes est un atout.

**ENVIRONNEMENT DE TRAVAIL**

- Le poste nécessite des déplacements réguliers vers les formations sanitaires appuyées par l'IRC, les zones de santé et les sites de réponse en RDC.
- Le rôle peut nécessiter des visites dans des environnements cliniques, y compris des zones de dépistage, strictement conformément aux protocoles de PCI et de sécurité approuvés.
- Le poste exige une flexibilité pour répondre à l'évolution rapide des conditions épidémiologiques, opérationnelles et sécuritaires.

**Employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances** : L'IRC est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. L'IRC évalue tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur de peau, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, de situation matrimoniale, de statut d'ancien combattant, de handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**Normes professionnelles** : Tous les collaborateurs de l’International Rescue Committee (IRC) doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes fondamentaux énoncés dans le document « IRC Way – Normes de conduite professionnelle ». Nos normes sont l’intégrité, le service, l’égalité et la responsabilité. Conformément à ces valeurs, l’IRC met en œuvre et applique des politiques relatives à la protection des personnes, aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’intégrité financière, au signalement des irrégularités et à la protection contre les représailles. L’IRC s’engage à prendre toutes les mesures préventives nécessaires et à créer un environnement où chacun se sent en sécurité, ainsi qu’à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires et correctives en cas de préjudice. L’IRC constitue des équipes de professionnels qui favorisent la réflexion critique, le partage des responsabilités, le débat et l’objectivité afin d’offrir les meilleurs services possibles à nos bénéficiaires.

**BACKGROUND**

On 15 May 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) declared its seventeenth Ebola outbreak following confirmation of cases in Ituri Province. The outbreak has since expanded to other affected and at-risk areas, placing additional pressure on an already fragile health system. The response is unfolding in a complex humanitarian context characterized by conflict, population displacement, limited access to health services, and persistent gaps in infection prevention and control (IPC), WASH, surveillance, referral systems, and essential medical supplies. These challenges increase the risk of healthcare-associated transmission and disruption of essential health services.

IRC has launched an integrated Ebola response in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and relevant national, provincial, and health zone response structures, including the COUSP, Provincial Health Divisions (DPS), Health Zone management teams (BCZ), health facilities, and other response partners. IRC’s response brings together Health, IPC/WASH, Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Protection, and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). The health response focuses on strengthening the capacity of health facilities to safely detect and refer suspected Ebola cases, improving IPC and patient safety, strengthening facility-based surveillance and referral pathways and supporting the continuity of safe.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Health Coordinator provides overall technical leadership and program oversight for IRC’s Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) health response in DRC. Reporting to the Ebola Deputy Director of Programs (DDP), the position is responsible for ensuring that IRC’s health response is technically sound, operationally feasible, monitored against agreed results, and aligned with Ministry of Health (MoH), national EVD response structures and IRC standards.

The Health Coordinator leads the technical direction of the facility-based EVD programming, including Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), screening and triage and temporary isolation, facility-based surveillance, occupational exposure prevention and safe continuity of essential health services. The position directly supervises Senior IPC Managers and provides technical oversight, mentoring and quality assurance to health IPC teams across response locations. The role works closely with WASH, RCCE and Protection teams to ensure an integrated and accountable response.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Technical Leadership and Program Quality**

- Provide overall strategic and technical leadership for IRC’s EVD health response, translating outbreak epidemiology, response priorities and field evidence into clear program priorities and technical direction.
- Ensure health interventions are implemented in accordance with MoH protocols, national EVD response guidance, donor commitments and IRC technical standards.
- Provide technical oversight of facility-based EVD prevention and response measures, including screening and triage, temporary isolation, patient flow, standard and transmission-based precautions, hand hygiene, environmental cleaning and disinfection, healthcare waste management, PPE use and occupational exposure prevention.
- Ensure IRC-supported health facilities can safely identify, isolate and refer suspected EVD cases while maintaining safe access to essential health services and reducing healthcare-associated transmission risks.
- Guide development, adaptation and application of technical protocols, SOPs, checklists, job aids, assessment tools and quality-improvement approaches for the EVD response.
- Ensure program priorities and facility support are risk-based and responsive to evolving epidemiology, health-facility risks, healthcare-worker exposures, service-utilization trends and identified IPC/WASH gaps.
- Provide technical guidance during significant clinical or IPC incidents, ensure appropriate escalation and follow-up, and support program adaptation based on lessons learned.

**Program Management, Monitoring and Quality Improvement**

- Oversee implementation of IRC health/EVD programs against approved work plans, results frameworks, performance indicators, spending plans and grant commitments, ensuring timely corrective action where implementation is off track.
- Conduct regular field visits and technical reviews to assess program quality, mentor teams, verify implementation and follow up agreed corrective actions.
- Work with MEAL teams to ensure appropriate monitoring systems, databases, indicators and data-quality processes are in place and consistently used across the health response.
- Review and analyze program data, IPC assessment scores, surveillance and screening data, service-utilization trends, training and mentorship results, healthcare-worker infection/exposure events and commodity information to guide decisions and program improvement.
- Ensure timely, accurate and high-quality program updates, internal reports, donor reports and technical inputs to situation reports, clearly documenting achievements, gaps, risks, corrective actions and priorities.

**Staff Supervision, Leadership and Development**

- Directly supervise Senior IPC Managers and other senior health staff as assigned, setting clear priorities, reviewing performance and ensuring accountability for program quality and delivery.
- Provide regular technical supervision, coaching and mentoring to Senior IPC Managers and ensure consistent technical standards and approaches across response locations.
- Lead recruitment of key health/EVD positions in coordination with the DDP, HR and field management.
- Identify capacity gaps and ensure structured technical training, mentorship and professional development for health teams.
- Ensure appropriate duty-of-care measures for teams working in outbreak settings, including adherence to staff safety protocols, exposure prevention and incident reporting

**Business Development, Grant Management and Budget Oversight**

- Participate actively in development of Ebola-response concept notes and proposals, providing technical leadership for needs analysis, program design, activity packages, indicators, targets, implementation approaches and technical narratives.
- Work with Grants, Finance, Operations, MEAL and technical colleagues to develop realistic proposal budgets, staffing structures, procurement requirements and implementation plans aligned with program design.
- Oversee the health component of grant implementation and maintain responsibility for program budget management, including regular review of Budget versus Actuals (BvA), spending plans, burn rates, forecasts and identified variances.
- Ensure health teams maintain updated procurement plans and forecasts for PPE, IPC commodities, medical supplies, equipment and other program inputs, with appropriate linkage to activity and spending plans.
- Ensure quantification is informed by facility type, service volume, risk level, consumption data and program plans, with early action to prevent stock-outs or inappropriate use.
- Contribute to grant review meetings, donor reporting and program close-out, ensuring technical deliverables, expenditure and program results remain aligned.

**Coordination and Representation**

- Represent IRC in relevant national, provincial and Health Zone coordination forums, including Health Cluster and EVD-response technical structures.
- Maintain constructive working relationships with the MoH, DPS, Health Zone authorities, health-facility leadership, UN agencies, donors, NGOs and other response partners.
- Strengthen the quality of IPC activities through regular supportive supervision with the DPS and Health Zones.

**Partnerships**

- Serve as IRC’s health technical focal point for partnerships supporting the EVD response in Ituri and North Kivu, working collaboratively with partner technical leads.
- Contribute to joint technical planning, review and adaptation of the response, ensuring IRC’s health activities are complementary to those of partners and aligned with agreed response priorities.
- Represent IRC in relevant partnership technical discussions and ensure agreed technical actions relevant to IRC are communicated and followed up internally.

**Safety, Safeguarding and Accountability**

- Work with Safety and Security and field leadership to monitor risks affecting health teams and program delivery and ensure incidents or concerns are promptly reported and addressed.
- Promote client centered and accountable programming, including awareness and appropriate use of feedback and complaint mechanisms in supported services.
- Build safeguarding risk analysis and relevant risk mitigation measures into project design and implementation.
- Maintain updated, multisector service mapping and referral pathway for violence response. (This serves programming purposes but also underpins IRC's standard operating procedures for response to all safeguarding harm.

**REQUIRED PROFILE**

- Health professional with a strong public health background (MPH desirable).
- At least 3- 5 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian or emergency health programming, including management of complex health programs and supervision of senior technical staff.
- Demonstrated operational experience in Ebola Virus Disease, another viral haemorrhagic fever, or comparable infectious-disease outbreak response is strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated leadership, communication, and facilitation skills.
- Experience managing multidisciplinary teams across multiple field locations, with strong coaching, performance-management and problem-solving skills.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and routine program monitoring tools.
- Fluency in French is required with strong English proficiency; relevant local languages are an asset.

**WORKING ENVIRONMENT**

- The position requires regular travel to IRC-supported health facilities, Health Zones and response locations in DRC.
- The role may require visits to clinical environments, including screening areas, strictly in accordance with approved IPC and safety protocols.
- The position requires flexibility to respond to rapidly changing epidemiological, operational and security conditions.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Employment Specialist
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:** The Employment Specialist in Iowa assists newly arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to attain self-sufficiency through employment by guiding them through employment preparation, coordinating job placements, and other career advancement services.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake, assessment and provide program orientation to clients eligible for employment services. Develop comprehensive employment plans and budget strategies for each employable adult. Provide job readiness and job search coaching and connect clients with job opportunities.
- Develop and cultivate long-term relationships with area employers and staffing agencies to identify appropriate employment opportunities for clients.
- Assist clients and employers as necessary with post-placement issues and continuing employment needs.
- Monitor client job performance, wage levels, and related metrics.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of support staff, volunteers, and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in workforce development field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Experience with job placement and job readiness training a plus.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Proficient in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($21.00/hr - $22.80/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law***.***

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $143 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: CRM, Systems and Data Specialist
jobs.body:
## **MSF Eastern Africa is looking for a CRM, Systems and Data Specialist**

*Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognizing the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.*

*Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organization from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.*

*For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as **Low** risk and will be monitored with this in regard.*

## ***Introduction***

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

## ***About MSF Eastern Africa***

MSF Eastern Africa is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

## ***Rationale/Objective for Position***

The CRM, Systems and Data Specialist is responsible for leading the effective management, development and continuous improvement of MSF Eastern Africa's CRM and fundraising systems, ensuring they are fit for purpose, integrated, secure, scalable and capable of supporting the section's fundraising strategy and growth.

This position will be ***hierarchically*** and ***functionally*** accountable to the ***Head of Fundraising***.

## ***Tasks & Responsibilities***

**CRM System Administration and Ownership**

- Act as the primary administrator and internal focal point for MSF Eastern Africa's CRM and connected fundraising systems.
- Maintain a clear overview of the CRM architecture, fundraising systems, integrations and data flows, ensuring these are documented and regularly updated.
- Manage day-to-day CRM administration, including user access, permissions, configuration and troubleshooting.
- Identify the root causes of system errors and coordinate sustainable solutions with ICT, internal users and external suppliers.
- Serve as the first point of contact for CRM-related queries and support for fundraising and relevant communications users.
- Maintain comprehensive and accessible system documentation, including configurations, integrations, processes, workflows and troubleshooting procedures.
- Ensure appropriate business continuity arrangements for critical fundraising systems.

**Data Processing, Quality and Protection**

- Ensure effective and accurate processing of donor data, including data imports, updates, transactions, extracts, reconciliations and data transfers between systems.
- Work closely with Finance to support accurate donor income consolidation, reconciliation and reporting processes.
- Oversee data flows between the CRM and relevant systems, including online donation/payment platforms, finance systems, marketing automation, website, telemarketing and other data sources.
- Maintain high standards of data quality through data cleansing, validation, automation, quality controls and regular reviews.
- Identify and resolve data quality issues and implement sustainable preventative measures.
- Ensure donor data is processed in compliance with applicable data protection requirements and MSF policies.
- Work with relevant colleagues to strengthen data protection processes, data retention, access controls and responsible use of donor information.

**CRM Development, Integrations and Continuous Improvement**

- Lead or coordinate CRM development initiatives in collaboration with ICT, Fundraising, Communications and external suppliers.
- Identify system and process gaps proactively and propose improvements that strengthen fundraising efficiency, donor experience and data quality.
- Manage CRM development projects, including integration, workflow and process development, segmentation, reporting and automation.
- Develop and maintain a prioritized CRM development backlog in consultation with the Head of Fundraising and relevant stakeholders.
- Translate fundraising and communications requirements into clear technical specifications and business requirements for ICT and suppliers.
- Coordinate user acceptance testing, frontline testing, issue resolution and implementation of system changes.
- Monitor new CRM, fundraising technology and digital developments and assess their relevance to MSF Eastern Africa.
- Support the Head of Fundraising and Director of Communications & Fundraising in decisions relating to CRM development, system investment and prioritization.

**CRM Selection and Fundraising Technology**

- Work closely with ICT, Fundraising and Communications to assess, identify and implement a CRM solution that is fit for MSF Eastern Africa's current and future fundraising needs.
- Support the Head of Fundraising and Director of Communications & Fundraising in defining the business requirements, functionality and technical specifications for the section's CRM.
- Assess how the CRM will integrate with digital fundraising, payment platforms, finance, communications, marketing automation, website and other relevant systems.
- Coordinate with ICT to ensure that the selected solution meets MSF EA requirements for security, scalability, interoperability, data protection and business continuity.
- Support vendor assessment, requirements gathering, demonstrations, testing, implementation and transition to ensure the selected CRM delivers value for the Fundraising Department.
- Ensure the CRM roadmap remains aligned with the section's fundraising strategy and future growth requirements.

**Donor Data, Analytics and Insight**

- Analyse donor, campaign, channel and digital data to identify trends, segments, opportunities and risks.
- Develop dashboards and reports covering income, acquisition, conversion, retention, attrition, reactivation, upgrade, average gift and donor lifetime value.
- Provide regular and ad-hoc analysis to support fundraising strategy, campaign planning, forecasting and decision-making.
- Develop donor segmentation and profiling approaches to improve targeting, personalisation and donor value.
- Support A/B testing and campaign optimisation through data analysis.
- Translate complex data into clear, actionable recommendations for fundraising and communications teams.

**Marketing Automation, Digital Fundraising and Donor Journeys**

- Support the digital fundraising specialist in designing, building, testing and optimising automated email flows and multi-channel donor journeys covering acquisition, welcome, onboarding, conversion, retention, reactivation and upgrade.
- Work closely with the fundraising team to implement segmentation and personalisation across automated communications.
- Work closely with the Digital Fundraising Specialist and fundraising team to align donor journeys with acquisition and retention strategies.
- Support implementation and optimisation of digital fundraising platforms and donation/payment solutions.
- Ensure fundraising landing pages, forms, payment journeys, tracking and CRM integration function effectively.
- Support campaign tracking, attribution, tagging and data capture across digital fundraising channels.
- Identify opportunities to improve the end-to-end donor experience through better systems, data flows and automation.

**Enabling Fundraising Excellence and Capacity Building**

- Enable the Fundraising Department to effectively use the CRM and related systems to achieve fundraising and donor management objectives.
- Work closely with the Digital Fundraising Specialist and the other fundraising teams to leverage donor insights and improve segmentation, targeting, retention and fundraising performance.
- Build the capacity of fundraising users through onboarding, training, user guidance and development of CRM training materials.
- Develop and maintain user resources, SOPs, FAQs and other support materials to improve adoption and reduce unnecessary system support requests.
- Promote best practices and efficient ways of working across the Fundraising team.
- Identify opportunities to automate manual processes and improve fundraising team efficiency.
- Support the adoption of data-driven decision-making across Fundraising.

**Supplier and Stakeholder Management**

- Maintain a professional and constructive relationship with CRM, technology, digital and data suppliers.
- Act as a key technical/business focal point with suppliers, coordinating requirements, development priorities, testing, troubleshooting and delivery.
- Support the Head of Fundraising with supplier management, budgeting, planning and performance monitoring related to CRM and fundraising systems.
- Work closely with ICT to ensure appropriate technical governance and integration of fundraising systems within the wider MSF EA technology environment.
- Collaborate closely with Communications, Fundraising, Finance and other relevant departments to ensure systems meet cross-functional requirements.
- Participate in relevant MSF systems communities of practice and share learning and best practices with other MSF offices.

**Reporting, Forecasting and Performance**

- Develop regular CRM and fundraising performance reports for the Head of Fundraising and wider team.
- Support income modelling, forecasting, reforecasting and budget monitoring using reliable fundraising data.
- Provide monthly and quarterly reporting on donor acquisition, retention, attrition, campaign performance and donor value.
- Respond to national and movement-wide fundraising reporting requirements and data requests.
- Provide evidence-based recommendations for planning and performance reviews.

**OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Integrate EDI & Safeguarding aspects in area of work responsibility, including policies and practices.
- Recognize, respond, and document any form of abuse or inappropriate behaviour and alert the safeguarding unit of any suspected potential abuse.
- Proactively participate in the individual performance management process including objective setting, performance monitoring and performance evaluation.
- Embed duty of care principles into all initiatives, CRM administration, and staff relations.

## ***Qualifications***

**Education**

- Bachelor's degree in data science, statistics, information systems, computer science, marketing, business administration or a related field.

**Experience**

- At least 3-5 years' professional experience in CRM administration, development, data management, analytics, or a related systems role.
- Demonstrated experience in a digital environment, including digital fundraising, digital marketing, e-commerce or customer/donor relationship management.
- Hands-on experience with CRM and marketing automation platforms such as Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics 365, HubSpot, Mailchimp, Brevo, Active Campaign or similar.
- Experience managing CRM integrations with websites, donation/payment platforms, email/marketing automation and other digital systems.
- Experience building reports and dashboards from CRM and fundraising data.
- Strong experience in data analysis, segmentation, campaign performance analysis and donor/customer behavior analysis.
- Experience coordinating system or digital development projects with external suppliers and internal stakeholders, including requirements gathering, testing and delivery.
- Experience with Power BI, Tableau or equivalent business intelligence tools.
- Experience with statistical analysis; machine learning or predictive analytics is an asset.
- Experience with donor lifecycle management, retention, reactivation, upgrade and lifetime value analysis.
- Experience with API-based integrations, data migration, data cleansing and system implementation.
- Experience with digital analytics tools such as Google Analytics/GA4 and campaign tracking/attribution.
- Experience supporting payment and online donation platforms.
- Experience working across multiple teams, countries or culturally diverse environments.
- Experience in fundraising or the non-profit/humanitarian sector.

**Competencies**

- ***Technical Competencies***
    - Strong understanding of data quality, data governance, privacy, data protection and information security principles.
    - Ability to translate technical/data issues into clear business implications and actionable recommendations.
    - Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
- ***Behavioural/General Competencies***
    - Commitment to MSF principles
    - Analytical Thinking
    - Planning and Organizing
    - Results and Quality Orientation
    - Teamwork and Cooperation
    - Initiative and Innovation
    - Networking and Building Relationships
    - Service Orientation
    - Ethics: High ethical standards and a commitment to protecting the data of individuals and furthering MSF mandate.

## ***Conditions and Benefits:***

- **Job Location**: MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya).
- **Contract**: 1-year renewable full-time contract.
- **Start date**: As Soon As Possible.
- **Salary:** An annual salary of **EUR 27,145 at HQ Grade 8** based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
- **Work-life balance financial benefit;** ranging between **EUR 620 to 1,159/month** based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
- **Other benefits include;**
    - **Annual Leave:** 25 days of annual leave per year.
    - **Other Holidays:** sick leave, circumstantial leave, maternity leave (21 weeks), paternity leave (4 weeks), own affairs days off, etc.
    - **Employer Pension contribution**: 10% of basic salary:
    - **International insurance** for both medical and disability**.**
    - **Relocation support**; based on MSF EA terms/conditions.
    - **Work-life balance**: Daily flexi-hours and 2 days working from home possible.
    - **School fees benefits**: for eligible dependents, based on individual & administrative status.
    - **Diverse team composition**; Collaborate with a global network of talented professionals, bringing diverse perspectives and expertise from around the world.
    - **Career Development**: MSF provides many learning resources (online learning resources, regular trainings – including language, Peer to peer learning.
    - **Mobility**: You will have opportunities to travel abroad for work, meetings, trainings and workshops; giving you a chance to experience different cultures and broaden your professional network.
    - **Annual home leave ticket**: To be taken once every year for both staff and eligible dependents back to their home country for vacation. Only applicable to non-Kenyans and based on individual & administrative status.

**Annex 1-Terms of Reference: Mapping Barriers to Women’s Entry and Participation in the ECCD Workforce in Jordan, with a Focus on Refugee Women and Women with Disabilities**

**Terms of Reference**

**RFP\\JOR\\2026\\730**

**Background:**

Burden of Childcare Reduced and Addressed for Women in Jordan (BUCRA - meaning Tomorrow in Arabic) is a 5-year initiative (2024-2029) funded by Global Affairs Canada and designed to enhance the economic empowerment of women in Jordan. BUCRA takes a system approach that engages and supports local stakeholders from government, training bodies, the private sector and communities to drive gender-transformative change that addresses the most pressing childcare issues preventing women from participating and remaining in the workforce in Jordan. BUCRA targets over 8,600 women in 7 regions. The approach of equipping key stakeholders to address systemic barriers will enable the impacts to be experienced by women throughout Jordan over the long term.

In partnership with several local implementing partners including relevant government agencies, the Vocational Training Corporation (VTC) and the National Council of Family Affairs (NCFA) and civil society organization (Rayat Alyawm) under the umbrella of the Ministry of Social Development (MoSD). WUSC and partners will deliver under five key outcome areas: i) enhance the capacity of training providers to provide quality, market-relevant, and inclusive Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) training; ii) increase access by women to ECCD-related services to secure employment or start/expand their home-based nurseries; iii) improve capacity of key stakeholders to develop and implement gender-responsive policy and regulation fostering the availability of quality ECCD services; iv) improve attitudes among women and their communities about women's work and ECCD; and v) enhance the capacity of ECCD employers to provide quality, gender-responsive and inclusive ECCD services.

**Context:**

Women’s participation in the labour market in Jordan is influenced by a range of structural, institutional, economic, social, and cultural factors. While childcare is an important factor affecting women’s ability to enter and remain in the workforce, the Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) sector itself also represents an important area of employment and economic opportunity for women.

Women seeking to enter and participate in the ECCD workforce may face barriers related to policy and regulatory requirements, qualifications and training, recruitment and employment practices, working conditions, career progression, accessibility, transportation, and social and cultural norms etc.. These barriers may be particularly significant for refugee women and women with disabilities, who may face additional legal, institutional, accessibility, or social barriers.

While various studies and assessments in Jordan address women’s economic participation, gender norms, refugee employment, disability inclusion, and ECCD, there is a need to consolidate the existing evidence specifically on women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce and identify key research and knowledge gaps.

The consultancy will therefore map the existing evidence, identify key barriers and enabling factors, and highlight priorities for further research, policy and regulatory attention, advocacy, and programmatic action. The findings will also inform WUSC’s advocacy and policy dialogue with relevant policymakers and regulators.

#### **Purpose & scope of the Consultancy:**

The research aims to review and map existing studies and research on the key policy, regulatory, institutional, social, cultural, economic, accessibility, and other barriers affecting women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce in Jordan; identify what is currently known and where critical research and knowledge gaps remain, with particular attention to refugee women and women with disabilities; and highlight priority areas for further research, advocacy, policy, and programmatic action.

The findings will also provide an evidence base to inform WUSC’s advocacy and policy dialogue with relevant policymakers, regulators, and other stakeholders on barriers and potential actions to strengthen women’s participation in the ECCD workforce.

**Scope of Work:**

The consultant will be responsible for the following tasks:

- Develop a detailed inception plan and proposed research methodology for the assignment, including the analytical framework, research questions, data sources, consultation approach, tools, and timelines.
- Review and map existing research, studies, assessments, policies, laws, regulations, and available data relevant to women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce in Jordan.
- Build on relevant BUCRA research, including the In-Depth Needs Assessment on Guardian Engagement, Gender Norms, and Women’s Economic Opportunities and Right to Work in the ECCD Sector.
- Identify and analyse the key barriers affecting women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce, including policy, regulatory, institutional, social, cultural, economic, accessibility, and other relevant barriers.
- Examine barriers at different stages of women’s participation in the ECCD workforce, including entry and recruitment, access to training and qualifications, employment, retention, working conditions, professional development, and career progression, where evidence is available.
- Examine how these barriers may differ for different groups of women, with particular attention to refugee women, women with disabilities, and, where evidence is available, refugee women with disabilities.
- Identify what is currently known based on existing evidence and identify critical research, evidence, and knowledge gaps.
- Identify relevant enabling factors, promising practices, and existing approaches that may support women’s entry into and sustained participation in the ECCD workforce.
- Identify priority areas for further research, policy and regulatory attention, advocacy, and programmatic action.
- Generate practical, evidence-based recommendations that can support WUSC and relevant stakeholders in policy dialogue and advocacy with policymakers and regulators.
- Prepare a draft research report presenting the research findings, evidence and knowledge gaps, key barriers, and initial recommendations.
- Conduct a validation session with relevant stakeholders, as facilitated by the project team, to validate the draft findings, gather additional insights, and identify key issues and evidence gaps.
- Revise the draft research report based on feedback from the project team and relevant stakeholders.
- Finalize the research report based on feedback from WUSC and relevant stakeholders, ensuring clarity, coherence, an evidence-based approach, and usability for policy dialogue and advocacy purposes.
- Support the dissemination of the final research findings and recommendations through stakeholder presentations, as agreed with the project team.

**Deliverables:**

**Inception Report and Research Methodology**

- Detailed inception plan outlining the proposed research methodology, analytical framework, research questions, data sources, consultation approach, tools, approach, and timeline.

**Desk Review and Evidence Mapping**

- Comprehensive desk review and mapping of existing research and evidence on women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce in Jordan, including key barriers and enabling factors, with particular attention to refugee women and women with disabilities.
- Identification of what is currently known, critical research and knowledge gaps, priority issues, and areas requiring further research.

**Draft Research Report**

- Draft report presenting the research findings, key barriers and enabling factors affecting women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce (with particular attention to refugee women and women with disabilities), evidence and knowledge gaps, policy and regulatory issues, priority areas, and initial recommendations.

**Validation Session**

- Validation session with relevant stakeholders to present and validate the draft research findings, gather additional insights, and identify key issues and evidence gaps.

**Final Research Report and Recommendations**

- Final research report incorporating feedback from WUSC and relevant stakeholders following the validation session.
- Clear and actionable, evidence-based recommendations for further research, advocacy, policy and regulatory action, and programmatic action, with particular attention to issues that can inform engagement with policymakers and regulators.

**Research Dissemination**

- Stakeholder presentation and/or dissemination session to present the final research findings and recommendations, as agreed with the project team.

**Location:**

The consultant should be based in Jordan . Any travel cost related to the assignment should be included in the financial proposal.

**Qualification requirements of the Consultant:**

The consultant is expected to meet the following qualifications and competencies:

**Education**: The lead consultant should possess at least a Master's degree in Business Administration, International Development, Social Sciences, Education, Public Policy, Gender Studies, or a related field. A Bachelor's degree with extensive relevant experience may be considered.

**Experience**:

- Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in research, policy analysis, or program evaluation in the areas of women’s economic empowerment, ECCD, education, social development, gender, or related sectors.
- Demonstrated experience in working on projects related to the childcare sector, early childhood development, or social enterprises is highly desirable.
- Demonstrated experience working on inclusion of marginalized populations, with relevant expertise on children and youth, refugees, and persons with disabilities.
- Proven experience conducting policy, legal, regulatory, and institutional analysis, preferably within the education, ECCD, social protection, gender, or related sectors.
- Strong knowledge of the Jordanian ECCD context, including relevant policies, regulations, national strategies, institutional frameworks, and the broader ECCD ecosystem affecting women’s economic participation.
- Demonstrated experience engaging with government institutions, civil society organizations, service providers, NGOs, and development partners through consultations, interviews, focus groups, or other participatory research processes.
- Strong research and analytical experience, including evidence synthesis, identification of research and data gaps, and qualitative and/or quantitative research methods, with the ability to translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
- Fluency in Arabic and English both written and spoken.
