jobs.title: Epidemiologist - Training
jobs.body:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Public Health Division (PHD)** employs around 42 staff based in Noumea and Suva. It supports members in developing healthier Pacific Island people and communities. The primary focus of the division is to provide scientific and technical assistance and to support the implementation of plans and programmes in member countries and territories. The primary goal for all PHD activities is to promote population health and well-being, prevent diseases, restore and/or maintain health and reduce inequalities in health. PHD is primarily concerned with improving and protecting public (population) health, rather than individual treatment services.

The role – **Epidemiologist – Training** will strengthen and contribute to public health surveillance, preparedness and response and research in the Pacific Island Countries and Territories (PICTs) and the Pacific region. This is through strengthening capacity for coordinated regional surveillance, effective team management, administration and communication, enhancing evidence-based service delivery through research and strengthening national and regional preparedness and response to public health threats or events. This role will also work closely with Fiji National University and with other stakeholders in the delivery of the Strengthening Health Interventions in the Pacific - Data for Decision Making (SHIP-DDM) programme.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Strengthening capacity for coordinated regional surveillance**

- Form effective relationships with member countries and partner agencies in the implementation of the SHIP-DDM programme in the Pacific.
- Consult with crosscutting technical bodies within PHD and SPC to support the identified public health priorities in the SHIP-DDM course and develop joint approaches for action.
- Lead in developing capacity development plans for the implementation of SHIP-DDM in coordination with, or in consideration of, PHD and SPC’s programme activities, and the Pacific island countries and territories’ priorities.
- Support planning and scaling up training in field epidemiology including surveillance, outbreak investigations, and data use among PICT health professionals.

**Team management, administration and communications**

- Contribute to an environment that fosters effective and harmonious working relationships.
- Contribute to monitoring and evaluation of capacity development activities’ implementation.
- Provide technical inputs in the development of concept papers, protocols, and proposals.
- Contribute to programme, divisional and corporate meetings, publications and reports.

**Enhance evidence-based service delivery through research**

- Supervise the conduct of research activities as part of the output of SHIP-DDM programme including the PGDAE course.
- Document the results of research studies, and findings presented in appropriate medium and forums.
- Develop in-country capacity to systematically analyse health data to address specific health problems and use data for decision making and policy development.

**Strengthening preparedness and response to public health threats or events**

- Support the development and strengthening of in-country capacities in surveillance and response.
- Promote and increase harmonisation of surveillance activities across PHD and SPC, and at regional and national levels in PICTs.
- Strengthen surveillance and response capacity at regional and national levels through system improvements.
- Provide technical support for enhanced surveillance during mass gatherings and emergency response to public health events (if required).

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- MBBS and master’s degree in public health, epidemiology, or related discipline or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- 10 years of experience in public health surveillance, including communicable and non-communicable disease surveillance.
- Experience in outbreak preparedness and response.
- Experience in the provision of capacity building or on-the job training in field epidemiology.
- Experience in operational research and writing scientific reports and papers.
- Cross-cultural skills and ability to work with colleagues from different cultural backgrounds.
- Highly developed oral and interpersonal communication skills.
- Willingness to travel frequently (up to 30% of the time) in the Pacific region and internationally.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **3 years** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Epidemiologist – Training** is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 3,245‒4,057 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 10,028–12,535 (USD 4,349–5,436; EUR 3,924–4,905). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer, POWER Partnership
jobs.body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee helps people affected by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and regain control of their future. The Violence Prevention and Response Unit leads IRC's work across women's protection and empowerment, child protection, and protection and rule of law, positioning social work in crises as the connective practice across these areas.

POWER is a multi-country strategic partnership funded by Irish Aid, running from 2025 to 2027 across Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan. Its core logic is holistic gender-based violence prevention and response delivered through strengthened local women-led organizations, including partners such as SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya, with a quarter of country budgets channeled directly to local partners under a feminist partnership framework and the PEERS power-sharing principles. The program includes a dedicated advocacy pillar, an emergency response pillar, and a partnership learning pillar, and it works through practices such as women-led safety audits that already constitute community-generated risk analysis feeding into local advocacy and decision-making.

**Job overview**

The Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer coordinates quality and learning across the six POWER country programs. The role works through country WPE and program teams, POWER’s women-led and local partners, and the WPE Global Practice, and coordinates with the Award Management Unit (AMU), which leads the donor relationship with Irish Aid. It is accountable for technical quality assistance against IRC core WPE standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards for the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, and for tracking and reporting delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six countries so that deviation is identified early. The position contributes to the partnership’s advocacy pillar and to the design of the next partnership phase.

**Major responsibilities**

The role holds the technical quality of POWER delivery to IRC's WPE standards, keeps the partnership and the WPE Global Practice in two-way exchange ,rather than a one directional flow of standards downward, and tracks delivery across six countries against scope, timeline and budget so that deviation is flagged early enough for adaptive management

- Provide quality oversight across the six country programs, so that survivor-centered response, case management, women and girls' safe spaces, clinical and MHPSS referral pathways, and social norms work meet IRC WPE technical standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
- Serve as the connective role between the POWER partnership and the WPE Global Practice, translating core standards into partnership contexts and carrying partnership-generated practice back into the core.
- Support the sequencing of prevention and social norms activities to context, so they are introduced only where women-led community analysis confirms the preconditions for safe implementation are met.
- Maintain coherence of approach across the six countries without flattening contextual difference, identifying where a shared standard applies and where local adaptation is warranted.
- Track and report on delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six country programs, flagging deviation early enough for adaptive management rather than end-of-cycle correction.
- Ensure MEAL and program data feed directly into program adaptation, so that what the data shows changes what the program does, not only what it reports.
- Connect program data and implementation evidence to wider sector trends and debates, including comparable protection and GBV programming elsewhere.

**Learning, evidence, and the partnership learning agenda**

The role leads the program's learning function, treating implementation learning as a legitimate evidence pathway rather than a lesser substitute for external research. It also support the partnership’s advocacy pillar, so that evidence generated with the partners informs partners’ own advocacy and IRC’s policy positioning.

- Lead the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, coordinating cross-country learning cycles, documentation, and structured reflection between IRC and partners.
- Position women-led safety audits as community-generated risk analysis, and strengthen the pathway from that analysis into local decision-making and adaptive management.
- Build the program's evidence base on what enables and constrains change in protracted crisis settings, surfacing failure modes honestly, including referral systems that exist on paper but not in practice, and norms work that shifts survey scores without shifting community behavior.
- Ensure learning is co-owned with partners and feeds their own institutional positioning, not only IRC's reporting obligations.
- Steward the POWER advocacy pillar, supporting partners to carry community-generated analysis into local, national, and global advocacy where they hold standing in their own right.
- Work with advocacy and policy colleagues so the partnership's evidence informs IRC positioning toward donors, multilaterals, and normative bodies.

**Strengthening the core and surge capacity of women-led and local organizations**

The role supports partners on two distinct fronts, their institutional core and their capacity to surge in emergencies, resisting the pattern where localization language coexists with authority still held by the international actor.

- Support partner institutional strengthening across governance, financial systems, safeguarding, and MEAL in ways partners define and lead, consistent with the PEERS principles and the direct funding commitment.
- Strengthen partner surge and emergency response readiness under the emergency response pillar, so local organizations hold a credible role when crises escalate rather than being displaced by international surge.
- Advance the shift of analytical and decision-making authority toward partners with genuine institutional standing, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya, co-designing tools and thresholds with them rather than imposing them.
- Support the broader civil society and women's movement ecosystem the partnership connects to, recognizing partners as governance and coordination actors in their own right.

**Strategic focus on women and girls in conflict settings**

The role keeps women and girls in active conflict and protracted displacement at the center of the partnership, including where conflict-related sexual violence is a feature of the context.

- Ensure program design and adaptation are anchored in the realities faced by women and girls across the six contexts, several of which are shaped by active conflict and large-scale displacement.
- Support conflict-related sexual violence sensitive practice where relevant, including safe and consent-based documentation, clinical pathways, and Do No Harm decisions taken at closest proximity to violence, with pattern awareness fed upward.
- Keep adolescent girls visible as a distinct group rather than folded into a general women-and-girls category.

**Partnership and donor relationship management**

The role supports coherence of technical delivery across countries and reporting cycles, contributing technical content into the strategic relationship with Irish Aid, which AMU stewards and holds overall.

- Serve as a central program coordination point for the POWER partnership, supporting planning, adaptive management, amendments, and quality reporting to Irish Aid in coordination with the European DE & Frameworks team (Irish Aid).
- Feed technical content on program direction, learning, and strategic opportunities into AMU's communication with Irish Aid and the Department of Foreign Affairs. .
- Coordinate across the six country teams and the relevant IRC technical, advocacy, awards, and finance functions to keep the partnership coherent and its commitments met.
- Contribute technical input to AMU's design and negotiation of the next Strategic Partnership phase (post-2027), including program scope, theory of change, and the monitoring, evaluation and learning framework, coordinating input from WPE pillar leads, country teams, and partners, under AMU's overall lead on negotiation, timeline, and the donor relationship.

**Key working relationships**

**Works closely with:** AMU, Global and VPRU Advocacy; VPRU MEAL/METAL Unit.

Country WPE and program leads across the six POWER countries; POWER women-led and local partners, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya; IRC Awards Management Unit (AMU); VPRU Business Development; Irish Aid and Department of Foreign Affairs counterparts.

**Job requirements**

**Education:** Advanced degree in a relevant field such as social work, gender studies, international development, human rights, public health, or law, or an equivalent combination of qualification and experience.

**Work experience:** A minimum of 8 years professional experience in GBV, WPE, or protection programming in humanitarian and conflict-affected settings, at a technical lead level, including demonstrated experience in partnership and locally-led social action, in program quality or learning, and in program or grant management including budget oversight.

**Demonstrated skills and competencies:**

- Strong technical grounding in WPE practice and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
- Practical experience in feminist partnership and localization, including working with women-led organizations as partners rather than subgrantees.
- Learning and MEAL capability, with the judgment to treat implementation learning as evidence and to surface difficult findings.

jobs.title: National Technical Expert
jobs.body:
## **National Technical Experts in Eastern and Southern Africa (M/W)**

Departement Economie Durable et Inclusive - EDIN > Pôle Entreprenariat et Innovation  
Published on : 2026/08/25

**SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA BURUNDI**

### Mission description

Expertise France is launching a call for applications for the position of National Technical Experts (NTEs) to be based in the 3 potential countries of implementation of the SWITCH to Circular Economy in Eastern and Southern Africa (SWITCH 2 CE in ESA) Programme, namely: Burundi, Malawi and Mozambique,

These NTEs will support the implementation and success of the SWITCH-2-CE in ESA Project through the following thematic areas.

**ACTIVITY 1. Stakeholder Engagement and coordination**

I. Map and maintain relationships with key national stakeholders, including:

a. Relevant line ministries (e.g., Environment, Industry, Trade, Finance, SME Development) and RECs.

b. National development agencies, investment promotion authorities, and Environment Agencies.

c. Financial institutions (banks, micro-finance institutions, development banks) and Micro, Small and Medium Scale Enterprises involved in CE, in particular in the 2 Project Value chains.

d. Business Associations, CE Advocacy Associations, and CSOs involved in CE.

II. Support Project engagements with the stakeholders and facilitate implementation efforts.

**ACTIVITY 2. Enabling CE Policy Frameworks**

I. Act as the first point of contact for stakeholders in-country regarding Outcome 1

II. Policy Support Facility

a. Coordinate support efforts to beneficiaries of the Policy Support Facility.

b. Support efforts to raise awareness on the Policy Support Facility

III. Policy Dialogues

a. Support the implementation of national policy dialogues on CE

IV. Knowledge Production and dissemination on CE

a. Support Project efforts on knowledge production and dissemination activities relating to CE

**ACTIVITY 3. Matching Grant Facility (MGF)**

I. Act as the first point of contact for stakeholders in-country regarding the MGF

II. Assist in the identification and pre-screening of potential applicants for 3rd party organisations that would manage grants

III. Assist in the identification and pre-screening of BDS providers that would provide CE technical expertise to CE businesses.

IV. Facilitate outreach to local financial institutions.

V. Facilitate the outreach to potential eligible MSMEs that could benefit from the MGF

VI. Provide local insights and intelligence on financial ecosystem dynamics, MSME challenges, and enabling environment.

VII. Monitor in-country developments in circular economy and report on opportunities or risks for the MGF.

**ACTIVITY 4: Monitoring and Learning**

I. Produce periodic reports on Project activities and progress made in CE in the respective country.

II. Carry out monitoring activities and contribute to the collection and consolidation of M&E data to feed into project indicators and reporting requirements.

**Activity 5: General Support**

Provide general country support such as identifying local experts and supporting with local administrative processes.

### Project or context description

Expertise France and GIZ are jointly implementing the Switch to Circular Economy (SWITCH-2-CE in ESA) programme, funded by the European Union. The overall objectiveof the SWITCH-2-CE in ESA programme is to foster an inclusive transition to circular economy in East and Southern Africa (ESA). The programme seeks to contribute to the mitigation of climate change by promoting green and circular business models and strengthening the regulatory and policy framework for circular economy.

The SWITCH-2-CE in ESA Project would be implemented in 13 ESA countries, namely Angola, Botswana, Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia. The identification of these countries is provisional and may be further validated or adjusted based on the outcomes of the inception and analysis phase.

SWITCH-2-CE in ESA programme is structured around three main objectives (outcomes), with two priority value chains: “packaging/plastics waste” and “electronics/e-waste”. The three main objectives are:

· **Outcome 1:** Establish an enabling policy framework for circular economy across the ESA region.

*Under Outcome 1, the Project efforts will seek to improve access to resources on inclusive circular economy (CE) best practices by Policymakers, support integration of CE principles into policy frameworks and grow public sector capacity to support CE through Extended Producer Responsibility schemes.*

· **Outcome 2:** Enhance the participation of formal and informal workers and SMEs, including women and youth, in circular economy models.

*Under Outcome 2, the Project efforts will seek to support the integration of CE topics into Higher Education and TVET with gender-sensitive approaches, improve the availability of inclusive CE training to women, youth, and informal workers, and improve firm’s access to CE knowledge and best practice materials across the region.*

· **Outcome 3:** Improve access to and use of financing by circular economy businesses.

*Under Outcome 3, the Project efforts will seek to improve access to financial services to CE start-ups and SMEs, especially those led by youth and women, and improving availability of incubation and advisory support for business planning, financial readiness, and technology development.*

*The MGF will be implemented via third-party organisations, which will be responsible for co-selecting and disbursing grants to eligible businesses operating within the two targeted value chains.*

***Structure of the MGF:** Expertise France → Third-party organizations → Final beneficiaries (MSMEs & start-ups)*

In terms of definitions, **E-waste** encompasses discarded electrical and electronic equipment with a plug or battery, including items like smartphones, laptops, televisions, refrigerators, and small household appliances. **Plastic packaging** includes plastic materials used to contain, protect, handle, or deliver products, such as bottles, containers, wrappers, films, and single-use plastics like bags, straws, and takeaway food packaging.

### Required profile

- At least 5 years’ experience in stakeholder mobilisation, coordination or policy advocacy preferably in sustainable development, private sector development or green economy.
- Advanced University degree in economics, business administration, environment or related fields.
- Strong knowledge of national economic, financial, and environmental policy landscape.
- Proven track record of engaging with government ministries, RECs, private sector actors, and development partners.
- Proven experience working in supporting the private sector and knowledge of the MSME support ecosystem is a strong advantage.
- Familiarity with circular economy concepts and green financing mechanisms is an added advantage.
- Individual with strong networks and a solid understanding of their national circular economy landscape
- Ability to work independently and remotely, with strong organizational skills.
- Nationality or proven professional expertise in one of the 13 target countries
- Excellent communication, facilitation, and reporting skills.
- Language: English and Portuguese in the case of Mozambique

### Additional information

**Documentation to Be Submitted**

· CV (Focused on relevant experiences, not more than 2 pages)

· A brief technical proposal (2-3 pages max). The technical proposal should explain how the consultant will meet requirements (addressing Chapter “Assignment” of this ToR), specifying particularly which actors they can mobilize and how they plan to reach out to them.

· Explicitly state which country you are applying to be focal point for in the technical proposal.

**Accountability and Oversight**

The NTE will report to the SWITCH-2-CE Project Co-Lead or the designated officer.

**Nature of the contract and duration**

· Individual consultancy framework contract with purchase orders

· 40 months contract (expected start date – January 2026)

· Approximately 30 to 60 days per year subject to demand.

**Compensation**

· Daily fees will be assessed based on qualifications, level of expertise, and the applicant’s financial offer

jobs.title: Burundi Recruitment Intern
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## About the Young Professionals Program

One Acre Fund’s Young Professionals Program offers high-performing African graduates meaningful internships and training opportunities at a high-performing, mission-driven organization. Our internships are paid and all interns can expect to receive substantive work assignments working on high-impact projects that support One Acre Fund's operations.

When joining, interns will participate in an onboarding program and receive training on how to design and execute projects. Over the period of your internship, you will get the opportunity to work with like-minded individuals and receive learning opportunities to build strong foundations for your future career.

## About the Role

You will provide support to all departments within the Burundi Program in carrying out recruitment activities for all junior-level positions. You will also handle administrative tasks and support Global Recruitment on a need basis.

## Responsibilities

Direct ownership of 10 - 12 pipelines

- Manage the recruitment process for all junior-level positions, from the application stage through to the offer stage.
- Review CVs and conduct phone interviews in French or English.
- Ensure timely posting of job openings both internally and externally; proactively collaborate with job posting agencies.
- Edit and format job descriptions to ensure clarity and consistency.
- Organize data and manage all communications within the electronic applicant tracking system (Greenhouse).
- Maintain and regularly update the recruitment tracker (for new and closed positions) to support timely reporting to the hiring commission.
- Identify and manage small-scale process improvement projects.
- Collaborate effectively with the Corporate Operations department to coordinate logistics for final interviews and ensure candidates have a positive experience throughout the recruitment process.
- Manage the Burundi Recruitment email inbox used for receiving applications for certain junior-level positions:
    1. Respond to candidate inquiries.
    2. Import candidate files into the electronic applicant tracking system (Greenhouse).

Global Recruitment Team support

- Provide support to the global recruitment team with any additional tasks related to daily recruitment operations, as delegated by the manager.

Other duties: As requested by your manager to advance our mission

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we deeply invest in our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training, and regular feedback on your performance. We’ll hold career reviews every one-three months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and gain rewarding technical experience.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- A Bachelor's degree in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Communications, or a related field.
- Must be a Burundian national.
- Language proficiency: English (required), French (required), Kirundi (preferred).

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Bujumbura, Burundi

## Benefits

Interns will be provided with a reasonable stipend for the duration of their contract. Rural area based fellows will be provided assistance in locating suitable housing.

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Burundi.

## Application Deadline

11 December 2026. We hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Mental health and psychosocial suppport coordinator (F/M) - Yemen
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## **MdM in Yemen**

Yemen remains one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises, after more than a decade of conflict, economic decline, climate shocks, and political instability. In 2026, over two-thirds of the population require humanitarian assistance, including 9.4 million people identified as most in need of life-saving support.

The health system is under extreme strain, with only 59.3% of health facilities fully operational and 19.3 million people requiring healthcare services, including more than 660,000 pregnant women in need of urgent care. Cholera continues to pose a major public health challenge, adding pressure to an already weakened system.

The operational environment remains highly volatile, marked by security incidents, service disruptions, funding cuts, and economic challenges that regularly affect humanitarian activities.

Médecins du Monde operates across northern and southern Yemen, with a coordination office in Sana’a and field offices in Aden and Marib. Its interventions focus on two strategic priorities:

- Supporting 29 health facilities to deliver primary healthcare services, including outpatient care, vaccination, nutrition, and reproductive health.
- Providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through healthcare facilities and community-based networks trained in identification, referral, and awareness-raising activities.

## **About the role**

As MHPSS coordinator you will be in charge of overseeing all MdM’s MHPSS programming for the Yemen mission. You will contribute to proposal writing and development of new projects or concepts as per MdM’s mandate. You will also take part in the country strategy elaboration for the MHPSS sector, led by the general coordinator.

## **Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the general coordinator and in close collaboration with the mental health advisor, you will provide technical leadership and functional management to the MHPSS Officers based in Sana’a, Aden and Marib.

Working closely with other MdM departments, local NGO partners and focal points within the Ministry of Public Health and Population (MoPHP), you will support the implementation, coordination and monitoring of activities aimed at integrating Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) components across MdM programmes.

## **What you’ll do**

? **MHPSS programme development and management**

- Lead the development, implementation and monitoring of the country MHPSS strategy and programme
- Ensure MHPSS activities are integrated into MdM-supported primary health care services and delivered in line with gender-sensitive and empowerment approaches
- Guarantee compliance with MdM and international MHPSS standards, and contribute to the development and review of training materials, SOPs, guidelines and reports in collaboration with the MHPSS Advisor
- Strengthen MHPSS referral pathways with partners and service providers, and support the mapping of needs, assessments and programme design to address identified gaps
- Ensure services remain culturally appropriate, responsive to changing contexts and emerging needs, and delivered according to quality standards
- Monitor programme implementation, budget utilisation and community-based MHPSS interventions

? **Capacity building and technical support**

- Participate in the recruitment, induction and onboarding of MHPSS staff, ensuring adequate orientation to MdM's MHPSS framework and tools
- Provide technical supervision and day-to-day support to MHPSS teams, including field-based officers, while contributing to performance management and staff development
- Develop and deliver capacity-building initiatives, including Training of Trainers (ToT) programmes on PFA, PM+ and other relevant MHPSS approaches
- Support the rollout of trainings for national staff and promote the integration of MHPSS standards across MdM teams

? **Coordination and representation**

- Foster close collaboration with health, protection and support teams to ensure integrated programme implementation
- Coordinate with local authorities, NGO partners, UN agencies and other stakeholders involved in MHPSS interventions within MdM areas of operation
- Represent MdM in relevant MHPSS coordination forums and technical working groups, contributing to information sharing, referral mechanisms, advocacy efforts and the promotion of good practices

? **Monitoring, reporting and evaluation**

- Oversee monitoring, evaluation and learning processes for MHPSS activities, including the development of tools, data collection and analysis
- Ensure regular review of programme performance and recommend corrective actions when required
- Act as the focal point for MHPSS reporting and contribute to donor reports, proposal development and fundraising efforts

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you...**

- Hold a Master's degree in Psychology, Social Work, Public Health or a related field, complemented by training in MHPSS and project management
- Have proven experience managing MHPSS programmes in humanitarian settings, including programme design, quality assurance, monitoring and donor reporting
- Are confident integrating MHPSS into primary health care services and have a solid understanding of IASC and WHO MHPSS frameworks and interventions
- Can lead and support multidisciplinary teams, providing technical guidance, building capacities and fostering collaboration across locations and departments
- Are comfortable working with donors and budgets, and have experience developing proposals, reports and funding opportunities
- Excel at coordination and representation, building constructive relationships with authorities, partners, UN agencies and other stakeholders
- Combine strategic thinking with strong organisational skills, enabling you to adapt programmes to evolving humanitarian contexts and changing needs
- Communicate fluently in English, both verbally and in writing; knowledge of Arabic and experience in Yemen would be strong assets

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Prefer working in highly predictable environments rather than responding to evolving humanitarian needs and priorities
- Are not comfortable balancing strategic leadership with hands-on technical support to field teams
- Find stakeholder engagement, coordination forums or external representation challenging
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 392 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting in January 2027
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Sanaa but may be temporarily based in Aden depending on the security situation
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are offically recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Employment Specialist
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:**

The Employment Specialist helps newly arrived refugee clients achieve self-sufficiency through employment. This role delivers job readiness services, career coaching, and employer connections while supporting clients through the application and placement process. The Specialist maintains strong relationships with local employers, coordinates with other IRC staff, and ensures compliance with donor and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake and assessment for employment-eligible clients and develop individualized employment plans.
- Deliver job readiness orientations in both group and one-on-one settings, focusing on essential skills for employability.
- Cultivate and maintain relationships with area employers to identify appropriate opportunities for clients.
- Match clients to employment opportunities and guide them through applications, interviews, and hiring processes.
- Monitor job placements, wages, and satisfaction of both clients and employers, providing post-placement support.
- Assist clients with Unemployment Insurance applications and weekly claims when applicable.
- Maintain accurate case notes and data entry in required systems; prepare employment vouchers and other documentation.
- Participate in program meetings, trainings, and professional development activities; follow all IRC policies including safeguarding and confidentiality standards.
- Perform other related duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, workforce development, or related field strongly preferred; equivalent work experience may be considered.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years of case management, employment, job placement, or business experience in a social services setting.
- Experience working with vulnerable or underserved populations strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of U.S. job search process and ability to coach clients through securing employment.
- Strong organizational and time-management skills; detail-oriented.
- Computer proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams).
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills; public speaking/presentation skills preferred.
- Proven ability to problem-solve, prioritize tasks, and meet goals independently or as part of a team.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Program Support Director - Francophone & Lusophone Africa
jobs.body:
This position is 100% remote. Candidates may work remotely from any of the following countries: Burundi, Chad, Benin, Madagascar, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa, and Zambia. Candidates in West Africa are preferred.

The Program Support Director (PSD) is a senior leadership position within Ipas’s Global Program Support Team. The PSD serves as strategic thought partner to the Regional Directors (RDs), Country Directors (CDs) and other leaders across the Ipas network, helping strengthen organizational effectiveness, program quality, risk management and leadership capacity. The PSD provides strategic leadership, technical guidance, and operational oversight to 4–5 regional or country programs. This role supervises 3-5 direct reports which include CDs and RDs as well as Senior Program Managers (SPMs), who are part of the global Program Support Team. Reporting to the Deputy Chief Operating Officer (DCOO), the PSD ensures alignment with Ipas strategy and quality standards, donor and award compliance, and risk mitigation. The PSD serves as a bridge between Ipas global teams and regional / country offices, promoting cross learning and providing supportive supervision and thought partnership to country team leaders.

The PSD will bring significant team and program leadership experience, cross cultural knowledge, relevant language skills, a focus on user-centered approaches, and a dedication to shared leadership. The job responsibilities include working collaboratively with country program staff to ensure strong program results and strong project and risk management. The PSD provides high level stewardship and serve an “internal control” function with assigned regional and country programs, to ensure compliance with Ipas’s quality standards and as a steward of the Ipas’s global reputation. The position contributes significantly to addressing programmatic challenges and problem solving; ensuring we achieve desired goals, donor satisfaction and compliance with award terms and conditions, strengthening systems to improve value for money, organizational learning; and promoting a positive and empowering work culture.

The PSD has a strong commitment to reproductive justice and Ipas’s mission. Demonstrates a strong commitment to the individuals and communities we serve, acting with a sense of urgency and providing candid timely support and guidance to their team and peers.

Job Description

## **Primary Responsibilities:**

## Strategic Leadership

- Partner with regional and country leadership to advance organizational priorities, strengthen strategic decision-making, and promote alignment with Ipas's mission, values, strategic framework, global standards, policies and shared leadership practices.
- Support leaders in monitoring organizational, programmatic, and financial performance and in addressing emerging challenges, risks, and opportunities
- Participate in global strategic initiatives and other organizational development efforts to strengthen the Ipas Network, such as global strategic planning, expanding implementation of shared leadership practices and risk management.
- Represent Ipas on national or regional Boards of Directors, as needed.
- Support and provide thought leadership to regional and country leadership in translating organizational strategy into high-quality, contextually relevant program strategies.

## Program Quality, Stewardship and Support

- Provide high-level strategic inputs and assistance in project and program management with a focus on addressing challenges and problem solving with assigned regional and country teams.
- Facilitate periodic reviews with country and regional leaders to strengthen compliance, program quality, organizational learning, and accountability towards Ipas policies and quality standards, donor requirements, local laws and regulations, and standard accounting and business practices.
- Lead or support special assessments or learning initiatives, as needed.

## Regional and Country Program Support

- Serve as a trusted advisor to RDs and CDs, supporting leadership effectiveness, adaptive management, and cross-organizational collaboration
- Provide supportive supervision and thought partnership with RDs and CDs.
- Promote strong communication, collaboration, and cross learning among Ipas network technical and support units, and other country programs to strengthen programmatic and operational results.
- Support RDs, CDs and SPMs in addressing implementation challenges, risk management, and adaptive programming.
- Contribute to developing/updating and implementing strong regional/country strategic plans as requested, ensuring alignment with the Ipas mission and strategic framework.
- Provide coaching and support to RDs and CDs in recruiting and developing a high functioning team that practices shared leadership and maintains a positive and effective work culture.
- Provide strategic input on annual work plans, annual operating budgets, reports, and high-priority deliverables, as requested and needed.
- Oversee the strengthening of a variety of mechanisms to support a positive and effective work culture, organizational learning, sharing, and peer support across teams.
- Support start-up, scale-up, and close-out of country programs.

## Staff Management & Capacity Strengthening

- Foster a culture of shared leadership, accountability, learning, trust, and inclusion by empowering staff to contribute expertise, exercise leadership, and make informed decisions appropriate to their roles.
- Provide supportive supervision and manage the performance of direct reports, including RDs, CDs and Program Support Team staff.
- Support capacity strengthening of regional/country teams in program management, donor compliance and risk management.
- Promote organizational training and other capacity strengthening efforts as needed.

## Donor Engagement & Compliance

- Support RDs and CDs in managing complex donor-funded portfolios by strengthening systems, decision-making, compliance practices, and cross-node coordination.
- Ensure programs comply with donor requirements and organizational policies.
- Contribute to resource mobilization efforts by contributing to proposal development, donor briefings, and strategic partnerships as requested and needed.
- Work with program leaders to ensure that new business efforts and proposals are aligned with the country/region’s strategic plan, Ipas strategic framework, technical excellence and innovation, good stewardship of funding, and optimal cost recovery.
- Represent Ipas in donor meetings, technical forums, and external engagements as required.

## Risk Management & Safeguarding

- Ensure timely identification and mitigation of programmatic, operational, and reputational risks, working with country/regional program leaders.
- Promote safeguarding, protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), and ethical programming across all supported programs.
- Conduct regular reviews and work with country / regional leaders to ensure adherence with organizational policies on safeguarding, gender equality, and inclusion.
- Guard Ipas interests and reputation through oversight on adherence to policies, performance against the annual operating budget, addressing audit findings and ethical issues, and compliance with donor requirements.
- Work closely with regional and country leaders and other Ipas units to ensure adequate internal controls to reduce the risk of fraud and mismanagement of funds;
- Play an internal control function where needed, such as to reduce perceived or actual conflicts of interest.

## Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning & Accountability (MEL)

- Promote strong monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning practices across assigned regional and country programs.
- Support the use of data for decision-making, learning, and program improvement.
- Encourage documentation of best practices, innovations, and lessons learned across all projects.

Minimum Requirements:

## Essential

- Commitment to sexual and reproductive health and rights, especially safe abortion and access to contraception, and an understanding of principles, policies, and best practices related to sexual and reproductive health, and related intersectionalities.
- Knowledge of the issues and context of women's sexual and reproductive health and rights in the Africa region, including demonstrated experience working with NGOs in Africa, preferably having worked in an Ipas implementing country in the West Africa region.
- Demonstrated commitment to shared leadership principles, with experience fostering distributed leadership, collaboration, accountability, and trust across geographically dispersed teams
- Proven ability to lead and motivate teams and create a positive work environment through supportive supervision, strong communication and teamwork, and shared leadership approaches, including demonstrated successes in program management, team leadership, strategic planning and problem solving.
- Proven ability to build and maintain positive working relationships with a variety of partners, including government officials, regional or global donors and partner organizations.
- Ability to work across cultures and manage complex relationships remotely.

## Minimum

- At least 15 years of increasing responsibility in non-profit leadership and program management in the international development or NGO-sector.
- Minimum of 7 years of senior program leadership experience overseeing multiple country programs and proven ability to provide strategic and technical leadership across diverse country contexts.
- Strong experience managing donor-funded programs (e.g., bilateral, multilateral, foundations) including budgetary management.
- Demonstrated experience supporting organizational risk management, compliance monitoring, and implementation of internal control systems
- Relevant post-graduate degree (e.g., MBA, MIA, MPH).
- Respect and credibility as an advocate for reproductive health and rights
- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
- Fluency in French required. Knowledge of Portuguese will be an added advantage and of other local languages will be an asset.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, SharePoint, etc.

Travel Requirements:

Estimated 20%-25\*\*%\*\* time travel to regional and country programs and regional/global meetings.

Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employee's country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise.

jobs.title: US Response Team Lead - Emergency Response Roster
jobs.body:
- **Job Purpose**
    
    CORE (Community Organized Relief Effort) is a crisis response organization that brings immediate aid and recovery to underserved communities across the globe. Our mission is simple: save lives and strengthen communities impacted by or vulnerable to crisis. Wherever the crisis is and whenever people are in need, we are there. CORE’s ability to impact communities is directly emboldened by each member of our staff and leadership.
    
    We are seeking experienced and mission-driven Response Team Leads to join our emergency response roster for limited-term deployments within the United States. This role leads CORE's response operations on the ground while serving as a key relationship builder — cultivating and managing institutional partnerships with emergency management agencies, VOAD networks, local governments, and community-based organizations. The Team Lead oversees site functions and programmatic teams (such as distribution, home repair, community hubs, or resource navigation), executes CORE's response strategy, and helps position CORE for funding and partnership opportunities across the domestic disaster landscape.
    
    The Team Lead acts as CORE's primary field leader and external representative, responsible for coordination, safety, quality control, and effective communication across all functions. They serve as the primary point of contact for government agencies, VOAD and coalition partners, local implementing partners, support agencies, and internal leadership throughout the response. This position requires exceptional leadership and relationship-building skills, decisiveness, and the ability to adapt under rapidly evolving conditions.
    
    **Roster work is available on an as-needed basis (it is not full-time or continuous).**
    
    Roster members may be activated based on needs arising from emergencies and must be prepared for rapid deployment, sometimes on short notice, for durations ranging from 2 to 10 weeks.
    
    Main Responsibilities
    
    **Institutional Partnerships and Relationship Building**
    
    
    - Serve as CORE's primary relationship holder with government emergency management agencies at the federal, state, and local levels (FEMA, state EMAs, county/municipal emergency management), building trust and positioning CORE as a go-to response partner.
    - Develop and sustain active membership and engagement with **VOAD networks** (National VOAD and relevant State VOADs) and other disaster coalitions, representing CORE in member meetings, committees, and working groups.
    - Cultivate partnerships with local governments, community-based organizations, faith-based networks, long-term recovery groups, and other implementing partners to expand CORE's reach and access.
    - Establish CORE's presence and credibility in new response geographies by proactively connecting with local and regional stakeholders ahead of and during deployments.
    - Represent CORE in EMA-led coordination structures, ESF (Emergency Support Function) briefings, and multi-agency coordination calls.
    
    **Funding and Business Development**
    
    
    - Identify, track, and pursue funding opportunities relevant to US disaster response, including government grants, foundation funding, and private donor opportunities.
    - Build relationships with institutional donors and funders active in the domestic disaster space, positioning CORE for both rapid-response and longer-term recovery funding.
    - Support the development of concept notes, proposals, and letters of intent in coordination with CORE's Development and Partnerships teams.
    - Monitor the funding landscape and flag emerging opportunities tied to declared disasters, anticipatory action, and recovery programming.
    
    **Project Leadership and Implementation**
    
    
    - Oversee the planning, execution, and real-time adjustment of emergency response programs, including but not limited to tarping, home repair, debris removal, WASH, case management, relief distributions, infrastructure repair, and community engagement.
    - Lead rapid and ongoing needs assessments to inform program strategy and prioritize interventions.
    - Ensure program activities are grounded in contextual analysis, community feedback, and operational feasibility.
    
    **Deployment and Operational Oversight**
    
    
    - Serve as CORE's senior-most representative in the field, providing strategic and operational leadership across all scopes of work.
    - Ensure quality, safety, and accountability standards are upheld across all response activities.
    - Represent CORE in coordination meetings with government agencies, humanitarian actors, and local partners.
    - Ensure compliance with internal protocols, donor requirements, and humanitarian standards.
    
    **Interdepartmental Coordination**
    
    
    - Facilitate coordination between field operations and HQ departments including Communications, Partnerships, Development, Finance, and Logistics.
    - Ensure timely flow of accurate data, narrative updates, and documentation for internal and external stakeholders.
    
    **Team Supervision and Training**
    
    
    - Supervise and support field-based staff, roster members, and volunteers across programmatic and operational roles.
    - Lead onboarding, mentoring, and just-in-time training for incoming team members.
    - Support the adaptation and dissemination of SOPs, assessment tools, and training materials specific to the deployment context.
    - Promote a culture of safety, inclusivity, and continuous learning among field teams.
    
    **Administrative and Reporting Duties**
    
    
    - Ensure accurate tracking of project outputs, deliverables, and key performance indicators.
    - Contribute to donor and HQ reporting, including situation reports, lessons learned, and end-of-deployment summaries.
    - Support documentation of program impact, gaps, and recommendations to inform transition to recovery and long-term programming.
    
    Scope and Travel
    
    
    - Supervises: Program Managers, Program Coordinators, Roster members, local hires, and/or volunteers assigned to specific projects
    - Travel nationwide to U.S.-based emergencies as assigned
    - Called upon with short notice for deployments of 2-12 weeks as needed
- Requirements
    - Relevant experience in emergency response, humanitarian aid, community development, or related fields.
    - A bachelor's degree is welcomed but not required—equivalent experience, including lived or professional experience in disaster-affected communities or crisis settings, is strongly valued.
    - Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage projects, and work across diverse communities and partners during emergency or high-pressure situations.
    - Commitment to CORE's mission and a strong understanding of the challenges faced by underserved or crisis-impacted populations.
    - Proven experience in US emergency operations or volunteer management.
    - Excellent communication and coordination abilities, with experience working across multiple departments and teams.
    - Flexibility to deploy to various locations in response to disasters and humanitarian crises.
    - Minimum 3 years of professional experience in US emergency response, humanitarian aid, or related program implementation.
    - Prior experience leading teams or managing response projects in humanitarian contexts.
    - Familiarity with construction, distribution, CVA, or other sectoral experience is a plus.
    - Valid Driver’s License and clean driving history
    - Spanish or other secondary language proficiency preferred

jobs.title: Tupande Cashew Extension & Aggregation Officer (Fixed-term)
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## About the Role

Seeking a hands-on Extension and Aggregation Officer to run a cashew buying centre and aggregate raw cashew nuts on Kenya's coast — building market access opportunities for smallholder farmers in a scaling program.

## Responsibilities

Manage the buying center:

- Operate it during scheduled hours.
- Keep it clean, organised, and secure.
- Handle, dry, and store RCN according to Tupande standard operating procedures.

Aggregate accurately and with integrity:

- Weigh RCN accurately.
- Quality control each purchase (sorting damaged, moldy, or poor-quality nuts).
- Process payments via FieldPro and ensure compliance (i.e., KRA/eTIMS).
- Escalate any disputes, discrepancies, or irregularities to your Supervisor immediately.

Support farmers in the field:

- Deliver agronomic training to farmers in your assigned location.
- Communicate purchase and quality requirements.
- Executive field visits and prepare field reports for your Supervisor.
- Coordinate with Tupande Agents and Zone Supervisors to mobilize farmers.

Collect accurate data:

- Interview farmers and brokers.
- Record data on time using provided digital tools (i.e., stock take, farmer/broker scouting).
- Escalate any data-quality issues to your Supervisor.

Coordinate logistics:

- Work with loaders, Tupande’s logistics team, and your Supervisor to schedule and execute RCN collection.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You'll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You'll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Required:

- Demonstrable prior experience with an agricultural, aggregation, trading, or comparable operations employer (verifiable references or employment record).
- Ability to read and write in English/local language and perform basic arithmetic.
- Demonstrated integrity and accountability in handling agricultural goods, weighing, and record-keeping.
- Fluency in Kiswahili and familiarity with local coastal language(s).
- Computer literacy and comfortable with tablet/smartphone data-collection tools.
- High attention to detail in quality control, record-keeping, and payment processing.
- Independent, proactive, problem-solving - comfortable operating with limited daily supervision.
- Willingness and ability to travel across the assigned area, and to do hands-on RCN handling.
- Strong connection to the local farming community

Nice to have:

- Prior experience in Cashew and/or the Coast
- Prior experience operating a buying or collection center
- Familiarity with Tupande

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Lamu, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Contract Duration

8 months

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

10 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization's mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Medical coordinator (F/M) - Yemen
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Yemen**

Yemen remains one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises, after more than a decade of conflict, economic decline, climate shocks, and political instability. In 2026, over two-thirds of the population require humanitarian assistance, including 9.4 million people identified as most in need of life-saving support.

The health system is under extreme strain, with only 59.3% of health facilities fully operational and 19.3 million people requiring healthcare services, including more than 660,000 pregnant women in need of urgent care. Cholera continues to pose a major public health challenge, adding pressure to an already weakened system.

The operational environment remains highly volatile, marked by security incidents, service disruptions, funding cuts, and economic challenges that regularly affect humanitarian activities.

Médecins du Monde operates across northern and southern Yemen, with a coordination office in Sana’a and field offices in Aden and Marib. Its interventions focus on two strategic priorities:

- Supporting 29 health facilities to deliver primary healthcare services, including outpatient care, vaccination, nutrition, and reproductive health.
- Providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through healthcare facilities and community-based networks trained in identification, referral, and awareness-raising activities.

**About the role**

You will be responsible for designing, implementing, adapting and reporting the quality medical program activities for the Yemen mission. You will ensure the relevance and quality delivery of all medical activities, and practices, with a particular focus on health data analysis. You are the technical supervisor for the medical team (MdM or implementing partners) within the mission.

You will take part in the country strategy elaboration for the medical sector led by the general coordinator.

**Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the General coordinator, you will work alongside the deputy general coordinator, the HQ desk officer, the HQ medical, mental health, and protection advisors/referents. You will be the technical supervisor for the medical team: health activity managers, Marib medical supervisor and pharmacy advisor.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the General coordinator, your main responsibilities are the following:

- Participate in the definition of the country strategy led by the general coordinator and drive the medical and technical aspects in the development of this strategy
- Design, plan, implement, adapt and monitor the programme’s health activities
- Ensure the quality and relevance of health activities, supervise the collection and analysis of medical data
- Recruit, manage, train, and motivate the medical team
- Ensure the management of pharmaceutical products
- Carry out health needs assessments and evaluations of medical partners
- Cooperate with the administration team regarding budgeting and supervise the medical purchase process
- Represent MdM with authorities, partners and other NGOs on health issues
- Participate in the writing of proposals and reports

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you...**

- Hold an MD qualification or an advanced degree in Public Health, Nursing, Midwifery, or another relevant health discipline. Additional training in public health, epidemiology, project management, or humanitarian programme management is a strong asset
- Have proven experience in humanitarian and/or development contexts, with at least 2 years in a similar role involving programme development, proposal writing, donor reporting, budget management, and donor compliance
- Demonstrate strong technical knowledge in nutrition and sexual and reproductive health and rights, combined with a solid understanding of results-based management approaches, logical frameworks, and strategic planning
- Are skilled in developing high-quality funding proposals, technical reports, and impact narratives in English, and have experience working with institutional donors and multi-donor funding mechanisms
- Combine strong analytical, organisational, and coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, work autonomously, build capacity within teams, and collaborate effectively in multicultural environments
- Speak English fluently. Arabic is highly appreciated.

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Are uncomfortable working in complex, unstable, or rapidly evolving humanitarian contexts that require flexibility, resilience, and adaptability
- Prefer close supervision and highly structured processes rather than taking initiative, anticipating needs, and working independently
- Do not have strong written English skills or experience producing donor proposals, narrative reports, and other high-quality programme documentation
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. Seeking a procurement professional to lead fertilizer procurement, ensuring cost-efficient sourcing and reliable on-time delivery. Drive strong individual execution and contribute to team success. In this role, your focus will be dedicated to deep-dive data analysis to determine optimal purchasing windows, and managing and executing the entire procurement process independently.

## **Responsibilities**

Execute Procurement with Excellence

- Strategy & Delivery: Support the creation and execution of seasonal procurement strategies to deliver +90% OTIF (On-Time, In-Full) delivery, market-competitive costs, and 5% year-on-year cost savings.
- Quality Assurance: Ensure absolute quality control, achieving 0 quality issues reaching the farmer, and maintain an +80% on-time payment rate for suppliers.
- Supply Chain Reliability: Proactively address future supply gaps by evaluating farmer needs against global market trends, supplier capacity, and current inventory levels.
- Process Optimization: Drive lead-time improvements through streamlined delivery and process automation. Regularly improve key operations like the goods receipt process and loading quality control.
- Data & Analytics: Spend time developing, maintaining, and continuously improving complex Google Sheets data models to track global market trends and landed costs. Use this data to provide crucial decision support on when to purchase (or not purchase) fertilizers to maximize cost savings.

Build Partnerships & Market Liaisons

- Strategic Relationships: Help build and maintain deep partnerships with fertilizer suppliers and industry organizations beyond seasonal procurement needs.
- Country Team Collaboration: Act as a critical business partner for our country operations teams, actively identifying and sharing opportunities to improve our offering to farmers.
- Industry Representation: Serve as a representative for One Acre Fund externally with suppliers and market actors to drive long-term, systematic supply chain improvements.

People Management

- People Management: Manage and mentor a small team, setting clear goals, providing timely feedback, and conducting high-quality career coaching and performance reviews.
- Team Growth:Contribute to staffing, recruitment, and succession planning to build a high-performing procurement unit.

- Supply Chain Expertise: Solid foundational knowledge of global procurement processes, international shipping, and supply chain operations.
- Data Fluency: An advanced analytical mindset with high proficiency in Google Sheets to build pricing, forecasting, and decision-support models. Comfortable spending half of your time analyzing data to help make decisions.
- Language: Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Management & Execution Skills:

- Relationship Builder: Exceptional collaboration and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence both internal stakeholders and external global suppliers.
- Project Management: Strong organizational skills with a proven track record of managing multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
- Solution-Oriented: An innovative thinker who approaches obstacles with a results-driven mindset and is comfortable making data-driven decisions under medium-risk conditions.
