jobs.title: Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment
jobs.body:
Terms of reference (TOR)

Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment

UGANDA & KENYA

· Project: Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP)

· Procuring Organisation: IsraAID

· Contract Type: Consultancy

· Contract Period: October 2026 to December 2026, 75 days (Phased implementation)

· Target Start Date: Tentatively 26/10/2026

· Application Deadline: 23/10/2026

· Submission Method: EMAIL – see 'how to apply'

BACKGROUND

IsraAID is an International Humanitarian Non-Governmental Organization founded in 2001 and headquartered in Israel. It supports people and communities affected by humanitarian crises, combining rapid emergency response with longer-term recovery, resilience, and preparedness. Over the years, IsraAID has worked in more than 60 countries, responding to disasters, displacement, epidemics, and other crises. Its mission is centered on partnering closely with local communities to provide urgent assistance while helping them rebuild and strengthen their resilience to future shocks.

IsraAID is implementing a project titled Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement in Uganda and in Kakuma Refugee Camp in Kenya. The programme intends to improve health outcomes and reduce morbidity and mortality associated with malnutrition in vulnerable communities participating in the Program. ICNMP is designed as a regional initiative that responds to acute and chronic nutrition needs across East Africa, beginning its phase zero in Q2 of 2026, and actual implementation in September 2026. Although the immediate program launch focuses on Uganda and the emergency phase in Kenya, early 2027 will see Kenya incorporating the full package while the broader intention is to establish a model that can later expand to South Sudan as funding becomes available. The regional framing is essential, as the scale of displacement, vulnerability, and recurring shocks across these countries requires harmonized technical standards, shared learning, and coordinated supply chain approaches. The program will expand decentralized nutrition services by placing screening, early identification, and treatment within spaces that families already use daily, including schools, Child-Friendly Spaces, transit points, and primary health facilities. To be able to achieve the intended outcomes, IsraAID seeks services of a consultant to conduct a baseline upon which project progress and successes will be measured.

This Terms of Reference (ToR) sets out the background, purpose, objectives, scope of work, expected deliverables, and management arrangements for the baseline study, and invites eligible firms to submit technical and financial proposals for consideration.

PURPOSE

This assignment aims at establishing both quantitative and qualitative baseline information on access to integrated nutrition services, nutrition and food security practices and programme systems to ensure that these are addressed by programme interventions to realise the intended overall goal. The baseline will also establish baseline information on several learning areas under the OECD criteria and the IsraAID Community Resilience framework (CRF). The baseline therefore aims at obtaining verified, disaggregated benchmark values for the programme indicators, enabling precise measurement of outcomes and impacts at endline (Year 2, 2028).

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The assignment will specifically

A. Assess the 3 programme outcome indicators

1\. Vulnerable communities — especially children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) — access integrated, quality nutrition services delivered through a multi-tier workforce (community and formal system) and functional multi-sectoral pathways.

2\. Caregivers and community structures adopt improved nutritional and food security practices that prevent and protect against malnutrition.

3\. Programme systems — accountability, information, governance and supply chain, inventory management systems, logistics & distribution modalities — are functional and progressively integrated into and owned by national, district and community structures.

B. Provide baseline information on the specified Community Resilience Framework (CRF) and OECD learning questions.

SCOPE

The baseline survey will be conducted in programme’s area of implementation, covering Nakivale Refugee Settlement and its surrounding host communities in Western Uganda and Turkana West Sub-County specifically targeting Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kalobeyei settlement and its surrounding host communities in Kenya. There are several credible data sources that will benefit the project including, among others, District Information Health System (DHIS 2),

Food Security and Nutrition Assessment reports (FSNA), Demographic Health Surveys, and Population Census reports. Primary baseline information will be obtained from, among others, health facilities, schools, households, children-friendly spaces, community structures and partners engaged in nutrition interventions

METHODOLOGY

IsraAID anticipates a mixed-methods baseline design combining quantitative and qualitative approaches, consistent with the evidence requirements set out in the MEAL Plan. The final design will be proposed by the Firm and refined collaboratively with IsraAID’s MEAL team.

The baseline study should be designed so that its instruments, sampling frame, and methodology can be replicated with fidelity at endline, enabling credible before and after comparison and contribution analysis.

ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS

The consultant will be expected to demonstrate how the assessment will be conducted in line with research ethics while protecting the human rights of the participants. It will also be the responsibility of the consultant to ensure strict adherence to IsraAID Safeguarding Policy. The consultant will also be responsible for ensuring that any persons hired, engaged, or consulted during the process are familiar with the policy and commit to abide by it during the delivery of the assignment.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE

This assignment will last approximately 75 days from the date of signing of the contract. The consultant will provide a detailed work plan with realistic timelines to the logical conclusion of the baseline survey. The following deliverables are expected from the consultant:

The baseline assessment will be undertaken by one consultant/firm. Fieldwork will be conducted sequentially, beginning in Uganda and subsequently moving to Kenya.

1\. Inception & Evaluation Design – Week 1

Key activities

· Desk review of programme proposal, Theory of Change, Logic Model and MEAL Plan.

· Inception meetings with IsraAID.

· Refine evaluation design, sampling strategy and evaluation matrix.

Deliverables

· Inception report.

· Refined methodology and sampling plan.

· Approved work plan and evaluation/indicator matrix.

2\. Tool Development, Piloting & Field Preparation – Weeks 2–3

Key activities

· Finalize quantitative and qualitative data collection tools aligned with Indicator Reference Sheets.

· Share tools with relevant teams and incorporate feedback.

· Pilot testing and tool refinement.

· Enumerator training/orientation and field preparation.

· Ethics/safeguarding clearance preparation.

Deliverables

· Approved final data collection tools and protocols.

· Pilot findings and revisions.

· Enumerator training/orientation completed.

· Ethics/safeguarding documentation.

3\. Data Collection – Uganda – Weeks 4–5

Key activities

· Deploy quantitative and qualitative surveys/interviews with agreed respondents in Uganda.

· Conduct ongoing field-level data quality assurance.

· Hold regular field debriefs with participating stakeholders.

· Complete Uganda fieldwork and initial data quality checks.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

Deliverables

· Uganda quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Uganda dataset.

3\. Transition & Data Collection – Kenya – Weeks 5–7

Key activities

· Close out any outstanding Uganda data collection activities.

· Uganda findings first draft submission

· Transition/travel from Uganda to Kenya.

· Conduct quantitative and qualitative data collection in Kenya.

· Maintain ongoing data quality assurance and stakeholder debriefs.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

· Complete Kenya fieldwork and initial data checks.

Deliverables

· Uganda fieldwork close-out and initial findings draft shared.

· Kenya quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Kenya dataset.

4\. Analysis & Validation – Weeks 7–9

Key activities

· Clean, code and analyze quantitative and qualitative data.

· Triangulate findings across methods and countries.

· Develop and populate indicator baseline values.

· Prepare and conduct validation workshop with IsraAID/programme stakeholders.

Deliverables

· Analyzed datasets.

· Populated indicator baseline table.

· Draft findings.

· Validation workshop summary.

5\. Reporting & Dissemination – Weeks 9–10

Key activities

· Incorporate feedback from IsraAID.

· Finalize evaluation/baseline report.

· Prepare executive summary/brief and presentation deck.

· Present findings to relevant stakeholders.

· Hand over final datasets, tools and supporting documentation.

Deliverables

· Final report in MS Word and PDF.

· Executive summary/brief.

· Presentation deck.

· Final clean datasets and tools.

Summary of Key Milestones

· Week 1: Inception phase completed

· Week 2 & 3: Tools finalised/piloted and field preparation completed

· Week 4 & 5: Uganda fieldwork completed

· Weeks 6 & 7: Kenya fieldwork completed and initial Uganda finding draft

· Weeks 8 & 9: Analysis and validation completed; draft report ready

· Week 10: Final report, presentation and data/tools handover completed

Note: The timeline is indicative and may be adjusted in consultation with IsraAID, provided the overall 10-week period and Uganda-to-Kenya sequencing are maintained. Analysis may overlap with final data cleaning. IsraAID will want to be provided access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected, to enable ongoing data quality checks and early identification of gaps or issues.

Summary of Key Baseline Deliverables

· Inception report by the consultant within one (1) week upon signing of the consultancy contract.

· Draft Baseline Survey report with clear findings in line with the aim and outcomes of the programme, conclusion, and recommendations for review.

· Final Baseline Survey report in electronic format (MS Word as well as PDF)

· Summary of the findings in (MS PowerPoint) to be used for subsequent dissemination.

· All raw data: transcripts from In-depth Interviews, Individual Surveys, FGDs and cleaned data set used for analysis and production of the final report in an acceptable electronic format shared on a rolling basis.

KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

IsraAID and the Programme Team

· Draw the contract and manage its implementation within the period.

· Coordinate the baseline study

· Share relevant documentation that are important for this assignment

· Introduction of the consultant and team to the relevant bodies within the study locations.

· Organize a validation meeting for the baseline findings.

· Review and approve the deliverables presented by the consultant.

Consultant

· Recruit, contract, remunerate, train, coordinate, and supervise data collectors, ensuring compliance with the agreed methodology, ethical standards, data quality requirements, and timelines.

· Lead consultancy assignment including data collection and analysis.

· Develop and review the data collection tools.

· Lead the development of the consultancy report and incorporate any feedback from IsraAID

· Ensure all deliverables of the assignment are accomplished and approved by IsraAID

· Present findings to the IsraAID team and relevant stakeholders for validation.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

IsraAID expects the successful consultant/firm to field a multidisciplinary team with a balance of quantitative, qualitative, and GESI expertise, complemented by strong in-country presence across ICNMP priority geographies where possible. The indicative team composition below is provided as guidance; consulting firms may propose an alternative structure provided all required competencies are demonstrated and justified.

· Team Leader / Baseline Study Lead: Advanced degree in public health, social sciences, statistics, international development, or related field; minimum 10 years’ experience leading baseline/endline evaluations for complex, multi-country development programs; demonstrated experience with forced displacement, refugee, or migration programming; strong track record managing mixed-methods research teams across multiple African countries. Excellent interpersonal and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with the IsraAID team.

· Quantitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in statistics, economics, or related field; expertise in survey design, sampling methodology, and quantitative data analysis (e.g., STATA, R, SPSS); experience with mobile data collection platforms (e.g., KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, ODK).

· Qualitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in social sciences; expertise in qualitative methods including KIIs, FGDs, and complexity-aware approaches (e.g., Outcome

· Data Management / MEL Support: Experience in data cleaning, database management, and dashboard/data visualization; familiarity with data protection standards applicable to work with protected persons.

GOVERNANCE AND REPORTING LINES

The consulting firm will report to IsraAID’s ICNMP MEAL Coordinator, who holds day-to-day responsibility for the MEAL leadership of the ICNMP programme, and will work closely with the ICNMP program teams in both Uganda and Kenya Country Offices on tool design, data quality assurance, analysis, and reporting. The ICNMP MEAL Coordinator retains overall accountability for the assignment and will review and approve the inception report and final baseline report.

PAYMENT PLAN

50% after the approval of the inception report, 50% after the approval of the final report.

APPLICATION PROCESS

Interested candidates should submit the following:

· Technical proposal outlining approach and methodology

· A financial proposal in US Dollars (USD), detailing all consultancy-related costs (operational, and logistical costs for conducting the assignment in Kenya and Uganda).

· CVs of the Lead Consultant and the entire team

· At least three relevant samples of previous similar work

· At least two (2) recommendation letters from recent clients for similar assignments.

· Copy of the company registration, Memorandum, and Articles of Association if a company/ firm is applying.

· Copy of tax compliance Certificate

· TIN Number

· VAT Number

· Any other relevant information supporting the application.

EVALUATION CRITERIA FOR SELECTION OF THE CONSULTANT/CONSULTING FIRM

Proposals from the interested bidders will be evaluated against the following criteria:

1\. Technical Approach & Understanding of the Assignment (30%): Understanding of the programme, evaluation objectives and scope; quality and appropriateness of the proposed methodology; sampling approach; quantitative and qualitative

methods; data analysis, triangulation and validation; and ethical/safeguarding considerations.

2\. Relevant Experience & Technical Capacity (25%): Demonstrated experience conducting baseline studies, evaluations or similar assignments, particularly in humanitarian, refugee, displacement and development contexts. Experience working with refugee and host communities in Uganda and/or Kenya will be an advantage. Qualifications and expertise of the proposed consultant/team will also be considered.

3\. Workplan, Fieldwork & Data Quality Approach (20%): Feasibility of the proposed workplan within the 10-week period; capacity to undertake fieldwork sequentially in Uganda and Kenya; approach to data quality assurance, data management, safeguarding and secure access to data on a rolling basis during data collection.

4\. Financial Proposal & Value for Money (25%): Completeness, clarity and reasonableness of the financial proposal, including professional fees and all logistical and operational costs required to conduct the assignment in Uganda and Kenya.

ANNEXES

1\. Program Document

2\. Program LogFrame

RESERVATION OF RIGHTS

Nothing contained in this RFP/TOR shall be construed as creating any obligation on the part of IsraAID to enter into a contract with any bidder. IsraAID reserves the unrestricted right to determine the evaluation criteria, request additional documentation, waive minor irregularities, seek clarifications, reject any or all proposals, and terminate the procurement process at its sole discretion and without prior notice.

  
Appendixes can be found here - [**public folder**](https://israaid-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/eoyoo_israaid_org/IgC0MsUIQfMjR5rArPJsF2AmAZsbCmAQ5eV4Ul5n7Gh-fS8)

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Finance, Ebola Response
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we’d like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

On 15 May 2026, the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) officially declared the country's seventeenth Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak following the confirmation of cases in the health zones of Rwampara, Mongbwalu, and Bunia in Ituri Province. In the past 90 days, more than 6,700 cases have been reported with over 3,500 deaths - and more than 8,000 cases and nearly 4,000 deaths since the outbreak began, making this the fastest spreading Ebola outbreak documented. The vast majority of all cases are in Ituri province, but cases are also reported in 63 of the country’s 104 health zones, across North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, and Bas-Uélé provinces, highlighting the scale and complexity of the response.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home.

**RESPONSE BACKGROUND**

The Ebola outbreak is unfolding in a fragile humanitarian context characterized by protracted conflict, population displacement, weak health systems, and limited access to essential services. Health facilities remain under significant pressure, with persistent gaps in infection prevention and control (IPC), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) infrastructure, healthcare waste management, triage capacity, and the availability of essential IPC supplies. These challenges continue to increase the risk of healthcare-associated transmission, compromise the safety of health workers and patients, and disrupt the continuity of essential health services.

In response, IRC has rapidly launched an integrated Ebola emergency response in close collaboration with the Ministry of Health, provincial and health zone authorities, and other partners. The response combines Health, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), WASH, Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Protection, and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) interventions to strengthen outbreak prevention, detection, and response at both health facility and community levels.

**Position Overview**

As a member of the Emergency Response Team (EERT) Senior Management Team (SMT), the Deputy Director of Finance provides financial leadership and management necessary to ensure that the emergency response has the appropriate financial infrastructure and systems in place to support the strategic vision and mission of the organization. They will contribute to the development of the response’s strategic and operational plans and be accountable for ensuring and monitoring delivery against the financial plans through targeted and comprehensive financial analytical review. The Deputy Director of Finance is responsible for the overall policy and management for the financial and accounting management of the emergency response. Emphasis will be placed on financial management policies, practices, and systems that are compliant with local laws and US as well as adhering to donor requirements, but are also conducive to the effective implementation of country programs.

As Deputy Director Finance, they will have responsibility for all aspects of strategic and operational finance for the emergency response, acting as the principal finance business partner to the Emergency Senior Management team and the Ebola Response Director, the Emergency Unit team, as well as conforming to IRC's financial control environment and CFO standards and objectives.

Based in Bunia, the Deputy Director of Finance will have dual reporting to the Ebola Response Director and the global Director of Emergency Finance, with key coordination and technical lines of collaboration with both the Deputy Director of Operations and Deputy Director of Finance from the non-Emergency DRC Country Program.

**Major Responsibilities**

**Strategic Planning & Analysis**

- Provides financial information which supports the Response Director and EERT SMT in making business decisions in line with IRC & Country Program strategies
- Provides strategic analysis on the overall financial health of the country program to the Response Director and EERT SMT
- Contributes and provides feedback to the development of the Emergency Response Plan

**Controllership**

- Ensures that all in-country practices are in compliance with IRC and donor policies and procedures
- Establishes in-country finance procedures to supplement global policies as needed
- Closely monitors financial activities and advises the Response Director on the financial performance of the office, issues with internal controls, or financial management
- Ensures monthly balance sheet reconciliations are completed on a timely basis
- Manages the finance department activities and schedules to meet the financial reporting requirements and deadlines specified by headquarters and donors
- Identifies requirements for and develops reporting formats to aid in the management of country operations and grant expenditures
- Directs the preparation of and approves all donor financial reports in respect to accounting, legal, and contractual requirements, and ensures the review of such reports by the Response Director and Emergency Finance Director prior to submission
- Ensures in-country internal control reviews of operations are regularly undertaken.
- Facilitates external, internal, donor, or government audits
- Oversees the protection of the country’s assets (cash, inventory, fixed assets) through the enforcement of internal control policies and procedures
- Maintains current knowledge of local government requirements related to finance and complies with tax and other legal requirements
- Is the principal liaison with IRC HQ on all finance, accounting, grant budget management, and cash management

**Training & Staff Management**

- Establishes a finance department roles and responsibilities matrix; staff job descriptions are current; recruits and maintains qualified staff to perform finance functions
- Ensures comprehensive and constructive performance reviews are completed annually; career planning and development plans are in place for all finance staff
- Develops and implements a training program for the country’s finance staff
- Oversees finance training and technical support to non-finance staff for skills improvement in the areas of accounting, reporting, and internal control

**Treasury**

- Supervises all country program bank relations and bank account activities, including negotiation of fees, interest, and currency exchange rates
- Oversees the review and approval of all monthly bank account and cash reconciliations
- Maintain, on a current basis, accurate forecasts of cash requirements for meeting future spending, including commitments that obligate IRC to future spending
- Ensures that appropriate balances are maintained to facilitate grant implementation and cash held in the headquarters is drawn regularly
- Ensures the development and implementation of a plan to minimize the country’s foreign exchange exposure to currency gains and losses
- Supervises the collection of contractual and other receivables

**Budget and Forecast**

- Oversees the preparation and revision of grant proposal budgets; supports programs with guidance on costing and inputs in creating budgets for submission
- Prepares and maintains the country’s annual operating budget; ensures cost coverage for in-country operating costs and updates the operating budget regularly
- Presents and facilitates the review of actual to budget expenditures with the Country Director and program managers

**Partnerships**

- Demonstrated genuine interest in and commitment to collaboration and partnership with local actors in emergencies.
- Champion a culture of effective and respectful partnerships. Promote partner-led programming in line with IRC’s “why not partner?” and “partner as equals” approach.
- As a member of the EERT Senior Management Team (SMT), prioritize and promote IRC’s internal capacity to partner.
- Develop staffing structures with the appropriate number of staff to effectively manage partnerships and ensure quality.
- Actively contribute to the relevant sections of Partner Capacity Analysis (PCA) and the subsequent development of partner support plans.
- Manage the implementation of action items in the finance sections of partner support plans.
- Lead and/or support collaborative project and budget design with partners.
- Work collaboratively with partners to ensure that project budgets reflect fair market value.
- Ensure appropriate budget allocation for IRC to support partners in alignment with the overall response/program design.
- Actively participate in the Partnership Working Group (PWG).

**Accountability**

- Hold the Senior Management Team (SMT) accountable for outcomes related to safeguarding; regularly review progress, barriers, and enablers.
- Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and IRC values.

**Job Requirements**

- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business Administration, Commerce, or Finance required; recognized professional certificate in accounting, such as CPA, or a Master’s degree in Accounting is preferred
- Extensive, senior-level experience, and a minimum of five years of managerial experience in Finance is essential
- Senior-level experience working within the Ukrainian Financial sector is an advantage
- Prior experience leading large, complex multi-donor funded programs and grants, including experience with USG, European, DFID, and UN funding streams, foreign currency and exchange management, and budget development and oversight
- Extensive experience in working with computerized accounting systems, standard spreadsheets, and database programs (SUN System, Dynamics 365, Vision, Integra, etc)
- Demonstrated skills in building strong finance teams and establishing new finance operations, including the ability to communicate and work effectively with senior management, operating, and program staff and functions
- Ability to act as a proactive member of the Senior Management Team. Proven track record of proactively identifying and communicating potential problems and proposing solutions
- Capacity to function effectively in a complex, changing work environment, setting appropriate priorities, and managing competing priorities and pressure
- Ability to carry out responsibilities independently with minimal technical support
- Excellent interpersonal communication skills and professional patience, and be able to interact, partner, and thrive in a diverse environment
- Committed to staff training, capacity building, and development, and effective at facilitation
- Cultural awareness and ability to build relationships quickly with a wide variety of people
- French and English language communications skills are required
- Commitment to ongoing learning and reflection on personal and organizational biases, and willingness to adapt practices to promote inclusion.
- Demonstrated genuine interest in and commitment to collaboration and partnership with local actors in emergencies.

***French version:***

**CONTEXTE**

En intervenant face aux pires crises humanitaires mondiales dans des rôles très variés, le personnel de l'International Rescue Committee (IRC) incarne une force au service de l'humanité et de l'espoir. Si vous possédez les compétences et la passion nécessaires, nous aimerions associer votre énergie à la nôtre.

Grâce à son Unité d'urgence (EmU), l'IRC figure parmi les plus grandes organisations humanitaires au monde ; elle pilote des interventions d'urgence rapides visant à fournir une aide vitale, ainsi qu'un soutien au relèvement précoce et à la stabilisation, aux populations touchées par des conflits, des déplacements de population, des catastrophes naturelles et des situations d'urgence complexes dans des contextes variés à travers le globe. Nous misons sur l'innovation, l'agilité et des partenariats solides pour mener une action humanitaire efficace et opportune.

Le 15 mai 2026, le gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a officiellement déclaré la dix-septième épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola (MVE) du pays, suite à la confirmation de cas dans les zones de santé de Rwampara, Mongbwalu et Bunia, dans la province de l'Ituri. Au cours des 90 derniers jours, plus de 6 700 cas et plus de 3 500 décès ont été signalés ; le bilan total s'élève à plus de 8 000 cas et près de 4 000 décès depuis le début de l'épidémie, ce qui en fait l'épidémie d'Ebola à la propagation la plus rapide jamais documentée. Si la grande majorité des cas se concentre dans la province de l'Ituri, des cas ont également été signalés dans 63 des 104 zones de santé du pays — notamment dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu, du Sud-Kivu, du Haut-Uélé, de la Tshopo et du Bas-Uélé — ce qui témoigne de l'ampleur et de la complexité de la réponse.

Actifs dans les domaines de la santé publique, de l'éducation en situation d'urgence, des moyens de subsistance, de l'autonomisation des femmes, du développement de la jeunesse ainsi que de la protection et de la promotion des droits, nous accompagnons les personnes depuis les situations de danger jusqu'à leur retour à une vie stable.

**CONTEXTE DE LA RÉPONSE**

L'épidémie d'Ebola se déroule dans un contexte humanitaire fragile, marqué par des conflits prolongés, des déplacements de population, des systèmes de santé défaillants et un accès limité aux services essentiels. Les établissements de santé sont soumis à une forte pression ; des lacunes persistent en matière de prévention et de contrôle des infections (PCI), d'infrastructures d'eau, d'assainissement et d'hygiène (WASH), de gestion des déchets médicaux, de capacités de triage et de disponibilité des fournitures essentielles de PCI. Ces défis continuent d'accroître le risque de transmission au sein des structures de soins, de compromettre la sécurité du personnel soignant et des patients, et de perturber la continuité des services de santé essentiels.

En réponse, l'IRC a rapidement mis en place une intervention d'urgence intégrée contre Ebola, en étroite collaboration avec le ministère de la Santé, les autorités provinciales et celles des zones de santé, ainsi que d'autres partenaires. Cette réponse conjugue des interventions dans les domaines de la santé, de la prévention et du contrôle des infections (PCI), de l'eau, de l'assainissement et de l'hygiène (WASH), de la communication sur les risques et de l'engagement communautaire (RCCE), de la protection, ainsi que de la santé mentale et du soutien psychosocial (SMSPS), afin de renforcer la prévention, la détection et la réponse à l'épidémie, tant au niveau des établissements de santé qu'au sein des communautés.

**APERÇU DU POSTE**

En tant que membre de l'équipe de direction (SMT) de l'équipe d'intervention d'urgence (EERT), le directeur adjoint des finances assure le leadership et la gestion financière nécessaires pour garantir que l'intervention d'urgence dispose des infrastructures et des systèmes financiers adéquats pour soutenir la vision stratégique et la mission de l'organisation. Il contribuera à l'élaboration des plans stratégiques et opérationnels de l'intervention et sera responsable du suivi de leur exécution par rapport aux plans financiers, grâce à des analyses financières ciblées et approfondies. Le directeur adjoint des finances est responsable de la politique globale et de la gestion financière et comptable de l'intervention d'urgence. Une attention particulière sera portée aux politiques, pratiques et systèmes de gestion financière qui sont conformes aux lois locales et américaines ainsi qu'aux exigences des bailleurs de fonds, tout en favorisant la mise en œuvre efficace des programmes nationaux.

En qualité de directeur adjoint des finances, il sera responsable de tous les aspects de la gestion financière stratégique et opérationnelle de l'intervention d'urgence. Il agira en tant que principal partenaire financier auprès de l'équipe de direction de l'urgence, du directeur de l'intervention Ebola et de l'équipe de l'unité d'urgence, tout en veillant au respect du cadre de contrôle financier de l'IRC ainsi que des normes et objectifs du directeur financier (CFO).

Basé à Bunia, le directeur adjoint des finances sera placé sous la double supervision du directeur de l'intervention Ebola et du directeur mondial des finances pour les urgences (Global Director of Emergency Finance). Il entretiendra également des liens de coordination et de collaboration technique essentiels avec le directeur adjoint des opérations et le directeur adjoint des finances du programme national de l'IRC en RDC (hors urgence).

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS**  
**Planification et analyse stratégiques**

- Fournit des informations financières qui aident le directeur de réponse et EERT SMT à prendre des décisions commerciales conformément aux stratégies de l'IRC et du programme pays.
- Fournit une analyse stratégique sur la santé financière globale du programme de pays au directeur de la réponse et à l'EERT SMT.
- Contribue et fournit des commentaires à l'élaboration du plan d'intervention d'urgence

 **Contrôle**

- S'assure que toutes les pratiques dans le pays sont conformes aux politiques et procédures de l'IRC et des donateurs.
- Établit des procédures financières nationales pour compléter les politiques mondiales si nécessaire
- Surveille de près les activités financières et conseille le directeur de réponse sur la performance financière du bureau, les problèmes de contrôles internes ou de gestion financière.
- S'assure que les rapprochements mensuels des bilans sont effectués en temps opportun
- Gère les activités et les calendriers du service financier pour répondre aux exigences en matière de reporting financier et aux délais spécifiés par le siège et les donateurs.
- Identifie les exigences et développe des formats de reporting pour faciliter la gestion des opérations pays et des dépenses de subventions
- Dirige la préparation et approuve tous les rapports financiers des donateurs en ce qui concerne les exigences comptables, juridiques et contractuelles, et assure l'examen de ces rapports par le directeur de la réponse et le directeur des finances d'urgence avant leur soumission.
- Veiller à ce que des examens de contrôle interne des opérations dans le pays soient régulièrement effectués.
- Facilite les audits externes, internes, des donateurs ou du gouvernement
- Supervise la protection des actifs du pays (trésorerie, stocks, immobilisations) grâce à l'application des politiques et procédures de contrôle interne
- Maintient ses connaissances actuelles des exigences du gouvernement local liées aux finances et se conforme aux exigences fiscales et autres exigences légales
- Est le principal agent de liaison avec le siège de l'IRC pour toutes les finances, la comptabilité, la gestion du budget des subventions et la gestion de la trésorerie.

 **Formation et gestion du personnel**

- Établit une matrice des rôles et responsabilités du service financier ; les descriptions de poste du personnel sont à jour ; recrute et maintient en poste du personnel qualifié pour exercer des fonctions financières
- Veiller à ce que des évaluations de performance complètes et constructives soient effectuées chaque année ; des plans de planification de carrière et de développement sont en place pour tout le personnel financier
- Élabore et met en œuvre un programme de formation pour le personnel financier du pays
- Supervise la formation financière et le soutien technique au personnel non financier pour l'amélioration des compétences dans les domaines de la comptabilité, du reporting et du contrôle interne.

 **Trésorerie**

- Supervise toutes les relations bancaires et les activités des comptes bancaires du programme pays, y compris la négociation des frais, des intérêts et des taux de change.
- Supervise l'examen et l'approbation de tous les rapprochements mensuels de comptes bancaires et de trésorerie
- Maintenir, sur une base actuelle, des prévisions précises des besoins de trésorerie pour faire face aux dépenses futures, y compris les engagements qui obligent l'IRC à effectuer des dépenses futures.
- S'assure que les soldes appropriés sont maintenus pour faciliter la mise en œuvre des subventions et que les liquidités détenues au siège sont régulièrement tirées.
- Assure l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre d’un plan visant à minimiser l’exposition du pays aux gains et pertes de change
- Supervise le recouvrement des créances contractuelles et autres

 **Budget et prévisions**

- Supervise la préparation et la révision des budgets des propositions de subventions ; soutient les programmes en leur fournissant des conseils sur les coûts et des contributions à la création de budgets à soumettre
- Prépare et maintient le budget de fonctionnement annuel du pays ; assure la couverture des coûts de fonctionnement dans le pays et met régulièrement à jour le budget de fonctionnement
- Présente et facilite l'examen des dépenses réelles par rapport au budget avec le directeur pays et les responsables de programme

 **Partenariats**

- Démontré un réel intérêt et un engagement envers la collaboration et le partenariat avec les acteurs locaux en cas d'urgence.
- Promouvoir une culture de partenariats efficaces et respectueux. Promouvoir la programmation menée par des partenaires conformément au principe « pourquoi pas partenaire ? » de l'IRC. et une approche « partenaire sur un pied d’égalité ».
- En tant que membre de l'équipe de direction de l'EERT (SMT), prioriser et promouvoir la capacité interne de l'IRC à établir des partenariats.
- Développer des structures de dotation en personnel avec le nombre approprié d'employés pour gérer efficacement les partenariats et garantir la qualité.
- Contribuer activement aux sections pertinentes de l'analyse des capacités des partenaires (PCA) et à l'élaboration ultérieure des plans de soutien des partenaires.
- Gérer la mise en œuvre des éléments d'action dans les sections financières des plans de soutien des partenaires.
- Diriger et/ou soutenir la conception collaborative de projets et de budgets avec les partenaires.
- Travailler en collaboration avec les partenaires pour garantir que les budgets des projets reflètent la juste valeur marchande.
- Assurer une allocation budgétaire appropriée à l'IRC pour soutenir les partenaires conformément à la conception globale de la réponse/du programme.
- Participer activement au Groupe de travail sur le partenariat (PWG).
- Responsabilité
- Tenir l'équipe de direction supérieure (SMT) responsable des résultats liés à la sauvegarde ; revoir régulièrement le programme obstacles et facteurs favorisants.
- Favoriser l'apprentissage continu, le dialogue honnête et la réflexion afin de renforcer la protection des personnes et les valeurs de l'IRC.

**EXIGENCES DU POSTE**

- Licence (Bachelor) en comptabilité, administration des affaires, commerce ou finance requise ; certification professionnelle reconnue en comptabilité (ex. : CPA) ou master en comptabilité privilégié.
- Expérience approfondie à un niveau de direction et au moins cinq ans d'expérience en gestion financière.
- Une expérience de haut niveau au sein du secteur financier ukrainien constitue un atout.
- Expérience préalable dans la direction de programmes et de subventions d'envergure, complexes et financés par plusieurs bailleurs de fonds (notamment les États-Unis, l'UE, le DFID et l'ONU), incluant la gestion des devises et des taux de change ainsi que l'élaboration et le suivi budgétaires.
- Solide expérience des systèmes comptables informatisés, des tableurs courants et des logiciels de base de données (SUN System, Dynamics 365, Vision, Integra, etc.).
- Compétences avérées pour constituer des équipes financières solides et mettre en place de nouvelles opérations financières ; capacité à communiquer et à collaborer efficacement avec la haute direction ainsi qu'avec le personnel opérationnel et les équipes de programme.
- Capacité à agir en tant que membre proactif de l'équipe de direction. Expérience avérée dans l'identification et la communication proactives de problèmes potentiels ainsi que dans la proposition de solutions.
- Capacité à travailler efficacement dans un environnement complexe et en constante évolution, à définir des priorités adéquates et à gérer des priorités concurrentes ainsi que la pression.
- Capacité à assumer ses responsabilités de manière autonome, avec un soutien technique minimal.
- Excellentes compétences en communication interpersonnelle et patience professionnelle ; capacité à interagir, à nouer des partenariats et à s'épanouir dans un environnement diversifié.
- Engagement envers la formation, le renforcement des capacités et le développement du personnel ; aptitude avérée à l'animation et à la facilitation.
- Sensibilité culturelle et capacité à nouer rapidement des relations avec des personnes d'horizons très variés.
- Maîtrise du français et de l'anglais requise.
- Engagement envers l'apprentissage continu et la réflexion sur les biais personnels et organisationnels, ainsi que volonté d'adapter les pratiques pour favoriser l'inclusion.
- Intérêt sincère et engagement avéré envers la collaboration et le partenariat avec les acteurs locaux dans les situations d'urgence.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.  
  
**IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer:** Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) - We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, religion, or any other status.

jobs.title: Head of Support Services - Lebanon (Readvertised)
jobs.body:
**Who are we?**

DRC has been responding to various humanitarian crises in Lebanon since 2004, working with Palestinian, Iraqi and Syrian refugees. Since 2011, DRC has focused on responding to the Syrian refugee crisis in Lebanon and the resulting impact on Lebanese host community, and more recently the impact of the economic and financial crises as well as responding to the ongoing conflict. DRC Lebanon’s focus is to ensure that we are able to respond to critical emerging humanitarian needs whilst improving the living conditions of displacement-affected populations and contributing to the achievement of durable solutions. DRC is focusing its response in protection, economic recovery, shelter and site coordination and management, and humanitarian mine action across the country directly and through partners. DRC is also contributing to the broader humanitarian response through our Referral Information Management System (RIMS), utilised by 170 organisations.

**About the job**

The Head of Support Services (HoSS) is operationally and strategically responsible for Finance, Human Resources, Logistics and Procurement, Administration and/or IT. S/he oversees, develops and provides strategic direction to his/her support areas. This role has a country focus (Lebanon) and ensures compliance to DRC procedures and guidelines within the country. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides support and/or technical guidance to country operations while overseeing country activities.

With senior level management experience, you are expected to have demonstrable successful track record of organizational development and resource mobilization and play a leadership role in developing and implementing country-specific strategies as well as improving operational systems, processes, and policies in support of DRC’s mission and values.

**Previous experience in a Finance Manager/Director or similar role and/or a Finance-related qualification is highly recommended.**

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**Responsibilities:**

**Staff Management**

- Lead and manage the support managers (including people planning, performance, well-being and development) whilst providing dotted technical line support to wider country support team.
- Work to build the capacity of the operational support staff throughout the operation though frequent in-service training sessions, mentoring support and frequent visits to field offices.
- Role model and lead the wider country programme against DRC values, diversity and inclusion as well as code of conduct.

**Support Services Management**

- Responsible for the strategic development, management and implementation of the support operations as per DRC operational handbook. This includes developing and improving operational approaches, compliance and systems, and support the Country Director to build and deliver effective and sustainable interventions.
- Support the Country Director and the Senior Management Team in liaising with donors and authorities, especially as relates to issues of compliance, registration, and audit
- Ensure appropriate technical support is available to programs, in line with organizational priorities
- Provide strategic guidance to the HR/Admin department to develop and implement DRCs HR policy in Lebanon. This includes providing strategic guidance for all staff management, career & development recruitment and induction process as well as appropriate stress management and care for Expatriates and National Staff.
- Lead on DRC Lebanon annual master budgets and ensuring that monthly monitoring of expenditure informs management decision making.
- Lead on the effective implementation and adherence of organization and stakeholder financial regulations.
- Overseeing the operationalization of the contextual/localized finance handbook.
- Ensure the implementation of sustainable and robust supply chain and financial system for an efficient and effective support to all DRC programs and support services.
- Ensure an efficient ICT Operating environment is in place to meet operational needs.

**Operational Management**

- Responsible for maintaining and improving operational resource management in the mission, together with SMT, identifying both short term and long-term resource needs and translate these into objectives and priorities for future DRC projects in Lebanon
- Responsible for leading the development and update of the resource management component of the Country Strategy, ensuring the Support Services facilitate the delivery of the strategy in line with DRC global policies and strategy.
- Ensure that DRC retains and continually develops its operational capacity to provide rapid emergency response in particular within its procurement and HR systems
- Ensure that Lebanon operation complies to DRC Risk Management Framework, and operational Compliance Tools and processes are duly implemented. This includes development of a risk management plan for the country that identifies the major financial and operational risks and implement a mitigation strategy
- Regular review and improvements to Country SOPs to ensure the internal control environment strengthened as well as develop policies as required where gaps are noted.
- Supervision, audits and controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to DRC’s operational standards within support area. This also includes ensuring the timely implementation of DRC’s internal audit and external audit recommendations and contextualize HQ understanding of local challenges.
- Participate as a member of the SMT in drafting project proposals, and on the use of resources according to budgets and policies.
- Together with the Head of Programs, lead the mainstreaming of Project Cycle Management and partnership best practices throughout the organization.
- Contribute to the delivery of DRC Lebanon’s localisation strategy, development and oversight of partnerships and ensure Support Services are fit for purpose to support equitable partnerships and capacity exchange.
- Ensure that all administrative and legal-related systems are accurate and maintained, and that DRC Lebanon is legally compliant with Government of Lebanon directives and processes.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of DRC’s global development initiatives
- As and when required, substitute the Country Director when is requested as such (leaves, field visits, long meetings etc)

**DRC Dynamics ERP System**

- Ensure ERP functionality is properly used by relevant staff
- Apply reports and data analytics from DRC Dynamics to improve overall performance
- Act as heavy user for most of the Projects & Finance functionalities

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect the following:

*Required*

- Minimum 7 years’ experience in a similar role in an international NGO.
- 4 years’ experience in people management with proven leadership skills.
- Proven operational management experiences and capability, including in complex and emergency settings
- Proven significant financial, information and systems management experience as well as in procurement and tender processes
- Understanding and experience of institutional fundraising.
- Excellent communication, negotiation and problem-solving capacities; with the ability to work flexibly in a diverse team in a dynamic environment, fostering a positive working environment
- Strong capacity building, facilitation, and presentation skills with the ability to collaborate, network and negotiate in order to facilitate communication and support to staff, local partners, Governments, UN, donors & other NGOs without losing sight of the strategic objective
- Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple competing deliverables on varying timelines
- Experience working in an ERP system, including Supply Chain, Finance and HR systems
- Full professional proficiency in English and Arabic

*Desirable*

- Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple competing deliverables on varying timelines
- Experience working in an ERP system, including Supply Chain, Finance and HR systems

**Languages**

- Full professional proficiency in English
- Full professional proficiency in Arabic

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Education**

A Master’s Degree or advanced professional qualification in Finance, Business Administration, Logistics or HR

**We offer**

- Contract length: 1 year
- Band: Management - E1
- Designation of Duty Station: Beirut - Lebanon
- Start date: ASAP

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for **national and expatriate employees.**

  
**DRC as an employer**  
By working in DRC, you will be joining a global workforce of around 6000 employees in approximately 30 countries. We pride ourselves on our:

- Professionalism, impact & expertise
- Humanitarian approach & the work we do
- Purpose, meaningfulness & own contribution
- Culture, values & strong leadership
- Fair compensation & continuous development

  
  
DRC’s capacity to ensure the protection of and assistance to refugees, IDP’s and other persons of concern depends on the ability of our staff to uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. DRC conducts thorough and comprehensive background checks as part of the recruitment process.  
  
**If you have questions or are facing problems with the online application process, please visit** [**drc.ngo/jobsupport**](https://drc.ngo/jobsupport)**.**  
  
  
***Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer and we consider all applicants based on individual merit and qualifications, regardless of personal characteristics or attributes. We are committed to increasing the diversity of our workforce, aiming for a 50% balance of men and women in management roles and ensuring that at least 50% of management roles are filled by national staff. We recognize that a diverse and inclusive team is crucial for achieving our organizational goals and making a positive impact on the communities we serve.***

jobs.title: Country Finance Manager Lebanon
jobs.body:
**Position**: Country Finance Manager Lebanon

**Location**: Beirut, Lebanon

**Reporting Relationship**: Country Representative (Line Management) and Regional Finance Manager (Functional Management)

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline**: 07/11/2026

**Working Context**

WeWorld has been working in Lebanon since 2006 and is currently supporting vulnerable refugee, IDP and host community populations through WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods, Local Economic Development, Education and Social Cohesion in Bekaa, Baalbek-Hermel, Akkar, Saida and Beirut. Our interventions span immediate emergency response and recovery in view of building preparedness and longer-term resilience for populations affected by conflict and/or displacement. The operation is run by over 50 employees, divided in three offices (Beirut, Zahle and Saida). We work closely with local partners, including NGOs and institutional actors at different levels, and are part of large consortia with other actors.

**Purpose of the Role**

The **Country Finance Manager** is responsible for all the administrative and accounting processes, including financial reporting, budget planning, development and monitoring. They manage staff within the Finance Department in country.

**MAIN FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES**

**General Administration**

- Track and manage deliverables and timelines related to grants, contracts, vendors, and partners
- Monitor grant administration to ensure compliance with reporting and expenditure requirements
- Supervise compliance of administrative documents and their proper filing
- Ensure the smooth flow of administrative information and data to the HQ
- Supervise flow of administrative information from project partners and the compliance with MoU
- Ensure smooth and punctual communications and reporting with local banks

**Accounting**

- Supervise and approve regular accounting, including monthly reconciliations, monthly and yearly closing of accounts, monthly journal entries
- Supervise cash and bank balance checking process when closing the monthly accounts

**Financial Reporting**

- Responsible for the preparation of financial reports, in coordination with Regional Finance Manager, and administrative team
- Ensure the compliance of financial reports with donors’ and internal rules and procedures

**Budget & Planning**

- Prepare and regularly monitor/updateWeWorld’s core budget for the Lebanon operation and provide an analysis to the Country Representativefocusing on gaps and risks
- Collaborate with the Country Representative, Head of Programmes and Project Managers to develop project budgets with quality, on time, in line with the operation’s core budget and according to donors’ regulations;
- Review administrative/financial terms of grant contracts before signature (payment & financial reporting schedule, etc.)
- Collaborate with the Head of Programmes, Project Managers and Procurement & Logistics Managers to regularly monitor actual and forecasted expenses against budget to avoid under and overspending on the projects in compliance withdonor flexibility rules
- Monitor financial flows of ongoing projects
- Anticipate financial risks, present budget updates and mitigation plans and report them to the Country Representative;
- Participate with the Country Management Team in reflecting on the evolution of the mission, and the programming of new projects and/or reorientation

**Audit Process**

- Collaborate to the management of financial audit performed on the projects
- Supervise yearly financial audit on general accounting for local authorities
- Prepare information and is directly responsible for any assessment/audit performed by donor on WeWorld administrative procedure

**Procedure**

- Design and implement administrative routines, procedures, and systems to increase efficiencies within the finance department, in particular relating to better structuring Budget Follow Ups, Forecasts, Payment Follow Ups and optimizing staff roles and responsibilities within the team
- Update the Local Operational Manual based on WeWorld procedures to implement organizational policies related to the Finance Department

**Operational**

- At Country level, liaise with the Human Resources and Procurement and Logistic departments for a fluid and collaborative collaboration
- Follow-up payments from donors and financial project close-out

**Human Resources**

- Participate in analyzing staffing needs & costs, compensation & benefits
- Supervise administrative and finance local personnel to complete routine tasks
- Capacity building of local finance staff and partner organizations in areas such as financial management, administration, good governance and management of accountability and transparency
- Support the Country Representative and the HR Manager to monitor and revise salary scale, if necessary

**Representation**

- Participate in inter-admin meetings with other INGOs and NGOs
- Ensure official representation for the administrative management of the Mission to the competent authorities

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a first 6 (six) month collaboration contract subject to verification of the achievement of specific objectives (these objectives will be agreed together with the Line Manager upon arrival on assignment); a second collaboration contract of 6 (six) months renewable, following the positive evaluation of the first months of contract and availability of funds.

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy Base Salary (2950€ - 3550€ monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family duty Station**: NO

**R&R**: NO

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

We are committed to building talented teams and welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent experience in Financial/Accounting management
- Knowledge of institutional donor procedures (AICS, EU, AFD, UN)
- Fluent in English both written and verbal

**Professional experience**

- At least 5 years of specific experience in finance/administrative positions in the international cooperation sector, in similar roles and levels or responsibility
- Experience of representation to institutions and participation in coordination meetings
- Experience in budget design and management and monitoring of logistics procedures
- Experience in using accounting software
- Experience in managing teams

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong flexibility and capacity to adapt behavior to the needs of the situation
- Capacity to work autonomously and in problems prevention/resolution
- Proven organizational skills and ability to effectively manage multiple tasks while fostering quality, team spirit and positive working relationships with colleagues
- Ability to identify, initiate and maintain good relationships with partner organizations, donors and national authorities including building professional relationships with senior decision-makers and influencers / leaders
- Good communication, negotiation skills and sensitivity in dealing with local institutions on critical issues
- Cultural, gender, religion, and age sensitivity and adaptability
- Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld, genuine interest for international cooperation development topics

**Desirable Requirements**

- Knowledge of Arabic would be considered an asset
- Previous experience in the Middle East Region is an asset

jobs.title: Consultancy for an Inclusive Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) in DR CONGO
jobs.body:
## **Background**

CBM (Christian Blind Mission) is an international development and humanitarian organisation dedicated to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the world's poorest countries. We are providing inclusive humanitarian assistance in contexts of disasters, conflict, and displacement. CBM’s humanitarian activities aim to equally reach and actively involve persons with disabilities, addressing specific needs while promoting and facilitating full inclusion in mainstream services. We work together with our partners on programmes that are context specific, from disability-inclusive preparedness to immediate life-saving needsto resilience strengthening. CBM is based in Germany with 23 country offices in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America. With over 115 years of experience, CBM is considered as one of the world’s oldest organisations working in this field.  
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) faces one of the world's most complex humanitarian crises, marked by armed conflict, displacement, protection risks, epidemics, food insecurity and natural disasters. Persons with disabilities, women, children, older persons, IDPs and returnees face heightened barriers to accessing assistance and essential services.  
To inform future humanitarian programming, including potential interventions under ECHO HIP 2027 and other funding opportunities, CBM seeks to conduct an Inclusive Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) in selected crisis-affected areas. Findings will support evidence-based programme design, strategic positioning and partnership development.  
CBM is seeking a qualified consultant or consulting team to lead this assessment.

## **Purpose of the Assignment**

The assessment aims to generate evidence on humanitarian needs, vulnerabilities and service gaps among crisis-affected populations, particularly persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups, to inform protection-centred, disability-inclusive and integrated humanitarian programming.

## **Objectives**

The assessment shall:

- Identify and analyse priority humanitarian needs and vulnerabilities.
- Assess barriers to accessing humanitarian assistance and essential services, particularly  
    for persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.
- Assess the availability, accessibility, quality and inclusiveness of essential services.
- Examine protection risks and inclusion concerns.
- Analyse existing services, referral pathways, coverage and response gaps.
- Identify geographic areas with the highest humanitarian needs through a comparative  
    analysis of severity, operational feasibility and CBM's potential added value.
- Establish the priority order of needs but also of geographic areas.
- Generate recommendations on geographic focus, sectoral priorities, targeting,  
    partnerships and implementation modalities for future humanitarian programming,  
    including ECHO HIP 2027.

## **Scope of Assessment**

The assessment will focus on selected conflict-, displacement- and epidemic-affected areas in  
eastern DRC and analyse:

- Needs and reintegration challenges of returnees.
- Opportunities for integrated multi-sector programming and referral pathways.
- Capacities of local actors, including OPDs, local NGOs and community-based  
    organisations.
- Community feedback systems, communication preferences and accountability  
    mechanisms.
- Humanitarian access constraints and operational feasibility.
- Community preparedness, surveillance and early warning systems.
- Environmental and climate-related risks affecting humanitarian programming.  
    Geographic scope :
- North Kivu (Masisi, Beni, Lubero)
- South Kivu (Kalehe)
- Mai-Ndombe (Kwamouth)

### *Thematic scope :*

The assessment should analyse current and emerging humanitarian needs, service gaps and  
trends affecting programming in 2027, including:

- Humanitarian needs and vulnerabilities.
- Access barriers to services and assistance.
- Availability and functionality of services and referral mechanisms.
- Areas and population groups with the highest unmet needs.
- Implications for future ECHO and other donor-funded interventions.

### *Key minimum sectors :*

- Health (+MHPSS)
- Protection
- GBV
- Food Security
- Education
- Nutrition
- WASH
- Disaster Preparedness (+Epidemic and Health Risks)

### *Cross-cutting themes*

- Disability Inclusion
- Gender and Age
- Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP)
- Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)
- Safeguarding and Child Safeguarding
- Protection Principles and Do No Harm
- Localisation and Community Engagement
- Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus

### *Priority Population Groups*

- IDPs
- Returnees
- Host Communities
- Women and Girls
- Children and Adolescents
- Older Persons
- Persons with Disabilities

## **Expected Methodology**

The consultant shall propose a mixed-method approach including:

- Secondary data review.
- Quantitative household surveys.
- KIIs.
- FGDs.
- Stakeholder consultations.
- Analysis of existing response capacities and gaps.
- Direct observation of selected services and community structures where feasible.

The methodology must ensure meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and comply  
with humanitarian principles, safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent, protection and Do  
No Harm standards.

## **Expected Deliverables**

The selected consultant/team will be expected to provide:

1. Inception Report, including methodology and workplan;
2. Data collection tools and protocols;
3. Preliminary findings presentation;

jobs.title: Psychiatrist or Clinical Psychologist - West Africa
jobs.body:
**Position summary:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is anticipating a project in West Africa with a focus on managing the flow of migrants into the region. Included in the project’s objectives will be structured movement and resettlement of migrants within and outside Guinea-Bissau, while providing basic food, shelter and other humanitarian assistance.

SFL is seeking a clinical psychologist to provide mental health and social support to migrants in West Africa. The clinical psychologist will be responsible for designing and implementing a psychological and psychosocial support program for migrants who are navigating displacement and resettlement. This role involves providing direct clinical care, occasional crisis intervention, and building the capacity of local staff to ensure culturally appropriate mental health services during the resettlement process. The position will be based in Bissau, Guinea-Bissau.

**Areas of Responsibility:**

- Conduct psychological assessments and provide professional mental health support to newly arrived and transitioning migrants, with referral to in-country medical professionals if needed.
- Develop and implement support protocols for individuals experiencing stress or trauma.
- Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, including medical staff as needed, to ensure a holistic approach to migrant well-being and basic needs.
- Conduct psychoeducational workshops to help migrants cope with acculturative stress, build resilience, and prepare for resettlement in new host countries.
- Maintain strictly confidential clinical records and monitor mental health trends within the migrant population to adapt programs and inform SFL management.

**Education and Experience Requirements:**

- Medical doctor degree (M.D., D.O., or M.B.B.S.) with Psychiatry residency, Master’s degree or Doctorate (Ph.D. or Psy.D.) in Clinical Psychology from an accredited institution.
- Valid professional license to practice clinical psychology in your home jurisdiction.
- Minimum of 3 to 5 years of post-graduate clinical experience, specifically focusing on trauma, displacement, or working with refugee/migrant populations.
- Must be fluent in English (written and spoken), with a working knowledge of Spanish. Additional language skills relevant to the demographic context (e.g., French, Portuguese) are a plus.
- Proven experience working in humanitarian emergencies, international development, or low-resource, post-conflict settings.
- Experience in cross-cultural counseling and effectively conducting clinical sessions with the assistance of language interpreters.

**Personal Skills and Abilities:**

- Exceptional cross-cultural communication skills and sensitivity to the diverse religious, cultural, and social backgrounds of multi-national migrants.
- Strong adaptability and psychological resilience, with the capacity to thrive in a dynamic and challenging physical environment with limited local amenities.
- High emotional intelligence and the ability to maintain strong professional boundaries to prevent burnout in a high-stress environment.
- Collaborative leadership style with the ability for capacity-building and empowering local staff for assistance.
- Sound judgment, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to make rapid clinical decisions independently in the event of crises.
- Commitment to the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, as well as the core mission of Shelter For Life International.

SFL is interested in applicants whose professional ethics, values, and determination to achieve impact are evident and aligned with organizational priorities.

Additional Notes:

- A minimum of 12 months' commitment to live and work in Guinea-Bissau is required.
- Applicants must be comfortable with travel within the project area.
- Competitive pay and benefits, including paid time off, ACA-compliant health insurance, and housing allowance.

Job description in PDF here: [https://shorturl.at/gYIwz](https://shorturl.at/gYIwz)

**About us:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is an international faith-based relief and development organization with over 30 years’ experience providing sustainable development and humanitarian assistance to post-conflict countries worldwide. We are currently operational in Afghanistan, The Gambia, and Ukraine, with headquarters located in Minnetonka, MN, USA. Our team provides support and assistance in the following areas:

1. Population Movement and Settlement
2. Public Infrastructure Reconstruction
3. Economic and Social Development

Our mission is to demonstrate God’s love by enabling people affected by conflict and disaster to restore their lives and rebuild their communities. To learn more about us, please visit [www.shelter.org](http://www.shelter.org/)
