- Experience in donor engagement, resource mobilisation, proposal development and results-based project management; and,
- Experience in engagement with regional economic communities, regional consultative processes, intergovernmental dialogue or the United Nations Network on Migration is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of IOM’s Route-Based Approach and its institutional framing, and of IOM’s strategic and planning instruments, including the Strategic Results Framework and regional strategies;
- Knowledge of migration governance frameworks, including the Migration Governance Indicators (MGI) and the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration;
- Knowledge of migration dynamics, actors and coordination structures along the region’s priority migration routes;
- Strong analytical, drafting and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to synthesise multi-country inputs into coherent products; and,
- Ability to work across reporting lines and to reconcile regional and Headquarters priorities.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Communications, Advocacy and External Engagement Manager
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As Communications, Advocacy and External Engagement Manager, you will provide strategic communications leadership and support to World Vision CAR by developing and implementing communication strategies that will strengthen organizational trust, reputation, visibility, advocacy influence, and fundraising efforts.

You will ensure high-quality content production, stakeholder engagement, media relations, and advocacy support while promoting World Vision's impact on children and communities.

You will develop and implement integrated communications strategies, strengthen World Vision’s brand and reputation, produce high-quality multimedia and child-focused content, and ensure effective management of digital platforms and social media. You will lead emergency communication preparedness and response, manage media, donor, and high-profile visits, provide strategic communications advice to senior leadership, and lead advocacy communications related to World Vision’s sectors, conflict, displacement, and protection. You will also strengthen internal communications by building staff communications capacity, promoting engagement and organizational culture, establishing systems for content generation and information sharing, training organizational spokespersons, producing emergency reports, SitReps, alerts, and declarations, and ensuring compliance with World Vision communications policies and branding standards.

You will contribute to external engagement and influence strategies, support national advocacy initiatives, engage local and international media, and develop advocacy messaging for humanitarian and development issues. You will lead the development and implementation of an integrated advocacy agenda across humanitarian, development, and grant-funded programming, ensuring coordinated advocacy efforts and alignment of organizational positions, messaging, and external engagement with World Vision’s humanitarian advocacy priorities, including protection, humanitarian access, accountability to affected populations (AAP), and localization. You will ensure advocacy efforts are grounded in evidence and child and community participation, linking humanitarian response and grants programming into one coherent advocacy narrative.

You will develop and implement an external engagement strategy and build strong relationships with donors, UN agencies, INGOs, government authorities, and local partners. You will represent World Vision in coordination forums and ensure that proposals and concept notes reflect advocacy and communication priorities. You will also develop and implement campaign strategies aligned with the ENOUGH Campaign objectives, coordinate advocacy initiatives targeting policymakers and key institutions, engage children, youth, faith leaders, communities, and civil society organizations, and facilitate awareness campaigns on child hunger, nutrition, and food security. You will build partnerships to strengthen collective action against child hunger and malnutrition, monitor campaign progress, document achievements, support media and communication activities, and promote child participation so that children’s voices are reflected in advocacy actions.

You will monitor and manage reputational risks, support crisis communication and incident response, protect World Vision’s brand and stakeholder trust, and coordinate with regional teams on sensitive issues. You will also supervise communications and advocacy staff, provide performance management and coaching, identify capacity gaps and implement development plans, and support the recruitment and onboarding of new team members.

**Requirements include:**

- A degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Humanitarian Studies, or a related field (Master's preferred).
- At least 5 years of experience in advocacy, communications, donor engagement, and policy influence.
- A minimum of 3 years in a management role within the humanitarian or development sector, preferably with INGOs.
- Experience working with government institutions, multilateral agencies, and donors; strong leadership and team management skills; ability to work independently under pressure in multicultural environments.
- Excellent communication and writing skills, fluency in English, good French communication skills, and a solid understanding of humanitarian principles, standards, and disaster management.
- A strong alignment with World Vision's Christian values, vision, and mission is essential, along with willingness to travel and work in field locations.
- Proven ability to develop and implement communication strategies, create high-quality content, and manage organizational messaging across multiple channels.
- Experience designing and implementing advocacy campaigns, developing policy briefs, and influencing decision-makers, including government, donors, and partner organizations
- Strong skills in media engagement, crisis communication, spokesperson preparation, and managing relationships with journalists and media outlets
- Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain strategic relationships with governments, NGOs, UN agencies, donors, private sector partners, and community leaders
- Proficiency in digital platforms, social media, content management systems, analytics tools, and managing multi-channel communication and advocacy campaigns.

**Travel and/or Work Environment, Language Requirement**

- Good physical health is required
- Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% of the time in the region
- English and French required

 **Applicant Types Accepted:** Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.title: Emergency Human Resources Coordinator
jobs.body:
To fulfill its mission of assistance to victims of conflicts, epidemics or natural disasters, OCG has created an Emergency Pool, whose members are experienced individuals capable of evaluating a humanitarian crisis, opening, closing and coordinating emergency projects.

The Emergency Human Resources Coordinator is a key member of this pool and reports directly to the Emergency Coordinator, as well as to the E-Cell HR Referent.

The successful candidate is expected to:

- Deploy rapidly in all contexts set by the Emergency cell
- Have the flexibility to assume different HR roles according to operational needs (HR Coordinator but also HR/Administration Manager)
- Gap fill in regular cells if required.

As a member of the Emergency Pool, the Emergency HR Coordinator must be available for deployment within 48 hours for short-term emergency interventions. You will be part of a multidisciplinary response team -including medical, paramedical, and support staff - mobilized for emergencies such as epidemics, armed conflicts, natural disasters, and other acute crises. You may also be involved in exploratory missions, short-term assignments within regular missions or gap filling in the Emergency Cell in Geneva HQ.

Job Description (but not limited to)

- Act as a strategic partner to Operations by contributing to mission planning and execution. Support the design of appropriate emergency organizational structures and ensure adequate HR capacity and sizing.
- Define, adapt, and oversee the implementation of human resources policies for emergency interventions, ensuring alignment with the operational context and challenges.
- Ensure MSF operates as a responsible employer within the mission. Oversee all HR management, administrative, and legal matters, proactively addressing HR-related risks and adapting processes to the emergency context.
- Is the technical referent for all HR and Administration related issues at Mission level (recruitment, management and development of teams, contracting and remuneration of national staff, follow up of daily workers, etc.). Coordinates the urgent recruitment of HR required for the mission. Ensures the timely deployment of critical staff in coordination with the E-Cell HR Referent.

- Monitor working conditions and staff wellbeing, with a focus on high-stress environments. In collaboration with the medical department, coordinate psychosocial support as needed.
- Design, recruit and train the HR teams at coordination and project level.
- Contribute to emergency preparedness and surge capacity planning by assessing HR risks and implementing appropriate mitigation strategies.
- Participate in exploratory missions and evaluations, upon request of the Ecell.

Your Profile

Required Skills and experience

**Field Experience**

- Minimum of 2 years in HR management in the field with MSF, gained through exposure to various contexts, including emergency contexts (population displacement, epidemic outbreaks, natural disasters and/or conflicts).
- At least one field experience with MSF in HR coordination (HR Coordinator or Deputy HR Coordinator).
- Ability to quickly evaluate an emergency on the ground and propose an adapted HR strategy.
- Experience in Finance management is an advantage.

**Strategic and Interpersonal Skills**

- Ability to work effectively in volatile and insecure environments, with strong resilience and stress management skills.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills
- Strong people management skills.
- Strong coordination and organizational skills.
- Strong adaptability and flexibility to navigate changing priorities, dynamic operational environments, and evolving team dynamics.
- Responsible behavior that contributes to the safety and integrity of everyone - prevent, report, and refuse any abusive behavior and/or behavior that goes against MSF's values.
- Ability to thrive in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, inclusive and non-discriminatory attitudes and behaviors.

**Language skills**

- Fluency in both French and English is highly desirable. Alternatively, candidates must demonstrate an excellent command of either language and at least B1 proficiency in the other.
- Knowledge of other mission languages is an advantage (Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic).
- Proficiency in an additional language, especially Spanish, Arabic, and/or Portuguese.

Terms of Employment

- Field-based contract. One year fixed-term contract, renewable based on operational needs and performance.
- Duration of field assignments: 4 weeks to 3 months (flexibility required according to needs).
- Accommodation and travel arrangements such as visa-related costs will be taken in charge by MSF.
- Comprehensive support and guidance will be provided by dedicated technical referents throughout the assignment.

**We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment.**

jobs.title: ETHIOPIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - TIGRAY
jobs.body:
**Desired start date: 01/12/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**  
**Location: Adwa - Tigray Region**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION:

Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region).

In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors.

In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement.

SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area.

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone.  
Representation and Internal / external communication:  
The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings  
The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures   
The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep).

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES :

Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements.

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

-Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams.   
-Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans.   
-Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components.   
-Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring.   
-Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies.   
-Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context  
-Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making.

YOUR PROFIL :

DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required.

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years

EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes.

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection).

LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset.

SI WILL OFFER YOU :

**A salaried position:**

  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions:**

Guest House conditions :

\- There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit.  
-Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa  
-Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa :

\- Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

jobs.title: Oficial de Recuperación Económica - Medios de Vida (Caracas -Personal Nacional) - Republicado
jobs.body:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Oficial de Recuperación Económica altamente calificado/a con sede en Caracas, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

En el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto ocurrido en el mes de junio 2026, DRC está abriendo una nueva oficina de implementación en Caracas, independiente de la oficina de país, para atender las necesidades de las poblaciones afectadas. Para ello, busca incorporar un/a Oficial de Recuperación Económica – Medios de Vida será responsable de implementar de manera efectiva y oportuna las actividades de los programas de Recuperación Económica de DRC en Venezuela.

**Objetivo general del puesto**

Bajo la supervisión del/la Team Leader de Recuperación Económica o del Gerente de Recuperación Económica, el/la Oficial de Recuperación Económica – Medios de Vida será responsable de implementar de manera efectiva y oportuna las actividades de los programas de Recuperación Económica de DRC en Venezuela. Esto incluye el acompañamiento técnico en terreno para el fortalecimiento de emprendedores, micronegocios y otras iniciativas productivas en comunidades vulnerables, expuestas a riesgos de protección y desastres, así como el desarrollo de habilidades blandas y competencias para el emprendimiento, la empleabilidad y la generación sostenible de ingresos, promoviendo su vinculación con oportunidades de mercado y empleo.

Asimismo, el/la Oficial será responsable de facilitar procesos de orientación ocupacional, fortalecimiento de competencias para la empleabilidad, y articulación con actores del sector privado, instituciones de formación técnica y otros aliados estratégicos que contribuyan a la inserción laboral y recuperación económica de las Personas de Interés (PDI). Igualmente, facilitará la transferencia de metodologías de formación a socios locales mediante herramientas desarrolladas por DRC y garantizará la correcta recopilación de los medios de verificación necesarios para el seguimiento, monitoreo y rendición de cuentas de las actividades implementadas.

También podrá apoyar en la implementación de actividades del proyecto en terreno, principalmente en la preparación y ejecución de las jornadas de distribución de alimentos, así como en procesos logísticos, comunitarios y de documentación garantizando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos y directrices de DRC.

El/la Oficial promoverá una programación integrada y articulada con los equipos de Protección, WASH y Preparación para Desastres, asegurando intervenciones intersectoriales y de calidad en todas las etapas del proyecto. Además, será responsable de coordinar efectivamente con el equipo de Recuperación Económica, socios locales, instituciones públicas, centros de formación y empleadores potenciales, asegurando el cumplimiento del plan de acción, el logro de resultados y el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia económica de las comunidades atendidas.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Identificación de actividades propias del sector de Medios de Vida**

- Liderar diagnósticos socioeconómicos y de mercado para identificar cadenas productivas, ecosistemas de actores claves del sector público y privado, y oportunidades de inclusión financiera (instituciones, banca, sector privado) que fomenten la autosuficiencia y resiliencia de las Personas de Interés (PDI).
- Evaluar la viabilidad técnica, social, ambiental y económica de propuestas de generación de ingresos, asegurando que los proyectos de medios de vida sean sostenibles, pertinentes culturalmente y sensibles a los riesgos de protección y desastres.
- Contribuir con datos del contexto local para el ajuste y formulación de propuestas, garantizando la integración del enfoque de Recuperación Económica con otros sectores (Protección, WASH y Preparación para Desastres).
- Con el apoyo y la orientación de su supervisor y coordinación técnica, sugerir ideas innovadoras y técnicas adecuadas para las intervenciones de Recuperación Económica en función del contexto.

**Implementación técnica y logística**

- Responsable de implementar la planificación, ejecución, seguimiento y cierre técnico de las actividades de medios de vida (focalización, diagnósticos, selección, formación, entregas, encuestas PDM, líneas base/salida y gestión de bases de datos), en coordinación con el Team Leader o Gerente de Recuperación económica, y con los equipos de Logística y finanzas para asegurar el cumplimiento del plan de acción y el reporte oportuno de los indicadores propuestos.
- Diseñar e implementar procesos de formación en planes de negocios, habilidades para el empleo, orientación vocacional, habilidades blandas, planes de marketing, estructuras de costos, gestión y educación financiera. Entre las actividades se contempla la facilitación directa, la Formación a Formadores (ToT) para socios y la gestión logística/financiera necesaria para su ejecución.
- Con la orientación técnica de la coordinación de Recuperación Económica, en conjunto con la supervisión del Team Leader o Gerente de Recuperación Económica, ser el punto focal de alianzas estratégicas con actores del sector privado, público o institucional para actividades propias de medios de vida, como lo pueden ser alianzas estratégicas para emprendedores.
- Realizar planes de seguimiento a las PdI relacionados al incremento de su generación de ingresos y de medición de indicadores establecidos en el programa de Recuperación Económica.
- Identificar, coordinar y entregar apoyos en especie (como insumos productivos, herramientas, equipos, etc.) de acuerdo con las necesidades socioeconómicas y productivas identificadas, así como con los lineamientos técnicos de la coordinación y el enfoque de protección.
- Apoyar la planificación y ejecución de las jornadas de distribución y demás actividades logísticas del proyecto, incluyendo la recepción, descarga, verificación de cantidades y calidad de los insumos, la organización y acondicionamiento de los sitios de atención, el control de inventarios y materiales en terreno.
- Participar en la preparación de informes mensuales/trimestrales/anuales aportando análisis técnicos sobre el componente y las actividades realizadas, así como en la orientación técnica para elaborar presupuestos de este componente en formulaciones de proyectos.
- Transferir conocimientos, acompañar, hacer seguimiento sobre la implementación de programas de Recuperación Económica implementadas por organizaciones locales, utilizando metodologías desarrolladas por DRC. La transferencia de conocimientos y de acompañamiento incluyen las fases de focalización, formación, evaluaciones de planes de negocio, y seguimiento de la evolución de los participantes.

**Participación comunitaria**

- Facilitar procesos de información, convocatoria y participación de la comunidad que permitan el acceso y la aceptación comunitaria.
- Monitorear la participación de grupos vulnerables (mujeres, personas mayores, personas con discapacidad) y necesidades específicas para su participación
- Garantizar la calidad, participación comunitaria y mecanismos de rendición de cuentas en la ejecución de actividades.

**Monitoreo y reporte**

- Garantizar la compilación de los medios de verificación requeridos y datos cualitativos de las actividades del proyecto.
- Aplicar encuestas para el registro, línea base, PDMs, línea de salida y otras encuestas necesarias para la implementación del proyecto.
- Reportar a los supervisores, incidentes, retrasos o cualquier otro desafío o reto para la implementación de las actividades a nivel programático, logístico y/o financiero.
- Monitorear el avance de las personas beneficiarias, documentar resultados y generar lecciones aprendidas.
- Aportar a la documentación de buenas prácticas, historias de vida o casos de éxito.
- Contribuir a la elaboración de informes técnicos y narrativos según los requerimientos del proyecto.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- 2 años de experiencia relevante en trabajo relacionado con medios de vida, especialmente con la recuperación económica de emprendimientos, empleos y fuentes de ingresos. Experiencia desarrollando estructuras de costos para pequeños negocios, planes de marketing y/o fortaleciendo habilidades blandas para emprender es valorado.
- Experiencia en trabajo articulado con proyectos de protección, preparación para desastres, WASH, trabajo social, derechos humanos u otro trabajo similar de terreno, relacionado a una ONG u otra organización sin fines de lucro.
- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo con comunidades en zonas urbanas de difícil acceso, personas desplazadas, y/o migrantes y refugiadas.
- Experiencia en la facilitación de modelos de aprendizaje híbridos y uso de herramientas digitales (como Moodle) para la capacitación de poblaciones vulnerables es valorada.
- Experiencia y capacidad para relacionarse con las personas, interactuar con equipos multidisciplinarios, resolver conflictos y gestionar dinámicas de grupos.
- Habilidades y experiencia en capacitación y desarrollo de capacidades de personal de organizaciones sin fines de lucro con conocimiento básico o intermedio en medios de vida.
- Habilidades de redacción de informes y otros documentos de comunicación interna.
- Excelente habilidad en MS Word, Excel y PowerPoint.
- Experiencia en manejar bases de datos.

**Educación:**

Título universitario pertinente relacionado a administración de empresas, contabilidad, economía, desarrollo humano, trabajo social, psicología, mercadeo, docencia o cualificación profesional equivalente.

**Idioma:**

- Ingles (A2 Deseable)
- Español

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 6 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.
- Contratación nacional.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Viernes 16 de Octubre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio:** Octubre 2026

**Nota:**

- Nos reservamos el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha indicada de cierre de postulaciones
- Debido a una contratación de emergencia, DRC no se obliga a enviar las notificaciones de rechazo a los candidatos que no sean considerados en el proceso

jobs.title: Mission France - Médiateur.ice Interculturel.le - Basé à Dunkerque F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e : Médiateur.ice Interculturel.le - Basé à Dunkerque.

**CONTEXTE**

La Mission France de MSF porte assistance aux personnes migrantes en situation de grande vulnérabilité sociale, médicale et/ou psychique sur le territoire français et mène des actions de plaidoyer pour faciliter leur accès au droit commun.

Depuis décembre 2017, la Mission France apporte une assistance aux personnes migrantes.

Elle assure la prise en charge médicale, psychologique, juridique et sociale des personnes exclues des soins de santé et plaide en faveur de l'accès aux soins des personnes étrangères vulnérables, notamment les femmes vivant dans les campements du dunkerquois.

La Mission France compte actuellement trois projets :

- En Ile-de-France. Le projet est ouvert depuis décembre 2017. Orienté dès les origines sur la prise en charge médicale, psychologique, sociale et juridique des mineurs non accompagnés en recours (accueil de jour et hébergement), il a connu une évolution importante en se spécialisant sur le public des jeunes filles en recours de reconnaissance de minorité. S’y ajoute une activité de clinique mobile animée par une équipe de bénévoles
- A Calais et sur le Littoral Nord. Ouvert à l’été 2023. Accueil de jour pour mineurs non accompagnés offrant répit et activités ; cliniques mobiles à destination du public général (adultes, familles, mineurs), incluant des activités de santé mentale. Des activités saisonnières viennent compléter les activités avec, du printemps à l’automne, une activité de maraudes littorales à destination des personnes exilées rescapées de naufrage et en hiver une activité de mise à l’abri des personnes les plus vulnérables.
- A Dunkerque. Le projet vise à répondre aux besoins croissants des femmes, jeunes filles et familles exilées vivant dans des conditions extrêmement précaires sur le Littoral Dunkerquois. En partenariat étroit avec le Refugee Women’s Centre, il se concentre sur la prise en charge médicale en santé des femmes (gynécologie, suivi de grossesse, santé sexuelle et reproductive), une prise en charge en santé mentale, un dispositif d’abri d’urgence pour les femmes seules, le renforcement de la détection et de la prise en charge des violences sexuelles, ainsi qu’un volet de documentation et plaidoyer sur les violences et l’absence de services essentiels sur le territoire.

Le volet communication et plaidoyer est central sur cette mission qui évolue dans un pays ayant les moyens d’accueillir dignement mais qui néglige volontairement les populations migrantes.

**Mission**

Soutenir la communication et l'interaction entre les bénéficiaires (migrant.es et réfugié.es) et l’équipe pluridisciplinaire, en traitant les conséquences des barrières linguistiques, des différences socioculturelles et de la discrimination, en suivant les protocoles et les procédures de MSF, afin d'améliorer l'accès à des soins de santé de qualité et à d'autres services pertinents et de permettre de mieux comprendre les déterminants socioculturels locaux.

**Responsabilités**

Faciliter la relation entre les patient.e.s et les prestataires de soins impliqués dans les consultations médicales, de soin de santé somatique et mentale ainsi qu’entre les patient.e.s et la prise en charge par l’équipe sociojuridique :

- Fournir un interprétariat de qualité entre l’équipe pluridisciplinaire et les patientes dans leur langue maternelle, en prenant en compte l’aspect interculturel, la sensibilité et la clarté de la communication entre les parties.  
    Aider l’équipe pluridisciplinaire et les patient.e.s à remédier aux conséquences négatives des différences socioculturelles et identifier et signaler les obstacles qui entravent l'équité et l'égalité dans l'accès aux services.
- Accompagner et suivre les patient.e.s vers les structures d'orientation (établissements de santé et de soins sociaux) si nécessaire.
- Soutenir l'intervention thérapeutique/sociale en partageant avec l’équipe pluridisciplinaire les aspects pertinents du contexte culturel du patient, en agissant en tant qu'intermédiaire culturel.le.
- Participer aux réunions pluridisciplinaires.
- En collaboration avec les autres membres de l'équipe du projet, fournir des informations aux patientes sur le fonctionnement du système de soins et des autres services de soutien (abri, nourriture, transport, soutien juridique) fournis par MSF et d'autres acteurs, dans le but de favoriser la responsabilisation et l'autonomie des patientes.

Contribuer à la compréhension du contexte et à la collecte de données sur les questions médicales et sociojuridiques, en accordant une attention particulière aux vulnérabilités, afin de fournir des informations fiables pour la prise de décisions opérationnelles :

- Assurer une traduction linguistique et interculturelle de qualité lors de la collecte de témoignages à des fins de plaidoyer et de communication.
- Apporter un soutien à la mise en oeuvre d'évaluations ou d'enquêtes, le cas échéant.
- Rapporter toutes les informations importantes exprimées par les patientes et les communautés, en garantissant la confidentialité à tout moment.
- Apporter un soutien à l'analyse des médias et à la création de contenus à des fins de communication.

**Responsabilités spécifiques à la mission France**

Sous la responsabilité de la Coordinatrice projet Dunkerque et en collaboration avec une équipe pluridisciplinaire, le.la médiateur.ice interculturel.le :

- Participe à la réflexion et l’adaptation des activités d’aller-vers mises en oeuvre par MSF sur le littoral Nord, ainsi que plus spécifiquement des activités de santé sexuelle et reproductive sur le Dunkerquois.
- Accompagne les différent.es professionnel.les (soignant.es, pyschologue.s, travailleur.seuses sociaux.les) en tant qu’intermédiaire linguistique et interculturel.le pour assurer un interprétariat en direct lors des consultations, des activités externes, des cliniques mobiles, des groupes de discussions, sensibilisation, formations, des maraudes, des activités d’allers vers et autre cas échéant et permet aux collaborateur.ices d’offrir une qualité de soins et/ou de soutien psychosocial à la hauteur des standards de l’association.
- Sensibilise le reste de l’équipe à des codes culturels qui pourraient être une barrière à l’accès aux services.
- Accompagne dans les activités pour l’identifications des besoins exprimés lors des activités.
- Participer à l’éducation à la santé des femmes et à la promotion des services en santé sexuelle et reproductive
- Tester, diffuser et animer des supports et activités de sensibilisation et d'éducation à la santé auprès des communautés.
- Apporte un soutien à l’élaboration d’outils linguistiques et communicationnels en support aux activités à destination des personnes accompagnés, en collaboration avec l’équipe pluridisciplinaire.
- Participer à l’élaboration des plans de sensibilisation et de mobilisation communautaire.
- Contribuer à l’identification des groupes cibles et des canaux de communication appropriés.
- Animer des séances de sensibilisation, causeries éducatives et campagnes communautaires.
- Assurer la promotion des bonnes pratiques de santé au sein des communautés.
- Mesurer le niveau de compréhension et l'adoption des messages clés.
- Documenter les retours, difficultés et bonnes pratiques observées.
- Participe à la formation des équipes partenaires et/ou du personnes accompagnées dans le cadre des activités sur le nord littoral et en particulier sur le Dunkerquois
- Contribue au recueil de témoignages et s’inscrit dans la démarche MSF en termes de communication et de plaidoyer concernant les enjeux humanitaires
- Participe à la collecte et la capitalisation des données individuelles de suivi des situations médico-psycho-sociales des personnes rencontrées.
- Participe aux réunions pluridisciplinaires.•Participe la communication et la coordination adéquate avec les autres organismes et institutions déployés ou consultés.
- Soutient les autres activités des projets de Calais et du Littoral Nord en cas d’absence prolongée de besoins sur le Dunkerquois.

jobs.title: Regional Humanitarian Access and Safety Adviser (Colombia, Venezuela, Honduras nationals)
jobs.body:
All NRC employees are expected to work in accordance with the organization’s values. To be dedicated, innovative, inclusive and accountable are attitudes and beliefs that shall guide our actions and relationships. NRC has a commitment to safety and wellbeing and together we build a positive working culture to feel valued, empowered, supported, safe and have a sense of belonging. NRC does not tolerate employees exploiting or abusing people and has zero tolerance to inaction.

## What we are looking for

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking a **highly qualified,** **resilient, and dynamic professional** to take up the role of **Regional Security Adviser for Latin America**. This role is responsible for **developing, evaluating and monitoring NRC’s regional security risk management approach in accordance with global standards, with an overall objective to enable the delivery of a safe and principled humanitarian response.**

While NRC has largely been successful with regards to delivering assistance to people in need, security and access constraints pose a challenge to humanitarian operations across the region. Conflict and violence, environmental and physical challenges, bureaucratic obstacles, interference in humanitarian operations, are all obstacles to delivery of services and protection to displacement affected people. **The Regional HAS Adviser plays a fundamental role in security risk management, in capacity building of HAS colleagues and country management, as well as in operationalizing Duty of Care and humanitarian access strategies across the region.**

## What you will do

- Promote and stimulate a culture of enabling a safe and principled humanitarian response, in line with the Humanitarian Principles and taking Programme Criticality into account.
- Ensure quality recruitment, induction, guidance, support, mentoring, capacity building, and development of HAS staff in the country offices to strengthen operational leadership.
- Maintain a detailed understanding of the context within the region, including analysis and forecasting, and brief regional management on key security developments, access impediments, and emerging threats within the region. Work with management to ensure that the relevant mitigation measures are in place.
- In collaboration with People & Organisation, the Regional Head of Operational Support and the Regional Director, ensure Duty of Care standards are upheld, reflecting the diversity of the NRC workforce in the region.
- Provide technical review of HAS management documents for all countries in the region to ensure they comply with NRC standards, including Security Risk Assessments (SRA), Contingency Planning, Medical Emergency Plan, and Hibernation, Evacuation and Relocation Plans.
- Technically support the development and implementation of access strategies across the region, ensuring a systematized approach to engagement.

Please download the [detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCKG0SB_f8mQ7MFr7J3vCnMAQZ0PuLW-2rmcy7PXsd-7ME?e=636y5s)to learn more about the position.

What you will bring

- **Minimum five years of experience from working as a manager in a humanitarian/recovery context.**
- **Advanced knowledge of principles and practices in broad humanitarian action, NGO safety and risk management, humanitarian access, and civil-military coordination**
- Strong understanding of Humanitarian Principles and their application in programmatic and advocacy responses
- Previous experience from working in complex and volatile contexts.
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities.
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile.
- **Fluency in English and Spanish, both written and verbal.**
- Valid driver’s license.
- Prior work experience at the country level, with programme implementation as a plus. Country Director and Area Manager are relevant profiles in addition to Access and/or Security Manager profiles.
- Experience or qualifications in humanitarian access and negotiations.
- Experience in risk management for implementing partners and remote management.
- Prior experience as a trainer
- Working proficiency in French is an asset.

## What we offer

- **Duty station: Bogotá, Colombia**
- **Contract: fixed national contract Sept 2027**
- Travel: 30%
- Salary/benefits**: grade 9 on NRC’s salary scale**, with accompanying terms and conditions
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

## Important information about the application process

- *Internal candidates only: please click on the suitcase icon labelled “I am an employee” to be redirected to NRC’s internal careers site.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email aela.recruitment@nrc.no with the job title as the subject line.

## Why NRC?

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We contribute to the development of policy aiming to protect the rights of the displaced and we call for increased humanitarian funding and engagement on processes that will generate structural changes in protection and assistance in the region.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation dedicated to protecting the rights of displaced and affected people during crises. NRC delivers high-quality programmes to support people forced to flee, helping them rebuild their lives and establish a new future. NRC provides immediate humanitarian assistance, prevents further displacement, and contributes to durable solutions. It operates across both new and protracted crises across 40 countries.

 NRC’s Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS) function’s purpose is to enable principled humanitarian response in a safe manner, for the communities and partners we work with and our staff. The Regional Humanitarian Access and Safety Adviser serves as the lead technical resource on safety and security, access, and crisis management within the region. This function is line managed by the Regional Head of Operations Support and managed in a technical line by the Global HAS Director. This role acts as the technical supervisor for Country HAS Managers or equivalent within the region and serves as a core member of the regional management team and crisis management team.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee.

Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

### About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: A CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT SCREENING, ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION FOR INCLUSIVE WELLBEING FOR CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL EDUCATION NEEDS AND DISABILITIES .
source: Adventist Development and Relief Agency International
jobs.body:
**REQUEST FOR CONSULTANTS**

The Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA) is a global humanitarian organization with a mission to work with people in poverty and distress to create just and positive change. ADRA Somalia belongs to the worldwide network, comprised of more than 130 supporting and implementing country offices. ADRA Somalia is seeking to recruit a consultant to undertake the following assignment: **SCREENING, ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION FOR INCLUSIVE WELLBEING FOR CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL EDUCATION NEEDS AND DISABILITIES**

1. **Background Information**

In many contexts, even where there is strong commitment to promoting the rights, inclusion and wellbeing of children with disabilities, adequate systems for identification, assessment, referral and individualized support remain limited. Children with disabilities have diverse needs that may relate to physical, sensory, intellectual, developmental, communication, behavioral or psychosocial functioning. Without appropriate mechanisms to identify these needs and connect children and their families to suitable services, many conditions may remain unrecognized or inadequately addressed. Early identification, comprehensive assessment and targeted follow-up are therefore essential to ensuring that children with disabilities receive appropriate support and can participate meaningfully in family and community life.

Disability and poverty are deeply interconnected, with persons with disabilities often experiencing disproportionate levels of social and economic exclusion and reduced access to essential services, livelihood opportunities and civic participation. Children from economically vulnerable, displaced or otherwise marginalized households may face additional barriers to accessing assessment, rehabilitation, assistive devices and specialized support. In some cases, relatively straightforward interventions can significantly improve functioning and independence. For example, unidentified visual impairment may restrict a child's ability to undertake everyday activities but may be substantially addressed through appropriate assessment and corrective devices. Similarly, hearing, mobility, communication, cognitive, developmental and psychosocial difficulties may remain undetected or unsupported where appropriate screening and referral mechanisms are unavailable.

Children with less visible disabilities, including intellectual, developmental, communication, behavioral and psychosocial difficulties, are particularly vulnerable to remaining unidentified. Their challenges may be misunderstood or attributed to behaviour, personality or other factors, resulting in stigma, isolation or inadequate support. Families and caregivers may also lack information about available services or may face financial, geographic and social barriers to accessing specialized assistance. Without timely identification and intervention, these challenges can become more pronounced and adversely affect children's development, independence, wellbeing, social participation and future opportunities.

There is therefore a clear need to strengthen disability inclusion beyond any single sector or service. A holistic and systematic approach is required that considers the child within the broader family and community environment and recognizes the interconnected nature of health, protection, psychosocial wellbeing, rehabilitation, social inclusion and economic vulnerability. Such an approach should strengthen the capacity of relevant institutions, service providers, communities and families to identify children with disabilities, understand their individual needs and facilitate access to appropriate interventions and services.

While broader improvements in accessibility and inclusion can benefit many children, some barriers experienced by children with disabilities require specialized and individualized responses. These may include functional assessments, assistive devices, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech and communication support, psychosocial services, medical referrals, caregiver support and adaptations to the physical and social environment. Effective support therefore requires mechanisms that can identify individual needs and translate assessment findings into practical interventions.

Strengthening these systems requires clear and accessible pathways for screening, assessment, referral, intervention and follow-up. It also requires appropriate coordination among relevant government institutions, service providers, community structures, families and other stakeholders. Addressing gaps in accessibility, technical capacity, service availability and referral mechanisms will contribute to an environment in which children with disabilities can exercise their rights, enhance their functioning and independence, participate more fully in their communities and achieve improved overall wellbeing.

1. **Rationale for Disability Assessment and Intervention**

Children with disabilities continue to experience significant barriers to accessing essential services, participating fully in their communities and realizing their rights and potential. The number, characteristics and specific support needs of children with disabilities remain inadequately documented in Somalia, limiting the ability of families, service providers and relevant institutions to plan and provide appropriate assistance. These challenges are particularly pronounced among vulnerable and marginalized populations, including internally displaced children, children living in rural and nomadic communities, working children, orphans and children from economically disadvantaged households. Gender, displacement, poverty and geographic isolation can further compound disability-related vulnerabilities and should therefore be considered when identifying and responding to individual needs.

Promoting disability inclusion requires more than identifying the presence of an impairment. Children with disabilities should have opportunities to participate meaningfully in family and community life, access appropriate services and support, develop their capabilities and achieve greater independence and wellbeing. This requires a holistic approach that recognizes each child's individual circumstances, strengths and needs while addressing the physical, social, economic, communication and attitudinal barriers that may restrict participation.

Comprehensive assessment is an important component of early identification and intervention for children with disabilities, developmental delays and other functional difficulties. A structured assessment process can help determine a child's functional abilities and support needs and identify appropriate interventions, assistive devices, specialized services and referral pathways. Assessments should consider relevant areas of functioning, including mobility, vision, hearing, communication, cognition, behaviour, psychosocial wellbeing, self-care, social interaction and participation in everyday activities.

Assessment should be undertaken with a clear understanding of its purpose and should inform subsequent intervention planning, implementation, referral and progress monitoring. It should also consider the child's family and living environment, recognizing that parents and caregivers play an important role in identifying challenges, understanding the child's day-to-day functioning and implementing recommended support.

Assessment processes should therefore be individualized, child-centred, inclusive and sensitive to age, gender, disability and contextual vulnerabilities. Most importantly, assessment should not be treated as an end in itself but as the starting point for practical action. Findings should lead to appropriate and feasible interventions, referrals and follow-up mechanisms that strengthen children's functioning, independence, participation, protection and overall wellbeing.

1. **Consultancy Objective**

The objective of the assignment is to gather information for decision-making and intervention in the following four areas:

1. Screening.
2. Recommending intervention.
3. Individual program planning and implementation.
4. Progress monitoring and evaluation.
5. **Scope of Work**

Assessment teams must consider the purpose of each assessment and gather initial information at the onset of the process. The following are some general considerations, which will vary depending on the purpose of the assessment.

- What is the purpose of this assessment, or why is it being conducted (for example, screening, recommending intervention, program planning and implementation, progress monitoring, program evaluation)?
    - What are the characteristics of the child (for example, age, physical abilities, communication skills, temperament, delay or disability)?
    - Who will take the lead or coordinate the assessment (for example, early childhood special educator, physical therapist, speech–language pathologist)?
    - Where will the assessment sessions take place (for example, home, childcare program, classroom, playground)?
    - Who will be involved in the assessment (for example, parents, other family members, early childhood special educator, related service practitioners), and what roles will these individuals assume (for example, facilitator, observer, assessor)?
    - When will the assessment sessions take place (for example, in the morning, after child’s nap)?
    - How will the assessment be conducted (for example, formal testing, observation, interview)?
    - What areas of development or content will be assessed? Will all integrated developmental domains or content areas be the focus of the assessment?
    - What assessment instrument(s) will be used (for example, formal test, observational checklist, play- based measure, family interview)?
    - How will the assessment area(s) be set up (for example, amount of space needed, equipment or materials needed)?
    - What skills or behaviors are important to the child’s family, and what are the family’s priorities (for example, walking, talking, social skills, eating, toileting, literacy)?
    - What skills or behaviors are important to the child in his or her environment (for example, communicating, toileting, turn-taking, following directions)?
    - What adaptations are necessary for the child to display optimal skills (for example, use of an alternative communication system, adaptive seating, assistive technology)?

1. **Deliverables**

The following services and outputs are expected:

1. Detailed work plan for undertaking the assessment.
    1. Assessment Report and Debrief on the findings
    2. Proposed intervention e.g. (type of equipment, availability, estimated price) other recommended support.
    3. Workplan on the way forward
2. **Supervision and Management**

ADRA Somalia

1. **Timeframe**: The assignment will be conducted over a duration of **40 days** during the months of October 2026 and November 2026.

Proposals should include:

1. Detailed description of proposed approach and methodology
2. Projected budget – including projected travel and in-country accommodation and subsistence costs.
3. Short overview of how the candidate (s) meets the qualifications, experience and skills requirements
4. **Qualifications and Experience of the Preferred Consultant**

The assignment may be undertaken by an individual consultant, consultancy firm, or multidisciplinary team with expertise in disability screening, functional assessment, rehabilitation and individualized intervention planning.

The preferred consultant/team should meet the following requirements:

- Hold an advanced university degree in a relevant field such as rehabilitation sciences, occupational therapy, physiotherapy, psychology, developmental psychology, speech and language therapy, public health, social work, disability studies, medicine, nursing or another closely related discipline.
- Have at least five (5) years of demonstrated professional experience in disability screening, functional assessment, rehabilitation, early intervention, assistive technology, case management or related disability-inclusive programming.
- Demonstrate practical experience conducting comprehensive assessments of children with disabilities, developmental delays or functional difficulties, including identification of individual support and intervention needs.
- Have demonstrated experience assessing functional needs across areas such as mobility, vision, hearing, communication, cognition, developmental functioning, psychosocial wellbeing, behaviour, self-care and activities of daily living.
- Demonstrate experience in recommending appropriate assistive devices and technologies, including mobility aids, visual and hearing support, communication devices, adaptive equipment and other individualized solutions.
- Have experience developing individualized intervention, referral and follow-up plans based on assessment findings.
- Demonstrate knowledge of available rehabilitation, health, psychosocial, protection and disability-support services and experience establishing or utilizing referral pathways for children requiring specialized assistance.
- Have a strong understanding of child safeguarding, informed consent, confidentiality, protection and ethical standards applicable when working with children and persons with disabilities.
- Demonstrate experience working with vulnerable and marginalized populations, including internally displaced persons, rural and nomadic communities, economically vulnerable households and other crisis-affected populations.
- Previous professional experience in Somalia is highly desirable. Familiarity with the Somali context, including available disability services, cultural considerations and barriers affecting persons with disabilities, will be a strong advantage.
- Demonstrate strong skills in data collection, analysis, documentation and preparation of high-quality technical reports and practical recommendations.
- Demonstrate the ability to engage effectively with children, parents and caregivers, community structures, government institutions, service providers and humanitarian/development actors.

**Mandatory Statutory and Compliance Requirements**

- Consultants/firms must be legally eligible to undertake consultancy services in Somalia and must submit the applicable registration and statutory documentation.
- A valid Somalia Tax Compliance Certificate (TCC) issued by the relevant tax authority is mandatory and must be submitted as part of the application. Proposals that do not provide a valid Somalia Tax Compliance Certificate may be considered non-responsive.
- The consultant/firm should also disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest and confirm its commitment to ADRA's safeguarding, protection, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and other applicable policies and codes of conduct.

1. **Submission of Proposals**

To achieve the objectives of the assignment, the consultant will be expected to take complete responsibility for all the activities identified in the TOR. The Technical Proposal should contain a complete description and explanation of the proposed methodology for the Assignment (work plan), timelines and any other resources that the consultant will make available to effectively execute the assignment.

The Financial Proposal should stipulate the professional fees, travel, taxes, etc for the assignment. All fee and costs are to be expressed in USD.

jobs.title: Casework Supervisor
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:**   
The Casework Supervisor manages staff providing direct client services across the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR) and Refugee Social Service (RSS) case management program. The Casework Supervisor plans programming, coordinates service delivery, supervises a team, ensures program goals are met, and satisfies budgetary, compliance, and reporting responsibilities for the assigned portfolio. This position is based in Louisville, Kentucky, with regular on-site presence within the office.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Staff Supervision responsibilities**

- Lead and develop direct service staff through facilitation of team meetings and individual supervision, including coaching and goal setting.
- Liaise regularly with HQ colleagues for guidance, case consultations, direct financial assistance, and other support as needed, and share relevant information with the casework team.
- Cultivate a respectful and supportive environment for team members and clients.
- Recruit, train, and manage the team in accordance with IRC’s People Manager Standards.
- Carry out timely, professional interventions to ensure responsive, appropriate, and client-centered service delivery.
- Train direct reports on using IRC systems such as Integra, ETO, and IRIS.
- Representing IRC in public, professional, and governmental fora as needed.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Service Delivery**

- Guide PIR program implementation and ensure all required services are completed in a timely manner.
- Assign cases to caseworkers and manage timely provision of services including airport pickups, provision of safe, sanitary, and affordable housing, home visits, school enrollment, domestic health assessments, and connection to community resources as applicable.
- Supervise the RSS Case Management Program, including staff referrals, connection of clients to services, and tracking client participation and progress
- Ensure follow-up on all necessary services, including application to public benefits as applicable, referrals to immigration services, applications for Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and medical and mental health needs.
- Provide oversight so each client receives at least one meaningful interaction every 30 days during their service period.
- Ensure case closeout procedures are followed once a client has reached the goals of their program.

**Partnership Building**

- Manage relationships with property owners and managers to expand access to sources of affordable housing.
- Collaborate with colleagues to encourage timely internal referrals for additional services, such as employment, immigration services, and intensive case management.
- Identify and maintain relationships with local government and community-based organizations to connect clients with necessary benefits and services.
- Develop relationships with community resources such as shelters for temporary housing, domestic violence shelters, mental health providers, and medical specialists.
- Develop and maintain vendor relationships that create budgetary savings and improve efficiency.

**Documentation, Reporting and Contract Compliance**

- Ensure that case file documentation is maintained in compliance with contract requirements.
- Guide the timely implementation of program updates as needed.

jobs.title: ReDSS Kenya Policy Coordinator
jobs.body:
**About ReDSS**

The Regional Durable Solutions Secretariat (ReDSS) is a coalition of 14 NGOs working in the search of durable solutions in East Africa. ReDSS Secretariat is hosted by DRC and based in Nairobi with a country unit in Somalia and Ethiopia. ReDSS is an interagency coordination and information hub that focuses on research and knowledge management, program support, capacity development, learning, and policy influencing. The ReDSS Steering committee is composed of DRC, IRC and NRC. For more information [http://www.regionaldss.org/](http://www.regionaldss.org/)

**Overall purpose of the role:**

The ReDSS Kenya Policy Coordinator will be responsible to implement the advocacy and policy strategy at national and local levels, working with a wide range of stakeholders to ensure sustainable solutions for refugees and hosts in Kenya. S/he will work with the Kenya Manager as necessary to support the overall development of ReDSS’ work in Kenya, including representing ReDSS members in relevant forums and coordination platforms.

**Responsibilities:**

**Advocacy and Policy Influencing**

• Implement and monitor ReDSS Kenya advocacy strategies at national and county levels and ensure frequent updates based on changing dynamics

• Monitor and analyze relevant legislation and policy changes, providing timely analysis and recommendations to ReDSS members and partners

• Build and maintain strategic relationships with government, development, humanitarian, civil society and other relevant stakeholders to advance ReDSS policy and advocacy priorities

• Contribute to the generation and translation of evidence and learning into clear advocacy positions and policy recommendations

**Capacity strengthening and learning**

• Strengthen capacities of local authorities and humanitarian and development stakeholder to cooperate in developing integrated approaches for displaced and host communities (including through durable solutions and area-based approaches trainings etc.)

• In close coordination with the ReDSS Learning Specialist, support cross learning and peer to peer exchanges between government authorities in displacement affected Counties, particularly Garissa, Turkana and Nairobi Counties.

• Support the ReDSS + structure and meaningful partnerships with local networks and organizations based on trust, respect and joint accountability

• Ensure that ReDSS research work is having the maximum impact on current policy and programming in relation to solutions for refugees in Kenya .

• Lead initiatives at both national and local levels to ensure local policy planning processes are informed by the communities they serve

- Strong experience in translating evidence and research into programming and policy guidance
