jobs.title: Disaster Preparedness ECHO Project Coordinator - Libya
jobs.body:
North Africa is increasingly vulnerable to climate-related hazards, environmental degradation and socio-economic pressures.  
In Libya, these risks are compounded by fragile infrastructure, institutional fragmentation, displacement and unequal access to essential services.  
The 2023 Derna floods exposed significant gaps in preparedness, early warning and coordination.  
Strengthening disaster preparedness, early warning systems and anticipatory action is therefore essential to reduce the impact of future shocks.

The purpose of the Disaster Preparedness (DP) ECHO Project Coordinator is to coordinate and provide technical and programmatic support to the implementation of the Libya component of the ECHO-funded disaster preparedness and anticipatory action project, in close partnership with the Libyan Red Crescent Society (LRCS) and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC). The position strengthens LRCS capacity to anticipate, prepare for and respond to multi-hazard risks through risk-informed preparedness, anticipatory action, early warning, contingency planning, operational readiness and community preparedness.

The position also supports regional coordination and technical coherence across the ECHO North Africa project by maintaining close engagement with IFRC Regional Office technical teams and designated country focal points in Libya, Egypt and Morocco, facilitating harmonized planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, learning and exchange of good practices.

## Duties and responsibilities

**Strategic responsibilities**

1\. In collaboration with LRCS, support implementation, technical quality and donor compliance of the Norwegian Red Cross-supported Libya component of the ECHO disaster preparedness and anticipatory action project.

2\. Strengthen LRCS institutional and operational preparedness by embedding anticipatory action, early warning, contingency planning, information management, coordination and Operations Room capacities within existing National Society systems.

3\. Promote cross-country coordination and learning across the ECHO North Africa project, aligning technical approaches, implementation standards, monitoring and reporting frameworks, and knowledge management with IFRC Regional Office and country focal points in Egypt and Morocco.

4\. Promote locally led implementation and effective coordination between LRCS headquarters and branches, relevant authorities, Movement partners and humanitarian actors, ensuring complementarity, sustainability and learning.

**Operational responsibilities**

The responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to, the following tasks:

1\. Support LRCS day-to-day planning and follow-up of the Libya component, translating the approved proposal, logframe and budget into practical implementation plans and tracking progress, risks and corrective actions.

2\. Coordinate with Norwegian Red Cross finance, logistics, grants and technical colleagues to support timely, compliant implementation, procurement, monitoring, reporting and project documentation.

3\. Provide technical support to priority Libya deliverables, including contingency planning, simplified Early Action Protocols, early warning and Operations Rooms, information management, eVCA/community preparedness, simulations/readiness drills and Cash-in-Emergency preparedness, with health preparedness supported where relevant.

4\. Support capacity strengthening of LRCS staff, volunteers and relevant stakeholders, ensuring Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI), Accountability to Affected People (AAP), responsible data management and sustainability are integrated.

5\. Maintain technical and operational coordination in Libya with LRCS headquarters and branches, relevant authorities and the National Meteorological Centre, IFRC, ICRC, Partner National Societies and other humanitarian/DP/DRR actors.

6\. Coordinate regular project review and planning with IFRC Regional Office and designated focal points in Egypt and Morocco to monitor progress, address implementation challenges and maintain technical coherence across countries.

7\. Facilitate cross-country exchange of technical guidance, tools, templates, lessons learned and good practices, promoting harmonized implementation of disaster preparedness and anticipatory action activities.

8\. Support consolidation of cross-country progress, achievements, challenges and lessons learned for donor reporting, regional knowledge products and learning, in coordination with IFRC and participating National Societies.

## Collaboration and Qualifications

**Collaboration**

- Reports to the Regional Operations Manager - MENA / Libya Portfolio and maintains regular communication on implementation progress, risks and priorities.
- Works in close partnership with LRCS Operations/Disaster Management, Information Management and relevant Health structures, as well as LRCS branches in Benghazi, Derna and Al Kufra.
- Acts as a key NoRC coordination point for the North Africa ECHO project, working closely with IFRC Regional Office technical teams and designated focal points in Egypt and Morocco.
- Collaborates with Norwegian Red Cross finance, logistics, grants, support functions and Disaster Preparedness technical resources to ensure timely and compliant support.
- Engages relevant authorities, Movement partners and humanitarian actors and represents Norwegian Red Cross in relevant technical coordination fora and project meetings when delegated.

**Qualifications**

**Formal Competence**  
Relevant university degree in Disaster Risk Management, Disaster Management, Humanitarian Action, Climate or Environmental Studies, Emergency Management, Development Studies, Public Health, Social Sciences or another relevant discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

**Personal qualifications, skills and knowledge**

- Minimum five years of relevant professional experience, preferably including at least three years in disaster preparedness, DP/DRR, emergency response, anticipatory action or related humanitarian programming.
- Fluency in Arabic and good professional working proficiency in English, written and spoken.
- Demonstrated experience in project/programme coordination, including planning, monitoring, risk management and donor reporting.
- Practical experience in contingency planning, anticipatory action, early warning systems, EOCs/Operations Rooms, simulation exercises, community preparedness and/or participatory risk assessment.
- Demonstrated experience working with local or national partners, strengthening institutional capacity and coordinating with public authorities and humanitarian stakeholders.
- Good understanding of results-based management, monitoring and evaluation, data quality and project-cycle management.
- Experience with the Red Cross/Red Crescent Movement, Libya, eVCA, information management/GIS, Cash and Voucher Assistance preparedness and/or DG ECHO-funded programmes is an asset.
- Public health or emergency health experience, particularly epidemic preparedness, community-based surveillance or climate-related health risks, is desirable but not mandatory.
- Ability and willingness to travel regularly within Libya, including to Derna and Al Kufra, subject to security procedures.

## Personal qualities

\- Very good ability to work towards achieving objectives and results.

\- Very good ability to cooperate, build partnerships and share competency.

\- Very good ability to communicate effectively and facilitate technical processes.

\- Very good ability to convince, gain acceptance and build trust with diverse stakeholders.

\- Very good ability to analyse complex situations and think holistically.

\- Good ability to be solution oriented, adaptable and work independently.

\- High level of integrity, accountability and commitment to the Fundamental Principles of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.

## We can offer

**Meaningful:** You`ll be a part of the world's largest humanitarian organization, reaching the most vulnerable people in their local community.  
**Impact:** You will help National Societies in the region to become strong, self-sustained and accountable humanitarian actors.  
**Career:** You will be connected to an international organization with staff based all over the world  
**A great place to work:** You will work in a multicultural environment with hard-working, dedicated and fun colleagues with a strong culture of collaboration, continual improvement, and celebration of wins.

**Reporting to:** NoRC MENA Regional Operations Manager  
**Position is based in:** Libya  
**Contract length:** 12 months’ contract.

Norwegian Red Cross striving to build a working culture based on respect, honesty and generosity.  
We do a thorough background check on relevant candidate.

jobs.title: Consultancy to support development of NORCAP Expert Reporting System
jobs.body:
## Introduction to NORCAP

NORCAP is part of Norwegian Refugee council (NRC), and has a mission is to improve aid to protect and empower people affected by crises and climate change. With expertise in the humanitarian, development, and peacebuilding sectors, we collaborate with local, national, and international partners on finding solutions that meet the needs of people at risk.

## Context of the assignment

NORCAP is working on development of an internal expert reporting system (ERS) that will tie together reporting sources within one MS Fabric workspace. In the first phase of the project we have worked on collecting, analysing and prioritizing our requirements, designed the data architecture and created user profiles.

This assignment will support the second phase of the project, where we will create a data architecture within MS Fabric, and develop and test a minimum viable product of the system.

## Objective of the assignment

This assignment will support the NORCAP in:

- Organizing the MS Fabric workspace for the reporting system, integration of data sources from various NRC /NORCAP systems, creation of relevant data flows and semantic models.
- Piloting solutions (MVP) for surveying and data analysis, testing, collecting and integrating feedback.
- Creating and piloting relevant analytical tools and dashboards.
- Piloting AI powered search for data sorting and RAG within the expert reporting system.
- Documenting processes for users and admins in an ERS manual.

## Scope of work for the assignment

Please see the Terms of Reference attached for the scope of work.

## Expected Outputs and Timeline

Key deliverables of the assignment:

- Updated architecture and data model document
- Operational Fabric workspace with a working survey pipeline
- Operational analytics model (dashboards/business analytics)
- AI assistant MVP capable of semantic search and summarization of qualitative variables/fields in reports
- User documentation – admin and user guides

Please see the detailed list of expected outputs in the attached Terms of Reference document.

The schedule will be agreed upon with the consultant(s). The timeframe for the work is between October and December 2026. The estimated time for the assignment is 50 days. NORCAP reserves the right to make changes to the schedule.

## Required Qualifications for the Consultant(s):

- At least 5 years of relevant professional experience:
- Demonstrated experience integrating enterprise source systems, including HR, CRM, ERP, ITSM, and survey platforms, into cloud-based data platforms. Experience with Oracle HR systems, Freshworks/Freshdesk, Microsoft 365/SharePoint, and Kobo Toolbox is considered an advantage.
- Experience with Azure Data Factory / MS Fabric
- Demonstrated experience designing and developing Power BI semantic models, dashboards and reports.
- Experience creating testing and documenting copilot AI agents
- Extensive experience with reporting in international humanitarian and development sector
- Experience in data management and knowledge management approaches
- Experience in communication, facilitating workshops, and collecting inputs from users and stakeholders.
- Knowledge of NRC and/or NORCAP ICT systems is an asset.

jobs.title: Caseworker
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet basic needs and support client achievement of self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs, engaging a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements. The Caseworker is expected to follow guidelines and standard practices, connecting clients to services that support wellbeing.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has living essentials such as housing, food, medical care, access to transportation and community orientation
- Purchase necessary items, conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery orientation, bus orientation and other field-based services related to the immediate needs of newcomers. Lift, transport, drive and move items as needed for program delivery.
- Conduct intake to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals. Address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Collaborate with colleagues across grants and programs, ensuring that clients access services for which they are eligible. Complete program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required, including casework and/or pre-arrival services
- Prior experience navigating program eligibility and program requirements; ensuring services are provided and appropriately documented

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build relationships with clients, colleagues and collaborators
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in spoken and written English. Proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group strongly desired.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Ability to transport, lift and move items as needed to set up homes and otherwise support new arrivals. Lifting and carrying of items 50+ lbs, including larger items such as furniture
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Ability to drive a large van or other passenger vehicles, as needed to conduct work.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities. Typically, this position is based at the office 4 days/week and remotely 1 day/week, with potential field work all days.
- Requires schedule flexibility to perform weekend and/or evening work, including but not limited to airport pick-ups.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $26.80/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Director - Head of International Programs
jobs.body:
PCPM - Polish Center for International Aid is one of the leading Polish INGOs, operating in Ukraine, Lebanon, Syria, oPt, Ethiopia, South Sudan and Kenya, funded by the Polish Government, DG ECHO, OCHA pooled funds, WFP and other institutional donors.

PCPM has three pillars of operations: 1) emergency preparedness and response, including through the WHO-classified Emergency Medical Team.

2\) humanitarian aid, including assistance in refugee crises

3\) long-term development programs, including refugee-centered and social programs in Poland.

As part of its new programmatic approach, PCPM aspires now, funding permitting, to open humanitarian and/or development operations in new geographic and sectoral areas.

Responsibilities:

1. Participate in development of and take lead in implementation of strategy of expanding PCPM's international program presence.
2. Set up or expand PCPM program presence abroad in selected countries, including identification of programs and local partners, establishing and registering local presence as appropriate, implementing initial program activities.
3. Supervising PCPM project teams and staff in designated countries of PCPM program presence, particularly Ukraine, Lebanon, Syria, Kenya and Ethiopia.
4. Apply for institutional and other funding to set up or expand PCPM program presence abroad in selected counties, which includes developing project proposals, including DG ECHO, BHA and others and building strategic relationships with regional and national actors to form consortia and secure joint funding.
5. Undertake frequent travels and field missions to the countries of current and prospective PCPM program presence abroad of Poland.
6. Contribute video and other materials to PCPM fundraising activities./Promote PCPM's visibility and institutional presence by representing the organization at national and international events, as well as capturing and delivering compelling field materials to support public outreach and fundraising.
7. Actively participate in media interviews and other related activities.

Goals (KPIs):

1. First-year objectives: Establish a strategic partnership with at least one major institutional actor (such as an INGO, UN agency, or bilateral donor) and successfully launch operations or projects in at least one new target country.
2. Three-year objectives: Build long-term, multi-year strategic partnerships with at least two key institutional donors/partners and expand PCPM’s operational presence into at least two new geographic locations.

Requirements:

1. Proven experience in humanitarian crises and implementation of donor-funded humanitarian / development aid at the medium management level or above,
2. Familiarity with and proven experience in securing institutional donor financing, including EU institutions, UN Agencies, BHA and other donors as appropriate.
3. Flexibility to undertake field missions with a short advance notice.
4. Fluency in English and knowledge of at least one more language relevant to the current or prospective countries of PCPM program presence.
5. Fluency in Polish would be a major advantage.
6. Citizenship of a EU Member states or another country with privileged access to the EU / Poland labor market.

Working arrangements

1. Preferred: part-time work from Warsaw with part-time travels or field missions. Alternative working arrangements possible, but preference given to office work.

jobs.title: COUNTRY DIRECTOR – MYANMAR
jobs.body:
"Open for all Nationals preferably from Asia"

“Female professionals are encouraged to apply”.

**Contract:** 2 years fixed-term contract with possibility of extension

**One Oxfam Grade:** B1

**Salary and benefits:** in line with Oxfam values and according to location

**Flexible working:** We believe flexible working is key to building the Oxfam in Asia of the future, so we’re open to talking through the type of working arrangements that might work for you

## About Oxfam Myanmar

Oxfam has been working in Myanmar since 1990s. Oxfam works with local partners across Myanmar to support humanitarian response, resilience, gender justice, sustainable livelihoods and locally led development, while adapting its programmes to a diverse and rapidly changing operating environment.

Myanmar is one of the largest countries in Southeast Asia, with a diverse geography ranging from coastal areas and river deltas to central dry zones, highlands and mountainous border regions. It is home to a population of more than 50 million people and is characterised by significant ethnic, linguistic, cultural and socio-economic diversity, with large parts of the population living in rural areas.

The country is experiencing a complex and evolving humanitarian and development context, with communities affected by displacement, economic pressures, climate-related risks and recurrent natural disasters. The March 2025 earthquake further increased humanitarian and recovery needs in several parts of the country. At the same time, local organisations and communities continue to play a vital role in responding to needs and supporting longer-term recovery and resilience.

## **The Role**

**Oxfam** is looking for the **Country Director -Myanmar** who provides overall leadership and strategic direction for Oxfam's work in Myanmar, ensuring effective delivery of humanitarian, development, advocacy, and influencing programmes. The role is accountable for programme quality and impact, organizational performance, and sound financial and people management. Working closely with the Asia Regional Platform and Regional Director, the Country Director leads the implementation of Oxfam's 2030 Global Strategy and Asia Regional Strategy, positioning the Myanmar programme to contribute effectively to regional and global goals.

## ***Who we’re looking for***

**Country Director- Myanmar will be an experienced, dedicated, and highly motivated professional, with a strong commitment to Oxfam's values and beliefs with the following qualification and competencies:**

- At least 5 years of senior leadership experience leading country programs at Director level, leading and managing complex development, humanitarian, and advocacy programmes in fragile and challenging environments, with experience in Asian countries.
- 10 years of proven track record of leading and motivating multi-disciplinary teams across national and international settings, including complex environment.
- Strong experience in strategic planning, programme management, organizational change, and adaptive leadership.
- Demonstrated expertise in conflict-sensitive programming, gender justice, and rights-based approaches.
- Proven success in building and maintaining effective partnerships with civil society, donors, governments, UN agencies, and other key stakeholders.
- Strong advocacy, influencing, negotiation, and representation skills at national, regional, and international levels.
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to convey complex issues clearly to diverse audiences and represent the organization publicly and with the media.
- Sound financial management experience, including budget oversight, resource mobilization, fundraising, and donor engagement.
- Demonstrated ability to manage security, operational, legal, and reputational risks in complex operating environments.
- Strong analytical and political acumen, with the ability to navigate complex contexts, assess risks, and make sound strategic decisions.
- Experience leading humanitarian preparedness and response initiatives in emergency settings.
- Commitment to feminist, rights-based, and inclusive approaches, with a strong dedication to women's rights and the empowerment of marginalized communities.
- High levels of integrity, resilience, cultural sensitivity, emotional intelligence, and self-awareness.

## **What we offer**

This role will give you an opportunity to lead the Myanmar country team, make a difference, to act as key contributor in leading Oxfam Myanmar’s strategic goals and to work with a group of passionate people that are specialists in their technical fields. The role offers opportunities for training and professional development, and fair pay and competitive benefits package.

Oxfam is committed to providing a fair compensation package and to providing a flexible, supportive, working environment.

## **About Oxfam**

At Oxfam we respond to emergencies and advocate for people in crisis, partnering with local organizations to deliver essentials and help rebuild communities. We work with activists and partners to fight poverty and injustice. We campaign for economic, gender, climate justice and accountable governance, striving for sustainable growth and transformation. **We fight for a future that is equal, just and fair** – one in which people have more equal opportunities and rights, and one in which we can all flourish, not just survive.

jobs.title: Caseworker Assistant
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of 30 September 2027.***

**Job Overview:**

The Program for Initial Resettlement Caseworker Assistant supports refugee and other ORR-eligible populations during their integration into the United States by assisting with service delivery, client support, documentation, transportation, and resource coordination. Working under the guidance of the Cash and Medical and Initial Resettlement Coordinator, the Caseworker Assistant helps ensure clients have access to essential services and resources while promoting self-sufficiency, stability, and successful community integration.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Assist in coordinating pre-arrival and post-arrival services to ensure clients receive essential support upon arrival.
- Support airport pickups, housing setup, food assistance, transportation arrangements, and community orientation activities.
- Assist clients with navigating community resources and accessing essential services.
- Conduct client intake and assessment activities to help identify household strengths, needs, and priorities.
- Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide referrals and follow up on service connections, appointments, and action items.
- Support the distribution of direct assistance and program-related resources according to organizational and funder requirements.
- Maintain regular communication with assigned clients to support progress toward established goals.
- Document client interactions, services provided, referrals, and outcomes accurately and timely.
- Enter and maintain client records in ETO and other required databases.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Associate degree in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years’ experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Experience providing customer service, case management support, or community outreach preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Will require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($18.45). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Asistente de Protección Santa Bárbara del Zulia - Personal Nacional
jobs.body:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Oficial de Protección altamente calificado/a con sede en Santa Bárbara del Zulia, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

**Objetivo general del puesto:**

Bajo la supervisión del Líder de equipo de Protección (Zulia), el Asistente de Protección apoyará la implementación en terreno de todos los objetivos de protección bajo los proyectos de DRC. El Asistente de Protección desarrollará y mantendrá buenas relaciones con las personas de interés, las partes interesadas relevantes y otros actores humanitarios, para apoyar la implementación y coordinación adecuadas de las actividades de Protección de DRC que se desarrollarán en el área de intervención. Apoyar la implementación de enfoques diferenciales, especialmente de edad, género, y diversidad en las actividades de protección.

**Responsabilidades:**

- Contribuir eficientemente a la implementación del proyecto de protección en los municipios del sur del lago del estado Zulia de acuerdo con los objetivos acordados.
- Implementar periódica el Monitoreo de Protección en las comunidades de intervención, incluyendo el levantamiento de datos cuantitativos y cualitativos sobre necesidades/riesgos de protección mediante la aplicación de entrevistas a unidades familiares, grupos focales e informantes claves.
- Contribuir al fortalecimiento del enfoque de edad, género y diversidad en las acciones de y respuestas de protección.
- Apoyar en la identificación y documentación sistemáticamente las necesidades específicas y riesgos de protección de las personas más vulnerables en las comunidades de intervención –a través del Monitoreo de Protección, actividades informativas realizadas en las comunidades y otros medios— a fin de referir y/o brindar una repuesta oportuna a las personas de interés.
- Participar en el Comité de Asistencia de Protección Individual (IPA), y contribuir con los planes de respuestas que respondan a las necesidades específicas protección de los casos, y apoyar con los planes de entrega de las asistencias y/o remisiones a servicios especializados internos y/o externos.
- Manejar la información confidencial de manera correcta, de acuerdo con las políticas de protección de datos de DRC, gestionando los archivos de protección de manera precisa, correcta y completa.
- Apoyar en la recopilación de información para la elaboración de reportes, informes, e insumos productos del Monitoreo de Protección.
- Asegurar la más alta calidad de las intervenciones de protección y la coherencia entre todos los proyectos, en curso y propuestos, de acuerdo con la estrategia general.
- Apoyar en la orientación de las personas de interés según las rutas de protección, el mapeo de servicios y de los actores humanitarios e institucionales.
- Apoyar en la organización y facilitación de grupos focales y sesiones informativas sobre temas de protección.
- Apoyar y asistir en conjunto con la línea supervisora en el desarrollo de actividades legales conforme a los objetivos y metas.
- Participar bajo supervisión en el asesoramiento individual de las principales necesidades legales identificadas.
- Acompañar a los beneficiarios a instituciones públicas según sea necesario.
- Participar en espacios de formación y retroalimentación de las acciones de protección.
- Participar de manera colaborativa en las acciones del equipo de protección y otras áreas.
- Participar activamente a las reuniones de equipo proporcionando insumos, desafíos y lecciones aprendidas.
- Contribuir al desarrollo de herramientas de procedimiento operativos estándar.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva de las actividades programática asignadas, mientras el plan de trabajo.
- Apoyar en la preparación de informes y presupuestos mensuales.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 1 año de experiencia relevante en protección humanitaria, trabajo social, derechos humanos u otro trabajo similar de terreno, relacionado a una ONG u otra organización sin fines de lucro.
- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo con comunidades urbanas, y/o rurales, y/o indígenas.
- Experiencia y capacidad para entrevistar a personas de todas las edades, género y diversidad.
- Buenas habilidades para trabajar con tabletas y computadores.
- Buenas habilidades en MS Word y Excel.
- Voluntad y habilidad de aprender.

**Educación:**

Título Universitario pertinente en logística y / o gestión de la cadena de suministro o cualificación profesional equivalente.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 6 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.
- Contratación nacional.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Miércoles 14 de Octubre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio:** Octubre 2026

**Nota:**

- Nos reservamos el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha indicada de cierre de postulaciones
- La vacante está sujeta a aprobación del proyecto y disponibilidad de fondos
- Debido a una contratación de emergencia, DRC no se obliga a enviar las notificaciones de rechazo a los candidatos que no sean considerados en el proceso

jobs.title: Junior Project Assistant
jobs.body:
**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

**Organizational Context and Scope**

Under the direct supervision of the project manager and under the guidance of the Head of Unit for Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion (LMI) and under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission in the Country Office for Belgium and Luxembourg, the incumbent will assist the LMI team with the implementation of projects of the IOM Country Office. In addition to this, the incumbent will be expected to support some activities related to the development of new projects in the LMI Team.

**Responsibilities**

In particular, the incumbent will:

  
I. ASSIST WITH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECTS

1\. In close coordination with the LMI Head of Unit, assist the Project Management Teams with the implementation and follow-up on project activities. This includes supporting the team with research tasks, administrative tasks and the (logistical) organization of meetings and events.   
2\. Assist with the drafting/ formatting of reports; routine correspondence, type letters, reports and memoranda as well as IOM documents and forms related to IOM operational and administrative matters;   
3\. Assist the Project Management Team with the development of new projects and initiatives in the field of Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion. This includes assistance with the drafting/ formatting of concept notes and project proposals.   
4\. Assist in drafting/ formatting public information documents, website articles, press releases and information dissemination on IOM activities towards public and private stakeholders.   
5\. Any other tasks as may be required.

  
II- ASSIST WITH POLICY SUPPORT AND OUTREACH

6\. Assist in identifying possible partnerships with the private sector, civil society (NGOs, diaspora associations, etc.) and other stakeholders (such as the Belgian government and universities) in order to improve knowledge on migration initiatives and policies.   
7\. Assist with the drafting/ formatting of presentations and speeches related to integration for the LMI Head of Unit or the Chief of Mission.   
8\. Prepare for, participate in and follow-up on meetings/conferences on behalf of the organization.   
9\. Any other tasks as may be required.

**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

**•**  Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in economics, social science, migration studies or related field from an accredited academic institution with one year of relevant professional experience.   
OR   
• Completed High School degree with three years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

• Demonstrated first working experience or internship in the area of project management, or evaluation of projects;   
• Demonstrated first working experience or internship in the area of migrant integration or labour migration;   
• Strong organizational and time-management skills;   
• Ability to work independently;   
• Experience in liaison with non-governmental organizations, national, regional and international authorities and institutions is an advantage.

**Skills**

• Strong organizational and time-management skills;   
• Strong communication and diplomatic skills, applied in a professional environment;   
• Ability to work independently against tight deadlines.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Advanced knowledge of Dutch is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators Level 1

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

jobs.title: Country Director Palestine – based in Amman
jobs.body:
## **Fixed term contract: 12 months from 01/01/2027**

## **PUI all around the world**

**With its 40 years of experience, Première Urgence Internationale :**

- Supports close to **6** millions beneficiaries
- With more than **100** millions € yearly budget
- Present in **22** countries, on **5** continents

Thanks to the work and commitment of :

- More than **2000** national staffs
- Around **200** expatriates from 45 different nationalities
- And **90** employees at HQ

PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity.

Learn more on [our history](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [our values](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [our areas of intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

## **What about the Country Director?**

As Country Director, you will be responsible for the smooth functioning and the development of the mission. For this purpose, you will be responsible for:

- **Safety & Security**: You will be responsible for the safety & security of the mission.
- **Programmes**: You will coordinate the teams and ensure that the programmes implemented on the mission are properly carried out. You will also monitor needs and suggest new operations and development tracks for the mission.
- **Human Resources**: You will ensure that the mission is adequately staffed and supervise the teams (defining objectives, follow-up).
- **Logistical, administrative and financial monitoring**: You will ensure that logistical and administrative practices in place respect PUI procedures and formats and are in compliance with donors’ rules and regulations.
- **Medical and technical monitoring**: You will ensure that medical and technical practices respect PUI’s procedures and formats and are in compliance with PUI’s operational framework and policy.
- **Representation**: You will represent the association in its relations with partners, donors, the media and different authorities.
- **Relations with Headquarters**: You will ensure that information is properly circulated between Headquarters and the field and ensure that due dates are respected.

## **The challenges that await you**

- **Unprecedented crisis in Gaza**: Responding to extraordinary humanitarian needs while maintaining operational continuity, staff safety, programme quality, and accountability in an extremely volatile environment.
- **Deteriorating situation in the West Bank**: Adapting programmes and operations to increasing insecurity, movement restrictions, displacement pressures, and rapidly changing access conditions.
- **Legal, registration and access constraints**: Navigating a complex and evolving regulatory environment while securing the operational access required to deliver programmes effectively.

## **What you will need to succeed**

**Training**: You hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in Humanitarian action: project management, a technical background related to one of our activity sectors, in human resources management, financial management…

**Experience**: Strengthened by minimum 3 years of experience in the field with international NGOs in project coordination, you master international team management, the project cycle and security management. Previous experience as Country Director or in an equivalent position would be appreciated. You already worked with Première Urgence Internationale? It would be a definite asset!

**Skills**: You master humanitarian project management and team management; you have a detailed knowledge of donors’ prerequisites. You also have excellent writing skills.

**Qualities**: You are a good communicator, both in writing and orally. You demonstrate good team spirit, leadership skills and the ability to make decisions, trustworthiness and a sense of responsibility, organizational skills, reactivity, ability to be thorough and to adapt. You have a strong resistance to stress and particularly in unstable circumstances.

**Languages**: English has no secrets for you! All the better, it is mandatory for this position. If you speak Arabic and/or French, it would be a definite asset.

## **A word from the manager**

*« Join PUI as Country Director in Palestine and help drive humanitarian action in one of today’s most challenging environments. Working across Palestine and Jordan, you will bring adaptability, resilience and commitment to lead through complexity, navigate uncertainty and make a lasting difference. »*

## **PUI will offer you**

- **Status:** Cadre with a Fixed-Term Contract
- **Monthly Gross Income:** 3 330,00 – 3 730,00 EUR depending on your experience in International Solidarity + 50€ per semester of seniority with PUI
- **Insurance** including medical coverage and complementary healthcare, 24/24 assistance and repatriation
- **Daily Living Expenses** (« Per Diem »)
- **Break Policy:** 5 working days at 3 and 9 months + break allowance
- **Paid Leaves Policy:** 5 weeks of paid leaves per year + return ticket every 6 months

## **Our commitments**

PUI is committed to preventing all forms of inappropriate behavior in the workplace, including harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct, while promoting the well-being of children and adults with whom PUI interacts.  
PUI expects all employees to fulfill their professional duties and responsibilities in accordance with PUI’s Ethical Framework. All employees will receive appropriate training and commit to promoting, disseminating, and upholding the principles set forth in its Ethical Charter.  
The holder of this position may potentially have access to personal data concerning children and vulnerable adults as part of their work (Category 2 in the safe recruitment risk classification). Consequently, all recruitments will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate background checks, which include criminal record and counter-terrorism financing checks.  
Première Urgence Internationale considers the diversity of nationalities, genders, beliefs, backgrounds, and statuses within its Human Resources as a major asset for its humanitarian work. The organization is therefore committed to strictly upholding the principle of non-discrimination throughout its recruitment process.  
We are dedicated to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.  
Please note that Première Urgence Internationale shall not in any case request a financial contribution for administrative costs related to recruitment. Any such information would be fraudulent, please disregard it.  
**Early applications are encouraged, as we may close the process earlier than the deadline mentioned above if a suitable candidate is identified.**

You recognize yourself in this profile and you adhere to our commitments ? You feel ready to take up the **challenge and** to join **PUI great family ?**

jobs.title: Senior Case Management Officer
source: International Network For Aid Relief and Assistance
jobs.body:
**GENERAL INFORMATION**

Job Title : Senior Case Management Officer

Location : Ankara, Türkiye (On-site)

Job Type : Full-time

Contract Duration : The contract is for an initial period of **one (1) year**, with the possibility of extension depending on the availability of funding and the continued need for the role.

**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

**Vision**

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

**Mission**

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

**Purpose**

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Senior Case Management Officer is responsible for supervising and supporting INARA’s case management and MHPSS staff in Türkiye while directly managing and following up medical cases in Ankara. The position ensures that children and their families receive coordinated, timely, safe, and high-quality support throughout assessment, treatment, recovery, and case closure. The role provides day-to-day supervision to Case Management Officers and MHPSS Officers, reviews case documentation and service quality, coordinates closely with hospitals and service providers, and maintains an active caseload in Ankara. The position also verifies hospital and treatment-related expenses against services received, reconciles case expenditures and cash advances with Finance, prepares donor-required case and program reports, and works with Partnerships/Program Management and Communications to ensure reporting, case stories, and communication materials are accurate, timely, and appropriately documented.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Case Management, Medical Follow-up & Care Coordination**

- Manage an active caseload of children receiving medical support in Ankara, ensuring continuous follow-up from intake and assessment through treatment, rehabilitation, recovery, referral, and case closure.
- Conduct and/or review comprehensive assessments of children’s medical, psychosocial, protection, social, and practical needs and develop individualized care plans in coordination with children, caregivers, medical providers, and relevant INARA staff.
- Coordinate appointments, diagnostics, procedures, hospitalization, rehabilitation, medication, referrals, transportation, and other treatment-related needs, and follow up with hospitals and service providers to ensure continuity and quality of care.
- Maintain regular contact with children and caregivers, provide practical guidance and support, explain treatment pathways and next steps, and ensure that changes in needs or treatment plans are communicated promptly.
- Advocate for children and families with hospitals, healthcare providers, social services, and other relevant actors to address barriers to care and secure appropriate services.
- Ensure timely identification and escalation of safeguarding, protection, medical, or psychosocial concerns in accordance with INARA policies and referral pathways.
- Ensure medical and MHPSS services are coordinated as part of an integrated, child-centered case management approach.

**Team Supervision, Technical Oversight & Quality Assurance**

- Provide direct day-to-day supervision to Case Management Officers and MHPSS Officers, ensuring clear work planning, appropriate caseload allocation, service coverage, and accountability.
- Conduct regular team meetings, individual supervision, case review sessions, and multidisciplinary discussions to monitor progress, address complex cases, and support sound case management decisions.
- Review case files, assessments, care plans, follow-up notes, referrals, service records, and closure documentation to ensure completeness, accuracy, confidentiality, and compliance with INARA standards.
- Monitor staff caseloads, case progress, service timelines, and follow-up actions, and intervene where delays, gaps, risks, or quality concerns are identified.
- Provide coaching, technical guidance, and practical support to staff; identify capacity-building needs and support learning and consistent application of case management and MHPSS procedures.
- Promote a supportive, respectful, and accountable team environment and ensure adherence to safeguarding, confidentiality, data protection, professional boundaries, and organizational policies.
- Coordinate with relevant managers on staff performance, workload, operational challenges, and corrective actions where required.

**Hospital & Service Provider Coordination**

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with hospitals, doctors, rehabilitation providers, pharmacies, laboratories, and other service providers supporting INARA children.
- Confirm treatment plans, services delivered, follow-up requirements, and relevant medical documentation with providers, while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and informed consent.
- Review hospital invoices, treatment bills, and related medical expenses against the treatment and services actually received by each child, flagging discrepancies or unclear charges for clarification before processing.
- Support resolution of service delivery issues, appointment delays, documentation gaps, or billing discrepancies in coordination with hospitals, Finance, and relevant INARA colleagues.

**Case-related Financial Reconciliation & Cash Advances**

- Work closely with Finance on a regular basis to reconcile medical and case-related expenditures with approved treatment plans, supporting documents, and services received.
- Maintain clear records of treatment-related expenses and provide the programmatic and case documentation required to validate hospital, pharmacy, transportation, accommodation, and other approved day-to-day medical costs.
- Manage and clear cash advances received for children’s treatment and day-to-day medical expenses in a timely manner, ensuring that receipts and supporting documentation are complete and submitted in accordance with INARA procedures.
- Follow up on outstanding advances, missing documentation, discrepancies, or corrections with Finance and relevant staff until fully reconciled and cleared.
- This role verifies and reconciles case-related costs but is not responsible for program budgeting, financial management, or budget ownership.

**Monitoring, Documentation & Donor Reporting**

- Maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date beneficiary records, medical follow-up information, service documentation, consent records, and case progress notes in accordance with INARA’s data protection and confidentiality requirements.
- Track case progress, treatment status, outputs, outcomes, pending actions, and relevant indicators and ensure reliable information is available for internal monitoring and donor reporting.
- Prepare monthly and quarterly reports on children and case management activities using existing donor templates, ensuring that information is accurate, evidence-based, complete, and submitted on time.
- Share completed reporting inputs and supporting information with the Partnerships and Program Management Department for review, consolidation, and donor submission.
- Maintain and follow a clear calendar of donor reporting deadlines and required case-related deliverables, including narrative inputs, beneficiary information, case updates, and communication materials.
- Provide timely clarifications, case data, and supporting documentation requested by Partnerships/Program Management for donor reports, reviews, monitoring visits, or audits.

**Communications, Case Stories & Visibility**

- Work closely with the Communications Department to identify appropriate treatment journeys, case stories, milestones, and impact examples that can be documented in line with consent, safeguarding, confidentiality, and dignity standards.
    - Coordinate access to accurate case information and appropriate follow-up with children and caregivers so that treatment progress and case stories are captured responsibly and without disrupting care.
    - Review case-related facts in communication materials for accuracy and ensure that medical and treatment information reflects the services actually received.
    - Track and follow up on donor deadlines for required communication, visibility, case-story, photo, video, or other program materials, coordinating with Communications and Partnerships/Program Management to ensure timely completion.

**Cross-Departmental Coordination**

- Work closely with Program Management, Partnerships, Finance, Communications, Administration, and Operations to ensure coordinated support to children and timely completion of case-related actions.
- Participate in relevant internal meetings and provide concise updates on case progress, team workload, treatment challenges, reporting requirements, and issues requiring management attention.
- Support coordination with external service providers and relevant actors where this directly contributes to referral pathways, continuity of care, or improved services for children.

**REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS**

**Qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Nursing, Public Health, or another relevant field; a Master’s degree is an asset.
- Strong understanding of child-centered case management, care coordination, safeguarding, confidentiality, and data protection.
- Strong organizational, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and sensitive cases.
- Fluency in Turkish and strong working proficiency in English are required; Arabic is a strong asset.
- Ability to work on-site in Ankara and to travel locally to hospitals and service providers as required.

**Experience**

- Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in case management, medical care coordination, protection, MHPSS, or humanitarian programming, preferably with an international NGO.
- Demonstrated experience supervising case management, MHPSS, social work, or multidisciplinary teams.
- Proven experience coordinating medical cases with hospitals and healthcare providers and following treatment pathways and patient needs.
- Experience reviewing case documentation and treatment-related supporting documents and coordinating expense reconciliation with Finance.
- Experience preparing accurate narrative or beneficiary-level reports using donor or organizational templates and working to fixed reporting deadlines.
- Experience working with children and families affected by conflict, displacement, disaster, or other vulnerabilities is strongly preferred.

**CONFIDENTIALITY AND SAFEGUARDING**

**Confidentiality**

As the position is involved in sensitive topics, he/she must observe absolute discretion within and outside the organization. Non-respect of this clause or any breach of responsibility may result in a written warning or immediate dismissal.

**Safeguarding**

INARA has zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, or harm to children and vulnerable adults. INARA employees must adhere strictly to safeguarding policies, maintain professional boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

jobs.title: Consultant.e Expert.e en Architecture et IA Générative – Projet HAVA
jobs.body:
**Titre : Consultant.e Expert.e en Architecture et IA Générative – Projet HAVA**  
**Date : 11/09/2029**  
**Projet :**  
**Référence : ​HULO-TDR-BAR-2026-001​**

Cet appel à candidatures est ouvert à tous les consultants éligibles, en accord avec les procédures et principes de hulo.

**Contexte de la consultance :**

La **Coopérative hulo**, créée en juin 2021, est la première Société Coopérative Européenne (SCE) opérant dans le secteur de l’humanitaire. En décembre 2025, hulo compte 16 organisations membres : ACTED, Action contre la Faim (ACF), Bioport, la Croix-Rouge française (CRF), Fleet Forum, Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI), International Federation of the Red Cross, International Rescue Committee (IRC), INTERSOS, Médecins du Monde (MDM), Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Oxfam Intermón, Plan International, Première Urgence International (PUI), Solidarités International (SI), et Welthungerhilfe (WHH).

Son objectif est d'accroître l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant les liens et la solidarité entre les acteurs de la logistique humanitaire et en améliorant les performances grâce à la mise en commun des ressources et de l'expertise en matière de logistique et de chaîne d'approvisionnement. Les « initiatives mutualisées » de hulo, sont déjà en cours dans 7 countries (Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, RDC, Liban, Jordanie pour la crise syrienne, Colombie, et Tchad). Les activités sur le terrain sont composées d'achats mutualisés, de ressources humaines partagées, d’une plateforme web permettant la mise en commun de ressources, et d’initiatives environnementales mutualisées. Ces initiatives permettent d'économiser du temps et de l'argent, d'améliorer la qualité des biens et des services fournis, et donc de fournir une aide plus efficace à ceux qui en ont le plus besoin.

Hulo développe actuellement son écosystème Data autour de Microsoft Fabric, avec l'objectif de renforcer ses capacités en matière de Data Science, Business Analytics et Business Intelligence.  
L'utilisation des outils d'Intelligence Artificielle Générative (GenAI) se développant rapidement en interne, cela crée de nouvelles opportunités pour les équipes de hulo, mais également des risques, notamment concernant le shadow AI.  
Hulo souhaite donc étudier et préparer la mise en place de HAVA (Hulo AI for Value-added Assistance), un assistant d'IA générative d'entreprise, sécurisé et gouverné.  
Le concept actuellement réfléchi repose sur une approche Hybrid Enterprise AI Assistant, combinant des modèles d'IA générative opensource et les documents et mécanismes de sécurité contrôlés par hulo.  
L'architecture envisagée s'appuie notamment sur :

- Azure OpenAI Service
- Microsoft Fabric
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Microsoft Entra ID
- Microsoft Purview
- Microsoft Defender
- les bases de données et modèles analytiques de hulo

Le concept HAVA et ses annexes constituent le premier kit de travail qui servira de base à la présente consultance.

**Perimètre général du travail attendu du.de la Consultant.e :**

L'objectif principal de cette consultance est d'accompagner hulo dans la revue, la validation et la finalisation du cahier des charges fonctionnel et technique du projet HAVA.  
Le.la consultant.e apportera une expertise indépendante en matière de :

- Generative AI
- Large Language Models (LLM)
- Architecture Cloud
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Sécurité des données
- Gouvernance de l'IA
- Microsoft Azure et Microsoft Fabric

Le.la consultant.e n'aura pas pour objectif de développer l'intégralité de HAVA pendant cette mission.

La mission devra permettre à hulo de disposer, à l'issue de 20 jours estimés (A confirmer dans la proposition), d'un cahier des charges suffisamment complet et robuste pour permettre la mise en œuvre ultérieure de HAVA, en interne et/ou avec l'appui d'un prestataire externe.

Cette mission de consultant sera mise en oeuvre en coordination avec le département Business Analytics & Research (BAR). Une personne ressource sera désignée par département pour identifier les enjeux et faciliter les échanges.

**Priorités et livrables :**

**Cahier des charges HAVA finalisé** **incluant** :

1\. Analyse de situation -

- Contexte et enjeux
- Besoins identifiés et priorisés par service
- Contraintes techniques et d’intégration
    - Analyse de l'architecture existante, points forts, limites et recommandations
    - Données disponibles et leur qualité
    - Exigences éthiques, réglementaires et de gouvernance
    - Budget, planning et modalités de collaboration

2\. Solution recommandée

- Périmètre -
    - Objectifs
    - Périmètre fonctionnel
- Proposition -
    - Recommandation sur les modèles IA (Comparaison et recommandation des modèles et stratégie de modèles)
    - Connexions / liens avec d’autres usages IA internes (ex. Usages spécialisés de certains départements)
    - Modèle de coûts et ressources (Coûts d'implémentation, coûts récurrents et ressources nécessaires)
    - Registre des risques (Risques techniques, sécurité, données, opérationnels et adoption)
    - Spécifications sécurité et gouvernance (Identité, accès, confidentialité, RAG sécurisé, logs, gouvernance et guardrails)
    - Architecture RAG (Ingestion documentaire, métadonnées, recherches web, embeddings)

3\. Préparation de la mise en oeuvre

- Déploiement - Livrables, calendrier et responsabilités
- Critères de réussites
- Maintenance, support et réévaluation après déploiement

**Qualifications et expérience:**

- Minimum 3 ans d'expérience dans les domaines de la Data, de l'IA ou de l'architecture Cloud ;
- Expérience démontrée dans la conception de solutions Enterprise Generative AI ;
- Solide connaissance des LLM et architectures RAG ;
- Expérience de l'écosystème Microsoft Azure ;
- Bonne connaissance de la sécurité des données ;
- Expérience en gouvernance de l'IA ;
- Expérience dans la conception de solutions utilisant des documents internes ;
- Capacité à transformer des besoins métier en spécifications techniques ;
- Expérience avec des environnements humanitaire contenant des données sensibles ou confidentielles.

**Management et lignes hiérarchiques**

Ce · tte consultant·e sera placé·e sous la responsabilité du directeur du département « Business Analytics & Research » et travaillera de concert avec un Data Scientist.

**Calendrier**

Mi-octobre – décembre 2026
