jobs.title: External Assurance Engagement on the Empowerment Guarantee Fund (EGF) managed by the Iraqi Company for Bank Guarantees (ICBG)
jobs.body:
External Assurance Engagement on the Empowerment Guarantee Fund (EGF) managed by the Iraqi Company for Bank Guarantees (ICBG)

## Introduction andBackground

Iraq, including the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, has faced a series of compounding crises over the past decade, including armed conflict, the rise of ISIL, mass displacement, fiscal instability, the COVID-19 pandemic and fluctuations in global oil prices. These have weakened the labour market, eroded enterprise resilience and exposed structural vulnerabilities in the financial system.

Access to finance remains a major constraint for small and medium-sized enterprises. According to the International Finance Corporation, the SME financing gap in Iraq is estimated at nearly USD 6 billion, and only 8 per cent of SMEs hold a business bank account. A particular obstacle is the level of collateral required by banks, which can reach up to 125 per cent of the loan value.

The International Labour Organization (ILO), with financial support from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and under the leadership of KfW Development Bank, is implementing the Promotion of the Development of SMEs in Iraq Project (IRQ/23/05/DEU). The Project is structured around three interrelated components: strengthening the capacity of the Iraqi Company for Bank Guarantees (ICBG) to implement an effective credit guarantee scheme; supporting participating financial institutions in establishing dedicated SME finance windows; and improving the financial literacy and credit-readiness of SMEs.

A central instrument of the Project is the Empowerment Guarantee Fund (EGF), a partial credit guarantee facility established at, and managed by, ICBG. Under the Fund, ICBG issues partial credit guarantees on eligible SME loans originated by Participating Financial Institutions (PFIs) from their own balance sheets. All lending decisions, risk assessment and client relationships remain the responsibility of the PFIs.

These Terms of Reference concern the external assurance engagement over the Fund. They form Annex III to the Request for Proposals and, together with the other Annexes, constitute the basis on which proposals are invited.

This assignment does not comprise the statutory audit of ICBG under Iraqi law, which is a separate matter procured and financed by ICBG and is outside the scope of these Terms of Reference.

## Section 2:The Entity and theFund —Profile and Overview

1. ### TheIraqi Company for Bank Guarantees

ICBG is the only formally established bank guarantee provider in Iraq. It was founded in 2006 under Companies Law No. 21 of 1997 as a limited liability company, initially owned by eleven private banks, and is licensed by the Central Bank of Iraq. As of 2020 its ownership comprised fifteen private banks and several individual shareholders. The principal shareholders are the Investment Bank of Iraq (19.97 per cent), Gulf Commercial Bank (17.69 per cent), Ashur International Bank (12.30 per cent), Sumer Commercial Bank (9.98 per cent) and the Iraqi Middle East Investment Bank (8.74 per cent).

ICBG has undergone a programme of institutional strengthening under the Project, including the adoption of a revised organizational structure, the development and approval of institutional policies and standard operating procedures, targeted recruitment, and the procurement and installation of an Enterprise Resource Planning system.

1. ### TheEmpowerment Guarantee Fund

Phase I of the Fund comprises EUR 9,000,000, disbursed by the ILO to ICBG against six milestones defined in the Project ToR. The first tranche was released in September 2025.

As at the date of these Terms of Reference, the disbursement position is as follows. The tranches corresponding to Milestones 1 and 2 have been disbursed and verified by the ILO. The tranche corresponding to Milestone 4 is in the course of disbursement. The tranche corresponding to Milestone 5 is expected to be disbursed in September 2026 and the tranche corresponding to Milestone 6 by October 2026. With the agreement of the donor, the tranche corresponding to Milestone 3, relating to the amendment of the composition of the Board of Directors to include independent private sector representatives, has been deferred to the final position in the disbursement sequence and is expected to be disbursed in the first quarter of 2027.

Phase II of the Fund comprises a further EUR 12,000,000. Phase II is conditional upon the satisfactory operationalization of the guarantee scheme and upon formal approval and signature of the Exit Strategy and Sustainability Framework by the ILO, KfW and the relevant stakeholders. Phase II is currently anticipated in the second quarter of 2028. Where Phase II proceeds, the resources concerned form part of the Fund and fall within the scope of this engagement from the Reporting Period in which they are received, without amendment to these Terms of Reference.

The Project target is 3,000 guaranteed SME loans by the second quarter of 2031. The volume of guarantees issued, of claims settled and of loans repaid or defaulted is expected to increase across the Reporting Periods. Bidders should have regard to that profile when proposing sample sizes and when pricing each Reporting Period.

Separately from the Fund, the ILO contributes up to EUR 100,000 towards the cost of a Resident Advisor engaged directly by ICBG. That contribution is a Project expense and does not form part of the Fund or of the milestone-based disbursement structure. It is outside the scope of this engagement and shall not be treated as Fund expenditure.

The Fund is not a separate legal entity and does not prepare standalone statutory financial statements. It is maintained through segregated, ring-fenced bank accounts and separate financial records, and is reported through dedicated financial reports prepared in accordance with the financial management provisions of the Project ToR. Fund resources may not be commingled with ICBG’s general funds or shareholder capital, nor distributed as dividends.

Key parameters of the guarantee mechanism, as set out in the Project ToR, are summarised below. The Practitioner is referred to the Project ToR for the complete provisions.

1. ### Participating Financial Institutions

Four financial institutions are currently engaged under the Fund: National Bank of Iraq (NBI), Al Mashreq Al Arabi Bank (AMB), First Finance Company (FFC) and Bank of Baghdad (BoB). Each has concluded a guarantee agreement with ICBG. The Assignment extends to procedures at each PFI, as set out at Section 3.5.2.

## Section 3:Assignment andObjectives /Scope ofWork

1. ### Objective of theAssignment

The objective of the Assignment is to enable the Practitioner to express a conclusion, with reasonable assurance, on whether the Subject Matter Information is free from material misstatement regarding the proper use of KfW funds, by reference to the Criteria set out at Annex A, and to express a separate conclusion on each criterion.

1. ### Form of Engagement

The Assignment is a reasonable assurance engagement performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements ISAE 3000 (Revised), Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information, as issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board of the International Federation of Accountants.

A limited assurance engagement will not be accepted.

The Practitioner shall operate a system of quality management consistent with ISQM 1 and shall comply with the independence and ethical requirements of the IESBA International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants.

The Practitioner shall plan and perform the procedures considered necessary to obtain reasonable assurance about the Subject Matter Information, including on-site procedures as set out at Section 3.5.

1. ### Subject Matter

It is the responsibility of the Entity to prepare the project financial reports (the "Financial Reports"), an overview of the Project Accounts, the Statements of Expenditure (the "SOE") and the related disbursement requests, together the "Subject Matter Information".

The Practitioner shall verify which accounts have been opened and are used by the Entity and by any Participating Financial Institution in connection with the Fund, including internal accounts in the case of separate accounting. All such accounts, together the "Project Accounts", shall be stated at Annex B and shall be considered within the scope of the engagement.

The financial information shall be established in accordance with consistently applied accounting standards and in conformity with the disbursement-related provisions of the Relevant Agreements listed at Annex C.

source: International Network For Aid Relief and Assistance
jobs.body:
**GENERAL INFORMATION**

Job Title : Head of Support Services

Location : Remote

Job Type: Full-time

Contract Duration : The contract is for an initial period of **one (1) year**, with the possibility of extension depending on the availability of funding and the continued need for the role.**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

Vision

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

Mission

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

Purpose

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Head of Support Services provides strategic leadership and oversight of INARA’s global finance and operational support systems across all country operations and legal entities. The role ensures strong financial management, compliance, internal controls, budgeting coherence, donor financial accountability, and organizational financial sustainability.

The post-holder serves as the central finance oversight function between Headquarters and Country Offices, ensuring that financial systems, reporting processes, fund management, and accounting practices operate in alignment with donor requirements, organizational policies, and applicable regulatory frameworks.

The role also supervises finance staff across country operations, supports organizational audits and compliance obligations, oversees financial systems optimization, and strengthens institutional financial management capacity across the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

Key responsibilities include and may not be limited to:

1. **Financial Planning and Budget Oversight**

The Head of Support Services leads organizational budgeting processes and ensures financial planning aligns with operational realities and strategic priorities.

Tasks:

- Review and consolidate annual organizational budgets and donor project budgets from all country operations
- Ensure consistency between programmatic plans, operational priorities, and financial forecasts
- Validate budget assumptions including exchange rates, inflation projections, staffing costs, and operational estimates
- Review cost allocations across grants, shared costs, and general organizational operations
- Support Country Offices and program teams in developing realistic and compliant donor budgets
- Ensure budget structures align with donor regulations and internal financial controls
- Monitor overall organizational financial sustainability and resource allocation

Key Competencies:

- Strong financial planning and budgeting expertise
- Advanced analytical and forecasting skills
- Understanding of donor budgeting requirements
- Strategic financial oversight capacity

1. **Fund Management and Financial Oversight**

The role oversees organizational fund management processes and ensures financial liquidity and accountability across all operations.

Tasks:

- Oversee inter-office fund transfers and HQ financial allocations
- Review and approve fund requests from Country Offices
- Monitor cash flow, liquidity, and financial reserve levels
- Monitor foreign exchange exposure and associated financial risks
- Ensure donor funds are utilized in accordance with approved budgets and restrictions
- Track organizational spending thresholds and authorization compliance
- Support the CEO on high-level financial decision-making and risk management

Key Competencies:

- Strong treasury and cash-flow management skills
- Financial risk management expertise
- Understanding of multi-country fund management
- Strong attention to accountability and financial control

1. **Expenditure Management and Internal Controls**

The Head of Support Services ensures organizational expenditures comply with internal policies, donor regulations, and approval frameworks.

Tasks:

- Review expenditures above approved authorization thresholds and submit to the CEO for final approval where required
- Review complex procurement packages including competitive bidding documentation and vendor justifications
- Ensure expenditures comply with donor restrictions and organizational policies
- Monitor implementation of internal control procedures across all country operations
- Identify and address financial control weaknesses and operational risks
- Ensure procurement and expenditure documentation is audit-ready and properly archived

Key Competencies:

- Strong internal control and compliance knowledge
- Procurement and donor compliance understanding
- Risk identification and mitigation skills
- Attention to detail and accountability

1. **Accounting, Reconciliation, and Financial Systems Oversight**

The role ensures the accuracy, integrity, and efficiency of organizational accounting systems and financial records.

Tasks:

- Oversee organizational accounting and bookkeeping processes across all country operations
- Ensure financial entries, reconciliations, and classifications are accurate and completed on time
- Review month-end and year-end closing processes
- Conduct periodic spot checks of financial records and supporting documentation
- Ensure bank reconciliations and petty cash reconciliations are completed accurately and on schedule
- Supervise organizational use of QuickBooks Online (QBO)
- Coordinate with system consultants on QBO structure optimization and reporting systems
- Maintain oversight of chart of accounts, donor classes, and financial coding structures

Key Competencies:

- Advanced accounting and bookkeeping knowledge
- Strong financial systems management skills
- QBO proficiency and oversight experience
- Strong reconciliation and audit trail management skills

1. **Financial Reporting and Donor Compliance**

The role oversees organizational financial reporting processes and ensures compliance with donor and regulatory requirements.

Tasks:

- Consolidate financial data from all country operations into organizational financial reports
- Review and validate donor financial reports prior to submission to the CEO and donors
- Ensure financial reports meet donor formatting, compliance, and deadline requirements
- Review budget versus actual (BvA) reports and variance explanations
- Provide structured feedback to Country Offices on reporting quality and compliance gaps
- Ensure consistency between programmatic implementation and financial reporting
- Support donor financial reviews and due diligence processes

Key Competencies:

- Strong donor financial reporting expertise
- Financial analysis and variance interpretation skills
- Understanding of humanitarian donor compliance frameworks
- Strong organizational and coordination skills

1. **Audit, Compliance, and Organizational Risk Management**

The Head of Support Services leads financial compliance and audit coordination processes across all INARA operations.

Tasks:

- Maintain and update financial policies, SOPs, and internal control frameworks
- Coordinate external audits including donor audits, IRS filings, and independent organizational audits
- Ensure implementation and follow-up of audit recommendations
- Oversee submission of IRS Form 990 and other compliance-related financial filings
- Support compliance across INARA’s legal entities and jurisdictions
- Identify organizational financial risks and recommend mitigation measures
- Ensure compliance with donor regulations, anti-fraud standards, and applicable legal requirements

Key Competencies:

- Strong audit and compliance management experience
- Knowledge of nonprofit regulatory frameworks
- Risk management and governance expertise
- Strong policy development and implementation skills

1. **Systems Strengthening and Capacity Building**

The role strengthens organizational financial systems and supports finance staff development across all operations.

Tasks:

- Supervise and support Country Finance Leads and finance staff across all country operations
- Conduct finance staff performance evaluations and capacity development planning
- Organize training workshops and refresher sessions on financial procedures and systems
- Identify inefficiencies within financial systems and recommend improvements
- Support automation and financial process optimization initiatives
- Strengthen organizational financial documentation and reporting systems
- Promote standardization of financial practices across all country operations

Key Competencies:

- Leadership and staff management skills
- Capacity building and mentoring experience
- Systems improvement and problem-solving skills
- Strong coordination and communication abilities

**Key working relationships**

- CEO: Primary line manager and final financial approval authority
- Country Directors: Coordination on budgets, expenditures, and operational finance oversight
- Country Finance Leads: Technical supervision and financial management oversight
- Partnerships & Development Department: Coordination on proposal budgets and donor financial reporting
- Program Teams: Budget planning and financial monitoring support
- Auditors and External Consultants: Compliance, audit, and systems coordination
- SMT: Strategic financial planning and organizational decision-making

**THE POST-HOLDER WILL BE EXPECTED TO DEMONSTRATE MEASURABLE PROGRESS AGAINST THE FOLLOWING WITHIN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS:**

The post-holder will be expected to demonstrate measurable progress against the following within the first six MONTHS:

- Reporting validation process fully established and adhered to across all active country operations
- Zero reports submitted to Partnerships & Development without completed quality review
- SMT action tracker operational and actively maintained, with no overdue items going unescalated
- Entity documentation archive created and populated for all INARA legal entities
- Coordination gaps between Country Offices, Finance, and Partnerships & Development visibly reduced
- Positive feedback from Country Directors, Finance, and the CEO on coordination quality and turnaround times

**Requirements & Qualifications**

**Qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or related field
- Professional accounting qualification preferred

**Experience**

- Minimum 7 years of progressive finance and operational management experience
- Experience in humanitarian or nonprofit sector finance management
- Experience managing multi-country financial operations
- Strong knowledge of donor compliance and nonprofit financial systems
- Experience with QuickBooks Online and financial reporting systems

**CONFIDENTIALITY AND SAFEGUARDING**

**Confidentiality**

As the position is involved in sensitive topics, he/she must observe absolute discretion within and outside the organization. Non-respect of this clause or any breach of responsibility may result in a written warning or immediate dismissal.

**Safeguarding**

INARA has zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, or harm to children and vulnerable adults. INARA employees must adhere strictly to safeguarding policies, maintain professional boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

jobs.title: Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Advisor
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we’d like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action. Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home.

The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, asking “Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

**Job Overview:**

IRC’s Global Crisis Analysis, Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security, and Preparedness teams have come together to form ‘ASAP’ (Analysis, Security, Access and Preparedness) to strengthen global and regional support to IRC teams to deliver in the most complex, volatile and high-risk operating environments to reach the worst-affected and least-served people in need. Housed within the IRC’s Emergency Unit, but supporting countries and emergencies responses across IRC’s footprint, the Advisor allies with country and emergency response leadership, ASAP colleagues, and Regional Safety and Security Directors, to provide strategic, technical and operational support to enable IRC to open, expand, and sustain programs in emergencies, major crises, and complex environments – to reach the worst-affected and least-served populations.

The Advisor will work alongside the Director, and the Emergency Response Team Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Coordinator, to split responsibilities by country portfolio and/or thematic demands and/or level of complexity based on their respective scope of work and experience. The role brings additional capacity, and challenges and supports teams to meet IRC’s mandate through effective analysis and scenario planning to inform program and operational ambitions, and support to deliver on these with enhanced humanitarian access and security management.

The International Rescue Committee’s Emergency Unit (EmU) leads IRC’s global emergency preparedness and response to sudden-onset crises, complex emergencies, and high-risk contexts. EmU strengthens IRC’s ability to operate safely and effectively in volatile environments through surge capacity, systems development, and expert technical leadership.

***Location:** This position is open to national candidates or candidates who have residency in either Kenya, UK or Geneva. Candidates from any other country that has an IRC Office, are welcome to apply as well and will be hosted in that country.*

***Fluency in both written & Spoken French & English required***

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Humanitarian access management**

- Plan and deliver inclusive in-person and remote scenario development workshops as part of wider ASAP support to frontline program teams responding to major crises, linking those scenarios relevant strategies to support the IRC to serve the worst-affected and least-served populations despite conflict, volatility and risk.
- Support frontline program teams to develop and track indicators for tracking crisis developments in support countries, where requested as part of wider support, and actively contribute to information sharing with IRC colleagues about key crisis developments in support countries.
- Support country leadership to develop and implement specific access and acceptance strategies, in support of the Country Director/Emergency Team Leader, ASAP and/or RSSDs to enable and safeguard principled, secure, and sustained humanitarian access to reach target populations, in line with IRC policy and international humanitarian law – these may include a wide range of access approaches including broader risk management and remote management.
- Ensure strategies include how IRC builds relationships, engages and negotiates with authorities, key power brokers, security actors, and community stakeholders, including with state and non‑state actors, to ensure IRC’s mission and activities are understood and accepted, and that staff and programs can operate safely and without disruption.
- Build and maintain an active network of humanitarian access and security staff internally and across organisations.
- Maintain currency with methods, approaches and professional developments in relevant topics, and represent IRC in relevant global fora where needed.

**Safety and security management**

- Support country leadership and access, safety and security teams to identify, analyze and mitigate safety and security (S&S) risks across emergency responses, ensuring alignment with IRC Security Minimum Standards (SMS), Duty of Care, GEDI and PEERS principles, and integrate into access, security, preparedness strategies where relevant.
- Support the implementation of S&S standards and approaches to strengthen humanitarian access, and ensure S&S preparedness and contingency align with program ambitions.
- Support country/response teams in incident management, where relevant.

**Emergency preparedness**

- In close collaboration with ASAP and the Director, Emergency Performance and Quality, support country programs to develop and implement humanitarian access, safety and security approaches in their emergency preparedness and contingency plans, streamlining existing strategies and plans where relevant/possible, through in-country or remote mentoring, training and technical support.
- Support EmU in the development and adaptation of humanitarian access, safety and security systems, practices and resources, and centralized knowledge management.

**Learning & Development**

- Co-develop, with consortium partners, a humanitarian access framework that is accessible and used by partners to define access ambitions and strategies.
- Support the development, revision and uptake of IRC’s technical resources for analysis, security, access and preparedness, learning from operational experience, as well as global trends and good practices.
- Guide, train, coach and mentor IRC country leaders and frontline staff on humanitarian access approaches, safety and security, including Security Risk Management (SRM), and partner capacity strengthening, ensuring the inclusion of gender-sensitive approaches that address gender-specific risks.
- Design, deliver and track humanitarian access, safety and security capacity strengthening activities (including training, coaching, peer-to-peer learning) for EmU and priority country teams in access, safety and security training (including READI and humanitarian negotiation) and context analysis and scenario planning – leveraging internal and external resources.
- Ensure an ongoing exchange of learning and good practice in ASAP methods and approaches with partners; and deliver capacity sharing activities on analysis, access and security where relevant and prioritized.
- Contribute humanitarian access, safety and security content to EmU trainings and conferences and support cross-learning, and to global Safety and Security resources, as relevant.

**Partnerships**

- Champion a culture of effective and respective partnerships across the EmU, including supporting country and emergency teams to provide technical or operational support to partners.
- To further IRC’s partnership ambitions, ensure partners play a central role in the development of access, security and engagement strategies, and the identified approaches, including capacity sharing initiatives.
- Working with the EmU Partnerships focal points, ensure IRC technical resources for humanitarian access, safety and security are adapted and/or oriented towards partners for their own adaptations, and support partners in their uptake and cross-contextual learning and application amongst partners and IR.
- Design and deliver capacity sharing activities with partners where this is identified by the country program and ASAP access and security support, including peer-to-peer exchange and humanitarian negotiation.
- Collaborate closely with consortium partners to learn, coordinate and ensure the shared delivery of each organisation’s analysis, security, access and preparedness approaches within the defined Project results, including grant reporting and capturing case studies.

**Team Culture**

- Build and maintain strong working relationships across EmU, the Global S&S Department and regional/country colleagues to promote a culture of partnership, collaboration and One IRC.
- Cultivate and maintain a positive, collaborative, safe and protective work environment, while additionally setting an example of ‘One IRC’-way of working within the team, EmU, and the wider organization.
- Contribute to efforts across EmU and through ASAP support to safe, diverse, and inclusive culture and ways of working across our programming.
- Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding, GEDI commitments, and IRC values.

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Work Experience:**

- At least 8 years of non-profit or NGO work experience within international humanitarian assistance programs with demonstrated successes in planning, organizing and managing safety and security in complex and volatile environments.
- Significant practical experience in humanitarian access, humanitarian negotiation, civil-military coordination, security management or related competencies.
- Substantial and documented prior experience as a facilitator – the ability to develop, implement, facilitate and impart learning to a wide range of audiences.
- Experience with collaborative/inclusive development of tools, guidance and learning materials for/with practitioners.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of legal and normative frameworks for humanitarian action and expertise in applying humanitarian principles in practice.
- Thorough familiarity with principles and current approaches to humanitarian access and acceptance models of security management, including demonstrated understanding and successes in gender security management and gender equality.
- Ability to gain a precise understanding of the various local, regional, country and international policies, operational positions and interactions, and ability to support analysis and its uptake into decision making before and during emergencies and major crises.
- Advanced skills in humanitarian negotiation, humanitarian-military relations and/or engagement with armed groups.
- Strong communication, diplomatic, relationship building and interpersonal skills, including to influence and obtain cooperation of individuals not under supervisory control.
- Proficiency in facilitating challenging conversations, and challenge teams, on strategic, technical and operational subject matter to create shared understanding and inform decisions.
- Proficiency in delivering training and coaching support to individuals, teams and/or partners.
- Humility in analysis, ways of working and willingness to learn with teams in the most complex settings.
- Able to work as member of multinational team and manage a variety of external and internal relationships to achieve results.
- Excellent ability to produce user-centered, effective, and responsive guidance, tools and materials.
- Ability to summarize sophisticated topics and information inclusively, clearly and succinctly.
- Demonstrated commitment to gender equality, diversity, and inclusion in humanitarian settings.
- Ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized and underrepresented groups in emergency response.
- Experience working with diverse teams and communities, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other groups at risk of exclusion.
- Commitment to ongoing learning and reflection on personal and organizational biases, and willingness to adapt practices to promote inclusion.

**Language Skills:** Proficiency in English and French required; Arabic and Spanish of additional added value.

**Key working relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Director of Emergency Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security

**Position directly supervises:** N/A

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:** ASAP colleagues, Regional Safety and Security Directors, Emergency Safety & Security Coordinator

**Working Environment*****:*** Up to 40% international travel may be required, including to environments affected by armed conflict.

**Compensation:** (Switzerland Pay Rate: CHF 100,000 - 115,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: GBP 60,000 - 66,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Gender Equality**: The IRC is committed to advancing gender equality, diversity, and inclusion in all aspects of our emergency response. We recognize that diverse teams and inclusive approaches are essential for effective humanitarian action and for ensuring that the needs and rights of all affected populations are respected and addressed.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Caseworker
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive case management services enrolled clients.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:**  Casework Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusivity:** IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**Compensation:** ($20.97). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Head of Humanitarian Mine Action
jobs.body:
**The Danish Refugee Council (DRC)** is a leading protection agency with a mandate to protect, advocate for and promote durable solutions for displacement-affected populations. DRC has been operating in Ukraine since 2014 and currently employs over 800 staff implementing emergency and recovery programming across the Protection, Livelihoods, Shelter/NFIs and Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (humanitarian mine action) sectors through direct interventions and support to duty bearers and civil society organisations (CSOs).

DRC’s programming is based on an integrated approach in which sectors are designed to complement and reinforce one another to maximise impact for conflict-affected communities. Within this model, humanitarian mine action is not viewed solely through clearance outputs such as square metres released, but as an enabler for recovery and durable solutions. The focus is on outcomes for communities — whether land can safely be cultivated again, infrastructure restored, services resumed and displaced populations supported to rebuild their lives.

DRC implements this approach through a decentralised operational model in which most of the programme delivery, coordination and day-to-day decision-making takes place through its area offices rather than the Country Office. The Country Office provides strategic coordination, technical guidance, oversight and support services to enable field operations. This structure is intended to ensure that programmes remain closely connected to local realities and community needs while maintaining coherent technical and operational standards across the response.

This integrated and outcome-oriented approach differentiates DRC from other mine action operators. The Head of HMA, while focused on the responsibilities outlined below, is therefore expected to work across functions and sectors to enable integrated, area-based programming and support operational decision-making that contributes to broader recovery outcomes for conflict-affected communities.

**Overall purpose of the role**:

**The role of the Head of Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA)** is to provide the overall leadership, management and oversight of the delivery of DRC’s HMA portfolio in Ukraine.

The Head of HMA works under the supervision of the Head of Operations (HoO) and in close collaboration with the Head of Programs and Country Director (CD). The Head of HMA will cut across the Programme and Operations departments of DRC Ukraine and have responsibilities across both areas of work. Engagement on any programmatic elements will be in consultation with the Head of Programme (HoP) while engagement on operational elements with the Head of Operations (HoO).

The role of the Head of HMA is to guide the development of the HMA Programme Strategy, serve as the focal point for external engagement and fundraising on HMA and provide the overall leadership, management and oversight of the delivery of DRC’s HMA portfolio in Ukraine. The role also leads the liaison with Mine Action Authorities at central level and drives the capacity building and nationalization strategy for HMA staff.

**Your main duties and responsibilities will be:**

**People Management**

- Lead and line manage direct reports (including people planning, development, performance appraisal and well-being) in line with DRC policies and national legislation.
- Maintain strong oversight of the HMA team structure at Country and Area Office levels. Ensure sound management practices are in place within the team. Advise the management on critical positions and flag challenges.
- Drive capacity building of key HMA staff in technical functions and oversee the development and implementation of nationalisation plans for key roles within the HMA teams.

**Strategic Leadership and Programme Oversight**

- Sets the strategic direction of the HMA Programme in alignment with DRC Ukraine country and area strategies.
- Leads the design, review, and updating of the HMA strategy in coordination with the HoP.
- Ensures HMA priorities are aligned with national mine action strategies, donor priorities, and DRC global technical standards.
- Represent HMA in extended SMT.
- Work closely with Protection and VA teams to identify synergies and conflict-sensitive, people-centred programming opportunities.
- Identify and promote opportunities for integration between HMA and other DRC sectors (Protection, Shelter, Economic Recovery) and support joint analysis and integrated responses based on protection monitoring and community needs.

**Programme Design and Development**

- Participates in relevant Go/No-Go decision-making processes for HMA funding opportunities.
- Leads all HMA technical inputs to concept notes and proposals, including setting targets, outputs and indicators and developing budgets and workplans for both direct and partner-led implementation
- Conduct technical review of partner proposals and budgets in coordination with Grants, MEAL and Partnerships.

**Programme Reporting, Monitoring & Communications**

- Ensures quality and timely HMA inputs are provided to donor reports and communication products.
- Provides technical review of all HMA-related reporting before submission.
- Oversees data collection and management in line with IMSMA standards, in coordination with the Deputy Head of Programme and MEAL Manager.

**Localisation and Partnership Development**

- Lead the HMA localisation strategy under the coordination of the HoP.
- Ensures capacity assessments inform the selection of national HMA partners and that capacity development plans are designed in line with DRC's strategy.
- Ensures partner-led implementation and partners' capacity development meet DRC's technical and quality standards.

**Operational Delivery**

- Holds overall responsibility for the planning and delivery of DRC's HMA portfolio in Ukraine, ensuring workplans and technical implementation plans are followed throughout project implementation, with regular updates and adjustments as needed.
- Oversee all phases of implementation and closure for both direct and partner-led activities.
- With the support of the HMA Operations Manager, ensures operational planning for the delivery of clearance, survey, and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education activities.
- Ensure Training and Quality Management take place and are followed up.
- Ensure that priorities set by the NMAA, MAC, Oblast authorities and the donors are taken into consideration in the planning and implementation of operational activities.
- Ensure that HMA projects adhere to operational Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and National and International Mine Action Standards in the field.
- Accountable for centralized and country level initiatives including procurements, certifications, partners capacity building, team training etc. in close coordination with the relevant colleagues.
- Ensure regular monitoring and quality assurance are provided including direct and partner led implementation including monitoring report and support to corrective actions.
- Regularly follow up with IM, MEAL and Grants to ensure achievements are understood and reported
- In close coordination with the Head of Safety, ensure coordination with Safety and Management takes place at area level regarding the selection of training areas and polygons. Coordinate regularly with the HoS to discuss any challenges faced in the area

**Finance, budget, Supply Chain & Procurement – in close cooperation with the Humanitarian Mine Action Operations Manager**

- Prepares and updates monthly budget forecasts, workplans, and procurement plans for country office-level lines and initiatives
- Ensure all country office-level HMA procurements are planned, initiated and followed up.

**External Engagement**

**Donors:**

- Serve as the focal point for HMA donor engagement in close coordination with the HoP and CD.
- Prepare technical talking points for donor meetings, visits, and events.
- Contribute to donor relationship management, including participation in donor visits and sector events, in coordination with HoP and CD.

**Authorities**

- Ensures coherent and high-quality technical engagement with national and local mine action authorities.
- Maintains oversight of technical communication with authorities and inform SMT of key developments, policy changes, or risks.

**Mine Action Actors and UN System**

- Represent DRC Ukraine in mine action coordination mechanisms (e.g. AoR, technical working groups).
- Engages with other HMA actors to promote coordination, learning, and best practice sharing.

**About you**

To be successful in this role, we expect you to bring deep technical expertise and a strong track record in operations and people management. You are a confident and structured manager, able to lead diverse teams while keeping a clear focus on capacity building and the nationalisation of roles. Diplomatic, patient and persistent, you build lasting professional relationships with national authorities and other mine action actors while holding the line on technical and operational standards. A genuine team player, you approach challenges with a constructive, cooperative and problem-solving mindset.

Beyond technical excellence, you bring a genuine interest in integrated programming and are comfortable working across functions and sectors to contribute to broader recovery outcomes for conflict-affected communities.

We also expect the following:

- Minimum 7 years of working experience with strong knowledge in the HMA sector at senior level, evidenced by recognised technical qualifications. EOD qualifications are an asset but not a requirement.
- Minimum 5 years of experience managing and leading multi-disciplinary teams in complex humanitarian contexts, including experience of working in conflict settings.
- Demonstrated experience in programme strategy design and development, including proposal writing and budget management for multiple concurrent grants.
- Solid understanding of HMA programme cycle management, including IMAS/NMAS compliance.
- Experience in external engagement with donors, Mine Action Authorities and UN coordination bodies.
- Experience in partner and localisation management, including capacity development of national partners.
- Experience coordinating across departments (Programme, Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, HR) at field and country office level.
- Demonstrated commitment to DRC's integrated and outcome-oriented programming approach.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

- **Contract length**: 12 months fixed-term contract with the possibility of extension depending on performance and availability of funding after successful completion of a 3-month probationary period
- **Band**: E1 – Manager
- **Designation of Duty Station**: Kyiv, non-family duty station
- **Start date:** ASAP

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national and international employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-us/work-with-us/working-at-drc/salary-package-and-benefits/).

jobs.title: Partnerships and Private Sector Engagement Manager Ethiopia
jobs.body:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC Ethiopia is looking for an experienced **Partnerships and Private Sector Engagement Manager** to lead and strengthen how we build, manage, and grow meaningful partnerships.

In this role, you will play a key part in developing and implementing NRC Ethiopia’s Partnership Strategy and related SOPs, ensuring that our partnership approach is aligned with NRC’s vision, strategic priorities, policies, and commitment to localisation. You will help create a consistent and coordinated approach to partnerships across the Country Office and, where needed, Area Offices. You will build and maintain strong relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders, including civil society organisations, private sector actors, academic institutions, and public authorities. You will also oversee the full lifecycle of formal partnerships - from due diligence and partner selection to capacity assessments, agreement management, compliance monitoring, and audits. Working closely with Specialists, Area Programme Managers, Project Managers, and Finance teams, you will ensure that partnerships are well managed, compliant, and focused on delivering quality programmes.

A key part of your role will be to support and strengthen the capacity of NRC’s partners. You will ensure that partners understand relevant donor requirements, compliance regulations, reporting deadlines, and NRC procedures, while providing practical support to help them meet these requirements. Beyond partnership management, you will also help strengthen the culture of meaningful and equitable partnerships within NRC Ethiopia. You will advise colleagues and leadership on strategic partnership decisions, promote knowledge and capacity sharing, and contribute to advancing localisation across our programmes.

This is an important role for someonewho believes that strong partnerships are more than agreements on paper. They are relationships built on trust, shared responsibility, mutual learning, and a common commitment to achieving better outcomes for the people we serve.

If you are an ***Ethiopian National,*** and an experienced partnership professional who enjoys connecting people, organisations, and ideas - and who can turn partnerships into practical results - we would like to hear from you.

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBTQeJF3blRT5elCWWMeS2LARr8L5V6kYkRmB6UPbkATYQ?e=OSmpf8) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- 3-5 years of experience in working in a humanitarian/recovery/human rights or development context.
- University degree combined with relevant professional background.
- Knowledge of humanitarian principles.
- Experience in managing and implementing programs in humanitarian contexts.
- Ability to work independently and proactively.
- Ability to prioritise work given multiple competing deadlines.
- Fluency in English and Amharic, both written and verbal.
- Solid understanding of the Ethiopian civil society and private sector context.
- Documented/proven results related to the position’s responsibilities, particularly in private sector engagement and partnership relations, management and/or coordination.
- Excellent networking, coordination, training and facilitation skills.
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Excellent interpersonal skills, proactive, self -motivated and a self -starter.
- Excellent attention to detail, organisational skills and discretion with confidential information.
- Previous experience working in complex and volatile contexts is an asset.
- Programme management background is an asset. Experience in NRC thematic areas (e.g. ICLA, Shelter, LFS, Protection, Education etc.) is a strong asset.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Addis-Ababa, Ethiopia
- Contract: 12 months (Fixed -term contract renewal based on performance, funds availability and need for the position)
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s Resident/National salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Award Management Team Senior Assistant, AMEE (Asia, Middle East, Europe) - UK or NL
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Location:** UK or NL - flexible working

**Position Status:** Full-time, Exempt, Regular

**Salary : UK** starting £31,120 ; **NL** starting 36,720 euros

commensurate with professional experience and internal equity.

**Closing date:** Please submit application by **October 15th**

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) **☐ Level 3 ☐Level 2** X **Level 1**

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data

## **About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

## **The Awards Management Team**

The Awards Management Team (AMT) works in lockstep with Prosper Global’ country teams to ensure they have the resources, tools, and information they need to succeed in the implementation of high-quality programs across three areas by:

- Stewarding award management from kick-off to close out, supporting adherence to donor requirements, aligning donor contractual deliverables with internal program quality and compliance standards to deliver program impact, resolving compliance issues, and promoting knowledge management;
- Contributing to strategic new business development by identifying new funding opportunities, supporting high-quality program design, and leading submission efforts aligned with donor requirements; and
- Serving as liaison between Prosper Global' program teams and their most critical relationships with internal and external stakeholders

Prosper Global operates across a diverse and dynamic consolidated region spanning Asia, Middle East & Europe (AMEE), including Ukraine, Georgia, Moldova, Syria, Yemen, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Afghanistan, Indonesia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Thailand. Contexts range from protracted conflicts, displacement, and acute humanitarian crises to climate vulnerability, poverty, and rapidly evolving development landscapes. Across this spectrum, Prosper Global applies a layered resilience approach, delivering food and water security, economic opportunity, and energy access while fostering self-reliance and local leadership. The region also presents growing opportunities for private-sector engagement, blended finance, and innovative partnership models, enabling Prosper Global to bridge relief and long-term development through climate-smart, evidence-driven programming.

## **The Position**

The Awards Management Team Senior Assistant provides advanced administrative, logistical, and knowledge management support to the Awards Management Team, including Awards Management Team Lead, AMT Manager and AMT Program Officers (POs). The Senior Assistant plays a key role in maintaining organized workflows, managing programmatic information and data, directing information flows, and liaising with other Global and Regional departments.

## **Essential Responsibilities**

## **Awards Management Support:**

- Maintain organized workflow of program/department activities through tracking and record-keeping: track donor requirements, reporting deadlines, and reminders.
- Upon request, assist AMT POs with reviewing, editing, assembling, formatting, and ensuring timely submission of donor reports and other deliverables.
- Participate in and maintain records/notes of check-in calls with teams.
- As needed, prepare and communicate new award initiation summaries and support close-out processes.
- Support donor portal reporting and content uploading.

## **Proposal Support:**

- Track and identify upcoming proposal opportunities, searching databases for new opportunities and summarizing them for country and regional teams
- Upon request, provide administrative support for proposal development, such as drafting standard annexes (e.g., Past Performance Reports, capacity statements), copy-editing, formatting, obtaining signatures, and final compilation/submission.

## **Administrative Support:**

- Provide advanced project and team planning support, including assisting with Awards Management Team meeting administration (agendas, notes).
- Support finalizing agreements by coordinating signatures.

All other duties as assigned by supervisor.

## **Supervisory Responsibility**

None

- **Reports Directly To: Awards Management Team Lead, AMEE**
- **Works Directly With:** Regional Program teams, Country Directors and in-country Programs and Awards/Grants Management teams, Donor Compliance, International Finance, Institutional Donor Engagement, Philanthropic Growth & Engagement

## **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

## **Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information clearly and concisely for various audiences.
- Must be a detail-oriented, multi-tasker who is able to communicate clearly and work under pressure.
- Must demonstrate patience and flexibility and take initiative to solve problems.
- Proven ability to build and maintain strong, collaborative working relationships with diverse internal teams and external stakeholders across different cultures and time zones.
- Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, track deadlines, and ensure timely completion of tasks for self and direct reports.
- A robust sense of humor is greatly appreciated.
- A demonstrable passion for, and a clear empathy with, the organization's aims and values.

## **Required Education and Experience**

- Bachelor’s degree in International Development or related field, OR equivalent combination of education and 3+ years of administrative support experience.
- Demonstrated experience providing high-quality administrative, coordination, or program support to large and diverse teams, preferably at a distance.
- Proficiency with MS Office software (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, SharePoint)
- Prior NGO or international development experience preferred.
- Fluency in written and spoken English required. Proficiency in another regionally relevant language is preferred.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

This position may require up to 10% travel to support country programs, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited. Prosper Global Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short term assignment to a field posting. Staff are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and Prosper Global's policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

## **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

## **Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

jobs.title: Digital Community Liaison (Dari and Pashto)
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Digital Community Liaison for Settle In, a program providing information and support for newcomers in multiple languages through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on [https://www.settleinus.org](https://www.settleinus.org).

The Digital Community Liaison will support the Settle In Facebook page ([https://www.facebook.com/SettleInUS](https://www.facebook.com/SettleInUS)), which is available in Dari, Pashto, Spanish, Haitian-Creole, and English. Digital Community Liaisons interact with newcomers in the United States on social media primarily through private messaging and social media post comments. They help users navigate information on Settle In platforms, clarify and share information, support live events, and lend a friendly, empathetic ear. This position reports to Settle In’s Senior Digital Community Officer.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Support the Settle In Facebook page in collaboration with the Settle In team.
- Reply to messages and comments received on Settle In with the help of trusted resources and by following moderation guidelines and escalation protocols.
- Translate articles, video scripts, and social media posts in Dari and Pashto focused on key Cultural Orientation messages in coordination with the Senior Digital Community Officer.
- Record live event audio and other video scripts in Dari and Pashto
- Contribute to a Frequently Asked Questions document in English, Dari, and Pashto that can be used to answer user questions on the platform.
- Based on user messages, comments, and questions or misunderstandings, propose new content topics to feed into content creation.
- Share opinions, feedback, cultural awareness, contextual knowledge, and learning with the wider team on an ongoing basis. Present findings to relevant external partners, as needed.
- Collaborate with other staff to ensure maximum visibility and integration of all new resources.
- Support collection of monitoring and evaluation data for Settle In initiatives.
- As needed, backstop and support other Settle In team members.

**Job Requirements:**

- 4-year college degree in relevant field required (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum one year of relevant professional experience.
- Fluent in English and Dari and Pashto.
- Strong computer proficiency and well-acquainted with basic software tools. Can navigate autonomously in Windows and Microsoft Suite.
- Knowledge of social media platforms, especially Facebook, and cultural use of these platforms or ability to learn new technologies quickly.

- Excellent written and oral communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively in English and Dari and Pashto.
- High emotional intelligence (our users are in difficult periods of their lives and moderators need to empathize with them).
- An understanding of the power and importance of accurate information. Fantastic attention to detail.
- Solid organizational skills with the ability to juggle multiple tasks, set priorities, effectively manage time, and meet deadlines.

***Language Skills:** Fluent in written and spoken Dari, Pashto, and English.*

IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation.
