- Le poste nécessite des déplacements réguliers vers les formations sanitaires appuyées par l'IRC, les zones de santé et les sites de réponse en RDC.
- Le rôle peut nécessiter des visites dans des environnements cliniques, y compris des zones de dépistage, strictement conformément aux protocoles de PCI et de sécurité approuvés.
- Le poste exige une flexibilité pour répondre à l'évolution rapide des conditions épidémiologiques, opérationnelles et sécuritaires.

**Employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances** : L'IRC est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. L'IRC évalue tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur de peau, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, de situation matrimoniale, de statut d'ancien combattant, de handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**Normes professionnelles** : Tous les collaborateurs de l’International Rescue Committee (IRC) doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes fondamentaux énoncés dans le document « IRC Way – Normes de conduite professionnelle ». Nos normes sont l’intégrité, le service, l’égalité et la responsabilité. Conformément à ces valeurs, l’IRC met en œuvre et applique des politiques relatives à la protection des personnes, aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’intégrité financière, au signalement des irrégularités et à la protection contre les représailles. L’IRC s’engage à prendre toutes les mesures préventives nécessaires et à créer un environnement où chacun se sent en sécurité, ainsi qu’à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires et correctives en cas de préjudice. L’IRC constitue des équipes de professionnels qui favorisent la réflexion critique, le partage des responsabilités, le débat et l’objectivité afin d’offrir les meilleurs services possibles à nos bénéficiaires.

**BACKGROUND**

On 15 May 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) declared its seventeenth Ebola outbreak following confirmation of cases in Ituri Province. The outbreak has since expanded to other affected and at-risk areas, placing additional pressure on an already fragile health system. The response is unfolding in a complex humanitarian context characterized by conflict, population displacement, limited access to health services, and persistent gaps in infection prevention and control (IPC), WASH, surveillance, referral systems, and essential medical supplies. These challenges increase the risk of healthcare-associated transmission and disruption of essential health services.

IRC has launched an integrated Ebola response in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and relevant national, provincial, and health zone response structures, including the COUSP, Provincial Health Divisions (DPS), Health Zone management teams (BCZ), health facilities, and other response partners. IRC’s response brings together Health, IPC/WASH, Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Protection, and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). The health response focuses on strengthening the capacity of health facilities to safely detect and refer suspected Ebola cases, improving IPC and patient safety, strengthening facility-based surveillance and referral pathways and supporting the continuity of safe.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Health Coordinator provides overall technical leadership and program oversight for IRC’s Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) health response in DRC. Reporting to the Ebola Deputy Director of Programs (DDP), the position is responsible for ensuring that IRC’s health response is technically sound, operationally feasible, monitored against agreed results, and aligned with Ministry of Health (MoH), national EVD response structures and IRC standards.

The Health Coordinator leads the technical direction of the facility-based EVD programming, including Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), screening and triage and temporary isolation, facility-based surveillance, occupational exposure prevention and safe continuity of essential health services. The position directly supervises Senior IPC Managers and provides technical oversight, mentoring and quality assurance to health IPC teams across response locations. The role works closely with WASH, RCCE and Protection teams to ensure an integrated and accountable response.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Technical Leadership and Program Quality**

- Provide overall strategic and technical leadership for IRC’s EVD health response, translating outbreak epidemiology, response priorities and field evidence into clear program priorities and technical direction.
- Ensure health interventions are implemented in accordance with MoH protocols, national EVD response guidance, donor commitments and IRC technical standards.
- Provide technical oversight of facility-based EVD prevention and response measures, including screening and triage, temporary isolation, patient flow, standard and transmission-based precautions, hand hygiene, environmental cleaning and disinfection, healthcare waste management, PPE use and occupational exposure prevention.
- Ensure IRC-supported health facilities can safely identify, isolate and refer suspected EVD cases while maintaining safe access to essential health services and reducing healthcare-associated transmission risks.
- Guide development, adaptation and application of technical protocols, SOPs, checklists, job aids, assessment tools and quality-improvement approaches for the EVD response.
- Ensure program priorities and facility support are risk-based and responsive to evolving epidemiology, health-facility risks, healthcare-worker exposures, service-utilization trends and identified IPC/WASH gaps.
- Provide technical guidance during significant clinical or IPC incidents, ensure appropriate escalation and follow-up, and support program adaptation based on lessons learned.

**Program Management, Monitoring and Quality Improvement**

- Oversee implementation of IRC health/EVD programs against approved work plans, results frameworks, performance indicators, spending plans and grant commitments, ensuring timely corrective action where implementation is off track.
- Conduct regular field visits and technical reviews to assess program quality, mentor teams, verify implementation and follow up agreed corrective actions.
- Work with MEAL teams to ensure appropriate monitoring systems, databases, indicators and data-quality processes are in place and consistently used across the health response.
- Review and analyze program data, IPC assessment scores, surveillance and screening data, service-utilization trends, training and mentorship results, healthcare-worker infection/exposure events and commodity information to guide decisions and program improvement.
- Ensure timely, accurate and high-quality program updates, internal reports, donor reports and technical inputs to situation reports, clearly documenting achievements, gaps, risks, corrective actions and priorities.

**Staff Supervision, Leadership and Development**

- Directly supervise Senior IPC Managers and other senior health staff as assigned, setting clear priorities, reviewing performance and ensuring accountability for program quality and delivery.
- Provide regular technical supervision, coaching and mentoring to Senior IPC Managers and ensure consistent technical standards and approaches across response locations.
- Lead recruitment of key health/EVD positions in coordination with the DDP, HR and field management.
- Identify capacity gaps and ensure structured technical training, mentorship and professional development for health teams.
- Ensure appropriate duty-of-care measures for teams working in outbreak settings, including adherence to staff safety protocols, exposure prevention and incident reporting

**Business Development, Grant Management and Budget Oversight**

- Participate actively in development of Ebola-response concept notes and proposals, providing technical leadership for needs analysis, program design, activity packages, indicators, targets, implementation approaches and technical narratives.
- Work with Grants, Finance, Operations, MEAL and technical colleagues to develop realistic proposal budgets, staffing structures, procurement requirements and implementation plans aligned with program design.
- Oversee the health component of grant implementation and maintain responsibility for program budget management, including regular review of Budget versus Actuals (BvA), spending plans, burn rates, forecasts and identified variances.
- Ensure health teams maintain updated procurement plans and forecasts for PPE, IPC commodities, medical supplies, equipment and other program inputs, with appropriate linkage to activity and spending plans.
- Ensure quantification is informed by facility type, service volume, risk level, consumption data and program plans, with early action to prevent stock-outs or inappropriate use.
- Contribute to grant review meetings, donor reporting and program close-out, ensuring technical deliverables, expenditure and program results remain aligned.

**Coordination and Representation**

- Represent IRC in relevant national, provincial and Health Zone coordination forums, including Health Cluster and EVD-response technical structures.
- Maintain constructive working relationships with the MoH, DPS, Health Zone authorities, health-facility leadership, UN agencies, donors, NGOs and other response partners.
- Strengthen the quality of IPC activities through regular supportive supervision with the DPS and Health Zones.

**Partnerships**

- Serve as IRC’s health technical focal point for partnerships supporting the EVD response in Ituri and North Kivu, working collaboratively with partner technical leads.
- Contribute to joint technical planning, review and adaptation of the response, ensuring IRC’s health activities are complementary to those of partners and aligned with agreed response priorities.
- Represent IRC in relevant partnership technical discussions and ensure agreed technical actions relevant to IRC are communicated and followed up internally.

**Safety, Safeguarding and Accountability**

- Work with Safety and Security and field leadership to monitor risks affecting health teams and program delivery and ensure incidents or concerns are promptly reported and addressed.
- Promote client centered and accountable programming, including awareness and appropriate use of feedback and complaint mechanisms in supported services.
- Build safeguarding risk analysis and relevant risk mitigation measures into project design and implementation.
- Maintain updated, multisector service mapping and referral pathway for violence response. (This serves programming purposes but also underpins IRC's standard operating procedures for response to all safeguarding harm.

**REQUIRED PROFILE**

- Health professional with a strong public health background (MPH desirable).
- At least 3- 5 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian or emergency health programming, including management of complex health programs and supervision of senior technical staff.
- Demonstrated operational experience in Ebola Virus Disease, another viral haemorrhagic fever, or comparable infectious-disease outbreak response is strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated leadership, communication, and facilitation skills.
- Experience managing multidisciplinary teams across multiple field locations, with strong coaching, performance-management and problem-solving skills.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and routine program monitoring tools.
- Fluency in French is required with strong English proficiency; relevant local languages are an asset.

**WORKING ENVIRONMENT**

- The position requires regular travel to IRC-supported health facilities, Health Zones and response locations in DRC.
- The role may require visits to clinical environments, including screening areas, strictly in accordance with approved IPC and safety protocols.
- The position requires flexibility to respond to rapidly changing epidemiological, operational and security conditions.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Employment Specialist
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:** The Employment Specialist in Iowa assists newly arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to attain self-sufficiency through employment by guiding them through employment preparation, coordinating job placements, and other career advancement services.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake, assessment and provide program orientation to clients eligible for employment services. Develop comprehensive employment plans and budget strategies for each employable adult. Provide job readiness and job search coaching and connect clients with job opportunities.
- Develop and cultivate long-term relationships with area employers and staffing agencies to identify appropriate employment opportunities for clients.
- Assist clients and employers as necessary with post-placement issues and continuing employment needs.
- Monitor client job performance, wage levels, and related metrics.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of support staff, volunteers, and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in workforce development field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Experience with job placement and job readiness training a plus.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Proficient in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($21.00/hr - $22.80/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law***.***

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $143 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Annex 1-Terms of Reference: Mapping Barriers to Women’s Entry and Participation in the ECCD Workforce in Jordan, with a Focus on Refugee Women and Women with Disabilities**

**Terms of Reference**

**RFP\\JOR\\2026\\730**

**Background:**

Burden of Childcare Reduced and Addressed for Women in Jordan (BUCRA - meaning Tomorrow in Arabic) is a 5-year initiative (2024-2029) funded by Global Affairs Canada and designed to enhance the economic empowerment of women in Jordan. BUCRA takes a system approach that engages and supports local stakeholders from government, training bodies, the private sector and communities to drive gender-transformative change that addresses the most pressing childcare issues preventing women from participating and remaining in the workforce in Jordan. BUCRA targets over 8,600 women in 7 regions. The approach of equipping key stakeholders to address systemic barriers will enable the impacts to be experienced by women throughout Jordan over the long term.

In partnership with several local implementing partners including relevant government agencies, the Vocational Training Corporation (VTC) and the National Council of Family Affairs (NCFA) and civil society organization (Rayat Alyawm) under the umbrella of the Ministry of Social Development (MoSD). WUSC and partners will deliver under five key outcome areas: i) enhance the capacity of training providers to provide quality, market-relevant, and inclusive Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) training; ii) increase access by women to ECCD-related services to secure employment or start/expand their home-based nurseries; iii) improve capacity of key stakeholders to develop and implement gender-responsive policy and regulation fostering the availability of quality ECCD services; iv) improve attitudes among women and their communities about women's work and ECCD; and v) enhance the capacity of ECCD employers to provide quality, gender-responsive and inclusive ECCD services.

**Context:**

Women’s participation in the labour market in Jordan is influenced by a range of structural, institutional, economic, social, and cultural factors. While childcare is an important factor affecting women’s ability to enter and remain in the workforce, the Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) sector itself also represents an important area of employment and economic opportunity for women.

Women seeking to enter and participate in the ECCD workforce may face barriers related to policy and regulatory requirements, qualifications and training, recruitment and employment practices, working conditions, career progression, accessibility, transportation, and social and cultural norms etc.. These barriers may be particularly significant for refugee women and women with disabilities, who may face additional legal, institutional, accessibility, or social barriers.

While various studies and assessments in Jordan address women’s economic participation, gender norms, refugee employment, disability inclusion, and ECCD, there is a need to consolidate the existing evidence specifically on women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce and identify key research and knowledge gaps.

The consultancy will therefore map the existing evidence, identify key barriers and enabling factors, and highlight priorities for further research, policy and regulatory attention, advocacy, and programmatic action. The findings will also inform WUSC’s advocacy and policy dialogue with relevant policymakers and regulators.

#### **Purpose & scope of the Consultancy:**

The research aims to review and map existing studies and research on the key policy, regulatory, institutional, social, cultural, economic, accessibility, and other barriers affecting women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce in Jordan; identify what is currently known and where critical research and knowledge gaps remain, with particular attention to refugee women and women with disabilities; and highlight priority areas for further research, advocacy, policy, and programmatic action.

The findings will also provide an evidence base to inform WUSC’s advocacy and policy dialogue with relevant policymakers, regulators, and other stakeholders on barriers and potential actions to strengthen women’s participation in the ECCD workforce.

**Scope of Work:**

The consultant will be responsible for the following tasks:

- Develop a detailed inception plan and proposed research methodology for the assignment, including the analytical framework, research questions, data sources, consultation approach, tools, and timelines.
- Review and map existing research, studies, assessments, policies, laws, regulations, and available data relevant to women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce in Jordan.
- Build on relevant BUCRA research, including the In-Depth Needs Assessment on Guardian Engagement, Gender Norms, and Women’s Economic Opportunities and Right to Work in the ECCD Sector.
- Identify and analyse the key barriers affecting women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce, including policy, regulatory, institutional, social, cultural, economic, accessibility, and other relevant barriers.
- Examine barriers at different stages of women’s participation in the ECCD workforce, including entry and recruitment, access to training and qualifications, employment, retention, working conditions, professional development, and career progression, where evidence is available.
- Examine how these barriers may differ for different groups of women, with particular attention to refugee women, women with disabilities, and, where evidence is available, refugee women with disabilities.
- Identify what is currently known based on existing evidence and identify critical research, evidence, and knowledge gaps.
- Identify relevant enabling factors, promising practices, and existing approaches that may support women’s entry into and sustained participation in the ECCD workforce.
- Identify priority areas for further research, policy and regulatory attention, advocacy, and programmatic action.
- Generate practical, evidence-based recommendations that can support WUSC and relevant stakeholders in policy dialogue and advocacy with policymakers and regulators.
- Prepare a draft research report presenting the research findings, evidence and knowledge gaps, key barriers, and initial recommendations.
- Conduct a validation session with relevant stakeholders, as facilitated by the project team, to validate the draft findings, gather additional insights, and identify key issues and evidence gaps.
- Revise the draft research report based on feedback from the project team and relevant stakeholders.
- Finalize the research report based on feedback from WUSC and relevant stakeholders, ensuring clarity, coherence, an evidence-based approach, and usability for policy dialogue and advocacy purposes.
- Support the dissemination of the final research findings and recommendations through stakeholder presentations, as agreed with the project team.

**Deliverables:**

**Inception Report and Research Methodology**

- Detailed inception plan outlining the proposed research methodology, analytical framework, research questions, data sources, consultation approach, tools, approach, and timeline.

**Desk Review and Evidence Mapping**

- Comprehensive desk review and mapping of existing research and evidence on women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce in Jordan, including key barriers and enabling factors, with particular attention to refugee women and women with disabilities.
- Identification of what is currently known, critical research and knowledge gaps, priority issues, and areas requiring further research.

**Draft Research Report**

- Draft report presenting the research findings, key barriers and enabling factors affecting women’s entry into and participation in the ECCD workforce (with particular attention to refugee women and women with disabilities), evidence and knowledge gaps, policy and regulatory issues, priority areas, and initial recommendations.

**Validation Session**

- Validation session with relevant stakeholders to present and validate the draft research findings, gather additional insights, and identify key issues and evidence gaps.

**Final Research Report and Recommendations**

- Final research report incorporating feedback from WUSC and relevant stakeholders following the validation session.
- Clear and actionable, evidence-based recommendations for further research, advocacy, policy and regulatory action, and programmatic action, with particular attention to issues that can inform engagement with policymakers and regulators.

**Research Dissemination**

- Stakeholder presentation and/or dissemination session to present the final research findings and recommendations, as agreed with the project team.

**Location:**

The consultant should be based in Jordan . Any travel cost related to the assignment should be included in the financial proposal.

**Qualification requirements of the Consultant:**

The consultant is expected to meet the following qualifications and competencies:

**Education**: The lead consultant should possess at least a Master's degree in Business Administration, International Development, Social Sciences, Education, Public Policy, Gender Studies, or a related field. A Bachelor's degree with extensive relevant experience may be considered.

**Experience**:

- Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in research, policy analysis, or program evaluation in the areas of women’s economic empowerment, ECCD, education, social development, gender, or related sectors.
- Demonstrated experience in working on projects related to the childcare sector, early childhood development, or social enterprises is highly desirable.
- Demonstrated experience working on inclusion of marginalized populations, with relevant expertise on children and youth, refugees, and persons with disabilities.
- Proven experience conducting policy, legal, regulatory, and institutional analysis, preferably within the education, ECCD, social protection, gender, or related sectors.
- Strong knowledge of the Jordanian ECCD context, including relevant policies, regulations, national strategies, institutional frameworks, and the broader ECCD ecosystem affecting women’s economic participation.
- Demonstrated experience engaging with government institutions, civil society organizations, service providers, NGOs, and development partners through consultations, interviews, focus groups, or other participatory research processes.
- Strong research and analytical experience, including evidence synthesis, identification of research and data gaps, and qualitative and/or quantitative research methods, with the ability to translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
- Fluency in Arabic and English both written and spoken.

jobs.body:
**About the Context**

Nigeria continues to face a complex and protracted humanitarian crisis driven by armed conflict, insecurity, climate-related shocks, displacement, and economic challenges. The Northeast remains the epicentre of the crisis, where years of conflict have displaced millions of people and disrupted access to basic services, livelihoods, and protection. In addition, increasing levels of violence and displacement in the Northwest and North Central regions, alongside recurrent flooding and food insecurity, have further exacerbated protection and humanitarian needs across the country. The 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan estimates that 5.9 Million people are in need of humanitarian assistance.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been operating in Nigeria since 2015, delivering humanitarian assistance and durable solutions to conflict-affected and displaced populations. NRC works across multiple core competencies, including Education, Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Shelter, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), and Protection from Violence. Through direct implementation and partnerships, NRC supports displaced persons, returnees, and vulnerable host communities to meet their immediate needs, strengthen resilience, and pursue long-term recovery and self-reliance. NRC is committed to principled humanitarian action, safeguarding, accountability to affected populations, and ensuring that assistance reaches those most in need.

The purpose of the Finance function is to ensure the financial sustainability and integrity of the organization by managing its resources effectively, providing accurate financial reporting, and ensuring compliance with all legal, regulatory, and donor requirements. The function works in partnership with the other operational departments globally and in countries to enable NRC's mission.

The function is crucial for stewardship of organizational assets, providing strategic financial planning and analysis, managing internal controls, maximizing resource utilization, and ensuring accountability to all stakeholders.

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

**What we are looking for**

The Finance Manager is responsible for ensuring a functional finance structure in the country office, following organisational minimum standards. The role works towards providing optimal support to programme implementation and other functions within the structure. The position holder plays a key role in financial planning and analysis and the allocation of financial resources to the different areas of implementation.

**What you will do**

1. Oversee the implementation of all Finance related policies, procedures, strategies, and initiatives in coordination with the Finance team in country and area offices to ensure success, consistency, and compliance.
2. Line management responsibility for direct reporting staff and technical supervision responsibility for finance staff in area offices based on the NRC Technical Supervision. Guidelines. This includes: 
    - Performance management process setting clear goals aligned to strategic priorities and follow up and support staff’s achievement.
    - Workforce planning, recruitment, staff induction and development, and support for Duty of Care.
3. Develop and maintain country financial documents, procedures, guidance, and tools, including strategy, ensuring consistency across the country programme and in line with organisational standards.
4. Maintain the country’s overall budget control and monitor cash flows.
5. Ensure that budgeting, accounting, year-end procedures, and other financial processes take place in adherence to Financial Handbook, NRC policies, and donor and auditor requirements.
6. Train and develop NRC staff and partners’ capacity on financial and budgeting responsibilities.
7. Carry out a proper implementation for the Anti-Corruption Policy within all finance operations and activities.

**What you will bring**

**1.Professional Competencies**

- Minimum three years of experience working in a senior finance role with managerial responsibility in a humanitarian/recovery context.

- Coping with change

jobs.title: Research Manager for Afghanistan, based in Kabul
jobs.body:
## BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO with headquarters based in Paris and presence in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

### We are currently looking for a Research Manager to scope out and set-up a new Research Team focussing on the Economy, Markets, and Livelihoods

**Department**: IMPACT

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 4 months

**Starting Date**: 1st December 2026 (preferred); 1st January 2027 (latest)

**Location**: Kabul, Afghanistan.

## COUNTRY PROFILE

The humanitarian response in Afghanistan remains one of the largest in the world, with 21.9 million people identified as in need of assistance in the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan. The country is particularly vulnerable to climate change, with drought conditions affecting agriculture and livelihoods. Natural disasters, including flooding and earthquakes, remain prevalent – often causing displacement, damaging and destroying shelter and services, and disrupting livelihoods. Conflict remains a risk, with recent increase in conflict activity between Afghanistan and Pakistan. With millions of refugees in neighbouring countries, including Iran and Pakistan, forced return of refugees is also a driver of needs in the country.

Alongside this, since the De facto Authorities took control of the government in 2021, a range of restrictive policies have significantly restricted the rights of women and girls in society – leading to increased marginalisation and protection risks. The economic situation remains poor and authorities lack resources to run effective public services, with reliance on humanitarian assistance. As the USA was a major aid donor in Afghanistan, their withdrawal of all aid funding had a significant effect, for example on the closures of health centres. With political positioning of donor governments restricting a full development approach, a basic human needs response is increasingly complementing the humanitarian response across Afghanistan.

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives is planning a range of research activities to support an evidence- and needs-based humanitarian response. The IMPACT Deputy Country Representative (DCR) supports the Country Representative (CR) in overseeing programme strategy and implementation internally, as well as external representation of IMPACT.

## POSITION PROFILE

Following the development of our new Country Strategy, IMPACT Afghanistan is planning to establish a new research team with the aim of providing relevant information to humanitarian and basic human needs stakeholders linked to the economy, markets and livelihoods in Afghanistan.

IMPACT Afghanistan is therefore seeking an experienced Research Manager with knowledge of assessment and analysis, to scope out a programme of work for this new team, through internal and external consultations. The Research Manager will be responsible for drafting concept notes and research ToRs that can be used to solicit funding for the start-up of the team.

The Research Manager will be responsible for building an understanding of the relevant aid strategies existing in Afghanistan and identifying relevant data and research gaps that could be filled. This will involve connections with international and national NGOs (including members of Cash Consortium of Afghanistan), the UN, and donors. The Research Manager will review existing research in Afghanistan (including the MSNA and Joint Market Monitoring Initiative) and also connect across IMPACT to understand similar research being conducted elsewhere that could be adapted for the Afghanistan context.

## RESPONSIBILITIES

The Research Manager’s responsibilities will include:

***CONTEXTUAL UNDERSTANDING***

- Assess relevant strategic, analytical, and operational documents to develop an understanding of the current priorities relating to the economy, markets and livelihoods for the aid response in Afghanistan.
- Mapping existing IMPACT data, other research, and other relevant information sources to understand relevant areas for potential assessment and research.
- Connecting with national and international NGOs, UN colleagues, and the donor community to understand their priorities and to identify where IMPACT research could support their programmes and strategies.
- Provide SMT and other staff members with key updates from these efforts.

***DEPARTMENT STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT***

- Engage with IMPACT colleagues in HQ and in other country programmes to identify existing assessment and research tools that could be adapted for Afghanistan.
- Develop a series of concept notes that can be shared with prospective partners or donors, to seek funding for the set-up for the new team.
- Develop/draft relevant research ToRs, enabling technical discussion and approval of potential research projects.
- Develop a light-touch team strategy that could subsequently be further developed based on the eventual set-up and staffing of research activities.
- Coordinate with staff in the Cash Consortium of Afghanistan to identify potential assessment and research opportunities for the future of the Consortium.

***RESEARCH MANAGEMENT***

- As necessary, support the Humanitarian Coordination and Monitoring Unit in the delivery of research and analysis linked to Joint Market Monitoring Initiative and the Cash Consortium of Afghanistan.
- As required, work with the cross-cutting analysis team to support the develop of analysis products linked to the economy, markets, and livelihoods, which can better position IMPACT Afghanistan in this thematic field.

The Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## REQUIREMENTS

- **Work experience** Demonstratable relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as programme management, evaluation and assessments. Experience working with development responses is an advantage;
- **Thematic experience** Able to showcase experience in working with economy and market data in an aid environment’
- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research design, data collection, and data analysis experience required;
- **Familiarity with aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community.
- **Management experience** Demonstrated team management skills, including remote management;
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the region/supporting is desirable;
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting and reviewing;
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility and work independently;
- **Academic qualifications** A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline is preferred. However, significant relevant work experience can be considered.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset
- **Security environment** Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Dari or Pashto is an asset.

## COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

- For this position, salary between 3’050€ and 3’100 monthly before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Affiliation to French Social security (CFE) + health Complementary (Mobility Benefits) + Repatriation assistance (SOS International) + Private Pension Fund.
- Flight tickets every six months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- R&R after eight weeks, flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance
- Contribution to the transportation of luggage: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - three days at IMPACT Initiatives’ HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training (depending on previous inductions and security trainings taken);
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

jobs.title: Programme Manager (South)
jobs.body:
**Job Title:** Programme Manager (South)

**Department:** Programming

**Division:** Programme implementation

**Duty Station:** Mykolaiv, Ukraine (with frequent travel to Odesa and Kherson)

**Line Manager:** Head of Programme (HoP)

**Line Management Responsibility:** Team Leaders (South – Odesa & Mykolaiv & Kherson)

**Position Type:** Full-Time

**ABOUT US**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

Programming is founded on unarmed civilian protection and is thematically focused on protection in displacement, child protection, gender-based violence protection and inter-communal violence reduction, social cohesion, and civic engagement.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014/2015 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022. NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**JOB SUMMARY**

To manage the implementation of NP’s Programme, overseeing violence prevention programming in the South of Ukraine - covering Odesa, Mykolaiv and Kherson Oblasts - ensuring the project is implemented in accordance with NP’s mission and vision, compliances, and allocated budgets. The PM advances the collective effort of ensuring that programmes are evidence and needs driven, monitored closely, and are risk appropriate. The PM promotes and actively encourages coherency, quality assurance and crosspollination across field teams.

The PM will provide leadership for Team Leaders in close liaison with the HoP and will work directly with the Protection Advisor and Programme Development Team.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Programme Management**

- Responsible for the overall planning and effective delivery of the project(s) in areas of implementation through the application of Unarmed Civilian Protection approach.
- Provide technical advice and oversight for the field teams implementing violence reduction projects, either directly or through team leaders in field sites.
- Together with the SPM, guide teams in strategic planning, development of work plans and adapting implementation to address emerging protection needs and contextual or operational challenges.
- Provide oversight, monitoring and review of Salesforce reporting and contribute to internal reporting upon request (including context, programming, staffing and welfare). Highlight to SMT key points from Salesforce Activity Reporting.
- The PM will support field teams and serve as interlocutor with Management and the Programme Development team if programming has to be adapted to address dynamic contextual realities and/or if changing circumstances renders the project objectives irrelevant or impossible.
- Work very closely with MEL team to ensure the effective implementation of the monitoring, evaluation, and learning strategy of program in each of the program locations.
- Engage in direct programme implementation as needed, participate in integrated capacities and needs assessments and emergency response if needed. This may include direct support with in-house and partner technical trainings. Stand in as Acting Team Leader when necessary.
- Contribute to broader country programme strategy development together with the rest of the Programme and Management team.
- Participate in grant inception process with programme development, finance and operations and then lead grant inception process with field teams in partnership with Programme Development department.
- When requested, contribute to donor reporting for area of operations.
- When requested, support assessments and start-up in new areas of implementation.

**Representation and Advocacy**

- Represent NP in coordination and advocacy fora where appropriate and needed, including on issue-based advocacy in the South of Ukraine.
- Represent NP at the sub-national level (with local authorities in field locations) when Team Leaders request senior support.
- Provide guidance and direct support on access related negotiations in areas of operation as needed in close coordination with the SSA and HoM.
- In collaboration with the Programme Development team, represent NP in the South of Ukraine to donors, engaging in proactive communication to keep donors updated on the progress of the project and the evolving conflict and protection context.
- Represent NP in the South of Ukraine during donor visits to areas of operation and planning donor visits together with the Programme Development team and will whenever possible, accompany the donor on field visits.

**Financial & Operational Management**

- Supervise and ensure that teams comply with their internal and external reporting requirements.
- Support FPO and TL with field level budget management including coding of field level expenses in accordance with approved project budgets.
- Work directly with TLs to prepare monthly site forecasting and monthly reporting of actuals against forecasts and flag under/overspends and offer corrective measures.
- In coordination with SPM, establish site spending strategies to ensure best use of available funds as well as allocating team attention towards necessary budget line spending.
- Serve as interlocutor between field teams and programme support departments (HR, Finance and Operations), ensuring that the needs of field teams are met and that field teams are fully aware of what is happening operationally in the Country Office as it relates to their sites.

**Personnel Management**

- Serve as Line Manager for Team Leaders.
- Facilitate strong staff morale and positive working environment using and practicing the NP values as central guidance.
- Coach and guide team leaders on field-based personnel management, with the support of Human Resources colleagues, ensuring that labour law is adhered to, and NP Human Resources policies are known and implemented.
- Ensure sufficient level of staffing, identifying the need for new recruitment in a timely fashion.
- Participate in recruitment panels for South-based recruiting.
- Support Team Leaders to ensure that all field team staff (programme and programme support) receive timely performance reviews in close coordination with HR department.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- Master’s degree in project management, conflict resolution, conflict transformation, peace studies, international relations, political science, negotiation, mediation, human security or related area of study.
- 4-6 years work experience in civilian protection, violence prevention, social cohesion, peacebuilding.
- Minimum 1 year experience as a Team Leader or similar position with Nonviolent Peaceforce
- Demonstrated management experience in working in complex security environment.
- Demonstrated experience working with state authorities and negotiation
- Demonstrated ability to live, work and solve problems independently and effectively in remote, highly challenging locations
- Demonstrated ability to analyse conflict, security and political contexts
- Identify with NP values and UCP principles

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES:**

***Independent Judgment/Analytical:***

- Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data
- Ability to manage information with discretion
- Demonstrable conflict analysis skills, identify entry points and design prevention and protection strategies

***Interpersonal:***

- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and motivate and provide leadership to team and to work in a multi-cultural environment
- Solutions focused, creative problem solver
- Proven ability to build relationships with the full range of actors including government, various community leaders, military, police and non state actors
- Genuine commitment and interest in living and working at the community level
- Flexibility and adaptability

***Language:***

- Ability to interact confidently in English with colleagues and external contacts, to write documents and reports, and to present effectively relevant information
- Working Ukrainian language skills are an added benefit

***Information Technology:***

- Good skills in Microsoft Office applications. Hardware IT skills a definite asset

**Other Specialized Requirements**

- Ukraine is a complex security environment where conditions change rapidly – experience in insecure environments is essential to success in this position

**Working Conditions:**

- This field position may include challenging living conditions, limited access to amenities, and potentially unstable security situations.
- You must be prepared to live in basic or non-traditional accommodation, which may include shared housing, camps, or field-based settings
- Demonstrated ability to adhere to strict security protocols.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector. NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE**

**We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted** [**here** ](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/)**on our website.**

jobs.title: Endline Evaluation of the Strategic Partnership Agreement II Programme and Syria & Lebanon Top Ups
jobs.body:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**Endline Evaluation of the Strategic Partnership Agreement II Programme and Syria & Lebanon Top Ups**

**Commissioned by | ActionAid - Arab Region**

**Syria and Lebanon | 2022–2026**

**1. Background**

ActionAid Arab Region (AAAR), together with its local partners, has implemented the Strategic Partnership Agreement II funded by DANIDA in partnership with ActionAid Denmark in Syria and Lebanon from 2022 to 2026. The programme has been implemented in highly complex and protracted crisis contexts, requiring continuous adaptation to changing political, economic, humanitarian and protection conditions.

In Lebanon, implementation has been undertaken with SHIFT, Bassmeh & Zaitouneh, and RDFL, with interventions reaching communities in Tripoli, Jeb Jenine and Ba'albek.

In Syria, implementation was initially concentrated in Northwest Syria, through Violet and Bahar, and subsequently expanded to Latakia and Damascus in response to changing contextual and humanitarian needs.

The programme has also been complemented by two Top-Ups, one in Lebanon and one in Syria, which are included within the scope of this endline evaluation. The evaluation should therefore assess the overall contribution and performance of the core SPAII programme alongside the additional interventions and adaptations introduced through the Top-Ups.

The programme as a whole is expected to have reached approximately:

- **75,000+ people in Syria**, including people benefiting from humanitarian assistance in its various forms, including distributions, protection services and legal services; people participating in trainings; people accessing youth and safe spaces; and people participating in campaigns, collective action and other forms of civic engagement.
- **35,000+ people in Lebanon**, through similar combinations of humanitarian assistance, protection and legal services, trainings, youth and safe spaces, campaigning and collective action.

The programme has been structured around three Strategic Objectives:

**SO1: Rights and access to services**

**Young people, especially marginalised young women, enjoy fundamental rights through improved access to well-resourced programmes and public services in fragile situations.**

**SO2: Sustainable livelihoods and green solutions**

**Young people from refugee and host communities, especially marginalised young women, enjoy improved, sustainable livelihoods through government that is accountable towards building sustainable green solutions.**

**SO3: Resilience, protection and rights**

**Young people from refugee and host communities, especially marginalised women, are resilient to shocks and enjoy their rights to protection in protracted crises.**

The programme's Theory of Change (ToC) provides the overarching logic through which interventions are expected to contribute to improved rights, access to services, livelihoods, resilience, protection, collective action and longer-term systemic change.

Given the duration and complexity of the programme, the endline evaluation provides an opportunity not only to assess the extent to which the programme achieved its intended results, but also to examine how and why change occurred, the contribution of different interventions and partners, the quality of technical capacity and collective action, the programme's policy influence, and the extent to which programming remained relevant and adaptive in protracted crises\*\*.\*\*

**2. Purpose of the Evaluation**

The primary purpose of the endline evaluation is to provide an independent assessment of the performance, contribution and learning of the SPAII programme and its Top-Ups in Syria and Lebanon between 2022 and 2026.

The evaluation will assess the programme against the OECD DAC evaluation criteria of:

1. **Relevance** – Is the intervention doing the right things?
2. **Coherence** – How well does the intervention fit within its wider context and other interventions?
3. **Effectiveness** – Is the intervention achieving its intended objectives and results?
4. **Efficiency** – How well have resources been used to achieve results?
5. **Impact** – What difference has the intervention made?
6. **Sustainability** – Are the benefits, capacities, relationships and changes likely to continue?

In addition, the evaluation will place particular emphasis on the programme’s ability to adapt to changing and protracted crisis contexts, the quality and adequacy of ActionAid/AAAR’s technical leadership, guidance and support, the effectiveness and quality of collective action, the extent and nature of policy influence, and the relationship between programme implementation and the Theory of Change. The evaluation is expected to generate practical, forward-looking evidence and learning to inform future AAAR programming in Syria and Lebanon, the design of regional and country-level programmes, partnership and localisation approaches, adaptive programming in protracted and rapidly changing crises, technical leadership and support to partners, advocacy and policy influencing, youth engagement and collective action, and humanitarian-development-peace programming. Ultimately, the findings will contribute to AAAR’s organisational learning and strategic decision-making, helping to identify what worked well, where the programme could have done better, why particular approaches succeeded or underperformed, and what should be sustained, adapted or strengthened in future programming.

**3. Evaluation Questions**

The following questions should guide the evaluation. The evaluator should refine and prioritise these during the inception phase.

**A. Relevance**

1. To what extent did SPAII respond to the priority needs, rights and aspirations of young people, particularly marginalised young women?
2. To what extent did interventions remain relevant as the contexts in Syria and Lebanon changed between 2022 and 2026?
3. How well did the programme balance immediate humanitarian needs with longer-term rights, resilience, livelihoods and systemic change?
4. Were there important needs or groups that the programme did not adequately address?

**B. Coherence**

1. How well did SPAII complement other interventions implemented by AAAR and partners?
2. To what extent did the programme create meaningful links between humanitarian response, protection, rights, livelihoods, resilience and advocacy?
3. How well did interventions align with local systems, priorities and existing services?

**C. Effectiveness**

1. To what extent did SPAII achieve its intended outputs and outcomes?
2. Which interventions and approaches contributed most significantly to results?
3. Which interventions were less effective, and why?
4. To what extent did the programme achieve meaningful changes beyond activity and output-level results?
5. What factors enabled or constrained effectiveness?
6. Were there significant differences in results across countries, locations, partners, groups or types of intervention?

**D. Theory of Change**

1. To what extent did the programme's Theory of Change accurately explain how change occurred?
2. Which pathways of change were strongest?
3. Were there unexpected pathways or outcomes?
4. What contextual factors influenced the pathways of change?
5. What should be retained, modified or removed from the ToC for future programming?

**E. Efficiency**

1. Were resources appropriately allocated across interventions and locations?
2. To what extent did the programme achieve value for money?
3. Were programme resources sufficiently flexible to respond to changing needs?
4. How did partnership arrangements affect efficiency?
5. Were there significant operational or coordination constraints affecting implementation?

**F. Impact**

1. What meaningful changes can be attributed or plausibly contributed to by SPAII?
2. What difference did the programme make to young people's rights, resilience, protection, livelihoods and participation?
3. What unintended positive or negative effects emerged?
4. To what extent did the programme contribute to changes beyond direct beneficiaries?

**G. Technical leadership and guidance**

1. To what extent did AAAR provide adequate technical leadership and guidance to support the quality and effectiveness of SPAII implementation?
2. How well did AAAR's technical support respond to the specific realities of Syria and Lebanon, including the constraints associated with protracted crisis contexts?
3. Where were technical leadership or guidance gaps identified, and how did these affect implementation or results?
4. What technical guidance, systems or approaches should be retained, strengthened or developed for future programming?

**H. Collective Action and Policy Influence**

1. What was the quality and significance of collective action supported by SPAII?
2. To what extent did young people influence decisions, institutions, policies or public discourse?
3. What evidence exists of policy or systems-level influence?
4. What enabled or constrained meaningful youth participation?
5. Which collective action approaches should be continued or scaled?

**I. Adaptation in Protracted Crises**

1. How effectively did the programme adapt to changing political, economic, humanitarian and social conditions?
2. Which adaptations were most significant? Were adaptations timely and appropriate?
3. What enabled effective adaptation? What constrained adaptation?
4. Did adaptations maintain alignment with the programme's strategic objectives and ToC?
5. What does SPAII demonstrate about how programmes should be designed and managed in protracted crises?

**J. Sustainability**

1. What programme benefits are likely to continue after funding ends?
2. Which capacities, systems, relationships and practices are likely to be sustained?
3. To what extent have local partners been positioned to continue the work?
4. Are collective action and youth engagement mechanisms likely to continue?
5. What institutional or contextual risks threaten sustainability?
6. What should AAAR and partners do to strengthen sustainability?

**4. Evaluation Scope**

The evaluation will cover:

**Lebanon**: Tripoli, Jeb Jenine, Ba'albek

**Syria:** Northwest Syria, Latakia, Damascus

The evaluation should ensure adequate representation of different geographic and contextual settings rather than relying solely on the most accessible locations.

**Time period**

**2022–2026**

**Programme scope**

The evaluation will cover:

- Core SPAII interventions;
- all Top-Ups;
- all three Strategic Objectives including: humanitarian assistance; protection services; legal services; trainings and capacity strengthening; youth and safe spaces; livelihoods-related interventions; campaigns and collective action; advocacy and policy influence; partnership and localisation approaches; programme adaptation and learning.

**Partners**

**Lebanon**: SHIFT, Bassmeh & Zaitouneh RDFL

**Syria**: Violet, Bahar

**5. Evaluation Approach and Methodology**

The evaluation should use a mixed-methods, participatory and theory-based approach.

A purely indicator-based assessment will not be sufficient. The evaluation should combine quantitative evidence with qualitative investigation of contribution, change, adaptation and learning.

The evaluator is expected to propose a detailed methodology during inception. This should include, as appropriate:

**5.1 Document review**

The evaluation will include a review of key programme documentation, including the programme design and Theory of Change, logframes and IPTTs, monitoring and DQA data, partner and monitoring reports, assessments and previous evaluations, learning and advocacy documentation, Top-Up documentation, and relevant contextual and needs assessments.

**5.2 Quantitative analysis**

The evaluation will analyse available monitoring data to assess programme reach, participation, demographic and geographic coverage, achievement against targets, and trends across the implementation period and intervention types.

The evaluator should critically assess **data quality and limitations** and should not treat reported reach as equivalent to meaningful change.

**5.3 Qualitative research**

The evaluation will use qualitative methods to capture the perspectives of programme participants, young people and marginalised young women, communities, partners, volunteers, AAAR staff, technical teams, duty bearers, service providers, civil society and policy stakeholders.

Methods may include key informant interviews, focus group discussions, participatory reflection, outcome harvesting, contribution analysis and selected case studies, as appropriate.

**5.4 Theory of Change assessment**

The evaluator should conduct a dedicated assessment of the SPAII ToC, identifying:

**Inputs → Activities → Outputs → Outcomes → Strategic Objectives → Longer-term change**

while testing the assumptions and contextual conditions between each stage.

The evaluation should identify successful and unsuccessful pathways of change and explain why they occurred.

**5.5 Case studies**

The evaluator will develop a limited number of illustrative case studies highlighting significant examples of individual or community change, collective action, policy influence, technical leadership and guidance, adaptation to crisis, innovative or alternative solutions, and unintended change. Case studies should focus on the pathways and mechanisms of change, demonstrating how and why change occurred rather than simply describing activities or outputs.

**6. Partnership and Localisation**

The evaluation should assess the partnership model as an important determinant of programme performance.

Questions should include:

- Did partners have sufficient ownership and decision-making space?
- Was technical accompaniment appropriate?
- Did AAAR add value beyond financial support?
- How effective was knowledge transfer between AAAR and partners?
- Were roles and responsibilities clear?
- Did partnership arrangements support adaptation?
- How sustainable are capacities developed through the programme?
- What could AAAR do differently to strengthen locally led programming?

The evaluation should particularly examine the balance between partner autonomy and AAAR technical accompaniment, quality assurance and strategic support.

**7. Ethics and Safeguarding**

Given the sensitive nature of programming in Syria and Lebanon, the evaluation must adhere to ActionAid safeguarding requirements and ethical research principles, including informed consent, confidentiality, anonymity, data protection, do-no-harm and conflict-sensitive approaches, gender-sensitive research, and safe participation of young people. Appropriate referral procedures should be in place where sensitive protection concerns arise. The evaluation should minimise risks associated with discussing protection, legal assistance, displacement, conflict and other sensitive experiences. No personally identifiable information should be included in the final report unless explicitly authorised and ethically justified.

**8. Deliverables**

The selected evaluator/team will be expected to produce:

**I. Inception Report**

Including:

refined evaluation questions; evaluation matrix; detailed methodology; sampling strategy; data collection tools; analysis framework; ethical and safeguarding approach; workplan; limitations and mitigation measures.

**II. Data Collection Tools**

Including appropriate tools for:

KIIs; FGDs; participant consultations; partner consultations; policy stakeholder interviews; case studies; and other proposed methods.

**III. Preliminary Findings Presentation**

A presentation of emerging findings to AAAR and relevant partners for validation and reflection.

**IV. Draft Evaluation Report**

Including:

- executive summary;
- programme background;
- methodology;
- limitations;
- findings;
- conclusions;
- lessons learned;
- recommendations;
- annexes;
- and evidence supporting key findings.

**V. Final Evaluation Report**

Maximum recommended length: **40–50 pages excluding annexes**.

**VI. Learning Product**

A concise SPAII Learning Brief synthesising key lessons and practical recommendations, including what worked and what did not, why, what AAAR and partners should continue or do differently, and what should be adapted to strengthen future programming in protracted-crisis contexts.

**VII. Final Learning Workshop**

Facilitation of a participatory learning session with AAAR and relevant partners to validate findings, identify key lessons and priorities, translate findings into actionable recommendations, and discuss implications for future programming.

**9. Sampling**

The evaluator should propose a purposive sampling strategy that ensures representation across:

- Syria and Lebanon;
- geographic locations;
- partners;
- Strategic Objectives;
- intervention types;
- gender;
- age groups;
- marginalised groups;
- refugees and host communities where applicable;
- direct participants and wider stakeholders.

The evaluation should avoid relying exclusively on programme success stories or easily accessible participants.

**10. Key Evaluation Principles**

The evaluation should be:

**Independent** – providing an impartial assessment of programme performance.

**Utilisation-focused** – producing findings that can directly inform future decisions.

**Participatory** – ensuring meaningful engagement of partners and programme participants.

**Theory-based** – testing the programme's Theory of Change rather than simply measuring indicator achievement.

**Contribution-focused** – recognising that change in Syria and Lebanon cannot necessarily be attributed to SPAII alone.

**Context-sensitive** – recognising the complexity of protracted crises.

**Gender-responsive and youth-centred** – examining who benefited, who did not, and how power and inclusion influenced results.

**Learning-oriented** – identifying not only successes and failures but the reasons behind them.

**11. Key Expected Evaluation Outputs**

Ultimately, the evaluation should answer five practical questions for AAAR:

**A. Where did SPAII get it right?**

What approaches, interventions, partnerships and adaptations generated meaningful results?

**B. Where did SPAII have an opportunity to do better?**

What underperformed, and why?

**C. What actually contributed to change?**

Which pathways in the Theory of Change worked, for whom and under what conditions?

**D. What did SPAII learn about programming in protracted crises?**

How can AAAR become more adaptive, locally led and responsive?

**E. What should AAAR do differently next time?**

What should be continued, stopped, adapted, strengthened, scaled or tested differently?

**12. Timeline**

**Activity Timeline**

Inception phase Week 1

Data collection Week 2 to Week 6

Data analysis Week 7

Validation workshop Week 8

Draft final report Week 9

Final report and learning product Week 10

Final workshop Week 11

**13. Budget**

Maximum 16,230 JODs inclusive of 5% tax for Jordanians and 10% for non-Jordanians.

**14. Required Qualifications of the Consultant/Team**

- At least 7–10 years of experience in evaluation of multi-year development programmes
- Proven experience in youth-led programming, gender justice, climate resilience, and/or humanitarian programming
- Strong knowledge of Jordan context, refugee/host-community dynamics
- Demonstrated experience in designing exit strategies or sustainability assessments
- Strong MEL background, including OECD-DAC evaluations is preferrable
- Experience assessing advocacy and policy-influencing results
- Arabic and English fluency
- Experience working with grassroots organizations and youth structures

**15. Management & Coordination**

- The consultant will report to the AAAR PQMEAL Coordinator and SPA II Programme Manager.
- Local partners in Lebanon and Syria will facilitate, youth mobilization, and access to field sites.
- AAAR will provide project documentation, MEL data, and monitoring tools.

**16. Ethical Considerations**

The assessment must follow ActionAid’s safeguarding principles and ethical standards:

- Do-no-harm approach
- Informed consent, confidentiality, secure data handling
- Gender-sensitive and inclusive methodologies
- Special protection for youth under 18 and refugees

jobs.title: Job Counselor
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

Since 2017, IRC Hellas supports vulnerable youth refugee and host communities in Athens to access income generation through employment and self-employment services and skills-building activities, directly and in collaboration with partners. Building on this experience, IRC Hellas, with the support of UNHCR and in partnership with the Municipality of Thessaloniki, is implementing the Youth Empowerment and Self-Reliance project for the third year to promote socio-economic equal access for vulnerable youth in Thessaloniki.

To support with the implementation of the project, IRC Hellas is recruiting a Job Counselor, to be responsible for the day-to-day implementation of employability activities, including service mapping, stakeholder engagement, job counseling and Job Readiness Trainings.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Organize needs assessment and service mapping activities related to employability and skills development programming for youth;
- Participate in stakeholder engagement activities;
- Support the project implementation by designing, organizing and leading Job Readiness Trainings and information sessions for youth;
- Support the project implementation by providing individual employment support/job counseling for youth;
- Proactively working to identify issues related to clients’ participation and report them to the Project Manager.
- Ensuring relevant project data is accurately collected and updated on a weekly and monthly basis.
- Coordinate closely with the team to ensure effective implementation of the provided activities;
- Participate in regular team meetings;
