- Excellent academic qualifications, including Master's degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. development, humanitarian studies, international relations, research methods, social sciences).
- At least 2 years of experience in the humanitarian sector and/or field-based roles in fragile or development contexts.
- Experience with designing and implementing primary research, in particular large-scale quantitative surveys and/or humanitarian needs assessments. Experience in leading multi-sectoral assessments is an asset.
- Demonstrated experience designing and delivering training or capacity-building for adult professionals, including remote and online delivery considered a strong asset.
- Experience developing e-learning content (e.g. Didask, Moodle or comparable platforms) an asset.
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting.
- Strong interpersonal skills, including good external engagement and coordination skills, and the ability to build partnerships with regional and national actors.
- Familiarity with the humanitarian system and global humanitarian policy frameworks, in particular the Grand Bargain, the HPC and the JIAF.
- Willingness and ability for short term deployments, including to complex and challenging security environments.
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- Fluency in English and French required, given the regional remit of the position; Arabic, Spanish or Portuguese an asset.
- Prior experience leading the design or implementation of MSNAs an asset.
- Prior experience working in West and/or Central Africa an asset.
- Ability to operate InDesign, a strong plus.
- Ability to operate R, or a related statistical programming language, an asset.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 2’460 CHF and 2’520 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

jobs.title: Digital Prevention and Capacity Development Consultants
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**LOCATION: Home-based, with travel to Baghdad, Iraq, as required**

**NUMBER OF POSITIONS: 4–6 consultants across leadership, technical delivery and specialist roles**

**CONTRACT: Short-term consultancy with intermittent inputs, anticipated November 2026 to October 2027**

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Human Relief Foundation (HRF) is seeking experienced consultants to strengthen institutional capacity in preventing and countering violent extremism (PVE/CVE), with a focus on the digital environment. This is a single recruitment process for a Team Leader, a Technical Lead and 2–4 Specialist Consultants. HRF will assess applicants and match them to roles according to their qualifications and experience. Applicants are not expected to meet the requirements for every role or specialism.

The work combines learning-needs assessment, curriculum development, practical workshops, online learning and mentoring for institutional participants. Engagements are subject to funding and confirmation of the assignment. Responsibilities and reporting lines will depend on the role assigned.

Responsibilities will include:

- Assess learning needs and develop a capacity-development programme tailored to institutional roles and the Iraqi context.
- Develop or deliver practical training, exercises and reference materials within the consultant’s area of expertise.
- Support analysis of online radicalisation, extremist narratives and prevention approaches, using lawful and ethically appropriate methods.
- Coordinate with institutional counterparts and other consultants to ensure consistent, timely and high-quality delivery.
- Monitor learning progress and contribute to assessments, activity reports and documentation of results.
- Apply conflict sensitivity, Do No Harm, human-rights, privacy and data-protection principles. Use fictional, non-identifying scenarios in exercises.
- Participate in online meetings and travel to Baghdad where the agreed role requires in-person delivery, following applicable security procedures.

## PERSON SPECIFICATION

Applicants should meet the criteria for at least one of the roles described below. Relevant experience must be clearly evidenced in the CV with month and year dates, responsibilities and project examples. Strong written and spoken English at C1 level is required for all roles. Arabic language skills and relevant regional experience will also inform team composition.

## TEAM LEADER

Reporting to HRF Programme Management, the Team Leader will provide overall coordination, strategic oversight and quality assurance. Indicative input: up to 15 working days, including limited travel for coordination and review meetings.

**Role responsibilities**

- Oversee the Technical Lead and Specialist Consultants and coordinate communication with relevant partners.
- Quality-assure the learning-needs assessment, curriculum, training methodology, exercises, learning evidence and reports.
- Oversee workplans, milestones, risk management and reporting; lead key coordination and review meetings.

**Qualifications and experience**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in political or social sciences, peace and conflict studies, security studies, international relations, development studies or a related field.
- At least 7 years of experience in development cooperation, peacebuilding, stabilisation or closely related fields.
- At least 5 years of experience in PVE/CVE or related prevention activities.
- At least 5 years of management or leadership experience as a project team leader, project manager or in a comparable role.
- Demonstrated experience working with governmental or institutional counterparts in Iraq or the Middle East.

## TECHNICAL LEAD

Reporting to the Team Leader, the Technical Lead will manage technical design and delivery, coordinate Specialist Consultants and lead implementation with institutional counterparts. Indicative input: up to 60 working days, including repeated missions to Baghdad for preparation and workshop delivery.

**Role responsibilities**

- Lead the learning-needs assessment and translate findings into a tailored curriculum and practical capacity-development programme.
- Develop and oversee workshop materials, scenario-based exercises, mentoring and learning assessments.
- Coordinate technical contributions and institutional engagement; monitor participants’ progress and prepare reports and results data.

**Qualifications and experience**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in political or social sciences, peace and conflict studies, security studies, international relations, development studies or a related field.
- At least 7 years of experience in development cooperation, peacebuilding, stabilisation or closely related fields.
- At least 5 years of experience in PVE/CVE, online radicalisation or prevention policy, and at least 5 years in institutional capacity development or advisory services.
- Demonstrated experience managing and coordinating technical assignments or projects.
- Demonstrated experience working in Iraq or the Middle East, and experience with governmental or institutional counterparts in the Middle East or similar contexts.

## SPECIALIST CONSULTANTS

Reporting to the Technical Lead, 2–4 Specialist Consultants will support assessment, develop and deliver specialist sessions, facilitate exercises and contribute to materials and reports. Up to 100 working days will be shared across the pool; individual inputs and travel will depend on the expertise required.

**Qualifications and experience common to specialist roles**

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in political or social sciences, security studies, international relations, law, communications or media, information technology, data analysis or a field relevant to the proposed specialism.
- At least 7 years of professional experience relevant to the proposed area of expertise, and at least 5 years in capacity development, training or advisory services.

**Specialist areas**

Applicants should demonstrate one or more of the following areas. The selected pool will cover all five collectively; individual applicants do not need to cover every area.

- PVE/CVE and online radicalisation: at least 7 years in PVE/CVE, online radicalisation, extremist narratives, recruitment or mobilisation dynamics.
- Digital monitoring and analysis: at least 5 years in open-source research or intelligence (OSINT), platform-aware monitoring, digital content analysis, or narrative, trend or network analysis.
- Strategic communication and prevention: at least 5 years in strategic communication, prevention-oriented narratives, audience analysis or coordinated prevention approaches relevant to PVE.
- Legal, human-rights and ethical considerations: at least 5 years in legal, human-rights, privacy, digital-governance or ethical issues relevant to digital monitoring and prevention.
- Training design and adult learning: at least 3 years in scenario-based learning, adult learning or practical training design.

Arabic proficiency at B2 level or above and at least 3 years of relevant professional experience in Iraq or the Middle East are strongly preferred. The pool will include at least two consultants meeting each of these criteria. Candidates combining several specialisms are welcome.

jobs.title: Senior Research Monitoring Evaluation and Learning Officer
jobs.body:
**Role Summary**

Siren is seeking a Senior Research, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer to join a dynamic, multi-disciplinary team to help us bring together evidence from across our work, identify connections and emerging insights, and communicate the wider story.

This role will connect information across project activity, identify patterns, tensions and emerging questions, and turn complex findings into clear, credible and compelling narratives for a wide range of audiences.

The successful candidate will be an excellent researcher and writer with a strong understanding of the Lebanese socio-economic and political context. They will combine analytical rigour with curiosity and judgment, helping teams, partners and decision makers understand not only what is happening, but why it matters and what to do next.

Siren already runs a robust MEL system, and we are looking for the right person to join our team and help us draw even greater value from the evidence we generate. This is not primarily a role for designing or administering a MEL system. The priority is to connect and interpret evidence across our work, identify the bigger picture, and communicate with clarity and purpose.

Want to learn more about us? Check our digital brochure: [https://materials.sirenassociates.com/brochure](https://materials.sirenassociates.com/brochure)

**Key Responsibilities**

**Insight, synthesis and learning**

- Bring together quantitative and qualitative evidence from across projects to identify cross-cutting patterns, relationships, gaps and implications.
- Interpret findings in light of Lebanon's political, institutional, social and economic context.
- Contribute to regular sense-making and learning processes that help teams test assumptions, reflect on unexpected findings and adapt their work.
- Frame forward-looking questions and practical recommendations for programmes, leadership and partners.

**Research and evidence**

- Contribute to rigorous, proportionate research using qualitative, quantitative and mixed methods.
- Develop research questions, methodologies, sampling approaches and analytical frameworks suited to the decision at hand.
- Undertake data collection, analysis and synthesis, ensuring quality, ethics, inclusion and responsible data use.
- Assess the strength and limitations of evidence, triangulate across sources.

**Communication and evidence storytelling**

- Produce excellent written outputs in clear, precise English, including research reports, project narrative reports, policy briefs, learning products, articles, presentations and public-facing content.
- Translate technical findings into accessible stories tailored to audiences ranging from the general public to Lebanese institutions, international governments and development partners.
- Use data visualisation and narrative structure thoughtfully to translate evidence.Work with technical and programme colleagues to ensure that external communications are accurate, useful and grounded in evidence.  
    Present findings confidently and facilitate discussion with senior and non-technical audiences.

**RMEL quality and collaboration**

- Support credible evaluation and learning approaches, including theories of change and contribution analysis, while remaining attentive to non-linear change and unintended outcomes.
- Support the strengthening of an organisation-wide culture of inquiry and learning.
- Manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work when contexts, information and timelines shift.

## **Requirements**

**Essential**

- At least five years of relevant professional experience in research, evaluation, learning, policy analysis, applied social research or a closely related field. A relevant university degree or equivalent combination of professional experience and training.
- Strong understanding of the concepts and theories that underpin monitoring and evaluation practice.
- Demonstrated ability to synthesise varied and sometimes incomplete evidence, make connections across datasets and contexts, and generate useful insights.
- Strong qualitative and quantitative research skills, including research design, data collection, analysis, triangulation and critical appraisal of evidence.
- Excellent English writing and editing skills, with a portfolio of clear, engaging outputs for different audiences.
- Ability to communicate data through compelling narrative, well-chosen visualisation and concise presentation.
- Strong contextual understanding of Lebanon, including its institutions, political economy and social dynamics. Candidates do not need to be Lebanese.
- Experience working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and a range of senior, technical and community stakeholders.
- High integrity, sound judgment and discretion, particularly when handling sensitive evidence or relationships.

**Desirable**

- Professional proficiency in Arabic.
- Knowledge of security sector reform, security sector governance or public sector reform.
- Experience working with government institutions, civil society, donors or international partners.
- Experience with data visualisation, statistical analysis or qualitative analysis tools.
- A postgraduate qualification in social research, public policy, political science, development studies, evaluation or a related discipline.

**How we work**

Our approach is agile and multidisciplinary. We look for colleagues who act with integrity, stay curious and work cooperatively across disciplines. The Senior RMEL Officer will be comfortable making progress amid complexity: adapting as evidence changes and maintaining high standards when priorities or conditions shift. They will be intellectually confident and open to challenge, ready to test assumptions and attentive to perspectives that complicate the expected story.

**What success looks like**

- Teams and decision makers can see the larger story across projects, articulated in various reporting formats (contractual project reports, research pieces, communications products, data visualisation)
- Evidence reaches the right audience in a form they can understand and use.
- Learning leads to sharper questions, better decisions and timely adaptation.

## **Benefits**
