jobs.title: Request for Proposal Production Partner - Digital Micro Drama Series October 2026 India
jobs.body:
**Request for Proposal**

**Production Partner - Digital Micro Drama Series**

**October 2026**

**India**

## **Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title Production Partner for a Digital Micro Drama Series

Supplier Type Production house or lead production agency

Base Scope 25 episodes of 60–90 seconds, one original song and music video, and defined promotional assets

Optional Scope Series Adaptations into up to three regional languages

Primary Language Conversational Hindi with appropriate regional nuances

Delivery Period Approximately three months from Contract

Location India; agency preferably based in Delhi or Mumbai

Clarification Deadline 11 October 2026

Proposal Deadline 19 October 2026

Submission Email suppliers@girleffect.org

Proposal Validity 90 days

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology that girls want, trust and need. We use youth-centred storytelling, behaviour-change science and digital engagement to help adolescent girls make informed choices about their health, education, relationships and futures.

In India, our initiatives include Chhaa Jaa and Teeka Talk. These programmes provide trusted information and support on health, relationships, empowerment and HPV vaccination through social media, digital content, chatbots and community engagement.

## **Background and Objective**

Girl Effect India seeks an experienced production partner to develop and produce a compelling digital-first micro drama series for Instagram, YouTube and other short-form platforms.

The series will follow interconnected adolescent girls and the family members, friends, peers, boys and community members who influence their lives. It will use relatable family-drama storytelling to entertain audiences and promote positive role modelling, agency, empathy and informed decision-making.

The story will integrate themes including:

- Girl empowerment;
- Menstruation;
- Nutrition;
- Mental health;
- Gender-based violence; and
- HPV immunisation as a central theme.

These messages must be woven naturally into engaging stories rather than delivered as direct instruction. The production must be youth-friendly, gender-inclusive, body- and sex-positive, trauma-informed, rights-based and culturally credible.

## **Required Outputs**

**Output Included Base Quantity Requirement**

Micro-drama episodes 25-30 Each episode will be 60–90 seconds, serialised, digital- first and supplied in approved platform formats.

Optional additional episodes Up to 5 Separately priced per episode and produced only following written authorisation.

Original song and music video 1 each Original composition, production, master and agreed promotional cutdowns, with all rights cleared.

Series trailer 1 Up to 60 seconds, including an agreed vertical version.

Promos 3 Short-form campaign promos in agreed aspect ratios.

Cast interviews 5–6 Edited short-form interviews with approved cast members.

Behind-the-scenes and shoulder content Minimum 10 clips Edited clips suitable for episodic amplification.

Episode thumbnails and still Thumbnail sets and a curated

stills package for all episodes Editable templates and final exports.

Regional-language versions Up to 3 languages Optional and separately priced by language and episode or as a full-series package.

The quantities above constitute the base scope. Any additional output must be approved through the change-control process before production begins.

## **What You will do**

The selected production partner will be responsible for the end-to-end development and production of the series, including but not limited to:

- Concept & Story Development: Develop the overarching concept, story universe, and narrative arc for across all episodes of the micro-drama series featuring multiple adolescent girl protagonists and an interconnected universe of characters.
- Character & Story Arcs: Develop detailed character profiles and individual arcs, ensuring each girl’s and character's journey explores relatable adolescent experiences while contributing to the larger narrative.
- Scriptwriting: Develop episode-wise scripts that organically integrate key themes and messages around girl empowerment, menstruation, nutrition, mental health, gender-based violence, and a strong focus on HPV immunisation.
- Creative Development: Translate programme objectives and key messages into engaging, emotionally resonant, culturally relevant stories with strong role modelling and positive behavioural shifts.
- Digital-First Storytelling: Ensure episodes are structured, paced, and formatted for 1–1.5-minute short-form consumption, with strong hooks, narrative continuity, and platform-appropriate storytelling.
- Pre-Production: Casting of actors, location scouting, costume and production design, scheduling, shot planning, and all other pre-production requirements.
- Production: End-to-end filming of all episodes in conversational Hindi, incorporating appropriate regional and cultural nuances to ensure authenticity and relatability.
- Post-Production: Editing, sound design, music, colour grading, subtitles/captions, graphics, and final mastering of all episodes for digital distribution.
- Series Identity & Packaging: Develop the visual identity, title treatment, opening/closing elements, thumbnails, and other creative assets required for multi-platform release.
- OST & Music Video: Conceptualise, compose, produce, and deliver an original song/OST and accompanying music video that captures the spirit of the series and can be used across marketing and promotional campaigns.
- Language Adaptations: Support adaptations/dubbing/subtitling in up to three additional regional languages, as required and quoted separately.
- Final Deliverables: Provide all final episodes, scripts, character/story bibles, episode breakdowns, promotional assets, OST/music video, and relevant production/master files in agreed formats.
- Promotion Plan - A suggestive plan to amplify the series with an on-ground and digital component

## **Technical and Delivery Standards**

The agency must:

- Capture and master content at a minimum resolution of 4K unless Girl Effect approves otherwise.
- Frame footage safely for all agreed platform aspect ratios.
- Deliver files using the codecs, audio standards, naming conventions and folder structure agreed at inception.
- Ensure that dialogue, sound, music, colour, subtitles, captions and graphics meet professional digital-broadcast standards.
- Check all names, logos, health information, translations and on-screen text for accuracy.
- Use only properly licensed footage, music, fonts, graphics, photographs and other third-party materials.
- Retain project settings and original-quality production files throughout post-production.
- Securely store and maintain recoverable copies of production files until Girl Effect confirms final handover and acceptance.

No generative-AI material may be used without Girl Effect’s prior written approval. Any proposed AI use must be disclosed and must not compromise intellectual property, consent, privacy, safeguarding or authenticity.

## **Approvals, Revisions and Change Control**

The following provisions will apply:

- Corrections required because an output does not meet the approved brief, script, technical specification or quality standard will not count as creative revisions and must be completed at no additional cost.
- Reshoots or rework resulting from agency error, poor technical quality, missing coverage, continuity failures, rights failures or unauthorised deviations will be undertaken at the agency’s cost.
- Changes requested by Girl Effect that materially alter an already approved quantity, output, duration, language, cast, location, schedule or specification may be treated as additional scope.
- Before starting additional work, the agency must submit a written change request describing the reason, deliverables, cost, schedule and impact on the existing work.
- No additional fee, expense or deadline extension will be valid without written approval through an authorised change order or contract amendment.
- General discussions, meetings or emails with project team members do not authorise additional expenditure unless approved by Girl Effect’s authorised contract representative.
- The agency must continue delivering the unaffected parts of the approved scope while a proposed change is being reviewed.

## **Deliverables**

- Development
    - Creative vision and promotional strategy document
    - Series concept, overarching storyline, characterisation and narrative universe
    - Detailed episode-wise narrative breakdowns
    - Development plans, timelines, and production processes
    - Regular progress reports and production meetings
- Pre-Production
    - Finalised scripts for all episodes and promotional content
    - Storyboards
    - Cast/talent contracts, release forms, usage rights, and due diligence documentation
    - Pre-production plan for CTAs, social content, cast interviews, and other promotional assets
- Production
    - Pre-production deck and plan
    - End-to-end shoot of all episodes and agreed promotional assets
    - Original OST/song and accompanying music video
    - Relevant permission and licensing documents \[rights to rest with Gift Effect\]
- Post-Production
    - Episodic master files - release ready
    - Series visual identity, packaging, and promotional assets
    - Comprehensive promotional package including Teasers, Promos, BTS, Cast interviews \[5-6\]
    - Final OST/music video and associated assets
    - Weekly production status reports
- Final Handover
    - Final master files, clean files, open files, raw footage of all episodes, music video and promotional assets on Google Drive as well as physical HDD.
    - Complete rights, releases, licenses, and usage documentation
- Hosting & Amplification
    - Cast-led videos for amplification of episodes across their social media handles, with usage and promotional rights.
    - Episode-level BTS, cast bytes, shoulder content, teaser and other promotional content for audience engagement and amplification with usage and promotional rights.
    - Weekly performance reports covering reach, impressions, views, likes, shares, saves, comments, and reposts for all episodes and promotional content.

## **Who You Are**

We are looking for production houses that have fulfilled either all or at least two of the following criteria:

- Have extensive knowledge of creating PAN India serialised content at scale with a regional flavor while maintaining authenticity and relatability.
- Developed fictional content for the development sector, but with a youth-friendly content focussed approach.
- Worked with brands targeting younger audiences
- A portfolio of award-winning fictional storytelling work on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and WhatsApp will be a plus.
- Capacity to work on tight timelines.

**Skills and expertise:**

- You are based in India, preferably in Delhi or Mumbai, and have worked on fictional content with regional nuances.
- Fluency in English, conversational Hindi and Hinglish.
- Experience in creating health-related /behavior change content production in the field of gender based tech violence, mental health, health and immunization, sexual and reproductive health and rights and economic empowerment would be a massive bonus.
- Strong understanding of local trends, media landscape, and cultural nuances to tailor creative solutions that resonate with the target audience in the Indian market.
- Proficiency in creative and strategic thinking, project/time/budget management.
- Proficiency in creating content and branding for diverse platforms such as digital, social media, and emerging media channels, leveraging each platform's unique features to engage the target audiences.
- Experienced with the latest creative production tools and technologies, including design software, video editing tools, and content management systems, to ensure efficient and high-quality output.
- Basic safeguarding and digital safeguarding knowledge are a plus.
- Most importantly, we need you to ensure that you have a lens that is youth-friendly & fun, body and sex-positive, gender inclusive, trauma-informed and adopts a rights-based approach towards girls and young women.

## **Expected Commitment**

- The project is expected to have a duration of 3 months.

## **Location**

The Agency must be based in Delhi or Mumbai and have extensive experience in the country.

## **Management**

- The consultant will have a primary point of contact within our India Create team.
- The language of the materials and reports shall be English.
- The contract supervisor shall approve all deliverables submitted before any payment is made.

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: 8th October 2026
- Questions/Clarification Deadline: 11th October 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: 19th October 2026

## **Proposal submissions**

Your Technical Proposal, should you be interested (Max 10 pages), should cover the following in the form of a deck.

- Your approach - Your understanding of the requirement, outlining your approach and vision for the series.
- Portfolio - Please showcase previous work that you consider to be relevant. This can be related to our brand or similar brands, similar target audience, with the government, etc. Please share clickable links of published or completed works.
- The proposed production methodology.
- A creative vision and indicative story approach.
- A brief scan of relevant public-health, behaviour-change or commercial short-form content.
- Team capabilities - Describe the team size, their qualifications, experience, and capabilities in providing the requested services.
- Reference - Provide contact information of at least three references for similar contracts serviced in the past, with a description of the service provided and the contract periods of performance.
- A detailed schedule showing approval stages, script batches, shoot days, post-production workflow and delivery dates.
- The agency’s approach to quality control, safeguarding, rights management, health and safety, data security, risk and contingency planning.
- Information on additional Services – Please provide any information on additional services that you believe would be pertinent and align with the project

**Financial Proposal**

The financial proposal must be submitted in Indian Rupees and include:

- A fixed, all-inclusive base price for:
    - 25 episodes;
    - One original song;
    - One music video;
    - The defined promotional package; and
    - Final handover of all required files and rights documentation.
- Detailed costs for:
    - Creative development and scripting;
    - Key personnel;
    - Cast and contributors;
    - Shoot days;
    - Equipment;
    - Studios and locations;
    - Production design, props and wardrobe;
    - Travel, accommodation, catering and transport;
    - Insurance and permits;
    - Editing and post-production;
    - Music production;
    - Graphics, titles, subtitles and captions;
    - Data storage and backup; and
    - The physical hard drive.
- A separate unit price for each of the five optional episodes.
- Separate prices for regional-language dubbing, voice-over and/or subtitling, including translation, talent, studio, quality assurance and revised masters.
- Applicable taxes, licences, talent renewals, pass-through costs and reimbursable expenses shown separately.

Any cost not expressly excluded or separately priced will be treated as included in the agency’s fixed base price.

## **Evaluation Criteria**

Proposals will be evaluated in the following order:

- Mandatory pre-screening;
- Technical evaluation; and
- Financial evaluation.

The criteria against which proposals will be evaluated are listed below:

**Technical Evaluation**

- Interpretation and understanding of this TOR, and a Creative Scan of similar content formats existing for public health /social behaviour change/ commercial health products (not necessarily their own production) - \[10%\]
- Your vision and approach based on the shared brief - \[10 %\]
- Methodology, workplan, scope control and delivery capacity \[10 %\]
- Proposed team, cultural capability and technical resources \[5 %\]
- Safeguarding, rights, quality assurance and risk management \[10 %\]
- Portfolio of past works - \[10%\]
- Company profile and organizational capacity \[10%\]
- Evidence of a minimum of three contactable references - \[5%\]

Financial Evaluation

- Value for money/proposed budget breakdown - 30%

Girl Effect may request clarifications, creative presentations, interviews, reference checks, due diligence or best-and-final offers.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

Technical and Financial proposals will need to be submitted as separate documents. Financial bids will not be opened until the technical evaluation, and then only for those proposals deemed qualified and responsive.

In their Technical proposal, the bidder must demonstrate an understanding of the requirements described in the TOR and demonstrate how the bidder will meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria.

Please note that Girl Effect is not liable for any costs incurred during the award/contract preparation, submission, or negotiation of the award/contract. All submitted documentation and/or materials shall become and remain the property of Girl Effect.

## **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting and Payment:** The successful agency will sign Girl Effect’s standard agreement. Payments will be linked to satisfactory delivery and written acceptance of agreed milestones. The agency may not exceed the approved budget or commit Girl Effect to third-party costs.
- **Fixed Price and Taxes:** The base price must remain firm for the approved scope and proposal-validity period. Taxes, optional services, licences, talent renewals and approved pass-through costs must be itemised separately. Girl Effect will deduct or account for taxes as required by Indian law.
- **No Unapproved Costs:** No additional fee, expense, pass-through cost or commitment will be payable unless approved in writing by Girl Effect’s authorised contract representative before the cost is incurred.
- **Rights and Ownership:** Subject to the final agreement and payment, Girl Effect will own the commissioned materials and approved outputs. The agency must secure and document all contributor, talent, location, music, archive and third-party rights required for the agreed territories, media, term, editing, adaptation, promotion and paid-media use.
- **Talent and Contributor Rights**: Talent agreements must clearly address filming, editing, dubbing, subtitling, still-image extraction, social media, radio,broadcast, digital advertising, promotional use, territory, duration and any renewal costs. Restrictions and expiry dates must be disclosed before contracting.
- **Safeguarding and Consent:** The agency must protect the dignity, privacy and safety of all contributors. Anyone under 18 must be engaged through approved safeguarding procedures, legally valid parent or guardian consent and the young person’s assent. Sensitive topics must be handled using trauma-informed and do-no-harm practices.
- **Confidentiality and Data Protection**: The agency must protect scripts, unreleased content, personal information and other confidential materials and use secure transfer and storage methods.
- **Insurance and Compliance**: The agency is responsible for applicable permits, employment and labour obligations, production insurance, equipment insurance, public-liability cover and compliance with health, safety and other applicable laws.
- **Personnel and Subcontracting**: Material subcontractors and changes to key personnel require prior written approval. The lead agency remains responsible for all subcontracted work.
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Bidders must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest.
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes proposals from agencies with diverse professional, creative and cultural backgrounds and a strong understanding of the communities and audiences we serve.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may clarify, negotiate, amend or cancel the process, reject any or all proposals, award all or part of the requirement or make no award. Girl Effect is not liable for proposal-preparation or negotiation costs.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: Expression of Interest: Procurement of a Loans Management System for a Rural Based Informal MFI
jobs.body:
**Organization:** World Vision Somalia (SomReP)

**Project:** SERECA

**Donor Funded:** ANCP

**Position Type:** Contract

**Location:** Remote & in Somalia/Land (Dollow and Elefyne)

**Estimated working days:** 60 days

**Estimated number of staff required to work on the project:** 1-5

**Reporting to:** Economic Development and Market System Development Advisor - SomReP

**Starting Date:** Oct 2026

**Background**

The Somalia Resilience Programme (SomReP) is a consortium of seven international non-governmental organizations (INGO) and one Local NGO. SomReP works to enhance the resilience of chronically vulnerable households, communities and systems across Somalia.

The Somalia Resilience Program (SomReP) is an ambitious approach to tackle the challenge of recurrent droughts and the chronic vulnerability among pastoralists, agro-pastoralists, and peri-urban households in one of the poorest countries in the world. SomReP is being implemented through a consortium of 7 INGOs (ACF, ADRA, CARE, COOPI, DRC, Oxfam and WVI) and 1 Local NGO (Shaqodoon)

Through Somalia Enhanced Resilience through Inclusive Economic/Market Systems development and Climate Smart Approaches (SERECA), SomReP would like to engage a qualified and dynamic consultant to support development Loans Management System for a rural based informal MFI

District bank committee (DBC) is a rural-based informal microfinance model committed to providing affordable financial services to underserved communities in Dollow and Elefyne. To improve efficiency, transparency, and client service, SOMREP seeks to acquire a robust Loans Management System (LMS) for the DBC that support its operations.

**Objective**

To procure and implement a secure, scalable, and user-friendly LMS that automates the loan lifecycle from application to repayment while integrating with mobile money platforms and supporting offline field operations.

**Scope of Work**

The selected vendor will be required to:

- Develop, supply, install, and configure the LMS.
- Migrate existing loan and client data.
- Integrate with **Mobile money platforms** and other relevant payment channels.
- Enable offline data capture for field officers with automatic sync.
- Provide role-based access control and audit trails.
- Generate customizable reports (portfolio, arrears, compliance, etc.).
- Train staff and provide user manuals.
- Offer ongoing technical support and system updates.
- Complete systems handover, but maintain technical support

**Key Features Required**

- Loan Origination & Approval Workflow in line with credit policies
- Client Management & KYC Compliance in line with the regulation
- Automated Repayment Scheduling & Alerts
- Portfolio at Risk (PAR) Tracking 0-30 days/normal, 30-90 days/watch, 91-180days/Substandard, 181-360days doubtful, above 36 days/loss
- Portfolio automated reporting
- Multi-branch & Multi-currency Support
- Data Security & Backup Mechanisms

**Deliverables**

- Fully functional LMS meeting agreed specifications.
- Data migration report.
- Training completion report.
- System documentation and user manuals.
- Post-implementation support plan.
- Train credit officers and DBC credit committee on the use of the LMS.
- Validation of the installed system by stakeholders

**Timeline**

The project is expected to be completed within **60 days** from contract signing.

**Reporting and Communication**

The consultant will report to the Economic development and Market systems advisor and other SOMREP implementing partners. The consultant is expected to update advisor on a regular basis and submit progress reports according to an agreed schedule. Any issues, delays, or obstacles should be communicated promptly to ensure timely resolution.

**Vendor Qualifications**

- 10 years proven experience in implementing LMS for microfinance/Sacco’s in rural contexts.
- Masters degree in related Management information systems development like Computer science, Software engineering, IT and related area
- Demonstrated capacity for mobile money integration.
- Strong after-sales support.

**Proposal Submission & Evaluation Criteria**

The Selection of the firm will be made based on cumulative analysis (i.e., mandatory requirement and technical qualifications as follows

**Mandatory requirements**

- Copy of business registration (company/organization) s.
- Copy of the tax registration
- Successful bidder will be required to sign World Vision Supplier Code of Conduct form

**Technical Evaluation**

Applicants need to clearly articulate on the following, but not limited to:

**Criteria and Scoring (Total Score = 100%)**

1. **CVs and experience** - 10 years proven experience in implementing LMS for microfinance/Sacco’s in rural contexts. Master’s degree in related Management information systems development like Computer science, Software engineering, IT and related area. Demonstrated capacity for mobile money integration. Strong after-sales support. - (score - 20%).
2. **Systems Technical compliance** - System security, reliability and trustworthiness for the developed systems. This also involves adhering to relevant laws, regulations, standards and guidelines relevant to the industry, including all compliance like certifications etc. - (score - 20%)
3. **Clear work plan including time frames the consulting firm will undertake to finalize the assignment as per the scope of work** - (score - 15%).
4. **Consulting firm profile/cover letter** (Not exceeding two pages) - (score -15%).
5. **Up to two-page statement of capability (referencing the selection criteria) and the approach to be take in undertaking this assignment as per the scope of work, including relevant experience and at least 2 samples of similar work done.** - (score - 20%).
6. **Support and training plan** - (score - 10%).

**More Details to be provided in the full ToR upon Expression of Interest.**

**We hereby invite Expression of Interest from registered, approved and reputable consultants to provide above-named services to World Vision Somalia.**

jobs.title: Programme Development and Quality Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Overall purpose of the role**

The Program Development and Quality Coordinator (PDQC) is responsible for the coordination and management of key program processes, particularly in proposal development and grants management and reporting, ensuring timely reporting to donors, ensuring communication tools and strategies are in place. The PDQC contributes to increased quality by ensuring program coherence, adherence to program standards and appropriate learning from lessons learnt across the country program. The Coordinator is also responsible for donor compliance, application of correct procedures and guidelines, and liaison with support and partnership teams in support of grants processes.

**Responsibilities**

***Grants Support***

- Be responsible for the delivery of quality narrative reports, reflecting the progress and status of projects, in a transparent, timely and professional manner
- Contribute to addressing all comments and issues on proposals or reports, liaising with relevant Managers and finance to ensure coherence between financial and narrative reports;
- Ensure the DRC grants management system is regularly and fully updated. Includes Dynamics ERP system (creating grants, uploading documents, managing instalment tracking and billing rules, updating checklists and tasks assigned); internal funding tracker and reporting deadlines communications;
- Support grant relationships and communications with donors to ensure correct, compliant and smooth flow of information;
- Support the maintenance of simple grant tracking tools, such as reporting calendars, compliance trackers and MoV trackers.
- Support with communication and visibility tools and items as per donor and internal guidelines including their dissemination and availability to DRC teams and donors.
- Support / facilitate Go/No Go, Kick Off and grants closing meetings
- Help follow up on donor requirements, reporting deadlines and outstanding documentation.
- Support programme teams with questions around donor rules, budget flexibility and required approvals.
- Contribute to preparations for donor visits, TPMs, spot checks or other reviews.
- Support Grants & Business Development Manager in managing fundraising strategy, donor engagement plan, donor mapping by conducting research, maintaining and updating engagement plan and donor database.

***Program Development and Quality***

- Work closely with the Head of Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (HDP), PDQS, and Programme Manager to transform content and conceptual designs into competitive final proposals responsive to the donor guidelines.
- Coordinate and provide oversight to all aspects of the proposal development process from the development of a writing guide, proposal calendar, through to delivery and timely submission of proposals.
- Review proposals for consistency with the requirements of solicitations, requests or calls for proposals, predicting or preventing bottlenecks in the proposal development process and securing the necessary information to complete process.
- Ensure the proposal development and project implementation process takes into consideration the mainstreaming of CHS, global cross cutting themes such as Age, Gender and Diversity, AAP, and lessons learnt from previous programming
- Help track donor visibility requirements and planned communication outputs.
- Support the collection of case studies, success stories, photos and related consent/documentation.
- Ensure that the Technical teams and Managers provide input into reports and proactively communicate planned requirements of program design and implementation to the relevant area and country office functions.
- Ensure an appropriate level of technical assistance and capacity building is provided to DRC’s implementing partners.
- Support the Operations Manager in monitoring of project technical goals, objectives and policies. Link DRC’s MEAL processes with HDP IM processes to establish clear ways of working and project implementation monitoring and ensure project data and indicator tracking are aligned with reporting requirements.
- Assess opportunities to improve program quality through alignment with DRC’s Programme Quality Framework
- Support regular internal reviews of project progress and outstanding actions.

***Program Support***

- Collaborate with the HDP tech team to ensure field-based implementation processes and documentation are properly managed and compliant with DRC requirements and sector best practices.
- When necessary, support HDP team in developing comprehensive procurement plans. Upon receipt of project related goods and services, collaborate with the logistics and procurement teams in quality assurance. From time to time, support or facilitate tendering processes, procurement committee meetings and in the review of bid analyses.
- Ensure development of work plans and budgets for DRC projects. Ensure that appropriate management systems are followed and that the programs make progress towards objectives.
- Capacitate field teams to manage timely and quality completion of program deliverables and reports in accordance with donor guidelines.
- Support the development of project work plans and contribute to development of performance monitoring plans.
- Provide support to project technical managers in the interpretation of donor guidelines in the implementation of project activities.

***Partnerships***

- Support the development of partnerships such as implementing partner identification and mapping, due diligence, support with selection, relationship management, capacity building and any closure processes.
- Support partners with reporting requirements, documentation standards and donor compliance where needed.
- Review partner narrative and technical inputs and provide feedback before consolidation.
- Contribute to follow-up on partner agreements, scopes of work and related documentation

**Qualifications, experience and technical competencies**

- Bachelor's degree in communications, political science, international development, law or other relevant discipline
- Minimum 5 years of UN/INGO experience in proposal writing, including conceptualizing and technical writing under strict deadlines with demonstrated success
- Excellent project management skills
- Recognized leadership role in program development and quality
- Ability to work rapidly with staff in the field directly, and remotely in writing and where necessary revising concepts, proposals and reports.
- Capacity to work in a multi-sector team, including coordinating technical input into proposals
- Familiarity with requirements of key humanitarian donors and capacity to work in a multi-donor environment, including EU/ECHO, FCDO, UN donors among others.
- Good humanitarian and development programming skills, including capacity to prepare logical, coherent and consistent documents including log frames.
- Communication skills: excellent written and articulate oral communication skills, particularly in English.

**Languages:**

- Excellent written and spoken English.

**About you**

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:*

- *Striving for excellence:* You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- *Collaborating:* You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- *Taking the lead:* You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- *Communicating:* You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- *Demonstrating integrity*: Upholding and promoting the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Conditions**

*Contract:* Six Months’ contract with possibility of extension, subject to funding and performance. Salary and conditions in accordance with the Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for International staff. This position is graded at Band NM.G

*Start Date:* November

*Duty Station:* Omdurman

Reports to: Head of HDP

jobs.title: Expression of Interest: Annual Audit of Project/Programme Support Including ISRS 4400 - Revised (Annex D)
jobs.body:
**Introduction**

The World Vision Deutschland e.V., hereafter referred to as the “Cooperation partner” wishes to engage the services of an audit firm for the purpose of auditing the Somali Resilience Program (SomReP) phase 3: Inclusive livelihoods for vulnerable pastoral groups, as stipulated in the agreement between the Cooperation partner and Sida. The audit shall be carried out in accordance with international audit standards (ISA) issued by IAASB. In addition, an assignment according to International Standards on Related Services (ISRS) 4400 (Revised) shall be carried out. The audit and the additional assignment shall be carried out by an external, independent and qualified auditor.

**I. Objectives and scope of the audit**

The objective is to audit the financial report for the periods 2025-09-01 to

2026-08-31 as submitted to Sida and to express an audit opinion according to ISA, applying ISA 800/ISA 805, on whether the financial report of SomReP phase 3: Inclusive livelihoods for vulnerable pastoral groups is in accordance with the Cooperation partner´s accounting records and Sida’s requirements for financial reporting as stipulated in the agreement including appendices between Sida and Cooperation partner (Agreement).

**II. Additional assignment; according to agreed upon procedures ISRS 4400 (Revised), review the following areas in accordance with the Terms of Reference below**

Mandatory procedures that must be included:

1. Observe whether the financial report is structured in a way that allows for direct comparison with the latest approved budget.
2. Observe and inspect whether the financial report provides information regarding:
    
    a. Financial outcome per budget line (both incomes and costs) for the reporting period and columns for cumulative information regarding earlier periods under current agreement.
    
    b. When applicable, compare if the opening fund balance for the reporting period matches with what was stated as closing fund balance in the previous reporting period.
    
    c. A disclosure of exchange gains/losses. Inquire and confirm whether the disclosure includes the entire chain of currency exchange from Sida’s disbursement to the handling of the project/programme within the organisation in local currency/ies, if applicable.
    
    d. Explanatory notes (such as, for instance, accounting principles applied for the financial report).
    
    e. Amount of funds that has been forwarded to implementing partners, when applicable.
3. a) Inquire and inspect with what frequency salary costs during the reporting period are debited to the project/programme.

 *Choose a sample of six individuals for five different months and*:

 b) Inquire and inspect whether there are supporting documentation4 for debited salary costs.

 c) Inquire and inspect whether actual time worked is documented and verified by a manager. Inquire and inspect within which frequency reconciliations between debited time and actual worked time is performed.

 d) Inspect whether the Cooperation partner comply with applicable tax legislation with regard to personal income taxes (PAYE) and social security fees.

 4. Review and confirm that the Cooperation partner screens IP’s and/or suppliers to ensure that such parties are not subject to the European Union’s financial sanctions list of persons, groups and organisations (EU Sanctions list).

 Enquire whether there has been any reported findings from the screening process and if so, report on such findings.

 5 a) Inspect and confirm that the unspent fund balance (according to the financial report) at the end of the financial year is in line with information provided in the accounting system and/or bank account.

 **b) Applicable the final year:** Inspect and confirm the unspent fund balance (including exchange gains) in the financial report and confirm the amount that shall be repaid to Sida.

 **Follow up of funds that are channelled to implementing partners**

 Mandatory assignments that must be included if the Cooperation partner forward funds to implementing partners (IP’s):

 Choose a sample of a minimum of 50 % of the total of disbursed funds as well as 50 % of the number of IP’s or a maximum of 10 IP’s.

 6. Inspect and confirm whether the Cooperation partner has signed agreements with the selected IP’s.

 7. Inspect and confirm whether the Cooperation partner, in all agreements entered with IP’s, included the requirement to carry out annual audits. The requirement shall specify that these audits shall be carried out with application of ISA (reporting according to ISA 800/805) and a separate assignment according to ISRS 4400 (Revised) should be included for project/programme support. If agreements regarding core support are entered into with IP’s, the audit shall be conducted in accordance with ISA 700 or National standards on auditing.

 8. Inquire and inspect whether the Cooperation partner has received financial reports and auditor reports from all IP’s included in the selected sample:

1. Inquire and inspect whether the Cooperation partner has verified if reports from IP’s are in line with the requirements in the Agreement.
2. Inquire and inspect whether the Cooperation partner has documented its assessment of the submitted financial reports and reporting from auditors including management responses and action plans from selected IP’s.
3. Inquire and inspect whether the Cooperation partner has documented its follow-up actions based on the information provided in the financial reports and the reporting from the auditor of the selected IP’s.
4. Inquire and inspect whether the Cooperation partner has reported substantial observations from selected IP’s audit reports in its communication with Sida. List observations from IP’s audit reports which have been part of this sample.

**Additional procedures to be included**:

• **Follow-up from Efficiency Audit**:

Inquire and inspect whether the Cooperation Partner has implemented the recommendations from Efficiency Audit separately conducted. The follow-up includes inspecting whether the Cooperation Partner has implemented the action plan as described in Cooperation Partner’s management response submitted to Sida.

**III. The reporting**

The reporting shall be signed by the responsible auditor (not just the audit firm8) and shall include the title of the responsible auditor.

*Reporting from the ISA assignment*

The reporting from the auditor shall include an independent auditor’s report in accordance with the format in standard ISA 800/805 and the auditor’s opinion shall be clearly stated. The financial report that has been the subject of the audit shall be attached to the audit report.

The reporting shall also include a Management letter that discloses all audit findings, as well as weaknesses identified during the audit process. The auditor shall make recommendations to address the identified findings and weaknesses. The recommendations shall be presented in priority order and with a risk classification.

Measures taken by the Cooperation partner to address weaknesses identified in previous audits shall also be presented in the Management Letter. If the previous audit did not have any findings or weaknesses to be followed-up on, a clarification of this must be disclosed in the audit reporting.

If the auditor assesses that no findings or weaknesses have been identified during the audit that would result in a Management Letter, an explanation of this assessment must be disclosed in the audit reporting.

*Reporting from the ISRS 4400 (Revised) assignment*

The additional assignment according to agreed upon procedures ISRS 4400

(Revised) under section II, shall be reported separately in an “Agreed-upon procedures report”.

Performed procedures should be described and the findings should be reported in accordance with the requirements in the International Standard on Related Services 4400 (Revised).

When applicable, the sample size shall be stated in the report.

**Evaluation criteria For Annual Audit of Project/Programme Support including ISRS 4400**

**Introduction**

The audit report shall be carried out in accordance with conditions set out in article 8 or the Grant Agreement and Sida's standard Terms of Reference for annual financial audit, (Annex D).

The audit shall be carried out by an external, independent and qualified auditor. The audit shall be conducted in accordance with international audit standards issued by International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The signing auditor shall not be contracted for the assignment for more than a 7-year period.

Sida reserves the right to approve the Cooperation Partner's selection of the auditor and may require that the auditor shall be replaced if Sida finds that the auditor has not performed satisfactorily or if there is any doubt to the auditor's independence or professional standards.

**Application Process and Requirements**

 **Proposal Evaluation Criteria**

**1.0: Mandatory Requirements**

- Provide a certified copy of business registration(company/organization)
- Provide a certified copy of tax registration
- Successful bidder will be required to sign World Vision Supplier Code of Conduct form

 **2.0: Technical Evaluation**

 **2.1 Qualifications**

The consultant must have proven expertise and experience in Auditing with special focus. Proof of this is to be provided by submitting, together with the application:

- An overview of relevant works
- Contact details for references
- The proposed team's CVs

**2.2 Requirements in detail:**

- **Professional Certifications and Licensing** - Must have a valid professional registration certifying eligibility to practice as an external auditor and express audit opinions pursuant to the laws, rules and other requirements of the country.
- **Experience and Expertise**:
- Must be professionally competent with a minimum of seven years’ experience in planning and conducting audits of this nature
- Previous working experience in Somalia/Somaliland and/or similar challenging operating environments.
- Experience in similar SIDA assignments or other multilateral donors.
- **Staffing and Capacity**:

The core team must be fully qualified professionals with over seven years’ experience in planning and conducting audits of this nature, **three** of which must have been in Somalia or similar fragile contexts

- **References and Client Testimonials**: At least 3 References including names and contact information (similar assignments in a similar context)

 Must be an independent firm free from conflict of interest with World Vision Somalia/Somaliland

 **2.3 Proposal Contents**

*Proposals from Consultants should include the following information (at a minimum)*

- Technical Proposal with clear methodology on how to conduct the audit
- CVs of key consultant(s) attached to the technical proposal
- Proposed timeline/Work plan
- At least 3 References including names and contact information (similar assignments in a similar context)

 **Technical Evaluation Criteria**

- Professional Certifications and Licensing - E.g., ICPAK
- Experience and Expertise
- Knowledge of Applicable Standards as per TOR
- Audit Approach and Methodology
- Reporting and Communication
- Compliance and Ethical Standards-National standards or Global standards
- Technology and Security-Security of our Data
- References and Client Testimonials

**Weighted Technical Evaluation – 100 Points**

1\. Understanding of the Audit Assignment / TOR - 10%  
2\. Relevant Audit Experience: More than five years of relevant audit experience, including demonstrated experience working in fragile and complex operating contexts - 20%  
3\. Audit Methodology and Approach - 20%  
4\. Team Composition and Qualifications: For the Partner, please attach the relevant qualification certificates, as well as the CVs of the Partner and all proposed team members - 15%  
5\. Demonstration of Quality Assurance, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Measures - 10%  
6\. Detailed workplans and realistic timelines & Deliverables - 10%  
7\. Knowledge of Donor / NGO / Development-Sector Requirements - 5%  
8\. References / Past Performance please attach - 5%  
9 Technology, Data Security and Confidentiality - 5%

**More Details to be provided in the full ToR upon Expression of Interest.**

**We hereby invite Expression of Interest from registered, approved and reputable consultants to provide above-named services to World Vision Somalia.**

jobs.title: Account Manager
jobs.body:
Overview of position

The Account Manager is responsible for the overall management and delivery of services to clients, ensuring CTG’s operations align with client requirements, contractual obligations, and financial goals. This role oversees the end-to-end management of assigned projects, including client engagement, scope management, compliance, and team supervision. As the primary point of contact for clients, the Account Manager is accountable for resolving issues and ensuring that recruitment, onboarding, payroll, consultant contract issuance, and reporting processes are executed efficiently and within agreed timelines. They balance client expectations with CTG’s operational and financial interests.

Role objectives

**Project Management**

- Lead initial client engagements, clearly articulating CTG’s services and project scope as per contract terms and conditions.
- Ensure alignment between the scope of work, client expectations, and CTG’s service delivery, proactively managing and agreeing on any adjustments.
- Act as the focal point for clients, maintaining strong relationships and addressing concerns promptly to ensure satisfaction and smooth project execution.
- Take ownership of issue resolution, ensuring timely and effective solutions related to service delivery, consultant performance, or client concerns.
- Monitor financial performance, ensuring proper management of costs, revenue, and resource allocation to maintain project profitability.
- Ensure the timely and accurate delivery of monthly reports to clients, covering key metrics such as headcount, payroll, DSA amounts, consultant activities, and financial status.
- Contribute to financial forecasting and planning for ongoing and future projects.

**Operations, Legal, and Compliance Management**

- Oversee recruitment, onboarding, payroll, and contract issuance processes for CTG consultants, ensuring efficiency and compliance with CTG policies and legal frameworks.
- Ensure all operations related to the project comply with CTG policies, local labor laws, and client requirements, including adherence to deadlines, quality standards, and financial controls.
- Support the timely and compliant onboarding of international consultants per contractual requirements.
- Ensure the accurate and timely issuance of consultant contracts, ensuring compliance with CTG policies, local labor laws, and client agreements.
- Provide regular operational and financial updates to internal stakeholders, including the Country Operations Manager and Regional Director, regarding the status of client accounts, project delivery, and financial performance.
- Proactively implement measures to prevent mismanagement of resources, client expectations, or deliverable
- Ensure strict compliance with CTG’s operational policies to mitigate legal and financial risks
- Obtain necessary approvals for any deviations from CTG’s standard operating procedures to prevent legal or financial repercussions.
- Notify in-country management of any client-recommended deviations from CTG’s processes.
- Report any fraudulent activities or irregularities to in-country management immediately.
- Maintain professional and official communication channels to avoid disputes with clients.
- Uphold CTG’s ethical standards, ensuring all interpersonal interactions remain professional, culturally sensitive, and aligned with CTG’s core values.
- Foster a respectful and inclusive work environment that acknowledges diverse cultural values and beliefs.
- Promote CTG’s values in all aspects of team operations and client interactions.

**Client Relationship and Communication**

- Serve as the primary liaison for clients, maintaining long-term relationships and addressing any concerns or issues that arise.
- Ensure clear and transparent communication with clients to build trust and maintain satisfaction.
- Take ownership of any challenges that arise in client relationships, whether related to service delivery or internal operations, and ensure appropriate solutions are implemented swiftly.
- Ensure that client expectations are met without compromising operational efficiency or profitability.

**Business Development Support**

- Support the establishment and growth of CTG's presence in Afghanistan by building and maintaining relationships with clients, partners, government counterparts, and other key stakeholders.
- Monitor the humanitarian and development landscape, identifying upcoming opportunities, market trends, and potential areas for CTG engagement, and share relevant intelligence with Country Management and the Business Development team.
- Contribute to business development efforts by providing local market knowledge, operational insights, staffing plans, and technical inputs for proposals, concept notes, and client presentations.
- Represent CTG at client meetings, coordination forums, and networking events to strengthen the organisation's visibility and develop strategic relationships.
- Support the mobilisation and operational planning of newly awarded projects, ensuring a smooth transition from business development to implementation.
- Work closely with Country Management and the Business Development team to support the successful establishment and expansion of CTG's operations in Afghanistan.

Project reporting

This position reports to Regional Operations Manager

Key competencies

- Outstanding people management skills and very familiar with delegation, performance management, and providing feedback and guidance to team members.
- Strong communication, problem-solving skills.
- Financial acumen, ideally with experience managing budgets and financial reporting.
- Proficiency in HR systems and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
- Strong attention to detail, especially in managing contracts, consultant data, and reporting.
- Proactive and results oriented.
- Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

Team management

This role does not have team management responsibilities.

Further information

Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Coordonnateur·Trice de Projet
jobs.body:
**COORDONNATEUR·TRICE DE PROJET- RCEAM BÉNIN**

**RÉSUMÉ**

Sous la supervision du/de la Représentant(e) Pays et en étroite collaboration avec l’équipe programme de Catalyste+, le/la Coordonnateur·trice de Projet sera responsable de **coordonner et de soutenir la mise en œuvre efficace du projet** ***Renforcement des capacités d’exportation et de l’accès aux marchés des petites et moyennes entreprises (PME) béninoises (RCEAM-Bénin).***

Le/la Coordonnateur·trice assurera la planification, la coordination, le suivi de la mise en œuvre des activités du projet, en collaboration avec notre partenaire local, la Chambre de Commerce et d’Industrie du Bénin (CCI Bénin), les PME bénéficiaires, le/la conseiller.ère Catalyste+ et l'équipe projet de Catalyste+. Il/elle veillera au respect du plan de travail, des échéanciers, de la qualité des livrables, des objectifs du projet, et assurera la coordination des aspects opérationnels et logistiques nécessaires à la réalisation des activités.

Le/la Coordonnateur·trice sera également responsable du **suivi des résultats et de l’impact du projet**, notamment de la collecte, de la validation et de l’analyse des données relatives aux activités et aux indicateurs de performance. Il/elle contribuera à la documentation des résultats, des bonnes pratiques et des leçons apprises, ainsi qu’à la préparation des rapports d'activités et financiers destinés à Catalyste+ et aux bailleurs de fonds.

Le/la Coordonnateur·trice travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les différentes parties prenantes afin de **garantir la bonne mise en œuvre des activités et de contribuer à l’atteinte des résultats du projet**, dans le respect des politiques, procédures et normes de Catalyste+.

**Lieu d’affectation**

Le/la Coordonnateur·trice de Projet doit être basé(e) à **Cotonou, au Bénin,** et être disponible pour assurer une présence régulière auprès de la CCI Bénin et des autres parties prenantes du projet.

**Durée du contrat**

Il s’agit d’un contrat à durée déterminée jusqu’au 31 mars 2027.

**RESPONSABILITÉS PRINCIPALES**

**Gestion et coordination de la mise en œuvre du projet**

- Coordonner la planification, l’organisation et la mise en œuvre des activités du projet en collaboration avec la CCI Bénin, l'équipe projet et les autres partenaires concernés.
- Assurer le suivi du plan de travail et des échéanciers du projet, et identifier rapidement tout retard, risque, enjeu ou écart par rapport aux objectifs établis, en proposant des mesures correctives au besoin.
- Coordonner les aspects opérationnels et logistiques liés aux formations, ateliers, missions du/de la conseiller.ère et autres activités prévues dans le cadre du projet.
- Assurer la liaison et la coordination avec la CCI Bénin, les PME bénéficiaires, le/la conseiller.ère de Catalyste+, l'équipe projet et les autres parties prenantes du projet.
- Coordonner la préparation et le suivi des réunions de projet, avec les partenaires, l'équipe projet et le bailleur de fonds au besoin.
- Suivre l’avancement global de la mise en œuvre du projet et assurer la circulation de l’information pertinente entre les différentes parties prenantes.
- Contribuer à la préparation des rapports d'activités et financiers destinés à Catalyste+ et aux bailleurs de fonds.
- Participer au suivi administratif et financier du projet, notamment en contribuant au suivi des dépenses, à la planification budgétaire et à l’identification des écarts nécessitant une attention de la direction.

**Suivi des résultats, collecte et gestion des données**

- Assurer la collecte et la compilation des données nécessaires au suivi des activités et des résultats du projet.
- En collaboration avec l’équipe du projet, valider les méthodes et outils de collecte des données.
- Veiller à ce que les données collectées soient complètes, fiables et alignées avec les indicateurs et cibles établis dans le cadre du suivi et de l’évaluation.
- Suivre régulièrement les progrès du projet par rapport aux résultats et indicateurs prévus et signaler tout écart ou enjeu nécessitant un ajustement.
- Assurer le suivi de la qualité des résultats auprès des 30 membres du personnel de la CCI Bénin, des 10 formateurs et des 50 PME bénéficiaires.
- Contribuer à la préparation des données et informations requises pour les rapports de suivi et de performance du projet.

**Communications, visibilité et apprentissage**

- Contribuer à la mise en œuvre du plan de communication et de visibilité du projet, en collaboration avec l’équipe de Catalyste+ et les partenaires.
- Identifier et documenter les résultats, histoires de succès, témoignages et autres contenus pouvant être valorisés dans les communications du projet.
- Coordonner les activités de communication et de visibilité du projet, notamment la liaison avec les médias locaux, la couverture médiatique et la diffusion des résultats à travers les réseaux sociaux et les canaux des partenaires.
- Veiller au respect des exigences de visibilité de Catalyste+ et des bailleurs de fonds.

**Administration, conformité et soutien au projet**

- Veiller à la confidentialité et à la protection des données, conformément aux politiques et procédures de Catalyste+.
- Veiller au respect des procédures administratives, financières et opérationnelles applicables au projet.
- Appuyer la préparation et le suivi des documents administratifs et financiers nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des activités.
- Effectuer toute autre tâche pertinente confiée par la direction afin de soutenir la bonne mise en œuvre et l’atteinte des résultats du projet.

**CONNAISSANCES, COMPÉTENCES ET EXPÉRIENCE REQUISES**

**Formation et expérience**

- Diplôme universitaire en administration des affaires, gestion de projet, développement international, économie, commerce international, gestion des entreprises ou dans une discipline connexe, et/ou au moins trois (3) ans d’expérience pertinente dans un poste de coordination de projet ou dans un rôle similaire.
- Expérience démontrée en coordination et mise en œuvre de projets, idéalement dans le domaine du développement international, du développement du secteur privé, du développement des PME, du commerce ou du renforcement institutionnel.
- Expérience de travail avec des entreprises, associations professionnelles, chambres de commerce, institutions publiques, organismes de développement ou partenaires internationaux constitue un atout important.
- Expérience dans la coordination de formations, ateliers, missions, activités de renforcement des capacités ou autres activités impliquant plusieurs parties prenantes.

**Connaissances techniques**

- Bonne compréhension des enjeux liés au développement international, notamment le développement du secteur privé, les chaînes de valeur, le commerce, la gouvernance, l’environnement et les changements climatiques, ainsi que l’égalité des genres et l’autonomisation économique des femmes (EG/AEF).
- Bonne compréhension des principes de gestion axée sur les résultats (RBM), notamment la définition et le suivi des indicateurs, la collecte et la validation des données, la documentation des résultats et l’identification des écarts par rapport aux cibles.
- Connaissance des principes de suivi-évaluation et de gestion de données appliqués aux projets de développement.
- Connaissance des principes de gestion budgétaire, de suivi des dépenses, de conformité administrative et de reddition de comptes constitue un atout.

**Compétences en gestion de projet et de suivi des résultats et gestion des données**

- Excellentes capacités de planification, coordination et organisation permettant de gérer plusieurs activités et échéanciers simultanément.
- Capacité à assurer un suivi rigoureux des livrables et à veiller à leur qualité et à leur conformité aux attentes du projet.
- Capacité à anticiper les besoins opérationnels et logistiques et à résoudre rapidement les problèmes rencontrés lors de la mise en œuvre.
- Capacité à collecter, compiler, vérifier, analyser et présenter des données liées aux activités et aux résultats du projet.
- Capacité à suivre les progrès d’un projet par rapport aux résultats, indicateurs et cibles établis.
- Capacité à documenter les résultats, bonnes pratiques, leçons apprises, histoires de succès et changements observés auprès des PME bénéficiaires.

**Communication, relations avec les parties prenantes et visibilité**

- Excellentes aptitudes interpersonnelles et relationnelles, avec la capacité de travailler efficacement avec des interlocuteurs de différents niveaux et de différents milieux professionnels.
- Excellentes capacités de communication orale et écrite, notamment pour préparer des rapports, comptes rendus, présentations, notes de suivi et autres documents professionnels.
- Excellente capacité à établir et maintenir des relations de travail constructives avec les partenaires locaux et internationaux.
- Sensibilité culturelle et capacité à traiter des questions délicates avec tact, diplomatie et discernement.
- Bonne compréhension des principes de communication et de visibilité liés aux projets de développement international.
- Capacité à coordonner des activités de communication avec les partenaires, médias et autres intervenants.
- Bonne compréhension des principes de visibilité et de reconnaissance des bailleurs de fonds.

**Utilisation d’outils et langue**

- Capacité à utiliser les réseaux sociaux et les outils numériques pour contribuer à la diffusion des résultats du projet constitue un atout.
- Excellente maîtrise de Microsoft Office, notamment Word, Excel, PowerPoint et Outlook.
- Excellente maîtrise du français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit.

**Date limite de candidature : 10.22.2026**

jobs.title: Appel à propositions pour la mise en œuvre d’une enquête de couverture dénommée « PECS », après les activités de routinisation de la supplémentation e
jobs.body:
Guidée par l'héritage remarquable de sa cofondatrice, Helen Keller, Helen Keller Intl s'associe à des communautés qui s'efforcent de surmonter les cycles de pauvreté de longue date. En fournissant les éléments essentiels d'une bonne santé, d'une bonne nutrition et d'une vision claire, nous aidons des millions de personnes à créer un changement durable dans leur propre vie. Travaillant dans plus de 20 pays – à travers l'Afrique, l'Asie, l'Europe et les États-Unis – et avec une communauté mondiale de sympathisants, nous veillons à ce que chaque personne ait la possibilité – comme Helen l'a fait – d'atteindre son véritable potentiel.

Helen Keller Intl soutient la supplémentation en vitamine A de 40 millions d'enfants chaque année dans 14 pays d'Afrique subsaharienne. Lorsqu'elle est administrée deux fois par an à au moins 80% des enfants âgés de 6 à 59 mois dans les pays où la mortalité des enfants de moins de cinq ans est élevée et où les taux de carence en vitamine A sont élevés, la supplémentation en vitamine A peut contribuer à réduire la mortalité infantile jusqu'à 24%.

A Madagascar, Helen Keller Intl appuie techniquement et financièrement le Ministère de la Santé Publique pour la prestation de Supplémentation en Vitamine A (SVA) dans 08 régions à savoir Menabe, Ihorombe, Betsiboka, Boeny, Sofia, Melaky, DIANA et SAVA par le biais de l’activité de routine.

Afin d'évaluer le nombre d'enfants touchés par ces distributions en mode routine, Helen Keller Intl mène des enquêtes transversales auprès des ménages en suivant la méthodologie développée par l'OMS pour mesurer la couverture de la SVA.

Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d'un cabinet de consultance pour accompagner les équipes de Helen Keller Intl dans le pays afin de mener une enquête de couverture prévue en janvier 2027 et qui évaluera la couverture du second semestre de 2026. Elle concernera une strate qui sera composée des huit (08) régions soutenues par Helen Keller International, dont la liste est la suivante : DIANA, SAVA, SOFIA, BOENY, BETSIBOKA, MELAKY, IHOROMBE, MENABE

Le cabinet sera responsable de la préparation de l'enquête, y compris l'adaptation des protocoles et des outils, la soumission des protocoles et des outils au comité d'éthique, le recrutement et la formation des enquêteurs ainsi que la supervision de la collecte de données sur le terrain, l'analyse des données et la production de rapports.

jobs.title: Consultant(e) national(e) pour l'étude de faisabilité et conception d’une plateforme numérique intelligente
jobs.body:
L'Organisation Internationale pour les Migrations (OIM) basée à Djibouti, recrute un(e) consultant(e) national(e) pour la réalisation d’une étude de faisabilité et la conception fonctionnelle et technique d’un poste frontière standard et d’une plateforme numérique intelligente et interopérable de facilitation du commerce sur le corridor Djibouti–Éthiopie « Smart Trade Border Platform »

## **I. Contexte et justification**

La Zone de Libre Echange Continentale Africaine (ZLECAf) constitue une opportunité stratégique pour renforcer l’intégration économique africaine, stimuler le commerce intra-africain et faciliter la mobilité des personnes, conformément à l’Agenda 2063 de l’Union africaine. Dans cette dynamique, le corridor Djibouti–Éthiopie joue un rôle essentiel dans les échanges commerciaux et l’intégration régionale.

Toutefois, son fonctionnement demeure limité par l’insuffisance des infrastructures numériques, la faible interopérabilité des systèmes, la coordination insuffisante entre les acteurs frontaliers et l’inadaptation des mécanismes d’échange de données. Ces contraintes affectent la fluidité, la sécurité et l’efficacité des opérations transfrontalières.

Dans ce contexte, l’OIM prévoit de recruter un consultant chargé de réaliser une étude de faisabilité et de contribuer à la conception d’une plateforme numérique intelligente et interopérable de facilitation du commerce frontalier le long du corridor Djibouti–Éthiopie. La consultance définira les besoins techniques, opérationnels et institutionnels, les exigences fonctionnelles de la solution et une approche réaliste pour son déploiement progressif, tout en favorisant la modernisation numérique et le renforcement institutionnel.

## **II. Objectif général de la consultance**

La consultance a pour objectif de produire, pour le volet djiboutien, une étude de faisabilité assortie d’une conception fonctionnelle et technique et d’une feuille de route budgétisée pour la mise en place d’un poste-frontière standard et d’une plateforme numérique interopérable sur le corridor Djibouti–Éthiopie « Smart Trade Border Platform ».

## **III. Objectifs spécifiques**

De manière spécifique, la consultance vise à :

- Cadre juridique et institutionnel : Analyser les politiques, stratégies, cadres juridiques, normes techniques et initiatives existantes en matière de gestion des frontières, de facilitation du commerce, de transformation numérique, d’identité légale et de protection des données, tout en examinant les mandats, responsabilités et mécanismes de coordination des institutions concernées.
- Processus et parties prenantes : Cartographier les institutions publiques, les opérateurs privés et les autres parties prenantes intervenant dans la gestion des frontières et le fonctionnement du corridor Djibouti–Éthiopie, documenter les procédures de traitement des personnes, des marchandises, des véhicules, des documents et des informations, et identifier les difficultés opérationnelles, les chevauchements institutionnels, les contrôles répétitifs et les ruptures dans la circulation de l’information.
- Infrastructures et systèmes existants : Évaluer les infrastructures numériques, les équipements informatiques, les réseaux de communication, les solutions d’alimentation électrique et les systèmes d’information utilisés par les institutions concernées, en portant une attention particulière aux insuffisances liées à leur interopérabilité et à leur capacité à assurer la continuité des services.
- Besoins et conception de la solution : Évaluer les besoins des autorités frontalières, douanières, commerciales, portuaires, sécuritaires, migratoires et chargées de l’identité, ainsi que ceux des utilisateurs de la frontière, notamment les commerçants, les transporteurs, les migrants, les femmes, les jeunes et les communautés frontalières. Sur cette base, définir les exigences fonctionnelles, techniques, institutionnelles et sécuritaires de la plateforme numérique intelligente et interopérable, et proposer des options d’architecture, d’hébergement, de gouvernance, de maintenance et de continuité des services.
- Feuille de route, capacités et validation : Identifier les équipements informatiques et numériques prioritaires ainsi que les besoins de formation et d’assistance technique des institutions concernées. Formuler une feuille de route budgétisée pour la conception et la construction d’un poste frontière ainsi que pour le développement, le pilotage, la maintenance et l’éventuelle mise à l’échelle de la plateforme. Contribuer enfin à la mission d’évaluation et à la validation des solutions proposées avec les parties prenantes des sites sélectionnés.

## **IV. Résultats attendus**

À l’issue de la consultance, les résultats suivants sont attendus :

- Cadre juridique et institutionnel : Un diagnostic des politiques, stratégies, cadres juridiques, normes techniques et initiatives existantes en matière de gestion des frontières, de facilitation du commerce, de transformation numérique, d’identité légale, de cybersécurité et de protection des données est établi. Les mandats institutionnels, les responsabilités et les mécanismes de coordination et de gouvernance applicables sont analysés et documentés.
- Processus et parties prenantes : Une cartographie complète des institutions et des parties prenantes est produite, comprenant leurs mandats, rôles, interactions, systèmes utilisés, besoins d’échange de données et mécanismes de coordination. Les procédures de traitement des personnes, des marchandises, des véhicules, des documents et des informations sont documentées, tandis que les contraintes opérationnelles, les chevauchements institutionnels, les contrôles répétitifs et les ruptures dans la circulation de l’information sont identifiés.
- Infrastructures et systèmes existants : L’état des lieux des infrastructures numériques, des équipements informatiques, des réseaux de communication, des solutions d’alimentation électrique et des systèmes d’information des sites sélectionnés est établi. Les lacunes techniques, les insuffisances d’interopérabilité et les risques affectant la disponibilité et la continuité des services sont recensés.
- Besoins et conception de la solution : Les besoins des institutions concernées et des utilisateurs du corridor, notamment les commerçants, les transporteurs, les migrants, les femmes, les jeunes et les communautés frontalières, sont évalués de manière participative. Les exigences fonctionnelles, techniques, institutionnelles, sécuritaires et de gouvernance de l’infrastructure frontalière et de la « Smart Trade Border Platform » sont définies. Des options d’architecture, d’interopérabilité, d’hébergement, de maintenance et de continuité des services sont proposées dans une conception fonctionnelle et technique provisoire.
- Feuille de route, capacités et validation : Les équipements informatiques et numériques prioritaires, accompagnés de leurs spécifications techniques, ainsi que les besoins de formation et d’assistance technique sont identifiés. Une feuille de route budgétisée est élaborée pour la conception et la construction d’un poste-frontière ainsi que pour le développement, le pilotage, la maintenance et l’éventuelle mise à l’échelle de la plateforme. Les conclusions, la solution proposée et l’étude de faisabilité sont examinées et validées avec les parties prenantes, puis intégrées dans le rapport final et le rapport de mission.

## **V. Description des activités attendues**

**Activité 1** : Réaliser le cadrage de la mission, la revue documentaire et le développement des outils de collecte de données.

**Activité 2** : Cartographier les parties prenantes publiques et privées et analyser les mécanismes de coordination et de gouvernance existants.

**Activité 3** : Évaluer les processus frontaliers, les flux opérationnels et l’état des infrastructures et équipements existants.

**Activité 4** : Consulter les utilisateurs du corridor afin d’identifier leurs besoins, contraintes et priorités en matière de services frontaliers.

**Activité 5** : Définir les exigences fonctionnelles, techniques et de gouvernance de l’infrastructure frontalière et de la plateforme numérique intelligente et interopérable de facilitation du commerce frontalier du corridor Djibouti–Éthiopie « Smart Trade Border Platform ».

**Activité 6** : Élaborer la conception technique de la solution et une feuille de route détaillée pour son déploiement progressif.

**Activité 7** : Identifier les équipements prioritaires et préparer les spécifications techniques

**Activité 8** : Valider les résultats avec les parties prenantes et finaliser l’étude de faisabilité ainsi que l’ensemble des livrables du projet.

## **VI. Méthodologie**

La consultance adoptera une approche participative, multisectorielle et centrée sur les utilisateurs, intégrant les droits humains, le genre, l’interopérabilité et des solutions durables fondées sur des données probantes.

La méthodologie combinera revue documentaire, consultations, entretiens, groupes de discussion, visites de terrain, analyses techniques et ateliers de validation, avec des outils de collecte préalablement approuvés par l’OIM et les parties prenantes.

## **VII. Livrables attendus et calendrier prévisionnel**

Cette consultance, d’une durée de 30 jour ouvrable, sera mise en œuvre à travers quatre livrables successifs couvrant le cadrage méthodologique, le diagnostic national, la conception fonctionnelle et technique de la solution, ainsi que la finalisation de l’étude de faisabilité et de la feuille de route. Les paiements seront effectués par tranches après validation des livrables par l’OIM, selon la répartition suivante : 10 % (Livrable 1), 40 % (Livrable 2), 40 % (Livrable 3) et 10 % (Livrable 4).
