## **VIII. Parties prenantes et bénéficiaires de la consultation**

Les principales parties prenantes incluront les institutions gouvernementales chargées de la gestion des frontières, du commerce, des douanes, des transports, de la logistique, de la santé et de la sécurité, ainsi que les acteurs du secteur privé et les opérateurs économiques intervenant le long du corridor Djibouti-Éthiopie. Les bénéficiaires directs et indirects comprendront les institutions nationales, les opérateurs économiques, les migrants, voyageurs, femmes et jeunes commerçants transfrontaliers, ainsi que les communautés, entreprises et investisseurs dont les moyens de subsistance dépendent du bon fonctionnement du corridor.

## **IX. Rôles et responsabilités**

Les partenaires nationaux et l’OIM vérifieront la qualité des livrables et les valideront avant de procéder au paiement. L’OIM sera responsable des aspects logistiques pour l’organisation des missions d’évaluations.

## **X. Qualifications techniques et fonctionnelles requises**

Le/La Consultant(e) national(e) devra répondre aux critères suivants :

- **Expérience professionnelle** : Au moins 7 ans d’expérience dans les domaines de la gouvernance migratoire, de la gestion intégrée des frontières, du commerce transfrontalier, de la transformation numérique ou des systèmes d’information.
- **Expertise technique** : Expérience avérée dans les études de faisabilité, les évaluations techniques, la digitalisation des systèmes, la cartographie des processus, l’analyse des besoins et l’élaboration de spécifications fonctionnelles et techniques.
- **Connaissances sectorielles** : Bonne maîtrise des enjeux liés à la gouvernance migratoire, à la gestion des frontières, à la facilitation des échanges, à l’interopérabilité des systèmes, à la protection des données et du contexte institutionnel et logistique de Djibouti.
- **Compétences analytiques et opérationnelles** : Expérience dans la collecte et l’analyse de données, la facilitation de consultations multipartites, la rédaction de rapports techniques et le travail avec les administrations publiques, les organisations internationales ou les projets financés par des partenaires.
- **Qualités professionnelles et linguistiques** : Excellentes capacités de communication en français et en anglais, aptitude au travail sur le terrain et en équipe, intégrité professionnelle, sensibilité culturelle, discrétion et respect des valeurs et normes de l’OIM et des Nations Unies.

## **XI. Dossier de soumission**

Le dossier de candidature devra comprendre :

a. Une lettre de motivation précisant la disponibilité du candidat ;

b. Un curriculum vitae actualisé indiquant clairement les qualifications et les expériences pertinentes ;

c. Proposition technique de trois à cinq pages comprenant la compréhension de la mission, la méthodologie proposée, les étapes de mise en œuvre, ainsi que les mécanismes de contrôle qualité et de gestion des risques.

d. Un plan de travail et un calendrier indicatif pour l’achèvement des travaux ;

e. Une proposition financière distincte et détaillée, exprimée en dollars des États-Unis, incluant les honoraires ;

f. Les coordonnées d’au moins trois références professionnelles ;

g. Des exemples ou liens vers au moins deux travaux similaires réalisés par le candidat ;

h. Une copie du diplôme universitaire le plus élevé et des certifications pertinentes ;

i. Tout document administratif exigé par l’appel à candidatures.

*Seuls les candidatures sélectionnés seront contactés.*

jobs.title: Venezuela: Asistente de Protección – Respuesta a la Emergencia (Caracas)
jobs.body:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

**Contexto de la Emergencia: El Terremoto del 24 de junio**

El 24 de junio de 2026, el centro-norte de Venezuela fue sacudido por dos potentes terremotos de magnitudes 7.2 y 7.5, con epicentros cercanos a Morón y Yumare. El impacto ha sido devastador: al 2 de julio de 2026, se confirmaron 2.595 fallecidos y 12.400 heridos. El Gobierno nacional declaró el Estado de Emergencia Nacional, designando a La Guaira como zona de desastre debido a la severa destrucción de infraestructura. En Caracas, los colapsos estructurales han dejado a miles de personas desplazadas, con aproximadamente 12.800 personas ubicadas en 80 albergues temporales.

La emergencia ha exacerbado críticamente los riesgos de protección. Se ha identificado una alarmante incidencia de separación familiar y la presencia de niños, niñas y adolescentes (NNA) no acompañados o separados, quienes carecen de un sistema unificado de seguimiento. Asimismo, el colapso de los servicios básicos y el hacinamiento en albergues han incrementado la vulnerabilidad ante la Violencia Basada en Género (VBG), la explotación y el abuso sexual. El sistema médico-legal en La Guaira está saturado, lo que dificulta la gestión digna de cadáveres y el restablecimiento del contacto con familiares de personas desaparecidas.

Será el/la encargado(a) de:

**Propósito del cargo**

El/La Asistente de Protección apoyará la implementación operativa, logística y administrativa de las actividades de Protección, Género e Inclusión (PGI) en el marco de la respuesta al terremoto liderada por la Cruz Roja Venezolana. Su labor estará orientada a apoyar la gestión de los Centros DAPS, las actividades de Restablecimiento del Contacto Familiar (RCF/RFL), la identificación y derivación segura de personas con necesidades específicas de protección, la distribución de kits de dignidad, las campañas comunitarias de sensibilización y los mecanismos de rendición de cuentas y participación comunitaria. El cargo trabajará bajo la supervisión directa del Oficial de Protección.

**Funciones y responsabilidades**

**Apoyo a la implementación programática**

- Apoyar la instalación, organización y funcionamiento de los Centros DAPS fijos y móviles desplegados en la respuesta al terremoto.
- Brindar apoyo operativo durante actividades de protección, espacios seguros, jornadas informativas y actividades comunitarias desarrolladas en campamentos temporales, alojamientos temporales y comunidades afectadas.
- Apoyar los procesos de entrega, control y registro de kits de dignidad dirigidos a población en situación de vulnerabilidad.
- Facilitar actividades de orientación comunitaria sobre riesgos de protección, servicios disponibles y rutas de acceso a servicios especializados.
- Apoyar la organización logística de capacitaciones y talleres de PGI dirigidos a voluntariado y personal de la Cruz Roja Venezolana.

**Gestión de casos y derivaciones**

- Apoyar la identificación inicial de personas con necesidades específicas de protección y referirlas al Oficial de Protección para la activación de mecanismos de derivación segura.
- Mantener registros y bases de datos de derivaciones realizadas, respetando los principios de confidencialidad y protección de datos.
- Dar seguimiento administrativo a casos derivados cuando sea requerido por el Oficial de Protección.

**Restablecimiento del Contacto Familiar (RCF/RFL)**

- Apoyar la prestación de servicios de conectividad para personas afectadas por la emergencia, incluyendo acceso a internet, llamadas telefónicas y recarga de dispositivos electrónicos.
- Apoyar la organización y mantenimiento de equipos de conectividad, materiales RCF y registros asociados a los servicios prestados.

**Gestión de información y reportes**

- Sistematizar información de actividades realizadas en terreno mediante formularios, listas de asistencia, bases de datos y reportes operativos.
- Consolidar indicadores, estadísticas y medios de verificación requeridos por la operación.
- Apoyar la elaboración de informes narrativos, reportes mensuales y reportes de donantes.
- Garantizar el adecuado archivo físico y digital de la documentación del proyecto.

**Apoyo logístico y administrativo**

- Gestionar inventarios de equipos, kits, mobiliario y materiales de protección asignados a la operación.
- Apoyar los procesos administrativos relacionados con actividades de protección, incluyendo solicitudes de compra, logística de eventos y control documental.
- Mantener actualizado el inventario de voluntariado vinculado a las actividades de protección y PGI.
- Coordinar aspectos logísticos para desplazamientos, actividades comunitarias y capacitaciones.

**Salvaguarda y calidad programática**

- Promover la aplicación de los principios de Protección, Género e Inclusión, Salvaguarda y Prevención de la Explotación y el Abuso Sexual (PEAS) en todas las actividades de la operación.
- Garantizar el manejo confidencial de información sensible de participantes y sobrevivientes.
- Contribuir a la implementación de mecanismos de participación comunitaria y retroalimentación de las personas afectadas.

**Formación académica**

- Título universitario o estudiante de los últimos semestres en Trabajo Social, Psicología, Sociología, Derecho, Relaciones Internacionales, Educación, Desarrollo Social o carreras afines.

**Experiencia**

- Mínimo dos (2) año de experiencia en programas sociales, humanitarios o comunitarios.
- Deseable experiencia en contextos de emergencia, protección, género, inclusión, migración o trabajo con población vulnerable.
- Deseable experiencia en recolección y sistematización de datos y elaboración de reportes.

**Conocimientos**

- Conocimientos básicos de Protección, Género e Inclusión (PGI).
- Conocimientos básicos de derivación segura y enfoque centrado en la persona.
- Conocimiento de principios de confidencialidad y protección de datos.
- Manejo de herramientas Microsoft Office, especialmente Excel, Word y formularios digitales.
- Deseable conocimiento de Restablecimiento del Contacto Familiar (RCF/RFL).

**Competencias**

- Organización y planificación.
- Comunicación efectiva.
- Trabajo en equipo.
- Sensibilidad humanitaria y respeto por la diversidad.
- Orientación al servicio.
- Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión y en contextos de emergencia.
- Adaptabilidad y disponibilidad para movilización al terreno.

**Condiciones especiales**

- Disponibilidad para viajar a estados afectados por el terremoto según necesidades operativas.
- Disponibilidad para trabajo ocasional en fines de semana o fuera de horario regular durante activaciones de emergencia.
- Compromiso con los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.

jobs.title: Termes de référence pour un.e Consultant.e en APC - Aproche Par Competences (Deuxième phase)
jobs.body:
*Baccalauréat Technique Agricole et accompagnement de la formation de formateurs*

**1. Mission :**

La Fondation Jóvenes y Desarrollo, en collaboration avec la Fondation Rinaldi, le Ministère de l'Éducation Nationale d'Haïti et financée par l'Union Européenne, mène un projet, Ref. NDICI LA 2023/446-340, dont l'objectif principal est : « Promouvoir l'accès équitable et inclusif des jeunes haïtiens, en particulier des jeunes femmes et des jeunes en situation de vulnérabilité, à l'employabilité et/ou la permanence dans le système éducatif », visant à améliorer la qualité de la formation professionnelle en Haïti.

Dans le cadre de ce projet, un diagnostic curriculaire, des référentiels ainsi que des guides pédagogique et d'évaluation ont déjà été développés pour les filières Énergies Renouvelables (ER) et Nouvelles Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication (NTIC), selon la méthodologie de l'Approche Par Compétences (APC). Ce travail a nécessité une double révision, menée à la fois avec l'équipe technique interne et avec l'Institut National de Formation Professionnelle (INFP), ce qui a occasionné certains retards dans la validation finale des référentiels. Une première partie des travaux relatifs à la nouvelle spécialité de Baccalauréat Technique (BT) Agricole a également été engagée, avec la production du cadre éducatif et des contenus didactiques ; restent à produire le programme de formation, le guide pédagogique, le guide d'évaluation et le Guide d'Organisation Pédagogique et Matérielle (GOPM).

Cette deuxième phase vise à achever l'ensemble des livrables relatifs à la spécialité de BT Agricole, ainsi qu'à accompagner et superviser le processus de formation des Formateurs/trices de Formateurs/trices (FdeF), incluant la prise en charge d'un module technique spécifique.

**2. Fonctions essentielles :**

Le consultant assurera, d'une part, l'achèvement de la conception de la nouvelle spécialité de BT Agricole déjà engagée, et d'autre part, l'accompagnement et la supervision du processus de formation des Formateurs/trices de Formateurs/trices (FdeF), incluant la prise en charge d'un module technique spécifique, en cohérence avec les normes et standards du Ministère de l'Éducation Nationale et de la Formation Professionnelle (MENFP) et de l'INFP.

**3. Responsabilités et activités :**

**3.1 Accompagnement de la formation de formateurs (9.000 €)**

1\. Accompagner et superviser le processus de formation des Formateurs/trices de Formateurs/trices (FdeF).

2\. Dispenser un module technique spécifique dans le cadre de ce processus.

**3.2 Baccalauréat Technique Agricole (20.000 €)**

Sur la base du cadre éducatif et des contenus didactiques déjà élaborés lors de la première phase :

1\. Élaborer le programme de formation de la spécialité BT Agricole.

2\. Concevoir le guide pédagogique de la spécialité BT Agricole.

4\. Élaborer le Guide d'Organisation Pédagogique et Matérielle (GOPM) de la spécialité BT Agricole.

3\. Concevoir le guide d'évaluation de la spécialité BT Agricole.

**4. Qualifications requises :**

Le consultant devra remplir les critères suivants :

- Formation Académique: Diplôme universitaire en Éducation, Pédagogie, Gestion Éducative ou domaines similaires.
- Expérience Professionnelle: Expérience confirmée en formation professionnelle et méthodologie de l'approche par compétences (APC), idéalement démontrée par une expérience similaire sur la filière Énergies Renouvelables (ER) ou des filières techniques comparables.
- Compétences Techniques: Connaissance approfondie de la méthodologie APC et expérience dans le développement de référentiels et de matériel didactique.
- Expérience avérée de collaboration avec le MENFP et l'INFP.
- Expérience confirmée dans l'animation de modules de formation destinés à des formateurs/trices (FdeF).
- Bonne connaissance des besoins spécifiques du secteur agricole en Haïti.

**5. Durée de la consultation :**

L'accord couvre l'intégralité de la durée de cette deuxième phase, jusqu'au 31 décembre 2027.

Les budgets alloués à chaque activité sont les suivants :

**Activité**

**Budget**

Accompagnement formation de formateurs

9.000 €

Baccalauréat Technique Agricole

20.000 €

**TOTAL**

**29.000 €**

**6. Produits attendus :**

**3.1 Accompagnement de la formation de formateurs :**

1\. Rapport de formation du module technique dispensé : contenus, méthodologie, calendrier, listes de présence (par sexe), évaluation de la formation et canevas utilisés.

2\. Rapport de suivi du processus de formation des FdeF.

**3.2 Baccalauréat Technique Agricole :**

1\. Programme de formation de la spécialité BT Agricole.

2\. Guide pédagogique de la spécialité BT Agricole.

3\. Guide d'évaluation de la spécialité BT Agricole.

4\. Guide d'Organisation Pédagogique et Matérielle (GOPM) de la spécialité BT Agricole.

jobs.title: AI Platform Engineer
jobs.body:
**Job Background / Overview**

The IRC is actively investing in enterprise AI to improve the speed, quality, and scale of its programs and operations. As the organization expands its use of AI platforms, including tools from Anthropic, OpenAI, and integrated data environments, the IT department is building dedicated technical capacity to keep these systems running reliably, securely, and effectively.

The IRC is investing in enterprise AI to improve the speed, quality, and scale of its programs and operations. As that investment grows, so does the need for someone to own the technical layer underneath it: the systems, integrations, and infrastructure that make AI tools work at scale.

The AI Platform Engineer is that person. This is a technical operations role, not a user-facing one. This role is responsible for keeping the IRC's enterprise AI environment running managing platform configurations and API access, building and maintaining integrations between AI tools and IRC systems, writing scripts and automations, and serving as the technical point of contact for data engineering and InfoSec. Day-to-day, this person is more likely to be reading logs, troubleshooting a broken pipeline, or pushing a configuration change than answering questions from end users.

The role works in close coordination with the AI Platform Support Director, who owns vendor relationships, licensing, and adoption strategy. This role owns the technical execution underneath that, ensuring the systems are reliable, observable, and properly connected to the rest of the IRC's data and operational environment.

**Major Responsibilities**

**AI Systems Administration & Operations (40%)**

- Serve as primary technical administrator across IRC enterprise AI environments, currently including Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI platform deployments
- Manage user access, API key governance, workspace configurations, and environment-level settings across AI platforms
- Monitor system health, usage patterns, and API performance across AI tools; triage and resolve operational issues as they arise
- Maintain and improve observability across AI systems
- Tracking uptime, error rates, token consumption, and integration reliability
- Oversee and document configuration changes, environment updates, and deployment procedures across managed platforms
- Support responsible use by flagging anomalous usage patterns and coordinating with InfoSec on policy adherence and access controls

**Integrations & Technical Implementation (35%)**

- Coordinate with the DevOps, SW Engineering and Data Engineering team(s) on deployment processes, environment access, and infrastructure dependencies required to build and maintain AI integrations
- Follow established change management procedures for all configuration changes, environment updates, and integration deployments, including documentation, testing, and appropriate approvals before pushing to production
- Develop lightweight scripts, connectors, and automations to support AI-assisted workflows across teams, primarily in Python and/or JavaScript/TypeScript
- Troubleshoot integration failures, data flow issues, and API connectivity problems across the AI ecosystem
- Collaborate with the data engineering team on AI/KM pipeline work, including vector store ingestion, retrieval configuration, and source data connections
- Contribute to technical design discussions with engineering partners, translating operational requirements into implementable solutions
- Maintain technical documentation for all integrations, including architecture notes, runbooks, and dependency maps

**Monitoring, Resource Optimization & InfoSec Liaison (15%)**

- Track and report on AI resource utilization across platforms, identifying opportunities to reduce waste and improve cost efficiency in coordination with the AI
- Serve as the technical point of contact with the InfoSec team on matters related to AI system security, data handling, access controls, and compliance requirements
- Support risk assessments and security reviews for new AI tools or integrations by providing accurate technical context on system behavior and data flows
- Contribute to the development of technical SOPs and best-practice guidelines for AI system use, in coordination with the AI Platform Support Director and relevant stakeholders

**Stakeholder Support & Collaboration (10%)**

- Act as a technical resource for program and operations teams adopting AI tools, including answering implementation questions, supporting troubleshooting, and identifying configuration solutions
- Participate in rollout planning for new AI capabilities, providing grounded input on technical feasibility, integration requirements, and operational readiness
- Collaborate with the AI Platform Support Director on onboarding documentation and technical guidance materials for end users
- Contribute to sprint and project planning with accurate estimates on technical effort and dependencies

**Required Experience & Skills**

**AI & Cloud Platforms**

- Hands-on experience administering enterprise AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or comparable tools), including API management, access controls, and environment configuration
- Familiarity with LLM application infrastructure: prompt pipelines, Model Context Protocol (MCP), other tool-calling integration frameworks, vector databases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns, and embedding workflows
- Experience working with Databricks or comparable data/ML platforms is a strong plus

**Integration & Development**

- Proficiency in Python and/or JavaScript for scripting, automation, and lightweight integration work
- Experience building and maintaining REST API integrations, including authentication patterns, webhook handling, and error management
- Comfort reading and working within existing codebases without requiring significant architectural guidance
- Familiarity with version control (Git) and standard deployment practices for scripts and integrations

**Systems Administration & Monitoring**

- Experience monitoring distributed systems or SaaS platforms, including setting up alerting, reviewing logs, and diagnosing performance or availability issues
- Familiarity with usage/cost monitoring for cloud or API-based services
- Comfort operating in live production environments where reliability and data integrity are critical

**Security & Compliance**

- Working knowledge of information security principles as they apply to SaaS and API-based systems: access controls, credential management, data handling, and audit logging
- Ability to engage constructively with InfoSec teams, providing clear technical context to support reviews and risk assessments

**Collaboration & Communication**

- Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical colleagues and program staff
- Experience contributing to cross-functional teams alongside product, engineering, and operations stakeholders
- Strong documentation habits: runbooks, SOPs, architecture notes, and internal guides

**Working Environment**

This role is remote, with the possibility of in-person work depending on location. Stakeholders are located across multiple time zones (GMT-8 to GMT+3), which may require occasional early or late meetings.

**Compensation:** ($88,277 - $102,451 pay range annual). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Project Director (Kenya Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**Company/Division:** [inSupply Health Limited](https://insupplyhealth.com/)

**Reports to:** Chief Executive Officer

**Expected Project Start:** 1 January 2027

**Organization Overview:**

inSupply Health is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming to achieve business sustainability while advancing our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, and context-specific supply chain learning and innovations so that local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems, towards better health outcomes.

inSupply Health is headquartered in Nairobi, with offices in Dar es Salaam and across East Africa, and is affiliated with JSI Research & Training Institute, Inc. (JSI). We collaborate closely with public and private-sector clients to design optimized, responsive, and resilient supply chain systems. Our dynamic team of local consultants delivers critical services supporting essential health products, adapting proven methodologies to local contexts for long-term impact.

**Job Summary**

inSupply Health is seeking an experienced Project Director to provide strategic and operational leadership for a prospective donor-funded, multi-country project expected to commence on **1 January 2027.**

The project will focus on improving access to quality-assured maternal and newborn health (MNH) products through country-led interventions addressing systemic barriers across policy and guidelines, forecasting and quantification, financing, procurement, regulation, supply and distribution.

The Project Director will translate the approved project strategy into measurable results across participating countries, providing overall oversight of implementation, government ownership, consortium and partner coordination, financial and operational stewardship, donor compliance, risk management, quality, learning and sustainability. The role will also serve as a senior representative of inSupply Health, engaging with donors, governments, consortium partners, technical teams, communities and other strategic stakeholders.

**Important:** Appointment to this position is contingent upon the project being awarded and the position being confirmed in the final project staffing plan. Further details about the project and donor will be shared with candidates who reach the final stages of the selection process.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Leadership & Project Governance**

- Provide overall strategic leadership and direction for the project.
- Translate project objectives and contractual commitments into clear priorities, implementation approaches and measurable results.
- Establish effective governance, accountability, decision-making and performance management mechanisms.
- Provide strategic oversight across participating countries while ensuring interventions are adapted to country contexts and priorities.
- Champion equity, innovation, sustainability, local ownership and value for money.

**Country Implementation & Project Delivery**

- Provide strategic oversight of project start-up, country planning and implementation.
- Ensure country teams translate project strategy into realistic, prioritised and measurable implementation plans.
- Oversee delivery of agreed milestones, outputs and outcomes within approved timelines, resources and quality standards.
- Ensure effective coordination across country, technical, operational and functional teams.
- Lead timely corrective and adaptive action where implementation deviates from approved plans or expected results.

**Government, Consortium & Strategic Partnerships**

- Serve as the senior project representative with donors, governments, consortium partners and other strategic stakeholders.
- Build and maintain effective relationships with government ministries, procurement agencies, regulatory bodies, financing institutions and other national stakeholders.
- Promote government leadership, ownership and sustainability.
- Lead effective coordination across consortium partners, ensuring clear roles, accountabilities and delivery expectations.
- Represent inSupply Health in relevant national, regional and international forums.

**Financial & Resource Stewardship**

- Provide overall accountability for effective stewardship of project resources.
- Ensure resources are strategically allocated across countries, interventions and activities to maximise results and value for money.
- Review financial performance, forecasts, expenditure and material variances and ensure timely corrective action.
- Work closely with Finance and Operations leadership to ensure effective financial controls, forecasting, budget management and donor reporting.
- Ensure personnel, consultants and other project resources are appropriately planned and deployed.

**People Leadership & Project Capability**

- Lead multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed teams, fostering a collaborative, inclusive and accountable environment.
- Establish clear performance expectations, decision rights and accountability across the project leadership structure.
- Guide, coach and support Project Managers, technical leads and other project leaders.
- Ensure the project has the skills, capacity and leadership capability required to deliver its objectives.
- Promote staff engagement, wellbeing, safeguarding, inclusion and organisational values.

**Quality, Compliance, Risk & Safeguarding**

- Provide oversight of compliance with donor agreements, contractual obligations, applicable laws and organisational policies.
- Oversee strategic, financial, operational, implementation, safeguarding and reputational risks.
- Ensure high and critical risks have clear owners, mitigation measures and escalation pathways.
- Ensure material compliance issues, audit findings and management actions are addressed within agreed timelines.
- Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, ethical conduct and safeguarding.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning & Evidence**

- Provide strategic oversight of monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting systems.
- Ensure reliable data and evidence inform strategic decisions, adaptive management and resource allocation.
- Monitor progress towards improvements in MNH product access, including on-shelf availability of selected tracer products.
- Lead cross-country learning and knowledge exchange.
- Promote documentation and dissemination of evidence, innovations and good practices to support replication and scale-up.

**Sustainability, Scale & Project Development**

- Provide strategic leadership for project sustainability, institutionalisation, scale-up and transition.
- Strengthen local systems, government ownership and institutional capacity to sustain results beyond the project period.
- Identify opportunities to leverage complementary investments, partnerships and financing.
- Provide senior-level input into proposals, concept notes, project extensions, partnerships and resource mobilisation opportunities.

**Project Reporting, Communication & Close-Out**

- Ensure accurate, timely and high-quality donor, technical, financial and management reports.
- Communicate project performance, achievements, financial status, risks, challenges and opportunities to senior management, donors and stakeholders.
- Lead periodic project performance reviews and ensure agreed actions are followed through.
- Provide strategic oversight of project close-out and transition planning.
- Ensure final evaluations, reports, knowledge products, stakeholder handovers and sustainability or transition plans are completed to the required standards.

**Qualifications & Experience**

## **Academic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in Project Management, Business Administration, Public Health, Development Studies, International Development, Supply Chain, Economics or a related field.
- A Master's degree in a relevant discipline is **mandatory.**

## **Professional Qualifications**

- Membership in a relevant professional body, such as PMI or an equivalent recognised professional association.
- Professional certification in Project or Programme Management, such as **PMP, PRINCE2** or an equivalent internationally recognised qualification, is highly desirable.
- Additional certification in Monitoring & Evaluation, Results-Based Management, Risk Management, Agile Project Management or another relevant discipline is an advantage.

**Professional Experience**

- At least **12 years** of progressively responsible experience in global health, international development, health systems strengthening, health supply chains or a related field, including substantial senior project or programme leadership experience.
- Demonstrated experience providing strategic leadership for complex, multi-country, donor-funded projects, with accountability for strategy, implementation, budgets, teams, partnerships, compliance and results.
- Experience working with government institutions and public-sector health systems, preferably across multiple countries and operating contexts.
- Strong understanding of health systems and supply-chain ecosystems, including systemic barriers related to access, financing, procurement, policy, data, regulation or service delivery.
- Proven experience leading multi-partner or consortium-based projects.
- Demonstrated experience engaging and influencing donors, government institutions, implementing partners and senior stakeholders.
- Experience leading multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed teams.
- Experience overseeing workplans, budgets, forecasts, risks, contractual deliverables and performance frameworks.
- Demonstrated experience in monitoring, evaluation, learning, evidence generation and adaptive project management.
- Experience in maternal and newborn health, health products, pharmaceutical or medical supply chains, procurement, market shaping or related areas is highly desirable.

## **Key Competencies**

We are looking for a leader who demonstrates:

- Strategic & Systems Thinking
- Multi-Country & Consortium Leadership
- Government & Stakeholder Engagement
- Results & Adaptive Management
- People & Resource Leadership
- Risk, Integrity & Accountability

jobs.title: Deputy Finance Director (Kenya Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**Company/Division:** [inSupply Health Limited](https://insupplyhealth.com/)

**Reports to:** Project Director

**Functional Relationship:** Finance Director

**Expected Project Start:** 1 January 2027

**Organization Overview:**

inSupply Health is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming to achieve business sustainability while advancing our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, and context-specific supply chain learning and innovations so that local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems, towards better health outcomes.

inSupply Health is headquartered in Nairobi, with offices in Dar es Salaam and across East Africa, and is affiliated with JSI Research & Training Institute, Inc. (JSI). We collaborate closely with public and private-sector clients to design optimized, responsive, and resilient supply chain systems. Our dynamic team of local consultants delivers critical services supporting essential health products, adapting proven methodologies to local contexts for long-term impact.

**Job Summary**

inSupply Health is seeking an experienced **Deputy Finance Director** to provide senior financial and operational leadership to the Project Management Unit (PMU) for a prospective donor-funded project expected to commence on **1 January 2027**.

The role will provide financial and operational oversight across multiple countries, consortium members and implementation partners, ensuring effective stewardship of project resources, sound financial management, donor compliance and timely financial decision-making.

The Deputy Finance Director will work closely with the Project Director, Finance Director, country and technical teams, consortium partners and other stakeholders to translate project priorities into practical financial and operational plans and provide financial analysis and insights to support effective project delivery.

**Important:** Appointment to this position is contingent upon the project being awarded and the position being confirmed in the final project staffing plan. Further details about the project and donor will be shared with candidates who reach the final stages of the selection process.

**Responsibilities:**

## **1. Financial Leadership & Performance Management**

- Provide day-to-day financial leadership and oversight across participating countries and implementation areas.
- Monitor project financial performance and provide timely financial advice and analysis.
- Promote accountability, financial discipline, value for money and responsible resource utilisation.

## **2. Budgeting, Forecasting & Cost Management**

- Lead preparation, consolidation and review of annual and multi-year project budgets.
- Coordinate budget revisions, forecasts and financial projections across countries and project components.
- Monitor expenditure, commitments, burn rates and budget variances.
- Advise project leadership on the financial implications of implementation and resource decisions.

## **3. Financial Reporting & Analysis**

- Lead the preparation and review of accurate and timely financial reports and management information.
- Provide financial analysis and insights to support project performance and decision-making.
- Strengthen the use of financial data to identify trends, risks and opportunities.

## **4. Grant, Contract & Partner Financial Management**

- Provide financial oversight across the grant lifecycle, from budgeting and implementation through reporting, close-out and audit.
- Ensure compliance with donor requirements, grant agreements, contracts and organisational policies.
- Oversee financial aspects of consortium partners, subrecipients and implementing partners.
- **Identify financial risks and coordinate corrective actions and capacity strengthening.**

## **5. Financial Controls, Compliance & Risk Management**

- Implement and monitor effective financial controls and ensure compliance with delegated authorities and financial procedures.
- Identify control weaknesses and ensure corrective actions are implemented.
- Maintain oversight of project-level financial risks and ensure appropriate escalation.
- Ensure financial records and supporting documentation meet donor, statutory and organisational requirements.

## **6. Audit & Donor Compliance**

- Coordinate financial aspects of internal, external, donor and project audits.
- Monitor donor financial conditions and reporting requirements.
- Track audit findings and coordinate corrective actions.
- Escalate material compliance concerns and financial risks.

## **7. Cash Flow, Treasury & Financial Operations**

- Monitor cash requirements, liquidity, commitments and short-term funding needs.
- Prepare and review cash-flow forecasts.

jobs.title: Consultancy for the Design and Development of a Digital Caritas Internationalis Management Standards (CIMS) Platform
jobs.body:
**Caritas Internationalis** brings together 162 autonomous national organisations in more than 200 countries and territories across the world, each responding to its local context while forming one network that provides emergency relief, supports long-term development and calls for justice and peace.

**The Caritas Internationalis Management Standards (CIMS)** are a reference tool for member organisations, and for regional bodies and the General secretariat, to assess their progress at any given time, support ongoing institutional development, strengthen capacity and long-term sustainability. By applying them, the Confederation as a whole aims to become more effective through good governance, sound management and strong accountability.

**? Design & Development of a Digital Platform**

The assignment will support the next phase of the **Caritas Internationalis Management Standards (CIMS) Review**, transforming the revised CIMS processes and tools into a secure, user-friendly and sustainable digital platform including the digitalisation and integration of the Organizational Development Solidarity Fund (ODSF).

**? What will the consultancy cover?**

The selected consultant/firm will support Caritas Internationalis to:

?**Digitalise the CIMS process**

?**Develop a digital Organisational Review Tool (ORT)**

?**Digitalise the ODSF**

?**Build a CIMS information and reporting system**

- ? Dashboards and data visualisation
- ? Trend and comparative analysis
- ? Reports at Member Organisation, Regional and Confederation levels
- ? Secure, role-based access to information

? **Connect CIMS and ODSF** so that relevant information from CIMS assessments, risks, priorities and Improvement Plans can be linked to ODSF applications and supported activities, reducing unnecessary duplication.

**? Key requirements**

The platform should also consider:

? Multilingual functionality — English, French and Spanish  
? Data protection, cybersecurity and confidentiality  
? Role-based access and permissions  
? User-friendly and accessible design  
? Functionality for low or limited internet connectivity  
? Integration with other existing Caritas Internationalis systems (Baobab)  
? A CIMS Library and Knowledge Centre  
? Alerts, notifications and workflow management

**?‍? Who are we looking for?**

We are looking for a consultant or consultancy firm with:

✅ Proven experience developing digital platforms  
✅ Experience translating complex organisational processes into digital workflows  
✅ Strong UX/UI, database and application-development expertise  
✅ Experience with assessment, compliance or organisational-development systems  
✅ Experience with dashboards and reporting systems  
✅ Knowledge of cybersecurity and data protection  
✅ Experience with testing and deployment  
✅ Strong project-management capacity

? Experience with international NGOs, humanitarian/development organisations, multilingual platforms, safeguarding information systems or Caritas/faith-based networks is an asset.

**? Timeline**

?️ **Digitisation:** October 2026 – December 2027  
?️**Maintenance & technical support:** December 2027 – November 2029  
**? How to apply**

Interested consultants/consultancy firms are invited to submit:

? **Technical proposal**  
? **Financial proposal**  
? **Proposed methodology and work plan**  
? **Relevant experience and organisational capacity**

jobs.title: Mental Health and Protection Coordinator
source: Union of Medical Care and Relief Organizations
jobs.body:
**Title:** Mental Health and Protection Coordinator

**Location: Remote (with travels as required)**

**Organization:** UOSSM USA

**Contract Duration:** 6 months (with possibility of extension based on funding and performance)

**Start date:** November 2, 2026

**Type of Contract:** Full-time

**Salary:** USD 2,500/month

**Application Deadline:** October 16, 2026

**About UOSSM USA**

**The Union of Medical Care and Relief Organizations (UOSSM USA) is a humanitarian, non-profit medical organization committed to improving access to quality healthcare and strengthening health systems for vulnerable and conflict-affected populations. Through emergency response, recovery, and development programming, UOSSM USA works in partnership with national institutions, local organizations, and international stakeholders to deliver integrated health, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), primary health care (PHC), protection, and community-based services.**

**In Lebanon, UOSSM USA supports the strengthening of health and MHPSS systems through technical assistance, capacity building, quality assurance, and strategic partnerships with local organizations and the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH). The organization is committed to delivering evidence-based, people-centered interventions that improve access to high-quality, integrated services for vulnerable communities.**

**Position Summary**

UOSSM USA is seeking an experienced Mental Health and Protection Coordinator to provide strategic, technical and quality leadership for UOSSM USA's Mental Health, Psychosocial Support and Protection portfolio in Lebanon, while also providing regional technical support and advisory services to UOSSM USA programmes in other countries where needed.

The position will provide technical oversight to UOSSM-supported programmes and implementing partners, ensuring that mental health and protection interventions are designed and implemented in accordance with national policies, relevant sector standards, UOSSM USA policies, donor requirements, and recognized international guidelines and best practices.

**Purpose of the Role**

The Mental Health and Protection Coordinator provides strategic and technical leadership for UOSSM USA’s MHPSS and Protection portfolio in Lebanon and the region, across both direct implementation and partner-led programming. The position ensures the quality, relevance, and accountability of services through technical guidance, capacity strengthening, quality assurance, monitoring, and oversight, in line with national policies and systems, international standards, donor requirements, and UOSSM USA policies and priorities.

The Coordinator serves as the primary technical focal point for MHPSS and Protection, providing expertise on mental health and psychosocial support, child protection, protection case management, safeguarding, PSEA, and related protection standards and policies. The role supports the development and strengthening of organizational and partner systems, tools, SOPs, referral pathways, and staff capacities, while ensuring protection, safeguarding, accountability, inclusion, and do-no-harm principles are integrated across programming.

**Key Roles and Responsibilities**

**A. Technical Leadership & Health Program Quality**

***1. Strategic and Technical Oversight***

- Provide technical leadership and oversight for UOSSM USA’s MHPSS and Protection programming, whether directly implemented or delivered through partners, ensuring interventions are rights-based, inclusive, safe, accountable, evidence-informed, and responsive to identified needs.
- Develop, review, and strengthen MHPSS and Protection strategies, technical approaches, SOPs, guidelines, tools, referral pathways, and implementation standards, ensuring alignment with national systems, international standards, donor requirements, and the systematic integration of safeguarding, PSEA, accountability, inclusion, gender, disability, confidentiality, informed consent, and do-no-harm principles throughout the program cycle.
- Provide technical support to country teams and partners across projects, including needs assessments, program design, proposal development, implementation, case management, monitoring, quality assurance, reporting, learning, and program adaptation.
- Conduct technical capacity strengthening for staff and partners on MHPSS, protection principles, child protection, protection case management, safeguarding, PSEA, protection mainstreaming, safe identification and referrals, confidentiality, and survivor- and child-centred approaches; and support the establishment of appropriate protection policies, SOPs, accountability mechanisms, complaints and feedback systems, and safe programming practices.
- Conduct technical quality assessments, field monitoring visits, case management and file reviews, and program quality audits; document and analyse protection concerns and trends; and develop and follow up on technical improvement and corrective action plans.
- Strengthen safe and effective MHPSS and Protection referral mechanisms and linkages with relevant health, Protection, CP, GBV, disability, government, and specialized service providers, ensuring appropriate identification, referral, follow-up, confidentiality, and informed consent.
- Coordinate with country teams and technical leads to harmonize standards, tools, SOPs, and approaches; facilitate cross-country technical exchanges and learning; disseminate good practices; and provide coordinated technical support to country programs and partners.
- Lead technical coordination and representation in Lebanon with the MoPH, relevant government institutions, UN agencies, clusters, sector working groups, and other coordination mechanisms, while monitoring technical standards, priorities, gaps, emerging needs, and policy developments relevant to UOSSM USA’s programming.
- Contribute technical inputs to proposals, concept notes, budgets, donor discussions, resource mobilization, and partnership development, identifying MHPSS and Protection priorities, technical requirements, strategic opportunities, and potential areas for program expansion and sustainability.

***2. Partner Technical Support & Capacity Strengthening***

- Conduct partner capacity assessments and develop targeted capacity-strengthening plans addressing identified technical, operational, and institutional gaps, with a focus on improving the quality, effectiveness, and sustainability of MHPSS, Protection, and health services.
- Lead and coordinate partner capacity strengthening through training, coaching, mentoring, technical accompaniment, and supportive supervision on MHPSS, Protection, case management, safeguarding, PSEA, protection mainstreaming, safe identification and referrals, confidentiality, survivor- and child-centred approaches, and relevant technical standards.
- Strengthen and monitor partner systems and practices for safe identification and referral, case management and follow-up, documentation and information management, complaints and feedback, accountability, safeguarding, and compliance with UOSSM USA policies, donor requirements, national frameworks, and relevant MHPSS, Protection, and health standards.
- Conduct joint field visits, technical reviews, case file reviews, and quality assessments; identify gaps and agree on corrective actions and technical improvement plans; and facilitate partner learning, knowledge sharing, and exchange of good practices, lessons learned, and technical resources across projects.

***3. Quality Assurance & Clinical Governance***

- Conduct field monitoring visits to implementing partners in Beirut Mount Lebanon and Bekaa Baalbek El Hermel, for technical quality reviews across MHPSS and Protection services, assessing service quality, documentation, referrals, safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent, and adherence to technical protocols and alignment with relevant national and international standards, ethical principles, and donor requirements.
- Monitor quality and outcome indicators, analyze monitoring findings, service data, complaints, feedback, and incident trends, and support partners to develop and implement corrective actions and continuous quality improvement plans.
- Strengthen clinical and technical supervision systems, including safe management and referral of complex or high-risk cases and appropriate escalation of protection, safeguarding, and PSEA concerns.
- Ensure beneficiary participation, feedback, complaints and accountability mechanisms are systematically used to identify gaps, improve service quality, and inform program adaptation.

***4. Coordination & Technical Representation***

- Represent UOSSM USA in relevant MHPSS, Protection, Child Protection, GBV, PSEA, Health, and AAP coordination mechanisms, sector working groups, technical forums, and inter-agency meetings in Lebanon and, where relevant, at regional level.
- Lead technical coordination with the MoPH, relevant government institutions, UN agencies, clusters, sector working groups, and humanitarian and development actors, ensuring alignment with national priorities, strategies, standards, and coordination frameworks.
- Maintain regular engagement with technical stakeholders and partners to identify emerging needs, protection risks, service gaps, referral challenges, and coordination priorities, and translate findings into programmatic recommendations.

***5. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning (MEAL)***

- Support the development and review of technical indicators of mental health and protection outcome monitoring, ensuring the appropriate use of validated, age-appropriate assessment tools at intake and follow-up to measure beneficiaries’ symptoms, improvements, treatment response, wellbeing, functioning, and quality of life, in line with clinical protocols.
- Ensure MHPSS, Protection, and Case Management data collection and reporting comply with confidentiality, informed consent, safeguarding, ethical data management, and data protection requirements, particularly for sensitive and individual-level case information.
- Promote the systematic use of beneficiary feedback, complaints, satisfaction, participation, and accountability mechanisms to assess the accessibility, safety, relevance, and quality of MHPSS, Protection, community based and Case Management services.
- Use findings from clinical outcome monitoring, case file reviews, protection monitoring, multidisciplinary case reviews, field monitoring, and technical audits to inform continuous quality improvement, capacity strengthening, referral system improvements, and program adaptation.

***6. Reporting & Technical Documentation***

- Contribute to donor reports, concept notes, proposals, and technical documentation.
- Develop technical briefs, guidance notes, clinical tools, training materials, and knowledge products.
- Maintain updated technical documentation, programme records, and quality assurance reports.
- Ensure technical documentation accurately reflects programme achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and recommendations.

**B. Technical Advisory & Program Development**

- Provide technical leadership in the design and development of MHPSS interventions and Protection programs.
- Provide technical input to project proposals, budgets, logical frameworks, implementation plans, and monitoring frameworks.
- Identify emerging health needs, service delivery gaps, and opportunities for programme expansion.
- Support resource mobilization efforts through technical contributions to donor engagement and proposal development.

**C. Integrated Coordination Role**

- Serve as the primary technical focal point between UOSSM USA and implementing partners.
- Coordinate closely with internal Programme, MEAL, Finance, Operations, and Grants teams to ensure effective, integrated programme implementation and timely workplan delivery.
- Provide regular technical updates, risk analysis, and strategic recommendations to senior management.
- Support integrated planning, workplan development, and timely implementation of programme activities.

**D. Representation & External Coordination**

- Represent UOSSM USA in external technical meetings, coordination forums, workshops, and stakeholder consultations.
- Strengthen collaboration with the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH), WHO, UN agencies, donors, academic institutions, and local partners.
- Promote the visibility and technical leadership of UOSSM USA's health programming.
- Identify opportunities to strengthen strategic partnerships and enhance coordination across the health sector.

**Qualifications & Experience**

- Master’s degree in Mental Health, Psychology, Social Work, Public Health, Protection, International Development, or a related field; or Bachelor’s degree with substantial relevant experience may be considered.
- 6+ years of relevant professional experience in MHPSS, Protection, Child Protection, Case Management, or related humanitarian/development programming, including experience in technical coordination and program quality.
- Strong technical knowledge of MHPSS, Protection, Child Protection, Protection Case Management, safeguarding, PSEA, protection mainstreaming, and referral systems, with practical application of relevant national and international standards.
- Experience developing and reviewing strategies, SOPs, guidelines, tools, referral pathways, quality standards, and technical frameworks for MHPSS and Protection programs.
- Demonstrated experience in partner capacity assessment, technical support, coaching, mentoring, training, supportive supervision, and quality assurance.
- Experience integrating Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) within Primary Health Care programmes.
- Previous collaboration with the Lebanese Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) or other national health authorities is a strong asset.
- Experience working with international NGOs, UN agencies, donors, or donor-funded health programmes.
- Experience contributing to programme design, proposal development, donor reporting, and technical documentation is an asset.

**Skills & Competencies**

- Strong technical knowledge of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Protection, Child Protection, Protection Case Management, safeguarding, and PSEA, with practical application in humanitarian and community-based settings.
- Strong understanding of WHO, IASC MHPSS Guidelines, Sphere Standards, Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), protection principles, and relevant Lebanon MoPH/National Mental Health Programme frameworks.
- Strong technical leadership, coordination, facilitation, representation, and stakeholder engagement skills, including engagement with MoPH, UN agencies, clusters, partners, and technical working groups.
- Demonstrated ability in partner capacity strengthening, coaching, mentoring, supportive supervision, technical monitoring, and quality assurance.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, technical writing, reporting, and proposal development skills, with the ability to translate evidence and technical standards into practical programming.
- Strong understanding and application of safeguarding, PSEA, confidentiality, informed consent, data protection, accountability, inclusion, gender, disability, and do-no-harm principles.
- Excellent communication, interpersonal, facilitation, negotiation, and relationship-management skills, with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, provide technical leadership across partners and countries, and perform effectively in complex and changing humanitarian environments.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, data analysis, reporting, and relevant digital/health information management systems.

**Languages**

- Fluency in Arabic and English required.
- French is an asset.

**Reporting Line**

Reports to: Regional MHPSS Coordinator

- Technical and Managerial Reporting: The Mental Health and Protection Coordiantor will report technically to the Regional MHPSS Coordinator, ensuring alignment with UOSSM’s USA technical standards, protocols, and programmatic guidance.

**Disclaimer:**

- **Code of Conduct:** We uphold a strict Code of Conduct that prohibits any form of misconduct, including sexual exploitation and abuse, trafficking in persons, and violations of ethical standards. This includes addressing conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and harassment; and reporting violations promptly, maintaining ethical standards.
- **Compliance & Ethics:** We strive to maintain the highest standards of compliance and ethics across all aspects of our work. As a member of the team, you are expected to uphold these standards and adhere to UOSSM USA's and donor compliance and ethics policies. This includes conducting your work with integrity and communicating these values to colleagues and partners, ensuring their adherence to these principles.
- **Equal Opportunities:** UOSSM USA is dedicated to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability, or veteran status.
- **Safeguarding and Child Safeguarding:** At UOSSM USA, we prioritize the safety and protection of all individuals within the communities we serve. All staff and contractors share the responsibility to safeguard and uphold the rights of vulnerable populations, including children and adults at risk. This commitment extends to preventing and addressing instances of sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as any form of exploitation, neglect, or trafficking in persons perpetrated by our staff or partners.

**About Light for the World**

jobs.title: Development of E-Learning Module Content — Tdh Migration and Displacement programme
jobs.body:
## **1. Background**

Terre des hommes (Tdh) is Switzerland's largest child rights organisation, active in over 30 countries. Its Migration and Displacement sector has developed two evidence-based Models of Action (MoA) to guide Tdh staff and partners working with migrant, displaced and at-risk children and youth:

**MoA 1 — Employability and access to employment for young migrants and refugees:** Employability and access to employment through (1) Skills and capabilities development, (2) Labour market linkage, and (3) Policy and system strengthening.

**MoA 2 — Education for children and youth on the move:** Structured around the 4As (Availability, Accessibility, Acceptability, Adaptability), leading to empowerment and socio-economic (re)integration.

Tdh wishes to make these frameworks accessible to its staff and implementing partners through the **development of related self-paced e-learning modules**. Tdh already runs a Migration and Displacement e-learning course for staff: the two new modules will be produced in the same format and uploaded to the existing platform by Tdh. This assignment covers content development only as platform integration is handled internally.

## **2. Objective and scope of work**

The consultant will develop content for two standalone e-learning modules, one for each MoA. The modules are intended for individual, self-paced learners. For each module, the consultant will submit a complete Word script that Tdh's technical team can upload to the existing CYM e-learning platform. The assignment does not include visual design, coding, platform configuration or upload work

**2.1 Consultant deliverables**

For each of the two modules, the consultant will deliver the following:

- Full content script (Word document): A complete, structured module script covering all learning content, activities and resources. The script must follow the format of the existing Tdh Migration and Development module series and be clear enough for Tdh's technical team to translate it into the online platform. It must include section text, activity instructions, external resource links with precise timecodes where relevant, correct answers for exercises, definitions and call-out boxes. It must be sufficiently clear and structured for the technical team to identify content blocks, activity types, correct answers, feedback text and any resources to be embedded or linked.
- Glossary: A list of 10-15 key terms with concise, learner-friendly definitions tailored to the thematic focus of the module.
- Learner summary sheet: A one-page printable reference sheet summarising the module's key concepts and takeaways, suitable for download alongside the module.
- Review and revision: The consultant will take part in an iterative review process, incorporate consolidated feedback from Tdh and submit revised versions until the module content is validated within the agreed workplan and timeline.

**2.2 Module format, components and minimum requirements**

Existing Migration and Development module scripts will be shared with the selected consultant as a formatting and style reference at the start of the assignment. Each module should follow the expected approach and minimum requirements below.

**Component**

1. Learner experience. **Expected approach:** Individual, self-paced learning. Content should be structured into short thematic sections that combine explanation, examples and activities. **Minimum requirement per module:** 45–60 minutes of learning time.
2. Narrative and voice. **Expected approach:** Write directly to the individual learner in the second person, using a clear and accessible register suitable for practitioners with varied educational backgrounds and operating contexts. **Minimum requirement per module** : Consistent second-person learner voice throughout the script.
3. Script length.**Expected approach :** Provide enough detail for direct platform integration, including all section text, activity instructions, answer keys and feedback text. **Minimum requirement per module** 2,500–4,000 words, including activity instructions and answers.
4. External resources. **Expected approach :** Curate publicly accessible, up-to-date and directly relevant resources, such as short videos, interactive data tools, websites, maps, reports or other practical materials. For any video used, provide precise start and end timecodes.**Minimum requirement per module** : Relevant external resources selected according to the learning objectives and availability of suitable materials. Each resource must include guided comprehension questions and correct answers where appropriate.
5. Interactive activities.**Expected approach :** Embed activities throughout the script and describe them clearly for platform build. Suitable formats include flip cards, matching or association exercises, multiple-choice questions, fill-in-the-blank questions and open reflection prompts. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 interactive activities, plus at least 1 open reflection prompt. Correct answers and short feedback text must be provided where relevant.
6. Case studies.**Expected approach :** Use real-world or fictionalised case studies grounded in Tdh field contexts, including Asia, Africa and Europe/MENA where relevant. Cases should include named fictional or anonymised characters and guided analysis questions. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.
7. Glossary and key concepts. **Expected approach :** Define core terms in concise, learner-friendly language and use call-out boxes to reinforce critical concepts, legal definitions, common misconceptions and section takeaways.**Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.

## **3. Required profile**

## **Mandatory**

- Demonstrated experience writing e-learning content scripts or instructional materials for NGO or UN audiences
- Strong ability to translate programmatic frameworks into clear, engaging learning content for individual practitioners
- Capacity to identify and integrate high-quality external resources (videos, data tools, reports) into a structured learning narrative
- Substantive knowledge in at least one of the two thematic areas: youth employability, education in emergencies / migration
- Excellent written English; ability to write in a direct, accessible register suitable for diverse field staff

### **Advantageous**

- Familiarity with child rights frameworks and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
- Knowledge of all two thematic areas covered by the MoAs

jobs.title: Regional Coordinator – Middle East (M/F) - 4 Months
jobs.body:
HAMAP-Humanitaire is seeking for an interim Middle East Regional Coordinator to replace our collaborator for a period of 4 months, based in Lebanon with potential trips to Iraq, Syria and Jordan.

**Introduction to HAMAP-Humanitaire**

Founded in 1999, HAMAP-Humanitaire is a non-governmental organisation (NGO) dedicated to development aid. Its mission is to take concrete action to ensure that ever more men, women and children have access to safe drinking water and sanitation, education, healthcare and security. Its objective is to support and strengthen its local partners from the initial identification of needs right through to the implementation and sustainability of their projects. HAMAP-Humanitaire’s work focuses on two main areas of activity: water and sanitation engineering and hygiene, and Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA).

**Mine Action:**

HAMAP, which later became HAMAP-Humanitaire, originally stood for ‘Halte Aux Mines Anti-Personnel’ (Stop Anti-Personnel Mines). Mine action is therefore the organisation’s original purpose. Various training and awareness-raising projects on the risks posed by landmines have been carried out in Mauritania, Senegal and Benin in the past. HAMAP-Humanitaire is currently active in mine clearance, risk education and advocacy in the Middle East and Ukraine.

**HAMAP in Middle East:**

HAMAP currently has 3 simultaneous projects in Lebanon working alongside with the LMAC, Beatoona and the University of Balamand, under French, Belgian and German MoFA funds. In Syria HAMAP is working with Safe Land for a one year project funded by French government. The Regional Coordinator is responsible for monitoring programmes and project activities, liaising with partners and maintaining relations with HQ.

**JOB MISSION:**

Under the supervision of the Head of the HMA Division, the Regional Coordinator establishes the operational and strategic framework for the Middle East region by analysing the humanitarian, security, political and social situation. He or she is responsible for the growth of the HMA sector, provides support to country teams, oversees the coherence of support functions and drives the localisation agenda. The role **involves structuring, harmonising and developing the programmatic, operational, security and partnership frameworks** for missions in the Middle East.

**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1) Management, HR and Team Cohesion (25%)**

- **Support for Coordinators**: Support Syria Country Coordinator and the regional team in their management and steering roles.
- **‘Problem-Solving**’: Acting as a ‘*problem solver*’ to propose viable solutions to operational, institutional and financial bottlenecks, or issues arising in partnership relationships.
- **Supporting innovation**: Working with technical leads and head office, identify and propose innovations for projects: digital awareness, integration of artificial intelligence, and others.
- **Team dynamics**: Ensure teams are well-led and cohesive by fostering a positive atmosphere amongst staff and maintaining a suitable working environment.

**2) Supervision of Support Functions (40%)**

- **Budgetary consistency**: Ensure the financial balance of the region and oversee the preparation of provisional budgets in line with funding strategies.
