- **Curriculum mapping and reference points:** Map existing curricula, learning outcomes, training modules, trainer guides, learner materials, practical exercises and assessment tools against applicable Somaliland/Somalia TVET policies and strategies; the Vocational Qualifications Framework (VQF); relevant national occupational, qualification, assessment and certification standards; BLOOM Labour Market Assessment findings; current employer and industry competency requirements; relevant occupational health and safety, environmental and manufacturer standards; and, where national guidance is incomplete, appropriate regional or international competency-based TVET good practice.
- **Labour market and occupational alignment:** Review the extent to which curricula reflect current and emerging industry requirements, employer expectations, practical workplace tasks, employment and self-employment pathways, enterprise development opportunities, and work-based learning needs.
- **Competency and content gap analysis:** For every priority trade, produce a module-by-module gap matrix covering technical and occupational competencies, sequencing and duration, theory-practice balance, practical workplace tasks, employability and soft skills, entrepreneurship, digital skills, financial literacy, green skills, life skills, social and emotional learning (SEL), learner protection and workplace readiness. The analysis shall also specify implications for instructor competence, tools and equipment, consumables, learning resources, work-based learning and assessment.
- **GEDSI and inclusion review:** Assess whether curriculum content, images and language; teaching methods and materials; practical exercises; assessment approaches; entry requirements; timetabling; reasonable accommodation; and delivery arrangements are gender-responsive, disability-inclusive, accessible, safe and appropriate for vulnerable youth, adolescent girls and young women, persons with disabilities and other marginalized learners. The review shall identify barriers and practical adaptations for each trade, including participation of young women in non-traditional trades.
- **Assessment and certification review:** Examine whether assessment tools and certification pathways are competency-based, practical, inclusive, and aligned with relevant national qualification and certification frameworks.
- **Curriculum improvement decisions:** Apply clear, evidence-based criteria to classify each curriculum component as retain, revise, enrich, supplement or develop anew. For every decision, identify the evidence, affected competency or module, required learning outcomes and content, pedagogy, trainer guidance, learner materials, practical exercises, assessment method, equipment/resource implications and responsible validation authority. Recommendations shall distinguish essential minimum changes from desirable future improvements.

**Phase 3: Primary Data Collection**

- The consultant shall undertake primary data collection with TVET and labour-market stakeholders to complement the desk review and provide evidence for the curriculum and institutional gap analysis. The assessment shall cover 4 TVET institution selected by BLOOM in Hargeisa and Burao (2 in Hargeisa and 2 in Burao both public and private). At each institution, the consultant shall complete the institutional/facility observation, review all available curricula and institutional records relevant to the four priority occupational areas, interview management and relevant staff, and administer the structured learner sample. The proposal shall cost this full institutional coverage and shall not substitute a sample of institutions.
- **Key Informant Interviews (KIIs):** Conduct a minimum of 30 KIIs across the two locations. Coverage shall include, at minimum: one senior management or head-of-institution interview in every selected TVET institution; instructors representing each priority trade offered by the institution; learner support, safeguarding, inclusion or career-services staff; at least 4 government/TVET authority representatives; at least 8 employers, business owners, industry associations or work-based-learning partners across the four occupational areas; and at least two representatives of organizations of persons with disabilities, women or youth. BLOOM and the consultant may add respondents during inception, but shall not reduce these minimum categories or the total without written approval.
- **Focus Group Discussions (FGDs):** Conduct a minimum of 12 FGDs, normally with 6-8 participants per group and separated where necessary to enable safe and candid participation. The minimum composition shall be: four FGDs with current learners (young women and young men represented separately in each location); two FGDs with learners nearing completion; two FGDs with recent graduates, including employed, self-employed and unemployed graduates where feasible; two FGDs specifically with young women enrolled in or considering non-traditional trades; and two FGDs with parents/community representatives, including perspectives on disability inclusion. Persons with disabilities shall be purposefully included across learner and graduate groups, with accessible facilitation and reasonable accommodation. Final allocation by institution, trade, sex and disability shall be agreed in the inception report without reducing the minimum total
- .**Current TVET students:** learning experience, teaching quality, equipment, inclusiveness, career aspirations and access to support services.
- **TVET alumni:** transition to employment/self-employment, relevance of skills, skills gaps, and barriers to employment, including green jobs.
- **Community/parent representatives:** perceptions of TVET, factors affecting enrolment and completion, and socio-cultural barriers, particularly for AGYW and youth with disabilities.
- Structured learner sample: In addition to FGDs, administer a short-structured survey or scoring tool to at least 20 current learners in each selected institution, distributed across the priority trades offered and, as far as feasible, balanced by sex and inclusive of learners with disabilities. Where an institution has fewer than 20 eligible learners, include all eligible learners. The final respondent matrix shall show planned and achieved samples by institution, location, trade, sex, age, disability and learner status.
- Instructor coverage: Apply the structured instructor competency and practice tool to all instructors delivering the priority trades in the selected institutions where feasible. If the number is too large for a census, the inception report shall propose a purposive sample that covers every priority trade offered, both locations, women instructors where available, and differing levels of experience; BLOOM approval is required before sampling.
- **Institutional Observations:** Structured observations will assess the condition and adequacy of TVET facilities, equipment and learning environments, including:
- Classrooms and practical workshops.
- Training equipment relevant to priority sectors, green and digital skills
- Sanitation, hygiene and student welfare facilities.
- Health, safety and safeguarding measures.
- Accessibility and inclusion for PwDs.
- Teaching and learning resources.
- Career guidance, student support and referral arrangements

**6. Deliverables**

The consultant shall produce the following deliverables:

**1. Inception Report -** Methodology, work plan, stakeholder engagement approach, quality assurance measures, and curriculum development framework. (Week 2)

**2. Institutional and Curriculum Gap Assessment Report -** Occupational Analysis and Curriculum Gap Assessment Report presenting findings on labour market needs, occupational standards, curriculum relevance, TVET institutional capacity, training quality and employability, alongside gender, disability, and social inclusion considerations, with recommendations to enrich, adapt, supplement, or develop curricula for priority trades (Week 5)

**3. Draft Curriculum Package for Four Priority Trades -** Draft competency-based curricula, trainer guides, learner materials, and assessment tools for the four priority trades (Week 10)

**4. Validation Workshop Report and Revised Curriculum Package -** Summary of validation findings and stakeholder feedback, with revised curriculum packages. (Week 13)

**5. Final Curriculum Package and Implementation Roadmap -** Final curriculum packages, training and assessment materials, and an implementation roadmap for delivery, quality assurance, and curriculum review (Week 16)

**7. Duration of the Assignment**

The consultancy is expected to be completed within **16 weeks** from the date of contract signature.

**More Details to be provided in the full ToR upon Expression of Interest.**

**We hereby invite Expression of Interest from registered, approved and reputable consultants to provide above-named services to World Vision Somalia.**

jobs.title: Field Engineer MEAL Officer/الحسكه
jobs.body:
**Job Summary:**

The MEAL officer will be responsible for supporting the WATAN MEAL team in planning, tool design, documentation, data analysis, and reporting. Also, he/she will work closely with the WATAN programs team, the MEAL field team, INGO partners, and donors. This will include training field staff on best practice approaches to data collection, including ensuring the confidentiality and rights of beneficiaries are respected.

**Tasks and Responsibilities of the Job**

- Conduct regular field visits to home rehabilitation sites to monitor the progress of construction works and ensure compliance with technical and timeline standards.
- Track the achievement of project objectives and provide regular updates and reports to the direct Line Manager.
- Design and develop Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) plans in line with project requirements.
- Ensure the establishment and regular, accurate updating of the project's Master Beneficiary Database.
- Collect, document, and follow up on beneficiary feedback and complaints received through WhatsApp, email, and field feedback boxes, while maintaining confidentiality and ensuring appropriate response.
- Develop relevant data collection tools and templates aligned with donor frameworks and WATAN's logical framework.
- Train and build the capacity of field staff on best practices in data collection, ensuring data quality and beneficiary privacy protection.
- Analyze quantitative and qualitative M&E data, draw insights, and formulate recommendations.
- Prepare and submit comprehensive reports on needs assessments, monitoring, evaluation, and verification activities as required by projects and donors.
- Participate in meetings with WATAN partners and donors as necessary.
- Perform any other project-related tasks assigned by the Line Manager.

Fully commit to WATAN Foundation's **zero-tolerance policy** on sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) and promptly report any suspected violations in accordance with established procedures.

**Job specification**

Education Degree Civil Engineering

Languages Arabic

English

Travel Availability

Minimum 2 years of professional and proven experience in the MEAL field.

Minimum of three years of practical professional experience in the humanitarian or relief sector.

Proven prior experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL).

Practical experience in designing and managing feedback, complaints, and accountability mechanisms towards beneficiaries.

Outstanding analytical and strategic skills, with a proactive ability to identify challenges and collaborate effectively to resolve them.

Strong and demonstrated skills in preparing professional and analytical reports.

Flexible and initiative-driven personality, capable of managing variable and unpredictable workloads while efficiently prioritizing tasks.

High organizational skills, ability to multitask, and effective time management, with a proven track record of meeting deadlines.

Good knowledge of data visualization software (e.g., Power BI, or similar tools).

Fluency in written and spoken Arabic and English.

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel.

Strong teamwork spirit and ability to work collaboratively and effectively.

**Work Environment**

Office / Field

jobs.title: Country Finance Manager Lebanon
jobs.body:
**Position**: Country Finance Manager Lebanon

**Location**: Beirut, Lebanon

**Reporting Relationship**: Country Representative (Line Management) and Regional Finance Manager (Functional Management)

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline**: 07/11/2026

**Working Context**

WeWorld has been working in Lebanon since 2006 and is currently supporting vulnerable refugee, IDP and host community populations through WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods, Local Economic Development, Education and Social Cohesion in Bekaa, Baalbek-Hermel, Akkar, Saida and Beirut. Our interventions span immediate emergency response and recovery in view of building preparedness and longer-term resilience for populations affected by conflict and/or displacement. The operation is run by over 50 employees, divided in three offices (Beirut, Zahle and Saida). We work closely with local partners, including NGOs and institutional actors at different levels, and are part of large consortia with other actors.

**Purpose of the Role**

The **Country Finance Manager** is responsible for all the administrative and accounting processes, including financial reporting, budget planning, development and monitoring. They manage staff within the Finance Department in country.

**MAIN FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES**

**General Administration**

- Track and manage deliverables and timelines related to grants, contracts, vendors, and partners
- Monitor grant administration to ensure compliance with reporting and expenditure requirements
- Supervise compliance of administrative documents and their proper filing
- Ensure the smooth flow of administrative information and data to the HQ
- Supervise flow of administrative information from project partners and the compliance with MoU
- Ensure smooth and punctual communications and reporting with local banks

**Accounting**

- Supervise and approve regular accounting, including monthly reconciliations, monthly and yearly closing of accounts, monthly journal entries
- Supervise cash and bank balance checking process when closing the monthly accounts

**Financial Reporting**

- Responsible for the preparation of financial reports, in coordination with Regional Finance Manager, and administrative team
- Ensure the compliance of financial reports with donors’ and internal rules and procedures

**Budget & Planning**

- Prepare and regularly monitor/updateWeWorld’s core budget for the Lebanon operation and provide an analysis to the Country Representativefocusing on gaps and risks
- Collaborate with the Country Representative, Head of Programmes and Project Managers to develop project budgets with quality, on time, in line with the operation’s core budget and according to donors’ regulations;
- Review administrative/financial terms of grant contracts before signature (payment & financial reporting schedule, etc.)
- Collaborate with the Head of Programmes, Project Managers and Procurement & Logistics Managers to regularly monitor actual and forecasted expenses against budget to avoid under and overspending on the projects in compliance withdonor flexibility rules
- Monitor financial flows of ongoing projects
- Anticipate financial risks, present budget updates and mitigation plans and report them to the Country Representative;
- Participate with the Country Management Team in reflecting on the evolution of the mission, and the programming of new projects and/or reorientation

**Audit Process**

- Collaborate to the management of financial audit performed on the projects
- Supervise yearly financial audit on general accounting for local authorities
- Prepare information and is directly responsible for any assessment/audit performed by donor on WeWorld administrative procedure

**Procedure**

- Design and implement administrative routines, procedures, and systems to increase efficiencies within the finance department, in particular relating to better structuring Budget Follow Ups, Forecasts, Payment Follow Ups and optimizing staff roles and responsibilities within the team
- Update the Local Operational Manual based on WeWorld procedures to implement organizational policies related to the Finance Department

**Operational**

- At Country level, liaise with the Human Resources and Procurement and Logistic departments for a fluid and collaborative collaboration
- Follow-up payments from donors and financial project close-out

**Human Resources**

- Participate in analyzing staffing needs & costs, compensation & benefits
- Supervise administrative and finance local personnel to complete routine tasks
- Capacity building of local finance staff and partner organizations in areas such as financial management, administration, good governance and management of accountability and transparency
- Support the Country Representative and the HR Manager to monitor and revise salary scale, if necessary

**Representation**

- Participate in inter-admin meetings with other INGOs and NGOs
- Ensure official representation for the administrative management of the Mission to the competent authorities

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a first 6 (six) month collaboration contract subject to verification of the achievement of specific objectives (these objectives will be agreed together with the Line Manager upon arrival on assignment); a second collaboration contract of 6 (six) months renewable, following the positive evaluation of the first months of contract and availability of funds.

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy Base Salary (2950€ - 3550€ monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family duty Station**: NO

**R&R**: NO

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

We are committed to building talented teams and welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent experience in Financial/Accounting management
- Knowledge of institutional donor procedures (AICS, EU, AFD, UN)
- Fluent in English both written and verbal

**Professional experience**

- At least 5 years of specific experience in finance/administrative positions in the international cooperation sector, in similar roles and levels or responsibility
- Experience of representation to institutions and participation in coordination meetings
- Experience in budget design and management and monitoring of logistics procedures
- Experience in using accounting software
- Experience in managing teams

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong flexibility and capacity to adapt behavior to the needs of the situation
- Capacity to work autonomously and in problems prevention/resolution
- Proven organizational skills and ability to effectively manage multiple tasks while fostering quality, team spirit and positive working relationships with colleagues
- Ability to identify, initiate and maintain good relationships with partner organizations, donors and national authorities including building professional relationships with senior decision-makers and influencers / leaders
- Good communication, negotiation skills and sensitivity in dealing with local institutions on critical issues
- Cultural, gender, religion, and age sensitivity and adaptability
- Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld, genuine interest for international cooperation development topics

**Desirable Requirements**

- Knowledge of Arabic would be considered an asset
- Previous experience in the Middle East Region is an asset

jobs.title: Consultancy for an Inclusive Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) in DR CONGO
jobs.body:
## **Background**

CBM (Christian Blind Mission) is an international development and humanitarian organisation dedicated to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the world's poorest countries. We are providing inclusive humanitarian assistance in contexts of disasters, conflict, and displacement. CBM’s humanitarian activities aim to equally reach and actively involve persons with disabilities, addressing specific needs while promoting and facilitating full inclusion in mainstream services. We work together with our partners on programmes that are context specific, from disability-inclusive preparedness to immediate life-saving needsto resilience strengthening. CBM is based in Germany with 23 country offices in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America. With over 115 years of experience, CBM is considered as one of the world’s oldest organisations working in this field.  
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) faces one of the world's most complex humanitarian crises, marked by armed conflict, displacement, protection risks, epidemics, food insecurity and natural disasters. Persons with disabilities, women, children, older persons, IDPs and returnees face heightened barriers to accessing assistance and essential services.  
To inform future humanitarian programming, including potential interventions under ECHO HIP 2027 and other funding opportunities, CBM seeks to conduct an Inclusive Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) in selected crisis-affected areas. Findings will support evidence-based programme design, strategic positioning and partnership development.  
CBM is seeking a qualified consultant or consulting team to lead this assessment.

## **Purpose of the Assignment**

The assessment aims to generate evidence on humanitarian needs, vulnerabilities and service gaps among crisis-affected populations, particularly persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups, to inform protection-centred, disability-inclusive and integrated humanitarian programming.

## **Objectives**

The assessment shall:

- Identify and analyse priority humanitarian needs and vulnerabilities.
- Assess barriers to accessing humanitarian assistance and essential services, particularly  
    for persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.
- Assess the availability, accessibility, quality and inclusiveness of essential services.
- Examine protection risks and inclusion concerns.
- Analyse existing services, referral pathways, coverage and response gaps.
- Identify geographic areas with the highest humanitarian needs through a comparative  
    analysis of severity, operational feasibility and CBM's potential added value.
- Establish the priority order of needs but also of geographic areas.
- Generate recommendations on geographic focus, sectoral priorities, targeting,  
    partnerships and implementation modalities for future humanitarian programming,  
    including ECHO HIP 2027.

## **Scope of Assessment**

The assessment will focus on selected conflict-, displacement- and epidemic-affected areas in  
eastern DRC and analyse:

- Needs and reintegration challenges of returnees.
- Opportunities for integrated multi-sector programming and referral pathways.
- Capacities of local actors, including OPDs, local NGOs and community-based  
    organisations.
- Community feedback systems, communication preferences and accountability  
    mechanisms.
- Humanitarian access constraints and operational feasibility.
- Community preparedness, surveillance and early warning systems.
- Environmental and climate-related risks affecting humanitarian programming.  
    Geographic scope :
- North Kivu (Masisi, Beni, Lubero)
- South Kivu (Kalehe)
- Mai-Ndombe (Kwamouth)

### *Thematic scope :*

The assessment should analyse current and emerging humanitarian needs, service gaps and  
trends affecting programming in 2027, including:

- Humanitarian needs and vulnerabilities.
- Access barriers to services and assistance.
- Availability and functionality of services and referral mechanisms.
- Areas and population groups with the highest unmet needs.
- Implications for future ECHO and other donor-funded interventions.

### *Key minimum sectors :*

- Health (+MHPSS)
- Protection
- GBV
- Food Security
- Education
- Nutrition
- WASH
- Disaster Preparedness (+Epidemic and Health Risks)

### *Cross-cutting themes*

- Disability Inclusion
- Gender and Age
- Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP)
- Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)
- Safeguarding and Child Safeguarding
- Protection Principles and Do No Harm
- Localisation and Community Engagement
- Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus

### *Priority Population Groups*

- IDPs
- Returnees
- Host Communities
- Women and Girls
- Children and Adolescents
- Older Persons
- Persons with Disabilities

## **Expected Methodology**

The consultant shall propose a mixed-method approach including:

- Secondary data review.
- Quantitative household surveys.
- KIIs.
- FGDs.
- Stakeholder consultations.
- Analysis of existing response capacities and gaps.
- Direct observation of selected services and community structures where feasible.

The methodology must ensure meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and comply  
with humanitarian principles, safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent, protection and Do  
No Harm standards.

## **Expected Deliverables**

The selected consultant/team will be expected to provide:

1. Inception Report, including methodology and workplan;
2. Data collection tools and protocols;
3. Preliminary findings presentation;
4. Draft MSNA Report;
5. Final MSNA Report incorporating feedback;
6. Executive Summary;
7. Strategic recommendations for ECHO HIP 2027 and future programming, and integrated  
    response options.
8. Clean dataset and related assessment materials;
9. PowerPoint presentation of key findings.
10. Situational statistics on population movement (displaced or returned) in the assessment  
    areas

## **Duration**

The consultancy is expected to be conducted between October and December 2026.  
The anticipated level of effort is approximately 40 working days.

jobs.title: Area Manager, Tana River County
jobs.body:
**Job Title:** Area Manager

**Reports to:** Programme Coordinator

**Job Location:** Tana River

**Contract Details:** Fixed Term

**Salary Range:** Kes 299,930 per month

**About Concern:** Established in 1968, Concern is a non-profit, non-governmental humanitarian organisation, dedicated to the reduction of suffering and the ultimate elimination of extreme poverty in the world’s poorest countries.

Concern’s vision, our mission and our work are all defined by one goal – ending extreme poverty, whatever it takes. Concern strives for a world free from poverty, fear and oppression.

Our culture is values driven and we believe that our people are central to all that we do and are key to delivering on our goal of Reaching the Furthest Behind First. We are committed to ensuring a workplace where everybody feels valued and are enabled to succeed in their work and contribute to delivering on our mission.

**Job Purpose:**

The Area Manager is responsible for leading Concern’s projects in Tana River County. This responsibility covers programme delivery including coordination, programme planning and overseeing the day-to-day operations of field staff and supporting the operational functions (human resources, logistics, finance & administration, staff safety and security). In fulfilling these responsibilities, the Area Manager will work closely with the Programme Coordinator and Programme Director to ensure that the programmes are carried out in line with Concern’s policies and procedures. The Area Manager serves as Concern’s senior representative at the County level, providing leadership in external engagement and coordination with key stakeholders. Working in close partnership with the Programme Coordinator (PC) and Programme Director (PD), the Area Manager contributes to strategic planning, monitors programme performance, and identifies opportunities for scale-up or adaptation in response to emerging needs and contextual changes while providing technical support towards toward quality and timely implementation of programs. S/he will be responsible for developing the quarterly work plans, strengthening the capacity of the officers (Livelihoods, Health and Nutrition, Monitoring Evaluation Learning (MEL)and Governance & Advocacy) and leading the monitoring and documentation of all projects in the county.

**Programme Cycle Management**

- Provide leadership in implementation of the programs in Tana River County ensuring projects are executed in line with relevant strategies and donor guidelines. This also includes holding projects inception and planning meeting with County teams for effective implementation.
- Prepare and implement County specific program annual and quarterly implementation costed workplans that correspond to the approved donor proposals and budgets and update these on a timely basis.
- Prepare and share recruitment and procurement plans with HR and Logistics colleagues, and update these on a timely basis.
- Work closely with other Concern program teams and implementing partners to foster layering, sequencing and integration of various interventions towards desired outcomes.
- Timely initiate all program activities in line with the relevant program documents to ensure all planned activities are completed within set timelines and program commitments
- Support cross-sectoral periodic programme reviews to assess programme progress, capture lessons learnt and adapt programme strategies as necessary in accordance with Concern’s results-based management principles. Ensure mainstreaming of cross-cutting issues/approaches throughout the programme cycle including Accountability to Affected Population, Gender, Protection, Conflict Sensitivity, Accountability and do no harm philosophy.
- Ensure the local authorities and communities are meaningfully engaged in programme development in line with the Core Humanitarian Standards initiative and best practices.
- Support community entry process for all the projects implemented in Tana River, ensuring the project priority is aligned to community needs to strengthen existing capacities
- In collaboration with program Technical Advisors, develop, continuously review and adapt implementation strategies for various program approaches such as Climate smart agriculture, Village savings and Loans associations, value chain development, business development services, Market based approaches, Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM) Community Health Strategy, etc.
- Working closely with the program coordinators, Technical Advisors and County based project team, ensure program adaptation to the prevailing contextual changes to ensure relevance to the local needs.
- Actively promote intersectoral linkages such as Gender, Equality, Conflict and Peace, Protection, HIV and AIDS, Disaster Risk Reduction, Environment, Climate Change Adaptation, and Partnerships where relevant
- Contribute to development of donor proposals and budgets ensuring that all direct and indirect costs are fully and accurately budgeted.
- Work effectively with the support functions (operations and finance) to ensure that the programme, finance, HR and logistics needs are planned and met.

**Team Management**

- Line manages direct reports, contributing to their capacity building and career development through technical support and on-the-job training and coaching, including a thorough induction at the start of their contract.
- Provide technical mentorship to the officers(s) and including identification of capacity gaps and support in addressing them for effective implementation of the County program.
- Ensure that all department positions have accurate job descriptions and that each member of the team fully understands outcomes which are expected of them, by setting SMART objectives, and that they are aware of the success criteria relating to their work.
- Make recommendations on core staffing needs and training/capacity building needs for Tana River programmes and support in consultation with the PC.
- Develop, monitor and review performance development plans of all the staff reporting to him/her and hold staff accountable to meet their success criteria; give corrective feedback where required and take decisive action in the case of poor performance.
- Ensure that all department staff are aware of and comply with all of Concern’s policies and procedures.
- Ensure that work within the team(s) is planned and organized in a way which will meet the organization’s needs in the most cost-effective manner possible; ensuring that team members are given appropriate workloads and are working efficiently.

**Budget management**

- Monitor programme expenditures and budgets and work with Programme Officers and the PC to ensure optimal resource utilisation and spending in accordance with Concern's financial procedures and donor requirements.
- Monitor and report delegated program budgets against the costed work plan ensuring 100% completion of planned quarterly activities with >90% expenditure
- Review monthly management account reports from Finance to ensure that expenditure is being accurately recorded and to avoid any under- or over-spends
- Ensure all expenditure is authorized and spent in accordance with Concern’s internal procedures.
- Ensure the allocated budget is utilized effectively, and any necessary adjustments are requested in a timely manner.

**Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning**

- Develop a comprehensive detailed implementation plan for the project, oversee its implementation and undertake regular review and update on the progress.
- Initiate programme activities on time to deliver planned outputs within agreed timelines and commitments.
- Proactively provide capacity support in all the program evaluation exercises such as program participants registration, baseline/midline and end line surveys, post distribution monitoring exercise etc.
- Spend at least 50% of time visiting project sites with field visit reports prepared at the end of every monitoring trip.
- Participation in relevant monthly and quarterly review meetings and organizing similar progress review meetings at County level.
- Organizing and participating in field visits by donors and other technical support staff.
- Lead documentation of Tana River programming through development of success stories and program briefs

**Reporting and Donor Compliance**

- Support the timely submission of internal monthly and donor reports as per the grants/funding tracker
- Work with the Program Director and Program Coordinator to ensure the timely and high-quality development of programme proposals and concept notes for donors and other interested parties, including government departments.
- Ensure the timely production of high-quality annual reports, including reporting on PEER and CHS.

**Representation & Networking**

- Establishing and maintaining strong relationships with peer NGOs, County government staff and communities with whom we work.
- Participate regularly in County Steering Group, sectoral working groups and other relevant coordination meetings.
- Share information with other actors (other NGOs, UN agencies, private sector etc) for effective coordination and cooperation

**Responding to Emergencies**

- Participating and contributing towards Concern’s emergency response, as and when necessary
- Complying with Concern’s health, safety and security guidelines during emergencies

**Others**

- Adhere to and promote the standards outlined in the Concern Code of Conduct and associated policies to their team, program participants, and be committed to providing a safe working environment
- Working closely with Concern CRM and accountability officer, support in addressing all the complaints, response and feedback issues related to the program.
- Actively participate in collective exercises such as preparation or updates of Preparing for Effective Emergency Response (PEER) plan, Security Management Plan (SMP) and other Concern initiatives.
- Ensure the highest stands of accountability through ensuring good communication and information sharing within and outside the organisation.
- Contribute to security assessments for the County, monitoring and providing and/or advising security situation in the County and reporting of all security incidents on the Security Incident Reporting Tool (SIRT)
- Actively participate in any emergency response if called upon to do so (within the existing programme area or in a new one).
- All managers are responsible for upholding and promoting Concern’s values, demonstrating leadership on workplace equality, diversity and inclusion, and role modelling a positive safeguarding ethos.
- Managing administrative aspect such as office, vehicles and stores for smooth running of the office
- Undertake other related duties as may reasonably be assigned by the line manager.

**Role Holder Requirements:**

**Minimum Education, Qualifications & Experience Required:**

- A Bachelor’s degree in either of the following: Agriculture Economics, Agronomy, Agri-business Management, Environmental Science, Disaster Management, or any other relevant field.
- At least five (5) years’ experience implementing multi-sectoral projects with livelihoods, nutrition, WASH, community empowerment, Climatic resilience themes.
- Demonstrable experience in market-based approaches in livelihoods programming including Cash and Voucher Assistance, Value chain development, Enterprise and SME development, private sector partnerships and financial inclusion
- At least three (3) years’ experience in budget management.
- Proven experience and knowledge of Project Cycle Management, Climate Smart Agriculture, Community Managed Disaster Risk Reduction, WASH, Natural Resource, Management, Value chain development and Market Systems Development.
- Experience in rural community development and empowerment
- Experience in management of a diverse team of staff.
- Fluency in spoken and written language in English and Swahili
- Good computing and report writing skills

**Preference will be given to candidates who have:**

- High integrity and demonstrated ability to follow standards and policies
- Ability to work in a systematic and organized manner
- Ability to work under pressure and adhere to deadlines
- Energy to work long hours and be out in the field all day
- Analytical Skills - critical thinking & Data analysis.
- In-depth understanding of procedures with strong technical knowledge.
- Be able to work independently, as well as in a team
- Be willing to accept responsibility and to show good judgment, initiative, and resourcefulness
- Strong planning, leadership and management skills

**Important information:**

Concern has an organisational **Code of Conduct** supported by three Associated Policies: The **Programme Participant Protection Policy, the Child Safeguarding Policy, and the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Policy** accessible [here](https://www.concern.net/accountability/codes-and-policies/safeguarding). These have been designed to ensure the highest level of protection for everyone the organization engages through its work.

The policies set out the behaviours and responsibilities that Concern staff, and all its representatives (including consultants, contractors, sub-contractors, suppliers, partners, visitors, ambassadors and Board members) are expected to uphold. They also articulate Concern’s commitment to safeguarding and protecting adults and children from harm in all aspects of our work. We will therefore do everything possible to ensure that only those who are suitable to work or volunteer with adults and children are recruited by us for such roles. Consequently, working or volunteering with Concern may be subject to a range of vetting checks, including criminal background checking.

In this context, all staff and representatives of Concern have a responsibility to uphold the highest standards in their work, in accordance with Concern’s core values and mission. Any candidate offered a job with Concern Worldwide will be expected to sign the Concern Staff Code of Conduct and Associated Policies as an appendix to their contract of employment. By signing the Concern Code of Conduct, candidates acknowledge that they have understood the content of both the Concern Code of Conduct and the Associated Policies and agree to conduct themselves in accordance with the provisions of these policies.

jobs.title: Trainer for Youth Capacity Development in Conflict Analysis, Peacebuilding and Community Dialogue
jobs.body:
## 1. Background

Terre des Hommes Italia (TDH Italy) supports children, young people, families and communities in Syria through education, protection, inclusion and social cohesion programmes.

As part of its social cohesion work, TDH Italy intends to strengthen young people’s ability to understand conflict dynamics, design contextually relevant peacebuilding interventions, and plan and facilitate inclusive community dialogue. The training will combine practical knowledge with opportunities to apply skills through exercises, simulations and group work relevant to participants’ communities.

TDH Italy seeks an individual trainer to develop and deliver two complementary training programmes in Aleppo, Latakia and Idlib:

- Understanding Conflict and Designing Peacebuilding Interventions.
- Designing and Implementing Community Dialogue Processes.

## 2. Purpose of the Consultancy

The consultancy will equip participating young people with practical knowledge, skills and tools to analyse community tensions, identify opportunities for cooperation, develop conflict-sensitive peacebuilding interventions, and design and facilitate safe and inclusive community dialogue processes.

## 3. Objectives

- Strengthen participants’ understanding of conflict dynamics, causes, actors and effects.
- Develop their ability to apply conflict analysis tools to community situations.
- Support the design of realistic peacebuilding interventions informed by analysis and the principle of do no harm.
- Strengthen skills in planning, facilitating and reviewing community dialogue processes.
- Promote inclusive participation, respectful communication and constructive engagement with different perspectives.
- Enable participants to demonstrate their learning through practical group assignments and facilitation exercises.

## 4. Scope of Work and Key Tasks

### 4.1 Inception and planning

The trainer will

- Attend an inception meeting with TDH Italy to confirm participant profiles, learning needs, delivery arrangements and expected results.
- Prepare a detailed workplan covering preparation, delivery, assessment and reporting within the assignment period.
- Propose the sequence and dates of the eight courses, allowing adequate time for travel, preparation and review.
- Clarify in the technical proposal whether the two training programmes will follow a complementary approach for the same participants or be delivered as separate programmes for different target groups, specifying the rationale and any sequencing requirements.
- Agree daily training hours and accessibility requirements with TDH Italy before implementation.

### 4.2 Training design and preparation

- Develop two distinct training programmes with clear learning objectives, session plans, exercises and practical outputs.
- Prepare training materials in Arabic, including presentations, participant handouts, worksheets and assessment tools.
- Adapt language, examples and exercises to young people’s experience and the contexts of Aleppo, Latakia and Idlib.
- Design participatory activities that allow participants to practise analysis, intervention design and dialogue facilitation.
- Submit materials for TDH Italy’s review before delivery and incorporate agreed feedback.

### 4.3 Training delivery

The trainer will deliver the following courses:

- **Conflict Analysis and peacebuilding**: 2 in Aleppo, 1 in Latakia, 1 in Idleb
- **Community Dialogue:** 2 in Aleppo, 1 in Latakia, 1 in Idleb

For a total of 4 courses in Aleppo, 2 in Latakia and 2 in Idleb

Each course will accommodate approximately 20–25 participants.

The trainer will:

- Facilitate all eight courses in person.
- Use practical exercises, simulations, case studies, group work and structured reflection.
- Establish shared ground rules supporting dignity, confidentiality and respectful participation.
- Manage sensitive discussions impartially and respond appropriately to group tensions.
- Adapt delivery to participants’ learning needs while maintaining the agreed objectives.
- Coordinate with TDH Italy’s field teams on attendance, delivery arrangements and emerging concerns.

### 4.4 Assessment and learning review

- Prepare baseline and endline assessments appropriate to each programme, and conduct the assessment in coordination with TDH filed staff
- Assess practical skills through group assignments, presentations and observed simulations.
- In coordination with TDH filed staff, collect participant feedback on relevance, accessibility and training quality.
- Review learning after each course and make agreed improvements to subsequent delivery where needed.
- Document learning achievements and areas requiring further support without making unsupported claims about wider community impact.

### 4.5 Reporting and handover

- Submit a report for each course documenting delivery, participation, assessment findings, practical outputs and recommendations.
- Submit a consolidated final report in both Arabic and English covering all eight courses.
- Provide editable versions of the final training materials, tools and reports.

## 5. Minimum Technical Coverage

Applicants should propose a coherent agenda for each programme covering, at minimum, the following areas:

### 5.1 Understanding Conflict and Designing Peacebuilding Interventions

- Core concepts of conflict, peacebuilding and social cohesion.
- Conflict causes, dynamics, escalation and opportunities for constructive change.
- Practical tools for analysing conflict, stakeholders, relationships and power.
- Identification of factors that divide communities and factors that support cooperation.
- Conflict sensitivity and the interaction between interventions and their context.
- Translating analysis into realistic intervention objectives and activities.
- Participation, inclusion, risk management and do-no-harm considerations.
- Basic results chains, monitoring indicators and learning arrangements.
- Practical development and presentation of a peacebuilding intervention concept.

### 5.2 Designing and Implementing Community Dialogue Processes

- Purpose, scope and limitations of community dialogue.
- Assessing whether dialogue is appropriate for a particular issue or context.
- Stakeholder mapping and inclusive participant engagement.
- Defining dialogue objectives, structure, ground rules and facilitation arrangements.
- Active listening, questioning, respectful communication and management of disagreement.
- Managing participation imbalances, sensitive issues and challenging group dynamics.
- Safety, confidentiality, informed participation and conflict sensitivity.
- Documenting outcomes, identifying agreed actions and planning follow-up.
- Practical development of a dialogue process plan and facilitation simulations.

## 6. Expected Deliverables

1. **Inception note an detailed workplan:** Understanding of the assignment; methodology; proposed course schedule; preparation, delivery and reporting days; coordination and accessibility arrangements (timing: Before training delivery)
2. **Two complete training packages:** session plans; presentations; handouts; exercises; practical assignment templates; assessment and feedback tools (timing: Before the first delivery of each programme)
3. **Eight completed courses:** Delivery of all courses according to the approved plan, totalling training days (timing: within implementation period)
4. **Eight course reports:** Delivery summary; attendance records coordinated with TDH Italy; assessment findings; participant feedback; practical outputs; challenges and recommendations (timing: Following each course, according to the approved workplan)
5. **Consolidated final report and material handover:** Summary of delivery and learning across all locations; recommendations; final editable training materials and tools (timing: by mid-February 2027)

**Note:** All deliverables are subject to TDH Italy’s review and written acceptance. Applicants must propose delivery dates in their technical offer and confirm them in the approved workplan

## 7. Methodological and Quality Requirements

The trainer will:

- Apply a participatory approach appropriate to young people.
- Balance conceptual learning with substantial practical application.
- Use clear, respectful and non-stigmatising Arabic.
- Promote equitable participation across genders, backgrounds and abilities.
- Coordinate reasonable adaptations with TDH Italy to support participants with disabilities.
- Apply neutrality, conflict sensitivity and do-no-harm principles throughout delivery.
- Avoid requiring participants to disclose personal experiences of violence, trauma or sensitive affiliations.
- Use anonymised or fictionalised cases where disclosure could create risks.
- Distinguish training exercises from actual mediation or resolution of community disputes.
- Comply with TDH Italy’s safeguarding, code of conduct, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, confidentiality and data protection requirements.

## 8. Management, Coordination and Responsibilities:

The trainer will report to the TDH Italy Project Manager and coordinate delivery with designated field focal points.

**TDH Italy will:**

- Arrange training venues, agreed equipment, refreshments and printing of approved materials.
- Coordinate local logistics and provide relevant information on participant needs.
- Review the workplan, materials and deliverables.
- Support attendance monitoring and communicate applicable safeguarding procedures.

**The trainer will:**

- Support with selection and mobilising participants.
- Prepare and deliver both programmes and complete the agreed assessment and reporting.
- Identify equipment and printing requirements sufficiently in advance.
- Include travel and accommodation costs required for the assignment in the financial proposal.
- Maintain regular coordination with TDH Italy and promptly report issues affecting delivery.

Changes to the agreed scope, locations, course numbers or deliverables require prior written agreement.

## 9. Duration, Location and Indicative Level of Effort

Implementation will take place from mid-October 2026 to mid-February 2027.

The contract will cover training delivery days across Aleppo, Latakia and Idlib. All preparation, coordination, assessment, reporting and travel requirements must be included in the proposed daily rate and total contract price. Applicants must submit their financial offer based on implementation days only, with no additional billable days for these tasks.

The final schedule will be agreed with TDH Italy, taking account of participant availability and operational arrangements.

## 10. Required Qualifications and Experience

Applicants should demonstrate:

- A relevant university qualification in peace and conflict studies, social sciences, community development or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
- Practical experience in conflict analysis, peacebuilding and community dialogue.
- Demonstrated experience designing and delivering participatory training for young people.
- Experience facilitating sensitive discussions and managing diverse group dynamics.
- Understanding of the Syrian context and ability to adapt training to local community realities.
- Ability to develop clear training materials and assess practical learning.
- Excellent spoken and written Arabic.
- Availability to deliver the full assignment and travel to all three governorates.

Experience in peacebuilding, inclusion, safeguarding and work with humanitarian or civil society organisations will be considered an asset.

## 11. Evaluation Criteria

- **Technical proposal:** Understanding of the assignment, quality of methodology, agendas, practical learning and assessment (30% weight)
- **Relevant experience**: Conflict analysis, peacebuilding, community dialogue and youth training (25% weight)
- **Contextual knowledge and delivery capacity:** Understanding of the Syrian context and ability to deliver in all three governorates (10% weight)
- **Qualifications and work samples:** Relevant qualifications and quality of submitted materials (5% weight)
- **Financial proposal**: Cost-effectiveness, completeness and clarity (30% weight)

## 12. Payment Schedule

Payments will be linked to the satisfactory completion and written acceptance of the following deliverables by TDH Italy. Percentages apply to the total agreed contract price.

- 20%: Acceptance of Deliverable 1 and 2: Inception note and detailed workplan and two complete training packages
- 30%: Completion and acceptance of the first four courses and their four course reports under Deliverables 3 and 4, representing 50% of the training delivery.
- 30%: Completion and acceptance of the remaining four courses and their four course reports under Deliverables 3 and 4, bringing training delivery to 100%.
- 20%: Acceptance of Deliverable 5: Consolidated final report and material handover

## 13. Ownership, Confidentiality and Ethical Obligations

- Materials and reports developed specifically under the assignment will be handed over to TDH Italy in editable formats.
- Any pre-existing or third-party materials must be identified, appropriately acknowledged and authorised for the intended use.
- The trainer must protect participants’ personal information and comply with agreed consent, confidentiality and data protection procedures.
- Participant information, photographs and training outputs may not be published or shared externally without prior authorisation.
- The trainer must sign and comply with TDH Italy’s applicable ethical and safeguarding policies.
- Revisions needed to meet the approved scope and quality requirements are included in the agreed consultancy fee.

jobs.title: Country Representative
jobs.body:
Habitat for Humanity is looking for “**Country Representative**” that serves as primary country focal point of Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) and external representative in Jordan and is a key member of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) leadership structure.

**1.Introduction and background:**

**Habitat for Humanity (HFH)** is an international nonprofit organization founded in 1976 as the world’s leader in addressing the housing challenges faced by vulnerable communities. Currently it operates in more than 60 countries around the world and brings people together to build more prosperous and vibrant communities by making sure everyone has a safe, affordable place to call home. Since its founding in 1976, it has helped more than 62 million people globally build their futures on their own terms through access to decent housing. HFH works alongside people of all walks of life to build, repair and finance their homes, by innovating new ways of building and financing, and by advocating for policies that make constructing and accessing housing easier for everyone.

HFHI works through a broad network of national Habitat organizations and other strategic partners, such as corporations, financial service providers, individuals, non-governmental organizations, foundations, local governments, as well as the private sector actors. HFHI supports program and project implementation by national HFH organizations and directly implements some projects and programs regionally. HFH started operating in Jordan in 1989 and has supported more than 48,000 households in 6 governorates across Jordan to improve their housing conditions in partnership with strategic local partners and community members.

**2. Position Description:**

The Country Representative (CR) reports to MENA Hub Director and supports the Director in identifying and nurturing relationships with country-based donors, local authorities, development partners, and target communities, all within the framework of HFHI’s regional and global strategies. Under the guidance of the MENA Hub Director, the CR is also responsible for leading country-level fundraising and resource mobilization efforts, while positioning HFHI as a housing thought leader in national dialogues and debates.

While the CR is also expected to deliver on standard country management tasks such as operational planning, financial and risk management, compliance, and safeguarding, our newly integrated model and structure require daily collaboration with MENA Hub staff on all the above.

The CR collaborates closely with thematic leads enabling and facilitating their technical leadership, and supports program managers in delivering against agreed objectives, embracing a people-centric approach.

**3.Scope of work and deliverables:**

**Strategic Alignment and Country Planning:**

1. Support overall strategic leadership for HFHI’s engagement in Jordan aligning country goals and plans with the MENA Strategy and HFHI global priorities.
2. Working closely with thematic leads to incorporating strategies and priorities into the overall country strategy, ensuring country plans reflect and operationalize agreed thematic approaches.
3. Support the annual country planning and budgeting process (for HFHI-funded work in-country), under the guidance of the MENA Hub Director and relevant Hub teams and monitor performance against approved plans.
4. Conduct regular country-level risk reviews, maintain a country risk register, develop mitigation plans, and escalate high/ “red” risks to the MENA Hub Director.

**Operation, Finance, Governance and Compliance:**

1. Oversee HFHI’s operational footprint in Jordan (offices, staff, contracts, and major activities), ensuring effective and efficient use of resources and compliance with HFHI standards, donor requirements and local legislation.
2. Ensure day-to-day operational compliance, local registration, and risk monitoring.
3. Provide day-to-day administrative line management for country-based staff, including leave approvals, budget oversight related to country operations, and coordination of operational support in line with HFH policies and procedures.
4. Ensure HFHI complies with all relevant registration, licensing, tax, and regulatory requirements in Jordan, working closely with the MENA Hub, Legal and Finance teams.
5. Enforce the Code of Conduct, Conflict of Interest, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies, ensuring they are understood and applied in day-to-day operations and partnerships.
6. Oversee basic financial management and internal controls for HFHI operations in-country, including oversight of budgets, expenditures, and financial reporting to the MENA Hub
7. Ensure procurement, contracting and vendor management for HFHI activities in Jordan comply with HFHI and donor policies, and that value for money, transparency and fairness are upheld.
8. Implement and oversee HFHI global safety and security standards for all HFHI staff, consultants, and visitors in-country, including maintaining country security plans, contact trees and incident protocols.
9. Ensure prompt reporting, investigation and follow-up of safeguarding and security incidents in line with HFHI policies and national law.
10. Coordinate external and internal audits related to HFHI’s country presence and support the timely closure of audit findings and implementation of management actions.

**Program Implementation Oversight, Resources mobilization and Partnership:**

1. Support local funding opportunities relevant to Jordan (institutional donors, multilaterals, private sector, foundations, etc.) and share intelligence with the MENA Hub.
2. Network and coalition building.
3. Support the development of country-level concept notes and project proposals, and support HFHI’s participation in multi-country or regional proposals that include Jordan.
4. Support the identification, scoping and design of quality projects in Jordan, aligned with HFHI’s priorities and in collaboration with the MENA Hub Subject Matter Experts (SMEs)
5. Map and engage potential donors, partners, and stakeholders in Jordan (government, private sector, financial service providers, civil society, faith organizations, academia, UN and other international actors)
6. Maintain a country partnership mapping and engagement tracker, including pipelines, contacts and agreed follow-up actions.
7. Facilitate the negotiation of country-level Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) and partnership agreements, in coordination with the MENA Hub, Legal Programs and Finance.

**Advocacy, Policy Engagement & External Representation:**

1. In coordination with the MENA Hub Director and HFHI Advocacy teams, support the development and implementation of a national advocacy and policy engagement plan aligned with regional advocacy priorities (e.g. housing policy, housing finance, urban development, resilience).
2. From an advocacy perspective, supports building and maintaining relationships with government counterparts, donors, United Nations (UN) agencies, European Union (EU) delegations, financial institutions, sector networks, civil society organizations, and other policy stakeholders at country level.
3. Represent HFHI in national forums, sector working groups, donor coordination platforms and, where appropriate, media opportunities, positioning HFHI as a credible housing and urban development actor in Jordan.
4. Support the development and implementation of a country communications approach that promotes HFHI’s brand, programs and advocacy messaging, and provides content for regional and global communications.
5. Ensuring advocacy and communication efforts are evidence-based, reflecting learning and impact from HFHI-supported programs and partnerships in Jordan.

**People Leadership, Culture and Volunteer Engagement:**

1. Provide direction, support to any HFH staff and consultants based in Jordan, fostering a culture of accountability, inclusion, learning and safeguarding.
2. In collaboration with Regional Human Resources (HR), support recruitment, onboarding, performance management and development of country-based staff and key consultants, as applicable.
3. Model and promote HFHI’s values and commitments to safeguarding, diversity, equity and inclusion in all country-level interactions and decisions.
4. Where applicable, support planning and hosting of HFHI-associated volunteer builds and events in Jordan, ensuring that they are safe, ethical, and aligned with HFHI standards and community priorities.
5. Ensure volunteer activities comply with safeguarding and duty-of-care standards, and that relevant stories and data are captured for visibility and fundraising purposes.

**4.Required Skills & Competencies:**

1. Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, combined with substantial professional experience in international development, organizational leadership, or a related area. An advanced degree is an asset.
2. Experience:
    - 7-10 years of progressively responsible experience in international development, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership or management role.
    - Experience with traditional and emerging institutional donors including the Gulf countries.
    - Proven experience in resource mobilization including donor engagement and proposal development.
    - Experience managing diverse teams remotely.
    - A proven track record of both winning and executing multimillion projects.
    - Extensive experience working in Jordan's international development sector, with a strong understanding of the local operating environment, stakeholder landscape, and partnership networks.
    - Ability to adapt a changing environment and navigating market turbulences.
    - Management of teams and experience operating in a matrix structure.
    - Excellent written and spoken English and Arabic language.
    - Experience working with private philanthropy is an asset.
    - Previous experience in a hub structure is a plus.
3. Active support for **HFHI Values**:

**Humility** – We are part of something bigger than ourselves,

**Courage** – We do what’s right, even when it is difficult or unpopular,

**Accountability** – We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission),

***Safeguarding:***

*HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work*

*Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct).*

jobs.title: Consultor Experto en Diseño de Ejercicios y Preparación ante Crisis
jobs.body:
## Términos de Referencia (TdR)

**Título**: **Consultoría –** Consultor Experto en Diseño de Ejercicios y Preparación ante Crisis

**Fecha en que se emite la convocatoria**: 30 de septiembre de 2026

**Fecha de cierre**:30 de octubre de 2026

**Mecanismo de contratación**: Consultoría

**1.ANTECEDENTES**

La Fundación Panamericana para el Desarrollo (PADF) busca crear un hemisferio justo, pacífico y próspero donde todas las personas tengan la oportunidad de prosperar. Trabajamos con personas vulnerables en todo el hemisferio para abordar algunos de los mayores desafíos de desarrollo de nuestra región. Nos asociamos, empoderamos y capacitamos a la sociedad civil, los gobiernos y el sector privado para el bien mayor de los pueblos de América Latina y el Caribe.

**VISIÓN**

Fortalecer la preparación y capacidad de coordinación de las instituciones civiles panameñas para anticipar, gestionar y responder de manera articulada a crisis que puedan afectar la continuidad y resiliencia del Canal de Panamá y su infraestructura crítica. A través de un ciclo progresivo de ejercicios, aprendizaje y mejora, la consultoría contribuirá a consolidar capacidades institucionales sostenibles y a desarrollar un marco conjunto de preparación y respuesta ante crisis.

**Descripción de la posición**

Como parte de la implementación de CANAL READY – Strengthening Panama Canal Crisis Preparedness and Response, un programa de 24 meses orientado a fortalecer las capacidades de las autoridades civiles panameñas para prepararse, coordinar y responder ante amenazas físicas, cibernéticas, geopolíticas y ambientales que puedan afectar el Canal de Panamá y la infraestructura crítica asociada, PADF contratará a un/a Líder Senior de Diseño de Ejercicios y Preparación ante Crisis, con base en la Ciudad de Panamá.

La supervisión técnica, programática y operativa de la consultoría estará a cargo del área temática de Paz, Justicia y Seguridad (PJS), con sede en Washington, D.C. Para facilitar una adecuada implementación y articulación a nivel país, el consultor/a requerirá coordinación con la oficina nacional de PADF en Panamá.

**2. ESPECIFICACIONES**

**Objetivos de la consultoría**

Brindar servicios técnicos especializados para diseñar, preparar, facilitar, evaluar y documentar ejercicios y actividades de fortalecimiento de capacidades que contribuyan a mejorar la coordinación interinstitucional ante amenazas físicas, cibernéticas, geopolíticas y ambientales que puedan afectar el Canal de Panamá y la infraestructura crítica circundante.

### Alcances:

- Diseñar una metodología integral para el ciclo de ejercicios, incluyendo diagnóstico de capacidades, definición de objetivos, desarrollo de escenarios, validación técnica, preparación de participantes, ejecución, evaluación, informe posterior y plan de mejora.
- Realizar consultas, revisión documental y análisis de amenazas, vulnerabilidades, capacidades, dependencias y consecuencias relacionadas con el Canal de Panamá y la infraestructura crítica circundante, incluidos puentes, represas, carreteras, ferrocarriles, plantas eléctricas y líneas de transmisión.
- Diseñar ejercicios de mesa, simulaciones, escenarios y otras actividades apropiadas para autoridades civiles de nivel medio y superior, de acuerdo con los objetivos, resultados e indicadores del proyecto.
- Desarrollar los materiales técnicos requeridos para cada ejercicio, incluyendo situaciones iniciales, eventos, líneas de tiempo, preguntas de decisión, mapas de actores, matrices de roles, guías de facilitación, manuales de participantes, instrumentos de observación y criterios de evaluación.
- Incorporar en los escenarios amenazas físicas, cibernéticas, geopolíticas y ambientales, así como efectos en cascada, dependencias intersectoriales y necesidades de coordinación bilateral e interinstitucional.
- Asegurar, en el marco de los servicios contratados, que los escenarios desarrollados se mantengan dentro del alcance civil autorizado por el proyecto y no constituyan capacitación, asistencia operativa ni apoyo prohibido para fuerzas militares o policiales.
- Facilitar técnicamente los ejercicios y actividades programadas, manteniendo el enfoque en toma de decisiones, coordinación, comunicación, continuidad de operaciones y recuperación.
- Preparar sesiones de orientación para facilitadores, evaluadores y participantes sobre objetivos, supuestos, roles, reglas de participación, confidencialidad y criterios de desempeño.
- Facilitar y apoyar técnicamente los procesos de validación técnica de escenarios y materiales con especialistas sectoriales y representantes institucionales autorizados, resguardando la información reservada o sensible.
- Diseñar y aplicar, en coordinación con el equipo de Monitoreo, Evaluación y Aprendizaje (MEL), instrumentos de evaluación pre y post actividad, rúbricas de observación, encuestas y otras herramientas para medir cambios en capacidades y coordinación.
- Conducir sesiones de retroalimentación posteriores a los ejercicios y elaborar informes con hallazgos, lecciones aprendidas, recomendaciones y acciones de mejora.
- Elaborar y actualizar una matriz consolidada de brechas de capacidad, buenas prácticas, lecciones aprendidas, acciones de mejora, responsables sugeridos y avances identificados.
- Brindar asesoría técnica respecto de los requisitos, secuencia metodológica, perfiles de participantes, recursos, riesgos y criterios de calidad aplicables a cada actividad.
- Proporcionar servicios técnicos especializados para desarrollar el contenido y los componentes técnicos del plan conjunto Facilitar la revisión técnica y validación del plan conjunto con las partes autorizadas, incorporando las lecciones obtenidas de los ejercicios y resguardando la información sensible.
- Preparar insumos técnicos para informes, presentaciones y reuniones del proyecto, cuando sean requeridos por PADF.

**Perfil Requerido:**

- Título universitario en gestión de emergencias, gestión de riesgos, seguridad, continuidad de operaciones, ingeniería, ciberseguridad, relaciones internacionales, políticas públicas o carreras afines. Se valorará maestría en áreas relacionadas.
- Mínimo diez (10) años de experiencia profesional en preparación y respuesta ante crisis, gestión de emergencias, continuidad de operaciones, resiliencia de infraestructura crítica o áreas afines.
- Mínimo diez (10) años de experiencia comprobable en diseño, facilitación y evaluación de ejercicios de mesa, simulaciones o ejercicios interinstitucionales para participantes de nivel medio y superior.
- Experiencia en desarrollo de escenarios multimodales, elaboración de informes posteriores a ejercicios, lecciones aprendidas y planes de mejora.
- Experiencia de trabajo con instituciones gubernamentales y equipos multidisciplinarios. Se valorará experiencia en Panamá o Centroamérica y conocimiento del Canal de Panamá o de sistemas de infraestructura crítica.
- Experiencia en al menos dos de las siguientes áreas: amenazas físicas, ciberseguridad o tecnología operacional, riesgos geopolíticos y amenazas ambientales.
- Dominio profesional del español e inglés, con capacidad para facilitar sesiones técnicas y elaborar productos de alta calidad en ambos idiomas.
- Se valorarán certificaciones en diseño de ejercicios, gestión de emergencias, continuidad del negocio, gestión de riesgos, ciberseguridad o metodologías equivalentes.

**Productos Esperados:**

- Plan de trabajo y metodología integral para el diseño, facilitación y evaluación de ejercicios.
- Diagnóstico técnico de amenazas, vulnerabilidades, capacidades, dependencias y brechas relevantes para el diseño de las actividades.
- Paquetes técnicos para cada ejercicio, incluyendo escenarios, guías de facilitación, manuales de participantes, matrices de roles, instrumentos de observación y criterios de evaluación.
- Informes posteriores a cada ejercicio, con hallazgos, lecciones aprendidas, recomendaciones y acciones de mejora.
- Matriz consolidada y actualizada de lecciones aprendidas, brechas de capacidad, buenas prácticas y avances.
- Borrador técnico del plan conjunto de preparación y respuesta ante crisis.
- Versión final validada del plan conjunto de preparación y respuesta ante crisis.
- Informe final de consultoría, con el resumen de actividades, productos entregados, resultados, riesgos y recomendaciones.

**Precio y Duración del contrato:**

- El costo del contrato es de USD $3,000 mensual. El periodo del contrato es de 11 meses con la posibilidad de una renovación de hasta 12 meses adicionales para el segundo año - sujeta a desempeño satisfactorio y disponibilidad de fondos.

**Forma de Pago:**

- Los pagos se realizarán de manera mensual contra entrega de informe de actividades y productos, previa aprobación técnica. Se incluirán los costos asociados a la impresión de materiales y actividades de divulgación.

**Lugar de Prestación del Servicio:**

Principalmente en Ciudad de Panamá con modalidad híbrida (presencial y remota) según las necesidades del servicio.

**3. CRITERIOS DE EVALUACIÓN**

**Criterios de elegibilidad - Puntuación (de 100)**

- Experiencia en diseño, facilitación y evaluación de ejercicios de mesa, simulaciones o ejercicios interinstitucionales - 30 puntos
- Experiencia en preparación y respuesta ante crisis, continuidad de operaciones, gestión de emergencias o resiliencia de infraestructura crítica - 30 puntos

**4. PROPIEDAD INTELECTUAL**

Al profesional le queda prohibido cualquier tipo de publicación, divulgación o comercialización de los productos objeto de esta contratación pues se entenderá que pasará a ser propiedad de PADF, de la misma forma le queda prohibida la divulgación de información confidencial que llegue a su conocimiento como parte de la ejecución de sus actividades.
