jobs.title: Regional Humanitarian Access and Safety Adviser (Colombia, Venezuela, Honduras nationals)
jobs.body:
All NRC employees are expected to work in accordance with the organization’s values. To be dedicated, innovative, inclusive and accountable are attitudes and beliefs that shall guide our actions and relationships. NRC has a commitment to safety and wellbeing and together we build a positive working culture to feel valued, empowered, supported, safe and have a sense of belonging. NRC does not tolerate employees exploiting or abusing people and has zero tolerance to inaction.

## What we are looking for

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking a **highly qualified,** **resilient, and dynamic professional** to take up the role of **Regional Security Adviser for Latin America**. This role is responsible for **developing, evaluating and monitoring NRC’s regional security risk management approach in accordance with global standards, with an overall objective to enable the delivery of a safe and principled humanitarian response.**

While NRC has largely been successful with regards to delivering assistance to people in need, security and access constraints pose a challenge to humanitarian operations across the region. Conflict and violence, environmental and physical challenges, bureaucratic obstacles, interference in humanitarian operations, are all obstacles to delivery of services and protection to displacement affected people. **The Regional HAS Adviser plays a fundamental role in security risk management, in capacity building of HAS colleagues and country management, as well as in operationalizing Duty of Care and humanitarian access strategies across the region.**

## What you will do

- Promote and stimulate a culture of enabling a safe and principled humanitarian response, in line with the Humanitarian Principles and taking Programme Criticality into account.
- Ensure quality recruitment, induction, guidance, support, mentoring, capacity building, and development of HAS staff in the country offices to strengthen operational leadership.
- Maintain a detailed understanding of the context within the region, including analysis and forecasting, and brief regional management on key security developments, access impediments, and emerging threats within the region. Work with management to ensure that the relevant mitigation measures are in place.
- In collaboration with People & Organisation, the Regional Head of Operational Support and the Regional Director, ensure Duty of Care standards are upheld, reflecting the diversity of the NRC workforce in the region.
- Provide technical review of HAS management documents for all countries in the region to ensure they comply with NRC standards, including Security Risk Assessments (SRA), Contingency Planning, Medical Emergency Plan, and Hibernation, Evacuation and Relocation Plans.
- Technically support the development and implementation of access strategies across the region, ensuring a systematized approach to engagement.

Please download the [detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCKG0SB_f8mQ7MFr7J3vCnMAQZ0PuLW-2rmcy7PXsd-7ME?e=636y5s)to learn more about the position.

What you will bring

- **Minimum five years of experience from working as a manager in a humanitarian/recovery context.**
- **Advanced knowledge of principles and practices in broad humanitarian action, NGO safety and risk management, humanitarian access, and civil-military coordination**
- Strong understanding of Humanitarian Principles and their application in programmatic and advocacy responses
- Previous experience from working in complex and volatile contexts.
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities.
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile.
- **Fluency in English and Spanish, both written and verbal.**
- Valid driver’s license.
- Prior work experience at the country level, with programme implementation as a plus. Country Director and Area Manager are relevant profiles in addition to Access and/or Security Manager profiles.
- Experience or qualifications in humanitarian access and negotiations.
- Experience in risk management for implementing partners and remote management.
- Prior experience as a trainer
- Working proficiency in French is an asset.

## What we offer

- **Duty station: Bogotá, Colombia**
- **Contract: fixed national contract Sept 2027**
- Travel: 30%
- Salary/benefits**: grade 9 on NRC’s salary scale**, with accompanying terms and conditions
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

## Important information about the application process

- *Internal candidates only: please click on the suitcase icon labelled “I am an employee” to be redirected to NRC’s internal careers site.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email aela.recruitment@nrc.no with the job title as the subject line.

## Why NRC?

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We contribute to the development of policy aiming to protect the rights of the displaced and we call for increased humanitarian funding and engagement on processes that will generate structural changes in protection and assistance in the region.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation dedicated to protecting the rights of displaced and affected people during crises. NRC delivers high-quality programmes to support people forced to flee, helping them rebuild their lives and establish a new future. NRC provides immediate humanitarian assistance, prevents further displacement, and contributes to durable solutions. It operates across both new and protracted crises across 40 countries.

 NRC’s Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS) function’s purpose is to enable principled humanitarian response in a safe manner, for the communities and partners we work with and our staff. The Regional Humanitarian Access and Safety Adviser serves as the lead technical resource on safety and security, access, and crisis management within the region. This function is line managed by the Regional Head of Operations Support and managed in a technical line by the Global HAS Director. This role acts as the technical supervisor for Country HAS Managers or equivalent within the region and serves as a core member of the regional management team and crisis management team.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee.

Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

### About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: République Démocratique du Congo : Coordinateur.rice de Zone – Uvira
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.body:
**CDD | 6 mois | Mi-janvier 2027**

## Acted

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## Acted République Démocratique du Congo

La République Démocratique du Congo fait face à une crise humanitaire prolongée, marquée par la persistance des conflits armés, des déplacements massifs de populations, des chocs climatiques et des chocs épidémiques récurrents, tels que le choléra, le mpox ou la rougeole. Ces dynamiques combinées affectent durablement les conditions de vie des populations déplacées, retournées et hôtes, en particulier dans les provinces de l’Est et certaines zones de l’Ouest du pays.

Dans ce contexte, Acted intervient principalement dans les provinces du Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika, Nord-Ubangi et Sud-Ubangi, à travers des projets financés notamment par le Department of State / US, ECHO, FCDO, SDC, le Fonds Humanitaire, ainsi que le CDCS, afin de répondre aux besoins humanitaires immédiats et aux vulnérabilités persistantes des populations les plus affectées. Afin de renforcer la couverture et la complémentarité de ses interventions, Acted intervient en coordination avec plusieurs partenaires opérationnels, et est membre de consortiums humanitaires.

Cette coordination permet à Acted de mettre en œuvre des réponses d’urgence rapides et multisectorielles pour couvrir les besoins vitaux liés aux conflits, aux déplacements forcés, aux catastrophes naturelles et aux crises sanitaires. Les interventions portent notamment sur l’assistance alimentaire, les abris et articles ménagers essentiels, l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), la gestion et coordination des sites (CCCM) ainsi que l’éducation en situation d’urgence, avec une attention particulière portée, dès le premier kilomètre humanitaire, à la protection et à la dignité des personnes vulnérables. Au Sud-Kivu, Acted est par ailleurs un acteur clé du Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM), contribuant à des réponses rapides et coordonnées en lien avec les déplacements de populations et aux chocs soudains.

En parallèle, Acted développe des interventions visant à renforcer la résilience des communautés, à travers le soutien aux moyens d’existence, la relance agricole, la sécurité alimentaire et la relance économique locale, afin de réduire la vulnérabilité face aux chocs récurrents.

Acted apporte également un appui structurant aux organisations de la société civile (OSC) en renforçant leurs capacités organisationnelles et opérationnelles. Cet accompagnement inclut l’appui à la structuration des initiatives locales ainsi que la mise en place de mécanismes de financement en cascade, permettant aux OSC de développer des activités directement liées aux problématiques locales et aux priorités identifiées par les communautés.

Enfin, Acted intègre progressivement dans ses programmes des approches sensibles à l’environnement, visant à la préservation des écosystèmes et des aires protégées, à la réduction de l’empreinte environnementale des interventions et à la promotion de solutions à faible émission de carbone. À travers l’appui aux communautés, Acted encourage le développement d’activités génératrices de revenus durables et d’une économie locale plus verte, contribuant à la protection des ressources naturelles tout en renforçant les moyens d’existence.

## Rôle et responsabilités principales

Le.a coordinateur.rice de zone représente Acted vis à vis des autorités locales, des bailleurs, des populations bénéficiaires et des autres acteurs clefs.

Le.a coordinateur.rice est membre de l’équipe de management, il/elle garantit la qualité du programme et sa mise en œuvre opérationnelle, ainsi que son déploiement là où c’est approprié et réalisable, il/elle assure un fort rôle de représentation. Le.a coordinateur.rice supervise directement les responsables de projet en contrôlant que les projets et les programmes sont adaptés aux besoins des bénéficiaires et qu’ils sont mis en œuvre en accord avec la stratégie globale d’Acted , avec les orientations du bailleur. Une fois les plans de travail et les budgets validés, le coordinateur de zone supervise également au jour le jour les opérations et la sécurité dans la zone concernée.

***Principales responsabilités***

1\. Positionnement

- Analyse contextuelle
- Stratégie de mise en œuvre
- Réseau, positionnement et représentation générale
- Développement de propositions :
- Plaidoyer
- Promotion des organisations sœurs d’Acted

2\. Management et coordination interne

- Gestion d’équipe
- Coordination interne

3\. Suivi de la mise en œuvre des projets

- Suivi de la mise en œuvre des projets
- Contrôle qualité des projets
- Management des partenaires

4\. Management FLATS

- Gestion Finances
- Gestion logistique et IT
- Gestion administrative et RH
- Gestion transparence/conformité
- Gestion sécurité

## Qualifications et compétences requises

- Formation en développement international, les opérations d’urgence, les programmes humanitaires etc. ;
- Expérience approfondie de la gestion de projets dans des programmes d’urgence et/ou de développement ;
- Des compétences en gestion de base sont préférables (RH, finances, logistique) ;
- Au moins quatre ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente, comprenant de préférence la gestion de la sécurité ;
- Capacités avérées en matière de leadership et de gestion d’équipe requises ;
- Capacité à travailler sous pression ;
- Solides compétences en négociation et en relations interpersonnelles, et flexibilité ;

## Termes de référence

Pour plus d'informations sur le poste, [cliquez ici ](https://www.acted.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ac-uvira-rdc-2026.pdf).

## Conditions

- Salaire défini par la grille des salaires Acted en fonction du niveau d’études, de l’expertise, du niveau de sécurité et du niveau d’expérience : entre 3600 et 3700€ net mensuel (avant impôts sur le revenu)
- Indemnité mensuelle de frais de vie 300$
- Logement en guesthouse et nourriture pris en charge par Acted
- Sécurité sociale, mutuelle (MSH) et assistance rapatriement (SOS International) pris en charge par Acted
- Transport vers la mission et billet retour totalement pris en charge tous les 6 mois (vers l’adresse spécifiée sur le contrat de travail)
- Frais de visa pris en charge par Acted
- R&R tous les 3 mois (billet d’avion pris en charge jusqu’à 500$ + indemnité supplémentaire de 200$)
- Une semaine de préparation au départ comprenant 4 jours de formation sécurité en immersion
- Possibilité d’avoir un appel de 30minutes avec un.e consultant.e en fiscalité

jobs.title: ICT Systems Integration Technician EFMS/CARLOG
jobs.body:
Overview of position

CTG is looking for an ICT Systems Integration Technician EFMS/CARLOG to support its client operation, administration, integration, maintenance, and modernization of the UN mission Electronic Fleet Management System (EFMS) utilizing the CARLOG platform. The incumbent will be responsible for the administration and operational support of fleet technology systems, fuel monitoring systems, SQL databases, GPS tracking infrastructure, CAN Bus integrations, and related transport technology solutions.

The objective of the assignment is to ensure the reliable, secure, and efficient operation of the CARLOG Electronic Fleet Management System and its interoperability with Umoja ERP, Transport Management systems, Fuel Management Enhancement Solutions, and other approved services.

The incumbent will maintain fleet technology infrastructure, vehicle monitoring systems, receiving stations, communication networks, databases, and operational reporting systems while supporting fleet oversight, operational compliance, fuel management, investigations, data analytics, and platform modernization initiatives.

Role objectives

Within delegated authority, the incumbent will be responsible for the following duties:

A. EFMS / CARLOG Administration and Operations

Administer, configure, maintain, and support the CARLOG Electronic Fleet Management System (EFMS).

Maintain CARLOG databases, SQL Server environments, and associated applications.

Manage fleet master data including vehicles, drivers, devices, users, and organizational structures.

Create, modify, suspend, and maintain user accounts, permissions, and access privileges.

Maintain the World Fleet Log platform, including reporting and access administration.

Manage CARLOG F1 3G and F2 LTE/Wi-Fi devices and ensure their continuous operation.

Monitor system performance, synchronization services, scheduled jobs, and data transmission activities.

Establish and maintain backup, recovery, and business continuity procedures.

Maintain system documentation, architecture diagrams, asset inventories, and technical records.

Coordinate with the client sections, E-Drive Technology (EDT), vendors, and internal stakeholders on technical support activities.

Ensure completeness, integrity, and accuracy of fleet monitoring data.

B. Systems Integration and Platform Modernization

Maintain reliable and secure integration between CARLOG, Umoja ERP, Transport systems, Fuel Management Enhancement solutions, and other approved platforms.

Monitor and support automated data exchange and synchronization processes.

Validate interface configurations and ensure proper data flow between integrated systems.

Support modernization initiatives and migration from legacy CARLOG environments to web-based platforms.

Assist with requirements analysis, configuration, testing, data migration, deployment, stabilization, and user adoption activities.

Maintain integration documentation and interface inventories.

C. Receiving Station Administration

Establish, administer, maintain, and support all CARLOG Receiving Stations throughout the mission area.

Monitor receiving station availability, communications, data downloads, and synchronization performance.

Ensure continuous connectivity between receiving stations and CARLOG servers.

Troubleshoot hardware, software, communications, network, and synchronization failures.

Perform system restoration and recovery activities following communication outages.

Maintain operational records and performance statistics for all receiving stations.

D. Fleet Monitoring and Operational Compliance

Monitor and track mission vehicles using CARLOG systems.

Monitor real-time vehicle movements, deployment activities, and utilization patterns.

Analyze vehicle operational performance and fleet usage trends.

Monitor speeding violations, unsafe driving practices, and road safety compliance.

Monitor unauthorized vehicle movements, curfew violations, and misuse of assets.

Investigate vehicle activity anomalies and driver behavior irregularities.

Monitor excessive idling and operational inefficiencies.

Generate alerts, notifications, and operational compliance reports.

Maintain fleet performance indicators and statistical data.

E. Fuel Management and Monitoring

Monitor fuel consumption, fuel efficiency, and fuel-system performance.

Analyze fuel monitoring data generated through CARLOG and Fuel Management Enhancement systems.

Investigate fuel anomalies, unauthorized fuel usage, fuel loss, and suspected theft incidents.

Validate fuel performance indicators and consumption trends.

Support fuel-related investigations and corrective actions.

Produce fuel consumption, efficiency, and utilization reports.

F. Vehicle Systems Integration and Diagnostics

Review vehicle technical manuals, wiring diagrams, and electronic documentation.

Analyze vehicle communication networks including CAN Bus, J1939, OBD-II, LIN, and ECU interfaces.

Support installation, configuration, calibration, and validation of CARLOG devices and vehicle integrations.

Configure data acquisition from vehicle electronic control units.

Support mechanics, electricians, workshop staff, and installation teams during deployments.

Diagnose communication, electrical, and integration faults.

Verify compliance with CARLOG installation standards.

Perform testing and operational acceptance of installations and upgrades.

G. SIM Card and Communication Management

Administer and monitor active SIM cards supporting CARLOG live communications.

Maintain communication performance and monitor transmission quality.

Coordinate activation, replacement, provisioning, and troubleshooting activities with the section and service providers.

Maintain SIM card inventories, assignment records, subscriptions, and data plans.

Resolve communication outages and connectivity disruptions.

Ensure uninterrupted transmission of vehicle data to fleet monitoring platforms.

H. Monitoring, Incident Resolution and Service Support

Monitor application availability, server performance, interfaces, synchronization services, logs, and exception queues.

Investigate incidents and restore services within agreed service levels.

Provide Level 1 and Level 2 technical support to users.

Maintain complete incident records, root-cause analyses, and resolution documentation.

Escalate unresolved issues appropriately and coordinate corrective actions.

Support system upgrades, patching, and maintenance activities.

I. Data Quality and Reconciliation

Validate vehicle, driver, fuel, trip, maintenance, mileage, and operational data.

Perform data reconciliation between CARLOG, Umoja ERP, and other integrated systems.

Investigate inconsistencies and data anomalies.

Coordinate corrective actions with stakeholders and business owners.

Maintain data quality standards and reporting accuracy.

J. Reporting, Business Intelligence and Analytics

Generate and distribute:

Daily fleet monitoring reports.

Weekly and monthly operational reports.

Vehicle movement and utilization reports.

Management dashboards and KPI reports.

Driver behavior and road safety reports.

Curfew violation and compliance reports.

Fuel consumption and efficiency reports.

Fuel anomaly and investigation reports.

Receiving station performance reports.

Fleet deployment and operational readiness reports.

Annual mileage audit reports.

Historical vehicle activity reports.

Statistical reports for the CTO and Transport Management.

Data-driven recommendations to improve fleet efficiency, safety, compliance, and resource utilization.

K. Investigation and Compliance Support

Support Safety and Investigations Unit (SIU) inquiries and transport-related investigations.

Analyze vehicle movement histories and reconstruct routes.

Produce evidence-based reports using CARLOG data.

Support accident investigations and vehicle misuse assessments.

Monitor compliance with transport regulations, policies, and operational procedures.

Provide analytical support for management decision-making.

L. Workshop and Maintenance Support

Support vehicle maintenance management activities.

Maintain vehicle maintenance records within CARLOG.

Monitor maintenance schedules and vehicle service status.

Ensure maintenance activities are accurately recorded.

Support vehicle diagnostics and troubleshooting activities.

Assist in identifying technical faults and reducing unnecessary parts replacement through accurate analysis.

M. Security, Change and Release Management

Apply role-based access control and user security management.

Implement approved system changes, upgrades, configurations, and releases.

Maintain audit trails, access records, and security documentation.

Support testing, validation, rollback procedures, and change-control processes.

Ensure compliance with applicable UN ICT security standards and policies.

N. Training, Knowledge Management and Stakeholder Coordination

Deliver technical and user training on CARLOG, EFMS, fleet monitoring systems, and related technologies.

Develop technical procedures, user guides, and training materials.

Conduct knowledge-transfer sessions and support user adoption initiatives.

Provide vehicle tracking support to the Security Operations Centre (SOC).

Liaise with Transport, ICT, IT section, Finance, Supply Chain, Fuel Management personnel, vendors, and service providers.

Maintain knowledge repositories, operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and technical documentation.

Perform other related duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Monthly Deliverables

Monthly service-performance report covering system availability, incidents, service requests, recurring problems, changes implemented, outstanding risks, and corrective actions.

Fleet monitoring report covering vehicle utilization, operational compliance, driver behavior, curfew violations, and fleet performance indicators.

Fuel monitoring and reconciliation report covering fuel consumption trends, anomalies, investigations, and corrective actions.

Integration and data-quality report covering CARLOG, Umoja ERP, Transport systems, Fuel Management Enhancement solutions, and related interfaces.

CARLOG modernization status report covering migration progress, testing, deployment readiness, user adoption, and stabilization activities.

Receiving station performance report covering availability, connectivity, synchronization status, and maintenance activities.

Updated technical documentation, system inventories, operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and knowledge articles.

Training and knowledge-transfer report identifying sessions delivered, participants, materials used, and follow-up actions.

Forward work plan outlining priorities, milestones, dependencies, risks, and resource requirements for the following month.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Education

High school diploma or equivalent is required.

Technical training in Information Technology, Electronics, Telematics, Automotive Technology, Fleet Management Systems, Vehicle Diagnostics, Computer Science, Transport Technology, or related disciplines is required.

A university degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Computer Science, Electronics, Automotive Engineering, Transport Management, or a related field is desirable.

Work Experience

A minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in fleet management, fleet monitoring, telematics systems, transport operations, fuel management systems, vehicle tracking technologies, or comparable operational systems in a multi-site environment.

Demonstrated experience in the administration and support of Electronic Fleet Management Systems (EFMS), GPS tracking platforms, telematics solutions, and fleet-monitoring applications.

Practical experience in systems integration, data validation, database administration, incident management, testing, deployment support, and technical documentation.

Experience administering and maintaining SQL databases, fleet management applications, and reporting systems.

Proven experience with CAN Bus integration, vehicle communication protocols (OBD-II, J1939, LIN), vehicle diagnostics, and automotive electrical systems.

Experience maintaining vehicle communication networks, monitoring devices, fuel monitoring systems, and related fleet technology infrastructure.

Experience supporting large and geographically dispersed vehicle fleets of 500 vehicles or more is highly desirable.

Experience supporting web-based application deployments, platform upgrades, or migrations from legacy client/server environments is highly desirable.

Knowledge of CARLOG, World Fleet Log, Umoja ERP, UN transport operations, fuel management systems, or comparable fleet-management platforms is highly desirable.

Experience within the United Nations, military, government, humanitarian, peacekeeping, or other international organizations is an advantage.

Demonstrated ability to analyze operational data, produce management reports, and support evidence-based decision-making through fleet analytics and performance monitoring.

Technical Skills

CARLOG Fleet Monitoring System Administration

Electronic Fleet Management Systems (EFMS)

World Fleet Log Platform Administration

Fleet Telematics and Vehicle Tracking Technologies

GPS Monitoring and Geolocation Systems

Microsoft SQL Server Administration and Database Management

Database Design, Querying, Data Validation, and Reporting

Systems Integration and Data Synchronization

Umoja ERP Interface Support and Data Reconciliation

CAN Bus, J1939, OBD-II, LIN, and ECU Communications

Vehicle Diagnostics and Automotive Electronic Systems

CARLOG F1 3G and F2 LTE/Wi-Fi Device Administration

Fuel Monitoring Systems and Fuel Analytics

SIM Card, GSM, LTE, and Mobile Data Connectivity Management

Receiving Station Administration and Communications Management

Server Administration, Performance Monitoring, and Troubleshooting

Incident Management and Technical Support

Business Intelligence, Data Analytics, and Dashboard Development

Microsoft Excel (Advanced)

Microsoft Power BI

Technical Documentation and Knowledge Management

Technical Reporting, Fleet Analytics, and Performance Measurement

Change Management, Testing, Deployment, and Release Support

Information Security, Access Control, and Audit Compliance

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Qualified female candidates are strongly advised to apply.

Sightsavers is looking for an experienced Project Officer with excellent partner management skills and experience of Digital Health, to support the continued success of Neglected Tropical Disease projects in Benin.

**NTD Project Officer**   
Salary: Local terms and conditions apply  
Location: Benin, Cotonou  
Contract: 12-month Fixed-term Contract  
Hours: 35 hours per week - Standard office hours

We are looking for an experienced Project Officer with excellent partner management skills and experience of Digital Health, to support the continued success of Neglected Tropical Disease projects in Benin, in collaboration with The Reaching the Last Mile Funds (RLMF) and several other donors.

In Benin, Sightsavers has successfully supported the elimination of trachoma in 2022. However, Benin like many other Sub-Saharan African countries is endemic to several NTD and in line with the WHO roadmap, the country ambition to eliminate most NTDs by 2030. Sightsavers is supporting Benin for the elimination of onchocerciasis, lymphatic filariasis with the ambition of growing the portfolio to include schistosomiasis and soil transmitted helminth.
