jobs.title: Protection Officer (PRoL)-Daraa
jobs.body:
**Background/IRC Summary:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview/Summary:** The Protection Officer (PRoL) is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day implementation and technical quality of integrated protection programming delivered through partner organizations in Daraa and other assigned locations. The position has a primary focus on Protection and Rule of Law (PRoL) interventions, including legal awareness, legal assistance, civil documentation support, housing, land and property (HLP) issues, referrals, and community-based protection activities, while also supporting the quality and effective implementation of Child Protection (CP) and Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE) interventions delivered by partners.

The Protection Officer serves as the primary technical focal point for partner field teams, providing ongoing coaching, mentoring, capacity building, and technical guidance to ensure services are delivered in accordance with IRC standards, donor requirements, and international protection principles. The role includes conducting regular field visits, monitoring service quality, verifying program data and documentation, identifying implementation gaps, and working collaboratively with partners to strengthen program performance and accountability.

The Protection Officer supports the establishment and strengthening of community-based protection mechanisms, promotes meaningful participation of affected populations, and ensures that vulnerable individuals are safely identified and referred to appropriate services. The position works closely with partner staff, community structures, and IRC technical teams to promote integrated protection outcomes, strengthen referral pathways, enhance service quality, and ensure that protection interventions effectively address the needs of women, girls, boys, men, and individuals with specific needs.

The position also contributes to strengthening partner capacity, quality assurance processes, project reporting, coordination with stakeholders, and continuous improvement of protection programming to ensure the effective and accountable delivery of services across all project locations.

**Major Responsibilities:** Major responsibilities of the **Community-based Protection Officer** (not exhaustive) are listed below:

- Lead the day-to-day technical support and oversight of Protection and Rule of Law (PRoL) activities implemented through partners, ensuring adherence to IRC technical standards, donor requirements, and international protection principles.
- Support partners in the implementation of legal awareness, legal information dissemination, HLP-related activities, civil documentation support, protection advocacy, and referral services.
- Provide technical guidance to partner staff on protection case management principles, safe identification, referrals, protection mainstreaming, confidentiality, and survivor-centered approaches.
- Support the implementation and quality assurance of Child Protection (CP) and Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE) activities delivered by partners, ensuring compliance with sector standards and quality benchmarks.
- Ensure that integrated protection approaches are applied across all project interventions and that protection risks are systematically identified and addressed.
- Accompany partner teams during field visits and service delivery activities to provide mentoring, coaching, and technical support.

**Community Protection Systems Strengthening & Sustainability**

- Assess partner capacity gaps and develop capacity-strengthening plans in coordination with relevant technical coordinators and managers.
- Deliver training, coaching, mentoring, and on-the-job capacity-building for partner staff on PRoL, CP, WPE, safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, referrals, and case management principles.
- Facilitate regular technical review meetings with partner teams to discuss challenges, lessons learned, and corrective actions.
- Support partners in developing action plans to improve service quality and ensure timely implementation of recommendations.
- Support sustainable capacity strengthening and knowledge transfer initiatives to enhance partners’ long-term ability to deliver quality protection services independently.

**Referral & Coordination Oversight**

1. Oversee referral pathways to ensure effectiveness, continuity, and proper coordination with partners and service providers.
2. Work closely with the partner to ensure gradual handover of responsibilities and knowledge transfer.

**Data Validation, Compliance & Reporting**

1. Verify beneficiary data and ensure its accuracy and reliability.
2. Manage documentation and achieving in line with donor requirements.
3. Prepare impact reports, closure reports, and ensure full compliance with donor regulations and requirements.

**Program Closure & Transition Planning**

1. Support final evaluations and lessons learned exercises.
2. Lead or contribute to closure planning, ensuring safe and structured transition of activities to partners or communities.
3. Ensuring protection mainstreaming is integrated across remaining program activities.
4. **General**

- Perform any other duties as required by program needs or as requested by the supervisor.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Protection Senior Manager.
- **Position directly supervises:** Protection field staff – local partner activities.
- **Indirect Reporting:** IP Coordinator.
- **Other Internal and/or external contacts:**
- ***Internal:*** Protection Officers, Health team, WPE, and CP teams, ERD team. IP senior managers, IP Coordinator.
- ***External:*** INGOs, local actors, and local authorities.

 **Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- A bachelor's degree in social work, international relations, human rights, community development, or any other university degree.

***Work Experience:***

- Proven experience 2-4 yearsin Protection, PRoL, legal assistance, civil documentation, case management, or related humanitarian programming.
- Experience working with NGOs and implementing programs through partner organizations.
- Experience in providing technical support, coaching, and capacity strengthening to staff and partners.
- Experience in field monitoring, quality assurance, reporting, and compliance with donor and organizational standards.
- Knowledge of Child Protection (CP), Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE), referral pathways, and protection principles.
- Strong understanding of the Syrian humanitarian context and commitment to protection, inclusion, and gender equality.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Strong management and organizational skills.
- Excellent time management skills and ability to meet deadlines.
- Strong communication, negotiation and persuasion skills
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team, as well as independently.
- Flexible and able to work in a dynamic and diverse environment.
- Experience in regular report writing.
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team, as well as independently.
- Flexible and able to work in a dynamic and diverse environment.
- Must be computer literate (Microsoft Word and Excel).

***Language Skills:***

- Arabic & English are required
- Travel: If requested

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based and are currently located outside of your home country and possess over two years of international work experience, the Middle East Region has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENA, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

IRC is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful and safe work environment where all persons are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. jobs.title: DIRECTRICE GÉNÉRALE OU DIRECTEUR GÉNÉRAL - FRANCE
jobs.body:
**Action contre la Faim**

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis près de 50 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d’urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d’activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale et Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d’Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2025, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 21 millions de personnes dans 52 pays à travers le monde. [www.actioncontrelafaim.org](http://www.actioncontrelafaim.org)

Le secteur humanitaire traverse une crise profonde marquée par une baisse drastique et durable des financements alors que les besoins humanitaires atteignent des niveaux sans précédent. Comme de nombreuses ONG., Action contre la Faim France a dû adapter son modèle : elle a engagé une profonde transformation de son organisation, à laquelle ses équipes ont largement contribué. L'association, qui aborde une nouvelle étape forte de l'investissement d’équipes professionnelles, engagées et solidaires, cherche une dirigeante ou un dirigeant qui s'inscrive dans la durée pour consolider la confiance, mener la transformation à son terme et renforcer la dynamique collective.

C’est dans ce contexte que nous recherchons notre prochain·e Directeur·rice Général·e.

**Mission :**

Rattaché·e à la Présidence, vous dirigez l'exécutif d'ACF France et animez le comité exécutif. Cette équipe regroupe actuellement les directions des opérations, de l'expertise et du plaidoyer, de la communication et du développement, administrative et financière, des ressources humaines, de la logistique, des systèmes d'information, et de l'audit, des risques et de la conformité, ainsi que l'unité stratégie et transformation. Vous êtes appuyé par des chargé·es de mission et une assistante de direction. Cette organisation est appelée à évoluer dans le cadre de la réorganisation globale qui a été engagée.

- Veiller au bon fonctionnement du lien avec la gouvernance associative: vous assurez l'articulation entre le CA et l'exécutif, participez aux réunions, aux temps forts de la vie associative et présentez chaque année les accomplissements de l'association.
- Fédérer l'équipe de direction : vous animez le comité exécutif, favorisez la prise de décision collégiale et accompagnez le développement de ses membres.
- Porter le cap stratégique : vous proposez au CA un plan d'action pluriannuel conforme aux orientations stratégiques, en pilotez la mise en oeuvre.
- Sécuriser les grands équilibres financiers : vous veillez au respect et à la viabilité du modèle économique , vous assurez le pilotage de la trajectoire financière et contrôlez la stabilité de la trésorerie au niveau global.
- Conduire la transformation : vous menez à bien la transformation organisationnelle engagée avec les équipes, en capitalisant sur le travail accompli et en l'ajustant lorsque nécessaire.
- Représenter Action contre la Faim : vous portez la parole de l'association auprès des partenaires, des bailleurs, des médias et des organisations internationales.
- Incarner ACF France au sein du réseau international : vous coordonnez l'action d'ACF France avec les membres du réseau et veillez au respect des valeurs et principes communs, à la cohérence des opérations, et des actions de plaidoyer ainsi qu'à la réputation d'ACF.
- Prendre soin du collectif : attentif·ve aux personnes, vous portez une culture managériale fondée sur la responsabilisation et la confiance. Vous entretenez l'engagement et une dynamique collective positive, y compris à distance, et conduisez un dialogue social avec les instances représentatives du personnel.
- Garantir la sécurité et la conformité : vous pilotez la gestion des crises et assumez la responsabilité légale del'organisation.

**Profil :**

Vous avez une solide expérience en ONG, en partie acquise sur le terrain. Vous avez dirigé une entité de grande envergure, en tant que DG ou directeur·rice pays, et avez exercé au sein d'une association en France. Une expérience au sein d'ACF serait un atout.  
Vous connaissez le fonctionnement des associations en France, notamment en matière de gouvernance et de dialogue social.  
Reconnu·e pour votre vision stratégique et votre capacité d'anticipation, vous analysez les évolutions géopolitiques et leurs effets sur l'action humanitaire.  
Vous avez déjà conduit une transformation organisationnelle et accompagné les équipes dans le changement.  
Doté·e d'un leadership fédérateur, vous portez une culture managériale fondée sur la responsabilisation. Vous savez animer une équipe de direction, décider en collectif et trancher lorsque la situation l'exige, avec courage, écoute et empathie.  
Vous vous exprimez avec aisance, y compris face aux médias.  
Solide, humble et optimiste, vous faites preuve d'endurance et de persévérance.  
Vous avez une parfaite maîtrise du français et de l'anglais.

**Conditions d'emploi**

- Statut : Cadre dirigeant
- Lieu : Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis)
- Rémunération :De 87K à 100Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience
- Avantages:
    - 30 jours par an de CP
    - Couverture santé: Prise en charge à 80% par ACF
    - Indemnités Transport : prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail
    - Tickets-restaurant: prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8 euros
    - Oeuvres sociales
- Télétravail :
    - ACF dispose d'une politique de télétravail ouverte, depuis le territoire métropolitain.
    - Une présence au siège de 8 jours/ mois est requise pour ce poste.
    - Des temps de présence collective sont fixés par l'employeur pour les réunions collectives, jusqu'à 3 jours par mois.
    - Une présence continue au siège sera requise pendant la période d'intégration.
    - Indemnités de télétravail.
- Le poste implique des déplacements réguliers en France et à l'étranger.

**ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.**

***This position has an end date of 30 September 2027.***

**Job Overview:**

The Program for Initial Resettlement Caseworker Assistant supports refugee and other ORR-eligible populations during their integration into the United States by assisting with service delivery, client support, documentation, transportation, and resource coordination. Working under the guidance of the Cash and Medical and Initial Resettlement Coordinator, the Caseworker Assistant helps ensure clients have access to essential services and resources while promoting self-sufficiency, stability, and successful community integration.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Assist in coordinating pre-arrival and post-arrival services to ensure clients receive essential support upon arrival.
- Support airport pickups, housing setup, food assistance, transportation arrangements, and community orientation activities.
- Assist clients with navigating community resources and accessing essential services.
- Conduct client intake and assessment activities to help identify household strengths, needs, and priorities.
- Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide referrals and follow up on service connections, appointments, and action items.
- Support the distribution of direct assistance and program-related resources according to organizational and funder requirements.
- Maintain regular communication with assigned clients to support progress toward established goals.
- Document client interactions, services provided, referrals, and outcomes accurately and timely.
- Enter and maintain client records in ETO and other required databases.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Associate degree in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years’ experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Experience providing customer service, case management support, or community outreach preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Will require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($18.45). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Asistente de Protección Santa Bárbara del Zulia - Personal Nacional
jobs.body:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Oficial de Protección altamente calificado/a con sede en Santa Bárbara del Zulia, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

**Objetivo general del puesto:**

Bajo la supervisión del Líder de equipo de Protección (Zulia), el Asistente de Protección apoyará la implementación en terreno de todos los objetivos de protección bajo los proyectos de DRC. El Asistente de Protección desarrollará y mantendrá buenas relaciones con las personas de interés, las partes interesadas relevantes y otros actores humanitarios, para apoyar la implementación y coordinación adecuadas de las actividades de Protección de DRC que se desarrollarán en el área de intervención. Apoyar la implementación de enfoques diferenciales, especialmente de edad, género, y diversidad en las actividades de protección.

**Responsabilidades:**

- Contribuir eficientemente a la implementación del proyecto de protección en los municipios del sur del lago del estado Zulia de acuerdo con los objetivos acordados.
- Implementar periódica el Monitoreo de Protección en las comunidades de intervención, incluyendo el levantamiento de datos cuantitativos y cualitativos sobre necesidades/riesgos de protección mediante la aplicación de entrevistas a unidades familiares, grupos focales e informantes claves.
- Contribuir al fortalecimiento del enfoque de edad, género y diversidad en las acciones de y respuestas de protección.
- Apoyar en la identificación y documentación sistemáticamente las necesidades específicas y riesgos de protección de las personas más vulnerables en las comunidades de intervención –a través del Monitoreo de Protección, actividades informativas realizadas en las comunidades y otros medios— a fin de referir y/o brindar una repuesta oportuna a las personas de interés.
- Participar en el Comité de Asistencia de Protección Individual (IPA), y contribuir con los planes de respuestas que respondan a las necesidades específicas protección de los casos, y apoyar con los planes de entrega de las asistencias y/o remisiones a servicios especializados internos y/o externos.
- Manejar la información confidencial de manera correcta, de acuerdo con las políticas de protección de datos de DRC, gestionando los archivos de protección de manera precisa, correcta y completa.
- Apoyar en la recopilación de información para la elaboración de reportes, informes, e insumos productos del Monitoreo de Protección.
- Asegurar la más alta calidad de las intervenciones de protección y la coherencia entre todos los proyectos, en curso y propuestos, de acuerdo con la estrategia general.
- Apoyar en la orientación de las personas de interés según las rutas de protección, el mapeo de servicios y de los actores humanitarios e institucionales.
- Apoyar en la organización y facilitación de grupos focales y sesiones informativas sobre temas de protección.
- Apoyar y asistir en conjunto con la línea supervisora en el desarrollo de actividades legales conforme a los objetivos y metas.
- Participar bajo supervisión en el asesoramiento individual de las principales necesidades legales identificadas.
- Acompañar a los beneficiarios a instituciones públicas según sea necesario.
- Participar en espacios de formación y retroalimentación de las acciones de protección.
- Participar de manera colaborativa en las acciones del equipo de protección y otras áreas.
- Participar activamente a las reuniones de equipo proporcionando insumos, desafíos y lecciones aprendidas.
- Contribuir al desarrollo de herramientas de procedimiento operativos estándar.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva de las actividades programática asignadas, mientras el plan de trabajo.
- Apoyar en la preparación de informes y presupuestos mensuales.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 1 año de experiencia relevante en protección humanitaria, trabajo social, derechos humanos u otro trabajo similar de terreno, relacionado a una ONG u otra organización sin fines de lucro.
- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo con comunidades urbanas, y/o rurales, y/o indígenas.
- Experiencia y capacidad para entrevistar a personas de todas las edades, género y diversidad.
- Buenas habilidades para trabajar con tabletas y computadores.
- Buenas habilidades en MS Word y Excel.
- Voluntad y habilidad de aprender.

**Educación:**

Título Universitario pertinente en logística y / o gestión de la cadena de suministro o cualificación profesional equivalente.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 6 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.
- Contratación nacional.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Miércoles 14 de Octubre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio:** Octubre 2026

**Nota:**

- Nos reservamos el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha indicada de cierre de postulaciones
- La vacante está sujeta a aprobación del proyecto y disponibilidad de fondos
- Debido a una contratación de emergencia, DRC no se obliga a enviar las notificaciones de rechazo a los candidatos que no sean considerados en el proceso

jobs.title: Consultancy – Consulting Risk Tool & Appetite Assignment
jobs.body:
## **Find the all supporting documents in our** [**PUBLIC TEMPLATES**](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=IgDIi3ew57_-QbmSZCPQ3PHgAV02EJ44vp-Xum-N7sehfJI&e=tKvdjB) **and the Terms of Reference and Request for Proposal:** TD 2026 1386 [**Consultancy – Consulting Risk Tool & Appetite Assignment**](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=IQCtEzHz-Ho9TLRypUuafKgZAa8xwOXVF_v0oUGA029j6GU&e=Z3Rey3) including the exact evaluation process and selection criteria.

**Indicative Timeline:**

Deadline for submission of proposals: 14 October 2026  
Evaluation and selection of audit firm: 19 October 2026  
Notification of award and contracting week of 19 October 2026  
Assignment start and end date: As soon as possible after contracting  
Deadline for submission of final deliverables: 20 December 2026

## 1.Introduction

The Netherlands Red Cross International Assistance Department (NLRC) seeks external expertise to  
provide advice on the further development and operationalization of its risk management approach. The assignment focuses on strengthening decision-making related to partnership management and localization of assistance by defining and operationalising risk appetite and tolerance,  
improving risk assessment methodologies, and translating these into practical guidance and minimum control frameworks for staff.  
The assignment is structured into three separate groups of deliverables:

**1. Deliverable A** – Risk Assessment Tool Review and Improvement: assessment of the  
existing NLRC and CRRA risk assessment tools and development of practical improvements to ensure the process scope, risk categories, questions, scoring methodology  
and resulting financial control measures are clear, objective, proportionate and fit for  
NLRC use (including guidelines on how to use the tool).

**2. Deliverable B** – Risk Appetite and Minimum Controls Advisory: advisory support regarding  
the design of a future risk appetite, risk tolerance and minimum controls framework, including  
governance, guidance and implementation recommendations.

**3. Deliverable C** – Process Facilitation and Framework Development: facilitation of NLRC management and staff in translating the recommendations from Deliverable B into draft frameworks and agreed outputs.  
Service providers are requested to provide separate (financial) proposals for the different deliverables. NLRC reserves the right to award Deliverables A, B and C separately or in combination to one  
or more service providers. Technical and financial proposals shall therefore clearly distinguish between Deliverables A, B and C.

## 2. Context and background

NLRC works closely with other (Movement) partners in both long-term and short-term partnership/ projects. Recent risk management experiences have identified recurring challenges regarding the consistent assessment of risk, determination of acceptable risk levels, and selection of proportionate mitigation measures. The absence of clearly defined risk appetite, risk tolerance guidance, and minimum controls has resulted in differing interpretations across teams, inconsistent risk assessments, prolonged discussions on mitigation measures, and uncertainty regarding risk acceptance and sharing decisions. These challenges are particularly evident in:  
• Long-term partnerships periodic assessments, and engagement and continuation decisions.  
• Short-term (technical assistance) project arrangements.  
• Localization ambitions and risk-sharing efforts with partner National Societies.

NLRC aims to further align its risk management approach with relevant IFRC-network frameworks,  
tools and Movement-wide developments including the Capacity Review and Risk Assessment  
(CRRA), the Way of Working (WoW) initiative, and the General Terms and Conditions developments  
while ensuring that risk management remains practical, adaptive and proportionate to context.

## 3. Purpose and Objectives

Purpose of the assignment: To provide independent advice on how NLRC can strengthen its partnership risk assessment approach and how it should organize the development of a risk appetite and tolerance framework, a minimum internal controls set, and practical tools and guidance for risk management related to long-term partnerships, short-term partnerships/projects and localization and risk sharing ambitions. Additionally, and depending on the offer, the assignment has the objective to focus on facilitation of the process to set up this risk appetite framework and minimum control framework, including supporting documentation.  
Although this assignment is commissioned by and primarily focused on the International Assistance Department, NLRC seeks recommendations that are scalable and capable of supporting future organizational developments. In particular, the consultant is encouraged to consider how the proposed improvements to partnership risk assessments, risk appetite, risk tolerance, minimum controls and associated guidance could serve as building blocks for a future Netherlands Red Cross-wide approach. Where relevant, the consultant should therefore identify opportunities for  
standardization, harmonization and governance arrangements that would enable future adoption beyond IA, while ensuring that recommendations remain practical and proportionate to the specific objectives and context of this assignment.

Key questions

The consultant shall answer the following questions during the assignment:

1. Partnership risk assessments

• How can we improve our risk assessment tool?  
• Which risk categories and related assessment questions are most relevant for NLRC, particularly from a financial control perspective, and how can these be balanced so the assessment remains complete but not unnecessarily extensive?  
• What objective and transparent rating or scoring methodology would be most appropriate for the NLRC context, including clear criteria, weighting and escalation thresholds?  
• How can the NLRC risk assessment tool remain efficient, user-friendly and adaptable to different contexts, including regular partnerships, short-term projects and exceptional or rapidly changing situations?  
• Following the rating outcome, what clear set of financial and operational control measures should be implemented, monitored and reviewed, including guidance on residual risk and cases where the standard template may not be sufficient?

2\. Risk appetite, risk tolerance and minimum controls

• How should NLRC define and articulate risk appetite and risk tolerance in relation to engaging  
and continuing with both long-term and short-term partners, and to localization objectives?  
• Which stakeholders should be involved, what decisions are required, and at which management level should these decisions be made?  
• How should NLRC distinguish between risk appetite, risk tolerance, thresholds, minimum controls and escalation criteria?  
• What scope, structure and content should a appetite and threshold framework contain?  
• What types of minimum controls should be considered mandatory across all contexts, and which controls could be adapted based on risk profile, partner capacity or context?  
• How can the controls framework remain proportionate while ensuring adequate assurance, accountability and safeguarding of NLRC standards?

3\. Governance and operationalization

• How should risk appetite, tolerance and minimum controls be translated into practical staff guidance?  
• What tools, templates, decision aids, training or examples would be required to support consistent application by staff?  
• How should the future framework and guidance be embedded in existing risk management, partnership management and localization-related processes and documents?

4\. Process facilitation and framework development

• What facilitation approach is most suitable to support management and staff in defining risk  
appetite and tolerance parameters?  
• How can differing stakeholder perspectives be effectively reconciled during the framework-development process?  
• What workshop formats, decision-making tools and facilitation techniques are most suitable  
for reaching agreement on risk appetite and minimum controls?  
• How should draft frameworks be validated, tested and refined before formal approval?  
• What level of management engagement is required throughout the facilitation process?  
• What practical outputs should be produced during the facilitated sessions to ensure ownership  
and readiness for implementation?  
• How can the facilitated process support long-term adoption and consistent application of the  
future frameworks?

5\. Methodology

The consultant is expected to design and present a methodology for the different deliverables that  
is based on a participatory approach and at least including the following:  
• Review and analysis of the existing NLRC and CRRA risk assessment methodologies, processes, questions, scoring approach and related tools.  
• Assessment of whether the current tools produce sufficiently clear, objective and actionable ratings and whether the rating outcomes are linked to proportionate financial control measures.  
• Review of relevant donor protocols (e.g. from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and DG ECHO).  
• Desk research into relevant Movement-wide and other National Society risk assessment processes and case studies, approaches and tools to identify opportunities for adoption, adaptation and harmonization.  
• Alignment with Red Cross/Red Crescent good practices, frameworks and initiatives, including IFRC-WoW.  
• Interviews and workshops with key stakeholders.  
• Development of recommended improvements to the risk assessment tool, including process scope, risk categories, assessment questions, scoring methodology, escalation thresholds and links to minimum financial controls.  
• Development of draft threshold and appetite frameworks with consolidated information from stakeholder input sessions.  
• Validation workshops to discuss preliminary findings and recommendations, and proposed frameworks and guidance.  
• (Practical testing of proposed approaches against real partnership and emergency-response scenarios.).

## Deliverables

**Deliverables – Part A. Risk management process review**  
1\. Assessment report and improved risk assessment tool, including: a review of the existing NLRC and CRRA risk assessment approaches, processes, questions and related documents; a gap analysis; recommended risk categories and proportionate assessment questions; an objective rating/scoring methodology with clear criteria and escalation  
thresholds; and a practical set of financial and operational control measures linked to the rating outcome, including guidance on monitoring, review, residual risk and exceptional cases.

**Deliverables – Part B. Risk appetite and minimum control advisory**  
2\. Advisory process design for developing a risk appetite and tolerance framework for partnership engagement and the localization trajectory, including:  
a. Recommended steps, decision points and governance route for defining, discussing and approving risk appetite and tolerance.  
b. Suggested structure and key components of a future risk appetite and tolerance framework.  
c. Advice on stakeholder involvement, management facilitation and validation of the future framework.  
3\. Advisory process design for developing a minimum internal controls set regarding partnership engagement and the localization trajectory, including:  
a. Recommended approach for identifying mandatory and context-adaptable controls.  
b. Advice on linking controls to risk profiles, partner capacity, context and localization ambitions.  
c. Advice on governance, monitoring and review of the future controls set.  
4\. Advisory guidance approach for staff, including:  
a. Recommended tools, templates, decision aids, examples and training needs to support consistent application.  
b. Advice on embedding the future guidance in existing risk management, partnership and localization-related processes and documents.  
5\. Final advisory report and presentation to the Management Team, summarizing findings, recommendations, proposed process designs, key decisions required and suggested next steps.

**Deliverables – Part C. Process facilitation**

Deliverable C focusses on putting the advices from deliverable B in practice, and facilitating the NLRC in implementing those advices.

6\. Facilitation sessions to guide NLRC relevant staff and management in setting-up the risk appetite and minimum controls framework for partnership engagement and its localization ambitions.

7\. Draft risk appetite and tolerance framework, consolidated from the facilitated sessions with relevant staff and management.

8\. Draft framework for internal controls, consolidated from the facilitated sessions with relevant staff and management.

## 7. Profile of the desired Service Provider/Company

a) Experience with and knowledge of  
o Enterprise risk management and governance, with a focus on risk appetite, thresholds and minimum controls;  
o The Red Cross Red Crescent Movement and the broader humanitarian and development sector, and preferable of the Netherlands Red Cross;  
o Partnership and project risk assessment processes, including risk categories, assessment questions, rating/scoring methodologies and links to financial control measures;  
o The concept of localization and locally led action within the humanitarian and development sector.  
o Familiarity with donor compliance requirements (e.g. DG ECHO, Ministry of Foreign  
Affairs)  
b) Skillsets:  
o Process analysis  
o Facilitation and presentation;  
o Planning and time management;  
o Report writing;  
c) Language:  
o Professional level of written and spoken English

## 8. Planning

• The full assignment should be completed before December 31st  
• If it is not deemed possible to complete all deliverables before December 31st, the focus should primarily be on Deliverable A, including the improved risk assessment tool, and then Deliverable B.  
• Specific timelines can be discussed between the providing party and the NLRC.

## 9. Responsibilities and lines of communication

The assignment as described in the ToR will be coordinated by the Netherlands Red Cross and for any questions or issues about the conditions of the assignment the consultant should refer to the Risk Management Officer of the Netherlands Red Cross.  
For anything related to the assignment's execution, the consultant will liaise mainly with the Risk Management Officer and the Financial Control department, particularly for Deliverable A and the translation of risk ratings into financial control measures.

## 10. Relevant documentation

The contracted party will be receiving a comprehensive documentation package including relevant information about ongoing IFRC practices and developments such as the IFRC CRRA and General Terms and Conditions process, relevant NLRC processes and documents, case studies of risk assessment processes, and others.

## 11. Budget

The available budget for this assignment is estimated at EUR 40,000 (excluding VAT). Consultants are requested to submit a detailed financial proposal demonstrating value for money. NLRC reserves the right not  
to award the contract if submitted proposals exceed the available budget or do not meet the required quality  
standards.  
Payments will be made against approved deliverables and receipt of a valid invoice. No advance payments  
will be made unless explicitly agreed in writing.

## Key Assessment Criteria

**• Experience, skills, and capacity of the service provider**  
Proven experience conducting audits for donor-funded projects (references); qualifications (short CVs) and language skills of the proposed team members (fluency in  
English is mandatory); capacity of the bidder to meet the requirements of the Netherlands Red Cross (NLRC).  
**• Technical approach and implementation plan**  
Clear and structured audit methodology; risk management approach; proposed  
tools and procedures to deliver the assignment in line with the ToR.  
**• Work plan and project management**  
A realistic and detailed timeline; allocation of resources; identification of a project  
manager; logistical feasibility.  
**• References**  
At least two relevant and contactable references for clients served within the past  
twenty-four months.

***Knowledge***  
***The proposal must clearly state whether the bidder has the knowledge needed to meet the ToR requirements and demonstrate any relevant presence or familiarity with the context.***  
***All reports, tools, frameworks, templates, methodologies and other outputs developed under this assignment shall become the property of the Netherlands Red Cross. The consultant may not disclose or reuse project materials without prior written consent from NLRC***

jobs.title: Médecin support Unité Santé des Equipes F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Le.la Médecin participe à la politique préventive en identifiant et en traitant, de manière adaptée, les questions liées à la santé du personnel de terrain, individuelles ou collectives, avant, pendant et après une mission avec MSF OCP.

**Objectif principal du/de la médecin de la SHU**

Participer au déploiement d’une politique de prévention ; identifier et répondre de façon adéquate aux questions liées à la santé du personnel de terrain, individuelles ou collectives, avant, pendant ou après une mission avec MSF OCP.

**Principales responsabilités**

**Santé du personnel international OCP : focus sur la prévention :**

En tant que médecin, vous êtes référent·e pour l’infirmière chargée des départs et les intervenants externes (consultants Pasteur ou autres structures) en cas de découverte d’un problème de santé chronique ou aigu avant une mission, vous :

- Evaluez les risques d’un départ sur un terrain de mission des candidats présentant un problème de santé, avec les intervenants externes et les référent·e·s santé du personnel sur le terrain (coordinateur·rice médical·e ou autre) et/ou référent·e médical·e de cellule.
- Pouvez demander à annuler ou décaler un départ en concertation avec les intervenants précédemment cités.
- Vous assurez avec l’infirmière chargée des préparations aux départs de la mise à jour régulière des prérequis santé par terrain et de la diffusion de ces informations.
- Participez avec les membres de la SHU à adapter le processus de préparation au départ selon les besoins, les circonstances (ex. épidémie) et dans l’optique d’une stratégie de décentralisation à mettre en place progressivement.

**Support aux points focaux santé (coordinateurs médicaux ou autres) des projets OCP:**

- En cas de sollicitation pour des problèmes médicaux touchant le personnel international ou national, oriente les coordinateurs médicaux ou points focaux santé terrain par rapport à la meilleure prise en charge de cas individuels et sollicite des avis adaptés à la complexité des cas (département médical, réseau externe, institut Pasteur, assureur ou compagnie d’assistance par exemple).
- Aider à l’organisation des références et rapatriements de personnel internationaux pour raison de santé.

**Guides et politiques :**

- Se tenir informé·e de l’évolution des recommandations internationales (OMS ou autres sources), des contextes épidémiques ou de tout évènement ou nouvelle recommandation médicale ou scientifique ayant un intérêt pour les équipes MSF sur le terrain.
- Diffuser les documents et l’information concernant la santé des équipes (généraux ou spécifiques lors d’une épidémie : Covid, Ebola, etc.) auprès des coordinateurs médicaux ou points focaux, cellules opérationnelles et département RH siège.
- Briefer les points focaux sur les aspects administratifs liés aux problèmes de santé sur le terrain : déclaration des accidents du travail, des accidents d’exposition au sang et fluides entre autres.
- Aider à organiser l’archivage et l’organisation des données et documents de la SHU ainsi qu’à la collecte de certaines données (ex. cas de COVID, accidents du travail, AES, rapatriements etc.).
- Travailler avec la responsable SHU et les départements impliqués (médical, RH) à la mise à jour ou création de documents spécifiques à la santé des équipes.
- Participer à la formation et aux briefings des coordinateurs médicaux ou des points focaux.
- Organiser ou participer aux différentes sessions de formation/information/webinar sur des thématiques en lien avec la santé du personnel (Covid, ebola, autres épidémies, AES, hépatites etc.).

**Contexte de fièvre hémorragique:**

- Mettre à jour et diffuser les documents relatifs à la santé du personnel concernant les FHV, incluant les politiques de vaccination contre le virus Ebola.
- S’assurer qu’un briefing individuel est donné aux internationaux avant départ (par le/la médecin ou un autre poste en renfort si l’épidémie est très importante), qu’une visite médicale systématique est effectuée et que le/la candidat/e est ou sera vacciné si la possibilité existe; assure le suivi au retour du terrain (« politique des 21 jours »).
- S’assurer que les coordinateurs et points focaux santé soient briefés sur le risque VHF et mettent en place le suivi du personnel, national comme international pendant et après tout déploiement sur une mission FHV.
- Diffuser les informations nécessaires concernant les politiques en place aux différents intervenants de sièges (recruteurs, gestionnaires de pool, bureau des départs, GRH, département des opérations etc.) ainsi qu’aux coordinateur·rice·s (coordinateur·rice médical·e (CoMed), adjoints CoMed, points focaux santé, chef·fe de mission, coordinateur·rice RH).

**D’autres activités peuvent éventuellement se rajouter en fonction des besoins. Vous devez être flexible et ouvert·e.**

**Profil recherché**

**Formation:** Diplôme de médecin.

**Expérience :**

- Expérience avec MSF de 24 mois minimum
- Au moins une expérience de référent·e médical·e projet à MSF
- Une expérience comme personnel international MSF dans au moins 2 contextes différents.
- Une expérience en médecine du voyage ou médecine tropicale est un plus

**Langues :** français et anglais : niveau B2 (obligatoires).

**Aptitudes:**

- Excellent contact humain, écoute
- Capacité à prioriser en restant focalisé sur les priorités liées à la santé
- Patience et bonne gestion du stress

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Statut :** CDD de 13 mois à temps plein. Poste cadre, basé à Paris.

**Rémunération et avantages** : 50,8 K€ brut annuel sur 13 mois. 22 jours de RTT par an. Télétravail selon les règles en vigueur chez MSF (2 j/sem.). Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%. Titres-restaurant de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF). Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

**Poste à pourvoir :** 1er décembre 2026.
