Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

## **About the Role**

To drive seamless data flow between the Back Office Portal and SAP B1 and to optimize workflows to ensure 100% data delivery to MCF within 45 days. Key role in process improvement.

## **Responsibilities**

Accounting Systems & Systems Integration

- Drive data flow management and system integration between the Back Office Portal and SAP Business One (SAP B1), troubleshooting integration errors and optimizing system workflows.

Master Data Management & Process Improvement

- Manage and update vendor master records to ensure data accuracy, completeness, and compliance with company policies and donors’ audit-required standards.

Cross-Functional Communication & Technical Translation

- Serve as the technical bridge between Tech, FRC, and FAS teams by translating complex data insights and system requirements into actionable process improvements.

Collaborative Quality Assurance

- Partner across departments to make sure that processes are fully documented, maintain spreadsheet audit standards, streamline reporting workflows, and establish organization-wide data management best practices.

## **Career Growth and Development**

jobs.title: Zambia Field Operations & Performance Specialist (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

In Zambia, from our hub in Kabwe, we run a specialised climate-smart input and agroforestry program to address challenges such as irregular rainfall and soil degradation. By partnering with local Tree Nursery Operators, we raise and distribute agroforestry trees that enrich soils and build long-term financial resilience. Supported by a structured frontline field team across Central and Southern Provinces, we use rigorous, data-driven frameworks to measure our impact and ensure we drive meaningful improvements in farmer yields, asset accumulation, and food security.

## **About the Role**

We are looking for an experienced, analytical, and resilient Field Operations Specialist to lead and expand our rural field operations. You will act as the key link between field leadership and headquarters, improving performance mainly through the Field Director (FD) layer while working closely with Field Officers (FOs) and Group Leaders.  
  
The ideal candidate can turn complex field data into clear, targeted operational strategies, manage teams effectively under tight deadlines, and design community leadership frameworks that can grow with the programme. You will also lead with strong emotional intelligence, especially in demanding and remote environments.

## **Responsibilities**

Field Performance Management & FD Leadership

- Lead field performance through field directors, ensuring teams deliver against key programme targets, including farmer adoption, tree survival and growth, repayment, and customer service
- Use field performance data to identify gaps, diagnose root causes and drive timely corrective action.
- Regularly engage with field teams and visit sites to validate performance, coach teams and address operational challenges.

Field HR Coordination & Risk Oversight

- Oversee key field staff processes, including onboarding, staff movements, performance management, disciplinary processes and payroll coordination.
- Provide leadership during urgent field staff and operational issues, including staff exits, fraud cases and other high risk incidents.
- Ensure field staff processes, incidents and risks are appropriately documented and managed in line with organisational policies.

Group Leader Management System

- Develop and continuously improve a strong, consistent Group Leader system across field sites.
- Establish clear approaches to Group Leader selection, onboarding, performance management, coaching and incentives.
- Strengthen accountability within groups and ensure underperforming Group Leaders and groups are appropriately supported or managed.

Training, Coaching & Staff Development

- Build the capabilities of Field Directors and field officers through structured training, coaching and mentorship.
- Strengthen communication and feedback between field teams and HQ, ensuring field realities inform programme decisions.
- Develop a strong talent pipeline and support the progression of high-performing field staff into future leadership roles.

Operational Prioritisation & Execution

- Lead the effective execution of multiple field priorities, balancing programme performance, people needs, operational risks and organisational deadlines.
- Ensure teams are focused on the highest-priority activities and that responsibilities are appropriately delegated while maintaining accountability for results.
- Identify opportunities to improve field systems, processes and ways of working as the programme grows.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

- 3 to 5+ years leading and growing multi-layered field teams (extension agents) in agriculture, rural development, or social enterprise.
- Demonstrated ability to analyse quantitative operational metrics (adoption rates, loan repayment percentages, yield impact) and translate insights into immediate field action plans.
- Proven track record of operating effectively across expansive, remote geographical regions with limited network connectivity and challenging logistics.

jobs.title: Consultant - Financial Systems Review, Benchmarking, and Alignment under One Program Approach (OPA) with Localization Focus
source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
jobs.body:
## **Organizational Context**

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian organization, with a network of 191-member National Societies (NSs). The overall aim of IFRC is “to inspire, encourage, facilitate, and promote at all times all forms of humanitarian activities by NSs with a view to preventing and alleviating human suffering and thereby contributing to the maintenance and promotion of human dignity and peace in the world.” IFRC works to meet the needs and improve the lives of vulnerable people before, during and after disasters, health emergencies and other crises.

IFRC is part of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement (Movement), together with its member National Societies and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The work of IFRC is guided by the following fundamental principles: humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General, and has its Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. The Headquarters are organized into three main Divisions: (i) National Society Development and Operations Coordination; (ii) Global Relations, Humanitarian Diplomacy and Digitalization; and (iii) Management Policy, Strategy and Corporate Services.

IFRC has five regional offices in Africa, Asia Pacific, Middle East and North Africa, Europe, and the Americas. IFRC also has country cluster delegations and country delegations throughout the world. Together, the Geneva Headquarters and the field structure (regional, cluster and country) comprise the IFRC Secretariat.

IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

## **Consultancy Purpose**

The Lebanese Red Cross (LRC), as the host National Society, leads humanitarian action in Lebanon. Multiple Partner National Societies (PNSs) operate using varied financial and operational systems.  
LRC has already initiated a mapping of partner systems and internal processes. However, in light of evolving international financial standards, compliance requirements, and localization priorities, there is a need to:

- Update and validate the existing mapping.
- Benchmark LRC financial systems against current best practices and Movement  
    standards.
- Identify gaps in alignment between LRC and partners.
- Analyze discrepancies across partners (e.g., why some partners meet standards while  
    others do not).

This assignment will support strengthening financial governance, accountability, and host National Society leadership under the One Program Approach (OPA).

##   
**Objectives**

The consultant will:

1. Conduct a comprehensive financial review of LRC systems (Finance & Accounting as a  
    priority, with linkages to HR, Logistics, and Procurement where relevant).
2. Update and validate the existing mapping of Partner National Societies’ systems against LRC frameworks.
3. Benchmark LRC financial systems against best international standards, ensuring  
    relevance to today’s operational and compliance environment.
4. Analyze gaps and discrepancies, including:
    - Why LRC may not fully meet certain standards (if applicable).
    - Factors influencing varying levels of alignment with the benchmarking framework, including donor requirements, headquarters policies, operational modalities, system configurations, and internal governance arrangements.
5. Provide actionable recommendations to strengthen alignment, improve financial systems, and ensure partners adopt best processes.

## **Consultancy Duties and Responsibilities**

- **Finance & Accounting**  
    Review LRC financial policies, procedures, and systems.
- Assess alignment with best international standards (audit, compliance, donor  
    requirements).
- Evaluate:
    - Budget consolidation under OPA.
    - Financial tracking systems and tools.
    - Reporting cycles and compliance.
    - Documentation and audit trails.
- Identify gaps in practice versus standards and propose practical improvements.

**Comparative Partner Analysis**

- Update existing mapping of PNS financial systems.
- Categorize partners based on level of alignment (high, medium, low).
- Conduct comparative analysis, including:
    - Partners that meet standards vs. those that do not.
    - Practices that enable compliance (good practices).
    - Constraints preventing alignment.

**Cross-Functional Linkages**

Where relevant, assess how financial processes interact with:

- Procurement (compliance, documentation, supplier payments)
- Logistics (inventory valuation, tracking)
- HR (payroll, staff cost allocation)

**Scope of Work**

**Financial Systems Review (LRC)**

- Review existing financial frameworks, SOPs, and tools.
- Benchmark against up-to-date international
- Identify strengths, gaps, and risks.

**Mapping Update and Validation**

- Review previously conducted mapping exercises.
- Validate accuracy with current practices.
- Update alignment scoring based on latest data.

**Comparative Analysis**

- Conduct a structured comparison between:
    - LRC vs. international standards.
    - Partner vs. LRC systems.
    - Partner vs. partner practices.
- Highlight reasons for misalignment and enabling factors for compliance.

**Recommendations**

- Provide:
    - Practical recommendations for LRC system strengthening.
    - Partner-specific alignment actions.
    - Priority actions based on risk and impact.
- Ensure recommendations are feasible, localized, and reinforce LRC leadership.

  
**Deliverables**

1. Financial Systems Assessment Report (LRC): Benchmarking against current international and Movement standards.
2. Updated Mapping Report: Validated and revised mapping of partner financial systems.
3. Comparative Analysis Report:
    - LRC vs. standards
    - Partner vs. LRC
    - Partner vs. partner
4. Including gap analysis and root causes.
5. Recommendations Matrix: Clear, prioritized actions for LRC and partners.
6. Presentation to Leadership: Key findings, comparisons, and strategic recommendations.
7. Methodology
    - Desk review of financial policies, reports, and prior mapping.
    - Interviews with LRC finance staff and partner representatives.
    - Validation workshops.
    - Use of updated benchmarking frameworks aligned with current global standards.
    - Comparative and evidence-based analysis.
8. Duration and Timeline

  
**Phase Duration Key Activities**

- Financial Review (LRC) 4 weeks : System assessment, benchmarking
- Mapping Update 3–4 weeks: Validate and update partner mapping
- Comparative Analysis 2–3 weeks: Gap analysis and cross-partner comparison
- Reporting & Presentation 1–2 weeks: Final deliverables

## **Education requirements**

- Advanced degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field.

## **Experience requirements**

- Minimum 15 years of experience in financial assessments, audits, or system  
    strengthening.

## **Knowledge, Skills and Languages requirements**

- Strong knowledge of current international financial standards and donor compliance  
    frameworks.
- Experience with different Red Cross/Red Crescent Movement.
- Experience with UN agencies is a strong asset.
- Proven experience in comparative analysis and system benchmarking.
- Ability to produce practical, actionable, and context-adapted recommendations.

## **Competencies, Values and Comments**

- **Values**: Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability
- **Core competencies**: Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision making; National society and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust

jobs.body:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date: 01/11/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**  
**Location: West and Central Darfur**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Following the outbreak of the conflict in April 2023 and forced evacuation of Khartoum and West Darfur (El Geneina), SI was one of the first international NGO to re-enter Darfur and resume its emergency response.  
In February 2024, SI opened a base in North Darfur to provide emergency assistance to populations, as very few humanitarian organizations were operational in the state. Similarly, SI opened an office in Zalingei, Central Darfur in November 2024 and East Darfur and West Kordofan in early 2026. In addition an office in Khartoum was maintained and in 2025 operations were opened in Jazeera state. Today, thanks to the support of SHF, CDCS, SDC, GFFO, SIDA, ECHO and BHA, activities are being implemented in West Darfur, Central Darfur, North Darfur, East Darfur, West Kordofan, Jazeera and Khartoum States across WASH, Shelter and NFI support, Food Security and Livelihood sectors.  
Across the Darfurs, the main share of the portfolio remains WASH with the provision of water through water trucking, rehabilitation of water points/water yards, borehole drilling, hygiene promotion, sanitation (emergency latrine construction, semi-permanent latrine, showers, desludging), solid waste management, WASH NFI distribution, and WASH in Health etc. In the East the focus is on rehabilitation and recovery of water systems as well as emergency WASH interventions for health crises. Besides, SI implements food assistance mostly through cash and voucher modalities. West and North Darfur team also implements agricultural support activities (seeds distribution, provision of tools, training) as well as market strengthening support.  
SI also has an Emergency Response Team based in Zalingei, Central Darfur, roving across Central and West Darfur, implementing rapid responses in WASH, Shelter/NFI and Food (CVA) as well as in North Darfur.  
In North Darfur, SI was one first to intervene and are presently a leader in WASH response. The FSL work has brought in some great result in North Darfur.   
Recently, we opened our new base in Al Dein in East Darfur and West Kordofan. The teams are already working on strong WASH response along with some critical Cash response. The team is currently assessing and opening new areas in Kordofans.   
In the Eastern part of the country, SI is present with Wash and FSL activities in Khartoum and Jazeera, under ECHO, CDCS, and SHF.  
Most of the programs are being implemented in Consortium, 2 led by SI, and require strong coordination efforts to provide area-based interventions. SI also has a strong localization approach, with diverse local partners in all states.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**General objective:**

The WASH PM will be in charge of launching and implementing SI's WASH activities in West and Central Darfur states.  
S/he will be in charge of ensuring projects are delivered in a timely manner according to WASH quality standard and in accordance with context specifications and communities preferrences.  
S/he will be in charge of coordinating and providing support to two technical teams accross West and Central Darfur states, providing adequate support and capacity-building when needed and working in a remote managemet set up.  
S/he will be in responsible to lead needs assessments in different areas of West and Central Darfur and consequently developing the SI response plan, including with local partners.

**The main challenges:**

- Important workload with a wide range of WASH activities in different geographical areas
- Remote management context as 2 WASH teams in 2 different states
- Access & security challenges

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

- Launch newly starting projects and update workplan according to priorities
- Supervision of technical works including new borehole drilling and water points solarization
- Coordinate WASH response with SI stakeholders, mainly WASH actors, authorities and line ministries

**Security constraints:**

Level 4: High risk environment, threats less predictable and requiring strict protocols, Curfews in place (often 6pm–8pm), Walking strictly limited to approved times, locations,

### YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

A Bachelor or Master's degree in Water Resource Management, Engineer, Project management

Experience in the humanitarian sector: 3 Years

Experience on a similar position : 3 Years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Proven experience in WASH emergency/ealry recovery programming and WASH in institutions
2. Strong experience in water points solarization, solid waste management
3. Proven experience in partnership - preferable with local organizations
4. Experience in cholera prepardness or response
5. Strong experience in management
6. Good analytical skills and proactive, solution-oriented approach to work.
7. Experience in protracted crisis context (being able to switch between short/medium/long-term solutions).

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Strong organizational skill
2. Interpersonal and communication skills
3. Ability to work under pressure
4. Ability to adapt to different implementation contexts including remote supervision
5. Experience working with SI and prior experience working in Sudan is an assest

**LANGUAGES**

- English Mandatory
- Arabic would be an advantage

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2310 gross per month (2100 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Guest house is of good standard, with good internet connexion, solar panels and running water. Social life is limited to contact with other NGO staff

jobs.title: Humanitarian Communications Officer
jobs.body:
**About ACT Alliance**

ACT Alliance is the world's largest coalition of Protestant and Orthodox churches, and church-related organisations engaged in humanitarian, development, and advocacy work. It consists of 164 members working together in over 125 countries, with headquarters in 73 countries, whose aim is to create positive and sustainable change in the lives of poor and marginalised people regardless of their religion, politics, gender, sexual orientation, race, or nationality, in keeping with the highest international codes and standards. For more details, visit [www.actalliance.org](http://www.actalliance.org/).

**Job Summary**

The Communication Officer is responsible for developing and implementing communication and visibility activities for ACT Appeals and the Rapid Response Fund, with the objective of:

- increasing the visibility and understanding of ACT Alliance's humanitarian response;
- communicating the impact and added value of ACT members' and forums’ work;
- supporting fundraising and donor engagement;
- strengthening the visibility of local and national ACT members;
- producing high-quality, timely and compelling digital content;
- ensuring accountability through transparent communication about humanitarian funding and results; and
- positioning ACT Alliance's humanitarian financing mechanisms as credible, effective and locally led.

The Officer will work closely with the HOHA and RRF Managers, head of communications, humanitarian colleagues, ACT members, communications colleagues and fundraising/donor engagement functions.

## Key responsibilities

**A. Communication Strategy and Planning**

- Develop and implement communication plans for the RRF and ACT Appeals in coordination with ACT Alliance Communication team.
- Ensure communication activities are aligned with ACT Alliance's broader communications and fundraising strategies.
- Identify communication opportunities throughout the humanitarian funding cycle, from crisis alert and funding mobilisation through implementation, results and close-out.
- Develop clear communication objectives, target audiences, key messages and content plans for each funding mechanism.
- Ensure that communication is timely and appropriate to the humanitarian context and does not compromise the safety, dignity or privacy of affected people and partners.

**B. RRF Communication and Visibility – 50%**

- Lead day-to-day communication activities related to the Rapid Response Fund.
- Develop communication packages around RRF-funded responses, including:
    - human-interest stories;
    - impact stories;
    - case studies;
    - photos and visual content;
    - short videos and reels;
    - social media content;
    - web stories;
    - donor-facing updates;
    - infographics and other digital materials.
- Proactively identify RRF-funded responses with strong communication and fundraising potential.
- Work directly with ACT members, forums and Regional Representatives to gather high-quality information, stories, photographs, quotes and other content.
- Develop clear procedures and tools to facilitate systematic collection of communication materials from RRF-funded members.
- Ensure that RRF results and impact are regularly documented and communicated.
- Develop an annual RRF communication and visibility calendar.
- Support communication around RRF milestones, including funding decisions, portfolio achievements, learning, localisation and innovation.
- Highlight the added value of the RRF as a rapid, flexible and locally led humanitarian financing mechanism.
- Communicate the role of the RRF within ACT Alliance's wider humanitarian architecture.
- Develop content that demonstrates how RRF funding translates into concrete results for crisis-affected communities

**ACT Appeals Communication – 50%**

- Support communication and visibility for ACT Alliance humanitarian Appeals.
- Develop and coordinate communication materials throughout the Appeal cycle.
- Support the production of:
    - Appeal launches;
    - situation updates;
    - human-interest stories;
    - impact stories;
    - donor updates;
    - social media campaigns;
    - website content;
    - newsletters;
    - videos and multimedia products.
- Coordinate with ACT members to collect timely information, photographs, testimonies and programme results and avoid duplication of efforts, particularly in major responses
- Lead the humanitarian communications group and coordinate calls as appropriate
- Translate technical humanitarian information into accessible and compelling communication products.
- Support fundraising campaigns linked to ACT Appeals.
- Ensure that Appeal communication demonstrates the collective added value of ACT Alliance members.
- Contribute to donor visibility and reporting requirements.
- Support communication around Appeal results, achievements, lessons learned and funding gaps.
- Identify stories and content that can help sustain donor engagement throughout the Appeal cycle.
- Support communication around the humanitarian system and mechanism as a whole.

**Fundraising and Donor Engagement**

A specific responsibility for both appeals and RRFs will be to ensure that communication contributes directly to **fundraising and resource mobilisation**.

- Develop compelling fundraising-oriented stories demonstrating the impact and added value of funding.
- Translate programme results into content suitable for donor engagement.
- Develop communication materials for prospective and existing donors.
- Support the preparation of donor presentations, fundraising campaigns, briefs and digital materials.
- Identify opportunities to use impact stories to demonstrate the value of investing in locally led humanitarian response.
- Work with colleagues to develop a pipeline of communication materials supporting future resource mobilisation.
- Support donor visibility requirements while ensuring that communication remains consistent with ACT Alliance policies, principles and partner ownership.
- Contribute communication inputs to donor proposals and fundraising materials where relevant.

**Digital Media and Content Production**

The position will have a strong focus on **digital communication and multimedia content**.

- Produce engaging content for ACT Alliance digital platforms.
- Develop social media content adapted to different platforms and audiences.
- Create short-form video content, including reels and other mobile-first formats.
- Develop simple visual assets, infographics and data-driven communication products.
- Support story, photography and video content collection from ACT members.
- Edit and package multimedia content for digital dissemination.
- Maintain content libraries in the ACT Mediabank and ensure appropriate informed consent, storage and accessibility of communication assets.
- Monitor digital engagement and use analytics to improve communication performance.
- Identify emerging digital communication trends and recommend approaches relevant to ACT Alliance humanitarian work.

**Storytelling and Content Development**

- Develop compelling stories that place affected people and local responders at the centre of humanitarian communication.
- Identify human-interest stories demonstrating the concrete impact of ACT funding.
- Ensure that stories are accurate, evidence-based and representative of programme results.
- Develop stories that demonstrate the contribution of local and national organisations and their leadership in humanitarian response.
- Ensure appropriate informed consent and compliance with safeguarding, data protection and ethical communication policies and requirements.
- Avoid communication approaches that portray affected people solely as victims or beneficiaries.
- Promote dignified, empowering and locally owned storytelling.

## Key working relationships

Head of Humanitarian Affairs; RRF Manager; Head of Communications; Secretariat communications team; humanitarian team; Regional Representatives; ACT members and forums; donor-reporting colleagues and communications focal-point network.

## Education, experience and skills

- University degree in communications, journalism, humanitarian affairs, international development, public relations or a related field.
- At least 5 years of relevant communications experience, preferably in humanitarian, NGO, faith-based or international network settings.
- Demonstrated experience developing and implementing communication strategies or campaigns.
- Strong experience in **digital communications and social media**.
- Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality written and visual content.
- Experience developing human-interest stories, case studies and impact stories.
- Experience working with photographs, video and short-form digital content.
- Demonstrated experience communicating complex information to different audiences.
- Experience of working with NGOs, humanitarian organisations, international organisations or similar institutions.
- Experience working with faith-based organisations is an asset.
- Strong understanding of ethical and responsible humanitarian communication.
- Demonstrated ability to work with multiple stakeholders and manage competing priorities.
- Excellent written and spoken English; additional languages relevant to ACT regions are an asset.

## General obligations

- Uphold and model ACT Alliance values, policies and ways of working, including safeguarding, PSEAH, accountability, inclusion, environmental responsibility and ethical conduct.
- Participate in ACT Secretariat planning, reporting, performance management and learning processes as required.
- Undertake other duties consistent with the purpose and level of the position, as reasonably assigned by the line managers.
- Undertake international travel as required in connection with the responsibilities and objectives of the position.

jobs.body:
**GENERAL INFORMATION**

Job Title : Türkiye Program Lead

Location : Ankara, Türkiye (On-site)

Job Type: Full-time

Contract Duration : The contract is for an initial period of **one (1) year**, with the possibility of extension depending on the availability of funding and the continued need for the role.**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

## Vision

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

## Mission

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

## Purpose

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Program Lead is responsible for the overall management, coordination, and quality implementation of INARA’s programs in Turkey, including medical case management and MHPSS activities.

The Program Lead supervises case management workers and psychologists, ensuring effective scheduling, technical guidance, and performance oversight. The role supports program budgeting, financial coordination, reporting, proposal development, and representation in coordination platforms.

The Program Lead works closely with Finance, Administration, Partnerships, and Communications teams and reports directly to the CEO.

## **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Include and may not be limited to:

**. Program Management and Supervision**

- Provide overall leadership and direct supervision of the case management and MHPSS teams, including psychologists, social workers, and case management staff, ensuring that services are delivered in accordance with INARA’s standards and clinical pathways.
- Develop and maintain structured staff schedules that ensure continuous service coverage, efficient workload distribution, and appropriate caseload allocation based on staff capacity and program priorities.
- Conduct regular team meetings, case review sessions, and technical supervision to monitor progress, address challenges, and ensure the consistent application of case management methodologies and MHPSS best practices.
- Provide ongoing mentoring, coaching, and performance management support to program staff, including setting individual objectives, reviewing performance, identifying capacity-building needs, and facilitating professional development opportunities.
- Ensure that all program activities are implemented with a high level of technical quality, adherence to ethical standards, safeguarding principles, confidentiality requirements, and INARA’s internal protocols.
- Oversee the quality and accuracy of case documentation, ensuring that case files, service records, and follow-up plans are complete, compliant, and up to date.
- Monitor team caseloads, service delivery timelines, and beneficiary progress to ensure that program targets, service standards, and donor commitments are met.
- Identify implementation challenges or operational risks affecting program delivery and develop corrective actions in coordination with relevant departments.
- Promote a collaborative, supportive, and accountable team environment that encourages effective communication, problem-solving, and adherence to organizational values.
- Ensure proper coordination between medical, case management, and MHPSS components so that beneficiaries receive integrated and holistic support.

**2. Program Planning and Budgeting**

- Lead the development of detailed program work plans, implementation schedules, and activity timelines that align with organizational strategy, donor agreements, and operational priorities.
- Translate approved project proposals into practical implementation plans with clear deliverables, milestones, and resource requirements.
- Support the preparation of annual and project-specific program budgets in coordination with the Finance Department, ensuring that all planned activities are adequately costed and aligned with available funding.
- Monitor program expenditures on a regular basis against approved budgets, identifying variances and recommending corrective actions to ensure efficient and compliant use of resources.
- Review and validate program-related financial requests to confirm their alignment with approved work plans, procurement plans, and donor requirements.
- Coordinate closely with the Finance team to ensure adherence to donor financial management regulations, reporting timelines, and internal financial control procedures.
- Participate in monthly budget review meetings and contribute to financial forecasting, burn-rate analysis, and cash flow planning.
- Support procurement planning by identifying programmatic needs in advance, preparing procurement requests, and ensuring timely acquisition of goods and services required for implementation.
- Ensure that procurement activities related to the program follow INARA procurement policies, transparency standards, and donor compliance requirements.
- Contribute technical inputs for grant budget revisions, cost extensions, and reprogramming requests as necessary.
- Maintain organized documentation of all program planning and budgeting processes for audit readiness and donor reporting.

**3. Financial and Administrative Coordination**

- Work closely with the Finance and Administration departments to ensure that all program-related financial documentation, including purchase requests, payment requests, contracts, and supporting records, are complete, accurate, and compliant with INARA policies and donor requirements.
- Review and verify program expenses prior to submission for approval, ensuring that all expenditures are justified, aligned with approved budgets and work plans, and supported by appropriate documentation.
- Ensure timely submission of all financial supporting documents, including invoices, receipts, timesheets, service confirmations, and procurement documentation, to facilitate accurate accounting and reporting.
- Coordinate with Finance to track expenditures against approved budgets, monitor burn rates, and address any discrepancies or variances in a timely manner.
- Support the preparation of periodic financial reports by providing programmatic justification, activity verification, and expenditure clarification as required.
- Ensure that all program-related transactions follow INARA’s internal financial controls, procurement procedures, and authorization levels.
- Assist in the preparation of documentation required for internal and external audits, donor financial reviews, and compliance checks.
- Liaise with Administration and Operations teams to ensure that program logistics, contracts, and service agreements are properly documented and executed.
- Maintain organized financial and administrative records for all program activities, ensuring traceability, transparency, and readiness for donor verification.

**4. Monitoring, Reporting, and Documentation**

- Prepare high-quality, accurate, and timely narrative reports for donors, ensuring that all reporting reflects program achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and alignment with approved project objectives and indicators.
- Track program performance against established targets and key indicators, ensuring that progress is systematically monitored and documented throughout the project lifecycle.
- Maintain up-to-date records of program outputs, outcomes, and beneficiary data, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with INARA’s data protection and confidentiality standards.
- Develop and document success stories, beneficiary case studies, and impact narratives that demonstrate program effectiveness and support donor engagement, communications, and fundraising efforts.
- Provide regular internal progress reports to the CEO and Senior Management Team, highlighting achievements, risks, implementation challenges, and recommended corrective actions.
- Coordinate closely with the MEAL (Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning) function to ensure that monitoring tools, indicators, and reporting frameworks are consistently applied across all program activities.
- Support data collection, verification, and analysis processes to ensure evidence-based decision-making and continuous program improvement.
- Ensure that all reporting deadlines are met in accordance with donor agreements and organizational requirements.
- Maintain organized and accessible program documentation, including reports, activity records, beneficiary tracking data, and verification materials, ensuring readiness for audits, evaluations, and donor reviews.
- Facilitate periodic program review meetings with relevant departments to assess progress, integrate lessons learned, and strengthen program effectiveness.

**5. External Representation and Coordination**

- Represent INARA in national and regional NGO coordination meetings, technical working groups, and relevant sector platforms in Turkey, ensuring that INARA’s programs, priorities, and achievements are effectively communicated.
- Actively participate in humanitarian coordination mechanisms, including health, protection, and MHPSS-related forums, contributing technical insights and sharing program updates where appropriate.
- Establish and maintain strong professional relationships with hospitals, medical service providers, mental health professionals, and other implementing partners to ensure effective referral pathways and quality service delivery.
- Coordinate closely with local NGOs, international organizations, and community-based actors to promote collaboration, avoid duplication of services, and strengthen integrated support for beneficiaries.
- Participate in stakeholder meetings, inter-agency working groups, and partnership discussions, representing INARA’s interests and identifying opportunities for collaboration and joint programming.
- Facilitate communication between INARA program teams and external partners to ensure smooth coordination of beneficiary services, referrals, and follow-up care.
- Support the development and maintenance of Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and service agreements with partner organizations and service providers, in coordination with senior management.
- Provide feedback to senior leadership on external developments, sector trends, policy changes, and emerging needs that may impact program implementation.
- Promote INARA’s visibility, credibility, and reputation through professional engagement with stakeholders and adherence to humanitarian principles.

**6. Proposal Development and Partnerships**

- Contribute to the identification of new funding opportunities in Turkey by providing programmatic insights, needs assessments, and contextual analysis to support the development of competitive proposals.
- Participate in the design and development of new project concepts, ensuring that proposed interventions are technically sound, evidence-based, and aligned with INARA’s strategic objectives and operational priorities.
- Provide accurate program data, beneficiary statistics, lessons learned, and implementation evidence to strengthen proposal narratives and demonstrate organizational impact and capacity.
- Support the preparation of detailed project budgets in coordination with the Finance and Partnerships teams, ensuring that cost projections are realistic, compliant with donor guidelines, and aligned with program work plans.
- Contribute technical inputs to proposal documents, including program descriptions, implementation methodologies, logical frameworks, and monitoring indicators.
- Coordinate closely with the Partnerships and Development team throughout the proposal development process to ensure timely submission and alignment with donor requirements.
- Work with the Communications team to ensure that program achievements, visibility materials, and impact evidence are effectively integrated into donor engagement and fundraising efforts.
- Support donor engagement activities by providing technical presentations, program updates, and clarifications during proposal discussions or donor meetings as required.
- Contribute to grant revision processes, budget modifications, and extension requests based on program implementation realities.
- Maintain organized records of proposal inputs, supporting documentation, and technical data to facilitate future funding opportunities.

**7. Cross-Department Collaboration**

- Work closely with:
    - Finance
    - Administration
    - Partnerships
    - Communications
    - Operations
- Ensure alignment between program implementation and organizational strategy.

## **REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS**

**Qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Psychology, Social Work, Humanitarian Studies, or related field (Master’s preferred).

**Experience**

- Minimum 5–7 years of experience in humanitarian or development programming.
- Experience supervising multidisciplinary teams.
- Strong understanding of case management and MHPSS programming.
- Experience with donor reporting and proposal development.
- Strong organizational and leadership skills.
- Fluency in English required; Turkish and/or Arabic preferred.

**CONFIDENTIALITY AND SAFEGUARDING**

**Confidentiality**

As the position is involved in sensitive topics, he/she must observe absolute discretion within and outside the organization. Non-respect of this clause or any breach of responsibility may result in a written warning or immediate dismissal.

**Safeguarding**

INARA has zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, or harm to children and vulnerable adults. INARA employees must adhere strictly to safeguarding policies, maintain professional boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

jobs.title: Consortium Coordinator Mozambique (f/m/d)
jobs.body:
For our office in Mozambique, the Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe e.V. International Assistance (JIA), is looking for a

Consortium Coordinator Mozambique (f/m/d)

*One year contract (with possible extension) based in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique*

**Organisation Description:** Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe e.V. is a German Christian non-governmental organisation, dedicated to excellence in the field of first aid, ambulance service, social service programmes and other projects in the medical and social field. Johanniter International Assistance (JIA) is the operational unit for humanitarian aid. The Federal Headquarters (HQ) is based in Berlin, Germany. Our Global Strategy 2027 focuses on three programmatic working areas: disaster response and preparedness, health and livelihoods, with climate change and gender equality as crosscutting issues. [www.thejohanniter.org](http://www.thejohanniter.org). Our commitment to a partnership approach and localisation agenda is based on mutual learning, respect and trust. We prioritise accountability, inclusivity and safeguarding in our work.

**Background**

Johanniter started its activities in Mozambique in 2019 and has expanded its program in Mozambique from short to medium term across Sofala, Manica and Cabo Delgado provinces. We are implementing projects to support the population affected by conflicts and climate related shocks in Mozambique. The projects focus on Health, Nutrition, WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods including crosscutting themes like DRR and peacebuilding. Projects are implemented with local partners and through self-implementation. Funds are secured through the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), the German Federal Foreign Office (GFFO), USAID, Aktion Deutschland Hilft (ADH), ECHO and as well as a variety of other donor agencies.

**OCHA/MHF Project Summary:**

This OCHA/MHF funded humanitarian project aims to deliver life-saving, multi-sector assistance to conflict-affected and displaced populations in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique, focusing on restoring access to primary healthcare while integrating nutrition, food security and livelihoods and protection support. The project is implemented by a consortium led by Johanniter International Assistance, combining complementary expertise in health, nutrition, food security and protection response to reach 45,000 vulnerable people in hard-to-access areas.

**In a Nutshell**

You will:

- serve as the focal point for consortium and oversee all aspects of consortium management and governance, ensuring quality implementation, compliance with OCHA/MHF rules, effective coordination among partners, and alignment with consortium objectives
- facilitate communication, oversee joint planning, implementation and reporting to maximize the impact of consortium-funded project

**You will do:**

Strategy and Vision

- actively support the values of Johanniter and shape our work accordingly
- contribute to the development and implementation of the global strategy of Johanniter International Assistance

Leadership

- actively live the Johanniter’s leadership principles by fostering trust, embracing diversity, communicating openly, supporting wellbeing, and taking responsibility to contribute to a positive, inclusive, and adaptable work environment
- this is reflected in the day-to-day activities in line with the Code of Conduct and related policies to achieve our goals

Coordination and governance

- lead structured coordination among consortium members including Johanniter, co-lead agencies and implementing partners
- serve as primary consortium representative to donor and other local and international stakeholders, responsible for addressing all project matters
- serve as the primary liaison among consortium partners, facilitating communication and alignment with project objectives, conflict resolution and constructive engangement
- establish and coordinate technical working groups (steering committee, project management, technical, advocacy, MEAL)
- organize and chair consortium meetings, document decisions, and track action points
- maintain clear and responsive communication with the donor and partners regarding project updates, challenges, and opportunities
- provide support to the development and roll-out of project communication strategies, including compliance with donor’s branding and marking requirements
- organize and coordinate OCHA/MHF donor visits, ensuring visibility and clear communications
- develop a Consortium Engagement Strategy and report progress to the Steering Committee

Programme Management & Implementation

- oversee implementation of consortium activities in line with approved proposals and workplans
- monitor progress against objectives, indicators, and targets; ensure timely delivery of outputs
- identify implementation challenges and risks; propose and follow up on corrective actions
- conduct regular field monitoring visits to verify progress and quality
- Supports in coordinating partner planning and delivering the project in full compliance with OCHA/MHF regulations and internal procedures
- track project indicators, activities, and budget, flag deviations and recommend corrective actions
- ensure lessons learned are shared and applied across partners
- support technical and operational staff in understanding donor reporting and compliance requirements
- Coordinates internal and external reporting processes, ensuring high-quality narrative and financial submissions

Monitoring and Evaluation

- facilitate and oversee sub-award life cycles, from vetting and agreement development to monitoring and close-out.
- Support in coordinating partner program, finance, and compliance monitoring, providing guidance to address any issues
- Support in drafting and reviewing sub-agreements in coordination with Country Director, HQ compliance, JUH internal departments, and partners
- maintain comprehensive electronic and physical files for all partnership activities
- Support in monitoring overall consortium budget utilization, burn rates, and forecasts
- Support in ensuring efficient, transparent, and compliant use of funds , flag discrepancies or risks
- coordinate with finance teams to support budget revisions and financial planning

Representation, Communication, Liaison, and Networking

- represent the Consortium Partners at the regular coordination/Cluster meetings
- establish regular mechanisms for exchange of information between the Consortium partners
- motivate Consortium Partners to participate in events (coordination meetings, working groups, training, workshop, assessments, etc.)
- contribute to the production of documents (strategies, work plans, advocacy briefs, and bulletins) with appropriate view and technical input from Consortium Partners
- ensure the accountability and transparency of the Consortium Partners decision and work on the OCHA/MHF project.

Capacity Building

- strengthen coordination mechanisms and build partner capacity in grant management
- provide technical support to consortium members on donor compliance and reporting

Safeguarding

- integrates safeguarding considerations into grant and partnership management by ensuring safeguarding commitments are reflected in grant agreements and partner documentation, monitoring partner adherence to Code of Conduct and PSEAH requirements, and flagging safeguarding risks through appropriate in-ternal channels

Gender

- ensure consortium activities, partner work plans, logframes, and reporting reflect Johanniter’s Gender Minimum Standards by applying current gender analyses, tracking SADD and gender indicators, budgeting required gender-responsive actions, assessing gender-related risks, and promoting do-no-harm messaging

**What you bring:**

Profession/Qualification

- university degree in Medicine, Public Health, Humanitarian Studies, International Development, Social Sciences, International Law, or related field

Experience

- minimum 5 years’ experience leading multi-partner projects in humanitarian settings
- strong Program Management and Coordination skills and experience
- strong knowledge of project planning, management cycles, and donor compliance requirements (especially OCHA Pool Fund and ECHO but also GFFO and BMZ)
- excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; ability to lead meetings with multiple stakeholders
- knowledge of protection programming or experience in protection/refugee contexts preferred
- excellent facilitation, negotiation, and communication skills
- fluency in English required; Portuguese language skills are an asset
- demonstrated experience and skills in project management cycle
- knowledge of national and international guidelines including SPHERE and CHS is an advantage
- excellent organizational, communication, and writing skills
- good working experience in Mozambique especially in the field of Consortium Coordination

Desirable

- strong organizational and documentation skills, capable of managing multiple competing deliverables
- excellent problem-solving, negotiation, and interpersonal skills
- experience coordinating across finance, MEAL, and communications departments
- proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
- fundraising abilities and understanding of various donors requirements
- ability to use Logical Framework Approach as a tool in project/programme design and follow-up
- significant understanding of complex emergencies and crisis contexts
- significant political and cultural awareness and experience of working in setting where insecurity is a major issue
- awareness of gender issues
- proven communication, interpersonal and negotiation skills
- flexible, high-pressure environment; may involve remote and insecure areas

**What we offer**:

- Remuneration: Competitive attractive salary
- Benefits: 13th cheque, social security, annual leave, flexible working hours, friendly and appreciative working atmosphere

jobs.title: Senior Programme Coordinator (f/m/d)
jobs.body:
For our office in Kyiv, Ukraine, the Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe e.V. International Assistance, is looking for a

Senior Programme Coordinator (f/m/d)

One-year contract based in Kiyv

**Organisation Description:** Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe e.V. is a German Christian non-governmental organisation, dedicated to excellence in the field of first aid, ambulance service, social service programmes and other projects in the medical and social field. Johanniter International Assistance (JIA) is the operational unit for humanitarian aid. The Federal Headquarters (HQ) is based in Berlin, Germany. Our Global Strategy 2027 focuses on key working areas in emergencies and health and implementing and supporting projects with a specific focus on climate change and gender equality worldwide [https://johanniter.org/](https://johanniter.org/). Our commitment to a partnership approach and localisation agenda is based on mutual learning, respect and trust. We prioritise accountability, inclusivity and safeguarding in our work.

**Background**

Johanniter International Assistance (JIA) resumed its work in Ukraine at scale following the full-scale invasion in February 2022. Working with Ukrainian and international partners, JIA now leads three consortia supported by institutional donors, including GFFO, BMZ and ECHO. The programme focuses particularly on health, primary and emergency care, preparedness and support to health facilities, alongside other humanitarian and recovery activities for people affected by the war.

**In a Nutshell**

Reporting to the Country Director, you will lead the Ukraine programme team and oversee delivery of JIA’s portfolio, including three consortia for which JIA is lead partner. You will manage two consortium coordinators, three PMEAL staff and two other project staff; support country strategy; and ensure coordination and complementarity across projects and partners. You will guide programme quality, planning, monitoring, donor reporting and new project development, working closely with finance and operations colleagues.

**What you will do:**

Strategy and Vision

- Support the Country Director in developing and implementing the Ukraine country strategy, drawing on programme learning, context analysis and the Johanniter global strategy
- Identify new programmes based on assessments that support the achievement of Johanniter’s strategic objectives in the country (including rapid humanitarian assistance in case of disasters in coordination with Country Director and HQ)
- Assess and build partnerships with new national, international and local partner organisations
- Ensure coordination and complementarity across consortium projects, other JIA activities and partners, identifying gaps, overlaps and opportunities for joint work
- Lead or commission needs and partnership assessments to inform programme decisions and proposals
- Lead project development processes and ensure the development and production of high quality concept notes and proposals for submission to various donors
- Assist Country Director in identifying new funding opportunities
- Assess capacity strengthening needs of national partners and address them by providing trainings or facilitating other capacity strengthening activities

Programme Monitoring and Evaluation

- Manage the PMEAL team and ensure appropriate monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems across projects and consortia
- Ensure accountability to affected people and communities, and use feedback and evidence to improve programme quality
- Oversee programme compliance with Johanniter and donor requirements in coordination with finance, operations and relevant HQ colleagues
- Monitor the evolving humanitarian context and advise the Country Director on implications for programme priorities and delivery
- Travel to project locations as needed, subject to security clearance
- Work with partner and consortium PMEAL teams to align monitoring, evaluation, accountability and reporting approaches

Representation and Communication

- Represent JIA, together with the Country Director, in relevant donor, government, partner and coordination meetings
- Contribute programme updates and evidence for donor communication and Johanniter communications, in coordination with the Country Director and HQ

Programme Management

- Lead, supervise and support the Ukraine programme team, including two consortium coordinators, three PMEAL staff and two other project staff; set priorities and strengthen coordination across their work
- Oversee JIA’s lead-partner role in its consortia, including governance arrangements, joint planning, partner coordination, follow-up of agreed actions and timely escalation of issues
- Review programme progress, quality, risks and budgets with consortium coordinators, partners and the finance and operations teams; help resolve implementation bottlenecks
- Coordinate grant start-up, partner agreements, donor reporting and programme compliance with the responsible colleagues, and keep the Country Director informed of significant risks and decisions

**What you bring (essential unless stated otherwise):**

- University degree (BA or MSc) in a relevant field
- More than 5 years of experience in a humanitarian context, of which at least 3 years have been with an international NGO
- Substantial experience managing and developing multidisciplinary programme and PMEAL teams
- Experience leading complex, multi-partner consortia, including governance, coordination and partner relationships
- Experience with institutional donors, including proposal development, grant management and quality reporting
- Experience overseeing complex programme budgets, financial planning and donor compliance in collaboration with finance colleagues
- Experience with monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning across multiple projects
- Experience working with national partners and supporting their organisational and technical capacity
- Ability to contribute to programme strategy and ensure coherence and complementarity across a portfolio
- Strong analytical, written/oral communication and reporting skills
- Negotiation abilities and diplomatic skills
- Willingness to live and work in Kyiv and travel in a high-risk context, subject to security procedures
- Fluency in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills
- Desirable: experience in Ukraine, knowledge of Ukrainian or Russian, and experience with GFFO, BMZ or ECHO grants

**What we offer:**

- Remuneration: Competitive, attractive remuneration, in line with internal tariff and relevant previous experience
- Benefits: 13th cheque; social security; annual leave; flexible working hours, friendly and appreciative working atmosphere

jobs.title: Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Base:** Kyiv

**Starting date:** November 2026

**Contract duration:** 4 months' probation period with prolongation upon successful probation period end

**About PIN Ukraine:**

People in Need (PIN) has been active in Ukraine since early August 2014. Currently, PIN is one of the major humanitarian actors in Ukraine responding to the recent military escalation, providing humanitarian aid to conflict-affected people across Ukraine. Since 2014, PIN has implemented emergency food and cash assistance, NFI, shelter, protection, livelihoods and WASH interventions supporting 5 million vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities in urban and rural areas.

PIN is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic. PIN encourages applications from individuals of diverse backgrounds and values diversity.

**General information about the role of the person:**

Under the supervision of the Economic and Green Recovery Technical Lead, the Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator will provide technical and analytical support to the design, quality assurance, monitoring, and continuous improvement of PIN's economic recovery programs in Ukraine.

The position involves:

• supporting the development and adaptation of economic recovery methodologies, tools, and technical guidance;

• providing technical support to program teams without taking over the management of their implementation;

• supporting the development of proposals, concept notes, needs assessments, studies, and program frameworks;

• documenting lessons learned, best practices, and evidence generated within economic recovery programs;

• supporting capacity development of teams on relevant technical approaches and tools;

• participating in coordination and technical exchange with relevant internal and external stakeholders;

• supporting the Technical Lead in ensuring coherence and quality across the economic recovery program portfolio.

• conducting and supporting field-based technical work, including field visits, assessments, consultations, data collection, and technical follow-up, either jointly with or on behalf of the Technical Lead;

• engaging with external stakeholders and representing PIN’s interests in relevant technical discussions, meetings, consultations, and coordination forums, as needed

**Description of general duties:**

**1. Technical Quality and Methodology**

• Facilitate the development, analysis, and adaptation of technical approaches, methodologies, tools, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and recommendations for economic recovery programs. Maintain a clear record of methodological revisions, consolidate feedback from teams, and submit proposed changes to the Technical Lead for review before wider use.

• Analyze the technical quality, relevance, and consistency of programmatic approaches and provide recommendations for their improvement.

• Provide support to teams in adapting and aligning technical approaches across different projects and contexts.

**2. Technical Support to Program Implementation Teams**

• Participate in grant committees and conduct application assessments. Review applications and business plans against agreed eligibility and scoring criteria, assess technical feasibility and market assumptions, and document recommendations and clarification requests for committee consideration.

• Provide program teams with technical advice on the application of economic recovery methodologies and tools. Respond to technical questions during implementation, review practical examples with staff, and escalate unresolved methodological issues to the Technical Lead. Keep programme delivery decisions with the responsible implementation teams.

• Support teams in interpreting and applying technical guidance, targeting approaches and selection criteria, monitoring requirements, and program methodologies.

**3. Technical Monitoring and Quality Assurance**

• Conduct regular technical monitoring visits to program implementation regions and activity sites. Agree visit objectives with the Technical Lead and implementation teams; prepare checklists, review available project records, and consult participants, businesses, partners, and staff as relevant. Conduct visits jointly with or on behalf of the Technical Lead as agreed.

• Assess the technical quality of implementation against approved methodologies, SOPs, program frameworks, and relevant standards.

• Identify technical, methodological, and quality issues and prepare recommendations for corrective actions.

• Coordinate monitoring work with MEAL, Protection, Grants, Partnerships, and Programme Implementation as needed.

• Prepare technical monitoring reports, action lists, and recommendations for follow-up. Record findings, supporting evidence, recommended actions, responsible colleagues, and agreed timeframes. Follow up on technical improvements with the relevant teams and flag recurring or unresolved quality issues to the Technical Lead.

**4. Program Analysis, Evidence, and Learning**

• Support the development and interpretation of economic recovery indicators and monitoring tools. Work with MEAL on indicator definitions, data sources, collection methods, and interpretation of baseline, monitoring, and endline findings. Identify data gaps and limitations before drawing conclusions about results.

• Contribute to the analysis of program results, including economic impact and changes in livelihoods, income, employment, business performance indicators, and resilience, as relevant. Compare results across locations and participant groups where the data allow; examine barriers to economic recovery and explain the practical implications for programme adjustments.

• Support the identification of needs within the economic recovery sector.

**5. Program Development and Proposal Preparation**

• Support the Technical Lead and relevant program teams in developing new economic recovery concepts and project proposals.

• Participate in technical discussions during program design and implementation where specialized economic recovery expertise is required.

• Collect and analyze information needed for program design.

• Conduct stakeholder mapping in the economic recovery sector.

• Support the development of intervention logic, targeting approaches, selection criteria, technical methodologies, and monitoring systems. Prepare technical inputs on activities, expected outputs and outcomes, assumptions, risks, and resource needs. Check that proposed approaches are feasible, evidence-based, and consistent with the agreed programme framework.

• Support the development of new economic recovery initiatives in line with PIN's strategic priorities and identified needs.

**6. Needs Assessments, Research, and Analytical Work**

• Support needs assessments, market and sector analyses, and other economic recovery research to contribute to PIN’s evidence base on economic recovery in Ukraine. Help define research questions, assessment tools, stakeholder consultations, and field data collection plans. Analyse market demand, employment opportunities, business constraints, access to services, and recovery needs as relevant; validate findings with teams and stakeholders and prepare practical recommendations.

**Coordination with Programme Implementation and Livelihood Functions**

The Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator works closely with the Livelihood Coordinator and relevant Programme Implementation teams.

The Coordinator does not:

• manage the day-to-day implementation of program activities;

• replace the Livelihood Coordinator in coordination with operational departments;

• take on responsibility for logistics, procurement, finance, or administrative support to implementation;

• take on Programme Implementation's responsibility for delivering program activities;

• duplicate the operational reporting and control mechanisms of the Programme Implementation structure.

**Internal Coordination**

• Maintain regular coordination with Programme Implementation, MEAL, Grants, Partnerships, and other relevant departments. Agree technical priorities and follow-up actions, share findings that affect programme quality or reporting, and clarify responsibilities where technical and implementation functions intersect.

• Coordinate with technical colleagues in Protection, WASH, Shelter, and Education when economic recovery activities involve cross-sectoral approaches.

**External Technical Engagement**

Under the guidance of the Technical Lead:

• participate in relevant technical working groups, coordination meetings, workshops, and consultations;

• support technical communication with relevant CSOs, private sector representatives, service providers, research institutions, and other stakeholders;

• support stakeholder mapping and identification of relevant technical resources and partnerships;

• represent PIN at selected technical meetings as needed. Prepare agreed technical inputs and briefing points, document discussion outcomes, and share relevant opportunities and follow-up actions with the Technical Lead and programme teams.

**Functional Relationship with the Livelihood Coordinator**

The two positions are complementary:

**Livelihood Coordinator > Programme Implementation**

• oversight of implementation;

• coordination with operational departments;

• implementation planning and follow-up;

• resolution of operational issues;

• ensuring delivery of program activities.

**Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator > Programme Quality / Technical Function**

• technical quality;

• methodology and tools;

• technical monitoring;

• analysis and learning;

• technical capacity development;

• program improvement;

• technical input into program design.

**Development of the Role**

The position of Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator is being created to strengthen PIN Ukraine's technical capacity in the field of economic recovery.

As the economic recovery program portfolio expands, the position may gradually take on responsibility for specific technical areas or thematic components, including coordination of particular technical strands across multiple projects.

The role may also evolve toward greater responsibility for technical coordination, quality assurance, program development, and technical representation, depending on program needs and demonstrated performance.

**Team and Partner Capacity Development**

• Identify technical capacity needs of teams and partners and agree development activities with the Technical Lead.

• Deliver technical onboarding, refresher training, and mentoring on economic recovery methodologies and tools. Use practical exercises and programme examples, gather participant feedback, and provide follow-up support to help staff apply the tools consistently.

• When requested, support technical recruitment, preparation of terms of reference, and assessment of candidates’ technical skills; this does not imply line management.

• Provide technical guidance to PIN partners, support monitoring of their programme quality, and facilitate knowledge sharing.

**Documentation and Application of Learning**

• Document lessons learned, good practices, and research findings; prepare technical materials, recommendations, and internal updates.

• With MEAL, support review of baseline and endline tools and use evidence to improve programmes.

**Inclusion, Environmental Sustainability, and Accountability**

• Integrate age, gender, diversity, equality, non-discrimination, and do-no-harm principles into technical approaches and selection criteria.

• Under the Technical Lead’s guidance, support environmental sustainability and climate resilience in relevant economic recovery activities.

• Ensure accountability through appropriate communication and information sharing within PIN and with partners and communities.

• Comply with PIN policies and procedures, including Finance, Logistics, HR, and Security; report identified technical risks to the relevant responsible staff.

**Qualification Criteria:**

**Education and Speciality:**

Higher education in economics, development studies, business administration, agriculture, social sciences, or a related field.

**Required Skills and Competencies:**

- Strong analytical and methodological skills. Ability to conduct field visits, assessments, and technical monitoring. Skills in preparing technical recommendations, reports, tools, and training materials. Ability to advise teams without taking over implementation management functions. Strong communication and coordination skills. Fluency in Ukrainian and working proficiency in English.

**PIN OFFERS**:

- A competitive salary according to the People in Need salary scale in amount of **1882 EUR Gross (Based on qualifications) + 3% after probation period.**
- Opportunities for professional development through various capacity-building activities, including trainings, workshops, and seminars.
- 28 calendar days of annual leave, plus 3 additional New Year bonus leave days.
