- Conduct regular internal I-9 audits — including audits of Tier 1's completed verifications — and prepare the organization to respond to any government inspection or Notice of Inspection with confidence
- Own and oversee the U.S. background screening program, including process governance, vendor management, and continuous improvement, ensuring compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA)
- Own the Workday ↔ HireRight integration, coordinating with HR Technology, Talent Acquisition, and the vendor to ensure the integration meets compliance and operational requirements, and manage any future changes or new requirements as they arise

**Multistate Compliance & Regulatory Tracking**

- Maintain a living compliance matrix of federal, state, and local employment law obligations across all U.S. operating locations, including state-specific holidays, paid family leave requirements, and other jurisdiction-specific nuances
- Maintain clear visibility into where employees are located by state, so compliance obligations can be mapped accurately as the distributed workforce evolves
- Partner with Payroll to monitor wage-and-hour compliance — including meal and rest break requirements and timekeeping accuracy — in high-risk states such as California, proactively closing gaps before they become costly
- Monitor regulatory changes and proactively update policies, handbooks, and practices before deadlines take effect

**EEO / EEOC Compliance**

- Serve as the HR Operations focal point for EEO/EEOC-related compliance and reporting, including EEO-1/Affirmative Action Plan obligations and applicable state-level equivalents (e.g., New Jersey), monitoring where federal requirements have lapsed but state requirements may still apply
- Own California Pay Data Reporting (SB 1162) — coordinating with Payroll and People Analytics to compile accurate pay band, race/ethnicity, and sex data by job category, and managing the annual submission to California's Civil Rights Department ahead of the required deadline
- Coordinate EEO-1 reporting — data collection, validation, and submission — in partnership with People Analytics, HR Technology, and Payroll to ensure data integrity and reporting readiness
- Coordinate responses to EEOC-related requests, inquiries, or audits in partnership with Legal

**Audit, Quality Control & Vendor Management**

- Establish and execute a regular internal audit cadence across all compliance domains, identifying gaps and remediating errors before they escalate
- Manage relevant HR compliance vendors (background screening, I-9/E-Verify, and related third-party providers), monitoring performance and ensuring consistent application of compliance processes
- Identify opportunities to automate, streamline, and standardize compliance-related processes in partnership with HR Technology

**Policy and Handbook Currency**

- Own the review and update cycle for U.S. employment policies and the employee handbook, ensuring alignment with current federal, state, and local law across all jurisdictions, including state-specific and local addenda and the NY State/NYC regulatory environment
- Own a central repository for all P&C policies, driving a regular review cadence with each policy's subject-matter owner (Compensation, Benefits, Recruitment, etc.) to confirm currency and surface any conflicts between policies for resolution by the relevant owners — this role owns the system and process, not the content of policies outside employment law
- Partner with HR Communications to effectively communicate policy and handbook changes to employees and managers
- Maintain a lightweight annual review cycle for handbooks across IRC's non-U.S. operations — collecting the most current version from each country and flagging any that are overdue for update — without taking on deep ownership of non-U.S. policy content

**P&C Partner Enablement & Reporting**

- Act as a standing SME resource for P&C Partners, fielding compliance questions and providing guidance on complex or gray-area cases, and identifying the appropriate process, policy, resource, or escalation path
- Develop FAQs, guidance materials, tools, and job aids that enable P&C Partners to independently navigate common compliance questions
- Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting for HR leadership and General Counsel on compliance status, open items, training completion rates, and emerging regulatory risk

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience); law degree not required
- 5–8+ years of experience in U.S. employment and labor law compliance, with demonstrated expertise in Form I-9, E-Verify, and multistate regulatory environments
- Demonstrated experience managing background screening programs and working knowledge of FCRA requirements
- Experience supporting EEO/EEOC compliance and reporting, including EEO-1 reporting; experience with state-level pay data or pay equity reporting (e.g., California SB 1162) is a plus
- Proven experience working with employees across diverse immigration statuses, including refugees, SIV holders, parolees, green card holders, visa holders, and naturalized citizens
- Track record of building or significantly maturing a compliance program, not just maintaining one
- Experience designing and delivering compliance training for non-legal audiences, including certifying frontline staff to perform compliance-sensitive tasks
- Experience with HRIS platforms and HR technology; Workday experience strongly preferred
- Experience managing HR compliance vendors and third-party providers
- SHRM-CP/SCP, PHR/SPHR, or a specialist certification in immigration or I-9 compliance is a plus

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong working knowledge of FLSA, Title VII, FMLA, ADA, PWFA, OSHA, WARN Act, and applicable state and local equivalents, particularly New York State and NYC
- Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and operate with credibility across all levels of the organization
- Strong diplomatic and relationship-building skills, able to guide and influence without formal authority over the teams they support
- Comfortable moving between hands-on casework and enterprise-level program building

**Working Environment:**

Standard office working environment with the ability to work remote 2-3 days per week.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $95,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Regional Analyst - Sudan
jobs.body:
**About INSO**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**INSO Sudan**

INSO Sudan is currently upscaling its services to better support its 126 partners. The coordination team is based in Port Sudan, and we are opening several offices in the country. Together, we will assist NGOs working in the volatile Sudan context with reports, analysis, coordination services, and advice. Working for INSO Sudan will allow you to experience this complex environment while you support humanitarian efforts to address the challenges Sudan faces.

**Job Summary**

As a Regional Analyst, you will complement and strengthen INSO’s existing products and services by assessing regional and cross-border trends, including contextual developments and actor dynamics that have a specific impact on humanitarian safety and access in Sudan. You will produce analytical products on regional developments relevant to the Sudan programme, provide tailored analytical support to NGO partners, and contribute to relevant briefings and meetings with the Country Director, Regional Director, and other INSO teams. The position is based in Khartoum, Sudan.

**Main Responsibilities**

*Service Delivery*

- Deliver a set of products and services addressing regional security and conflict dynamics and their impact on humanitarian safety and access.
- Propose and deliver ad hoc products on emerging regional challenges to humanitarian safety and access.
- Contribute to other country office products and inform decision-making at the regional level.
- Offer a responsive, tailored analysis service directly to INSO’s NGO partners upon their request.
- Convene and contribute to regional NGO coordination meetings and fora with humanitarian counterparts to discuss regional safety and access.

*Programme Development*

- Monitor regional and cross-border developments through a diverse range of sources, such as NGOs, the UN, civil society organisations, research institutes and media outlets.
- Cultivate an active network of contacts within the broader humanitarian community as well as other relevant stakeholders for information sharing, analytical exchanges and coordination.
- Liaise and coordinate with the GAT team to enable analytical capacity building in the country office.
- Liaise with the Country Director and Regional Director for a coherent programming approach, opportunities and synergies in regional networks covering the Sudan humanitarian response.
- Effectively represent and protect INSO’s principles of independence, impartiality and neutrality as well as actively promoting INSO within the humanitarian community.

**Requirements**

- 3+ years of work experience in an analytical capacity, preferably working in conflict or post-conflict contexts
- Ability to analyse a complex set of data and translate it into relevant analysis and operational recommendations for NGOs.
- Experience working in NGOs, international organisations, consultancy, or journalism
- Exemplary command of English, both written and spoken.
- Acceptance and strong understanding of humanitarian principles
- Demonstrable understanding of humanitarian safety practices and their application
- Proficient networking, diplomatic, and representative communication skills
- Post-Graduate-level education (Masters or higher) in political science, history, or humanitarian studies, or a related field, or equivalent work experience

**Nice to have**

- Experience delivering a partner-focused advisory service
- Experience in designing and delivering products based on close partner engagement
- Existing regional experience and/or information networks
- Experience in insecure/conflict-affected environments
- Experience in staff capacity development and training
- Detailed understanding of INSO’s mandate & services

**Core Competencies**

- Integrity – Acts ethically, maintains confidentiality, and avoids or appropriately manages conflicts of interest.
- Collaboration – Builds positive working relationships, communicates respectfully, and contributes effectively to a diverse team.
- Organisation – Plans and prioritises work effectively, manages responsibilities independently, and meets deadlines.
- Adaptability – Responds positively to changing circumstances, works effectively under pressure, and takes initiative when needed.
- Communication – Communicates clearly and effectively, with courtesy, humility, and sensitivity to multicultural environments.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

**Terms & Conditions**

12-month renewable contract. For international applicants: €5000 per month salary, 4 calendar days annual leave per month (including weekends) and 7 days of R&R every 2 months with a €1250 R&R allowance each cycle, global medical coverage (excluding USA) and AD&D insurance. **Please be aware that the selection of a national candidate will be subject to the local salary and benefits scheme.**

jobs.title: Directeur.trice Général.e
jobs.body:
*Zie hieronder voor een beschrijving in het Nederlands.*

**Avocats Sans Frontières (ASF), fondée en 1992 à Bruxelles, est une ONG internationale spécialisée dans la promotion de l'accès à la justice et la défense des droits humains. ASF lutte contre les injustices au sein de nos sociétés et promeut le principe de l'État de droit fondé sur les droits humains.**

La fonction de Directeur / Directrice Général(e) s’inscrit dans le pilotage stratégique et institutionnel global du réseau international d’ASF. Elle garantit la cohérence et l’impact d’ASF, tandis que les Directeurs Régionaux et les Directeurs Pays assurent le pilotage opérationnel de leurs zones respectives. Elle contribue ainsi à renforcer l’impact des interventions d’ASF pour les bénéficiaires finaux, tout en veillant à la qualité du fonctionnement, au développement et à l’intégrité d’ASF, dans le respect de ses valeurs fondatrices

## **Objectifs principaux de la fonction**

- **Garantir la performance, l’intégrité et le développement d’ASF**, dans le respect de ses valeurs et orientations, afin de renforcer durablement son impact auprès des bénéficiaires.
- **Piloter et fédérer l’organisation**, en définissant et en assurant la mise en œuvre de la stratégie globale, en mobilisant les équipes autour de l’approche « One ASF » et en garantissant la soutenabilité économique et la maîtrise des risques.
- **Porter et développer le rayonnement d’ASF**, en assurant sa responsabilité légale, administrative et financière, en renforçant la vie associative et les relations avec les organes de gouvernance, et en représentant l’organisation auprès des partenaires, bailleurs et réseaux d’ONGI.

## **Responsabilités de la fonction**

- *Définir et piloter la stratégie globale d’ASF* : élaborer le cadre stratégique avec le Comité stratégique, assurer sa déclinaison opérationnelle dans l’ensemble de l’organisation, définir les stratégies de financement et de partenariats, et piloter les évolutions nécessaires à la pérennité et au développement d’ASF.
- *Garantir la cohérence et la performance de l’action* : coordonner le Comité de Direction et les directions régionales/pays, mettre en place les outils de pilotage et de suivi, et veiller à la cohérence des stratégies d’intervention et de leur mise en œuvre avec le projet associatif défini par le CA et l’AG.
- *Assurer la responsabilité globale des opérations et des risques* : superviser les ressources humaines, les finances (incluant la définition d’adéquation des ressources aux besoins) et les opérations, garantir la mise en œuvre des dispositifs de sécurité et apporter un soutien direct aux équipes dirigeantes en cas de crises sécuritaires, juridiques, administratives ou opérationnelles.
- *Superviser le Comité de direction* à scope international et assurer, en collaboration avec les Directeurs Régionaux et les Directeurs Pays, l'animation globale et la cohésion de l'ensemble des équipes d'ASF dans ses différents pays d'intervention.

**Advocaten Zonder Grenzen (ASF) is een internationale NGO gespecialiseerd in het bevorderen van toegang tot de rechtspraak en de verdediging van mensenrechten, opgericht in 1992 in Brussel. ASF strijdt tegen onrechtvaardigheid in onze samenlevingen en draagt het principe uit van de rechtsstaat gebaseerd op mensenrechten.**

De functie van Algemeen Directeur/Directrice situeert zich in de globale strategische en institutionele aansturing van het internationale netwerk van ASF. Ze waarborgt de samenhang en de impact van ASF, terwijl de Regionale Directeurs en de Landendirecteurs instaan voor de operationele aansturing van hun respectieve zones. Op die manier versterkt de functie de impact van de interventies van ASF voor de eindbegunstigden en waakt ze over de kwaliteit van de werking, de ontwikkeling en de integriteit van ASF, met respect voor haar waarden vooropgesteld bij de oprichting.

## **Hoofddoelstellingen van de functie**

- **De prestaties, de integriteit en de ontwikkeling van ASF waarborgen**, met respect voor haar waarden en krachtlijnen, teneinde haar impact voor de begunstigden blijvend te versterken.
- **De organisatie aansturen en verenigen**, door de globale strategie te bepalen en de uitvoering ervan te verzekeren, de teams te mobiliseren rond de "One ASF"-benadering en de economische leefbaarheid en de risicobeheersing te garanderen.
- **De uitstraling van ASF dragen en uitbouwen**, door de juridische, administratieve en financiële verantwoordelijkheid op te nemen, door het verenigingsleven en de relaties met de bestuursorganen te versterken en de organisatie te vertegenwoordigen bij partners, donoren en netwerken van internationale ngo's.

**Verantwoordelijkheden van de functie**

- *De globale strategie van ASF bepalen en aansturen*: het strategisch kader uitwerken met het Strategisch Comité, de operationele vertaling ervan in de hele organisatie verzekeren, de strategieën inzake financiering en partnerschappen bepalen en de nodige evoluties sturen voor het voortbestaan en de groei van ASF.
- *De samenhang en de performantie van de actie waarborgen*: het Directiecomité en de Regionale Directeurs en Landendirecties coördineren, sturings- en opvolgingsinstrumenten invoeren en waken over de coherentie van de interventiestrategieën en de uitvoering ervan met de visie en het project van ASF zoals bepaald door de Raad van Bestuur en de Algemene Vergadering.
- *De algemene verantwoordelijkheid voor de operaties en de risico's opnemen*: toezicht houden op de human resources, de financiën (inclusief het bepalen van de afstemming van de middelen op de noden) en de operaties, de uitvoering van de veiligheidsmaatregelen waarborgen en de leidinggevende teams rechtstreeks ondersteunen bij veiligheids-, juridische, administratieve of operationele crisissen.
- *Het Directiecomité begeleiden* op internationaal vlak en in samenwerking met de Regionale Directeurs en de Landendirecteurs instaan voor de globale dynamiek en de samenhang van alle teams van ASF in de verschillende landen waar ASF intervenieert.

jobs.title: Communications Officer
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
Communications Officer

Full-time: 37.5 hours per week

Line managed by: Communications Manager

Salary: starting at £29,000

Location: London, UK – hybrid with at least 2 days in GISF’s London office

## About GISF

The Global Interagency Security Forum (GISF) is a member-led NGO network working to strengthen security risk management across the humanitarian and development sectors. With over 150 member organisations, GISF provides resources, convening spaces, and expertise to help keep aid workers safe.

GISF also leads communications for several strategic initiatives and delivers a programme of events, campaigns, and resources that strengthen NGO security risk management.

## About the role

We’re looking for an enthusiastic and organised Communications Officer to join our friendly team. This is a varied and hands-on role that would suit someone who enjoys working with people, is confident communicating with different audiences, and is keen to strengthen their skills across digital communications, content, and events.

The Communications Officer is responsible for the day-to-day delivery of GISF’s digital communications and content. Working closely with the Communications Manager and colleagues across GISF, the postholder will manage GISF’s digital channels, produce, and publish engaging content, and support communications for GISF’s programmes, events, publications, and campaigns.

A key focus of the role is strengthening GISF’s use of digital communications and data. The postholder will monitor performance across GISF’s website, social media, and email channels, using analytics and audience insights to understand what is working and inform continuous improvements to content and channel delivery.

As part of a small Secretariat, the postholder will work across multiple projects and priorities and will need to be organised, proactive, and comfortable taking ownership of day-to-day communications delivery. The postholder will work closely with colleagues across GISF to help deliver engaging communications and to ensure our members, supporters and stakeholders stay informed and connected.

## Key responsibilities

### Digital communication and content creation

- Manage the day-to-day delivery of GISF’s digital communications across its website, social media, newsletters, and member-only community platform.
- Plan, produce, schedule, and publish digital content, adapting messaging, format, and presentation for different audiences and channels.
- Gather stories, case studies, and updates from colleagues, members, and community partners, and explore creative and multimedia approaches to communicating GISF’s work.
- Help maintain GISF’s social media channels, creating simple graphics and promotional materials using Canva and existing templates.
- Keep up to date with social media trends, platform developments, and best-practice techniques, applying learning to strengthen content and drive audience engagement.
- Manage the production and delivery of GISF’s newsletters and other email communications, including building and scheduling campaigns and maintaining mailing lists and audience segments.
- Deliver engaging communications to GISF members, working closely with the Membership/Engagement team to ensure members receive timely and relevant information about GISF activities, opportunities, and resources.

### Analytics and digital performance

- Monitor and analyse performance across GISF’s website, social media and email channels, producing regular reporting against agreed objectives and KPIs.
- Use analytics and audience insights to understand audience behaviour and inform improvements to content, formats, targeting, timing and channel delivery.
- Support the Communications Manager to evaluate communications activities and strengthen GISF’s approach to measuring communications performance and impact.
- Keep abreast of developments in digital communications, platforms and tools, identifying opportunities to strengthen GISF’s digital communications.

### Events and communications delivery

- Support the planning and delivery of events, workshops, and community engagement activities, helping with registrations, event materials, presentations, signage, and promotional resources.
- Help coordinate practical arrangements with venues, suppliers, digital agencies, and colleagues.
- Gather feedback from participants to inform future events and communications.
- Support the delivery and dissemination of GISF research and publications, including coordinating copyediting, design, and other production processes where required
- Ensure communications outputs consistently meet GISF’s editorial, brand and accessibility standards.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues across GISF to coordinate communications requirements, deadlines, and inputs.
- Help keep communications templates and shared documents organised and up to date, and support consistent ways of working.
- Respond to, or route, general communications queries received through GISF’s shared inboxes.
- Undertake other duties as may reasonably be required, consistent with the level and purpose of the role.

## Person specification

### Essential experience and skills

- Experience creating digital communications, gained through employment, internships, volunteering, freelance work or other relevant settings.
- Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to produce clear and engaging content for different audiences and digital channels.
- Strong visual communication and design skills, with experience creating engaging graphics and digital content using tools such as Canva or Adobe Creative Suite.
- Creativity and a strong visual eye, with the ability to develop engaging content ideas and present information in accessible ways.
- An understanding of digital communications and how websites, social media, and email can be used to reach and engage different audiences
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines.
- Ability to work collaboratively and communicate effectively with colleagues and external stakeholders.
- Enthusiastic, with a can-do attitude and a willingness to learn, and an ability to build positive relationships with a wide range of people, including members, partners and colleagues.
- Confidence and technical know-how for using digital tools and learning new systems.

### Desirable experience and skills

- A degree in Communications or related qualifications
- Experience working in, or an interest in, the humanitarian, development, charity or NGO sector.
- Experience using website content management systems, email marketing platforms, or digital analytics tools
- Experience producing or editing video, photography, or other multimedia content.
- Experience creating content for social media, websites or newsletters, or supporting events and community activities.
- Familiarity with website CMS systems, social media scheduling tools, CRM systems, newsletter platforms and event platforms such as Eventbrite.

### What we offer

- 25 days of annual leave increasing annually after 2 years, up to a maximum 30 days (plus bank holidays)
- Office shutdown between Christmas and New Year
- Employer Pension contributions
- A focus on professional development, including access to overseas events, workshops; and CharityComms membership for training and development opportunities, mentoring, events, resources and networking with communications professionals across the charity sector.

jobs.title: Human Resources Payroll Associate (G.5)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
## Purpose of the Post

Under the supervision of the Senior Human Resources Officer and close coordination with the HR Officer (Entitlements and Information Management), the incumbent supports the accurate, timely, and compliant administration of payroll, compensation, benefits, and staff entitlements, contributing to the effective delivery of high-quality human resources services.

### Required Competencies

- Ability to plan, organize and prioritize a high volume of tasks/transactions and manage time efficiently to meet deadlines.
- Thoroughness and meticulous attention to detail, ensuring accuracy of output.
- Ability to work effectively under pressure with a hands-on and solutions-oriented approach.
- Effective oral and written communication skills, with the ability to provide clear guidance and explain complex payroll concepts and processes in a concise and understandable manner to diverse audiences.
- Ability to work harmoniously, build and maintain effective working relationships with staff at all levels in a multicultural team.
- Ability to maintain confidentiality and to deal tactfully in all situations and interactions.

### Professional Experience

A minimum of six years of relevant experience in payroll, HR, and social security/pension administration, or related areas are essential. Experience with an international Organization, especially within the United Nations Common System, would be an asset.

### Education

A minimum of completed secondary education is required for this role. A qualification in finance or human resources (payroll) would be an added advantage.

### Language Skills

Complete proficiency in English (oral and written), including ability to draft clearly and concisely. Working knowledge of any other UN languages would be an asset.

### Other Skills

Ability to effectively use MS Office tools (Windows, Word, Power Point, Excel and standard database software). Working knowledge of SharePoint, and an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system such as SAP, Umoja, PeopleSoft or similar Payroll/HR ERP is desirable.

## Main Duties and Responsibilities

The successful candidate would provide a broad range of administrative, HR (including payroll), and financial support to the team. The incumbent will:

- Create, maintain staff appointments and related personnel data in SAP, applying the appropriate salary, benefits and entitlements for different staff categories in accordance with applicable rules and procedures.
- Liaise with the Workforce Planning team to ensure the timely transmission of all required documentation for the smooth appointment and onboarding of staff.
- Respond to staff queries on all payroll-related matters and escalate to appropriate officers in cases of complex queries.
- Prepare staff cost estimates for incoming Junior Professional Officers (JPOs) and Senior Professional Officers (SPOs) based on Member States’ requirements and their Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).
- Administer and monitor compensation and benefits actions, ensuring timely and accurate payroll processing of staff status changes, including within-grade increases, promotions, and seasonal ticket loans as applicable.
- Create and administer health insurance-related-payroll records and process related changes for newly appointed, serving and retired staff members.
- Ensure all entitlements changes are processed before the payroll cutoff date and create entries for all payroll actions in the SAP log.
- Administer staff separations and end-of-service benefits, including separation processing, repatriation-related entitlements, payment of unused annual leave and recovery or referral of outstanding obligations, as applicable.
- Conduct thorough reviews of supporting documentation to determine staff entitlement and eligibility in accordance with the Staff Regulations and Staff Rules and escalate complex cases as required.
- Coordinate with the external pension administrators and other relevant stakeholders on pension-related notifications, deductions, separations and staff queries, within established procedures.
- Maintain accurate, secure and confidential payroll and personnel records in accordance with applicable information-management and data-protection requirements.
- Assist in the onboarding of newly recruited staff members.
- Contribute to initiatives, projects, and activities of Human Resources Services.
- Perform other duties, as may be required

## **Contract Information**

\*Local status requires applicants to have unhindered permission to live and work in the UK.

jobs.title: Project Officer, Slovenia (Europe and Asia)
source: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
jobs.body:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

DCAF Ljubljana is a permanent DCAF regional office, based in Slovenia. The office is responsible for two main programmes: implementation of the Police Cooperation Convention for Southeast Europe (PCC SEE) and the Western Balkans Border Security Programme (BSP). With funding from the United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), DCAF Ljubljana is implementing the “CHAIN BiH” project, which aims to strengthen sub-national case-building and inter-agency coordination against organised immigration crime (OIC) in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a focus on Una-Sana Canton. DCAF Ljubljana is looking to employ a motivated, well-organised and positive individual to be our next **Project Officer (Europe and Asia).**

**Location: DCAF Ljubljana, Slovenia, with frequent travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina \***

**Starting date: November 2026 or upon agreement**

**Work rate: 100%**

**Duration: Fixed-term employment until 31 March 2029, with the possibility of extension \*\***

**The role**

Join DCAF Ljubljana as a Project Officer, supporting the implementation of the project “CHAIN BiH”. Reporting to the Project Manager, you will be responsible for the operational, logistical, administrative and financial support of project activities, and will contribute to monitoring, evaluation and learning, reporting and coordination with national and cantonal partners in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

**Key areas of operation**

**Project implementation support**

- Support the Project Manager in the planning, organisation and day-to-day implementation of project activities, including workshops, trainings, field visits, working meetings and meetings of the Practice Review Forum.
- Manage the logistical and administrative preparation of activities, including travel, venues, interpretation and translation, participant lists and procurement of goods and services, in line with DCAF procedures.
- Prepare background materials, agendas, presentations, minutes and summary notes of meetings and activities.
- Support the evidence-gathering and diagnostic work of the project, including the collection, organisation and basic analysis of information from the field.

**Coordination and communication**

- Maintain regular contact with focal points in partner institutions, external experts and service providers.
- Support the organisation of the participation of officers from EU Member States within the framework of the PCC SEE.

**Financial and administrative management**

- Monitor project expenditure against the approved budget in close cooperation with the Project Manager and the DCAF finance and administration team.
- Prepare, verify and file financial documentation, contracts, invoices and supporting documents in compliance with donor and DCAF requirements.
- Keep project documentation and records complete, accurate and audit-ready.

**Monitoring, reporting and visibility**

- Collect and maintain monitoring data against project indicators, including sex- and age-disaggregated data, and support the documentation of lessons learned.
- Contribute to the preparation of narrative and financial reports for the donor and DCAF management.
- Support project visibility and communication activities in accordance with donor requirements.

**Your experience**

We are looking for a motivated, well-organised and detail-oriented professional with solid experience in supporting international projects, who enjoys working in a team and in a multi-cultural institutional environment.

You bring

- University degree (Bachelor’s or higher) in a relevant field (e.g., security studies, law, social studies, international relations, public administration, economics or related disciplines)
- 3 to 5 years professional experience, including a minimum of 2 years of experience in supporting the implementation of international projects
- Experience in the organisation and logistics of events, trainings and meetings
- Experience in contributing to project monitoring and to narrative and financial reporting
- Excellent organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work independently and collaboratively in multi-cultural environments;
- Professional working proficiency in English and Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, including the ability to provide consecutive interpretation;
- Very good knowledge of Microsoft Office tools, particularly Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.

**Desirable assets**

The following would be considered an advantage:

- Experience in project administration and financial monitoring, including handling of financial documentation in line with donor requirements
- Familiarity with UK Government (FCDO)-funded programmes or other bilateral donor-funded projects
- Experience working with international organisations or EU-funded programmes
- Understanding of gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) principles and experience with collecting disaggregated data

**We offer**

At DCAF Ljubljana, you will have the opportunity to contribute to a project that supports more effective, rights-based responses to organised immigration crime and stronger security sector governance in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

We offer:

- an opportunity to work on a high-impact international project with tangible regional impact
- a rewarding, dynamic and meaningful work experience
- the chance to be part of a diverse team of collaborative, respectful, hardworking and values-driven people
- opportunity for professional growth, international networking and continuous learning
- the chance to contribute to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices

***\* The post holder is expected to undertake regular travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina, in particular to Una-Sana Canton.***

***\*\* The post remains subject to continued project funding.***
