CAFOD is committed to acting at all times in the best interests of children and vulnerable adults, seeing these interests as paramount. Any candidate offered a job with CAFOD will be expected to adhere to CAFOD’s Safeguarding policy and sign CAFOD’s Code of Behaviour as an appendix to their contract of employment and agree to conduct themselves in accordance with the provisions of these documents. This post involves contact with children, young people and vulnerable adults, or has responsibility for people who will do, and applicants will be subject to specific checks related to safeguarding issues.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references, and appropriate screening checks can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. CAFOD also participates in the [Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of, and consent to, these recruitment procedures.

jobs.title: Midterm Evaluation of a USDA McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Project in Cameroon
jobs.body:
**Please read the full TOR here (below is only a summary):** [https://nascents.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Nascent-Solutions-MGD-Cameroon-FY23-ToR-midterm-evaluation-SEPT2026.pdf](https://nascents.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Nascent-Solutions-MGD-Cameroon-FY23-ToR-midterm-evaluation-SEPT2026.pdf)

**Midterm Evaluation of a 5-year USDA McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Project in Cameroon**

**Implementer:** Nascent Solutions Inc. (Nascent)

**Funder:** United States Department of Agriculture (USDA)

**Location:** Adamawa, East, North and North West regions of Cameroon

**Duration:** January-August 2027

**Purpose of this ToR:** To solicit bids for a midterm evaluation for Nascent’s McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Project in Cameroon. This will continue a quasi-experimental evaluation set up at baseline.

**Project Description**

This is a five-year project funded under USDA’s McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Program. Implemented by Nascent, the project is designed to improve the literacy of school-age children through improved literacy instruction, student attentiveness, and student attendance. Secondarily, the project intends to increase the use of positive health and dietary practices. The project runs from 2024-2029.

**Profile of Evaluation Team**

Firms and groups of independent consultants are welcome to apply. Team member skills should be complementary, with one person identified as the Team Lead, who will bear responsibility for all work products. Combined, the team should have the following skills and attributes:

- Demonstrated experience leading complex impact evaluations.
- Demonstrated expertise in study design and sampling.
- Demonstrated experience in the development of quantitative data collection tools and managing field data using SurveyCTO and Tangerine for digital data collection.
- Demonstrated experience in using qualitative methods such as focus group discussions and key informant interviews.
- Demonstrated experience in data management and analysis using statistical software, including analyzing complex (multi-stage cluster samples) surveys.
- Demonstrated experience using propensity score matching and difference-in-differences analysis techniques.
- Demonstrated experience in concise, illuminating report writing, including data visualization.
- Demonstrated experience in training and managing field data collectors and complex logistics.
- Subject matter expertise in literacy and education.
- Subject matter expertise in maternal nutrition, child nutrition, and hygiene.
- Strong teamwork ability across cultures and time zones.
- Demonstrated cultural sensitivity and gender balance to effectively communicate with a variety of stakeholders, ranging from young students to government officials.
- Experience with EGRA.
- Experience with the Stallings teacher observations method.
- Experience with dietary diversity surveys.
- Experience with USDA McGovern-Dole projects.
- Experience in Cameroon.
- High proficiency in written and verbal French.
- High proficiency in written and verbal English.

jobs.title: Portfolio Manager, Inclusive Health Initiative (IHI) – French Speaking
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
## **About CBM**

CBM (registered as CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V.) is an international development organisation committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the persons communities of the world. Based on our Christian values and more than 100 years of professional expertise, we address poverty as a cause and a consequence of disability. We work in partnership to create an inclusive society for all.

**About the role:**  
The Portfolio Manager supports the design and delivery of Inclusive Health Initiative (IHI) programmes that contribute to broader country programme goals. Working closely with country offices, national counterparts, and partners, you will support project design, proposal development, and programme implementation while promoting high-quality programme delivery and strengthening CBM's role as a trusted partner in inclusive health.

**This position is only filled locally in one of CBM permanent established entities.** (ex: Berlin or Bensheim (Germany), UK (Cambridge or remote), the US (remote), Nairobi (Kenya), Abuja (Nigeria), Lomé (Togo), Yaoundé (Cameroon), Lusaka (Zambia), Addis Abeba (Ethiopia), Guatemala City, Kampala (Uganda), Niamey (Niger), etc.).  
Local contractual conditions of the respective country will apply. An expatriation is not intended

## **You Will:**

- Provide programmatic support in project design, ensuring alignment with the IHI strategy and global best practices in eye health, ear and hearing care, and physical rehabilitation across assigned countries.
- Guide and support IHI project planning processes, ensuring detailed planning documentation for projects in assigned countries.
- Monitor the implementation of IHI plans and projects, actively contribute to evaluations, and ensure lessons learned inform future planning.
- Deliver training to country office programme staff and partner staff on Inclusive Health-related topics, such as inclusion in health projects.
- Proactively contribute to the development of high-quality funding applications for IHI projects.
- Monitor policies, trends, data, and research in eye health, ear and hearing care, and physical rehabilitation to inform programme implementation.
- Foster a culture of learning and adaptive management within the team and across country offices.
- Support country office teams to ensure data quality and promote the use of evidence for adaptive management.
- Work closely with Advocacy and Communications colleagues to translate programme data and learning into messages that influence policy and practice.
- Represent CBM's programmatic learning and quality initiatives to external audiences, including donors, technical working groups, and other development partners, as required.
- Participate in relevant networks.
- Contribute to research and publications to strengthen the evidence base for inclusive health, where appropriate.

## **These are your qualifications**

- An advanced degree in Public Health, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.
- A minimum of 7 years of experience in international development, including at least 3 years focused on health programmes.
- A strong understanding of trends and policy frameworks in the international health sector, with sound knowledge of project cycle management and logical frameworks.
- Strong analytical skills, with the ability to synthesise complex information into clear, actionable learning.
- Proven experience in proposal writing, developing monitoring and evaluation frameworks and budgets, and designing and delivering training to build the capacity of others.
- Excellent communication, presentation, and writing skills.
- Strong self-management, time management, decision-making, and problem-solving skills, with an independent, agile, flexible, proactive, and collaborative working style.
- Fluency in French and English is required, with strong written and verbal communication skills in both languages.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
- A demonstrated commitment to disability inclusion and safeguarding principles.
- Identification with the Christian values and mandate of CBM.

## **What we offer**

- A meaningful position with a lot of creative freedom in the world's leading organisation in the field of Disability Inclusive Development
- A fair salary and other social benefits based on the local conditions in the country you apply for
- An approachable, agile organisation with self-reliant people in a diverse and collegial team and great team spirit

jobs.title: Chef·fe de délégation – République démocratique du Congo
jobs.body:
L’EPER emploie plus de 1500 personnes à titre permanent. L’EPER est active sur 24 sites en Suisse et dans plus de 35 pays à travers le monde. Elle y mène 290 programmes et projets, pour un montant total de CHF 144 millions. En 2024, le travail de l’EPER a bénéficié à environ 16 millions de personnes.

Le travail de l’organisation est porté par la vision d’un monde juste, dans lequel la paix règne, la dignité de tous les êtres humains est respectée et les moyens de subsistance naturels sont préservés. L’objectif est d’amener une transition aux niveaux social, économique et politique. L’EPER contribue à améliorer les conditions de vie des personnes en Suisse et à l’étranger et revendique leurs droits. À cette fin, elle sensibilise et mobilise.

**Une diversité vécue – L'inclusion nous tient à cœur :**  
Nous accueillons les candidatures sans distinction de sexe, de nationalité, d'origine ethnique, de religion, d'âge ou d'orientation sexuelle.

**HEKS/EPER en RDC**

Confrontée à un conflit persistant dans l'est du pays, en particulier dans le Nord-Kivu, le Sud-Kivu et l'Ituri, la République démocratique du Congo fait face à une crise humanitaire majeure marquée par des déplacements massifs de population, une insécurité alimentaire chronique et des besoins de protection considérables. HEKS/EPER y déploie un programme d'aide humanitaire et de développement en cohérence avec sa stratégie institutionnelle, en s'appuyant sur des partenaires opérationnels et stratégiques locaux et internationaux, afin d'apporter une réponse pertinente et un impact substantiel aux populations affectées, notamment dans les zones difficiles d'accès et sous-desservies.

HEKS/EPER recherche un·e Directeur pays pour la RDC afin de diriger son programme à un moment déterminant de la réponse humanitaire dans l'Est de la RDC.

Basé·e au Nord-Kivu, le/la Directeur pays assurera la direction stratégique et opérationnelle du programme, tout en jouant un rôle central dans la mobilisation de ressources, les relations avec les bailleurs et la représentation de HEKS/EPER dans le pays.

**Lieu d'affectation :** Nord-Kivu, RDC

**Déplacements :** Réguliers sur les sites du programme (Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu et Ituri), ainsi qu'à Kinshasa

**Contrat :** Temps plein, durée d'un an, renouvelable

**Prise de fonction :** 1er janvier 2026 ou à convenir

## **Chef·fe de délégation – République démocratique du Congo**

### **Votre rôle**

Vous serez chargé·e de :

- Assurer la direction stratégique et opérationnelle du programme de HEKS/EPER en RDC, avec une attention particulière aux zones difficiles d'accès et sous-desservies, en cohérence avec la stratégie et les standards de l'organisation.
- Développer et positionner des programmes pluriannuels de stabilisation et de consolidation de la paix, incluant notamment la réhabilitation d'infrastructures routières, le développement d'infrastructures hydroélectriques et l'appui à des chaînes de valeur agricoles, en coordination avec les équipes de coopération au développement de HEKS/EPER.
- Développer et gérer un portefeuille de projets cohérent, incluant la sélection des partenaires stratégiques et opérationnels.
- Assumer la responsabilité finale des finances du bureau pays et des projets, en assurant un suivi budgétaire rigoureux.
- Mobiliser les fonds nécessaires au programme en développant et en mettant en œuvre une stratégie nationale d'acquisition.
- Développer des propositions de qualité pour les bailleurs bilatéraux et multilatéraux ainsi que les fondations.
- Entretenir des relations solides avec les bailleurs institutionnels, les agences des Nations Unies et les partenaires bilatéraux et multilatéraux.
- Représenter HEKS/EPER auprès des autorités, des bailleurs, des agences onusiennes, des structures de coordination, des ONG internationales et nationales.
- Diriger, encadrer et développer les capacités de l'équipe pays, et assurer la gestion de la sécurité du personnel, des opérations et des biens.
- Garantir un programme pays de haute qualité, pertinent et financièrement soutenable.
- Assurer une coopération étroite et continue avec le siège de HEKS/EPER.

### **Ce que nous recherchons**

Vous êtes un·e professionnel·le expérimenté·e de l'humanitaire ou de la coopération internationale avec :

- Un diplôme universitaire de niveau Master, ou une expérience équivalente.
- Au minimum 5 ans d'expérience à un poste de direction dans la conception, la gestion et la mise en œuvre de projets de dans le secteur de l’aide internationale, notamment dans les zones difficiles d’accès.
- Une expérience avérée dans l'acquisition et la mise en œuvre réussies de projets financés à l'international (en consortium, via des partenaires ou en mise en œuvre directe).
- Une connaissance approfondie de l'aide humanitaire internationale et du contexte régional en RDC.
- Une expérience de travail avec les principaux bailleurs humanitaires, notamment US, ECHO, la DDC et les Nations Unies.
- Une expertise solide en gestion financière, en développement stratégique et en gestion de la sécurité.
- De solides compétences en leadership d'équipe, communication, représentation et réseautage.
- Une expérience de travail dans des contextes fragiles ou à haut risque, avec une disponibilité pour des déplacements réguliers dans les trois provinces d'intervention.

**Langues**

- La maîtrise du français est obligatoire.
- Une bonne maîtrise de l'anglais est également requise.

jobs.title: Consultant: Humanitarian Needs Assessment & Strategic Implementation Review
Research Consultancy - Local and National Actors' perspectives on Accountability of the International Aid Sector to the Localisation Agenda
jobs.body:
**1. Background**

Over the past decade, the international humanitarian and development aid sectors have established an extensive set of commitments to localisation and local leadership. Through initiatives including the Grand Bargain, the Grand Bargain Caucus on Funding for Localisation, Charter for Change and Pledge for Change, international actors have committed to shifting greater power, resources and decision-making to local and national actors (LNAs), strengthening equitable partnerships, and supporting locally led humanitarian action.

These commitments are firmly based in Danish development and humanitarian policy. Denmark is a Grand Bargain signatory and has actively promoted localisation and local leadership in international policy dialogue. Denmark's 2025 Strategy for Development Cooperation, states that Danish-supported efforts are most often managed and run by local actors, that their leadership and responsibility should be strengthened, and that funding should be channelled more directly to where it creates the greatest benefit. The strategy identifies this as the essence of localisation. Danida calls for translation of this policy direction in Danish civil society through Strategic Partnership Agreements. Danish civil society organisations are therefore expected not only to work with local partners, but to support power shifts through change in ownership, resources, leadership and influence.

As the sector reflects on ten years of the Grand Bargain and considers the future of humanitarian reform, attention is increasingly shifting from committing to localisation to ensuring that these commitments result in meaningful changes in the behaviour, decisions and institutional practices of international actors. Accountability is central to this transition and a key focus of the next iteration of the Grand Bargain.

Existing accountability mechanisms for localisation have largely centred on international actors monitoring and reporting on their own commitments through organisational reporting, collective monitoring frameworks, independent reviews and, increasingly, partner feedback mechanisms. These approaches have generated important evidence about progress and persistent gaps. However, research and successive Grand Bargain reviews point to a continuing accountability deficit. Most localisation commitments are voluntary and non-binding, and monitoring relies heavily on self-reporting by signatories. Monitoring and reporting have mainly been focused on global level approaches, making I difficult to get an overview of progress at country level. Differences in definitions, indicators and reporting methods make performance difficult to compare or independently verify. Moreover, monitoring can identify gaps but is rarely connected to agreed consequences, incentives or requirements for corrective action when commitments are not met.

It is, furthermore, unclear how local and national actors have influence over what is measured, how progress is judged and what action follows. Partner feedback and consultation create opportunities to be heard, but they do not necessarily give LNAs the leverage to know how their inputs were used. Consultations and feedback mechanisms may make LNA perspectives visible, however without establishing clear answerability to LNAs or ensuring that evidence leads to changes in leadership decisions, institutional behaviour or resource allocation. There remains limited consolidated understanding of how LNAs find that international actors should hold themselves accountable and be held accountable.

Save the Children Denmark is therefore commissioning a small-scale study to examine localisation accountability from the perspective and experience of local and national actors. The study will explore existing LNA-led and LNA-informed accountability practices, examine what LNAs consider meaningful accountability for localisation commitments, how LNAs find that international aid actors should hold themselves to account and be held accountable, and identify what role LNAs could play in how international actors are accountable.

The study is not an assessment or evaluation of individual international organisations or existing or emerging LNA platforms, such as National Reference Groups (NRGs). Its primary purpose is to produce a small-scale learning paper for humanitarian actors committed to the localisation agenda.

However, it should generate practical recommendations for what the findings imply for how international humanitarian actors engage with and listen to LNAs when holding themselves accountable to the localisation agenda.

**2. Purpose of the study**

The study seeks to understand what local and national aid actors consider meaningful accountability for international actors’ commitments to the localisation and local leadership agenda.

Given the learning study is small-scale, it will not assess the full range of localisation commitments or map every accountability initiative globally and in-country. Rather, it will focus on the relationship between LNA localisation framing and input and international actors’ decisions, behaviour and follow-up.

Specifically, the study will examine:

1.What mechanisms do LNAs think are working well or have the potential to work well on accountability to the localisation agenda, and which are considered insufficient?

2\. Where do LNAs find they are able to influence with regard to accountability approaches, and where do they not?

3\. How do LNAs feel international actors can be more effectively held to account?

The study should conclude by identifying practical implications for international humanitarian actors.

**3. Scope of work**

The study will explore the overarching question:

***What does meaningful accountability to the localisation agenda look like from the perspective of local and national actors?***

The study will focus primarily on the experience and perspectives of local and national actors rather than on international organisations' internal accountability systems.

It should examine both formal and informal ways in which LNAs currently seek to influence how international actors are accountable to localisation commitments and narrow in on an illustrative selection of mechanisms globally and in-country through which LNAs may influence international actors' accountability. These may include:

\- partner feedback and partnership review mechanisms,

\- LNA networks, alliances and collective advocacy,

\- localisation platforms and national reference groups,

\- representation in policy dialogues, coordination and governance structures,

\- locally led monitoring, scorecards or accountability mechanisms,

\- Pledge for Change/PALM and other partner-informed accountability approaches,

\- Grand Bargain monitoring and review processes, and National Reference Groups (NRGs),

\- dialogue with donors and international organisations,

\- informal relationship-based accountability.

The illustrative mechanisms should be selected for their potential to show what LNAs consider to be working well and could potentially work well or insufficient, and where LNAs are and are not able to influence accountability approaches. The study is not expected to map or evaluate all mechanisms in the sector globally and in-country. It should explore both existing practice and LNA views on how international actors can be held more effectively to account. Particular attention should be paid to the distinction between participation in accountability processes and actual influence over decisions, responses and follow-up.

The study should not duplicate existing surveys of LNA perceptions of localisation. It should consolidate such data points and focus specifically on the accountability relationship between LNAs and international actors and the mechanisms through which LNA perspectives can influence international practice.

A full mapping of accountability mechanisms for localisation commitments across the sector globally and in-country is out of scope, as well as assessments of individual organisations full accountability mechanisms.

Two light touch country-cases, one with and one without an established National Reference Group, will provide contextualised sources of evidence for the study. One of these will be undertaken in-country separately by Save the Children Denmark and is not part of the consultant’s data-collection responsibilities. The consultant should draw on both light touch country cases, one undertaken in-country by Save the Children and one undertaken remotely by the consultant, as illustrative country-level input.

**4. Key questions to address**

The study should organise its analysis around the following three core questions:

1. What mechanisms do LNAs think are working well or have the potential to work well on accountability to the localisation agenda, and which are considered insufficient?
    
    a. What makes formal and informal existing mechanisms credible, useful or ineffective from an LNA perspective?
2. Where do LNAs find they are able to influence accountability approaches, and where do they not?
3. How do LNAs feel international actors can be more effectively held to account?
    
    a. What role should different entities of the humanitarian eco-system have to hold international actors accountable to the localisation agenda?
    
    b. What practical changes, incentives, consequences or follow-up arrangements would strengthen accountability to LNAs?

**5. Methodology**

The study should combine a desk review of existing evidence with targeted qualitative inquiry and LNA validation. It should build on existing evidence and examine a small number of illustrative accountability mechanisms rather than attempt a comprehensive mapping or evaluation of the sector.

The methodology should include, at minimum:

\- an inception phase to refine the analytical framework, terminology, sampling and criteria for selecting the illustrative mechanisms,

\- incorporation of evidence from a light touch country case conducted separately by Save the Children Denmark. The light touch country case is expected to comprise interviews for example with representatives of LNAs, national coordination platforms/NRGs and Localisation Labs. The consultant will not conduct these interviews, but should analyse and triangulate the material with the other study data and identify where it supports, qualifies or contrasts with the wider findings,

\- a light touch country case, (ensuring that the country cases cover a country with a well-established National Reference Group and one without a National Reference Group),

\- qualitative interviews, with the substantial majority undertaken with LNAs and representatives of LNA networks, platforms or locally led initiatives, including but not exclusively LNAs partnering with Save the Children Denmark.

The methodology should explain how LNA perspectives will influence the analytical framework, interpretation of findings and recommendations, rather than treating LNAs only as interview respondents.

During inception, Save the Children Denmark and the consultant should agree the format and timing for transferring the light touch country case material, and how it will be analysed, referenced and reported in line with the consent and confidentiality arrangements used for those interviews.

**6. Deliverables**

\- Inception report, including refined research questions, analytical framework, desk review approach, sampling strategy, methodology and detailed timeline. The inception report should specify how the country cases will be integrated into the analysis

\- Short emerging findings debrief with Save the Children Denmark’s refernce group,

\- Draft report, including findings, illustrative examples of accountability approaches and emerging implications.

\- Final report, including:

- executive summary,
- synthesis of existing evidence,
- LNA perspectives on the aspects of the localisation and local leadership agenda for which international actors should be held accountable,
- assessment of the accountability mechanisms that LNAs consider to be working well or insufficient,
- analysis of where LNAs are and are not able to influence accountability approaches, including barriers and enabling conditions,
- recommendations for how international actors can be more effectively held to account,
- Brief presentation of findings for Save the Children Denmark and, where appropriate, external sector audiences.

The final report should be suitable for external publication and should seek to contribute to wider sector learning on localisation and accountability.

**7. Timeline**

\- The work will be undertaken from October to December 2026.

\- Final report submission: ***December 2026***.

**8. Qualifications Required**

The consultant/consultancy team should demonstrate the following qualifications:

Essential

- Strong knowledge of global South based perspectives on local leadership,
- Proven experience working with or undertaking research with local and national actors and Global South-based organisations,
- Strong knowledge of localisation commitments and frameworks, including the Grand Bargain, Pledge for Change and related sector initiatives,
- Demonstrated experience researching accountability, power relations and local leadership,
- Strong understanding of the political and power dimensions of localisation and international-local relationships,
- Demonstrated qualitative research skills, including evidence synthesis, interviewing and analysis,
- Experience translating research findings into practical recommendations for international organisations and the wider aid sector,
- Excellent English writing, presentation and stakeholder-engagement skills.

The commissioning team particularly welcomes proposals from Global South-based consultants, researchers or organisations and collaborative teams that demonstrate meaningful LNA leadership of the research.

Total Budget: ***200.000 DKK (approx. 30.000 USD)***

jobs.title: Chargé(e) d’Administration et Finances
jobs.body:
## Contexte

Interpeace est une organisation intemationale de consolidation de la paix qui soutient des initiatives de consolidation de la paix menées localement dans le monde entier. Interpeace adapte son approche à chaque société et veille à ce que son action soit menée localement. En étroite collaboration avec ses equipes et partenaires locaux, Interpeace développe des programmes de consolidation de la paix et soutient la mise en place de processus de changement qui relient les communautés locales, la société civile, le gouvernement et la communauté intemationale.

En sa qualite de partenaire strategique des Nations Unies, Interpeace a son siege a Geneve, en Suisse, et possede des bureaux dans le monde entier.  
Pour plus d'informations sur Interpeace, veuillez visiter [www.interpeace.org](http://www.interpeace.org)

## Objet et aperçu général

Sous la supervision du gestionnaire principal des finances et de l'administration, le/la Chargé(e) de l’Administration et finances aura la responsabilité de veiller à la qualité des données financières des partenaires œuvrant dans la zone qui lui sera assignée. Il/Elle appuiera en outre dans la gestion administrative de sa zone et contribuera dans la gestion budgétaire de l’organisation en veillant sur les affectations budgétaires ainsi que les suivis budgétaires des partenaires.  
Il/Elle aura des rôles à jouer dans le secteur de la comptabilité, l’administration, les contrôles internes, les audits, l’appui à la gestion budgétaire et dans le renforcement des capacités des partenaires. Mais aussi dans le suivi et le soutien de la mise en œuvre du programme en veillant au respect des politiques internes, des réglementations des bailleurs de fonds et de la législation locale en RD Congo.

## Position au sein de l’organisation

Le/La chargé(e) d’Administration et finances est membre de la section financière de l'unité de soutien global, qui apportera un appui opérationnel dans le domaine d'administration, de finances et appui à l’audit. L'unité de soutien administratif mondial est dirigée depuis le bureau du siège à Genève, bien que les membres de l'équipe soient basés dans différents pays.  
Sous la supervision régulière du gestionnaire principal des finances et de l'administration, le /la chargé (e) d’administration et des finances travaille en étroite collaboration avec les autres membres de l’équipe opérationnelle, notamment le personnel administratif, les ressources humaines, le personnel du programme et le personnel des partenaires afin de créer une fonction financière et administrative plus efficace et efficiente pour un Interpeace agile, réactif et performant.

Taches Spécifiques

Sous orientations et en collaboration avec le gestionnaire principal des finances et de l'administration, ce poste aura comme objectifs principaux :

- Garantir l'exactitude de toutes les informations et de tous les documents comptables enregistrés dans le logiciel de comptabilité Quick Books pour les partenaires de mise en œuvre et Sun Systems pour Interpeace, tout en tenant compte du respect strict des procédures internes.
- Centraliser toutes les importations comptables de sa zone, pour ce qui est des partenaires et bureaux Interpeace sur une base mensuelle et dans les délais impartis.
- Réconcilier tous les paiements effectués par Mobile Money sur une base mensuelle.
- Apporter un appui au Gestionnaire Principal des Finances et Administration dans la réalisation des audits de projets et des audits statutaires de consolidation dans les délais impartis.
- Apporter un appui dans le suivi budgétaire des partenaires de sa zone : produire et partager le BvA avec une analyse détaillée après concertation et validation du gestionnaire principale de l’administration et finances.
- Fournir sur une base mensuelle, en temps opportun, des dossiers financiers révisés précis et complets et des documents justificatifs pour les partenaires et/ou le bureau assigné par le biais de l'outil en ligne pour la consolidation.
- Suivre avec les financiers des partenaires et/ou du bureau la mise en œuvre des recommandations de contrôle interne jusqu'à leur résolution (contrôles mensuels, audits internes et externes, revues internes, etc.)
- Avec les conseils du gestionnaire principal des finances et de l'administration, soutenir la performance d'Interpeace en examinant les politiques et les procédures, en offrant une formation au personnel et/ou aux partenaires, en surveillant les finances ou en évaluant les risques au sein des partenaires et/ou des bureaux assignés.
- Appui administratif dans sa zone en assurant les contacts avec les différents services étatiques ainsi que les partenaires externes conformément au besoin qui se présente.  
    Garantir l’exécution des opérations d’approvisionnement conformément à la procédure en vigueur.

### Compétences techniques requises :

- Maîtrise des outils comptables et de gestion financière (ex. : QuickBooks,, Sun System).
- Connaissance approfondie des normes comptables.
- Excellente maîtrise d’Excel et des outils bureautiques (Word, PowerPoint).
- Capacité à établir des rapports financiers clairs et fiables.
- Bonne compréhension des processus administratifs et financiers des ONG Internationales.

### Qualités personnelles :

- Rigueur, sens de l’organisation et discrétion.
- Esprit d’analyse et capacité à résoudre les problèmes de manière proactive.
- Bonne relationnel et aptitude à travailler en équipe.
- Capacité à gérer le stress et les priorités.
- Intégrité et sens de l’éthique professionnelle.

### Expériences souhaitées :

- Minimum 3 à 5 ans d’expérience dans un poste similaire, idéalement dans une ONG.
- Expérience en gestion opérationnelle des partenaires de mise en œuvre et des projets.
- Une expérience dans la gestion de fonds de bailleurs internationaux constitue un plus.

### Formation :

- Titulaire d’un Bac +5 en gestion financière, finance d’entreprise ou dans un domaine pertinent en lien avec les missions du poste, ou justifiant d’une expérience professionnelle significative dans le domaine.

*Interpeace attache de I 'importance à la diversite de son personnel et vise à atteindre une plus grande parite hommes-femmes à taus les niveaux de son travail.*

## Compétences d'Interpeace

- Collaboration
- Communication
- Recherche de résultats
- Adaptabilité et apprentissage continu
- Respect de la diversité

Facteurs de réussite :

- Excellentes compétences sociales et interculturelles, compétences de communication exceptionnelles pour une variété de parties prenantes de différents horizons ;
- Approche flexible pour travailler dans un contexte en évolution et capacité à livrer sous pression et dans des délais serrés ;
- Compétences exceptionnelles de développement des réseaux relationnels et de mise en confiance
- Créatif avec un engagement en faveur de l'inclusion et développement de consensus;
- Compétences exceptionnelles dans la coordination de processus complexes et sensibles et la conception de processus participatifs ;
- Être de bonne intégrité et forte sensibilité aux différences de culture, de genre, de religion, de sexualité, de nationalité et d’âge.
- Personnalité équilibrée et calme avec tact

### Désire

- Forte attention aux détails et une capacité à travailler de manière autonome et sous pression ;
- Esprit ouvert, créatif, flexible et orienté vers la recherche de solutions lorsqu’un problème se pose ;
- Bonne intégrité et forte sensibilité aux différences de culture, de genre, de religion, de race, de nationalité et d’âge ;
- Facteur de succès
- Identifie et adhère aux valeurs fondamentales et aux principes de travail d’Interpeace
- Engagement pour l’inclusion ;
- Un penseur novateur et critique doté de vastes compétences en résolution de problèmes

*Interpeace attache de l’importance à la diversité de son personnel et vise à atteindre une plus grande parité hommes-femmes à tous les niveaux de son travail.*

jobs.title: Strategic Planning and Projects Management Coordinator – (f/m/x) – MSF Belgium
jobs.body:
**CONTEXT**

A qualitative, lean, professional, and cost-effective supply chain is essential to enable MSF activities and ensure that critical resources are delivered efficiently and effectively to those in need, regardless of context or operational complexity.

OCB Supply Chain comprises several sites and segments, in the countries where we operate (including projects and capital), in regional hubs (for instance in Kenya and South Africa), in Europe with a global range (MSF Supply in Belgium). The Supply Chain Department defines the global strategy of this supply chain, pilots its performance, and ensures that each site has the relevant support for its development.

Supply Chain is a network of people, organizations, resources, processes, activities, and tools working together so that supply meets demand.

The technical domains to design and run a Supply Chain include procurement, warehousing, transport, customs, demand planning & inventory management, supply information systems, supply processes synchronization and user service management.

As a **Strategic Planning and Projects Management Coordinator**, you lead the strategic planning and project management office (PMO) function for the Supply Chain department of the **Operational Centre Brussels** and the joint Supply ecosystem with **Ubuntu Operational Directorate.** You support the Supply Chain Management Team in ensuring that priorities in countries of operation, departmental ambitions, and strategic initiatives across the MSF movement are aligned and fully operational.

You steer the Supply Chain department's strategic planning and budgeting cycles, helping transform the strategic ambitions of the Operational Centre Brussels, Ubuntu Operational Directorate and the wider MSF movement (including SPARC and Supply Chain Transformation initiatives) into measurable roadmaps. In doing so, you ensure coherence, impact, and long-term sustainability across Supply Chain activities and may contribute to the formalization of inter-operational directorate partnerships.

Occasionally, you provide strategic planning and PMO support to other MSF units, including departments within Operational Centre Brussels, the General Direction and the International Office.

You will report to the Supply Chain Director. You will have no team to directly manage.

**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Planning and Strategic Cycles**

- Lead the Supply Chain contribution to MSF's strategic planning cycles
- Ensure that strategic ambitions from countries of operation, Operational Centre Brussels, Ubuntu Centre, the European Supply Chain Centre and the Supply Chain department are translated into and integrated within Supply Chain roadmaps
- Monitor the implementation of strategic priorities and ensure alignment between departmental objectives and organizational ambitions

**Project Management Office**

- Lead the Supply Chain Project Management Office (PMO) and set project/scrum management standards across the department
- Monitor initiative prioritization, interdependencies, risks and resource allocation to ensure timely delivery of value
- Coach and support Supply Chain staff involved in project delivery, using both agile and waterfall methodologies
- Promote effective change management practices across projects and initiatives
- Lead the Supply Chain budgeting and prioritization process at headquarters
- Capture priorities from countries of operation and ensure alignment with departmental ambitions
- Provide the Supply Chain Management Team with the information required to assess priorities and arbitrate trade-offs where necessary

**Data-Driven Strategy and Decision Support**

- Develop and maintain portfolio performance and strategy analytics
- Provide timely and reliable qualitative and quantitative insights to support governance and decision-making bodies, including to the Supply Chain Management Team
- Identify trends, risks and opportunities, and recommend actions to support strategic objectives

**Inter-Operational Center Collaboration and Representation**

- Act as the focal point for Supply Chain participation in selected inter-operational directorate initiatives.
- Contribute to the negotiation and formalization of collaborative agreements and partnerships, such as the Ubuntu Common Supply Chain Ecosystem
- Represent Supply Chain interests in selected cross-organizational strategic discussions and working groups.

**Strategic Framework for Countries of Operation**

- Oversee the development and maintenance of a framework for multi-year strategic planning in countries of operation
- Ensure strategic coherence across countries of operation and facilitate the integration of operational priorities into departmental planning cycles

**Organisational Transformation and Change Adoption**

- Support the implementation of change management strategies within the Supply Chain department and countries of operation
- Facilitate the adoption of new ways of working, processes and organizational changes
- Contribute to transformation initiatives that strengthen the effectiveness and sustainability of Supply Chain operations

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Education & Experience**

- Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in program/portfolio management, ideally using waterfall and agile methodologies and within an international environment
- An advanced certification in program, portfolio or project management is a strong asset
- Proven experience in change management is a strong asset. Relevant certification is an asset
- Experience in humanitarian settings is a strong asset
- Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Strategy, or a related field is an asset
- Experience in developing and implementing complex supply chain strategies is an asset

**Competencies**

- Strong analytical and strategic skills
- Ability to apply systems thinking and data-driven decision-making
- Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills
- Organizational change leadership capabilities
- Proven ability to influence and drive change in complex environments
- Strong facilitation skills
- Cross cultural awareness and ability to work in multicultural environments

**Languages**

- Proficiency in English, written and spoken, is mandatory
- French is a strong asset, other languages (Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese) are an asset

**CONDITIONS**

- Expected starting date: asap
- Location: Brussels, Belgium
- Contract type: Open-ended contract, full-time
- Salary according to MSF-OCB grid
- Homeworking is possible as per MSF policy
- Meal Vouchers – Hospital Insurance (DKV) – Pension Plan – 100% reimbursement for public transportation costs
- *Adhere to the MSF principles and to our managerial values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust and Empowerment*
- *Adhere to the MSF Behavioral Commitments*

**Deadline for applications: 22 October 2026**

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) Officer (Goma, DRC)
jobs.body:
**Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) Officer – DRC**

**Organization:** Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC)  
**Duty Station:** Goma RDC  
**Reports to:** Senior Program Officer  
**Travel:** Sud Kivu, Ituri et Nord Kivu

**A propos CIVIC**

Le Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) est une organisation internationale à but non lucratif, présente dans le monde entier, qui œuvre pour améliorer la protection des civils pris dans des zones de conflit. CIVIC aspire à un monde où aucun civil ne subit de préjudice du fait d'un conflit. Notre mission consiste à soutenir les communautés touchées par les conflits dans leur quête de protection, ainsi qu'à renforcer la volonté et les capacités des acteurs armés pour prévenir les atteintes aux civils et y réagir. Nous défendons l'idée qu'aucun civil pris dans un conflit ne doit être ignoré et nous agissons en tant que conseillers, proposant des solutions concrètes pour prévenir et traiter les préjudices subis par les civils. Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur [https://civiliansinconflict.org/](https://civiliansinconflict.org/)

**Resumé du poste**

Le/la Chargé(e) du Suivi, de l’Évaluation et de l’Apprentissage (MEL) appuiera les programmes de CIVIC en République démocratique du Congo en renforçant la capacité de l’organisation à produire, analyser et utiliser des données probantes afin d’améliorer les résultats en matière de protection des civils.

Le/la Chargé(e) du MEL développera et assurera la maintenance de systèmes efficaces de suivi et d’évaluation, et veillera à ce que les données des programmes, les perspectives des communautés, l’analyse du contexte et les enseignements tirés soient utilisés pour éclairer l’adaptation des programmes, l’apprentissage, la stratégie et la prise de décision.

En étroite collaboration avec les équipes de programme, les partenaires et les collègues concernés de CIVIC, le/la Chargé(e) du MEL contribuera à l’ensemble du cycle des programmes — de la conception et de la mise en œuvre au suivi, à l’évaluation, à la réflexion, à l’adaptation et à la production de rapports — en mettant particulièrement l’accent sur la compréhension de ce qui évolue, pour qui, comment et pourquoi, ainsi que sur la manière dont le travail de CIVIC contribue à renforcer la sécurité des civils.

**Responsabilités clés**

1. **Suivi et mesure de la performance**

- Appuyer l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre des plans de suivi, d’évaluation et d’apprentissage (MEL), des théories du changement, des cadres de résultats et des cadres de mesure de la performance.
- Accompagner les équipes dans l’élaboration d’indicateurs pertinents permettant de mesurer les activités, les produits/résultats immédiats et, lorsque cela est approprié, les changements en matière de connaissances, d’attitudes, de comportements, de pratiques, de relations, de politiques et de résultats en matière de protection des civils.
- Élaborer, adapter et assurer la mise à jour des outils et systèmes de suivi et de collecte des données.
- Appuyer le personnel et les partenaires dans la collecte, la compilation, le nettoyage et l’analyse des données quantitatives et qualitatives.
- Effectuer ou appuyer les missions de suivi et de vérification sur les sites de mise en œuvre des programmes.
- Suivre les progrès réalisés par rapport aux objectifs fixés, identifier les lacunes dans la mise en œuvre ainsi que les tendances émergentes, et fournir aux équipes de programme des analyses et des recommandations.
- Tenir à jour des bases de données de suivi et des systèmes de suivi des performances, en veillant à leur exactitude et à leur actualisation régulière.

**2. Évaluation et production de données probantes**

- Appuyer la réalisation des études de référence (baseline), du suivi des effets/résultats, des évaluations finales (endline), des revues et des évaluations de programmes.
- Contribuer à la définition des questions d’évaluation, des méthodologies, des outils de collecte des données et des cadres d’analyse.
- Appuyer la collecte et l’analyse des données quantitatives et qualitatives.
- Contribuer à l’analyse des résultats attendus et inattendus ainsi que des changements dans les comportements, les pratiques et les réponses des parties prenantes, lorsque cela est pertinent.
- Veiller à ce que les points de vue et les expériences des communautés soient intégrés aux processus d’évaluation et d’apprentissage.
- Appuyer l’analyse de la contribution de CIVIC aux changements observés, tout en tenant compte du contexte et des autres facteurs susceptibles d’avoir influencé ces changements.
- Traduire les résultats des évaluations en recommandations claires, concrètes et directement exploitables pour l’adaptation des programmes et l’orientation stratégique.

**3. Apprentissage et programmation adaptative**

- Faciliter et/ou appuyer les sessions de revues post action (After Action Reviews), les sessions d’apprentissage et les revues de programmes.
- Aider les équipes à évaluer ce qui était prévu, ce qui s’est réellement passé, ce qui a changé, les raisons pour lesquelles les résultats ont été obtenus ou non, ainsi que les ajustements à apporter.
- Identifier, documenter et partager les enseignements tirés, les pratiques prometteuses, les innovations, les difficultés rencontrées et les résultats inattendus.
- Accompagner les équipes dans la transformation des données probantes et des enseignements tirés en adaptations concrètes des programmes.
- Assurer le suivi des principales recommandations issues des revues et des évaluations.
- Identifier les enseignements susceptibles d’être pertinents pour différents programmes, zones géographiques et domaines thématiques.
- Promouvoir l’utilisation des données probantes et de la réflexion dans la planification des programmes et la prise de décisions stratégiques.
- Appuyer les approches de gestion adaptative permettant de répondre aux évolutions du contexte, aux risques, aux opportunités et aux nouvelles données disponibles.

**4. Apprentissage et retours axés sur la communauté**

- Appuyer les mécanismes de collecte et d’analyse des retours d’information des communautés, de leurs points de vue et de leurs perceptions en matière de sécurité et de protection.
- Aider les équipes à évaluer si les interventions restent pertinentes au regard des priorités identifiées par les communautés affectées.
- Veiller à ce que les retours d’information des communautés soient pris en compte dans les revues et l’adaptation des programmes.
- Appuyer l’identification et la documentation des changements significatifs qui pourraient ne pas être pris en compte par les indicateurs standards.
- Promouvoir des approches éthiques, inclusives et sensibles aux conflits dans la collecte des données et l’engagement auprès des communautés.
- Veiller à ce que les activités de suivi, d’évaluation et d’apprentissage (MEL) n’entraînent pas de risques supplémentaires pour les communautés, les partenaires ou les personnes concernées.

**5. Gestion des connaissances et partage de données probantes**

- Élaborer et contribuer à la production de supports d’apprentissage, notamment des notes d’apprentissage, des études de cas, des récits de changements/résultats, des synthèses de données probantes et des documents présentant les enseignements tirés.
- Documenter les changements significatifs, les enseignements émergents et les données probantes issus des programmes de CIVIC.
- Organiser et maintenir les ressources de suivi, d’évaluation et d’apprentissage (MEL) ainsi que les ressources d’apprentissage, conformément aux exigences de CIVIC en matière de gestion de l’information.
- Appuyer le partage interne des connaissances et les communautés de pratique.
- Identifier les données probantes et les enseignements susceptibles d’éclairer le travail plus large de CIVIC en matière de plaidoyer, de politiques et de programmation.
- Contribuer à l’apprentissage organisationnel de CIVIC aux niveaux national, régional et mondial.

**6. Qualité, gestion et reporting des données**

- Mettre en place et maintenir des processus d’assurance qualité des données et effectuer régulièrement des contrôles de la qualité des données.
- Identifier et corriger les incohérences, les lacunes et les erreurs dans les données des programmes.
- Tenir à jour les bases de données appropriées et veiller à la bonne documentation des sources de données et des méthodes de collecte.
- Veiller à une désagrégation appropriée des données lorsque cela est pertinent et peut être réalisé en toute sécurité.
- Maintenir des normes appropriées en matière de stockage, de confidentialité et d’accès aux données, en particulier pour les informations sensibles.
- Préparer des rapports de suivi, des mises à jour sur les performances, des tableaux de bord et des visualisations de données.
- Contribuer, au moyen de données probantes et d’analyses MEL, aux rapports destinés aux bailleurs de fonds ainsi qu’à d’autres rapports externes.
- Transformer des données complexes en résultats clairs et en recommandations concrètes et directement exploitables.

**7. Renforcement des capacités et collaboration**

- Fournir un accompagnement, un appui technique et des conseils aux équipes de programme et aux partenaires sur les approches, outils et processus de suivi, d’évaluation et d’apprentissage (MEL).
- Former le personnel et les partenaires à la collecte des données, à la qualité des données, au suivi ainsi qu’à l’utilisation des données probantes.
- Renforcer les capacités des partenaires à mettre en place et à utiliser des systèmes MEL appropriés.
- Promouvoir des approches MEL pratiques, simples et faciles à utiliser.
- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes chargées des Programmes, de la Protection, du Plaidoyer et des Opérations, ainsi qu’avec les équipes régionales et mondiales concernées de CIVIC.
- Veiller à ce que les considérations relatives au MEL soient intégrées dès le départ dans la conception et la mise en œuvre des programmes.

**8. Protection, éthique et sensibilité aux conflits**

- Appliquer les principes consistant à Do No Harm, de consentement éclairé, de confidentialité et de recherche éthique dans le cadre de toutes les activités de suivi, d’évaluation et d’apprentissage (MEL).
- Évaluer et atténuer les risques liés à la collecte de données dans les environnements affectés par les conflits.
- Protéger, lorsque cela est nécessaire, l’identité et les informations relatives aux personnes et aux communautés.
- Veiller à ce que les activités de MEL n’exposent pas les communautés, les partenaires ou le personnel à des risques supplémentaires en matière de protection ou de sécurité.
- Respecter les politiques de CIVIC relatives à la protection contre les abus et l’exploitation, à la protection des données, à la conduite professionnelle, à la prévention de l’exploitation et des abus sexuels (EAS), ainsi qu’au harcèlement et à la discrimination.

**Qualifications & Expériences**

- Diplôme de niveau Master (Bac+5) en suivi et évaluation, statistiques, sciences sociales, développement international, méthodes de recherche, économie, politiques publiques ou dans un domaine connexe. Un diplôme de niveau Master constitue un atout.
- Au moins 5 ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans le domaine du suivi, de l’évaluation et de l’apprentissage (MEL), de la recherche, de la gestion des données ou dans un domaine connexe.
- Expérience avérée dans la conception et la mise en œuvre de systèmes, cadres et outils de MEL.
- Solides compétences en matière de collecte et d’analyse de données quantitatives et qualitatives.
- Expérience dans la facilitation de processus d’apprentissage, de réflexion ou de revue de programmes.
- Expérience professionnelle auprès d’ONG, d’organisations humanitaires, de protection, de défense des droits humains, de consolidation de la paix ou de la société civile.
- Une expérience dans des contextes touchés par les conflits ou fragiles est fortement souhaitée ; une expérience en République démocratique du Congo (RDC) ou dans la région des Grands Lacs constitue un atout.
- Une expérience de travail avec des partenaires locaux constitue un atout.

**Compétences techniques et fondamentales**

- Solide compréhension des principes et des approches de suivi, d’évaluation et d’apprentissage (MEL).
- Expérience dans l’élaboration de théories du changement, de cadres de résultats, d’indicateurs et de plans MEL.
- Solides compétences en matière d’analyse, de recherche et d’interprétation des données.
- Excellente maîtrise d’Excel et expérience avec des plateformes numériques de collecte de données telles que KoboToolbox, ODK ou des outils équivalents.
- Une expérience en visualisation des données et/ou avec des logiciels statistiques constitue un atout.
- Excellentes compétences en rédaction de rapports, en communication et en facilitation.
- Capacité à traduire les données probantes en recommandations pratiques et en adaptations concrètes des programmes.
- Bonne compréhension de la gestion adaptative, des principes de protection, de la sensibilité aux conflits et de la collecte éthique des données.
- Sens aigu du détail, esprit critique, capacité à collaborer, intégrité et respect de la confidentialité.
- Capacité à travailler de manière autonome et efficace dans des environnements complexes et en évolution rapide.

**Langues**

- Excellente maîtrise du français, à l'écrit comme à l'oral.
- Bonne connaissance de l'anglais.
- La connaissance du swahili et/ou d'autres langues locales pertinentes constitue un atout.

**À quoi ressemble la réussite**

La réussite dans ce poste ne sera pas évaluée uniquement au regard de la production de rapports ou de la tenue des bases de données de suivi. Le/la Chargé(e) du Suivi, de l’Évaluation et de l’Apprentissage (MEL) sera considéré(e) comme ayant réussi lorsque :

- Les équipes de CIVIC disposent d’informations fiables et disponibles en temps utile sur la mise en œuvre et les résultats des programmes ;
- Les résultats du suivi et des évaluations sont régulièrement utilisés pour éclairer la prise de décision ;
- Les points de vue des communautés contribuent de manière significative à l’apprentissage et à l’adaptation des programmes ;
- CIVIC capitalise systématiquement les ensignements tirés de son engagement auprès des communautés, des acteurs armés et des décideurs ;
- Les programmes sont adaptés sur la base des données probantes et de l’évolution du contexte du conflit ;
- Les données probantes contribuent à améliorer la compréhension, par CIVIC, de ce qui permet de renforcer la sécurité des civils ;
- Le MEL est intégré à toutes les étapes du cycle des programmes, notamment leur conception, leur mise en œuvre, les processus de réflexion et la prise de décision ;
- Les enseignements tirés des différents programmes contribuent à l’apprentissage organisationnel global et, lorsque cela est pertinent, au travail de CIVIC en matière de plaidoyer et de politiques publiques.

CIVIC est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances et s'engage à favoriser un environnement diversifié et inclusif ; l'entreprise ne pratique aucune discrimination fondée sur la race, la couleur, la religion, le sexe, l'orientation sexuelle, l'identité de genre, l'origine nationale, l'âge, le handicap ou toute autre caractéristique protégée.

Note aux recruteurs et aux agences de placement : CIVIC n'accepte pas les candidatures spontanées transmises par des agences et ne verse pas d'honoraires de placement pour les candidats soumis par des agences autres que ses partenaires agréés.

**Postuler avant le 15 Octobre 2026**

jobs.title: General Director f/m/x
jobs.body:
**Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international humanitarian aid organization that provides assistance in more than 70 countries to populations in distress, to victims of natural or manmade disasters and to victims of armed conflicts, without discrimination and irrespective of origin, religion, creed or political affiliation.** **Our actions are guided by medical ethics and the principle of impartiality, independence and neutrality.**

## **CONTEXT**

MSF Luxembourg celebrates its 40th anniversary in 2026. Throughout this time, we have maintained a fierce determination to act, providing care to those in need and bearing witness when the world looks the other way.  
From its first mission in Ethiopia in 1986, to becoming a fully operational cell of Operational Center Brussels (OCB), pioneering operational research, participating in movement-wide strategic platforms, and contributing to OCB and a new Operational Directorate with AKWABA, the Luxembourg section has demonstrated versatility, innovation, and unwavering commitment to the mission of Médecins Sans Frontières.

With 35 staff members, the section’s team works to raise awareness on humanitarian issues among Luxembourg’s population, raise funds needed to finance humanitarian interventions, hire and support MSF Mobile Staff deployed internationally and carry out, with the LuxOR unit, epidemiological support and operational research projects directly linked to health programs, helping to improve their efficiency and effectiveness.

## **ROLE PURPOSE**

As General Director, you will lead MSF Luxembourg in delivering its strategic ambitions while ensuring alignment with Médecins Sans Frontières' principles, values and international frameworks. Reporting to the Board, you will provide overall leadership of the section, represent MSF externally and within the international movement, and ensure the sustainable development of MSF Luxembourg's activities, teams and resources.

## **KEY RESPONSABILITIES**

### **Strategic Leadership and Governance**

- Guide and lead new collaboration with partners in the MSF movement, in the light of the MSF movement evolution, and the strategic vision of MSF Luxembourg section.
- Lead the implementation of MSF Luxembourg's strategic vision and organisational objectives.
- Ensure alignment of the organisation's activities with MSF's values, charter, international frameworks and governance requirements.
- Advise and collaborate closely with the Board and the Management Team. This includes regular reporting to the Board during board meetings and/or under specific requests.
- Monitor organisational performance, risks, compliance and accountability.

### **Organisational Leadership and People Management**

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the Management Team (LuxOR, Foundation, Communication & Fundraising, Public Engagement, Human Resources, Finance and IT), ensuring alignment with MSF Luxembourg's strategic objectives and organisational priorities.
- Foster a collaborative, high-performing inclusive and accountable organisational culture that promotes staff engagement, wellbeing, development and safeguarding.
- Ensure the organisation has the people, systems, resources and financial capacity required to deliver its strategic ambitions sustainably, through effective planning, resource allocation, budget oversight and financial stewardship.
- Drive organisational development, change management and continuous improvement.
- Ensure compliance with Luxembourg legal requirements (Association statute, financial audit &reporting, …)

### **Representation, Advocacy and Partnerships**

- Serve as the primary representative and spokesperson of MSF Luxembourg.
- Build and strengthen collaborative relationships with other MSF sections, further consolidate MSF Luxembourg's partnership with the Operational Centre Brussels (OCB) and actively contribute to the development of the AKWABA Operational Directorate while ensuring that MSF Luxembourg maintains its distinct identity, added value and recognition within the movement.
- Contribute actively to international MSF platforms, governance bodies and collaborative initiatives.
- Build and maintain strategic relationships with government authorities, media, private donors, academia, humanitarian organisations, civil society and Association members.
- Promote and advocate for MSF's humanitarian principles, medical action and positions on key humanitarian issues.

## **PROFILE REQUIRED**

We are looking for an inspiring leader with a strong commitment to humanitarian action and a proven ability to lead complex organisations and diverse stakeholders.

### **Essential**

- Strong commitment to MSF's principles, values and humanitarian mission.
- Significant senior leadership and management experience, ideally 10+ years.
- Experience within MSF (Intl - HQ experience) and/or humanitarian or non-profit sector.
- Understanding of MSF medical operations and humanitarian challenges.
- Demonstrated ability to develop and implement strategy.
- Structured and results-oriented professional with excellent organisational skills and a strong ability to translate strategy into measurable objectives, track performance through relevant indicators, and ensure high-quality reporting and accountability.
- Strong people leadership skills with experience managing senior teams and driving organisational change.
- Excellent stakeholder management, networking and partnership-building abilities.
- Strong analytical, political and negotiation skills.
- Proven financial and organisational management capabilities.
- Excellent communication, representation and public speaking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a complex international and multicultural environment.
- Fluency in English and French; Luxembourgish and/or German are considered assets.
- Availability for frequent travel, when necessary.

### **Desirable**

- Good understanding of the Luxembourg context and institutional environment.
- Strong knowledge of international humanitarian issues and the MSF movement.
- Experience in advocacy and engagement with high-level stakeholders.

## **CONDITIONS**

- Full-time contract, based in Luxembourg with frequent travels abroad
- Mandate of 4 years (extendable for max. 2 more years)
- Gross salary over 12 months from 75600 to 90600 € according to MSF experience
- 29 days annual paid leaves
- Possibility of teleworking 2 days per week
- Medical complementary insurance (including hospitalization)
- 18 Lunch vouchers each with a face value of 10,80 € (2/3 covered by MSF).
- Public transport allowance & relocation package (if applicable)
- **Expected starting date: January 2027** **(preferred)**

jobs.title: Country Manager, Jordan
jobs.body:
## **Country Manager, Jordan**

*A founding leadership role at a pivotal moment, shaping the future of Seenaryo in Jordan*

**Location:** Amman, Jordan (office-based)

**Contract:** Full-time, 5 days per week | 1-year contract with strong likelihood of renewal

**Salary:** 1,850 – 2,250 JD per month (commensurate with experience, inclusive of tax and social security).

*The advertised salary range reflects our current budget for the role. We recognise that exceptional candidates may have different salary expectations, and we would be open to discussing these with the right candidate.*

**Start Date:** Anytime from 1st September - 1st December 2026, based on candidates’ availability

**Reports to:** Joint CEO

**APPLICATION DEADLINE:** We are accepting applications on a rolling basis. The position will remain open until filled.

**About Seenaryo**

Working in Lebanon, Jordan, Palestine and Syria, Seenaryo uses theatre and play to support mental health, shape futures, and drive social justice. Over ten years, Seenaryo has developed a unique and radically participatory approach to theatre and learning. What began in community spaces in 2015, has moved into classrooms, onto stages and toured to international festivals. Reaching over 205,000 people in the last decade, Seenaryo won the Digital Innovation of the Year - Learning prize at the 2025 PIEoneer Awards, the Resilience in Action Award at HundrED 2024, and the Arts, Culture & Heritage prize at the 2023 UK Charity Awards.

**Seenaryo in Jordan**

Seenaryo Jordan is at a defining moment. Having established strong roots, a talented team, meaningful partnerships, a growing reputation, and a registered NGO presence, we are now moving into a phase of greater independence and autonomy from our UK office. We are looking for a Country Manager who will take ownership of that journey: someone who can hold the whole picture, the people, the finances, the culture, the partnerships, and lead Seenaryo Jordan with confidence, care and vision as it becomes a confident, autonomous entity, specific to the communities it serves in Jordan.

**About the Role**

This is a senior leadership role with full responsibility for Seenaryo Jordan's operational, financial, and organisational health. You will lead a talented and committed team, hold legal and governance accountability for the Jordan entity, and serve as the primary bridge between Seenaryo Jordan and our regional and UK leadership.

Day to day, this role will feel like: holding a team through complexity with calm and clarity; making decisions (sometimes under pressure) with incomplete information; building systems that last; representing Seenaryo with warmth and authority to funders, government and partners; and creating a workplace culture that centres on staff wellbeing and that people are proud to be part of. The scope of this role has the potential to grow significantly based on the strengths and ambitions of the right candidate.

## **Core Competencies**

We hire for character and competency first. These are the qualities we are looking for:

### **Commitment to theatre & play**

Seenaryo believes in the power of arts and play to change lives. This candidate does not need to be an artist themselves but having genuine respect and enthusiasm for what we stand for, is essential.

**Commitment to care**

We work with humans first and foremost - our team, our participants, our partners. Above all human care is at the centre of what we do. This means being able to be kind and hold space in a safe way - even when the answer is no or the conversations are difficult. Wellbeing and safety of those we work with is the priority and never something that should be compromised ‘to get the job done’.

### **Commitment to excellence**

At Seenaryo we believe in the dignity of excellence. We take our participants and the quality of our work seriously. We are looking for someone who takes pride in the quality of Seenaryo Jordan’s work - someone who does not cut corners, who notices what others miss and whose attention to detail reflects their respect for the organisation and those it serves.

### **Confident & accountable leadership**

Someone who can form a clear sense of where things are going and why and is able to take genuine responsibility for outcomes. This means being decisive when it matters but also knowing when consultation is critical, and knowing the difference between the two. We are looking for someone who can inspire confidence without demanding authority.

### **Open & effective communication**

This role means understanding the dynamics of a multicultural, cross-border organisation and using effective communication skills to bring a diverse group of team members and stakeholders on a journey with you. We are looking for someone who can be an open and clear communicator and someone who can navigate difficult conversations with directness and empathy.

**Growth mindset**

We are always learning and this happens most effectively when we celebrate and learn from failure, when we’re accountable for our own actions and when we seek solutions with humility and curiosity. We are looking for a leader who can model these qualities by embracing a growth mindset and a reflection approach to this leadership role.

### **Resilience and adaptability**

The nature of working with underserved communities in challenging social, political and economic circumstances requires a level of strength and resilience. We are looking for someone who can work under pressure without losing perspective or warmth and who can manage uncertainty well. When things go wrong, we need a leader who is able to stay grounded, problem-solve creatively, and help others do the same.

## **Key Responsibilities**

**Team Leadership & HR 30%**

- Lead, inspire and support the Seenaryo Jordan team, fostering a culture of collaboration, integrity, and excellence.
- Manage HR for the Jordan core team: recruitment, onboarding, performance management, conflict resolution, pastoral care and professional development.
- Oversee office management and operations, ensuring the team's physical workspace, equipment, and material needs are fully met, while guiding policies around office hours and hybrid working decisions to support a productive environment.
- Support staff wellbeing and be a visible, trusted presence for the team, especially in moments of difficulty or uncertainty.
- Monitor developments in Jordan and lead on crisis and risk management when needed, in collaboration with regional leadership.
- Line manage members of the Core Team providing technical support, coaching style support and pastoral and HR guidance

**Programmatic & grant oversight 20%**

- Maintain oversight of all grants related to Jordan and Palestine from a top-line perspective: aware of general progress, potential risks and any blocks.
- Manage some high level grants as budget holder and donor liaison where necessary.
- Have a thorough understanding of programmes being run in Seenaryo Jordan with an ability to troubleshoot blocks faced by the technical team and provide helpful advice as needed.
- Be able to present effectively and in detail on Seenaryo Jordan’s programmes and grants with an ability to discuss current gaps and potential opportunities with partners, donors and other stakeholders.
- Support the project team by attending partner meetings where needed.
- Support the fundraising and grants team as needed, including contributing to bid writing, donor reporting and evaluation.

### **Strategic Oversight 20%**

- Contribute to and take ownership of Seenaryo Jordan's strategic direction, in close collaboration with the UK and regional leadership team.
- Feed into quarterly UK board meetings and represent the Jordan programme at a senior organisational level.
- Support the long-term development of Seenaryo Jordan as an increasingly autonomous entity with its own identity, systems and leadership capacity e.g. establishing a Jordan advisory committee.
- In close collaboration with the Jordan Arts Team support on guiding the strategy for expansion of Seenaryo’s work in Palestine

### **Operational & Financial Management 20%**

- Ensure all Jordan operations comply with Seenaryo's Standard Operating Procedures and relevant Jordanian legislation, including registration, tax, social security and audit obligations.
- Lead on legal compliance, including liaising with the lawyer, maintaining NGO registration status, government permissions, and keeping activities current on the Takamul Platform.
- Provide financial oversight: budget management, payroll, bank signatory responsibilities, monthly reconciliation of petty cash and bank accounts with the Finance Manager.
- Lead on the annual office/overheads budget & procurement plan and track spending on this in close collaboration with the Jordan Finance Manager.
- Oversee end-of-year accounts in collaboration with the accountant, Finance Manager, and UK Finance Manager.
- Manage financial risk, governance and safeguarding in line with Seenaryo policy and Jordanian requirements.

### **Communication, Representation & Partnerships 10%**

- Represent Seenaryo externally with funders, government bodies, partner organisations and public platforms, building relationships that reflect the organisation's values and ambitions.
- Successfully pitch Seenaryo and tell the story of Seenaryo’s journey and impact.
- Liaise regularly with the UK and Lebanon teams, maintaining strong cross-organisational communication and coherence.

*As part of a growing and ambitious organisation, the Country Manager will also engage with tasks across the wider team as needed and in agreement with their line manager. This role has genuine scope to evolve.*

## **Experience & Qualifications**

We are looking for someone with the following background, though we know that experience takes many forms and we encourage applications from candidates who may not tick every box.

### Essential

- At least 5 years' experience in a senior operations, management or leadership role within an NGO or community-based organisation.
- Demonstrable success in people management including recruitment, performance management, and navigating conflict.
- Demonstrated experience contributing to organisational strategy and translating strategic priorities into effective operational delivery.
- Significant experience overseeing organisational finances, including budgeting, financial planning and multi-donor budgets.
- Demonstrated experience strengthening organisational systems, policies or operational processes.
- Experience leading organisations through periods of change, uncertainty or crisis.
- Excellent written and spoken English; ability to support Arabic-English communication.
- Understanding of the complex socio-economic, political, and humanitarian dynamics within Jordan and the wider region.

### Desirable

- Experience leading organisational growth, organisational change or institutional development.
- Experience establishing or strengthening new teams, systems or organisational functions.
- Experience supporting board governance, advisory committees or senior organisational leadership.
- Experience managing institutional donor relationships, including grant management and reporting.
- Experience leading or overseeing safeguarding within an organisation.
- Experience in play-based learning, theatre, arts or creative education.
- Strong knowledge of Jordan Labour Law, tax and social security requirements, and NGO compliance in Jordan.
- Experience building relationships with government bodies, ministries or other senior external stakeholders in Jordan.
- Experience working within arts, education, child development or community development related sectors.

## **What We Offer**

- 1,850 – 2,250 JD per month (commensurate with experience, inclusive of tax and social security)
- A 1-year employment contract with a strong likelihood of renewal based on performance and funding, with a 3-month probation period.
- A genuinely meaningful role at a pivotal moment for the organisation.
- A collaborative, values-driven team that cares deeply about its work and each other.
- Opportunities for professional development and growth, with scope for the role to expand.
- The chance to help shape what Seenaryo becomes in Jordan.
- An annual professional development budget for investment in career goals and wellbeing.

jobs.title: Senior Research Monitoring Evaluation and Learning Officer
jobs.body:
**Role Summary**

Siren Associates is seeking a Senior RMEL (Research, Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning) Officer to coordinate the design and implementation of ANCHOR’s RMEL system, ensuring rigorous data collection, analysis, and reporting across all components. Based in Amman and reporting to the Project Manager while working closely with Siren’s HQ RMEL Lead, the Senior RMEL Officer will lead perception surveys (baseline, midline and endline), and drive learning processes to inform adaptive management and donor reporting. This role combines technical expertise in quantitative and qualitative methods with strong field engagement and coordination skills.

*Want to learn more about us? Check our digital brochure:* [*https://materials.sirenassociates.com/brochure*](https://materials.sirenassociates.com/brochure)
