## BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for an Accounting and Audit Intern to support our team in Switzerland:**

**Department: Finance and Administration**

**Position:** Accounting and Audit Intern

**Contract duration:** 6 months

**Location: Geneva**

**Starting Date: January 2027.**

## **POSITION PROFILE**

Under the supervision of the Deputy Head of Finance, the Accounting and Audit Intern is responsible for supporting the Finance & Admin Unit from Geneva in the monthly tasks of the accounting cycle, in the collection, control and preparation of supporting documentation for external audits, while maintaining the databases up to date.

## **RESPOSIBILITIES**

The Accounting and Audit Intern responsibilities include:

***PAYMENT VOUCHERS***

- Contribute in the preparation of payment vouchers, making sure that all supporting documentation is available and coherent
- Account for the Payment Vouchers in the accountancy once the Payment Vouchers have been validated

***MONTHLY ACCOUNTING CYCLE SUPPORT***

- Preparation of import files that will be booked in the accountancy as expenses
- Examples of entries are travel invoices, reimbursements expenses & monthly salary associated costs

***EXTERNAL SCREENING***

- When requested, screen staff, partners, suppliers or any entity that may start a relationship with IMPACT Initiatives
- The screening process ensures that IMPACT Initiatives is only engaging with entities with clean records

***COLLECTION & CROSS CHECK OF SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS FOR AUDIT***

- When requested, collect & cross check all supporting documentation available for the sample received.

The Accounting and Audit Intern will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Software skills** Proficient knowledge of Microsoft office package, notably Excel;
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent verbal and written communication skills for effective reporting required;
- **Academic qualifications** Master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline (e.g. Finance, Business Administration, etc.);
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, French is a plus.

## **COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS**

- For this position, gross salary is 1’450 CHF monthly (before income tax). NB – IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education and experience of staff. A contribution to medical insurance of 520 CHF per month is already included in the salary figure.
- Insurance covering professional and non-professional accidents throughout the period of employment with IMPACT
- Health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance in case of field visits/temporary deployments
- Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- Up to 40% of remote work on a weekly basis.

jobs.title: Education Content Manager
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**SCOPE**

Education is central to that mission. The IRC works to ensure that even the hardest-to-reach children in the most challenging places are able to go to school and thrive, defining success through education outcomes spanning infancy to young adulthood: access to safe, functional and responsive education across all ages; early childhood learning and nurturing care; primary school-aged learning; post-primary learning; safety in school; and gender equality across all education outcomes. Delivering on these outcomes at scale increasingly depends on innovation - including the thoughtful use of education technology to strengthen the quality of teaching and learning and to extend support to teachers and learners who are otherwise out of reach.

To meet the sector's toughest education challenges, the IRC's Education Technical Unit (TU) collaborates with the Airbel Impact Lab - the IRC's research and innovation department - to design, test, and scale innovative solutions that reach last-mile teachers and learners. A flagship example is aprendIA, an AI-powered teacher professional development program delivered via low-tech, widely accessible channels to support teachers working in under-resourced, crisis-affected, and multilingual classrooms.

The Education Content Manager plays a central role in supporting content and pedagogy quality assurance across this work. Sitting at the intersection of pedagogy, quality assurance, and content development, the Manager helps ensure that what teachers experience is pedagogically sound, contextually appropriate, and safe. In the near term, the bulk of this role will focus on aprendIA; over time it may extend to the IRC's broader portfolio of teacher support and education innovation initiatives as priorities evolve.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Working under the direction of the Education Advisor and in support of senior technical staff, the Education Content Manager focuses on execution, quality, and content development - rather than setting technical strategy or leading external representation - across the following areas:

**Testing, quality assurance & troubleshooting for digital & AI-enhanced programming**

- Conduct regular testing of digital course flows, prompt responses, and chatbot behaviors - assessing accuracy, clarity, pedagogical alignment, and cultural appropriateness.
- Communicate testing notes with developer(s) on the team and collaborate on solutions that maintain pedagogical quality.
- Red-team digital content to identify edge cases, problematic outputs, and safety gaps.
- Maintain clear, actionable QA logs that track issues, findings, and resolution status across the initiatives supported.
- Synthesize findings into prioritized recommendations, distinguishing content fixes from product or design fixes, and flag where testing results suggest content may not be achieving its intended learning purpose.
- Review usage, completion, and engagement data findings alongside QA findings to surface early signals of whether content is supporting teacher learning and uptake, flagging patterns for senior technical and MEAL colleagues.
- Troubleshoot content-related issues flagged by country teams or surfaced through data and program monitoring, and support testing of new features, materials, and content updates ahead of release.
- Review and quality-assure teaching and learning content and materials across TU projects as requested, checking for pedagogical soundness, evidence alignment, and contextual fit.

**Capturing process & learning**

- Refine quality frameworks and rubrics for evaluating digitally delivered pedagogical content, including dimensions such as context fit and alignment with evidence-based practice.
- Document QA and content-development processes, criteria, and lessons learned for internal use and external sharing.
- Connect testing and QA insights to available evidence on teacher engagement, classroom practice, and learner outcomes, contributing to the team’s understanding of what is driving impact in digital an AI-enabled teacher support.
- Support senior technical and MEAL colleagues in translating content and QA insights into evaluation questions and learning agenda priorities, so that testing feeds directly into how the team understands outcomes and impact.
- Contribute to accessible knowledge products (e.g. blog posts, working papers, briefs) that articulate what quality looks like in technology-enabled and conventional teacher professional development, in support of the team's thought leadership and external engagement.
- Support presentations, funder updates, and partner briefings that draw on QA findings and learning across projects.
- Adapt and apply quality frameworks and documentation practices to other TU content and teacher-support materials as requested.

**Content development**

- Work alongside government, local partners and local content creators to develop and adapt content for programs, ensuring alignment with local curriculum, global best practices and user interface (UI) requirements.
- Draft and refine short, structured course content for digital modalities, aligned with strategy, templates, and evidence-based pedagogy.
- Develop one-off or thematic modules in response to identified needs (e.g. managing test anxiety during exam periods; supporting children with learning difficulties in large classes).
- Review and refine content deliverables such as quiz questions and strategy descriptions, and support localization review for new cultural and operational contexts.
- Develop and adapt teaching and learning materials for other TU teacher-support and innovation initiatives as requested, drawing on existing IRC resources, established course outlines, and context-specific input.
- Propose alternative formats through which courses and learning games can still qualify as recognized coursework (completion criteria, evidence of learning, assessment logic) while deliberately departing from the conventional module-and-assessment structure, grounded in how educators actually engage in low-connectivity, messaging-based, time-constrained settings.

**Broader innovation & cross-TU support**

- Support senior technical staff in scoping and needs assessment for new deployments, contexts, and delivery modalities.
- Provide flexible content, quality assurance, and documentation support across the Education TU and its collaboration with the Airbel Impact Lab as organizational priorities evolve.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Department:** Education Technical Unit; AcceleratED team

**Reports to**: Education Advisor for Foundational Learning & Content Innovation

**Works closely with**: AcceleratED team, including product and developer colleagues, as well as education technical advisors and country program teams

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

- **Internal:** Airbel Impact Lab colleagues, Education Technical Unit staff, country program teams supporting deployment and localization of education programming
- **External:** Subject-matter experts, consultants, and country-level partners engaged for content development, review, and localization, in coordination with senior technical staff.

**Job Qualifications:**

**Required**

- Master's degree in International Education or a related field (or a Bachelor's degree with equivalent additional professional experience).
- Classroom teaching experience.
- International experience, ideally in low-resource, crisis- or conflict-affected contexts.
- Experience developing education or teacher professional development content grounded in evidence-based pedagogy.
- Strong analytical skills and a demonstrated eye for detail, with the ability to test, evaluate, and troubleshoot content systematically.
- Excellent writing skills, including the ability to produce clear, concise, audience-ready content and documentation.
- Ability to work independently and productively in a fast-paced, collaborative, cross-functional, and geographically dispersed team.
- Ability to apply a diversity and inclusion lens to work, and excellent interpersonal and communication skills across a multicultural environment and multiple time zones.
- Commitment to the mission and values of the IRC.
- Proficiency in spoken and written English.

**Desirable**

- Strong interest in, or experience with, EdTech and the use of AI in education, particularly in low-tech modalities.
- Experience creating, adapting, or localizing content for multilingual or humanitarian contexts.
- Familiarity with teacher professional development frameworks and classroom observation or quality instruments.

***Travel***:

- Up to 20% travel for 1-3 weeks each time to assigned countries, including crisis- and conflict-affected contexts, in line with IRC’s security policies.

**Compensation:** ($68,000 - $74,000). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: PALESTINE - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - GAZA
jobs.body:
**Beginning of contract : 07/01/2027**

**Duration : 7 months**

**Localisation : Gaza / Deir el-Balah**

## ABOUT US 

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Solidarités International operates across the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, with operational teams in Deir el-Balah and Ramallah and mission coordination in Jerusalem (although some national coordination staff work out of Ramallah). The position works at coordination level and covers both Gaza and West Bank operations, ensuring consistent administrative, HR and financial support across the mission. SI delivers emergency and early-recovery WASH assistance, shelter and essential-item distributions, and is scaling up nutrition-sensitive FSL activities, including a EUR 1.3 million FIFSAN project with a Palestinian partner. The portfolio relies on close cooperation with local organizations and must continually adapt to volatile access, damaged infrastructure, fragile markets and supply constraints. The Palestinian context is a particularly volatile one, especially in recent months in the West Bank, and in Gaza there are for the moments no signs of a resolution to the political and humanitarian crisis engulfing the exclave and its 2 million residents.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**General objective:**

The Field Coordinator acts as delegated Country Director for the area of intervention. He/She leads the field base, defines and steers the operational strategy according to the humanitarian and geopolitical context, ensures programme quality and compliance with SI standards, mobilises the resources required for implementation, manages teams, and oversees safety, representation and external coordination.

**Issues and specific challenges**

1\) Managing a team in a highly complex and volatile security environment, even in a ceasefire context; ensuring vigilance on security rules, movement validation, and the overall security framework.  
2\) Training and guiding a less experienced team in a context where SI has operated in Gaza only since after the October 2023 attacks; ensuring the regularisation of our processes, communications, and ways of working.  
3\) Ensuring strong implementation capacity, especially if additional funding is secured from a new donor.  
4\) Expatriate-heavy base management team.  
5\) Need to develop programming into the very, very early stages of solutions that are in part more durable or which allow SI to reach more people at scale, especially on the WASH side.

**Priorities on the 2-3 first months :**

1\) Ensure the safety and security of the team.  
2\) Monitor the increase of the team, including possible changes in guesthouse and office, and the nationalization of certain positions.  
3\) With the programme team, deepen understanding of the context in a ceasefire environment, where more and more NGOs are not registered, in order to shape a clear vision of SI’s appropriate role.  
4\) Improving SI's representation in the Gaza Strip and ability to improve its decision making, quality of programming, and relationship with civil society/the Clusters as a result.

**Security constraints :**

Security constraints are extremely high in Gaza, with air, land and naval strikes, risks related to medium and light infantry weapons, and severe social tensions linked to war, deprivation and economic collapse. The position requires strong security awareness, strict adherence to protocols, and the ability to lead under pressure.

## YOUR PROFILE

**Education / academic background:**

Education background in logistics, transport, warehousing, IT, supply chain, management…

**Specific skills and experience:**

Technical skills

1\. Strong knowledge in team management and mentoring.   
2\. Capacity to deal with many different issues, to self- update and learn very quickly from a highly and constantly evolving environment.   
3\. Ability to manage and prioritize a high workload and multiple tasks with tight deadlines.   
4\. Good representational skills, Ability to liaise, INGOs, other agencies, authorities and donors.   
5\. A good understanding of security management.   
6\. A good understanding of humanitarian issues including IDPs, camp management protection, advocacy.   
7\. Ability to write/edit quality reports in English.

Transversal skills

1\. Ability to work in multi-cultural environment; more generally, excellent interpersonal and communication skills and strong cultural sensitivity.   
2\. Willingness to work in a volatile security context.   
3\. Ability to take initiatives, decisions and work in autonomy is essential.   
4\. Good problem-solving skills in day to day and crisis situations.   
5\. Important flexibility and adaptability.   
6\. Experience working with SI (or a similar organization) is an asset   
7\. Prior experience in South Sudan would be considered as an asset

**Language:**

Fluent in English, written and spoken. Arabic is a strong asset.

## SI WILL OFFER YOU

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2 310 gross per month (2100 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The position is based in Deir-el-Balah, where Solidarités International maintains its office and guesthouse, as do most INGOs. Since the ceasefire brokered on 10 October, living conditions have improved, and markets are gradually becoming more functional. At the time the position opened, most basic food items, including fruits and vegetables, were available in Gaza markets, although at high prices. Electricity at the SI office and guesthouse is entirely solar-powered, which, particularly in winter, may occasionally lead to temporary shortages. Internet is available at the GH and office with limited shortages. SI has one validated supermarket where expatriates can buy most goods for everyday life.

jobs.title: Endline Evaluation of the Strategic Partnership Agreement II Programme and Syria & Lebanon Top Ups
jobs.body:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**Endline Evaluation of the Strategic Partnership Agreement II Programme and Syria & Lebanon Top Ups**

**Commissioned by | ActionAid - Arab Region**

**Syria and Lebanon | 2022–2026**

**1. Background**

ActionAid Arab Region (AAAR), together with its local partners, has implemented the Strategic Partnership Agreement II funded by DANIDA in partnership with ActionAid Denmark in Syria and Lebanon from 2022 to 2026. The programme has been implemented in highly complex and protracted crisis contexts, requiring continuous adaptation to changing political, economic, humanitarian and protection conditions.

In Lebanon, implementation has been undertaken with SHIFT, Bassmeh & Zaitouneh, and RDFL, with interventions reaching communities in Tripoli, Jeb Jenine and Ba'albek.

In Syria, implementation was initially concentrated in Northwest Syria, through Violet and Bahar, and subsequently expanded to Latakia and Damascus in response to changing contextual and humanitarian needs.

The programme has also been complemented by two Top-Ups, one in Lebanon and one in Syria, which are included within the scope of this endline evaluation. The evaluation should therefore assess the overall contribution and performance of the core SPAII programme alongside the additional interventions and adaptations introduced through the Top-Ups.

The programme as a whole is expected to have reached approximately:

- **75,000+ people in Syria**, including people benefiting from humanitarian assistance in its various forms, including distributions, protection services and legal services; people participating in trainings; people accessing youth and safe spaces; and people participating in campaigns, collective action and other forms of civic engagement.
- **35,000+ people in Lebanon**, through similar combinations of humanitarian assistance, protection and legal services, trainings, youth and safe spaces, campaigning and collective action.

The programme has been structured around three Strategic Objectives:

**SO1: Rights and access to services**

**Young people, especially marginalised young women, enjoy fundamental rights through improved access to well-resourced programmes and public services in fragile situations.**

**SO2: Sustainable livelihoods and green solutions**

**Young people from refugee and host communities, especially marginalised young women, enjoy improved, sustainable livelihoods through government that is accountable towards building sustainable green solutions.**

**SO3: Resilience, protection and rights**

**Young people from refugee and host communities, especially marginalised women, are resilient to shocks and enjoy their rights to protection in protracted crises.**

The programme's Theory of Change (ToC) provides the overarching logic through which interventions are expected to contribute to improved rights, access to services, livelihoods, resilience, protection, collective action and longer-term systemic change.

Given the duration and complexity of the programme, the endline evaluation provides an opportunity not only to assess the extent to which the programme achieved its intended results, but also to examine how and why change occurred, the contribution of different interventions and partners, the quality of technical capacity and collective action, the programme's policy influence, and the extent to which programming remained relevant and adaptive in protracted crises\*\*.\*\*

**2. Purpose of the Evaluation**

The primary purpose of the endline evaluation is to provide an independent assessment of the performance, contribution and learning of the SPAII programme and its Top-Ups in Syria and Lebanon between 2022 and 2026.

The evaluation will assess the programme against the OECD DAC evaluation criteria of:

1. **Relevance** – Is the intervention doing the right things?
2. **Coherence** – How well does the intervention fit within its wider context and other interventions?
3. **Effectiveness** – Is the intervention achieving its intended objectives and results?
4. **Efficiency** – How well have resources been used to achieve results?
5. **Impact** – What difference has the intervention made?
6. **Sustainability** – Are the benefits, capacities, relationships and changes likely to continue?

In addition, the evaluation will place particular emphasis on the programme’s ability to adapt to changing and protracted crisis contexts, the quality and adequacy of ActionAid/AAAR’s technical leadership, guidance and support, the effectiveness and quality of collective action, the extent and nature of policy influence, and the relationship between programme implementation and the Theory of Change. The evaluation is expected to generate practical, forward-looking evidence and learning to inform future AAAR programming in Syria and Lebanon, the design of regional and country-level programmes, partnership and localisation approaches, adaptive programming in protracted and rapidly changing crises, technical leadership and support to partners, advocacy and policy influencing, youth engagement and collective action, and humanitarian-development-peace programming. Ultimately, the findings will contribute to AAAR’s organisational learning and strategic decision-making, helping to identify what worked well, where the programme could have done better, why particular approaches succeeded or underperformed, and what should be sustained, adapted or strengthened in future programming.

**3. Evaluation Questions**

The following questions should guide the evaluation. The evaluator should refine and prioritise these during the inception phase.

**A. Relevance**

1. To what extent did SPAII respond to the priority needs, rights and aspirations of young people, particularly marginalised young women?
2. To what extent did interventions remain relevant as the contexts in Syria and Lebanon changed between 2022 and 2026?
3. How well did the programme balance immediate humanitarian needs with longer-term rights, resilience, livelihoods and systemic change?
4. Were there important needs or groups that the programme did not adequately address?

**B. Coherence**

1. How well did SPAII complement other interventions implemented by AAAR and partners?
2. To what extent did the programme create meaningful links between humanitarian response, protection, rights, livelihoods, resilience and advocacy?
3. How well did interventions align with local systems, priorities and existing services?

**C. Effectiveness**

1. To what extent did SPAII achieve its intended outputs and outcomes?
2. Which interventions and approaches contributed most significantly to results?
3. Which interventions were less effective, and why?
4. To what extent did the programme achieve meaningful changes beyond activity and output-level results?
5. What factors enabled or constrained effectiveness?
6. Were there significant differences in results across countries, locations, partners, groups or types of intervention?

**D. Theory of Change**

1. To what extent did the programme's Theory of Change accurately explain how change occurred?
2. Which pathways of change were strongest?
3. Were there unexpected pathways or outcomes?
4. What contextual factors influenced the pathways of change?
5. What should be retained, modified or removed from the ToC for future programming?

**E. Efficiency**

1. Were resources appropriately allocated across interventions and locations?
2. To what extent did the programme achieve value for money?
3. Were programme resources sufficiently flexible to respond to changing needs?
4. How did partnership arrangements affect efficiency?
5. Were there significant operational or coordination constraints affecting implementation?

**F. Impact**

1. What meaningful changes can be attributed or plausibly contributed to by SPAII?
2. What difference did the programme make to young people's rights, resilience, protection, livelihoods and participation?
3. What unintended positive or negative effects emerged?
4. To what extent did the programme contribute to changes beyond direct beneficiaries?

**G. Technical leadership and guidance**

1. To what extent did AAAR provide adequate technical leadership and guidance to support the quality and effectiveness of SPAII implementation?
2. How well did AAAR's technical support respond to the specific realities of Syria and Lebanon, including the constraints associated with protracted crisis contexts?
3. Where were technical leadership or guidance gaps identified, and how did these affect implementation or results?
4. What technical guidance, systems or approaches should be retained, strengthened or developed for future programming?

**H. Collective Action and Policy Influence**

1. What was the quality and significance of collective action supported by SPAII?
2. To what extent did young people influence decisions, institutions, policies or public discourse?
3. What evidence exists of policy or systems-level influence?
4. What enabled or constrained meaningful youth participation?
5. Which collective action approaches should be continued or scaled?

**I. Adaptation in Protracted Crises**

1. How effectively did the programme adapt to changing political, economic, humanitarian and social conditions?
2. Which adaptations were most significant? Were adaptations timely and appropriate?
3. What enabled effective adaptation? What constrained adaptation?
4. Did adaptations maintain alignment with the programme's strategic objectives and ToC?
5. What does SPAII demonstrate about how programmes should be designed and managed in protracted crises?

**J. Sustainability**

1. What programme benefits are likely to continue after funding ends?
2. Which capacities, systems, relationships and practices are likely to be sustained?
3. To what extent have local partners been positioned to continue the work?
4. Are collective action and youth engagement mechanisms likely to continue?
5. What institutional or contextual risks threaten sustainability?
6. What should AAAR and partners do to strengthen sustainability?

**4. Evaluation Scope**

The evaluation will cover:

**Lebanon**: Tripoli, Jeb Jenine, Ba'albek

**Syria:** Northwest Syria, Latakia, Damascus

The evaluation should ensure adequate representation of different geographic and contextual settings rather than relying solely on the most accessible locations.

**Time period**

**2022–2026**

**Programme scope**

The evaluation will cover:

- Core SPAII interventions;
- all Top-Ups;
- all three Strategic Objectives including: humanitarian assistance; protection services; legal services; trainings and capacity strengthening; youth and safe spaces; livelihoods-related interventions; campaigns and collective action; advocacy and policy influence; partnership and localisation approaches; programme adaptation and learning.

**Partners**

**Lebanon**: SHIFT, Bassmeh & Zaitouneh RDFL

**Syria**: Violet, Bahar

**5. Evaluation Approach and Methodology**

The evaluation should use a mixed-methods, participatory and theory-based approach.

A purely indicator-based assessment will not be sufficient. The evaluation should combine quantitative evidence with qualitative investigation of contribution, change, adaptation and learning.

The evaluator is expected to propose a detailed methodology during inception. This should include, as appropriate:

**5.1 Document review**

The evaluation will include a review of key programme documentation, including the programme design and Theory of Change, logframes and IPTTs, monitoring and DQA data, partner and monitoring reports, assessments and previous evaluations, learning and advocacy documentation, Top-Up documentation, and relevant contextual and needs assessments.

**5.2 Quantitative analysis**

The evaluation will analyse available monitoring data to assess programme reach, participation, demographic and geographic coverage, achievement against targets, and trends across the implementation period and intervention types.

The evaluator should critically assess **data quality and limitations** and should not treat reported reach as equivalent to meaningful change.

**5.3 Qualitative research**

The evaluation will use qualitative methods to capture the perspectives of programme participants, young people and marginalised young women, communities, partners, volunteers, AAAR staff, technical teams, duty bearers, service providers, civil society and policy stakeholders.

Methods may include key informant interviews, focus group discussions, participatory reflection, outcome harvesting, contribution analysis and selected case studies, as appropriate.

**5.4 Theory of Change assessment**

The evaluator should conduct a dedicated assessment of the SPAII ToC, identifying:

**Inputs → Activities → Outputs → Outcomes → Strategic Objectives → Longer-term change**

while testing the assumptions and contextual conditions between each stage.

The evaluation should identify successful and unsuccessful pathways of change and explain why they occurred.

**5.5 Case studies**

The evaluator will develop a limited number of illustrative case studies highlighting significant examples of individual or community change, collective action, policy influence, technical leadership and guidance, adaptation to crisis, innovative or alternative solutions, and unintended change. Case studies should focus on the pathways and mechanisms of change, demonstrating how and why change occurred rather than simply describing activities or outputs.

**6. Partnership and Localisation**

The evaluation should assess the partnership model as an important determinant of programme performance.

Questions should include:

- Did partners have sufficient ownership and decision-making space?
- Was technical accompaniment appropriate?
- Did AAAR add value beyond financial support?
- How effective was knowledge transfer between AAAR and partners?
- Were roles and responsibilities clear?
- Did partnership arrangements support adaptation?
- How sustainable are capacities developed through the programme?
- What could AAAR do differently to strengthen locally led programming?

The evaluation should particularly examine the balance between partner autonomy and AAAR technical accompaniment, quality assurance and strategic support.

**7. Ethics and Safeguarding**

Given the sensitive nature of programming in Syria and Lebanon, the evaluation must adhere to ActionAid safeguarding requirements and ethical research principles, including informed consent, confidentiality, anonymity, data protection, do-no-harm and conflict-sensitive approaches, gender-sensitive research, and safe participation of young people. Appropriate referral procedures should be in place where sensitive protection concerns arise. The evaluation should minimise risks associated with discussing protection, legal assistance, displacement, conflict and other sensitive experiences. No personally identifiable information should be included in the final report unless explicitly authorised and ethically justified.

**8. Deliverables**

The selected evaluator/team will be expected to produce:

**I. Inception Report**

Including:

refined evaluation questions; evaluation matrix; detailed methodology; sampling strategy; data collection tools; analysis framework; ethical and safeguarding approach; workplan; limitations and mitigation measures.

**II. Data Collection Tools**

Including appropriate tools for:

KIIs; FGDs; participant consultations; partner consultations; policy stakeholder interviews; case studies; and other proposed methods.

**III. Preliminary Findings Presentation**

A presentation of emerging findings to AAAR and relevant partners for validation and reflection.

**IV. Draft Evaluation Report**

Including:

- executive summary;
- programme background;
- methodology;
- limitations;
- findings;
- conclusions;
- lessons learned;
- recommendations;
- annexes;
- and evidence supporting key findings.

**V. Final Evaluation Report**

Maximum recommended length: **40–50 pages excluding annexes**.

**VI. Learning Product**

A concise SPAII Learning Brief synthesising key lessons and practical recommendations, including what worked and what did not, why, what AAAR and partners should continue or do differently, and what should be adapted to strengthen future programming in protracted-crisis contexts.

**VII. Final Learning Workshop**

Facilitation of a participatory learning session with AAAR and relevant partners to validate findings, identify key lessons and priorities, translate findings into actionable recommendations, and discuss implications for future programming.

**9. Sampling**

The evaluator should propose a purposive sampling strategy that ensures representation across:

- Syria and Lebanon;
- geographic locations;
- partners;
- Strategic Objectives;
- intervention types;
- gender;
- age groups;
- marginalised groups;
- refugees and host communities where applicable;
- direct participants and wider stakeholders.

The evaluation should avoid relying exclusively on programme success stories or easily accessible participants.

**10. Key Evaluation Principles**

The evaluation should be:

**Independent** – providing an impartial assessment of programme performance.

**Utilisation-focused** – producing findings that can directly inform future decisions.

**Participatory** – ensuring meaningful engagement of partners and programme participants.

**Theory-based** – testing the programme's Theory of Change rather than simply measuring indicator achievement.

**Contribution-focused** – recognising that change in Syria and Lebanon cannot necessarily be attributed to SPAII alone.

**Context-sensitive** – recognising the complexity of protracted crises.

**Gender-responsive and youth-centred** – examining who benefited, who did not, and how power and inclusion influenced results.

**Learning-oriented** – identifying not only successes and failures but the reasons behind them.

**11. Key Expected Evaluation Outputs**

Ultimately, the evaluation should answer five practical questions for AAAR:

**A. Where did SPAII get it right?**

What approaches, interventions, partnerships and adaptations generated meaningful results?

**B. Where did SPAII have an opportunity to do better?**

What underperformed, and why?

**C. What actually contributed to change?**

Which pathways in the Theory of Change worked, for whom and under what conditions?

**D. What did SPAII learn about programming in protracted crises?**

How can AAAR become more adaptive, locally led and responsive?

**E. What should AAAR do differently next time?**

What should be continued, stopped, adapted, strengthened, scaled or tested differently?

**12. Timeline**

**Activity Timeline**

Inception phase Week 1

Data collection Week 2 to Week 6

Data analysis Week 7

Validation workshop Week 8

Draft final report Week 9

Final report and learning product Week 10

Final workshop Week 11

**13. Budget**

Maximum 16,230 JODs inclusive of 5% tax for Jordanians and 10% for non-Jordanians.

**14. Required Qualifications of the Consultant/Team**

- At least 7–10 years of experience in evaluation of multi-year development programmes
- Proven experience in youth-led programming, gender justice, climate resilience, and/or humanitarian programming
- Strong knowledge of Jordan context, refugee/host-community dynamics
- Demonstrated experience in designing exit strategies or sustainability assessments
- Strong MEL background, including OECD-DAC evaluations is preferrable
- Experience assessing advocacy and policy-influencing results
- Arabic and English fluency
- Experience working with grassroots organizations and youth structures

**15. Management & Coordination**

- The consultant will report to the AAAR PQMEAL Coordinator and SPA II Programme Manager.
- Local partners in Lebanon and Syria will facilitate, youth mobilization, and access to field sites.
- AAAR will provide project documentation, MEL data, and monitoring tools.

**16. Ethical Considerations**

The assessment must follow ActionAid’s safeguarding principles and ethical standards:

- Do-no-harm approach
- Informed consent, confidentiality, secure data handling
- Gender-sensitive and inclusive methodologies
- Special protection for youth under 18 and refugees

jobs.title: MD Chief of Finance, ML
source: UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East
jobs.body:
## Org. Setting and Reporting

UNRWA is a United Nations agency established by the General Assembly in 1949 and is mandated to provide assistance and protection to a population of some 5.8 million registered Palestine refugees. Its mission is to help Palestine refugees in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, West Bank and the Gaza Strip to achieve their full potential in human development, pending a just solution to their plight. UNRWA's services encompass education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure and improvement, microfinance, and emergency assistance.

UNRWA is the largest UN operation in the Middle East with more than 30,000 staff. UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions. If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you.

The MD Chief, Finance Division reports to the MD Director.

## Responsibilities

Is responsible for the standardization of MD's overall financial, accounting and treasury policies and procedures, in compliance with, and ensures adherence with finance and accounts policies and procedures as required by the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), International Accounting Standards (IAS) and UNRWA finance, budget and treasury technical instructions and regulations, including updating yearly adjustments to the Financial Technical Instructions and the Financial Manual in order to comply with IFRS and IAS.

Oversees and manages the financial projection and planning, including monitoring of cash balances and cash flows, liquidity and operational funding requirements are met on a timely basis.

Acts as a member of the executive management team and participates in key decisions and reporting to high-level management of MD and to donors, UN agencies, regulatory parties and other stakeholders with respect to financial aspects of MD.

Oversees the performance of MD Finance and Accounts Management staff, at HQs and Fields to ensure efficiency and effectiveness, including their capacity development and training, fostering teamwork and developing cooperation between finance and accounts staff through a shared vision and common goals to meet its financial standards and regulations.

Leads the MD's capital, assets, including assets registry and resource allocations Agency-wide to ensure appropriate, profitable and low-risk capital management; monitors, tracks and verifies the Department's donated and revolving loan funds, and provides recommendations on their efficient utilization and investment strategies.

Is responsible for the development, monitoring and controlling MD's risk profile, including financial liabilities; takes the required actions to mitigate such risks, ensuring the safeguarding of MD's assets.

Is responsible for the production of the annual and quarterly financial statements of the Department, HQs, Fields and branch offices as well as other financial specialised ad-hoc reports; submits the financial statements to the internal and/or external auditors and addresses all findings and recommendations.

Maintains proper and constructive relationships with all stakeholders, including respective banks in the Fields of operations to ensure efficient and smooth operations and banking transactions

## Competencies

UN Core Values of Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for Diversity, and Core Competencies of Communication, Working with People and Drive for Results apply by default.

Functional

- Deciding and Initiating Action
- Leading and Supervising
- Planning and Organizing
- Relating and Networking
- Analyzing

Leadership

- Managing Complexity and Change
- Delivering Results

## Education

Advanced university degree (Master or equivalent) from an accredited educational institution in business, finance, accounts or management.

## Job Specific Qualifications

Training in microfinance management is required.

## Work Experience

At least 10 years' experience in finance management, supervision, administration and development of a microfinance or financial institution of which five years should have been in a large governmental or international organization at a senior level is required.

Advanced university degree (Master or equivalent) from an accredited educational institution in business, finance, accounts or management is required.

Experience in the IAS, IFRS and CGAP standards and regulations; able to implement all requested accounting standards when preparing the Financial Statements of the department is required.

Experience in analysing and reviewing portfolio quality and formulation of credit policy initiatives to improve its performance and efficiency is required.

Excellent command of written and spoken English and Arabic is required. Experience in developing and conducting training courses is desirable.

Are you currently residing in Duty station. Please specify your current location. It is required. Please explain how you meet this criterion using examples.

Do you currently hold a contract of 1 year or more with UNRWA? If yes, please confirm whether you have completed your mandatory probation period. It is required

Indicate your current involvement in any outside activities, as it is required. Including but not limited to employment, independent contractor/freelance consultant, board member (corporate, academic, etc), expert group, lobby, public speaking/writing (article, book, blog, social media etc), teaching, conferences, training, press statement, voluntary work, political activity, fundraising/donation for non UNRWA entity, running for public office, role in political party or orgs, owning business, work for gov./NGO/private company/charity, UNRWA partner/vendor, full/part-time, paid or not. A "yes" answer doesn't necessarily lead to exclusion from future work at UNRWA, yet misrepresentation in

providing accurate/complete info can lead to disqualification/termination of appointment, if hired

## Languages

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English **and** Arabic are required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult [https://languages.un.org](https://languages.un.org/) for details).

## Required Languages

**Language**

**Reading**

**Writing**

**Listening**

**Speaking**

**English**

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

**Arabic**

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

### Assessment

Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by competency-based interview.

### Special Notice

Type of Contract: Fixed Term Appointment for 1 year, subject to the availability of funds, satisfactory performance, and continuing need.

Grade and Salary: Grade ML7 Monthly basic salary $2243.60 plus special occupational allowance (SOA) of 90% of the basic salary (SOA may change from time to time).

Other benefits: Other benefits include a monthly Provident Fund contribution (15.4% of basic salary paid by the Agency), compulsory medical insurance, 30 days of annual leave, and dependency allowance (if applicable).

Additional benefits:- 2 days of sick leave for each completed month of service.- 14 weeks of Maternity Leave.- 2 weeks paternity leave.

This vacancy notice is open to internal and external candidates. Only candidates residing in West Bank, and within commuting distance of the duty station with authorization to work in the duty station at the time of application are eligible to apply. The Agency will not assume responsibility or

accountability to support or facilitate the issuance of work permit in West Bank, and without a valid work permit, the appointment may be rescinded.

- The incumbent is required to travel frequently throughout the Agency's areas of operations.
- Possession of a valid driving license.
- The incumbent should have the willingness to work after normal duty hours and official holidays.

Preference will be given to registered Palestine refugees and candidates assisting the Agency to meet its commitment to gender parity.

Only applications that have been fully completed in UNRWA's online e-recruitment system inspira will be considered and no late applications will be accepted. The Personal History Profile (PHP) should be completed with full work experience under the experience tabs as per the requirements in the Job Opening. All university degrees must also be stated where applicable. UNRWA personnel must ensure adding their contract type and grade level. For UNRWA internal staff, they are required to specify and

include their current UNRWA grade level. To do so applicants should select under "Category" RLG, scroll down to see all categories, then select their local grade. Given the large pool of applicants, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further assessment. Applicants applying to positions for Grades 12 to 20 or LDC Bands E to H must submit a cover letter/motivational statement in order to be considered.

Providing incorrect or misleading information on an application form will result in the immediate disqualification of the candidate.

Advertisements published in English will only accept applications in English, other language submissions including Arabic will not be considered.

UNRWA welcomes applications from qualified candidates with disabilities.

A roster may be created from the selection exercise, and successful candidates may become eligible for appointments to the same post or a similar post, when the need arises.

Equivalency: Equivalency may apply for this post.

NB: Work experience alone or formal qualifications with no relevant work experience are not considered an acceptable combination.

The Agency disqualifies applicants whose name appears on the UN Sanctions List or a UN database of staff separated for reasons of misconduct or of staff who separated while a misconduct process was pending.

UNRWA shares investigation and misconduct information with other UN Agencies, and past and prospective employers about staff members who have been separated for misconduct, or who have separated while an investigation and/or disciplinary process for misconduct is underway; and those individuals may be prohibited from employment with the United Nations.

UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions from UN member states, regional bodies, business foundations and individual contributions. The mission of UNRWA is to help

Palestine refugees achieve their full potential in human development under the difficult circumstances in which they live.

For more details on UNRWA, please visit: [https://www.unrwa.org](https://www.unrwa.org/)

### United Nations Considerations

Staff members are subject to the authority of the Commissioner-General of UNRWA and to assignment by him or her.

UNRWA is committed to achieving gender parity at all levels of staffing under the current UN-wide gender agenda and strongly encourages applications from qualified applicants from under-represented groups.

At UNRWA, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. UNRWA is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. Reasonable accommodation for applicants with disabilities may be provided to support participation in the recruitment process when requested and indicated in the application.

UNRWA Considerations

UNRWA staff are expected to uphold the highest standards of efficiency, competence, neutrality, impartiality and integrity. This includes respect for and commitment to human rights, diversity and non-violent means of dealing with all kinds of conflict. Only persons who fully and unconditionally commit to these values should consider applying for UNRWA jobs. Candidates will not be considered for employment with UNRWA if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. jobs.title: Software Developer
jobs.body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME)** division is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the three programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Software Developer** will design, develop, maintain, and support Full-stack fisheries information and database management systems for both SPC and WCPFC member countries; develop, maintain, and enhance OFP mobile applications; develop and maintain data integration and workflow infrastructure to support fisheries and climate science programmes; provide technical support and training to National Fisheries staff and SPC personnel on system functionality, data workflows, and data management processes and contribute to the design and implementation of new technologies and data collection tools that support emerging fisheries research and climate change initiatives.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Information systems and application development**

- Develop and maintain fisheries database management systems, in particular, the Tufman2 tuna fisheries database management system
- Develop and maintain mobile applications used to collect tuna fisheries and environmental data to support fisheries and climate-related research
- New functionality is delivered in response to business, scientific, and operational requirements

**Data management and scientific data collection**

- Design, develop, document and maintain the regional tuna fisheries database systems for the registration, entry, importing and querying of data
- Data integration, validation, and workflow processes are maintained and improved

**WCPFC and SPC members support and collaboration**

- Technical support is provided to SPC staff, member countries, and regional partners
- Train and support national staff in the use of fisheries database management systems and mobile applications

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Specialized degree in IT, computing, science, or mathematics or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 4 years’ experience as software developer in web application and data workflow developments, using languages such as C#, JavaScript and Python
- At least 4 years’ experience administrating SQL databases
- At least 4 years’ experience with Git and CI/CD
- Demonstrated experience in the design and development of mobile device applications
- Experience as an Analyst, working with the client to get their information system requirements

**Language skills**

- Good communications skills (English)

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work and travel in a multicultural and multilingual environment

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Software Developer** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 3,727-4,562 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 537,766-658,322 (USD 4,994-6,114; EUR 4,506-5,517). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea** – SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor, VisionFund International
jobs.body:
**Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor, VisionFund International**

VisionFund International is World Vision’s microfinance provider serving vulnerable clients through loans, savings, and insurance. We enable families to grow their livelihoods in hard to reach, rural locations in 28 countries so that caregivers can create secure futures for their children.

We believe in brighter futures for children; empowering families to create incomes and jobs; unlocking economic potential for communities to thrive.

Join VisionFund as we seek to end intergenerational poverty through microfinance.

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor**, you will serve as the technical lead and focal point internally and externally for these three important, connected, and strategic areas of intervention for VisionFund. You will provide technical advice on current best practices, support the development of related products, guide strategy and organisational positioning, and support resource development and programme management for related Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems initiatives and grants.

You will manage the CrediEnterprise credit product pilot project in nine countries in Africa and Central America as part of the THRIVE 2030 programme, ensuring it delivers on its targets while coordinating with and reporting to World Vision partners. You will oversee grant reporting, project management, operational delivery, capacity building of national staff, and integration of this component with other interventions within the THRIVE 2030 programme.

You will provide technical leadership to position VisionFund for institutional funding to support its growing Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems interventions globally. You will support donor pre-positioning, grant writing, and the Resource Development team with technical content throughout proposal development processes.

**Technical Advisory**

You will provide technical advice to VisionFund Operations and MicroFinance Institutions across the network on Agricultural, Market Systems, and Climate industry best practices. You will lead VisionFund’s Internal Climate Financing working group, using your knowledge and experience to shape VisionFund strategy, products, and market positioning. You will also represent VisionFund in technical working groups, including Environmental and Climate Action forums, to communicate VisionFund strategy and strengthen brand visibility within the World Vision partnership.

**Resource Development**

You will support resource development activities for Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems initiatives through grant writing, review, and donor positioning. You will provide technical advice and content for new and existing grant applications, lead VisionFund’s positioning with agricultural, climate, and market systems-focused donors and opportunities, and leverage learnings from the implementation of CrediEnterprise under THRIVE 2030 to pursue additional institutional funding.

You will represent the organization in technical grant calls and donor visits as needed, establish a mechanism for tracking ESCA climate-finance engagements and opportunities, and provide technical advisory support for the implementation of new and ongoing institutional funding in partnership with the Resource Development and Operations teams. You will also lead sector learning, evidence documentation, and dissemination to support VisionFund’s positioning and acquisition activities.

**Operational Delivery**

You will oversee the implementation of CrediEnterprise as part of the THRIVE 2030 programme and other relevant Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems projects. You will manage CrediEnterprise implementation to achieve THRIVE 2030 targets, working closely with MFI Country Managers and World Vision field offices. You will supervise product training rollout and provide ongoing coaching and mentoring to MFI staff.

You will support the gathering of commodity profiles for the agrocalculator, lead the replication of standard tools and processes developed by Operations into CrediEnterprise projects, and ensure CrediEnterprise figures are accurately reflected in core banking and impact tracking systems. You will monitor performance metrics, assess progress, resolve implementation bottlenecks, and agree on corrective actions with MFIs, escalating issues to Regional and Operational Directors as needed.

You will ensure quality control of MFI partnerships supporting CrediEnterprise implementation, ensure integration with other financial products such as insurance and savings, and maintain coordination and differentiation between Savings Group linkage and the CrediEnterprise product. You will support MFIs in recruiting and developing Agri and Business Development Officers, provide training on THRIVE 2030, monitoring and evaluation, and reporting standards, and build the capacity of CrediEnterprise managers to use the e-THRIVE platform and other World Vision digital platforms for decision-making.

**Programme Reporting and Knowledge Management**

You will lead market systems, agricultural, and climate finance reporting, particularly for CrediEnterprise THRIVE 2030 programme reporting, learning, and knowledge management. You will establish a structured monitoring and evaluation framework, in collaboration with the VFI Global Impact team, to track product performance, gather field data, and assess client feedback.

You will coordinate technical input into VisionFund’s quarterly DME and narrative reporting for THRIVE 2030 quarterly AP and donor progress reports, aligned with THRIVE DME indicators. You will review quarterly THRIVE 2030 market systems reports to identify opportunities to scale CrediEnterprise financing across THRIVE countries and participate in regular country-specific quarterly THRIVE report reviews.

You will develop annual priorities, implementation plans, and budgets for the function in alignment with available resources. You will also develop case studies, implementation briefs, and other learning products to support Community of Practice learning.

**Requirements include:**

- 10 years' experience agri, climate and market systems finance, preferably in Africa
- Agricultural Economics or relevant agricultural degree (or equivalent practical experience). Post-graduate level degree
- Proven experience in market systems and agricultural lending i.e. understands farmer value chains production cycles and cashflows
- Able to communicate the fundamentals of market systems and climate resilience
- Proven ability to implement projects - action oriented, proven ability to implement and follow up
- Good communication skills with staff and partners
- Demonstrated experience in partnering, grant applications, reporting and other writing skills
- Experience across a range of countries (not limited to one or two places is a plus)
- Experience of Value chain/market systems financing or finance to agricultural cooperatives
- Demonstrated experience of working on and or designing programs with a climate change component
- Working level proficiency of written and verbal English. Spoken and written Spanish or French will be a plus

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement:** The position requires ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to **35%** of the time.

jobs.title: Job Counselor
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

Since 2017, IRC Hellas supports vulnerable youth refugee and host communities in Athens to access income generation through employment and self-employment services and skills-building activities, directly and in collaboration with partners. Building on this experience, IRC Hellas, with the support of UNHCR and in partnership with the Municipality of Thessaloniki, is implementing the Youth Empowerment and Self-Reliance project for the third year to promote socio-economic equal access for vulnerable youth in Thessaloniki.

To support with the implementation of the project, IRC Hellas is recruiting a Job Counselor, to be responsible for the day-to-day implementation of employability activities, including service mapping, stakeholder engagement, job counseling and Job Readiness Trainings.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Organize needs assessment and service mapping activities related to employability and skills development programming for youth;
- Participate in stakeholder engagement activities;
- Support the project implementation by designing, organizing and leading Job Readiness Trainings and information sessions for youth;
- Support the project implementation by providing individual employment support/job counseling for youth;
- Proactively working to identify issues related to clients’ participation and report them to the Project Manager.
- Ensuring relevant project data is accurately collected and updated on a weekly and monthly basis.
- Coordinate closely with the team to ensure effective implementation of the provided activities;
- Participate in regular team meetings;
- Ensure regular reporting from the projects is compiled and reports are submitted to the Senior Livelihoods Manager on a weekly/monthly basis;
- Any other task designated by the Project Manager as requested.

**REQUIREMENTS**

BA/BS Degree in social sciences, education, project management, and/or related certification required. Master’s degree or additional certification in Job Counseling is strongly preferred.

- Minimum 2 years’ experience in training, employment support, counseling or project management, primarily in relation to refugee protection. NGO experience preferred.
- Strong interest in supporting refugees and vulnerable populations (experience supporting youth a plus)
- Demonstrated understanding and ability to maintain confidentiality and respect for clients and partners
- Good interpersonal and strong negotiation skills essential with experience in conflict resolution desirable
- Excellent verbal communication skills
- Strong liaison and diplomatic skills
- Punctuality and attention to detail
- Computer skills, in particular Excel
- Fluency in both Greek and English is mandatory

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

**Working hours:** 9:00-17:00

**Travel and other requirements:** Occasionally to other areas of IRC programs in Greece.

**Disclaimer Clause:** This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skills, effort, duties and responsibilities associated with position.

Due to the expected high number of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: €1,631/month). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Training Officer
jobs.body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer for Switchboard, a project that provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:/Users/TigestCo/AppData/Local/Microsoft/Olk/Attachments/ooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe/69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdb/www.SwitchboardTA.org).

The Training Officer will be responsible for leading the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives related to newcomer and refugee services. This role includes providing training and technical assistance to service providers to support them in addressing the general resettlement and case management needs of refugees and newcomers. This role requires prior direct service experience working with clients, subject matter experts, and/or partners to develop culturally responsive service plans to address individual and family client needs utilizing a broad range of approaches, including client-centered, strength-focused, and trauma-informed to meet the social, safety and stability of newcomers.

This staff will be responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective resources, and facilitating learning experiences that contribute to improving outcomes for children, adults, and families.

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Produce written learning resources including blog posts, information guides and toolkits
- Incorporate feedback from internal and external reviewers
- Lead development of multimedia resources, including e-learning modules, videos, and podcasts, in collaboration with colleagues across teams

**Experience:**

**Required:**

- Master’s Degree in a relevant field, such as Master of Social Work (MSW) or equivalent experience.
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience providing pre- and post-arrival services to newcomer clients, supporting their access to educational, financial, medical, social, and community resources while promoting self-sufficiency

**Preferred:**

- Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), Master of Social Work (MSW), or equivalent experience
- Direct service work experience in refugee and newcomer education services
- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations
- Experience managing external subject matter experts and/or consultants
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines and efficient time management
- Adequate technology literacy including intermediate knowledge of MS Office Suite (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel), and Zoom, with adaptability to learning new and innovative technology.
- Strong attention to detail

***Language Skills:*** Fluent in written and spoken English***.***
