jobs.title: Consultance sur l'analyse et l’amélioration de la gestion des déchets de soins de santé dans les délégations internationales de la CRF
jobs.body:
## **Contexte de la mission de consultance**

La Croix-Rouge Française (CRF) met en œuvre des projets internationaux principalement dans les domaines de la santé et de la gestion des risques de catastrophes (GRC). Au sein de la Direction des Opérations Internationales (DOI), le Département Santé et Gestion des Risques de Catastrophe intervient notamment dans le renforcement des systèmes de santé, la réponse aux épidémies, la santé communautaire et la formation paramédicale. La CRF intervient également en situation d’urgence, notamment à travers son Pôle Urgence International (PUI), qui contribue au déploiement de capacités de réponse adaptées aux crises et aux besoins humanitaires.

La gestion des déchets de soins de santé dans ces différents contextes constitue un enjeu transversal de qualité des soins, de prévention des risques, de sécurité, de respect de la dignité des personnes et de protection de l’environnement.

Une attention particulière devra être portée à la gestion des déchets pharmaceutiques, compte tenu des risques sanitaires, environnementaux, réglementaires et de détournement associés. Leur gestion sera analysée depuis leur identification et leur mise à l'écart jusqu'à leur traitement et leur élimination finale, en incluant les modalités de stockage temporaire, de traçabilité, de transport et de destruction.

La gestion des déchets de soins de santé participe directement à la perception de la qualité des soins et à la crédibilité de la CRF et du Mouvement.

La présente consultance vise à analyser les pratiques de gestion des déchets de soins de santé au sein des délégations internationales de la CRF concernées, au regard des cadres réglementaires nationaux applicables, des pratiques des Sociétés Nationales Hôtes, des standards internationaux, des évolutions techniques du domaine et des contraintes propres aux différents contextes d’intervention.

Une attention particulière sera portée à la gestion des déchets de soins de santé en contexte d’urgence aiguë, notamment dans le cadre du déploiement de dispositifs de réponse aux épidémies et aux crises sanitaires tels que les Centres de Traitement du Choléra (CTC) et les Centres de Traitement Ebola (CTE) et plus largement les cliniques d’urgence déployables par la CRF lors de ce type de réponse. La consultance devra notamment analyser les besoins, contraintes et modalités opérationnelles spécifiques à ces contextes, notamment en matière de gestion des déchets infectieux et de prévention et contrôle des infections (PCI). Ce travail devra en particulier contribuer au processus en cours de la CRF relatif à la certification EMT de l’OMS, en identifiant les principes, procédures, équipements et capacités nécessaires à une gestion sûre et opérationnelle des déchets dans le cadre du déploiement d’une équipe médicale d’urgence.

Sur la base de l’état des lieux, la consultance formulera des recommandations opérationnelles, réalistes et contextualisées pour renforcer la qualité, la sécurité et la cohérence des pratiques de gestion des déchets de soins de santé.

## **Objectif général de la mission de consultance**

Analyser les pratiques de gestion des déchets de soins de santé dans les délégations internationales de la CRF et proposer des recommandations opérationnelles, priorisées et adaptées aux contextes d’intervention, en intégrant les exigences réglementaires, les standards internationaux, les innovations techniques et les contraintes opérationnelles.

## **Objectifs spécifiques de la mission de consultance**

Les objectifs spécifiques de la mission sont les suivants :

- **Réaliser un état des lieux des pratiques** de gestion des déchets de soins de santé dans les délégations concernées et, lorsque pertinent, dans les structures de santé appuyées, incluant, lorsque les données disponibles le permettent, une caractérisation des principaux flux de déchets de soins de santé et pharmaceutiques observés, de leur nature, de leur importance relative et des contextes dans lesquels ils sont générés, y compris la gestion en situation d’urgence aiguë ;
- **Conduire une revue de littérature et des pratiques internationales** afin d’identifier les évolutions, innovations et bonnes pratiques pertinentes ;
- **Analyser les cadres légaux et réglementaires applicables** et les mettre en perspective avec les pratiques observées au sein de la CRF et des systèmes nationaux de santé ;
- **Identifier les écarts, contraintes opérationnelles et risques associés** aux circuits de tri, stockage, transport, traitement et élimination ;
- **Proposer des recommandations opérationnelles** et priorisées permettant d’améliorer les pratiques de la CRF et, lorsque pertinent, des structures de santé appuyées, en distinguant, les principes ou standards minimaux applicables et les options devant être adaptées aux différents contextes d’intervention ;
- **Identifier, lorsque la qualité des données le permet, les éléments susceptibles d’alimenter une production scientifique** (publication ou poster) à soumettre à une conférence internationale ou un support de capitalisation.

## Méthodologie de la mission de consultance

La méthodologie sera proposée par le/la consultant·e et validée avec la CRF au démarrage de la mission. Elle devra notamment combiner :

- **Une phase de cadrage**, permettant de préciser le périmètre, les délégations concernées, les sources de données disponibles et les modalités de collecte ;
- **Une revue documentaire et bibliographique**, incluant les références réglementaires, les standards internationaux, les pratiques des Sociétés Nationales Hôtes (SNH), ainsi que les évolutions, innovations et bonnes pratiques récentes en matière de gestion des déchets de soins de santé ;
- **La conception des outils de collecte et d’analyse**, notamment questionnaires, guides d’entretien et/ou grilles d’analyse ;
- **La collecte et la consolidation des données** auprès des délégations concernées, à travers l’analyse documentaire, des entretiens avec les équipes et, lorsque pertinent, des observations de terrain. La gestion des déchets en situation d’urgence devra également être prise en compte ;
- **L’analyse des pratiques et des circuits de gestion des déchets de soins de santé**, notamment le tri, le stockage, le transport, le traitement et l’élimination, au regard des cadres réglementaires nationaux, des standards internationaux et des pratiques de référence, en intégrant, pour les solutions de traitement et d’élimination et lorsque pertinent, leurs consommations énergétiques, émissions et rejets, résidus générés, besoins de maintenance et de consommables, ainsi que leur adéquation aux capacités techniques locales ;
- **Une analyse spécifique du circuit des déchets pharmaceutiques**, comprenant a minima les modalités d'identification, de mise à l'écart, de stockage temporaire, de sécurisation, de traçabilité, de transport et de destruction, ainsi que les responsabilités des différents acteurs impliqués ;
- **L’identification des écarts, risques et contraintes opérationnelles**, en tenant compte des capacités disponibles et des spécificités des différents contextes d’intervention, ainsi que, lorsque ces éléments ressortent des données collectées, des principaux facteurs contribuant à la génération des déchets observés, afin de pouvoir alimenter les réflexions ultérieures sur leur prévention et leur réduction à la source ;
- **Des échanges réguliers avec la CRF**, notamment avec le Référent EHA, la fonction Environnement, les équipes concernées par l’EMT et, selon les sujets analysés, les autres fonctions métiers concernées, afin de partager les constats et d’alimenter l’analyse ;
- **La formulation de recommandations opérationnelles et priorisées**, tenant compte de leur pertinence, de leur faisabilité et des contraintes propres aux différents contextes d’intervention ;
- **L’identification des possibilités de valorisation des résultats**, notamment sous la forme d’une production scientifique ou d’un support de capitalisation, lorsque la qualité et la quantité des données le permettent.

## **Livrables attendus**

**Rapport de cadrage**

• Compréhension du besoin et du périmètre ; méthodologie détaillée ; outils de collecte ; délégations/contextes ciblés ; chronogramme indicatif ; modalités d’échanges et de validation.

**Livrable intermédiaire – état des lieux et analyses**

• Données consolidées et analysées ; synthèse des pratiques observées ; analyse des circuits de gestion ; principaux écarts, risques et contraintes ; premiers constats sur la gestion en urgence.

**Note de synthèse sur la littérature, les standards et les pratiques internationales**

• Synthèse des références examinées ; évolutions et innovations ; bonnes pratiques ; éléments transférables ou adaptables à la CRF.

• La note de synthèse comprendra une section dédiée présentant les principes et modalités opérationnelles applicables aux dispositifs de réponse sanitaire d’urgence, ainsi que les recommandations spécifiques pour le déploiement d’une EMT, incluant les besoins en équipements, consommables, organisation des circuits, traitement et élimination des déchets.

**Proposition d'un outil pratique d'aide à la décision pour la gestion des déchets de soins de santé et pharmaceutiques** (grille, arbre décisionnel, fiche pratique ou format équivalent), permettant aux délégations et, lorsque pertinent, aux structures de santé appuyées, à partir de la nature du déchet, des risques associés et des solutions disponibles localement, d’identifier les modalités recommandées de tri, stockage, transport, traitement et élimination. L’outil sera conçu dans un format modulaire permettant son adaptation aux différents contextes et son enrichissement ultérieur, notamment sur les dimensions de prévention et de réduction à la source

**Rapport final de consultance**

• État des lieux consolidé ; analyse réglementaire et comparative ; résultats de terrain le cas échéant ; recommandations opérationnelles priorisées, accompagnées, lorsque pertinent, d’éléments sur leur temporalité, les acteurs et responsabilités concernés, les principaux prérequis et les éventuels besoins d’investissement ; annexes avec outils et éléments utiles à la capitalisation.

**Support(s) de valorisation, si pertinent**

• Proposition de note technique, poster, communication institutionnelle ou contribution scientifique, selon la qualité des données et validation de la CRF.

## Organisation de la consultance et chronogramme

### **Phases de la consultance**

Phase 0 – Cadrage de la mission : validation du périmètre, revue documentaire initiale, méthodologie, outils de collecte et chronogramme.

Phase 1 – État des lieux et collecte : collecte documentaire, questionnaires/entretiens, consolidation des données et analyse des pratiques.

Phase 2 – Analyse comparative et terrain : revue de littérature, analyse réglementaire et des standards, comparaison des pratiques ; mission(s) terrain si retenue(s).

Phase 3 – Recommandations et capitalisation : formulation et priorisation des recommandations, restitution intermédiaire/finale, finalisation des livrables et propositions de valorisation.

Des temps d’échanges avec le/la consultant·e seront prévus entre et pendant les différentes phases.

### **Chronogramme**

La mission se déroulera entre novembre 2026 et avril 2027, selon une durée et un calendrier détaillé à proposer par le/la consultant·e dans son offre, selon le périmètre validé et la proposition méthodologique du/de la consultant·e. Le calendrier détaillé sera arrêté avec la CRF au démarrage de la mission.

Phase 0 : Cadrage et méthodologie – durée à proposer

Phase 1 : Collecte et état des lieux – durée à proposer

Phase 2 : Analyse comparative et terrain – durée à proposer

Phase 3 : Recommandations, restitution et finalisation – durée à proposer

Ce chronogramme constitue une base de structuration de la mission et sera finalisé avec le/la consultant·e retenu·e.

jobs.title: RFP- Donor Landscape Assessment in Kenya
jobs.body:
## Request for Proposal (RFP)

Issued on: September 25, 2026

Solicitation Number: **51495**

For: Donor Landscape Assessment

Quotes Deadline: October 9, 2026

1. **Background**

For nearly 70 years, Pathfinder International has been a catalyst for systems transformation, inclusive growth, and resilient communities. With a global footprint spanning Africa, South Asia, and the Middle East, we invest in women and girls by expanding access to essential health products and services, unlocking leadership pathways, and strengthening economic participation. By partnering with civil society, governments, and the private sector, we scale women-led innovations that deliver sustainable systems of support, while generating measurable impact with the goal to ensure every woman has the agency to shape her future and lead a healthy, fulfilling life.

Pathfinder International Kenya - a registered Non-Governmental Organization under Kenya PBO Act seeks to strengthen its sustainability and diversify its funding base in response to the evolving development financing landscape. While it has extensive experience working with all kinds of donors, , Pathfinder International Kenya aims to expand and diversify its funding portfolio by exploring opportunities within philanthropy, corporate social investment, and foundations in Kenya.

To support this ambition, Pathfinder International Kenya is seeking an external consultant to conduct a market assessment of various donor segments and provide strategic recommendations on engagement, investment requirements, and expected returns.

1. **Objectives of the Assignment**

- Assess the scope and size of the philanthropic, corporate social investment, and foundations targeting not-for-profit, Non-Governmental Organizations registered and implementing development projects in Kenya.
- Identify high-potential donors and funding mechanisms aligned with Pathfinder International strategic priorities and operational presence.
- Determine the investment (financial, human, operational) required to effectively engage all donor segments and the expected timeline for return on investment.
- Recommend realistic funding targets for the 2027–2033 for these donor segments.
- Assess the feasibility and competitive advantage of operating as a local organization versus an INGO.
- Identify potential opportunities for local NGOs versus INGOs.

**3. Scope of Work**

The consultant will:

**a. Review Pathfinder International Kenya’s historical and current funding trends,** with a specific focus on performance and lessons learned within philanthropy, corporate social investment, and foundations

**b. Conduct market research** to:

- Map the landscape of current donors in Kenya specifically relevant to Pathfinder International Kenya’s work.
- Identify key active bilateral, corporate donors, foundations, and social enterprises with strategic alignment to Pathfinder International and the type of organizations (local Vs International) they currently prefer to fund.
- Understand giving behaviors, motivations, and barriers for philanthropic giving in Kenya (specifically relevant to strategic interventions aligned with Pathfinder’s work in Kenya)

**c. Benchmark peer organizations** to understand:

- Who is accessing these funds?
- How much funding is being secured?
- What investments were required to achieve success.
- What is their legal status: Local versus International organizations.

**d. Analyze investment requirements**:

- Financial resources, staffing, systems, partnerships, and leadership support.
- Timeline and risk factors for return on investment.

**e. Recommend funding targets** for the 2027–2033 for these donor segments.

**4. Deliverables**

- **Inception Report**: Detailing methodology, work plan, and stakeholder engagement strategy.
- **Market Assessment Report**: Comprehensive analysis of donor segments, investment requirements, and strategic recommendations including type of registration recommended for Pathfinder.
- **Funding Target Recommendations**: Scenario-based projections for CS 2027–2033.
- **Presentation to Pathfinder International Management**: Summary of findings and recommendations.

**5. Duration and Timeline**

- **Estimated Duration**: 15 working days
- **Timeline**: October-November 2026
- **Budget**: Proposals should demonstrate a clear value-for-money approach. The total budget will be a key factor in the selection process.

**6. Consultant Profile**

- Proven experience in resource mobilization, donor landscape analysis, and strategic planning in Kenya and East Africa.
- Very strong understanding of Kenya’s donor landscape, including philanthropic, private sector and corporate giving environment.
- Experience working with NGOs or development organizations in Kenya.
- Excellent analytical, communication, presentation and stakeholder engagement skills.

**7. Management and Reporting**

The consultant will report to the Business Development Director or his appointee at Pathfinder International, who will be the primary point of contact. Key milestones and findings will be shared with the Country Management Team (CMT) and presented to the Board of Directors at the conclusion of the assignment for strategic approval.

**8. Payment Schedule**

All payments will be tied to the successful completion and approval of deliverables, ensuring accountability for outputs and quality.

**Key Milestones and Deliverables**

**Milestone / Deliverable(s) / Payment %**

Upon approval of Inception Report/ Inception Report (methodology, work plan, stakeholder engagement plan) / 30%

Upon approval of Draft Market Assessment / Draft Market Assessment Report (including donor analysis, investment requirements, operational & supply chain readiness) / 30%

Upon approval of Final Deliverables / Final Report, Annual Funding Target Recommendations for Pathfinder International Kenya, Dataset, and Presentation to Pathfinder International Management / 40%

- The consultant is responsible for managing all expenses within the agreed total budget.
- Payment tranches are fixed percentages of the total contract value and will not be adjusted based on actual spending differences.
- The consultant must arrange their own insurance coverage (including health and travel insurance) and ensure compliance with national tax laws (e.g., VAT or income tax obligations).

**Proposal Guidelines and Instructions**

Offerors will be required to submit two electronically sealed proposals, one a technical proposal and the other a cost proposal. All proposals must be signed and valid for a minimum of sixty (60) days.

Your proposal should provide basic information about your Company/Individual and relevant service offerings. It should have a section addressing each of the following areas:

Responses should include the following information:

**A, Technical Proposal**

1. **Technical Proposal** (offeror will be evaluated based on their responsiveness to the Scope of Work)
    - Overview of the proposed approach and methodology.
    - Description of tools and techniques for data collection and analysis
    - Outline of key activities and timeline.
    - Summary of relevant experience in similar assignments.
2. **Consultant/Firm Profile**
    - Summary of qualifications and expertise, including experience working with NGOs and the philanthropic/corporate sector in Kenya.
    - Key personnel and roles (include brief bios or CV highlights).
3. **References**
    - At least two references from previous clients for similar assignments.
    - Contact details and brief description of the work undertaken.

**B. Cost/Financial Proposal**

Provide detailed and complete information on the cost that will be incurred by Pathfinder International. Such costs must include all items and not limited to the following:

- Detailed budget breakdown including daily rates, number of days, and any anticipated reimbursable expenses.
- Budget must be inclusive of all taxes.

### Evaluation Criteria

In evaluating the proposals, Pathfinder International will seek the **best value for money**

rather than the lowest priced proposal. Pathfinder will use a two-stage selection procedure:

- the first stage will evaluate the Technical Proposal. The technical proposal opening will be attended only by Pathfinders, as no information other than who submitted an offer will be read out at this stage.
- the second stage will evaluate the Cost Proposal for proposals that pass the Technical Proposal evaluation. Only proposals with an average score of 70 and above will be considered eligible for stage 2

Specifically, the selection committee will evaluate each proposal upon the following criteria:

**Evaluation Criteria / Total Weight 100 points.**

**Bid Submission - Pass/Fail**

1. Bid submitted on time
2. Offeror is eligible to receive funding per background checks
3. Any potential conflict of interest is sufficiently mitigated

**Technical Proposal - 40 points**

- Overview of the proposed approach and methodology.
- Description of tools and techniques for data collection and analysis
- Outline of key activities and timeline.
- Summary of relevant experience in similar assignments.

**Consultant/Firm Profile - 30 points**

- Summary of qualifications and expertise, including experience working with NGOs and the philanthropic/corporate sector in Kenya.
- Key personnel and roles (include brief bios or CV highlights).

**References - 30 points**

- At least two references from previous clients for similar assignments.
- Contact details and brief description of the work undertaken.
- Provide any other information to demonstrate the Contractor’s capability in relation to the Scope of Work.

Pathfinder is not bound to accept the lowest or any proposal and reserves the right to accept any proposal in whole or in part and to reject any or all proposals.

Pathfinder shall not be legally bound by any award notice issued for this RFP until a contract is duly signed and executed with the winning offeror.

The evaluator will tally all the individual scores for each section and calculate the total score. If the total number points meet or exceeds the 70 point threshold, the suppliers cost proposal will be eligible for consideration.

The score for the cost proposal will be calculated in the following manner:

Cost proposal score = 100 x Lowest cost/ cost of the proposal under consideration. The lowest cost proposal will receive the full 100 points.

The total score will be calculated as follows:

Total Score= Technical proposal score of the proposal under consideration multiplied by 70 plus (+) Cost proposal score of the proposal under consideration multiplied by 30.

### Inquiries

If you have any questions/inquiries, please e-mail nairobiprocurement@pathfinder.org no later than close of business **October 1, 2026.** The solicitation number indicated above must be included in the subject line. Responses will be posted to all known offerors.

As part of this RFP process, Pathfinder reserves the right to conduct interviews with bidders.

### Proposal Deadline

All written responses to this RFP must be received by Pathfinder no later than **17:00hrs EAT** on **October 9, 2026**. The solicitation number indicated above must be included in the subject line/on the envelope.

Please email the quote and other information directly to: nairobiprocurement@pathfinder.org

Pathfinder International, Kenya.

Please label each proposal attachment. One should be labeled technical proposal and the other

Cost proposal. The solicitation number indicated above must be included in the reference line.

Late submissions will not be considered. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an interview or presentation to further discuss their proposed approach. The successful applicant will be selected based on technical expertise, relevant experience, value for money, and demonstrated capacity to comply with Pathfinder Kenya’s ethical and safeguarding standards

### Modification

If at any time prior to award Pathfinder deems there to be a need for a significant modification to the terms and conditions of this RFP, Pathfinder will issue such a modification as a written RFP amendment to all competing offerors. No oral statement of any person shall in any manner be deemed to modify or otherwise affect any RFP term or condition, and no offeror shall rely on any such statement. Such amendments are the exclusive method for this purpose.

### Resulting Award

Single contract: As a result of this solicitation, Pathfinder anticipates engaging a single independent contractor/company. Pathfinder reserves the right to split the SOW and make multiple awards.

Any resulting contract will be subject to the terms and conditions contained in Annex A. Part A of this annex will only apply to USG-funded assignments.

### Payment Terms

Pathfinder anticipates entering into a cost-reimbursable fixed-cost contract with the selected contractor.

### Terms

Pathfinder reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any point and is under no obligation to issue a subcontract as a result of this solicitation.

Pathfinder will not reimburse any expenses related to the preparation of any proposal related materials or delivery.

### Confidentiality

All information disclosed by either party regarding this RFP is confidential and shall be treated as such.

### Agreement

Any resulting contract will be subject to the terms and conditions contained in the annex. See Annex A

jobs.title: Operatrice Inserimento Lavorativo
jobs.body:
**Posizione:** Operatrice Inserimento Lavorativo

**Dipartimento:** Dipartimento di Comunicazione, Ricerca, Advocacy e Programmi Domestici

**Riporta a:** Coordinatrice Spazio Donna Milano

**Sede di lavoro:** Milano, Corvetto e Giambellino

**Data di inizio:** ottobre 2026

**Durata del contratto:** fino al 31/12/2026, con possibilità di rinnovo

**Scadenza per la candidatura:** 23/10/2026

**Chi siamo**

WeWorld è un’organizzazione italiana no profit e indipendente che da 50 anni difende i diritti di tutte le persone per costruire un mondo più equo e garantire loro una vita dignitosa, opportunità e un futuro migliore. Lavora in oltre 20 Paesi nel mondo, inclusa l’Italia, con progetti di emergenza, aiuto umanitario e cooperazione allo sviluppo. La sua azione si rivolge soprattutto a donne, bambine e adolescenti, protagoniste e protagonisti del cambiamento in ogni comunità per un mondo più giusto e inclusivo.

**Job description**

WeWorld sta cercando un’operatrice che supporti i percorsi di inserimento lavorativo delle persone che si rivolgono allo Spazio Donna di Milano e giovani ragazzi e ragazze NEET, svolgendo un ruolo di raccordo tra il servizio e gli enti del territorio che si occupano di orientamento, formazione professionale, politiche attive del lavoro e matching domanda-offerta.

La risorsa avrà il compito di accompagnare le persone nella definizione del proprio progetto professionale, valorizzandone competenze e potenzialità e facilitando l'accesso alle opportunità lavorative più coerenti.

Lo Spazio Donna è centro diurno di accoglienza, socializzazione, sostegno e orientamento per donne in situazioni di fragilità e che non di rado vivono situazioni di violenza.

**PRINCIPALI MANSIONI E RESPONSABILITÀ**

L'operatrice svolgerà, sotto la supervisione della Coordinatrice dello Spazio Donna, i seguenti compiti:

- Realizzazione di colloqui individuali di orientamento e accompagnamento al lavoro.
- Supporto nella stesura, revisione e aggiornamento dei curricula vitae.
- Raccolta, valutazione e preselezione delle candidature
- Individuazione delle opportunità lavorative più adeguate ai profili delle utenti.
- Invio delle candidature, monitoraggio degli esiti e follow-up con gli enti coinvolti.
- Attività di scouting e sviluppo di relazioni con aziende, cooperative e altre realtà del territorio interessate all'inserimento lavorativo e/o tirocini di persone in situazione di vulnerabilità.
- Attivazione e gestione di partnership con enti accreditati al lavoro, agenzie per il lavoro, imprese e servizi territoriali per favorire il matching tra domanda e offerta.
- Accompagnamento nelle diverse fasi di accesso al mercato del lavoro e monitoraggio dei percorsi attivati.
- Gestione iter burocratico avvio di potenziali tirocini
- Raccordo costante con l'équipe multidisciplinare di Spazio Donna per la definizione e l'aggiornamento dei progetti individualizzati.
- Mappatura e aggiornamento delle opportunità formative e occupazionali presenti sul territorio milanese

**Requisiti per la posizione**

**REQUISITI ESSENZIALI**

- Laurea in ambito umanistico/sociale
- Conoscenza delle principali misure, servizi e attori del mercato del lavoro del territorio milanese
- Buona conoscenza degli strumenti informatici e dei principali portali per la ricerca di lavoro
- Conoscenza delle tematiche legate all'empowerment femminile e all'approccio interculturale e intersezionale

**Esperienze professionali**

- Esperienza di almeno 2-3 anni nell'ambito dell'orientamento e dell'inserimento lavorativo di persone in condizioni di vulnerabilità
- Esperienza nella collaborazione con servizi sociali, enti di formazione e agenzie per il lavoro

**Competenze e capacità**

- Elevata capacità di ascolto e relazione empatica
- Capacità di costruire e mantenere relazioni con reti territoriali e stakeholder
- Forti capacità relazionali e di coinvolgimento/attivazione di singoli e gruppi
- Attitudine al lavoro in squadra, proattività, dinamicità, spirito critico e capacità di lavorare per obiettivi e nel rispetto dei tempi
- Sensibilità e adattabilità ai diversi contesti culturali, di genere, di religione, di etnia, di nazionalità ed età
- Precisione, affidabilità e capacità di pianificazione
- Forte impegno nei confronti della Mission di WeWorld e sincero interesse per gli argomenti di cooperazione internazionale e sviluppo

**COSA OFFRIAMO**

**Tipologia di contratto:** co.co.co/partita IVA

**Condizioni economiche:** compenso a partire da 17,26€ lordi/ora da definire in funzione dell’esperienza maturata e della tipologia contrattuale

**Disponibilità richiesta**: 20 ore al mese

**Cultura organizzativa orientata alle persone:** un ambiente di lavoro inclusivo e collaborativo, in cui benessere, rispetto e cooperazione sono al primo posto

**Pari Opportunità**

Ci impegniamo a promuovere un ambiente di lavoro inclusivo e rispettoso, in cui tutte le persone abbiano pari accesso alle opportunità professionali. Le decisioni relative all'impiego sono basate esclusivamente sul merito, sulle qualifiche e sulle esigenze organizzative, senza discriminazioni legate a genere, identità di genere, orientamento sessuale, razza, etnia, nazionalità, religione o convinzioni personali, età, stato civile o familiare, genitorialità, disabilità o qualsiasi altra caratteristica tutelata dalla normativa vigente.

Siamo impegnati a costruire team diversificati e di talento e accogliamo con favore le candidature di persone provenienti da ogni background ed esperienza.

jobs.title: Grants and Reporting Coordinantor
jobs.body:
**Country Programme:** Ukraine

**Contract Length:** 1 year with possible extension

**Base:** Kyiv

**Starting date:** November 2026

**Line Manager:** Head of Grants and Rerporting

**People in Need** (PIN) is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 20 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad.

## **About the Ukrainian Programme of People in Need:**

People in Need (PIN) began operations in Ukraine in 2003 with human rights programs and expanded to humanitarian assistance in 2014. With the full-scale invasion in February 2022, we significantly scaled up our programming across the country. Since then, PIN has reached almost 4 million people, working with a network of local partner organizations.

Today, PIN has its offices and teams in 8 oblasts in Ukraine with more than 500 local and international staff working in Lvivska, Kyivska (head office), Sumska, Kharkivska, Dnipropetrovska, Mykolaivska and Khersonska, Zaporizka, and Donetska oblasts.

PIN's assistance addresses both immediate and longer-term needs of war-affected people, focusing on safe water and sanitation, shelter repairs, protection services, and education in emergencies. Our recovery programming delivers more systemic solutions, including support to district heating systems and renewable energy initiatives.

PIN also provides comprehensive assistance to veterans and their families, including business grants and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), strengthens the quality of education in schools, and advances systemic improvements in social care for the most vulnerable. Funding comes from a diverse range of institutional and private donors.

## **About the role:**

As a member of the Country Programme (CP) and specifically a team member of the Grants and Reporting Unit, with the support of the Head of Grants and Reporting (HoGR), the Grants and Reporting Coordinator (GC) will oversee assigned grants’ implementation progress, particularly in relation to approved proposal and in compliance with donor’s rules and procedures. The GC will report on their assigned project/s in close collaboration with relevant teams. The Grants and Reporting Coordinator will act as a Grants Focal Point (GFP) as assigned during the proposal development, will support or lead the proposal development and project modification processes, and may act as a focal point for external liaison, including representing PIN vis-à-vis donors and in other coordination forums as assigned. Other tasks may be assigned by the HoGR as deemed necessary.

## **Main Duties & Responsibilities:**

**Program Coordination and Grants Management:**

- Maintains an internal tracking database of her/his assigned grants/donors, reporting timelines, project milestones/targets and modifications. Ensures comprehensive grant files, donor guidelines and resources are maintained, updated and available for use.
- Coordinates with Area Managers and Area teams, Programme Coordinators,
- MEAL, Technical Leads, as well as Advocacy and Communication, Procurement, Finance, Database, Partnership units, and Security department as well as Headquarters (HQ) focal points to ensure accurate tracking and reporting of programmatic adjustments throughout the project life cycle.
- Advises teams and partners, where needed, on donor’s compliance, rules and requirements in coordination with other relevant units.
- Prepares and leads the kick off, project review, and close out meetings, and participates in other project/grant-related meetings e.g. Lessons Learned meeting. Prepares documents and collects information from relevant Finance, Logistics/Procurement, Partnership (PI), MEAL, Comms and Advocacy, Security, Data and Programme teams in order to facilitate regular project review meetings.
- Prepares regular updates for key donors on project progress, achievement highlights and challenges as well as shares briefing notes, other project and communication materials with respective donors
- Provides information to relevant staff members on reporting timelines of the assigned project/s. Ensures relevant staff are provided with timely information and materials – including guidelines, templates and examples – to develop quality reporting contributions. Acts as a focal point for collection, compilation, review, quality control and editing of both quantitative and qualitative internal and donor reporting.
- Prepares all donor narrative reports and coordinates necessary clearances and submission of reports and necessary annexes; and flags inconsistencies, if identified to the Finance Department to ensure that financial and narrative reports are aligned.
- In collaboration with technical leads, ensures that all reports are in-line with the assigned donor/s requirements in structure and content, including mainstreaming issues such as protection, gender, do no harm, and conflict sensitivity.
- Works with Data team to report on all quantitative figures; flags any discrepancies if identified, to Data team; utilises dashboards and databases as primary source of information, working with Area teams to provide qualitative information where dashboards have gaps.
- In coordination with the PI and Technical Leads, reviews all MEAL products that will be submitted to the donor to ensure alignment with reports and donor communication.
- Prepares Modification Request, No-cost Extension, and/or Cost Extension packages in coordination with relevant departments. Supports finalisation of relevant project-related documents prepared by other departments, such as Evaluation Terms of References (ToRs), Third Party Monitoring (TPM) plans, etc. and coordinates with TPM organizations contributing to planning monitoring visits.
- Undertakes regular field visits to gain in-depth understanding of the context and implementation.
- Coordinates donor-related field visits as needed.

**Fundraising and Resource Mobilization:**

- Proactively supports in monitoring and analysis of new funding opportunities for PIN in Ukraine through relevant open sources (donor websites, humanitarian assistance portals), clusters, and bilateral consultation and scoping with existing and potential donors.
- Working in close collaboration with Technical Leads, Programme Coordinators and Area teams, as well as other relevant units and departments, acts as a GFP and/or Proposal Lead, as assigned; supports preparation for Go-No-Go and proposal kick-off preparation meetings, proposal development workplan/timelines; leads development of concept notes, proposals (including supporting the design of logical frameworks, targets, and budgets); ensures updated and current templates are available for narrative, finance, and other parts or annexes.
- Leads proposal modifications and situation analyses – including modifications in logical frameworks, targets, and budgets.
- As assigned, creates and shares a folder on SharePoint for the internal proposal preparation, creates a Teams chat for relevant colleagues, and were helpful organizes sectoral design chats/discussions.
- As assigned, creates the [Resource Folder in ELO](https://elo.pinf.cz/ix-CZE/plugin/de.elo.ix.plugin.proxy/web/?useSSO=true#/archive/(A5A8F0FF-3B32-48C6-A732-71520F4FB7B6)/) (PIN’s internal system) and initiates the workflow.
- Follows-up on relevant action items from Ukraine Fundraising and Resource Mobilization meetings, as well as other meetings, ensuring timely completion of relevant tasks.

**Internal and External Coordination:**

- Communicates with relevant donors and represents PIN at the appropriate level of representation.
- Participates in meetings with HQ and other coordination meetings as requested by the line manager.
- Coordinates with focal points from Finance, Data team, MEAL, Programme Quality, and Area teams during proposal development and reporting periods as well as partners, as needed.
- Coordinates with communications team to ensure that relevant communication materials (human interest stories, videos, etc.) are developed for projects as per workplan and donors’ requirements; as well as ensures distribution of readily available communication materials to donors.
- Acts as the main project focal point for respective donors.

## **Requirements:**

- Communicates with relevant donors and represents PIN at the appropriate level of representation.
- Participates in meetings with HQ and other coordination meetings as requested by the line manager.
- Coordinates with focal points from Finance, Data team, MEAL, Programme Quality, and Area teams during proposal development and reporting periods as well as partners, as needed.
- Coordinates with communications team to ensure that relevant communication materials (human interest stories, videos, etc.) are developed for projects as per workplan and donors’ requirements; as well as ensures distribution of readily available communication materials to donors.
- Acts as the main project focal point for respective donors.

## **We offer:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context;
- **Starting Salary** based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies, between 2600-2800 EUR;
- **Additional allowances include**:
    - Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR;
    - Monthly Hardship Allowance of 400 EUR;
    - Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance up to 1000 EUR;
- **Time off and Rest:**
    - 25 days of holiday annually;
    - 10 sick days
    - Rest & Recreation (R&R) policy in place: 3x 5 days of leave per year with 350 Eur lump sum allowance per each leave.
- **Travel benefits:**
    - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work;
    - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure;
    - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment;
    - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
- **Health and Well-being:**
    - 24/7 Medical Support available online;
    - Free psychological consultations available online;
- **Professional Development:** Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities, including Hostile Environment Awareness Training (HEAT);

## **Security situation in Ukraine**

Humanitarian workers continue to operate throughout Ukraine, although the front-line areas are being shelled almost constantly, and main cities are being targeted with missiles and UAVs quite regularly. PIN security SOPs require PIN staff to proceed to shelter should the risk level be assessed by the Security Department as the highest (launch of missiles or drones) and remain there until the air raid siren is cancelled, which cumulatively can be several times a week, occasionally for several hours at a time (although shorter periods are as well occurring). While air strikes that were targeting energy, infrastructure have finished after winter, they have succeeded in reaching their goals and are likely to resume in late autumn/winter. At the moment military and civilian objects are being targeted, including the west of Ukraine. While Kyiv enjoys relatively strong air defence systems that are intercepting most of the missiles and UAVs, other regions are covered much less significantly which results in bigger damage. Outside of the areas in the vicinity to the contact line, services such as medical care, shops, public transportation as well as restaurants or leisure facilities remain operational.

People in Need expects all staff to perform job duties and responsibilities in accordance with People in Need code of conduct and key policies (available at:* [*https://www.peopleinneed.net/key-policies-4142gp*](https://www.peopleinneed.net/key-policies-4142gp)*). People in Need Staff will undertake the appropriate level of training.*

*All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks.*

jobs.title: Consultancy – Food Insecurity and armed groups
jobs.body:
**Department:** Policy, Research & Legal

**Work place:** Remote

**Duration of the Consultancy:** Approximately 50-60 working days depending on rate between November 1 to January 31

## **Objective**

The objective of the consultancy is to conduct a global mapping of armed groups and de facto authorities’ (AGDAs) policies and practices and assess how they contribute to or threaten food security for conflict affected communities in order to generate evidence-based insights for programmatic decisions.

## **Scope of Work and Key Tasks** 

- Identify and document AGDA policies, directives, and practices affecting food security with a particular focus on Geneva Call’s areas of operations.
- Categorize practices along a spectrum from enabling to obstruction to harmful, including in relation to access to land, agricultural inputs, and natural resources; freedom of movement; taxation; looting; governance of markets, pricing, and distribution systems; facilitation of humanitarian access; and deliberate attacks or destruction, sieges, or blockades affecting access to or availability of food.
- Map variations depending on different types of armed groups (groups controlling territories, community-based groups, etc.) and the territorial governance context (contested, consolidated).
- Gender and inclusion lens to assess the differentiated impact on women, children, marginalized or minority groups, and returnees.
- Develop data collection tools to gather relevant information from Geneva Call field colleagues and other external stakeholders and undertake key informant interviews or focus group discussions.
- Analysis and reporting: Produce two final reports: first, an internal report with detailed findings, typology of AGDA practices, implications for engagement based on humanitarian norms, guidance on how to integrate all aspects of food insecurity into Geneva Call’s work, and recommendations for training and engagement materials; second, an external report to highlight key trends and evidence for advocacy purposes.

## **Expected Deliverables**

**Deliverable & Timeline**

- Inception Report (methodology, work plan, data collection tools, preliminary desk review 
    - November 13: Final timeline to be adjusted as needed
- Comprehensive desk review and tool refinement
    - November 20: Includes analysis of existing Geneva Call materials
- Data collection period 
    - December 10: Compilation of survey and consultation input
- First version of internal report 
    - December 23
- Revised version of internal report First draft of external report 
    - January 15
- Final versions of internal and external report 
    - January 31

**Total estimated level of effort: approximately 50-60 working days depending on rate between November 1 to January 31**.

## **Selection criteria**

**Education**

- Advanced degree international relations, political science, humanitarian law or human rights, develoment studies or related discipline.

**Personal skills**

- Minimum of 10 years of relevant professional experience in humanitarian action, human rights fieldwork, /or conflict analysis.

**Technical skills**

- Proven experience in food security, livelihoods, or protection programming in conflict affected or fragile settings.
- Demonstrated expertise in gender and inclusion analysis, with attention to the differentiated impacts on women, children, marginalized groups, and returnees.
- Strong track record in qualitative research methods.
- Excellent analytical and reporting writing skills, with experience producing both internal and external deliverables.
- Familitary with international humanitarian law and other relevant legal frameworks.

**Languages**

- Excellent communication skills in English (required).
- Knowledge of French or Arabic (an asset).

jobs.title: Head of Programmes, South Sudan
source: Polish Humanitarian Action - Polska Akcja Humanitarna
jobs.body:
**Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH)** is looking for a **Head of Programmes** for its Country Office in **South Sudan.**

**About PAH:** Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) is an international non-governmental organization which since 1992 has been providing humanitarian and development help worldwide. So far, the interventions have been carried out in 52 different countries. By possessing long-standing expertise in the implementation of projects in Water, Sanitation and Hygiene, Food Security and Livelihoods, Shelter NFI, as well as Protection and Education, PAH concentrates its global activities on ensuring sustainable and stable development of regions suffering from the consequences of armed conflicts, natural disasters and other humanitarian crises.

**PAH in South Sudan:** Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, as one of the first NGOs established in Jonglei State. We are a small team of dedicated individuals committed to delivering tangible and sustainable change in the largest, most populous, and most conflict-affected state of South Sudan. Due to the expertise, we have accumulated over the years especially in WASH and S/NFI, PAH led the coordination of the Jonglei Sub-national WASH and S-NFI clusters from 2014 to 2021 and 2019 to date respectively coordinating WASH emergency responses with partners to ensure that all vulnerable communities are served during crises. Our priority is to ensure that people have access to clean water and safe hygienic conditions. PAH also provides assistance to internally displaced people and most vulnerable communities, working in the sectors of WASH, Shelter NFI, Food Security and Livelihood, Protection and Education.

For more information, please refer to [www.pah.org.pl/en](http://www.pah.org.pl/en)

**We strongly encourage qualified candidates to apply as soon as it is possible as the applications will be reviewed on rolling basis.**

**General information:**

**Job title:** Head of Programmes

**Duty station:** South Sudan, Juba Office

**Contract Type:** 6 months with possibility to extend

**Working hours:** Full Time

**Report to:** Country Director

**Estimated start date:** ASAP

**Job summary:**

The Head of Programs provides strategic and operational leadership for PAH’s Program portfolio in South Sudan. The position is responsible for ensuring that Programs are strategically relevant, technically sound, effectively implemented, adequately resourced, compliant with PAH and donor requirements, and accountable to affected populations and other stakeholders. Working closely with the Country Director, HQ Head of Programs, Grants, MEAL and support departments, the Head of Programs leads Program strategy and development, quality assurance, implementation oversight, business development, grants and partnerships, Program team management and external representation. The position contributes to the overall development and strategic positioning of PAH in South Sudan and is a key member of the Country Management/Senior Management Team.

## **Key Duties and Responsibilities:**

**Program Strategy, Quality and Implementation**

- Lead the development, implementation and review of PAH’s country Program strategy, ensuring alignment with humanitarian needs, PAH priorities, policies and relevant standards.
- Oversee the quality, effectiveness and timely implementation of the Program portfolio across WASH, Shelter/NFI, FSL and emergency response.
- Ensure coherence and synergies across sectors, projects and locations, while monitoring Program performance, budgets, risks and key deliverables, including proactive management of project timelines to minimise the need for No Cost Extensions.
- Work with MEAL and Program teams to strengthen accountability, learning, evidence-based decision-making and continuous improvement, including regular Lessons Learnt reviews (at least every 4 months) in cooperation with MEAL.
- Ensure Program data, documentation and reporting are accurately and consistently maintained in the Project Management Tool (PMT) and other PAH systems

**Business Development, Fundraising and Grants**

- Lead the Program and funding pipeline and identify opportunities aligned with PAH’s strategy, capacity and humanitarian priorities.
- Lead or contribute to assessments, concept notes, proposals, budgets and Program designs, and support strategic donor engagement.
- Oversee grant performance and work with Grants and Finance to ensure effective budget management, compliance and fulfilment of contractual commitments, including approval of internal Program-related costs in line with PAH procedures.
- Support Program growth, strategic partnerships and consortium opportunities.

**Partnerships and Program Team Leadership**

- Develop and maintain effective relationships with national and international partners and support appropriate partner selection, due diligence, capacity strengthening and performance management.
- Promote meaningful participation of local and national actors and contribute to PAH’s localisation objectives.
- Lead, manage and develop the Program team, including recruitment, performance management, coaching, mentoring and professional development.
- Oversee day-to-day team administration including leave, attendance, overtime approval and maintenance of the Program team organigram.
- Strengthen the capacity and leadership of national Program staff and promote a collaborative, accountable and learning-oriented culture.

**Representation, Coordination and Senior Management**

- Represent PAH in relevant clusters, working groups and coordination forums and maintain effective relationships with donors, government, UN agencies, NGOs and other stakeholders.
- Support the Country Director in strategic engagement, mission development and positioning of PAH.
- Participate in the Country Management/Senior Management Team and provide Program analysis and recommendations for strategic decision-making.
- Promote effective coordination and information sharing within the humanitarian and development community.

**Cross-Departmental Cooperation, Risk and Compliance**

- Work closely with Finance, HR, Logistics, Supply, Security, Grants, MEAL and other departments to ensure coordinated and feasible Program delivery, including oversight of Program-related procurement planning and cost efficiency.
- Ensure compliance with PAH policies, donor requirements, contractual obligations and relevant humanitarian standards.
- Identify and manage Program, operational and reputational risks and ensure appropriate corrective action and escalation.
- Promote safeguarding, PSEA, accountability to affected populations and responsible use of Program resources.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Perform other duties relevant to the position as assigned by the Country Director.
- Contribute to relevant organisational and HQ initiatives as required.

## **The successful candidate will be selected based on the qualification requirements described below:**

- Minimum 7 years of progressive humanitarian and/or development experience, with at least 5 years specifically in humanitarian programming in field-based positions, including a minimum of 3 years as a Project Coordinator/Programme Manager and at least 2 years in a Head of Programme or senior/emergency programme coordination role.Demonstrated experience managing multi-sectoral programs in complex or emergency contexts, preferably including WASH, Shelter/NFI and FSL
- Proven experience in fundraising, proposal development, institutional donor management, program budgeting and financial oversight
- Demonstrated experience with ECHO-funded programs (proposal writing, compliance and implementation)
- Strong experience in program quality, MEAL, accountability, team leadership and staff development.
- Proven ability to represent an organisation and build effective relationships with donors, government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs and other stakeholders
- Strong communication, leadership, organisational, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work under pressure and manage competing priorities
- University degree in International Development, Humanitarian Affairs, International Relations, Social Sciences, Public Health, Development Studies, Emergency Management or a related field
- Excellent written and spoken English (C1 or above) and good working knowledge of Microsoft Office

**Desirable**

- Previous experience in South Sudan or a comparable complex humanitarian context or experience working in East Africa
- Experience managing multi-location or multi-sectoral humanitarian portfolios
- Experience with consortiums and/or strategic Program partnerships
- Experience with localisation and capacity strengthening of national partners

## **What PAH offers:**

- work experience with professional and flexible international NGO, which is one of the largest NGOs in the Central-Eastern Europe
- work in a dynamic and motivated team
- possibility for professional development
- For expatriate Staff, PAH offers the following additional benefits:
- free accommodation
- flights home covered at the beginning and at the end of the deployment
- R&R benefit
- annual leave of 26 working days and 5 additional days of leave
- medical insurance (including Emergency Evacuation)
- psychological Support Package

jobs.title: Copy Editing and Graphic Designer Consultant
jobs.body:
**Background**  
The International Planned Parenthood Federation (IPPF) is a global healthcare provider and a leading advocate of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for all. IPPF Humanitarian is committed to providing lifesaving SRHR and Ssexual and Gender Based-Violence (SGBV) services in crisis-affected areas. IPPF requires the services of a consultant/firm to finalize its Clinical Management of Rape, Intimate Partner Violence (CMR/IPV) toolkit resources designed to support frontline humanitarian responders to deliver human rights-based, survivor centred, trauma-informed and inclusive CMR/IPV services in humanitarian responses.

The CMR/IPV toolkit comprises two documents as follows:  
1\. a CMR/IPV protocol- 40 pages  
2\. a CMR/IPV pocket guide- 16 pages

This Terms of Reference (TOR) therefore, outlines the requirements for professional copy editing, proofreading, design and production of the CMR/IPV toolkit.

**Role Objectives**  
The overall objective of the consultancy is to produce a high quality, professionally edited and visually appealing publication of the CMR/IPV toolkit.  
*Specific objectives include;*  
• Proofreading, edit and format the final version of the reviewed and validated tools (2)  
• Design and produce the publication in digital formats.  
• Ensure the final documents adhere to professional publication standards and are ready for dissemination to relevant stakeholders.

**Duties and Responsibilities**  
The consultant(s) will work under the supervision of the senior SRH advisor to deliver the following services:

*A: Copy Editing and Proofreading*  
• Review the language, tone, and structure for accuracy, coherence and readability  
• Verify consistency of spelling, abbreviations, tables, figures, numbering and references  
• Ensure compliance with British English standards using Concise Oxford Dictionary (12th edition)  
• Apply all edits using track changes function in Microsoft Word  
• Prepare both tracked and clean copy versions of the edited documents.

*B: Design, Layout and Production*  
• Format and design the final layout of the documents, ensuring professional and visually appealing documents  
• Incorporate relevant graphics, tables ad photos ensuring clarity and visual balance and using the IPPF colour palette.  
• Apply the agreed final MS Word and PDF templates for the final output.  
• Prepare the publication for printing and digital dissemination to the following specifications;  
o CMR/IPV protocol (40 pages): Book size A4 , double-sided printing including front cover and back cover  
o CMR/IPV pocket guide (16 pages): Size A5, double-sided printing including front cover and back cover

**Key Deliverables**  
The work will commence immediately following agreement signing upon which the consultant(s) will share a detailed workplan of incorporating key tasks and periodic content reviews. The consultant(s) will work closely with the senior SRH advisor for technical guidance, content review and approval of deliverables.  
o ***Copy-Edited versions of the CMR/IPV Toolkit: Day 7***  
o ***Final Print-Ready Files***: High-resolution PDFs with bleed/crop marks for professional printing. (Day 24)  
o ***Digital/Web-Optimized Files***: Lightweight PDFs with interactive navigation (internal links and bookmarks). (Day 24)  
o ***Source Files & Asset Pack***: All original editable files (e.g., Adobe InDesign, Illustrator) and a folder containing all custom icons/illustrations created. (Day 24)

**Qualifications**  
***Essential:***  
• Proven experience in professional copy editing, proof reading, and publication design.  
• Evidence of at least two (2) similar assignments completed.  
• Proficiency in MS Word, Adobe InDesign or equivalent design software.  
• Strong attention to detail and ability to meet deadlines

**Competencies, Skills and Experience**  
***Core Competencies:***  
• Expert proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop).  
• Proven track record in taking heavy text and creating charts, infographics, and layouts that improve readability.  
• Experience working with an INGO or NGO is highly desirable.  
• Excellent command of the English language and ability to consistently apply editorial standards

jobs.title: Expression of Interest: Board Member(s) for RET Americas
jobs.body:
**Location:** Worldwide, with preference for US-based candidates

**Term:** 3 years, renewable by mutual agreement – Unpaid (reasonable travel expenses can be claimed)

**Closing date:** Friday, October 16

**About RET Americas**

RET Americas is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization headquartered in Washington, D.C. We are part of the RET Alliance, a global network dedicated to alleviating suffering and catalyzing sustainable development in crises, conflicts, and fragile contexts.

Founded in 2000 by Sadako Ogata, the trailblazing former UN High Commissioner for Refugees, RET has implemented more than 460 projects across 35 countries and provided critical programming to over 2.5 million program participants. Today, our mission is more urgent than ever.

The world is facing intersecting crises: Displacement, conflict, unpredictable weather and increasingly devastating disasters. These fall disproportionately on the populations RET Americas serves: Youth, women, and girls in Latin America, the Caribbean, Africa, the Middle East and beyond. We are at a pivotal moment, actively growing our board, deepening our resource base, and expanding our impact.

We are looking for board members who bring strategic thinking, professional networks, and a genuine commitment to humanitarian values. This is an opportunity not just to govern but to shape the future of a high-impact organization at a critical moment.

If you believe in the power of education, protection, and community resilience to transform lives, we would love to hear from you.

**Purpose of the Board**

The RET Americas Board of Directors is the governing body of the organization. It is responsible for the strategic direction of RET Americas, ensuring fiscal integrity, and overseeing the CEO and senior management. The Board meets quarterly with the Executive Leadership Team to review progress, ensure organizational health, and guide long-term strategy.

As an independent 501(c)(3), RET Americas Board members carry full legal fiduciary responsibility under U.S. nonprofit law and are expected to act in the best interests of the organization and the communities it serves.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Fulfill the statutory duties of a nonprofit board director under U.S. law and IRS requirements.
- Approve and monitor organizational strategy, annual plans, and major policies.
- Appoint, support, and evaluate the CEO, and ensure appropriate succession planning.
- Attend and actively contribute to quarterly board meetings and relevant committee sessions.
- Fulfill the annual Give/Get obligation and serve as an ambassador for RET Americas.
- Review financial statements, the annual audit, and key compliance documents.
- Serve on or contribute to a relevant task force or working group based on professional expertise.
- Maintain confidentiality and adhere to the organization’s Conflict of Interest Policy.
- Advocate for RET Americas’ mission within your professional and personal networks.

**Priority Expertise Areas**

We are currently recruiting for board members with experience in one or more of the following sectors:

- Legal – Particularly international law, nonprofit governance, compliance, or human rights law
- Communications and media – Public relations, graphics, marketing, or social media
- Finance & Accounting – Financial oversight, audit, investment, or endowment management
- Corporate – Technology, media, finance, business development, extractive industries, agricultural or pharmaceutical sectors
- Government & Diplomacy – Including bilateral relations, international development policy, US Department of State networks
- Philanthropy & Fundraising – Major donor cultivation, foundation relations, or corporate social responsibility

**Skills & Abilities**

We are seeking board members who possess one or more of the following talents:

- Strategic thinker with the ability to contribute to long-term organizational planning and evaluate competing priorities.
- Inspirational communicator who can serve as a credible ambassador for RET Americas in professional and public settings.
- Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
- Financially literate with the ability to review budgets, audited financials, and organizational performance data.
- Curious and willing to probe, challenge constructively, and inquire deeply on behalf of the organization.
- Committed to good governance, including legal and fiduciary obligations of a nonprofit director.

**Personal Style & Attributes**

- Alignment with RET Americas' values: Accountability, transparency, and humanitarian commitment.
- Demonstrated engagement in the humanitarian, development, or social impact sector, whether through prior board service, philanthropy, or advocacy.
- Ability to fulfill the Give/Get commitment (details provided during initial vetting and meeting) and bring a meaningful network to the organization's resource development.
- Available to prioritize RET Americas board duties, including quarterly meetings and task force engagement.
- Self-aware, principled, and consistent; someone who models the right behaviors and treats all colleagues with respect.
- Meetings & Attendance
- Board meetings are held four times per year (quarterly), conducted virtually and/or in person.
- Board members are expected to review all pre-meeting materials at least 48 hours before each meeting.
- Ad hoc working sessions or committee calls may be convened between quarterly meetings.

**Term & Renewal**

- Initial board terms are three years, renewable by mutual agreement with the Board Chair.
- Renewals are subject to a brief annual review of Give/Get fulfillment and overall engagement.
- Board members wishing to step down should provide a minimum of 60 days' written notice.

jobs.title: Labour Mobility Communications and Creative Content Specialist (Consultant A)
jobs.body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23923**  
Position Title: **Labour Mobility Communications and Creative Content Specialist (Consultant A)**  
Duty Station City: **Honiara**  
Duty Station Country: **Solomon Islands**  
Contract Type: **Consultant A**  
*Recruiting Type:* **Consultancy**  
*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**  
Initial duration: **9 months**  
Closing date: **22 October 2026**

**Nature of the consultancy:**

Technical Assistance on Communications and Creative Content to the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) of the Government of Solomon Islands (Category A Consultancy).

**Context:**

Labour mobility has become a key income and skills pathway for Solomon Islanders, with over 9,000 nationals participating in the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) and New Zealand Recognized Seasonal Employer (RSE) schemes in 2025 alone. As participation grows, so does the need for stronger, more structured reintegration support. A 2023–2024 survey of 500 returned migrants found that returned migrant workers frequently faced limited access to employment, skills utilization, business support and financial services — highlighting the need for structured programmes that translate overseas experience and savings into sustainable livelihoods.

The proposed 12-month pilot project will contribute to improving sustainable economic reintegration outcomes for returned migrant workers in Solomon Islands (objective). The intervention has one outcome: The Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) provides enhanced, gender-sensitive economic reintegration support services to returned migrant workers, to facilitate their sustainable return and reintegration into their communities. This will be achieved through two complementary outputs: A comprehensive findings report on the sustainable reintegration of returned migrant workers, in support of implementing the Labour Mobility Policy and Action Plan 2024-2028, is available to the LMU (Output 1.1); and the LMU has enhanced capacity to deliver gender-sensitive economic reintegration support, particularly skills-building, networking and career opportunities for returned migrant workers (Output 1.2).

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:**

From Return to Resilience: Strengthening Economic Reintegration of Returned Migrant Workers in Solomon Islands (RR0593); Labour Mobility Unit (LMU), Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade (MFAET) with the Government of Solomon Islands.

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

The locally recruited Consultant will lead the implementation of Activity 1.2.3 and undertake other related tasks as requested by the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU). The Consultant will support the full process of developing and delivering gender-sensitive information, education and communication (IEC) materials for returning migrant workers, from information gathering and stakeholder consultation through to content development, production, dissemination, monitoring and adaptation.

The Consultant will undertake the following tasks:

1\. Gather information and undertake research

Conduct research to identify relevant information, resources, opportunities and good practices that can inform IEC materials for returning migrant workers in Solomon Islands. The IEC materials will primarily focus on economic reintegration, including information that supports returning migrant workers to access employment, develop livelihoods, pursue investment or entrepreneurship opportunities, and strengthen their financial resilience. Where relevant to sustainable reintegration, the materials may also incorporate information on social, psychosocial and other aspects of reintegration, including linkages to relevant services, resources and support available to returning migrant workers.

Information covered by the IEC materials may include, but is not limited to:

- Local employment and potential investment opportunities;
- Skills development, training and other education opportunities;
- CV and cover letter preparation, job search and interview preparation;
- Entrepreneurship, business development and financial literacy;
- Upcoming events and opportunities for returning migrant workers, including activities supported under the project;
- Pre-return counselling and other relevant information; and
- Relevant social, psychosocial and other support services or resources that may contribute to sustainable reintegration.

The Consultant will also research relevant good practices and examples from the Pacific region on engaging returning migrant workers and strengthening economic reintegration outcomes through awareness-raising and information interventions.

2\. Consult with stakeholders and target audiences

Consult with relevant stakeholders, LMU and target audiences, as appropriate, to validate information needs, identify key messages and ensure that the proposed IEC materials are relevant, accessible and responsive to the needs of returning migrant workers. The Consultant will communicate relevant findings and recommendations to LMU and incorporate feedback into the development of the materials.

3\. Advise on content and communication approaches

Provide technical and expert advice to LMU on the content, format, design, accessibility and communication approach for the IEC materials, including recommendations on appropriate channels and methods for effectively reaching returning migrant workers.

4\. Develop and produce IEC materials

Based on the information gathered, research undertaken, stakeholder consultations and agreed communication approach, support LMU in the development and production of high-quality IEC materials. Materials may include printed, digital, audio-visual and other creative communication resources, as appropriate to the target audience and intended purpose.

5\. Support dissemination of IEC materials

Support LMU, as required, in the dissemination of completed IEC materials through appropriate channels. These may include printed materials and direct sharing through in-person engagement and email; online platforms, including the [Labour Mobility Unit Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/people/Labour-Mobility-Unit-Solomon-Islands/61566025701376/) and official website channels; radio; and other appropriate and creative communication mediums.

6\. Monitor engagement and gather feedback

Track engagement with the IEC materials and gather feedback from target audiences and relevant stakeholders to assess the relevance, accessibility and effectiveness of the materials and dissemination approaches.

7\. Recommend adaptations and improvements

Based on monitoring, feedback and lessons learned, provide timely recommendations to LMU on adaptations or adjustments to the IEC materials, content or dissemination approaches. Findings and feedback will be used to inform subsequent material development, production and dissemination.

8\. Handover and knowledge sharing

Ensure that all materials, content, templates and relevant resources developed under the assignment are provided to LMU for ongoing use, adaptation and dissemination. The Consultant will also share relevant knowledge, findings and lessons learned with LMU to support continued development and dissemination of reintegration information beyond the assignment.

9\. Other related support

Provide other related technical assistance and support as reasonably required by the LMU and IOM Project Manager, within the scope of the assignment.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Complete all activities by no later than 31 July 2027
- Document and share with LMU and IOM relevant best practices and lessons learned on engaging returning migrant workers through gender-sensitive and inclusive IEC materials.
- Consult relevant stakeholders and target audiences and provide technical support to LMU in the development and production of at least 10 IEC materials, primarily focused on improving economic reintegration outcomes for return migrant workers
- Disseminate IEC materials through appropriate channels and engage at least 100 returning migrant workers
