**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Middle School Alliance Site Coordinator
jobs.body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:**

The Middle School Alliance (MSA) Site Coordinator provides day-to-day operational and administrative coordination for Out-of-School Time (OST) programming at assigned middle school sites, working within clearly defined procedures and under the general direction of MSA leadership. The coordinator carries out established site operations, logistics coordination, family engagement, and data-accountability tasks -- coordinating schedules and communication with program providers, volunteers, and site-based staff on clearly defined tasks, without formal responsibility for supervising their work -- and escalates unusual or non-routine issues to MSA leadership for resolution.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

***Site Operations & Program Coordination***

- Serve as the primary on-site coordinator responsible for overseeing daily MSA operations and implementation, including coordination of related logistics, schedules, and communication with program providers and site-based staff on clearly defined tasks.
- Coordinate daily program logistics including scheduling, room allocation, meal distribution, transportation coordination, dismissal procedures, and site transitions.
- Support scheduling and coordination of program providers to ensure alignment with site needs, school schedules, and MSA priorities.
- Monitor daily site operations to ensure programming is implemented with consistency, efficiency, and fidelity.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for site-based operational communication between school staff, providers, transportation, security, and MSA leadership.
- Troubleshoot routine operational challenges within established procedures and proactively communicate concerns and solutions, escalating unusual or non-routine issues to MSA leadership.
- Assist with coordination of site calendars, events, special activities, and school-based initiatives.
- Ensure site implementation aligns with MSA operational expectations, procedures, and standards.

***Student Recruitment & Family Engagement***

- Collaborate with the Manager of Partnerships & Community Engagement to support student recruitment and enrollment efforts.
- Support outreach and engagement efforts for students, families, teachers, and school personnel.
- Assist with family communication regarding programming schedules, attendance expectations, transportation updates, and special events.
- Promote inclusive access to OST opportunities and support student participation across diverse student populations.
- Build and maintain positive relationships with youth and families to encourage consistent engagement and participation.
- Support implementation of student and family engagement activities throughout the school year.

***Data Management & Reporting***

- Work closely with the Data & Evaluation Manager to support accurate and timely attendance tracking, data collection, and reporting.
- Monitor registration, attendance, participation trends, and Average Daily Attendance (ADA) data.
- Support implementation of evaluation tools, surveys, assessments, and data collection processes, including SAYO-Y and other program quality measures.
- Ensure site-based data systems and reporting procedures are completed accurately and consistently, following established formats and deadlines.
- Use data insights to identify operational challenges and support continuous improvement, in consultation with the Data & Evaluation Manager.
- Maintain organized and accurate records related to attendance, participation, case management, schedules, and operational documentation.

***Program Quality & Continuous Improvement***

- Collaborate with the Network Quality Manager to support implementation of NextUp quality standards and Youth Program Quality Initiative (YPQI) practices.
- Participate in professional development, coaching, training, and quality improvement activities.
- Support program providers in creating safe, engaging, and youth-centered learning environments.
- Monitor program implementation and communicate concerns related to quality, consistency, youth engagement, or operational effectiveness to MSA leadership.
- Gather and communicate feedback from youth, families, providers, and school staff to support continuous improvement.

***Relationship Management & Communication***

- Build and maintain collaborative relationships with school administrators, teachers, providers, families, community partners, and youth.
- Facilitate clear, timely, and professional communication between all stakeholders.
- Attend and support school-based meetings, provider meetings, site leadership meetings, trainings, and MSA planning meetings.
- Represent NextUp and the MSA professionally within school communities and partner spaces.

***Safety, Supervision & Risk Management***

- Support implementation and monitoring of established safety and supervision procedures during OST programming.
- Ensure students are properly supervised during transitions, programming, transportation, and dismissal.
- Maintain awareness of site safety concerns and communicate incidents promptly to MSA leadership.
- Assist with incident reporting, documentation, and follow-up procedures, per established protocols.
- Assist with emergency response coordination and communication when necessary, following established emergency procedures.

***Administrative & Organizational Support***

- Maintain organized operational records and documentation.
- Assist with inventory management, supply coordination, and site preparation.
- Support preparation of operational updates, reports, and presentations.
- Monitor implementation timelines, deadlines, and deliverables related to site operations.
- Follow site-based operational procedures and systems established by MSA leadership.

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree is preferred in education, youth development, nonprofit management, public administration, social work, or a related field.
- Minimum of 2–3 years of related experience in youth development, education, afterschool programming, or community-based programming.
- Proficient in English and Spanish, both spoken and written.
- Experience working with middle school youth, school communities, or after-school programming strongly preferred.
- Experience with attendance tracking, data systems, and reporting processes preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong organizational, time management, and project coordination skills.
- Ability to manage day-to-day operational responsibilities and site-based priorities within clearly defined procedures, escalating exceptions to MSA leadership.
- Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships and function effectively within a team environment.
- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal in Spanish and English.
- Ability to solve problems, adapt, and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Knowledge of positive youth development and youth engagement practices preferred.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality implementation.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and database/data management systems preferred.
- Ability to exercise sound judgment and maintain professionalism in school and community settings.

**Working Environment:**

- Primarily an in-person, school-based environment across assigned middle school sites, with standard office/administrative time for planning and reporting.
- Hours during programming are 11am-7pm. Biweekly staff meetings are held at IRC office.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $28.94-$29.90/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

jobs.title: Ebola Response Director
jobs.body:
*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and the vacancy may close before the advertised deadline if the position is filled.*

**Background:**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we would like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home. The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, ask ‘Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

**Context:**

The Ministry of Public Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared the country's 17th Ebola outbreak on May 15, 2026, following laboratory confirmation of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Ituri Province. On May 17, 2026, WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), and it has since become the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in DRC and the fastest-expanding on record. The outbreak is unfolding in a highly complex humanitarian and security context marked by chronic insecurity, armed group activity, repeated population displacement, and high levels of cross-border movement, particularly with Uganda and South Sudan.

The IRC is supporting containment of the outbreak in Ituri and North Kivu. IRC's primary focus is to support existing primary health care (PHC) facilities to ensure safe continuity of services, strengthen infection prevention and control (IPC) practices and infrastructure, raise community awareness of behaviors that limit further spread, and reinforce the protective environment, including through MHPSS support.

**Scope of Work:**

The Ebola Response Director (ERD) will lead IRC's emergency response to the Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in DRC, based in Bunia, driving a fast, high-quality, accountable operation that ensures continuity of primary health care, strengthens infection prevention and control, and reinforces community protection in line with IRC's strategic priorities.

The ERD will oversee all operational, financial, and programmatic aspects of the response, including supply chain, safety and security, finance, people and culture, partnerships, and program delivery. S/he will report to the Emergency Unit's ERMT Lead (Emergency Response Management Team), with a dotted line to the DRC Country Director (CD) for coordination on critical incidents, security, legal, donor, and media matters — shifting to a full reporting line into the CD once handover to the DRC Country Program is complete. As IRC's external face on the response, the ERD will be a compelling communicator with government officials, donors, UN agencies, and coordination bodies, driving visibility and funding for the response. S/he will also ensure the programmatic strategy is clear and effectively implemented, and participate in the DRC Country Program SMT to keep the response aligned with, and eventually integrated into, the broader country program.

Success in this role demands a strong, resilient leader who can motivate and steady teams operating in a highly insecure, high-pressure environment, paired with excellent communication and program implementation skills. The ERD is directly responsible for the response's overall coordination and strategic direction, oversight and coaching of the Ebola Response department leads, effective management of emergency funding, and timely reporting to donors, the CD, and the ERMT.

**Main Responsibilities:**

***Leadership and Representation***

- Serve as IRC's key representative for the Ebola response, coordinating with the DRC CD and wider country program as needed, and co-lead all donor and media engagement related to the response with the CD.
- Develop and maintain relationships with donors, UN agencies, INGOs, MOH, and local partners to promote effective collaboration and raise the visibility of IRC's response.
- Participate in DRC Country Program SMT meetings and maintain regular coordination check-ins with the CD to ensure alignment with the broader country program.
- Oversee safety and security aspects of the Ebola response, immediately reporting risks, incidents, or concerns to the CD and the ERMT.
- Join the Emergency Unit's weekly ERMT meetings and ad hoc Crisis Calls, ensuring production of a weekly Emergency Situation Report.
- Champion a culture of effective, respectful partnerships, promoting partner-led programming in line with IRC's "why not partner?" and "partner as equals" approach.

***Strategic Direction and Program Oversight***

- Lead and contribute to the execution of IRC's strategic response plan for Ebola, ensuring it reflects partnership considerations and active engagement of local partners in design and delivery.
- Oversee emergency program implementation across the Ebola response.
- Directly supervise the Ebola Response department Leads (Program Lead, Supply Chain, Finance, People and Culture, and Security) with the Program Lead further overseeing technical program coordinators, grants, and partnerships.
- Support strategic decision-making on program design, proposals, and budget development for new Ebola response funding, including appropriate budget allocation to support partners.
- Ensure staffing structures and partnership risk management are sized and aligned to the emergency context.
- Work closely with the DRC Country Program to ensure a smooth handover and integration of the response into the broader CP portfolio at time of transition.

***Stewardship and Operational Leadership***

- Drive operational excellence, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness across all Ebola Response functions, proactively identifying and eliminating redundant processes.
- Oversee the development, deployment, and utilization of financial and operational policies, procedures, and systems to ensure compliance with IRC and donor requirements.
- Ensure responsiveness and appropriate levels of in-person and remote support to all offices, particularly in the areas of people and culture, finance, and supply chain.
- Provide timely and effective oversight of the country program's financial position.
- Maintain effective and coordinated budget monitoring processes for both grant funds and discretionary funds.

***Organizational Culture and Communication***

- Role model IRC's Core Values, the "IRC Way - Global Standards for Professional Conduct," and Inclusion Principles through personal commitment and accountability.
- Foster an open, inclusive, and respectful team environment where staff feel valued and communication is honest and productive.
- Model accountability and commitment to safeguarding, including PSEAH, of all staff, partners, clients and others with whom we work; build a culture of safeguarding, where our clients and staff trust IRC and feel safe raising concerns.
- Hold all leaders accountable to their roles and areas of responsibilities for delivery in the Safeguarding Minimum Standards; dedicate and facilitate regular reviews of Safeguarding Minimum Standards progress, barriers, enablers and culture within the response to plan for action and investment needed.
- Maintain open and regular communication with DRC leadership, regional management staff, regional technical advisors, and HQ departmental staff to ensure alignment, support, and collaboration.

***People Leadership***

- Oversee the management, coaching, and development of national and international staff working in the Ebola Response to build a team of skilled, committed, engaged, and motivated staff.
- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives, providing regular and timely feedback, and leading performance reviews.
- Hold high-quality 1:1 meetings with each direct report on a regular and predictable basis, at least bi-weekly, focusing equally on interpersonal exchange and work priorities.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being, ensuring systems and practices where work supports life and modelling healthy work-life balance practices.
- Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs.
- Offer leadership support for successful adherence by all staff to IRC's country, regional, and global policies and procedures.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Position Reports to: Emergency Unit Emergency Response Management Team (ERMT) Lead, with a dotted line to the Country Director, DRC, for coordination and information-sharing on critical incidents, security, legal, donor, and media matters. Reporting will shift to Country Director when the response management handover is completed.
- Position Directly Supervises: Ebola Response Program Lead, Ebola Supply Chain Coordinator(s), Ebola Response Deputy Director Finance, Ebola People & Culture Lead and Ebola Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Lead
- Works Closely with: IRC DRC Country Program Senior Management Team (CD, DDP, and DDO)

**Job Requirements:**

- University degree in related field or equivalent experience preferred.
- 8 years’ experience leading complex on site emergency health response projects and/or programs requiring extensive judgment and interpretation. Diverse geographical professional experience preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to influence peer agencies, local government and community leaders to work effectively towards a common and agreed upon result.
- Demonstrated ability to evaluate and implement best practices and processes affecting multiple technical specialties to achieve rapid, consistent and high-quality outcomes.
- Experience developing, resourcing and leading large budget, complex projects spanning multiple technical specialties.
- Proven track-record of excellent management and leadership skills. Ability to set an example of leadership for staff in adherence to IRC management policies.
- High degree of comfort and successful track record in supervising in matrixed environments.
- Demonstrated commitment to inclusion and fair treatment of staff, and ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized groups in emergency response.
- Experience working with diverse teams and communities, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other groups at risk of exclusion.
- Excellent verbal and written skills in English and French required.

*Les candidatures seront examinées au fur et à mesure de leur réception, et l’offre pourra être clôturée avant la date limite annoncée si le poste est pourvu.*

**Présentation :**

Répondant aux pires crises humanitaires du monde dans une grande variété de fonctions, le personnel du Comité international de secours (IRC) est une force au service de l'humanité et de l'espoir. Si vous êtes compétent(e) et passionné(e), nous serions heureux d'ajouter votre énergie à la nôtre.

Par le biais de son unité des urgences (EmU), l'IRC est l'une des plus grandes agences humanitaires au monde, menant des interventions d'urgence rapides qui apportent une aide vitale, un redressement précoce et un soutien à la stabilisation aux personnes touchées par les conflits, les déplacements, les catastrophes naturelles et les urgences complexes dans de multiples contextes à travers le monde. Nous nous engageons à innover, à agir avec agilité et à établir des partenariats solides afin de fournir une action humanitaire rapide et efficace.

Actif dans les domaines de la santé publique, de l'éducation en situation d'urgence, des moyens de subsistance, de l'autonomisation des femmes, du développement des jeunes et de la protection et de la promotion des droits, nous accompagnons les personnes du danger vers un foyer. L'IRC reconnaît que les personnes touchées par une crise et les acteurs les plus proches d'elles sont les mieux placés, ont le droit et doivent avoir le pouvoir et les ressources nécessaires pour répondre à la crise et impulser un changement durable. Nous nous engageons à accroître la part du financement destiné aux acteurs locaux dans les situations d'urgence, à nous demander « Pourquoi ne pas nouer un partenariat ? » chaque fois que nous planifions un programme, et à établir des partenariats d'égal à égal.

**Contexte:**

Le ministère de la Santé publique de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a déclaré la 17e épidémie d'Ebola du pays le 15 mai 2026, après la confirmation en laboratoire de la maladie à virus Bundibugyo (MVB) dans la province de l'Ituri. Le 17 mai 2026, l'OMS a déclaré l'épidémie urgence de santé publique de portée internationale (USPPI), et elle est depuis devenue la plus grande épidémie d'Ebola jamais signalée en RDC et celle qui progresse le plus rapidement jamais enregistrée. L'épidémie se déroule dans un contexte humanitaire et sécuritaire hautement complexe, marqué par une insécurité chronique, l'activité de groupes armés, des déplacements de population répétés et des mouvements transfrontaliers importants, notamment avec l'Ouganda et le Soudan du Sud.

L'IRC appuie l'endiguement de l'épidémie dans l'Ituri et le Nord-Kivu. L'action prioritaire de l'IRC consiste à soutenir les structures de soins de santé primaires (SSP) existantes afin d'assurer la continuité des services en toute sécurité, à renforcer les pratiques et les infrastructures de prévention et de contrôle des infections (PCI), à sensibiliser les communautés aux comportements qui limitent la propagation, et à renforcer l'environnement protecteur, notamment par un soutien en santé mentale et psychosociale (SMSPS).

**Portée du poste :**

Le/la Directeur/Directrice de la riposte Ebola (DRE) dirigera la riposte d'urgence de l'IRC à l'épidémie de maladie à virus Bundibugyo (MVB) en RDC, basé(e) à Bunia, en pilotant une opération rapide, de haute qualité et responsable qui assure la continuité des soins de santé primaires, renforce la prévention et le contrôle des infections, et consolide la protection communautaire, conformément aux priorités stratégiques de l'IRC.

Le/la DRE supervisera l'ensemble des aspects opérationnels, financiers et programmatiques de la riposte, notamment la chaîne d'approvisionnement, la sûreté et la sécurité, les finances, les ressources humaines et la culture, les partenariats et la mise en œuvre des programmes. Il/elle rendra compte au/à la Responsable de l'ERMT de l'unité des urgences (Équipe de gestion de la riposte d'urgence), avec un lien fonctionnel avec le/la Directeur/Directrice pays (DP) de la RDC pour la coordination sur les incidents critiques, la sécurité, les questions juridiques, les donateurs et les médias — ce lien évoluant vers une ligne hiérarchique pleine et entière vers le DP une fois la transition vers le programme pays de la RDC achevée. En tant que visage extérieur de l'IRC pour la riposte, le/la DRE sera un(e) communicateur/communicatrice convaincant(e) auprès des responsables gouvernementaux, des donateurs, des agences des Nations Unies et des instances de coordination, afin d'accroître la visibilité et le financement de la riposte. Il/elle veillera également à ce que la stratégie programmatique soit claire et efficacement mise en œuvre, et participera à l'équipe de direction (SMT) du programme pays de la RDC afin de maintenir la riposte alignée avec, puis à terme intégrée dans, le programme pays plus large.

Réussir dans ce poste exige un(e) leader solide et résilient(e), capable de motiver et de stabiliser des équipes évoluant dans un environnement hautement instable et sous forte pression, doté(e) d'excellentes compétences en communication et en mise en œuvre de programmes. Le/la DRE est directement responsable de la coordination générale et de l'orientation stratégique de la riposte, de la supervision et de l'accompagnement des responsables de département de la riposte Ebola, de la gestion efficace du financement d'urgence, ainsi que de la production de rapports en temps voulu aux donateurs, au DP et à l'ERMT.

**Principales responsabilités:**

***Direction et représentation***

- Assurer la représentation clé de l'IRC pour la riposte Ebola, en coordination avec le DP de la RDC et le programme pays au sens large selon les besoins, et co-diriger avec le DP l'ensemble des relations avec les donateurs et les médias liées à la riposte.
- Développer et entretenir des relations avec les donateurs, les agences des Nations Unies, les ONG internationales, le ministère de la Santé et les partenaires locaux afin de promouvoir une collaboration efficace et d'accroître la visibilité de la riposte de l'IRC.
- Participer aux réunions de l'équipe de direction (SMT) du programme pays de la RDC et maintenir des points de coordination réguliers avec le DP afin d'assurer l'alignement avec le programme pays au sens large.
- Superviser les aspects de sûreté et de sécurité de la riposte Ebola, en signalant immédiatement tout risque, incident ou préoccupation au DP et à l'ERMT.
- Participer aux réunions hebdomadaires de l'ERMT de l'unité des urgences et aux appels de crise ad hoc, en veillant à la production d'un rapport de situation d'urgence hebdomadaire.
- Promouvoir une culture de partenariats efficaces et respectueux, en encourageant les programmes pilotés par les partenaires conformément à l'approche « Pourquoi ne pas nouer un partenariat ? » et « partenaires d'égal à égal » de l'IRC.

***Orientation stratégique et supervision des programmes***

- Diriger et contribuer à la mise en œuvre du plan de riposte stratégique de l'IRC pour Ebola, en veillant à ce qu'il reflète les considérations de partenariat et l'engagement actif des partenaires locaux dans la conception et la mise en œuvre.
- Superviser la mise en œuvre du programme d'urgence dans l'ensemble de la riposte Ebola.
- Superviser directement les responsables de département de la riposte Ebola (Responsable du programme, Chaîne d'approvisionnement, Finances, Ressources humaines et Culture, et Sécurité), le Responsable du programme supervisant en outre les coordinateurs techniques de programme, les subventions et les partenariats.
- Appuyer la prise de décisions stratégiques sur la conception des programmes, les propositions et l'élaboration des budgets pour les nouveaux financements de la riposte Ebola, y compris l'allocation budgétaire appropriée en soutien aux partenaires.
- Veiller à ce que les structures de personnel et la gestion des risques liés aux partenariats soient dimensionnées et adaptées au contexte d'urgence.
- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le programme pays de la RDC afin d'assurer une transition et une intégration harmonieuses de la riposte dans le portefeuille plus large du programme pays au moment de la transition.

***Gestion responsable et direction opérationnelle***

- Favoriser l'excellence opérationnelle, l'efficience et la rentabilité dans l'ensemble des fonctions de la riposte Ebola, en identifiant et en éliminant de manière proactive les processus redondants.
- Superviser l'élaboration, le déploiement et l'utilisation des politiques, procédures et systèmes financiers et opérationnels afin de garantir la conformité avec les exigences de l'IRC et des donateurs.
- Veiller à la réactivité et à un niveau approprié de soutien en présentiel et à distance à l'ensemble des bureaux, en particulier dans les domaines des ressources humaines et de la culture, des finances et de la chaîne d'approvisionnement.
- Assurer une supervision rapide et efficace de la situation financière du programme pays.
- Maintenir des processus de suivi budgétaire efficaces et coordonnés, tant pour les fonds de subvention que pour les fonds discrétionnaires.

***Culture organisationnelle et communication***

- Incarner les valeurs fondamentales de l'IRC, le « IRC Way - Normes mondiales de conduite professionnelle » et les principes d'inclusion, par un engagement personnel et une responsabilisation.
- Favoriser un environnement d'équipe ouvert, inclusif et respectueux, où le personnel se sent valorisé et où la communication est honnête et productive.
- Incarner la responsabilisation et l'engagement envers la protection, y compris la PSEAH (prévention de l'exploitation et des abus sexuels et du harcèlement), de l'ensemble du personnel, des partenaires, des clients et de toute autre personne avec qui nous travaillons ; bâtir une culture de protection où nos clients et notre personnel font confiance à l'IRC et se sentent en sécurité pour signaler leurs préoccupations.
- Tenir l'ensemble des responsables pour comptables de leurs rôles et domaines de responsabilité dans la mise en œuvre des normes minimales de protection ; consacrer du temps et faciliter des revues régulières des progrès, des obstacles, des facteurs favorables et de la culture en matière de normes minimales de protection au sein de la riposte, afin de planifier les actions et les investissements nécessaires.
- Maintenir une communication ouverte et régulière avec la direction de la RDC, le personnel de gestion régional, les conseillers techniques régionaux et le personnel des départements du siège, afin de garantir l'alignement, le soutien et la collaboration.

***Direction des ressources humaines***

- Superviser la gestion, l'accompagnement et le développement du personnel national et international travaillant au sein de la riposte Ebola, afin de constituer une équipe compétente, engagée, impliquée et motivée.
- Superviser et accompagner le personnel relevant directement de sa responsabilité, notamment en communiquant des attentes claires, en fixant des objectifs de performance, en fournissant des retours réguliers et rapides, et en menant les évaluations de performance.
- Tenir des entretiens individuels de qualité avec chaque collaborateur/collaboratrice direct(e) sur une base régulière et prévisible, au moins toutes les deux semaines, en accordant une attention égale aux échanges interpersonnels et aux priorités de travail.
- Promouvoir et suivre le bien-être et l'attention portée au personnel, en veillant à la mise en place de systèmes et de pratiques où le travail soutient la vie, et en modélisant de saines pratiques d'équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie privée.
- Soutenir les interventions appropriées en réponse aux besoins identifiés en matière d'attention portée au personnel.
- Offrir un appui de direction pour permettre à l'ensemble du personnel de respecter avec succès les politiques et procédures pays, régionales et mondiales de l'IRC.

**Principales relations de travail:**

- **Relève de:** Le/la Responsable de l'ERMT (Équipe de gestion de la riposte d'urgence) de l'unité des urgences, avec un lien fonctionnel avec le/la Directeur/Directrice pays de la RDC pour la coordination et le partage d'informations sur les incidents critiques, la sécurité, les questions juridiques, les donateurs et les médias. La ligne hiérarchique évoluera vers le/la Directeur/Directrice pays une fois la transition de gestion de la riposte achevée.
- **Supervise directement:** le/la Responsable du programme de riposte Ebola, le/les Coordinateur(s)/Coordinatrice(s) de la chaîne d'approvisionnement Ebola, le/la Directeur/Directrice adjoint(e) Finances de la riposte Ebola, le/la Responsable Ressources humaines et Culture Ebola, et le/la Responsable Accès humanitaire, Sûreté et Sécurité Ebola
- **Travaille en étroite collaboration avec:** l'équipe de direction du programme pays de l'IRC en RDC (DP, DDP et DDO).

**Exigences du poste:**

- Diplôme universitaire dans un domaine pertinent ou expérience équivalente souhaité(e).
- 8 années d'expérience dans la direction de projets et/ou programmes complexes de réponse sanitaire d'urgence sur site, nécessitant un jugement et une interprétation approfondis. Une expérience professionnelle diversifiée sur le plan géographique est préférée.
- Capacité démontrée à influencer les agences homologues, les autorités locales et les leaders communautaires afin de travailler efficacement vers un résultat commun et convenu.
- Capacité démontrée à évaluer et à mettre en œuvre les meilleures pratiques et processus touchant plusieurs spécialités techniques afin d'obtenir des résultats rapides, cohérents et de haute qualité.
- Expérience dans le développement, la mobilisation des ressources et la direction de projets complexes à budget important, couvrant plusieurs spécialités techniques.
- Expérience avérée d'excellentes compétences en gestion et en direction. Capacité à donner l'exemple en matière de direction pour le personnel, dans le respect des politiques de gestion de l'IRC.
- Grande aisance et parcours réussi dans la supervision au sein d'environnements matriciels.
- Engagement démontré en faveur de l'inclusion et du traitement équitable du personnel, et capacité à identifier et à lever les obstacles à l'inclusion pour les groupes marginalisés dans le cadre de la réponse d'urgence.
- Expérience de travail avec des équipes et des communautés diversifiées, y compris les femmes, les jeunes, les personnes en situation de handicap et d'autres groupes exposés au risque d'exclusion.
- Excellentes compétences orales et écrites en anglais et en français requises.

jobs.title: Business Development and Grants Manager
jobs.body:
**Country Programme:** Moldova

**Contract Length:** 1 year

**Base:** Chisinau

**Starting date**: September 2026

**Line Manager**: Deputy Head of Programmes

**People in Need (PIN)** is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has been providing humanitarian and development assistance worldwide since 1992. Today, PIN operates in more than 40 countries, responding to humanitarian crises and supporting long-term development through programmes in education, human rights, climate resilience, and social inclusion. As one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, PIN works across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe to support vulnerable communities, strengthen civil society, and promote democratic values and human dignity.

## **About the Moldovan Programme of People in Need:**

People in Need (PIN) has been operating in Moldova since 2003, delivering development and humanitarian assistance across social protection and inclusion, civil society empowerment, agriculture and economic development. Following the escalation of the war in Ukraine in February 2022, PIN significantly scaled up emergency programming, including protection, cash assistance, education, winterization, and livelihoods support for refugees and host communities.

PIN Moldova currently manages a large and diverse portfolio of emergency and development projects implemented nationwide and funded by a range of institutional donors, while increasingly shifting toward long-term development assistance, particularly in the context of Moldova’s EU integration and the need to support local CSOs and line ministries in meeting EU accession commitments.

## **About the role:**

The Business Development and Grants Manager works closely with Programme, Grants, and Partnership teams to secure funding and build sustainable donor relations. The role drives strategic resource mobilization for the Country Programme – identifying, mapping, and pursuing donor opportunities aligned with the Country Programme’s strategic direction.

The position collaborates with Programme Leads in Moldova and HQ Technical Advisors and partners to co-create high-quality concept notes, pitches, and funding proposals, including leading complex multi-stakeholder proposals, and ensures that all concept notes and pitches reflect dignified, non-paternalistic narratives that respect local knowledge and partner expertise.

The role also ensures communication, with donors and maintains strong donor relationships through high-quality reporting and proactive relationship management, including with the Czech Embassy and the Czech Development Agency (CzDA), the European Union Delegation, and other current and prospective donors (e.g. GCF, U.S. Government donors, FCDO, and Swiss Cooperation, etc.). Additional responsibilities include supporting visits of international experts and study visits to countries outside Moldova, conducting institutional funding and proposal design, development and writing mentorship sessions for local team and local partners, and providing broader support to the Programme and Grants functions.

The Business Development and Grants Manager reports to the Deputy Head of Programmes and works in close cooperation with senior CP management (HoP/CD/HoSo/Head of MEAL) and relevant HQ departments.

The Business Development and Grants Manager supports the Grants and Reporting Team on grants health review and oversight, particularly on compliance and donor communications, and may also act as a secondary focal point for external liaison, including representing PIN vis-à-vis donors and in other coordination forums (clusters, working groups, etc.).

## **Main Duties and Responsibilities:**

**1. Strategic Pipeline Management and Donor Intelligence**

- Maintains and regularly updates the donor mapping and funding strategy, tracking funding trends and donor priorities, with particular attention to diversifying the portfolio into development sector in line with PIN’s Country Programme Strategy; keeps management informed of opportunities and strategic trends.
- Continuously monitors emerging and anticipated funding opportunities through donor websites, humanitarian assistance portals, clusters, and bilateral scoping with existing and potential donors; leads funding opportunity review (Go/No-Go) meetings.
- In coordination with the line manager and/or HoP, engages with donors during field visits to build and nurture relationships and promote PIN’s work in its strategic domains; documents donor intelligence and engagement efforts.
- Liaises with HQ funding advisors to strengthen donor knowledge and support proactive fundraising for the Country Programme.
- Maintains up-to-date grant files, donor guidelines, and resource materials, coordinating with relevant HQ desk colleagues.

**2. Proposal Development and Co-Creation**

- Collaborates with Programme Leads in Moldova and HQ Technical Advisors and partners to design high-quality concept notes, pitches, and funding proposals, facilitating a collaborative proposal-design process.
- Leads complex, multi-stakeholder proposals, coordinating the development process across all relevant departments — including supporting the design of logical frameworks, setting realistic and measurable targets, and supporting the development of narrative proposals and budgets.
- Ensures concept notes and proposals reflect dignified, non-paternalistic narratives that respect local knowledge and partner expertise.
- Supports proofreading and translation of proposals and budgets ahead of submission.

**3. Grants Compliance and Reporting Oversight**

- Supports the Grants and Reporting Team on grants health review and oversight, with particular focus on compliance and donor communications.
- Ensures reports meet donor requirements in structure and content, including mainstreaming issues (protection, gender, do-no-harm, conflict sensitivity), and that programme staff receive timely guidelines, templates, and examples to develop quality reporting contributions.
- Oversees compliance with donor guidelines on programme implementation, information collection and storage, and project deliverables.
- Maintains standardized reporting formats and an internal tracking database of reporting timelines by donor/grant, coordinating with the Deputy Head of Programmes, Programme/Project Managers, and MEAL to ensure timely, quality data collection and compilation.
- Drafts, proofreads and compiles interim and final donor reports.
- Prepares documentation and collects inputs from finance and programme teams to facilitate regular project review meetings, using standardized tools provided by PIN.
- Supports administration of project documentation in ELO and Navision (IRPs and other project documentation).

**4. Donor and Stakeholder Relations**

- Ensures communication, with donors and maintains strong donor relationships through high-quality reporting and proactive relationship management, including with the Czech Embassy and the Czech Development Agency (CzDA), the European Union Delegation, and other current and prospective donors (e.g. GCF, U.S. Government donors, FCDO, and Swiss Cooperation, etc.)
- Acts as a focal point for selected donors and grant contracts, both in external representation and in internal coordination with programme and operations teams on programme development and reporting matters.
- May act as secondary focal point for external liaison, representing PIN with donors and in other coordination forums (clusters, working groups, etc.).
- Supports visits of international experts to Moldova and study visits to countries outside Moldova, and coordinates and finalizes related documentation with the regional desk and CP senior management.

**5. FSTP Schemes, Subgranting and Partners Management**

- Oversees the design and set-up of Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) schemes, ensuring the scheme’s objectives, eligibility criteria, and financial ceilings comply with EU and other donors’ grant agreement requirements.
- Leads or supports the launch of calls for proposals to sub-grantees (e.g., local CSOs, community structures), including drafting guidelines for applicants, organizing information sessions, and managing the selection and evaluation process.
- Coordinates capacity and due diligence assessments of prospective sub-grantees, ensuring findings inform award decisions, tailored support plans, and risk mitigation measures.
- Ensures sub-grant agreements are properly contracted, with clear deliverables, budgets, and reporting obligations, in line with PIN’s internal grant management policy and donor rules.
- Maintains a subgrant tracking system/database recording contract values, disbursement schedules, reporting deadlines, and compliance; flags, and provides regular updates to the line manager and relevant donors.
- Identifies and flags subgranting risks (financial, reputational, safeguarding) in a timely manner and proposes mitigation measures, including site visits and spot-checks as needed.
- Ensures proper close-out of sub-grants, including final financial and narrative reporting, asset verification/transfer where applicable, and archiving of documentation for audit purposes.

**6. Capacity Strengthening and Partner/Programme Support**

- Conducts institutional funding and proposal design, development and writing mentorship sessions for local team members and local partners.
- Provides general support, direction, and advice to staff as workload and time permit.
- Supports internal coordination of meetings and events.
- Updates the grants management tools provided by PIN and liaises with other departments (Finance, MEAL, etc.).
- Supports proofreading and translation of project documents during implementation.
- Compiles documentation and supports related administrative tasks as needed.

## **Main requirements:**

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in development and/or humanitarian programming, with demonstrated involvement in program and project implementation in Eastern Partnership or comparable contexts.
- At least 2 years of experience in senior or middle management roles, such as Program Manager, Portfolio Manager, or similar positions with responsibility for overseeing and supporting project teams.
- Proven experience in program and project design, program development, and preparation of project proposals for institutional donors.
- Solid experience in humanitarian and development sectors relevant to PIN Moldova's portfolio, such as civil society support, including governance, protection, social inclusion, livelihoods, education, agriculture, or climate resilience programming.
- Proven experience managing and coordinating multi-partner or consortium-based initiatives.
- Experience engaging and collaborating with governmental stakeholders, including representatives of central and local government institutions, and representing programs in institutional and policy dialogue.
- Experience supporting Project Managers across the full Project Cycle Management, including planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and project closure.
- Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to guide, support, and coordinate Program Managers and Project Managers and engage effectively with donors, partners, and internal teams.
- Good contextual understanding of the Moldovan operating environment, including humanitarian needs, development challenges, and coordination mechanisms.
- Strong program planning and coordination skills, ensuring coherence between project objectives, donor requirements, work plans, and budgets.
- Proven ability to operate effectively in complex, high-pressure, and evolving environments, including emergency and politically sensitive contexts.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, enabling timely identification of implementation risks and support to practical, solutions-oriented responses.
- High commitment to quality programming, accountability, and continuous improvement, including the use of monitoring data to inform decision-making.
- Demonstrated commitment to safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, and accountability to affected populations, in line with PIN policies and humanitarian
- Languages – English - Fluent in all aspects

## **We Offer:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context;
- **Salary & Benefits**: Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies; expected salary range between 2900 - 3350 EURsuper gross (based on the assessment of the candidate’s knowledge, skills, abilities and previous experience)
- **Additional allowances include**:
- - Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR; - Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance of up to 750 EUR;
- **Time off and Rest:**
- - 25 days of holiday annually; - 10 sick days
- **Travel benefits:**
- - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work; - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure; - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment; - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
- **Health and Well-being:**
- - 24/7 Medical Support available online; - Free psychological consultations available online;
- **Professional Development:** Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities;
- This positions is unaccompanied.

**Application Deadline –** **Sunday, October 11, end of day**, by COB.

**Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. Candidates will be assessed as applications are received, and the recruitment process may be closed before the stated deadline if a suitable candidate is identified.**

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Safety, Health & Wellness
jobs.body:
**Background:**

IRC Arizona operates Health, Safety, and Wellness programming across both the Phoenix and Tucson offices, addressing the health, safety, and stabilization needs of refugees, asylees, survivors of trafficking and torture, and other vulnerable populations. The Health Program addresses vulnerable populations' health needs through medical case management, health education, and public health interventions, working in collaboration with the healthcare sector, public health authorities, medical providers, facilities, universities, and community agencies. The Safety & Wellness Department provides therapeutic services, asylum casework, survivor support, anti-trafficking and victim services, and case management for individuals with acute safety and stabilization needs.

As IRC Arizona continues to rebuild and adapt to changing refugee arrivals, an uncertain federal funding environment, and evolving community needs, there is a growing need for statewide coordination across these programs. Rather than operating independently across Phoenix and Tucson, IRC Arizona can strengthen its statewide impact through a unified Safety, Health, and Wellness strategy that aligns resources, expands partnerships, builds staff capacity, and improves outcomes for clients and communities in both offices.

**Job Overview:**

The Senior Program Manager for Safety, Health & Wellness provides unified, statewide program oversight, staff supervision, partnership development, and grant maintenance for IRC Arizona's Health and Safety & Wellness programs across both Phoenix and Tucson. This position maintains service provision and contract compliance for Therapeutic Services, Asylum Casework, Survivors of Torture, Anti-Trafficking and Victim Services, the Arizona Asylum Network, Preferred Communities, medical case management (Program Initial Resettlement, Matching Grant, and Refugee Support Services), and public health and health literacy programming. This position builds a shared statewide strategy that strengthens program quality, expands partnerships and diversified funding, and coordinates growth and shared learning across both offices, while preserving the ability of each office to respond to its community's distinct needs.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Statewide Strategy & Coordination**

- Serve as IRC Arizona's statewide point of coordination for Health and Safety & Wellness programming, aligning strategy, tools, and resources across Phoenix and Tucson without centralizing day-to-day office operations.
- Identify statewide and office-specific program priorities and support leadership in decisions about program investment, expansion, consolidation, or redesign.
- Create a shared framework for collaboration and shared program standards that promote consistency and quality while preserving local flexibility.
- Build and disseminate knowledge and analysis of local and national public health, safety, and wellness trends that affect IRC clients; act as IRC Arizona's subject matter expert on these issues.

**Program Oversight & Quality**

- Oversee Health and Safety & Wellness program staff in a manner that supports the exchange of ideas, encourages camaraderie and collaboration, and fosters professional development.
- Design strategies and frameworks to effectively operate programs and coordinate logistics for grant implementation, program subcontracts, and monitoring of grant activities across both offices.
- Implement, monitor, and provide ongoing training on a trauma-informed service model for Health and Safety & Wellness staff.
- Provide appropriate supervision and case coordination to ensure acute client needs are met in a timely and culturally appropriate manner across all programs.
- Monitor provision of services through regular and systematic file reviews, client interviews, and field visits to ensure compliance with donor requirements and delivery of quality services.
- Track budgets, program expenditures, and activities across programs; ensure donor deliverables are met; compile data and draft reports as required by donor and agency specifications.

**Program Development & Community Expansion**

- Support the development of new and expanded programming, including intensive case management, anti-human trafficking and survivor support services, behavioral health and psychosocial support, chronic disease prevention, maternal and child health, healthcare navigation, community health worker initiatives, and health education.
- Identify key stakeholders, partners, resources, donors, and volunteers to support program growth.
- Assess opportunities to responsibly adapt or expand select services to broader underserved populations whose needs overlap with those of IRC's existing clients, consistent with IRC's mission, policies, and operational capacity.
- Coordinate with other IRC teams to create multi-disciplinary approaches to services that facilitate the best possible client outcomes.

**Partnership & Funding Development**

- Build and maintain statewide relationships with state and local health agencies, FQHCs, hospital systems, universities, Medicaid health plans, behavioral health providers, law enforcement, community organizations, and philanthropic partners.
- Develop strategies to enhance community outreach and engage new stakeholders.
- Review, recommend, and write new grant opportunities in alignment with the office strategic action plan and in partnership with the Grants Manager, identifying federal, state, county, municipal, foundation, healthcare, and victim-services funding opportunities.
- Support diversification of funding to reduce dependence on refugee arrival levels or any single government funding stream.

**Staff Supervision & Development**

- Provide direct supervision to program supervisors and staff across the Health and Safety & Wellness departments (see Key Working Relationships).
- Provide coaching, leadership development, technical assistance, and opportunities for cross-office collaboration to strengthen local leadership and staff capacity.
- Provide supervision to AmeriCorps members, MSW interns, and volunteers associated with each program.

**Compliance & Organizational Commitment**

- Ensure coordination with the development and implementation of outreach and training activities to meet program outcomes.
- Participate in senior management meetings and staff development activities as requested.
- Role model IRC values and commitment to mission and clients.
- Comply with all IRC policies, procedures, and protocols, including the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Site Director, Tucson

**Position directly supervises:** TBD

**Position indirectly supervises:** N/A

**Indirect Reporting:** N/A

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:** IRC staff, interns, and volunteers across Phoenix and Tucson*

***External:** Community partners, stakeholder partners, DES, law enforcement, medical providers, employers*

**Job Requirements:**

- Graduate degree in social work, public health, or a related field strongly preferred; undergraduate degree in social work or equivalent work experience required.
- At least 5 years of related professional experience, including proven skills supervising case management staff, grant reporting, and program development; multi-site or cross-program management experience preferred.
- Demonstrated experience with trauma-informed, victim-centered, and/or public health service models.
- Excellent written and spoken English skills; bilingual ability preferred.
- Strong organizational skills and detail oriented; excellent writing and analytical skills.
- Case management, victim's assistance, and/or workforce development experience preferred.
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Computer literacy; database experience preferred.
- Ability to work independently across multiple sites and be a flexible team player.
- Must have a valid driver's license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation to travel regularly between Phoenix and Tucson offices.
- Must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and field time within the service delivery area to perform the responsibilities outlined above.
- Regular travel between Phoenix and Tucson required; occasional domestic (non-local) travel required, up to 10%.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $69,939 - $92,500/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Head of Business Development, WACAR
jobs.body:
***This position is open to internal candidates in the WACAR Region, or other IRC locations in GMT and EAT time zones, who have significant experience working in West and Central Africa countries. Candidates based in these countries are encouraged to apply.***

**BACKGROUND**

The **International Rescue Committee** (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC works with people forced to flee from war, conflict and disaster and the host communities which support them, as well as those who remain within their homes and communities. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home.

**The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department**

The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department has a growing portfolio of humanitarian relief, post-crisis recovery, and development programs under their remit. This work focuses support in five key areas: ensuring safety from harm, improving health, increasing access to education, improving economic well-being and ensuring people have the power to influence decisions that affect their lives. In all these programs, there is a drive to address the unique needs of women and girls (who represent the majority of those displaced) – and the universal barriers they face.

**The Awards Management Unit (AMU)**

Established in January 2016, the Awards Management Unit (AMU) is a global department with the responsibility for identifying, securing, and managing all funding from statutory/government donors. The AMU is a bridge between donors and country programs: providing expert technical advice to the country teams, while maintaining portfolio-level visibility to ensure consistency and compliance and manage risk. This unit ensures that donor compliance policies and procedures are implemented consistently and supports all staff working across the award management cycle for all restricted funding from global government sources.

**West and Central Africa Regional Overview:**

**The West and Central Africa Region (WACAR)** supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges—conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation—through integrated, impactful approaches.

WACAR prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration.

The region responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. WACAR focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs.

WACAR comprises Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon and CAR, Chad, Cote d’Ivoire, DRC, Mali, Niger, Nigeria.

**The Purpose of the Role**

Reporting to the Director, Awards Management (DAM) and working in close collaboration with BD leadership, the Head of Business Development (HBD), WACAR leads IRC’s business development efforts in support of the WACAR region’s country programs and is a key part of IRC’s global business development team, serving as the Region's representative in developing and implementing IRC’s global business development strategy. HBD plays a strategic role in the planning, identification, and successful pursuit of new business in line with country Strategy Action Plans (SAP). HBD support includes all phases of the business development process, including strategic planning, donor outreach and engagement, pre-positioning (capture), partnering, proposal development, due diligence, issues letter and agreement negotiation.

The HBD is responsible for maintaining regional level oversight of all business development for institutional donors in the IRC’s WACAR.

**Scope and Accountability**

The Head of Business Development exercises overall leadership for business development in the region and line management of the regional Program Development Advisor (PDA). The role oversees the regional pipeline and supports country business development strategies and planning, including reviewing the pipeline and individual opportunities and ensuring appropriate resourcing for successful bid submissions, in coordination with the Senior Program and Award Advisor, (SPAA) as relevant. The HBD provides development oversight of regionally assigned opportunities and serves as a key regional focal point for global opportunities, which are supported by the Business Development team.

Key Working Relationships

The HBD manages the regional Program Development Advisor(s) (PDA) and works closely with the regional management team (RMT), all Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) team members, and the wider Global Business Development Team. The HBD also works closely with country program teams, collaborates with other teams within the Awards Management Unit, including the Compliance and Policy (C&P), and Awards management Systems (AMS) teams; the wider Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department including Technical Excellence; External Relations; Finance; Global Supply Chain; Finance; Office of General Counsel; and other key departments within IRC who contribute to regional business development efforts. The HBD serves as point of contact with external donor and partner stakeholders during the pre-award stage, as applicable per region.

**Direct Reports:**

-Program Development Advisor (PDA)

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES AND RESPONSABILITIES**

***Planning and Strategic Leadership***

- Provide strategic vision on regional BD efforts in support of country program Strategy Action Plans (SAP), in collaboration with regional and AMU leadership.
- Maintain visibility on the overall pipeline across all public and institutional donors, in collaboration with regional Program Development & Awards Advisors as well as private donors, in close collaboration with the Senior Advisor, Private Partnerships
- Maintain up to date knowledge of donor funding priorities and geographical interests relevant to IRC’s areas of work.
- Provide advice, analysis and guidance to AMU, Regional and Country leadership on BD trends, target-setting, donor engagement, and support needs in the region, ensuring leaders have the right level of information to make decisions.
- Lead and support BD strategy development efforts and planning at regional and country level, to establish clear funding priorities and targets, to support decision making and enable effective positioning and resource planning.
- Coordinate support to country teams in the identification, tracking and pursuit of new business opportunities across a variety of technical sectors and donors, including ensuring that technical brainstorming, partner, and competitor landscape analysis and win theme sessions with technical and country staff are occurring.
- Support country BD strategy development, BD and donor engagement planning and delivery.
- Maintain regional pipeline information and analysis. Lead pipeline monitoring routines at regional level, including but not limited to Quarterly Pipeline Calls. Coordinate with Regional Finance Director on and contribute to the Operating Budget process ahead of Business Development projection-setting.

***End to End Program Development***

- Provide BD summary of new opportunities (Cat A-C but excluding UN) and support CPs in analyzing opportunities (Cat A-D) to inform Go/No Go decisions.
- Support effective and timely Go/No Go decisions, including sharing initial assessment of new opportunities and providing insight and input based on donor knowledge, likelihood of success and experience.
- Plan and manage effective division of bid leadership across the portfolio at capture and live stages of development to ensure appropriate support on all opportunities.
- At the early stage of opportunity identification, work with country teams, DAM and BD leadership in identifying and addressing escalated support needs.
- Act as the regional business development focal point for escalated bid opportunities, providing regional advice and coordinating escalated support when needed.
- Collaborate with other Business Development colleagues, Business Development Specialist team members and technical staff on high demand opportunities and multi-country and Technical Units-led bids.
- Maintain visibility of all opportunities in the region throughout the proposal development process. Contribute to critical bids (Cat D) prioritization, decision-making and bid resourcing; provide relational support.
- Ensure the following Bid Leadership responsibilities are performed consistently and effectively by the assigned BD Lead (HBD, PDA, or other) on each public opportunity in the regional portfolio:
    - Collaborate with technical units, country offices, and other colleagues to support conceptualization of winning program and bid designs, including support to building effective partnerships and consortia.
    - Provide effective proposal support, ranging from proposal management to comprehensive support, confirming responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements. Ensure required reviews and approvals are secured prior to submission to donor.
    - Provide guidance on donor policies and ensure project design is responsive and compliant with donor expectations, rules, and regulations.
    - When providing proposal management support, coordinate concept note and/or proposal development, including sharing initial assessment of new opportunities, reviewing timelines, ensuring the proposal team adheres to deadlines, supporting recruitment, assisting in budget development, ensuring document completion, organizing meetings, and compiling notes, and drafting and proofreading proposal sections. This includes support to country office teams in the management and maintenance of IRC’s award management system.
    - Review agreements, in coordination with relevant RPAS post-award focal point, to ensure accuracy and highlight key compliance requirements, in coordination with post-award, Compliance & Policy and country Grants teams.
    - Facilitate internal After-action Reviews with country teams, technical units, regional team, and other relevant stakeholders to collect lessons learned. Support efforts to share feedback beyond the region as part of IRC’s wider business development learning agenda.
    - Work across teams to ensure successful handover from pre-award to post-award, that lessons learned are captured, and best practices are shared, in support of improved knowledge management and through the development of relevant tools.
    - Maintain complete and accurate electronic files, including final submission packages and internal trackers.

***Donor and Partner Engagement***

- In line with IRC’s Partnership Ambition, contribute to increasing the volume and equity of IRC's work with local and regional partners (with a focus on women-led national organizations) by coordinating support to country programs in identifying partnership opportunities, identifying strong partners, and finalizing teaming arrangements.
- Support partnering conversations with international partner HQs where needed.
- Support countries and the region in planning effective donor, partner, and peer engagement, collaborating with relevant Partnerships/Strategic Partnerships and post-award colleagues.
- Representing IRC externally to donors, peers, and partners.
- Partner with CPs and regional leadership and colleagues on donor engagement and stewardship for prioritized donors.
- Support countries in donor engagement by translating information and intelligence received at the global level into regional and country priorities.
- Support donor mapping and targeting at country and regional levels, as well as positioning and capturing for a limited set of priority opportunities.
- Contribute to donor briefings for country teams, in collaboration with Global BD, as needed.

***Capacity Building and Training***

- Collaborate with other HBDs and stakeholders to share best practices and lessons learned, and to develop and improve tools.
- Contribute to developing, updating, and delivering business-development related training for the region, including roll-out and refreshers of the IRC Business Development Process training.
- Develop, strengthen, and share capacity of other IRC staff - including direct reports, IRC country and regional teams - to identify opportunities and develop strong program design and proposals, including BD processes.
- Support in recruiting, onboarding, and training of new country and regional grants and partnerships team members in collaboration with RPAS team members.

***Staff Management, Learning, and Development***

- Supervise and mentor direct reports, including communicating clear expectations, providing regular and timely performance feedback, document and discussing performance issues if needed, and delivering high-quality documented annual performance reviews.
- Ensure direct reports are trained on all relevant IRC processes and donor regulations
- Support direct reports in achieving annual objectives, acting as a trusted and accountable manager, mentor, and professional resource, including promoting collaboration, enabling adequate resourcing, and ensuring accountability.
- Together with the Director of Awards Management, the Head of Business Development and other members of the team, ensure Regional Program Awards and Support team cohesion, identify team needs and continuous improvements in ways of working, strengthen communication and foster cross-portfolio experience-sharing and learning, as well as other relevant decision-making processes and practices in support of effective team management and well-being.

***Other Responsibilities***

- Contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities and initiatives.
- Support with French/English translation when necessary.
- Participate in special projects, working groups and other tasks as assigned.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Essential**

Skills, Knowledge, and Qualifications:

- Substantial experience and a successful track record leading large proposal teams on complex, multi-year, multi-partner proposals with minimal supervision.
- Experience developing and supporting humanitarian and development proposals for NGOs.
- Strong proficiency in English and French.
- Experience with strategies and proposal processes of key government/statutory donors – US Government (USAID and Department of State), FCDO, EU institutions (ECHO, INTPA), and other donors (GAC, Sida, GFFO, BMZ, SDC, etc.).
- Experience collaborating with and supporting national and community-based partners.
- Experience in proposal budgeting is a plus.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to effectively collaborate across a variety of relationships in a multicultural environment.
- Demonstrated ability to collaborate equally effectively with colleagues in remote and diverse teams, including as team leader for proposals.
- Clear, compelling writing skills, preferably with previous experience with proposal writing.
- Ability to multi-task and prioritize effectively.
- Ability to travel internationally (approximately 20% of time).

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

***Ce poste est ouvert aux candidats internes de la région WACAR ou d’autres sites de l’IRC situés dans les fuseaux horaires GMT et EAT, qui possèdent une expérience significative de travail dans les pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest et d’Afrique centrale. Les candidats basés dans ces pays sont encouragés à postuler.***

**CONTEXTE**

**L’International Rescue Committee** (IRC) intervient face aux pires crises humanitaires mondiales et aide les personnes dont la vie et les moyens de subsistance ont été bouleversés par les conflits et les catastrophes à survivre, à se reconstruire et à reprendre le contrôle de leur avenir. Fondé en 1933 à la demande d’Albert Einstein, l’IRC travaille auprès des personnes contraintes de fuir la guerre, les conflits et les catastrophes, ainsi qu’auprès des communautés d’accueil qui les soutiennent, sans oublier celles qui restent chez elles et au sein de leur communauté. Présent aujourd’hui dans plus de 40 pays et 22 villes des États-Unis, nous redonnons sécurité, dignité et espoir à des millions de personnes déracinées qui luttent pour survivre. L’IRC montre la voie pour passer de la détresse au retour chez soi.

**Le département « Réponse aux crises, relèvement et développement » (CRRD)**

Le département Réponse aux crises, relèvement et développement (CRRD) gère un portefeuille croissant de programmes d’aide humanitaire, de relèvement post-crise et de développement relevant de sa compétence. Ce travail concentre son soutien sur cinq domaines clés : garantir la sécurité face aux dangers, améliorer la santé, accroître l’accès à l’éducation, améliorer le bien-être économique et veiller à ce que les personnes aient le pouvoir d’influencer les décisions qui affectent leur vie. Dans tous ces programmes, un effort particulier est déployé pour répondre aux besoins spécifiques des femmes et des filles (qui représentent la majorité des personnes déplacées) – ainsi qu’aux obstacles universels auxquels elles sont confrontées.

**L’Unité de gestion des subventions (AMU)**

Créée en janvier 2016, l’Unité de gestion des subventions (AMU) est un service mondial chargé d’identifier, d’obtenir et de gérer l’ensemble des financements provenant de bailleurs de fonds statutaires ou gouvernementaux. L’AMU fait le lien entre les bailleurs de fonds et les programmes nationaux : elle fournit des conseils techniques spécialisés aux équipes nationales, tout en assurant une visibilité au niveau du portefeuille afin de garantir la cohérence et la conformité et de gérer les risques.
