- Implement data-management, processing and analysis processes for research activities undertaken by the Critical Infrastructure and Services Team, including assessments of infrastructure damage, disruptions to essential services, winter and energy access, and other issue-based research in conflict-affected and frontline areas, using **KoboToolbox, R/Python**, **Power BI** and **Excel**, including:
- Supporting data processing and cleaning following data collection, including data transformation and preparation of analysis-ready datasets using existing instruments and scripts.
- Support the development, deployment and maintenance of KoboToolbox data collection tools, including form testing, data quality monitoring and troubleshooting during data collection.
- Supporting survey data analysis using R/Python and producing analytical outputs, visualisations and dashboard updates in close coordination with the assessment team.
- Conducting systematic data quality checks and supporting troubleshooting of data issues throughout the research cycle.
- Provide data support to other research activities implemented by the **Critical Infrastructure and Services Team**, depending on operational priorities and workload.
- Provide ad hoc cross-cutting data support to the wider IMPACT Ukraine mission, in coordination with the **Cross-Cutting Data Team**.
- Support the development, adaptation and maintenance of scripts, tools and analytical workflows that improve the efficiency and reproducibility of data processing and analysis.
- Ensure timely delivery of datasets and analytical products and uphold rigorous data quality control standards.

**2) Internal Coordination**

- Work closely with the Associate Research Manager, Assessment Officers, GIS colleagues and other members of the Critical Infrastructure and Services Team to ensure the production of high-quality research outputs.
- Coordinate closely with the IMPACT Ukraine Cross-Cutting Data Team to ensure alignment with mission-wide data standards, workflows and priorities.
- Coordinate with relevant IMPACT HQ technical teams, when required, to validate cleaned datasets, analytical outputs and associated scripts.
- Contribute to troubleshooting and technical support for data-related issues affecting research implementation.

**3) Confidentiality and Data Protection**

- Maintain the highest standards of data confidentiality and security.
- Ensure data management processes comply with IMPACT data protection requirements and established internal procedures.
- Take proactive steps to prevent unauthorised sharing, access or use of sensitive data and information.

**REQUIRED SKILLS:**

- Bachelor’s degree completed or in process in a sphere of social sciences, data science, information management or other related specialization.
- Good knowledge of descriptive and inferential statistics, basic knowledge of data science
- Strong skills in Python and/or R for data analysis (pandas, tidyverse) and willingness to work with both.
- Strong skills and experience with Power BI.
- Good Excel skills.
- Fluency in English is required.
- Understanding data confidentiality and data security principles.
- Ability to multitask with tight deadlines, on numerous research cycles in complex environment.
- A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.

**NICE TO HAVE:**

- Experience with Kobo Toolbox or similar platforms.
- Experience in humanitarian sector.
- Experience with other analytics or automatization tools would be a plus.

jobs.title: Community Engagement Program Manager
jobs.body:
**IRC Background**

The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 29 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home.

**Job Overview**

The Kansas Office for Refugees (KSOR) serves as a “Replacement Designee” for the state of Kansas, administering the Refugee Cash and Medical Assistance (CMA) program and Refugee Support Services (RSS) program in accordance with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) regulations, through the KSOR office, based in Wichita.

Beginning in FY2026, ORR awarded RSS grants directly to the State of Kansas government. The Community Engagement Prom Manager (CEPM) will support the KSOR Director and Deputy Director (DD) in planning, implementing, and managing changes to a state-centric model of refugee resettlement. This role will also coordinate communication and foster collaboration with the State of Kansas, KSOR departments, and external partners.

In addition, KSOR responds to community needs by coordinating and supporting various events, including stakeholder meetings, quarterly consultation meetings, community forums, partner coordination meetings, and training sessions with guest speakers. As part of the KSOR team, the CEPM is responsible for helping plan and/or support stakeholders in executing these events. They also manage strategic outreach efforts to ensure all relevant stakeholders are engaged.

The CEPM supports the integration of refugees, asylees, and other immigrants by leading initiatives that leverage the power of welcoming communities. They work closely with the Senior Management Team to coordinate community outreach, build effective relationships, and connect clients with community-based resettlement resources through collaboration, research, evaluation, and partnership building. The CEPM's responsibilities also include coordinating resettlement efforts for ORR-eligible populations outside traditional resettlement provider service areas. This position reports to the Deputy Director (DD).

***This position is expected to end September 30, 2027.***

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Technical Support:**

- Support strategic planning and implementation of the RSS program transition to the State of Kansas.
- Ensure effective communication and coordination throughout the process.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for KSOR to the State of Kansas and act as a liaison regarding the RSS portfolio.
- Serve as a key resource for interpreting Kansas State and Federal policy and regulatory changes impacting RSS program operations.

**Community Partnerships:**

- Develop and execute a robust community engagement strategy that supports the well-being of local communities and ORR-eligible populations in Kansas in collaboration. This strategy will focus on fostering refugee integration in collaboration with the State of Kansas, businesses, civil society organizations, and faith-based groups.
- Work closely with resettlement providers to ensure ORR-eligible populations have access to essential

 services by leading the development of a streamlined referral process for benefits and available resources.

- Plan, implement, and collaborate with local actors to amplify messaging about refugee resettlement and how community members can support refugee and immigrant newcomers in Kansas.
- Increase community engagement through outreach, training, and representing KSOR at local meetings.
- Intervene in areas of the state where access to services and benefits is becoming a concern.
- Keep KSOR leadership informed of new developments, opportunities, and barriers
- Lead in organizing and promoting participation in all events, including coordinating logistics.

**Other:**

- Manage and curate the KSOR website, newsletters, and other communication resources.
- Support the development of all State grant-related reports.
- Lead the development and execution of the KSOR communication plan.
- Maintain the current and detailed knowledge of services available to ORR-eligible populations in Kansas.
- Coordinate local community resources and respond to requests for assistance from stakeholders, including troubleshooting local refugee-related issues.
- Participate in community events supporting refugee integration.
- Perform other related duties and activities as appropriate.

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university preferred.
- 2-3 years of related professional experience.
- Experience with website maintenance.
- Flexible work attitude and ability to meet unexpected demands.
- Prior volunteer or professional experience in community development or volunteer coordination strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Self-direction and initiative, when needed, to take the lead and to follow through to completion.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written;
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- This position is hybrid in Kansas with monthly meetings at the KSOR office in Wichita, Kansas. Up to 30% statewide travel expected for meetings and events.
- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $63,296.10-$66,760.23/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: DIRECTOR, COUNTRY - (5432)-Ethiopia
jobs.body:
## **DIRECTOR, COUNTRY - (5432)**

Job Title

Director, Country

Location

Ethiopia - ET (Primary)

Category

Programs

Date Needed By

12/1/2026

Program Description (Background)

Job Description

**JOB SUMMARY:** The Country Director is directly responsible for the overall strategic planning, human resources, program design and implementation, program support operations, finance, administration, safety and security monitoring and evaluation supervision, expansion/development, and required reporting for the country program. The Country Director plays a strong leadership role through a high level of strategic leadership and effective advocacy. The Country Director sets direction, leads, maintains team morale, safety and welfare, and manages resources while maintaining oversight and accountability. This role is ultimately accountable for all aspects of the country projects and ensuring that organizational setup is adapted to the operational context.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Program Management**

Develop country specific strategic plan and proposals for programs in line with IMC’s global operational framework, considering country priority needs and in collaboration with country Senior Management Team (SMT).

Coordinate with headquarters and country departments to design and implement high-quality programs, ensuring all programs are completed within time, within budget, achieving program objectives and in line with International Medical Corps principles, values, minimum standards, policies and strategic plans.

Work closely with partners to identify a strategy for the maintaining and strengthening essential services and systems.

Structure the country team for efficient operations and for accurate and timely collaboration and communication with headquarters, including the preparation and presentation of achievement of indicator targets, budget expenditure and procurement plans for monthly country-pipeline calls.

Participate in writing and reviewing proposal applications.

When applicable, provide technical inputs and assistance to programs with particular reference to financial management and reporting systems.

Ensure Country Office participation in UN Clusters or other relevant coordination and other high level and operational coordination to ensure country programs are playing a vital role and to secure required support from the cluster coordination mechanism and the UN funding instruments such as CERF, CHF, etc.

Coordinate and lead monthly pipelines review and follow on adequation between spending and program implementation.

Report regularly to headquarters, providing timely updates of all operational situational and project management developments.

Ensure monitoring, evaluation and reporting on all program activities and progress to headquarter office and donors.

**Compliance**

Oversee program operations and reporting, ensuring compliance with agency technical standards, policies and procedures, donor regulations and local laws.

Facilitate investigations on violations of policies as appropriate.

Oversee the preparation of annual work plans and budgets.

Ensure compliance with local labor, NGO and technicality laws or present concerns to Senior Director / HQ Legal.

Roll out protection risk assessment across all the projects and implement subsequent action plans.

**Program Development**

Develop a clear funding/resources mobilization strategy.

Maintaining and expanding the country donor and financial portfolio based on the needs.

Pursue new sources of donor funding and maintain adequate donor funding levels to sustain identified program and support activities, while meeting IMC technical standards and organizational policies, ensuring staff wellbeing.

Leadership in proposal design and development, ensuring timely submission and providing inputs when applicable.

Remaining aware of donor funding intention.

Establish country partnerships to allow for collective organizations efforts through consortia.

**Human Resources**

Oversee the recruitment and selection of relevant qualified field staff, recommend promotions, disciplinary action and termination of staff in consultation with supervisors.

Collaborate with security team in country to maintain security of staff in the field locations.

When needed, make site visits to facilities to provide operational support to field site staff and ensure programs are being conducted timely and according to project plan.

Plan for and manage any program critical incident including medical evacuation

Maintain open lines of communications with all field staff.

Sign all contracts for employment.

**Training/ Capacity Building**

Determine training needs for the field staff in coordination with relevant supervisors.

Ensure senior national staff are trained to increase their responsibilities in order to build capacity and ensure sustainability of programs.

Represent and plan for professional development for expat and national staff.

**Working Relationships**

Maintain frequent communication with direct supervisor to ensure program activities and objectives are communicated.

Work with Senior Management Team (SMT) to ensure the coordination of programs.

When possible, ensure representation of the organization at task force meetings, assessment missions, camp coordination meetings, UN coordination meetings, INGO coordination meetings.

Interface with national government and relevant agencies to ensure mutual understanding of programs and maximize resource distribution and allocation of available funds.

Ensure Source and lobby for resources for staff wellbeing.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning**

Overall responsibility for ensuring mission’s commitments towards donors and IMC’s requirements on Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (M/E) requirements.

Integrate M/E into country strategies, frameworks, policies and plans.

Include M/E related roles and responsibilities to all staff who are responsible for program management and implementation.

Direct country level management to adequately budget for M/E activities across all grants.

Ensures country level Community Based Feedback and Response Mechanism (CBFRM) procedure is in place, functioning, and adequately resourced.

Ensures all highly sensitive complaints and feedback from the CBFRM are addressed and closed appropriately.

Raises profile/awareness and importance of M/E with other senior management members through routine review and briefing sessions.

**Representation**

Represent the organization and liaise with local and national authorities, UN, NGO, and donor agencies, to promote the organization’s programs, facilitate successful coordination of activities and ensure transparency and accountability to all stakeholders.

Serve as the principal liaison with Donors on matters related to the program to ensure financial and programmatic accountability to Donors.

Establish and update contact details of potential Donors in-country.

Participate in Donor meetings and communicate relevant information to HQ.

Work with key Donor Staff to develop and maintain optimum financial and programmatic relationship

Ensure maximum visibility of the Agency amongst the NGO community.

Lead the production of reports and ensure the timeliness and accuracy of information provided, as well ensuring confidentiality of sensitive information.

Contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of the organizations Code of Conduct, ethics, values and standpoint with regard to internal and external actors.

**Security**

The Country Director is ultimately responsible for the security management of staff, operations, assets and directs country-specific response to security threats and incidents, up to and including management of evacuation.

Monitor security level in collaboration with Country Security Management and consult with the HQ Global Security Senior Management to upgrade or downgrade level.

Responsible for ensuring that Incident Report Forms are completed and submitted to HQ Security in a timely manner.

Responsible for ensuring all staff are given a security briefing, and required documentation upon entry into the country.

Ensure application and compliance of security protocols and policies.

In cooperation with the Security Management, monitor the security situation and inform the HQ Security Management through weekly security reports.

Ensure that country security guidelines, SOP’s and policies are updated twice annually (July 31 and January 31) including contingency planning for evacuation, in accordance with agency protocols and respected by all staff.

Ensure adequate security funding is budgeted.

Nominate security focal points at each operational site in country.

Ensure Security staff in country are collecting and documenting local security related information (social and political context, external players, presence/reasons for conflict, military developments, political economy of armed groups), and communicating to the HQ Global Security Senior Management.

Establish a reliable communication chain to disperse important information, whereby once the CD communicates a message, it is systematically passed on from one person to the next, with each person knowing who they are responsible for informing. (phone tree).

Collaborate with local agencies to aid with security management.

Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive.

Job Requirements

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

Typically, a Master's degree in business, health or social service related field. Equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Typically, 12+ years proven progressive and significant experience in humanitarian programs and/or emergency response, mainly in the health or related field (Health policy, health reforms); including 10+ years of project management experience (management, planning, staff development and training), skills in emergency/ development programs; including 5+ years of experience in a senior-level management position in a field-based post.

Comprehensive knowledge and working experience with , CDC, UN, World Bank, EU, DFID and other key donors.

Financial management acumen, including managing budgets, banking activities, contracts and negotiations.

Experience managing procurement and logistical procedures and policies.

Knowledge in program sustainability and capacity building, public private partnerships and project monitoring and evaluation (both quantitative and qualitative methods).

Strong writing, presentation and program development skills.

Extensive fundraising and representational experience.

Proven capabilities in leadership required.

Strong negotiation, interpersonal and organization skills.

Additional Technical or Language Requirements

English

### **ETHICAL CONDUCT AT INTERNATIONAL MEDICAL CORPS**

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our Code of Conduct and Ethics and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our Code of Conduct and Ethics, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the Code of Conduct and Ethics, all staff are required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our Code of Conduct and Ethics and Whistleblower Policy prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

### **EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES**

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

### **MISCONDUCT DISCLOSURE SCHEME**

All offers of employment at International Medical Corps are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. International Medical Corps participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme from the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). In accordance with this, we will request information from an applicant’s previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

jobs.title: Spécialiste de la Recherche Agricole en Milieu Paysan (Fixed-term)
jobs.body:
## **Description de l’organisation**

Fondée en 2006, One Acre Fund aide 5,5 millions de petits exploitants agricoles à accroître la productivité de leurs exploitations. Présents dans neuf pays qui regroupent les deux tiers des agriculteurs africains, nous fournissons des produits agricoles de qualité, des plants d'arbres, des crédits accessibles, des formations agricoles modernes et une large gamme d'autres services agricoles. En moyenne, ce modèle permet à tout agriculteur d'augmenter ses revenus et ses actifs de plus de 35 % sur les terres qu'il exploite, tout en améliorant durablement sa résilience. Tout cela est rendu possible grâce à notre équipe de plus de 9 000 employés à temps plein, issus d'horizons et de professions diverses. Pour en savoir plus, consultez notre article: [Pourquoi travailler ici](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here).

## **Description du poste**

Le/La Spécialiste de la recherche agricole en milieu paysan assure la mise en œuvre opérationnelle et le suivi rigoureux des essais agronomiques auprès de notre réseau de petits exploitants. Il/Elle est responsable de l'identification et de la hiérarchisation des produits à fort impact, de la gestion logistique des essais, de la conception de protocoles de terrain scientifiquement valides et de la garantie de l'intégrité des données grâce à des validations régulières sur le terrain. En tant que garant(e) de la qualité des essais, il/elle résout les défis concrets sur le terrain et collabore avec des départements tels que les Opérations de terrain et le MEL. Deuxièmement, il/elle fournit un soutien technique adapté au contexte au personnel de terrain et aux agriculteurs, en traduisant les résultats de la recherche en orientations claires, pratiques et centrées sur l'agriculteur.

## **Responsabilités**

Recherche et Essais (75 %)

- Recherche : Utiliser une variété de techniques de recherche documentaire (ex. revues de littérature, analyses de marché, enquêtes auprès des clients, entretiens approfondis/discussions de groupe de focalisation) pour identifier les domaines potentiels d'impact à travers de nouveaux produits, pratiques et services avec le support de Responsable de Impact. Sélectionner des produits viables pour les essais en utilisant une approche systématique. Anticiper les risques, les complexités, les opportunités et les taux d'adoption potentiels afin de hiérarchiser efficacement les projets et de les aligner sur les objectifs du département.
- Gestion opérationnelle des essais : Concevoir avec le soutien de responsable de l'impact des méthodes et des protocoles de mesure scientifiquement rigoureux pour les essais, ainsi que des dispositifs expérimentaux statistiquement valides (y compris la taille de l'échantillon), tout en garantissant leur faisabilité opérationnelle.
- Logistique et respect des délais : Diriger la coordination logistique (et exploiter les systèmes d'approvisionnement parallèles là où ils sont disponibles) pour garantir la livraison à temps des intrants d'essai. Gérer de manière proactive les calendriers afin d'éviter les retards qui pourraient compromettre la saison des essais.
- Collaboration transversale : Travailler avec les différents départements (Opérations de terrain, Logistique, MEL) pour assurer l'adhésion et l'intégration transparente des activités d'essai dans les opérations de terrain principales. Durant la contre-saison, conseiller sur le développement du matériel de formation des agriculteurs.
- Exécution sur le terrain et résolution de problèmes : Assurer une mise en œuvre de qualité des essais et la production de données utiles en fournissant aux équipes d'essai des informations et des instructions claires et opportunes, ainsi qu'un contrôle de qualité régulier des données. Agir en tant que principal résolveur de problèmes pour les défis sur le terrain, en adaptant rapidement les plans pour résoudre les problèmes sans compromettre l'intégrité des données.

Agronomie de terrain et soutien technique (25 %)

- Résolution de problèmes contextuels : Fournir un soutien pratique et de dépannage au personnel de terrain et aux agriculteurs, ancré dans des preuves solides mais allant au-delà de la théorie des manuels scolaires. Évaluer les conditions réelles sur le terrain et les réalités des agriculteurs pour développer des recommandations spécifiques au contexte.
- Passerelle entre recherche et pratique : Traduire les résultats de la recherche interne et les protocoles agronomiques en orientations claires et exploitables pour les agents de terrain, les vulgarisateurs et les agriculteurs avec le soutien de responsable de l'impact. S'assurer que les conseils sont opérationnellement réalisables et adaptés au contexte local.
- Renforcement des capacités : Diriger des initiatives de formation axées sur l'application des compétences plutôt que sur la théorie. Permettre au personnel de terrain de résoudre les problèmes de manière autonome sur le terrain et fournir aux agriculteurs des solutions pour faire face aux défis rencontrés.
- Assurance qualité : Superviser la mise en œuvre sur le terrain pour garantir la conformité avec les protocoles agronomiques, mais avec un accent particulier sur la compréhension des raisons pour lesquelles les écarts se produisent et sur l'ajustement des protocoles pour qu'ils soient plus centrés sur l'agriculteur.

Responsabilités transversales :

En plus des deux domaines de responsabilité principaux ci-dessus, les activités suivantes sont intégrées dans tous les aspects du poste :

Gestion de projet et coordination opérationnelle

- Collaborer avec le Responsable Impact (Impact Lead) et les autres programmes pays d'OAF pour co-concevoir les protocoles d'essai, en s'assurant qu'ils sont opérationnellement réalisables compte tenu des contraintes des opérations de terrain et des contextes des agriculteurs.
- Prendre en charge la planification logistique de bout en bout pour les essais.
- Développer et maintenir des calendriers de projet détaillés basés sur le chemin critique. Suivre les progrès de manière proactive et résoudre les goulots d'étranglement pour s'assurer que les superviseurs d'essais et les équipes de terrain respectent toutes les échéances.

Conception et mise en œuvre d'enquêtes

- Diriger la conception des enquêtes agronomiques avec le soutien de responsable de l'impact, en veillant à ce que les types de données et les méthodologies appropriés soient utilisés.
- Former le personnel de terrain à la mise en œuvre des enquêtes et aux meilleures pratiques de collecte de données.
- Effectuer des validations sur le terrain pour garantir la qualité et l'exactitude des enquêtes.

Analyse des données et recommandations

- Réaliser des analyses simples des résultats agronomiques des essais avec le soutien du responsable Impact.
- Avec l'appui de ce dernier, formuler des étapes d'action et des recommandations claires, pratiques et axées sur les petits exploitants. S'assurer que les résultats sont traduits en stratégies de programme spécifiques plutôt qu'en simples rapports théoriques.
- Présenter les résultats aux parties prenantes concernées et soutenir la prise de décision basée sur des données probantes.
- Documenter les leçons apprises et contribuer à la gestion des connaissances de l'organisation.

## **Croissance et développement de carrière**

One Acre Fund investit dans le développement des compétences en management et en leadership. Votre manager et une équipe globale d’appui consacreront beaucoup de temps à votre perfectionnement professionnel. Nous donnons en permanence des feedback concrets via le mentorat et des revues de carrière régulières sous forme de conseils en management. Nous organisons également des réunions individuelles régulières, au cours desquelles nous écoutons et discutons au sujet des objectifs de carrière, et travaillons en collaboration en vue de créer des rôles réellement passionnants. En raison de notre croissance rapide, nous avons constamment de nouveaux rôles de haut niveau qui s'ouvrent et plein d’opportunités dans différentes fonctions.

## **Conditions exigées:**

- Diplôme de licence (Bachelor) en agronomie, en agriculture ou dans un domaine connexe exigé.
- Plus de 3 ans d'expérience en gestion de projets agricoles, avec des antécédents éprouvés dans la gestion d'essais sur le terrain, la coordination de la logistique et l'obtention de résultats dans les délais et les limites budgétaires impartis.

jobs.title: Early Refugee School Impact Specialist
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND:**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees, and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 29 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC helps refugees resettle and become self-sufficient. Our programs are designed to ensure refugees thrive in America--whether ensuring children are enrolled in school, adults become self-reliant through employment or starting businesses, or families receive acute medical care they need to recover from trauma or illness. IRC Wichita has been assisting refugees since 2011. The Wichita office offers a range of services including trauma-informed family support, economic empowerment, education for youth and adults, and immigration services. The IRC helps those in need to rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in their new home.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

The Early Refugee School Impact (ERSI) Specialist engages in the implementation, coordination, and support of IRC’s early childhood programming in alignment with organizational goals. Program coordination includes conducting program intakes, presenting, and explaining information on childcare options, preschool services, and connecting caregivers to relevant resources. This position will serve caregivers of children ages 0-5. The ERSI Specialist reports directly to the Education Manager.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

 **Client Services**

- Develop resources and expand partnerships that promote the success of refugee families through material design and partner engagement.
- Nurture partnerships with childcare centers and preschool service providers to advocate and provide support for the caregivers.
- Assess that quality practices are implemented and program outcomes are met; maintain data and reports indicating such.
- Serve as a focal point in the community for referrals to educational programs and services.
- Design and implement activities, workshops, and services which directly contribute to positive outcomes for refugee families.
- Identify and connect with licensed childcare providers and preschools who may partner with IRC.
- Perform outreach and educate caregivers on the benefits of enrolling children in childcare and preschool.
- Liaise between childcare providers, preschools, parents, caseworkers, employment specialists, and other relevant colleagues.
- Conduct intakes with qualified program participants to assess the needs of each individual/family.
- Assist interested caregivers with applications for childcare and financial resources (through childcare provider or government assistance).
- Lead and facilitate educational workshops, meetings, and events to promote healthy parenting skills.
- Provide follow-up with providers and families to assess the effectiveness of childcare plans.
- Other duties as assigned.

 **Administration, Monitoring and Evaluation**

- Conduct assessments of caregivers’ understanding of age-appropriate resources, activities, and childcare options.
- Ensure required intake documents are fully completed and service plan updated as appropriate.
- Comply with all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.

**Team/Office Participation**

- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and other duties as assigned.
- Work as part of a team to provide comprehensive strength-based services to IRC clients through coordination of cases and effective communication between team members and departments.
- Comply with all policies, procedures, and protocols of the agency, placing importance on client confidentiality.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work, early childhood education, or a related field of study is preferred.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills, strong attention to detail, and the proven ability to prioritize duties and manage time effectively.
- Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively with colleagues and partners in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment, and the ability to present to a varied public.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; Bilingual a plus but not required.
- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook). Proven experience in web-based data entry systems.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time efficiently.
- Strategic, creative, problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.
- Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area for home visits, agency visits, and service provider visits.
- Well organized and enthusiastic about working in a multi-cultural and client-centered setting.

**WORKING ENVIRONMENT:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Occasional evenings and weekends may be required.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $23.50/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Coordinatrices.teurs Ressources Humaines F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Nous recherchons activement des Coordinateurs.trices Ressources Humaines (CoRH) pour intégrer les équipes opérant dans les pays d’intervention de MSF France.

**Votre mission**

Membre de l’équipe de coordination, vous êtes responsable de définir, adapter, planifier et superviser la stratégie RH de la mission. Vous garantissez une gestion des ressources humaines cohérente avec les besoins opérationnels, le cadre légal local, les politiques de MSF et les défis du terrain. Vous êtes un·e véritable partenaire stratégique des équipes opérationnelles.

**Vos responsabilités principales**

- En tant que Coordinateur·rice RH et membre de l’équipe de coordination, vous définissez et mettez en œuvre la stratégie RH de la mission, en garantissant sa cohérence avec les enjeux opérationnels, le contexte local, le cadre légal et les valeurs de MSF.
- Vous jouez un rôle de partenaire stratégique, en veillant à ce que la mission dispose des ressources humaines nécessaires, tant en quantité qu’en qualité, pour atteindre ses objectifs. Cela implique d’anticiper les besoins, d’ajuster la composition des équipes et de développer les compétences du personnel national et international.
- Vous êtes garant·e de la bonne gestion administrative, contractuelle et juridique du personnel, dans le respect des politiques MSF et des obligations locales. Vous assurez également la qualité du management RH, en accompagnant les responsables dans la définition des postes, veiller à l'établissement systématique des bilans individuels, identifier et suivre les besoins en formation, être force de proposition dans la réflexion sur la composition d'équipe.
- Vous êtes en charge du recrutement et de l’animation de votre équipe (support, visite terrain, bilans individuels…) en assurant un accompagnement régulier, notamment via des visites sur les projets.

**Profil recherché**

**Expérience :**

- Minimum **2 ans en gestion des ressources humaines et en management d'équipe**
- au moins **12 mois sur un poste de coordination dans le domaine humanitaire**

**Compétences et aptitudes :**

- Bonne maîtrise d'Excel
- Capacité à organiser et prioriser la charge de travail
- Capacité d'analyse
- Esprit de synthèse et capacité à formaliser et à conceptualiser.
- Diplomatie, médiation
- Pédagogie
- Capacité à évoluer dans un milieu multiculturel et à démontrer son engagement et son soutien en faveur de la diversité, des comportements et des attitudes inclusifs et non discriminatoires.

**Langues :**

- Français atout important
- Anglais (C1)
- Langues supplémentaires appréciées : **arabe, espagnol, portugais**.

**Disponibilité** : Engagement de **12 mois minimum**

**Ce que nous offrons**

- **Contrat CDD de 12 mois**, temps plein.
- **Salaire** (à partir du 1er novembre) **entre 50K€ et 60K€ brut annuel** en fonction de l'ancienneté et de l'expérience pertinente
- **Prise en charge** des fraacis liés à la mission (transport, visas, logement, vaccins, etc.).
- **Assurances** santé, rapatriement, retraite.
- **Perspectives d’évolution** : formations, accompagnement et développement de carrière dans un large éventail de contextes humanitaires.

**Pourquoi vous ?**

Vous êtes rigoureux·se, engagé·e, stratégique, à l’écoute, et vous souhaitez mettre vos compétences au service de populations en situation de vulnérabilité. Vous avez une vision globale de la gestion, et vous croyez qu'une mission réussie repose autant sur une bonne logistique que sur une gestion humaine et financière solide.

jobs.title: First, a community; then a job
jobs.body:
This ad is strange and very long. It’s like this because what we want to say is “we have found the job of our dreams”, but everyone would say that. So we wrote all of this instead.

The chance that it is the job of your dreams too is tiny, but exists. In truth, it’s not a job, it’s more of a community. Some would say a life choice. [Second Tree](https://secondtree.org/). Twenty-seven people from all over the world who left much better-paid jobs to work in refugee camps in Greece. Everyone in the team is here because of their commitment to help people, and to do that in a specific way we find ethically valuable.

But this is not for everyone; it’s actually not for most people. We all do an enormous amount of work (but for something really meaningful), for very small compensation (but it’s the same for everyone: founders, directors, top management, everyone).

And this level of transparency goes beyond our compensation policy: not only can you, but you are expected to, criticise your bosses. If you don’t, you are not a good fit for a group of people who want to improve.

So, if you have been close to the reality of refugees in Greece through social solidarity networks, legal work, or just rational compassion; or if you are a disillusioned humanitarian who is looking for a place that really cares; or you work in another sector and want to start doing work that is meaningful; this might be for you.

YOU

You are someone who is driven by purpose, not profit. There is nothing wrong in wanting to get rich, but we cannot do that here: our main criterion in deciding how to invest our time is trying to make the world a better place.

You might be surprised, maybe even sceptical, while reading this ad: can a place like that even exist? You want to find out, and you will ask us all of the questions that you have in your mind. You will not be polite; you want to really understand if this thing can actually exist.

You want to work with people who care deeply, you want to be in a team that’s just as committed as you are. People who are extremely effective at what they do, because they have the skills required or are willing to put in the hard work that is necessary to develop those skills.

You have the competence and the resolution to translate your ethical drive into meaningful and effective action. You have:

- Intelligence: You have changed your mind and made someone else change their mind, through rational conversations, at least once in the last two weeks
- Honesty: There is nothing you wouldn't say, except the things you say you wouldn't say. If you mess up, you say so. If someone else messes up, you say so too
- Engagement: When you read the Wikipedia entry for Aumann's Agreement Theorem you get excited. You don’t want to “be yourself”, you will try to improve us
- Ethical drive: You have decided (no matter how recently) that it’s not about what you’re good at or what you like to do, but about what is right to do
- Sense of humour: You are ruthless. Listening to [this advice](https://secondtree.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Ms-advice.mp3) for humanitarians, from an Afghan teenager with an extremely painful story, moves you

You also have:

- English Proficiency: Speaking good enough English is necessary since it’s our working language. Other languages (like Arabic or Persian) are valuable. But the language we communicate in is English.
- Possibility of Long-Term Commitment: Any new team member receives an incredible amount of investment. The most senior people in the organisation will sit down with you and try to see how you can grow and, hopefully, in the long term you can replace them. Of course, no one can commit to something like this without seeing it first. But if you already know that in two months, you’ll be doing something else, this is not worth it for either of us.
- Potential: Show us your skills, orthodox or unorthodox. Whether you have something you can contribute with, or you are someone eager and able to learn quickly. Here, new team members gain responsibilities; there is no ceiling. If you show that you are very capable, you might be the person who runs programmes in refugee camps in Greece, who delivers courses at universities across Europe, provides training in Syria or Iraq, or speaks with important institutions on the global stage.

US

Second Tree was founded by a group of volunteers working together in one of the worst refugee camps in Europe (Katsikas, close to Ioannina). Some lived in the camp, some did not. From the beginning, we realised that making such a distinction – even with good intentions – “othered” refugees. At the time we didn’t know that our actions were called community engagement; we just knew that we were building a community.

Ten years later, Second Tree has kept the same ethos and turned it into a community engagement model, a policy, and a package of training programmes for local authorities, international institutions and civil society organisations.

We still work in the refugee camps in Greece (Epirus), our root and innovation lab, where we keep learning and developing new ideas. But now we also advocate – through writing, public speaking and thought leadership – for a world reception system that sees refugees as equals.

But we live in the real world, and we understand trade-offs (if you decide to apply, alongside what’s written in the “how to apply” section, include in your email a description of how good you are with trade-offs). We understand that the life we all live is not for everyone. It’s a life full of meaning, but also of a lot of sharing, and some sacrifices. The very idea of having such a compensation policy, where everyone is the same, is a trade-off: we want as many resources as possible to go to the activities we do for the people who live in refugee camps. We are aware that this way we will lose some people, but we think this is better than giving higher salaries and doing less good things.

OUR PHILOSOPHY

We don’t see refugees as victims, but as human beings. The community engagement model we developed is called “Refugees Are People”, or RAP. Often, in the humanitarian world and in the reception systems of Europe, refugees are perceived and treated as victims.

People that you need to protect, because of their vulnerability, or celebrate because of their heroism, or avoid upsetting because of the culture they are reduced to. This depiction is often used by NGOs, activists, academia, and individuals to foster support, highlight injustice and counter anti-refugee sentiment. However, despite being well-intentioned, it undermines and disempowers refugees in a similar way to how the opposite form of “othering” (perceiving refugees as invaders, thieves, etc) does.

At Second Tree, we place significant emphasis on countering these victimising sentiments. It’s not easy. We all carry biases within us, and committing to this belief requires consistent discussion and self-reflection.

It means engaging intellectually, disagreeing, joking with refugees as you would with other people, and holding them to the same standards – not lower, not higher – as anyone else. This, practising joint responsibility and the same high expectations for everyone involved, is how Second Tree has managed to build strong communities.

FAQs

**1. Do you get money from the EU? How does this interact with your values as an organisation?**

Yes. Only for projects we write or contribute writing, with partners (local authorities, organisations, universities) around the world we value; and only for things and ideas we want to do. We believe very much in our work, and we think it would be immoral to turn down funding we could do important things with. Of course, unless it has constraints that go against our principles or requires us to do things we don’t want to. We have turned down projects (also big ones) that would have compromised this.

**2. Do you get money from the Greek government?**

No. But not in principle. If there was funding, offered by the Greek government, that would allow us to do things we consider meaningful, without having to compromise our principles, we would try to secure it. In these ten years it has never happened, but it might be that we haven’t been good enough at finding it.

**3. Where does the majority of your funding come from?**

We have legal entities in 4 different countries, with Greece, Ioannina, being our headquarter. Overall, last year 62% of our funding came from grants and foundations, 38% from small donations on our websites.

**4. Aren’t NGOs in Greece just businesses disguised as charities? Or scams?**

No. And definitely not Second Tree. The level of access and transparency we decided to commit to on topics like decision making, funding, policies, etc is totally at odds with that. Can you imagine a scam project where everyone knows what everyone else earns? If you'd like to talk to current or former team members, let us know. We are not transparent because we owe it to someone, but because it is our choice.

**5. Do you have a horizontal hierarchy? What does that mean?**

We don’t know either, what that means exactly. We have positions and responsibilities, but they don’t entail being right in a discussion (or a higher salary). Certainly, if a decision needs to be made with a tight time constraint, the person that is in charge of that position will make that decision. But that decision will be under everyone’s scrutiny. Actually, newer team members are required to provide points of improvement for their managers (and, hopefully, take their jobs!) We do not do this because we are “nice”, but because it’s the only way to keep improving the way we function.

**6. What does a week look like?**

Everyone creates their own schedule, with only a few meetings everyone is required to attend (for example, our team meeting is on Wednesday morning). That means that people often work very different schedules, some people prefer to work at night, some people on Saturday morning, some wake up early and finish early. But two things are true: we all work very hard, and there are commitments that have fixed times (e.g. if you are teaching Greek in a refugee camp, you’ll have a fixed schedule on the days you go there; if you work in the communication department, you’ll have fixed meetings with the comms team; etc).

**7. What’s the compensation policy you mention?**

Our compensation policy was created with the central idea that we are not rewarding a job description, but allowing team members to live a decent life while doing our meaningful work, for as long as we all want. And use the rest of the resources to benefit refugees. We don’t believe it is morally wrong for humanitarians to have high wages, but it’s not how we want to do things. You can read more[ here](https://secondtree.org/compensation-philosophy/). Of course, ask us all the questions you’d like. Don’t be shy about this.

**8. How long is the recruitment process?**

It’s long. We have put a lot of effort, and time, in our recruitment process. We commit to answer you in 48hs, and to have human beings read what you write and speak to you. That shows how much we care about choosing people well. That is also reflected in the length of the process. The full length depends on your answers and our interactions, but it will likely include multiple interviews.

**9. How likely is it that I will be selected?**

It’s quite unlikely. We don’t have lots of resources, and invest a lot in new team members. And, frankly speaking, only very few people are the right match for our team.

**10. Ok, right, but I want to know the likelihood of being accepted if I send this application?**

We don’t have a percentage, because we have never published an ad like this. In our normal volunteer applications, our acceptance rate is very low (in our latest internal report it was 1.8%).

**11. Is it possible to work remotely?**

Yes. But most of the people in the team are based in Ioannina. Some people work full time remotely, some of them abroad. However, the roles that can be done remotely are fewer, so it’s more unlikely that you’ll be selected. If you want to work remotely, specify it in your email.

**12. Is accommodation or food provided for?**

We have five houses in Ioannina that we all share, where the people in the team that ask for accommodation could stay. Wanting accommodation or not does not impact the likelihood of being selected. We do not provide food.

**13. You said everyone gets the minimum to survive, but do you have formal contracts?**

Yeah, we don’t do illegal stuff, and we don’t think we should. The policy is the same for everyone, and it depends on how long you’ll stay at Second Tree. New team members have a trial period, during which some expenses are refunded. For those of us who are staying longer, the easiest way to make sure we have enough money to survive is through a standard (and small) employment contract. The bureaucratic framework depends on the person’s circumstance (e.g. an American might be hired by Second Tree US). In general, for those who work in the headquarters in Greece, that is a normal EFKA contract.

**14. How much of the work is field-based versus office-based?**

It depends on your role. Even if your job is field based (like a Greek teacher), there will be a significant portion of other work (preparing your classes, Education meetings, etc).

**15. What were you all doing before Second Tree?**

Very, very different things. Some people worked in NGOs, some were in academia, some were doing manual jobs, some worked as journalists or in think tanks, many were (and some are) teachers. But there are many more options. One team member worked in finance, one was a scuba diving instructor, one for a TV channel.

**16. Is it really true that it’s ok to criticise and make fun of my managers?**

No. It’s not “ok”, it’s required.

**17. What is the thing that new team members struggle the most with?**

Generally speaking, it’s TAD (Trust And Discussion), our internal culture. We are very straightforward with each other. Our practices are: Good Faith, Transparency, Open Enquiry and High Expectations. Written this way, it can sound easy or vague, but caring for each other this much requires a lot of hard and very concrete effort.

**18. Why don’t you ask candidates to apply for a specific role?**

We value the person before the skills that they bring. It’s useful to know what you are good at (and what you are bad at), but if our way of sharing purpose doesn’t resonate with you, it won’t last. Some of us used to believe that the humanitarian sector needed professionals, not good people. Now it’s very clear to us that we need good people first.

**19. Can I really ask you any question and you won’t get offended?**

Yes.

jobs.title: eLearning Proposal Writer (Remote)
jobs.body:
Altamont Group is a mission-driven advisory and impact investment organization, working across advisory, consulting, digital, and investment services to help clients deliver meaningful impact. We are hiring an **eLearning Proposal Writer** to lead the development of complete, targeted, and compelling responses to RFPs for digital learning solutions, articulating Altamont Group's value and winning new business across our learning and development service lines.

**Description**

Altamont Group is hiring an **eLearning Proposal Writer** to respond to complex RFPs spanning **custom eLearning development, instructional design, learning management systems, mobile and blended learning, multimedia production, and learning analytics**, working with clients across government, enterprise, education, and non-profit/NGO sectors.

- The eLearning Proposal Writer will create complete and compelling responses to requests for proposals (RFPs) that communicate Altamont Group's learning expertise, solution approach, and value with the aim of winning new business
- The ideal candidate has a strong learning and development background with a solid understanding of instructional design, custom eLearning production, LMS platforms, and digital learning standards, along with three or more years of experience responding to RFPs from government, enterprise, education, and non-profit organizations, coupled with strong writing skills
- We need an energetic, motivated, and persistent person who can write winning proposals

**Responsibilities**

- Read incoming RFPs/TORs and develop the proposal development plan
- Develop bid development strategy and proposal project planning
- Complete the research and discovery needed to develop instructional, technical, implementation, and cost proposal documents
- Ensure content matches the RFP/TOR and includes approved proposal language according to company policy
- Ensure responses follow corporate brand style and tone guidelines
- Review and customize RFP responses
- Serve as a liaison between learning solution teams and proposal content, clearly articulating instructional approaches, learner journeys, content formats, platform requirements, accessibility considerations, and implementation plans
- Verify that responses address key client priorities, evaluation criteria, learner needs, measurable outcomes, and win themes
- Write all required and additional RFP response documents and attachments, including cover letters, executive summaries, needs-analysis narratives, instructional design approaches, development methodologies, implementation plans, quality-assurance plans, and project schedules
- Incorporate feedback from proposal review sessions
- Assist with proposal knowledge management and retention of content for future use
- Provide the proposal submission package, including accompanying documents and cover email
- Develop pitch and clarification-meeting materials, including presentations, solution overviews, learning journey summaries, briefing notes, demonstrations, and speaking points
- Support in other areas as requested
- Ensure:
    - Our unique value proposition is clear and evident in every part of the proposal
    - Our cover letter and executive summary clearly address what the client is looking for
    - Thoroughly yet concisely respond to all areas of the proposal
    - By the end of the proposal, the reader is left with no questions as to why they should choose Altamont Group
    - A complete, client-ready, proofread, and edited proposal is provided

**Required Skills and Experience**

- Bachelor's Degree from an accredited University; Master's preferred
- Learning and development background and experience across eLearning service areas, particularly in:
- Instructional design; custom eLearning and microlearning; virtual instructor-led and blended learning; learning management systems; storyboarding and multimedia production; assessments and learning evaluation; accessibility; and standards such as SCORM, xAPI, and LTI
- Expertise in developing evidence-based, well-researched learning solution methodologies in response to RFPs, including needs analysis, learner and audience analysis, instructional strategy, content development, implementation, quality assurance, and evaluation
- Three or more years of experience responding to eLearning, training, education technology, or learning management system RFPs
- Excellent writing, organizational, communication, and planning skills
- Previous experience writing successful bids/proposals
- Demonstrated history of winning bids
- Enhanced research and data analysis skills
- Able to articulate the linkage between client needs, learner profiles, instructional strategies, technology choices, deliverables, implementation plans, and measurable learning or performance outcomes
- Strong attention to detail
- Proven track record of timely and high-quality completion of assignments
- Ability to manage deadlines efficiently
- Strong critical thinking ability
- Ability to work independently
- Highly organized with strong time management skills, and an ability to learn quickly and produce high-quality work under tight deadlines
- Flexible attitude toward receiving feedback
- Proficient with MS Office and SharePoint; familiarity with common eLearning authoring tools, LMS platforms, and proposal collaboration systems is preferred

jobs.title: Nigeria Client Database Management Coordinator
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

We started working in Nigeria in 2018, serving just 150 farmers. That figure grew year on year, and we now serve more than 300,000 farmers across three regions in Niger State: Minna, Mokwa, and Iseyin.  
  
Between our tree program and a diverse staple crop program, xx staff are supporting farmers in Nigeria to grow their way to prosperity.

## About the Role

Seeking a data management pro with 1-2 years experience in databases, data warehousing and SQL to oversee client data ensure date integrity with out core operations team and enhance efficiency for Business Operations

## Responsibilities

Data Management:

- Oversee full client data lifecycles from enrollment to repayment.
- Maintain precise and updated client databases.
- Fulfill data analysis requests from partner departments to inform strategic decision-making and external needs.

Team & Communication Management:

- Directly manage 3–4 CDM Data Officers and supervise temporary data entry casuals during peak operational periods.
- Represent the CDM sub-department in meetings when assigned or when the manager is unavailable.
- Facilitate training for Field Officers on One Acre Fund (OAF) productivity tools and applications.

Operational Management:

- Evaluate and implement process/system improvements for managing client repayments and resolving repayment issues.
- Conduct periodic reconciliations between bank records and client databases.
- Provide support during operational audits.

Customer Service & SLA Management:

- Set achievable performance targets and drive process improvements.
- Maintain a 100% Service Level Agreement (SLA) standard throughout the year

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Advanced Data Analysis: Expert skills in Excel and Google Sheets to analyze data and make informed decisions.
- Work Planning & Organization: Strong ability to multitask, delegate, prioritize, and manage multiple projects with high accuracy.
- Leadership & People Management: Experience managing teams, resolving conflicts, and coaching/engaging field staff.
- Technical & Domain Knowledge: Proficient in Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides), with a strong understanding of organizational policies and an accounting or bookkeeping background.
- Growth Mindset: High willingness to learn and adapt.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Minna, Nigeria

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Nigeria.

## Application Deadline

20 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Tupande Mechanical Maintenance Engineer / Specialist (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## **About the Role**

Seeking an exceptional Mechanical Engineer to execute high-level mechanical maintenance, troubleshooting, and repairs across all Tupande Soko factories and reduce operational downtime for our processing operations.

## **Responsibilities**

Hands-on Mechanical Maintenance & Repair

- Execute hands-on mechanical repairs on critical processing machinery to ensure operational continuity across all factory locations.
- Troubleshoot complex mechanical equipment failures directly, providing on-the-spot technical interventions when standard maintenance staff or vendors are unavailable.
- Perform routine and deep-dive mechanical overhauls, component replacements, and structural alignments on heavy plant machinery.

Preventive Maintenance & Execution

- Physically execute mechanical preventative maintenance schedules and job plans assigned via the CMMS.
- Inspect, adjust, and overhaul mechanical assemblies (such as gearboxes, pumps, hydraulic rams, pneumatic lines, conveyors, and bearings).
- Track and provide direct data to the Lead Engineer on mechanical asset conditions, failure modes, and component wear rates.

Machinery Focus & Asset Care

- Act as the core mechanical technical intervention specialist for Soko factory machinery repairs and maintenance. Ensure all soko machinery is in a good performance state.
- Conduct technical repairs on industrial dehydrators, macadamia processing systems, and industrial-level biochar production equipment.
- Verify and list precise mechanical specifications for machines, spare parts, and consumables requested by factory teams.

Workforce Mentorship & TPM Support

- Mentor and model best-practice mechanical repair techniques during direct interaction with factory staff to elevate technical standards
- Assist in delivering TPM (Total Productive Maintenance) maintenance training for machine operators specifically regarding mechanical checks, cleaning, and precision lubrication
- Coach operators on identifying early mechanical warning signs like abnormal vibrations, heat, or noise

Safety, Food Safety, and Regulation

- Ensure all maintenance activities comply with safe systems of work: permit to work, LOTO, confined space, and relevant Kenyan regulatory requirements (KEBS, DOSH, NEMA)
- Maintain HACCP-required equipment records for food-contact assets; lead the maintenance function's contribution to food safety audits
- Champion a zero-harm safety culture on the shop floor; report hazards and quickly close out structural or machine risk issues

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You'll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You'll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Technical skills:

- Degree or Higher Diploma in Mechanical Engineering or appropriate engineering field
- Active registration/membership as an engineer or technical practitioner in Kenya
- Preventive/predictive maintenance programme design and implementation
- Experience with avocado oil machinery repairs and maintenance preferred
- Experience with industrial dehydrators, macadamia processing, and industrial level biochar production preferred
- Ability to utilize CMMS software (SAP PM, Maximo, Limble, etc.) to close work orders and log technical data
- Deep mechanical fault-finding and root cause analysis on industrial plant equipment
- Proficiency in mechanical drawings, pneumatics, hydraulics, and welding/fabrication techniques

Knowledge:

- Food safety management systems and HACCP requirements as applied to plant maintenance
- Kenyan occupational health and safety legislation (OSHA, DOSH requirements)
- TPM (Total Productive Maintenance) or World Class Manufacturing principles
- Kenyan regulatory environment for food manufacturing (KEBS, relevant standards)

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Rukanga, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, paid time off

## **Contract Duration**

2 years

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

20 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization's mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*
