In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable.

The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices.

## About the Role

Seeking a Government Relations & Program Support Coordinator to liaise with Zonal/Woreda offices, support program growth in North Shewa zone, strengthen partnerships, ensure compliance, de-risk fieldwork, and travel frequently. The duty station will be at **Debre Berhan Town**).

## Responsibilities

Manage work relationships with woreda government and Zonal Focal Persons (FPs)

- Serve as the primary day-to-day liaison with woreda and zonal project focal persons (FP) and other government stakeholders.
- Proactively identify government relations issues at the woreda and kebele levels by maintaining close communication with the program team, particularly Tree Officers (TOs) and Cluster Leads (CLs), and work with relevant government stakeholders to resolve them in a timely manner.
- Participate in the weekly cluster lead meetings to understand GR challenges that may exist in the field and resolve them on time by leveraging run alignment meetings with woreda and zonal FPs as needed
- Attend other government meetings as directed by the Senior Partnerships Associate
- Update contacts and meeting notes on Customer Relationship Management tool
- Leverage networks and knowledge of the landscape to help identify opportunities to expand and/or improve One Acre Fund’s work

Prepare, organize, review, and Submit documents as required on time to project signatory offices and other government offices, especially quarterly reports

- Gather inputs for quarterly reports from department leads or their designee
- Write and develop clear and concise quarterly reports that track progress and inform project stakeholders.
- Coordinate the review from his manager, incorporate comments, and finalize the report.
- Coordinate the submission of the reports to the woreda and zonal project signatory offices.
- Prepare project mid-term and terminal reports.
- Prepare outgoing letters for woredas as needed.
- Identify, monitor, and obtain all compliance requirements at the woreda and zonal government level and submit documents as required.

Track woreda FPs’ and DAs’ support to OAF activities and field staff on a weekly basis, evaluate results, and take appropriate actions to increase program efficiency

- Monitor the assistance provided by woreda FPs and DAs to OAF operations on a weekly basis using a tracker
- Evaluate results and resolve issues in consultation with Woreda SHs and zonal focal persons.
- Ensure that the woreda FPs and DAs are fulfilling their roles and responsibilities as per prior agreements with One Acre Fund
- Follow up and ensure the woreda office of agriculture takes appropriate actions on the focal persons and DAs with underperformance issues.
- Participate in the resolution of identified issues/risks with manager support.
- Troubleshooting of Woreda Government Relations in consultation with the Senior Partnerships Specialist and with escalation,

Organize and lead meetings and trainings as needed with support from your manager

- Provide GR capacity-building trainings to field team at least once a year
- Support on GR orientation and onboarding of new Woreda and Kebele employees,
- Co-lead project launch, mid-term, and terminal workshops
- Support/facilitate field visits and events for external stakeholders.
- Provide other administrative support as needed

Other Projects

- Other Partnerships and Program projects as assigned by your supervisor (when time and skill allow)

Special projects are the key to growth at OAF, and we want someone who is excited to grow their responsibilities through projects outside of their core responsibilities. Special projects in the first year might include things like data entry, translating documents into Amharic, scanning and binding of documents, support on inventory, support during input distributions, and support during seedling distribution.

## VISIT: [Tenders | MSF Eastern Africa](https://msf.or.ke/tenders) to download the full tender document

## RFP process

### RFP planning

Below is the target selection process timeline:

Issuance of Request for Proposal - 03.08.2026

Bidders’ confirmation of participation - 13.08.2026

Final questions/ request for clarifications - 20.08.2026

Feedback on clarifications - 27.08.2026

Reception of bids - 07.09.2026

Bidders shortlisting - 14.09.2026

Optional: shortlisted bidders’ interviews - 21.09.2026

Final selection for RFP - 28.09.2026

### Confirmation of participation

Bidders deciding to take part in this RFP are requested to send their written confirmation of participation by email to the contact persons by 13th August 2028 at the latest.

### Bid submission rules

The bidders must send their responses and related documents by email **msfea-proc-tenders@nairobi.msf.org**by **7th September 2026** at the latest.

Explicit reference must be made to the above RFP reference:

By email: in the email subject line

Proposals submitted beyond the above deadline will be rejected and returned to the bidder or discarded.

Bids submitted must remain valid for at least **90** days after submission.

### Supplier Response

The bidders are requested to write a specific and concise answer to each of the questions in this RFP and attached Terms of Reference. All questions and answers will be taken into account for the final supplier selection.

It is not permitted that local companies (registered in the country of the project) appear as joint-ventures or associate partners in more than one application.

### Request(s) for clarification

Bidders are invited to either submit questions / requests for clarification by email.

#### Project information visits

No project visit required for this RFP

#### Requests for clarification

Enquiries for further details on services/goods required are only permitted in writing and no later than **20th August 2026** Confirmation of receipt will be sent by e-mail to all bidders in a circular letter.

Bidders can send their questions to the following e-mail address stating as subject the title of the invitation for tender:

**msfea-proc-tenders@nairobi.msf.org**

If MSF Spain (Eastern Africa) at its own initiative or in response to a request from a bidder, adds or clarifies information to the RFP, this information may be sent in writing and shared at the same time with all bidders invited to tender.

### Response language

The responses and related documents must be submitted in English.

### Selection process

Bidders shall submit a technical and a financial proposal separately, in clearly marked separate envelopes or emails. The financial proposal shall be sealed, and no financial information shall be contained in the technical proposals. Both envelopes or digital documents must be submitted per the schedule and contact details detailed in sections 3.1 and 4.3.

First envelope containing the bid for services to be supplied, clearly marked on the outside "TECHNICAL PROPOSAL"

Second envelope containing the original and one copy of the detailed commercial offer, itemized per the technical proposal, clearly marked on the outside "FINANCIAL PROPOSAL"

Only technical Proposals shall be opened on the date of submission. Financial Proposals shall remain sealed until the technical evaluation is completed.

The technical proposal must show that the attached Terms of Reference and their objectives have been fully understood and the proposed methods and resources must match the detailed needs.

In drawing up the technical proposal for the services, the bidder should observe the Terms of Reference and any particular requirements in this document and the below evaluation criteria.

In assessing the technical bids for services, value will be attached to brief, precise and customized statements. The document should be clear, complete and arranged in a readable way. The presentation may include diagrams, tables and graphs as necessary.

**Interested candidates should submit:**

Company profile

Certificate of registration/incorporation

KRA PIN certificate

Valid Tax Compliance Certificate

CR-12 issued in the last one year

Project team Curriculum Vitae

Relevant experience

Detailed workplan detailing their understanding of the job and completion timeline.

Financial proposal/quotation

References from similar assignments

**Technical Evaluation Criteria**

The technical evaluation of proposals will be conducted based on the criteria below. Bidders must demonstrate a clear understanding of the assignment, relevant technical expertise, and capacity to deliver the project within the required timeline and quality standards.

**Criteria**

**Description**

**Maximum Score**

Understanding of the Assignment

Demonstrated understanding of the project objectives, scope, deliverables, and migration requirements

15

Proposed Methodology & Workplan

Quality, feasibility, and clarity of the proposed implementation approach, project plan, timelines, risk management, and collaboration model

20

Technical Expertise

Proven expertise in React (Next.js), Python, APIs, integrations, Docker, CI/CD, Linux, and system architecture

20

Relevant Experience

Experience implementing similar membership systems, portals, ERP integrations, and payment gateway integrations

15

Team Composition & Qualifications

Qualifications, certifications, and experience of the proposed personnel assigned to the project

10

UI/UX Capability

Demonstrated ability to deliver user-friendly, responsive, and accessible interfaces

10

Knowledge Transfer & Documentation Approach

Clarity of the proposed approach for handover, documentation, training, and code management

10

Total

100

**Minimum Technical Score**

Only bidders achieving a minimum technical score of 75 out of 100 shall be considered technically responsive and eligible for further financial evaluation.

**Technical and Financial Evaluation Weighting**

The final evaluation of proposals shall be based on the following weighting:

Technical Proposal: 75%

Financial Proposal: 25%

The technical proposal shall be evaluated first. Only bidders meeting the minimum technical score threshold will proceed to the financial evaluation stage.

The financial bids will be assessed on the basis of the total price (not including customs and excise duties, taxes, levies etc. in Kenya after correcting any arithmetical errors and after deducting cost items that, as stated in the request for tender, are not to be included in the assessment.

For the purpose of comparison, the total adjusted price calculated will be converted into one and the same currency Kenya Shilling (Ksh) at the exchange rate of the day.

Note: Bidders proposing to work as associates must specify the character and operating procedures of the suggested association scheme. In particular, information on the roles, responsibilities, contractual agreements and coordinating mechanisms among the partners shall be given as part of the technical proposal.

jobs.title: Country Program Manager, Mali (f/h/x)
jobs.body:
## **NOTRE MISSION**

Médecins du Monde est une ONG internationale de développement médical faisant partie d'un réseau international. Nous fournissons une assistance médicale aux groupes vulnérables, en Belgique et dans le reste du monde.

Nous voulons une couverture universelle de santé où chaque personne a accès aux soins, sans obstacles (financiers, culturels, géographiques, etc.).

Pour mener à bien notre mission, nous nous basons sur trois piliers :

- **Soigner** : donner un réel accès aux soins aux populations.
- **Changer**: plus qu'aider, nous voulons changer les choses à long terme.
- **Témoigner** : nous ne restons pas silencieux. Grâce à notre expérience et notre présence sur le terrain, nous interpellons les pouvoirs (locaux, régionaux et (inter)nationaux) avec des faits, des chiffres et des réalités.

Nos projets suivent une série de valeurs communes à toute notre organisation : Justice sociale, Empowerment, Indépendance, Engagement, Equilibre.

## **L’ESSENTIEL**

Sous la supervision du Directeur Régional Sahel vous avez la charge de concevoir, piloter, adapter et évaluer le programme de MdM Belgique (MdM-BE) au Mali. Vous proposez et mettez en œuvre, en fonction des évolutions et des contraintes internes et externes, la définition de stratégies, d’objectifs et de plans d’actions pour le programme Mali. Vous assurez également l’animation, la gestion sécuritaire et le management d’une équipe.

La fonction assure la supervision d'un groupe de : 4 à 5 collaborateur.trice.s (fourchette indicative) ainsi que la coordination et la collaboration avec différents partenaires nationaux.

## **TACHES ET RESPONSABILITES**

**Management de la stratégie opérationnelle pays :**

- Est responsable de la définition et du déploiement de la stratégie Institutionnelle pays du programme au Mali.
- Participe à la définition de la stratégie et du cadre logique du programme régional en lien avec le Directeur Régional Sahel et les coordinateur.trices techniques Sahel
- Est responsable de la planification, de la coordination de la mise en œuvre des activités et de la mise en place des outils de suivi adéquats.
- Supervise la collecte et l’analyse des données et en garanti la qualité, assurer le monitoring des activités et le suivi des indicateurs.
- Est responsable de déroulement de l’approche de localisation de MdM-be au Mali en lien avec les acteurs étatiques et les associations locales.

**Management des programmes :**

- Supervise la gestion comptable et assure le suivi budgétaire.
- Assure l’opérationnalisation de la Stratégie d’Institutionnelle Pays (SIP) et des plans d’action par département.
- Développe et entretien le réseau de partenaires et représente l’organisation auprès des interlocuteurs et partenaires des projets/ programmes en cours dans le pays sur les volets politiques, stratégiques et de plaidoyer.
- Valide et contribue à la rédaction des documents de projets internes, de positionnements (documents de référence, rapports d’activités, rapport de diagnostic, notes et documents de plaidoyer, cadres logiques etc.) et bailleurs (demandes de subvention, rapports, etc.).
- Pilote les évaluations de projets et monitore les recommandations qui en sont issues.
- Assure le suivi des recommandations issues du suivi budgétaire des projets, et émises lors des revues de projet ou lors des audits.
- Garantit la qualité, la fiabilité et la régularité des échanges d’informations entre le programme Mali et la région Sahel de l’organisation.
- Assure la veille sur le contexte sanitaire, politique, sécuritaire et humanitaire. Supervise la rédaction et la mise à jour de l’analyse de contexte pays selon les modèles internes de MdM-BE.
- Supervise une utilisation rationnelle et conforme des ressources de l'organisation
- S’assure de la mise à jour et de l’utilisation conformément au process MdM-BE de l’outil de gestion de projet par les coordinateur.rice.s des projets.

**Management des Ressources Humaines :**

- Applique et est le garant du respect de la charte managériale et des politiques de protections.
- Design l’équipe au regard de besoins, enjeux, moyens et objectifs du programme.
- Participe au recrutement et au management des postes directement rattachés à sa fonction et indirectement, appuyer ceux des autres postes sur le programme.
- Encadre et anime l’équipe programme (coordinateur.rice.s/chef.fe.s/ responsables/chargé.e.s de programmes/ projets) : définition d’objectifs, gestion des congés, recrutement et formation.
- Coach, arbitre et prend les dispositions nécessaires en cas de difficulté ou de dysfonctionnement.
- Renforce des compétences transversales des personnes de son équipe.
- Veille au respect des normes d'intégrité de l'organisation, incluant la PSEAH, la prévention de la fraude, de la corruption et des comportements abusifs

**Recherche de financement :**

- Supervise et/ou réalise une mise à jour de la cartographie des différents acteurs de la santé (bailleurs de fond, institutions et société civile) et de leurs priorités stratégiques à court, moyen ou long terme.
- Elabore et suit la stratégie de mobilisation de fonds locale.
- Identifie les opportunités de consortium et de partenariats internationaux et nationaux.
- Assurer une veille sur les éventuels appels à propositions concernant les thématiques prioritaires de MdM-BE au Mali et dans la région Sahel.

**Représentation :**

- Représenter MdM-BE auprès des autorités, des partenaires, des bailleurs et des médias.
- Assurer le suivi des accords de collaboration avec les partenaires et les bailleurs, rechercher et développer de nouveaux partenariats et réaliser ou superviser la recherche de financements.
- Représenter l'organisation auprès des organismes externes et internes, analyser communiquer et apporter les améliorations nécessaires afin de permettre le déroulement optimal des programmes.
- Participer aux sessions de travail au niveau des Clusters, groupe de travail des ONG internationales entre autres

## **VOTRE PROFIL**

**Formation et expérience**

- Diplôme universitaire en sciences politiques, gestion, droit, santé ou équivalent
- Vous avez minimum 5 ans d’expérience en gestion de projet, et idéalement dans le domaine humanitaire et de développement
- Expérience dans la gestion des consortiums
- Expérience dans des projets en lien avec la migration, la SDSR, le One Helth
- Expérience ou capacités en matière de plaidoyer

**Compétences spécifiques**

- Connaissance du contexte sahélien et une première expérience dans la zone.
- Connaissance des principaux bailleurs de fonds présents dans la zone Sahel et du Mali en particulier
- Connaissance du domaine de développement avec expérience avérée dans la gestion de projets de développement
- Compétences d’analyse et de synthèse
- Parfaite compétence en organisation personnelle
- Compétences en management et en coaching d’équipe
- Maitrise parfaite du français et bonne connaissance de l’anglais

## **NOUS OFFRONS**

- Une mission de terrain au cœur des activités de Médecins du Monde
- Un **contrat de travail de droit Malien** à durée déterminée d'1 an (renouvelable sous resèrve de financement) ; période d’essai d’un mois, renouvelable en fonction de la performance
    - Un salaire de base mensuel compris entre 1 485 828 et 1 576 773 francs CFA, selon l'expérience.
    - Prime de scolarité : 10.000 FCFA/enfant, pour 5 enfants maximum, à la rentrée scolaire
    - Prime Ramadan : 20.000 FCFA, 1 fois dans l’année à la veille du Ramadan
    - Prime Tabaski : 60.000 FCFA, 1 fois dans l’année à la veille de la fête de Tabaski.
    - Forfait frais médicaux : de 200 000 à 400 000 FCFA annuel en fonction du nombre de Charge familiale
    - Aide à la famille : de 5 000 à 10 000 francs CFA par mois en fonction de la situation matrimoniale et 2500 francs CFA par enfants à Charge.
    - Indemnité Kilométrique : 25 FCFA par Kilomètre X 2 X 22 jrs/mois.
    - Prime d’ancienneté : 3% après trois ans d’ancienneté. Plus 1% par année d’ancienneté en sus dans la limite maximale de 15%.
- Congés : 2 jours ouvrables par mois complet presté, soit 24 jours de congés légaux par an
- Congés Exceptionnels : 10 jours par an en fonction des évènements familiaux de l’employé
- Prise de poste : 01/09/2026
- Lieu de mission : Bamako

jobs.title: Grants and Compliance Coordinator (Syria - Damascus )
jobs.body:
**Job Title: Grants and Compliance Coordinator**

**Job Location: Syria - Damascus**

**Report to: Country Representative**

**Job Style : Full-Time**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Grants and Compliance Coordinator supports the effective management of UITYD’s Syria grant portfolio by ensuring timely, accurate, and compliant donor reporting; maintaining complete grant records and trackers; coordinating donor communications; and verifying that programmatic, financial, procurement, and contractual actions are aligned with approved donor agreements, budgets, policies, and applicable regulations. The role places particular emphasis on grants funded by United Nations agencies and other institutional donors, including preparation and follow-up of FACE forms and supporting documentation, expenditure tracking, reporting calendars, and compliance checks throughout the grant lifecycle.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Grants and Compliance Coordinator has the following responsibilities and duties:

***Grant Management and Donor Reporting:***

- Maintain a comprehensive grants portfolio tracker covering agreements, amendments, budgets, reporting schedules, payment tranches, key deliverables, donor conditions, and close-out requirements.
- Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, quality review, and timely submission of narrative, financial, and other donor reports in line with contractual requirements.
- Lead the preparation, review, and tracking of UN Harmonized Approach to Cash Transfers (HACT) documentation, including Funding Authorization and Certificate of Expenditures (FACE) forms, supporting schedules, and required evidence.
- Establish and maintain reporting calendars, send advance reminders to responsible departments, and follow up until inputs and approvals are complete.
- Review donor reports for consistency across narrative achievements, indicator results, expenditure figures, workplans, budgets, and supporting documentation.
- Coordinate responses to donor comments, clarification requests, spot checks, audits, verification exercises, and monitoring findings.
- Support grant start-up, implementation reviews, amendments, no-cost extensions, budget revisions, and grant close-out processes.

***Financial Tracking and Grant Compliance:***

- Track expenditures against approved budgets in coordination with Finance and program budget holders, using budget-versus-actual reports and other grant monitoring tools.
- Identify underspending, overspending, ineligible costs, budget variances, and delayed expenditure posting; promptly escalate risks and propose corrective actions.
- Verify that expenditures are charged to the correct project, budget line, period, and donor-approved category.
- Ensure financial supporting documents required for donor reporting, reimbursement, liquidation, and verification are complete, consistent, and readily retrievable.
- Support reconciliation of advances, donor installments, receivables, and grant balances, including timely follow-up on pending financial actions.
- Maintain an up-to-date matrix of donor rules, cost eligibility requirements, reporting templates, procurement thresholds, visibility obligations, and documentation standards.

***Contract, Procurement, and Operational Compliance Review**:*

- Review contracts, memoranda of understanding, sub-awards, partnership documents, purchase requests (PRs), procurement plans, and related operational documents to confirm alignment with donor agreements and approved budgets.
- Confirm that requested goods, services, quantities, specifications, delivery periods, procurement methods, and budget codes are eligible and consistent with approved project documents.
- Check compliance with donor-specific procurement conditions, competitive bidding requirements, authorization levels, sanctions requirements, branding/visibility rules, and record-retention obligations.
- Document compliance observations and required corrective actions clearly before commitments are made or documents are approved.
- Coordinate with Supply Chain, Finance, Programs, HR, and Operations to resolve compliance gaps while avoiding unnecessary delays to project delivery.
- Support due diligence and compliance review of implementing partners, vendors, consultants, and other third parties, as applicable.

***Donor Relations and Coordination:***

- Serve as a focal point for routine grant-related communication with donors, particularly UN agencies, under the direction of the Country Director.
- Prepare professional correspondence, meeting briefs, donor updates, action trackers, and follow-up notes.
- Participate in donor meetings, grant reviews, kick-off meetings, monitoring visits, and close-out discussions; record decisions and ensure agreed actions are completed.
- Support the development and review of concept notes, proposals, budgets, logframes, and donor applications when requested.
- Promote clear, timely, and consistent communication between UITYD Syria, headquarters, donors, and implementation partners.

***Documentation, Risk Management, and Capacity Building:***

- Maintain complete, organized, and audit-ready electronic grant files, with appropriate version control and secure access for online collaboration.
- Monitor grant risks and compliance issues, maintain action logs, and escalate material concerns to the Country Director and relevant technical leads.
- Track donor recommendations, audit findings, management actions, and deadlines through closure.
- Develop practical checklists, templates, and guidance notes to strengthen grant compliance across departments.
- Provide orientation and coaching to project and support teams on donor requirements, FACE forms, reporting responsibilities, documentation standards, and grant controls.
- Contribute to continuous improvement of UITYD’s grants management systems, workflows, and internal coordination.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS**

Should have the following skills, education, and experience:

*Educational Qualification*

- Bachelor’s degree in business administration, finance, accounting, international development, law, public administration, or a related field.
- A relevant master’s degree is an advantage.

*1. Experience*

- At least three years of relevant experience in grants management, donor compliance, financial monitoring, program operations, or institutional donor reporting within an NGO or humanitarian organization.
- Demonstrated experience with UN agencies or other institutional donors; practical experience preparing or reviewing FACE forms is strongly preferred.
- Experience reviewing donor agreements, budgets, procurement documentation, contracts, purchase requests, and supporting financial records.
- Experience supporting audits, spot checks, donor monitoring, grant amendments, and close-out processes.
- Experience in the Syria humanitarian or recovery context is strongly preferred.

*2. Technical Skills*

- Strong understanding of grant-cycle management, donor compliance, cost eligibility, internal controls, and documentation requirements.
- Strong analytical ability, with close attention to financial figures, deadlines, contractual conditions, and inconsistencies across documents.
- Excellent organization, follow-up, and record-management skills across multiple grants and competing deadlines.
- Strong written and spoken English and Arabic, including the ability to draft professional donor correspondence and reports.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, and online collaboration platforms; ability to work effectively in a remote or hybrid environment.
- High integrity, discretion, accountability, and commitment to humanitarian principles.
- Ability to communicate diplomatically, coordinate across departments, and raise compliance concerns constructively.
- Ability to work under pressure, prioritize effectively, and deliver accurate work with limited supervision.

**ABOUT UITYD**

UITYD is a global humanitarian organization providing medical and health services to people in need. With administrative operations based in Gaziantep, UITYD oversees comprehensive humanitarian and operational programs that extend across all regions of Syria.

**CODE OF CONDUCT** The Code of Conduct reflects the profession's core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. The postholder must comply with UITYD’s Code of Conduct and all applicable policies, including safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, child protection, anti-fraud and anti-corruption, conflict of interest, confidentiality, data protection, sanctions compliance, and whistleblowing.

**CHILD PROTECTION POLICY** Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable, and the organization recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. The organization is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

**DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE AND HARASSMENT POLICY** The organization provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise). Any suspected violation must be reported through the appropriate UITYD channels.

**Safeguarding & Code of Conduct** All employees must adhere to protection policies, principles, and rules of conduct. Strict compliance with safety and ethical standards is required. Employment is subject to UITYD policies, applicable law, satisfactory references, and required screening and verification.

jobs.title: Regional Advisor for Humanitarian Access & Risk for Africa (F/M) - Nigeria or Ethiopia
jobs.body:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

- Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
- Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
- Harm Reduction
- Environment and Health
- Humanitarian Space
- Healthcare systems and rights

## About the role

The main objective of the Regional Humanitarian Access and Risk Advisor (HARA) is to improve the analysis, support operational management and access, safety, security capacity building of the MdM team working in 9 countries (DRC, CAR, Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso, Nigeria, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Sudan).

You will establish regular remote relationships with MdM's key security managers in these countries and will work closely with the Desk officers.

You will conduct regular visits to the countries within your area of responsibility, support the facilitation of humanitarian access, and contribute to regional analysis.

## What you'll do

Under the supervision of the head of security and safety unit (based at the HQ), your main responsibilities are the following:

- Monitor and analyse the political and security context across the countries of responsibility, identify trends, assess risks, and produce timely alerts and recommendations
- Maintain security monitoring tools, incident databases, and regional analysis to support informed decision-making
- Develop and maintain a strong network of security and humanitarian stakeholders, representing MdM in coordination forums and strengthening information-sharing
- Provide technical guidance to country missions on security risk management, humanitarian access, and security assessments for new operational areas
- Review and validate security aspects of field missions, operational plans, and access management systems
- Support incident and crisis management, ensuring effective communication, post-incident analysis, and implementation of lessons learned
- Prepare high-quality security reports, regional analyses, and ensure accurate archiving and documentation in line with organisational standards
- Deliver security briefings, debriefings, and training to staff and partners, promoting compliance with MdM security policies and procedures
- Supervise and technically support Country Humanitarian Access & Risk Advisors (HARAs), contributing to their recruitment, performance management, and professional development
- Assess mission security management, identify capacity-building needs, and contribute to the continuous improvement of security practices through annual action planning

## Who you'll work with

Under the International Operations Department, the service supports our international and national programs and several members of the MdM network.

It is composed of 8 people:

- 1 Head of Unit
- 3 Regional HARAs dedicated to our International Programs (1 for Europ/Asia, 1 for Middle East, 1 for Latin America)
- 1 HARA for the MdM Network
- 1 HARA for our domestic programmes in France

## You are the right match if you:

- Hold a degree in humanitarian security, security management, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience)
- Have solid experience in humanitarian security management, including field missions in high-risk or complex environments
- Have worked in one or more countries within the region of responsibility
- Can analyse complex political and security contexts, anticipate risks, and provide clear operational recommendations
- Are confident managing security incidents and advising teams in dynamic and challenging environments
- Have experience delivering security training and supporting the development of colleagues' security capacities
- Build strong relationships with diverse stakeholders and communicate effectively across multicultural teams and networks
- Are organised, adaptable, and able to perform under pressure
- Are fluent in both English and French

## This role may not suit you if you:

- Prefer working in stable environments with limited exposure to operational security challenges
- Are uncomfortable making decisions or providing guidance in fast-changing or high-pressure situations
- Do not enjoy collaborating with diverse teams, partners, and external stakeholders
- Prefer a role with limited travel or field engagement
- Are not comfortable balancing strategic analysis with hands-on operational support
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

## **Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

## **Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **Employment conditions**

Contract & status:

- Gross monthly salary: 3 663 €
- Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting as soon as possible
- Trial period : 2 weeks
- Single posting

Work environment:

- Position based in Nigeria at Abuja or in Ethiopia at Addis Ababa
- Regular field visits (40% of the working time planned in the countries covered)

Benefits:

- 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

Essentials:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

## **Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Malawi Trees Execution Coordinator (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## About the Role

Seeking a Trees Execution Coordinator with 2+ years' experience implementing agroforestry programs to lead execution across four districts, driving high-quality delivery and helping achieve the program's 2030 goal of serving 1.5 million farmers.

## Responsibilities

Field Team Performance Management

- Assist the Agroforestry Associate and Execution Specialist in the recruitment and hiring of staff (e.g. Interns, District Snr Supervisors)
- Train District Supervisors, Senior Field Officers, and Field Assistants on various program activities
- Assist District Supervisors, Senior Field Officers to plan and prioritize their work by allocating their time and resources to the most impactful things
- Manage field teams performance using the program score cards and escalation tool
- Support District Senior Supervisors by visiting the field at least once a week splitting your time between HQ and the field.

Manage field Communication

- Provide actionable feedback to both District Supervisors and Senior Field Officers
- Compile field reports submitted by District Supervisors and submit them as a weekly report for the wider team
- Coordinate weekly IV Team and biweekly field team meeting
- Communicate various activity deadlines

Field Data management

- Design and create field data collection tools
- Analyze KPIs and recommend ways of improving low KPIs
- Collect and update village verification data at the EPA level
- Conduct seedlings distribution data reconciliation
- Track and record seasonal learnings to inform future expansion plans

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Technical Skills

- Strong communication and interpersonal skills
- Report writing skills
- Problem-solving and conflict-resolution skills
- Leadership skills
- Computer skills

Knowledge:

- Forestry/environmental management practices
- Community dynamics
- Leadership and management
- Bachelor’s Degree in Agriculture, Forestry, Environmental Management or related

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Ntcheu district, Malawi

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Contract Duration

1 year

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Malawi.

## Application Deadline

27 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

By 2030, our organisation will serve 10 million farm families annually. This growth will be fuelled by fundraising, and at One Acre Fund, our fundraising relies on industry-leading grant and partnership management. We have a 10-person grant management team within our larger Business Development department, responsible for stewarding our highest-value donor partnerships, and are now looking for new Strategic Partnerships Senior Associates / Managers to join this team.

These roles will manage some of our highest-value donor partnerships, leading the coordination and monitoring of grant-funded activities. All roles will report to leaders within our Global Business Development team, while closely coordinating with leaders for the relevant programs. All roles will also interact closely across 1AF’s programming, building deep fluency with our approach to smallholder agriculture: equipping farmers with high-quality products/services to increase their harvests and profits, build their climate resilience, and improve their long-term livelihoods.

Specific roles will have major emphasis areas based on the nature of each donor partnership, helping the organisation pioneer new approaches to thematic priorities including conservation agriculture, engaging women and youth farmers, and smallholder insurance.

## **Responsibilities**

Drive thematic partnerships happening in the field: You will bring an ambitious vision of smallholder prosperity to life in new thematic areas for the organisation, helping us build the capacity to deliver impact to smallholders through conservation agriculture, women/youth engagement, and/or smallholder insurance:

- Project Management and Coordination: Partner with program teams to set goals, design and run project activities, anticipate challenges, and keep every part of the plan moving forward smoothly.
- Collaborative Problem Solving: Work closely with program staff to tackle day-to-day and long-term challenges, bringing real-world insights directly to org leadership and the donor.
- Program Fluency: Spend dedicated time in the field with farmers and staff to fully understand work and ensure that all we do in the partnership remains tailored to what farmers really need.

Own, manage and/or support key donor relationships: You will ensure One Acre Fund builds and maintains an excellent relationship with our partners, translating field impact into clear, compelling narratives and keeping our partners deeply connected to our progress:

- Donor Engagement: Act as the main point of contact for all funder communications, seamlessly bridging the gap between donors and field teams in whatever ways are needed, including regular communications, coordinating visits, and more as required.
- Storytelling and Reporting: Through deep program fluency, deliver clear, high-quality narrative and financial updates that demonstrate to our partners the true impact of their support.
- Grant Administration: Manage the essential day-to-day details of the funding, including accurate data tracking, invoices, and otherwise ensuring all grant operations are running smoothly and on time.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor's degree in International Development, Public Policy, Business, Economics, or a related field.
- 5-10 years of professional experience in international development, strategic partnerships, grant management, consulting, or project management, depending on role level.
- Experience in a public-facing role and with managing external stakeholders, preferred.
- Strong writing and communication skills.
- Excellent organisational skills with a willingness to take initiative and be proactive.
- Proven negotiation and problem-solving skills.
- Comfortable with data and working in Google Sheets, preferred.
- Fluency in English required.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Kigali, Rwanda, Nairobi, Kenya or the United States *(Must be on the East Coast, with a strong preference for New York City)*.  
  
After you apply, we will notify you which opening/s you are being considered for based on your experience and existing work eligibility for each location as follows:

- Kigali, Rwanda: One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.
- Nairobi, Kenya: Open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.
- US: Open to citizens or permanent residents of the U.S.

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits.

## **Contract Duration**

2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance.

## **Travel Requirement**

At least two weeks per year. Candidates based in the US should expect to spend four weeks visiting our programs in their first year, with a minimum of two weeks annual travel expected thereafter.

## **Eligibility**

This role is open to all applicants; however, candidates with citizenship or permanent residency in Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania, or Burundi are strongly preferred.

## **Application Deadline**

23 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Coordinateur général voltigeur - Worldwide (F/H)
jobs.body:
**Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?**

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## **Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous**

Les interventions d'urgence face aux crises, conflits et catastrophes naturelles constituent un axe prioritaire de notre action. Grâce à son indépendance financière, à la solidité de ses partenariats et à l'engagement de ses équipes, Médecins du Monde déploie des réponses rapides et adaptées aux besoins des populations.

La Cellule Urgence intervient en priorité dans les pays où l'association est déjà présente, tout en pouvant être mobilisée dans de nouveaux contextes lorsque l'accès aux soins est fortement compromis et que les capacités locales sont insuffisantes. Elle apporte également un appui opérationnel et technique aux missions des pôles géographiques dans la préparation et la mise en œuvre de leurs réponses d'urgence.

En tant que membre de l'équipe des voltigeur·euse·s de la Cellule Urgence, vous êtes déployé·e sur des contextes d'urgence afin de lancer de nouvelles interventions ou de renforcer les équipes en place. Vous pouvez également participer à des missions exploratoires, à l'ouverture de nouvelles missions ou bases, assurer des renforts opérationnels temporaires (« gap-filling ») ou appuyer la mise en œuvre d'activités médicales spécifiques, telles que des formations ou des actions de préparation aux urgences.

## **Vos missions**

Vos principales responsabilités sont :

**Supervision des opérations d'urgence sur le terrain**

- Assurer l'ouverture de nouvelle(s) mission(s) en mettant en œuvre les procédures et politiques de MdM (approvisionnement, trésorerie, etc.)
- Mener des missions exploratoires : évaluation du contexte, cartographie des parties prenantes, conception de stratégies en lien avec les membres de l'équipe d'urgence, etc.
- Diriger, coordonner et superviser les interventions d'urgence
- Superviser les fonctions support (finance, ressources humaines, logistique, chaîne d'approvisionnement, sûreté et sécurité) en garantissant le respect des politiques, des procédures et des besoins opérationnels
- Développer et entretenir des relations de travail constructives avec les mécanismes de coordination locaux et l'ensemble des parties prenantes
- Identifier, évaluer et suivre les risques opérationnels, puis définir et mettre en œuvre les mesures d'atténuation adaptées afin de garantir la continuité des activités
- Assurer le rôle de point focal sécurité sur la zone d'intervention, veiller à la mise en œuvre du plan de gestion de la sécurité et au respect des procédures opérationnelles

**Contribuer à renforcer la réponse aux urgences de MdM au niveau du siège**

- Apporter un appui technique et opérationnel aux équipes des programmes nationaux dans la préparation et la réponse aux situations d'urgence
- Contribuer au développement et à l'amélioration des outils opérationnels dédiés aux interventions d'urgence
- Participer à l'évolution de la stratégie globale de notre réponse aux urgences sanitaires
- Capitaliser sur les retours d'expérience afin d'identifier les bonnes pratiques et de contribuer à l'amélioration continue des interventions

Le partage du temps de travail entre le terrain et le siège est évaluée à 80%-20%.

La durée d’un déploiement sur le terrain est de trois 3 mois maximum, et est suivie par un temps de récupération.

## **Vos collègues**

Vous travaillez sous la responsabilité du responsable de la cellule urgences basé au siège. Lorsque vous êtes déployé.e sur le terrain, vous reportez directement au/à la desk de la mission.

## **Vous êtes la bonne personne si vous:**

- Êtes titulaire d'une formation supérieure en gestion de projet ou généraliste (Bac+5)
- Justifiez d'au moins trois ans d'expérience dans le secteur humanitaire en tant que chef·fe de mission et/ou coordinateur·rice de site
- Avez conduit des missions exploratoires dans des contextes d'urgence
- Maîtrisez l'analyse des risques et l'élaboration de stratégies d'accès humanitaire
- Possédez une expérience de la gestion de programmes financés par des bailleurs de fonds
- Avez assuré la représentation auprès des acteurs humanitaires, des autorités locales et des bailleurs
- Disposez d'une expérience en gestion de la sûreté et de la sécurité, y compris dans des contextes volatils
- Faites preuve d'une forte capacité d'adaptation et d'une bonne résistance au stress dans des environnements sécuritaires complexes
- Maîtrisez le Pack Office
- Maîtrisez des outils de cartographie tels que Google Earth ou ArcGIS
- Maîtrisez couramment le français et l'anglais, à l'écrit comme à l'oral ; la maîtrise de l'espagnol et/ou de l'arabe constitue un atout

## **Ce poste n'est pas pour vous si :**

- La flexibilité, l’adaptabilité et la prise d'initiatives ne comptent pas parmi vos principales qualités ; les déplacements fréquents ainsi que les changements réguliers d’équipe représentent une difficulté
- Vous craignez de ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde.

## Les prochaines étapes

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec notre chargée de recrutement. Puis viendront l'entretien technique et managérial (auquel des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés).

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

## Nous attendons votre candidature

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, n’attendez plus, postulez !

## Vos conditions d’emploi

**Contrat & statut :**

- CDD à pourvoir à partir du 01/10/2026 pour 12 mois
- Salaire brut mensuel de 4 067 €
- Statut : cadre
- Poste à temps plein

**Les avantages :**

- Télétravail ponctuel
- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime de déplacement terrain de 198,18€ brut/mois au prorata du temps de présence sur le terrain
- Au siège, tickets restaurants d’une valeur unitaire de 10€ (participation à hauteur de 60% de MdM, 40% salarié.e) et sur le terrain via une allocation forfaitaire de restauration fixée en fonction du pays
- Au siège, remboursement du titre de transport en commun à 50% (abonnement mensuel) et prise en charge à 100% des allers-retours siège-terrain
- Logement pris en charge sur le terrain à 100%
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

**Les indispensables :**

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Engagement fort en faveur de l’inclusion et de la lutte contre toutes les discriminations
- Plus d’infos : [https://bit.ly/3x5MezL](https://bit.ly/3x5MezL)

**Cadre de travail :**

- Poste basé au siège à Saint-Denis (20% du temps) et sur les terrains internationaux (80% du temps)
- Déploiement sur le terrain pas avant 1 mois d’intégration
- Travail sur écran, en open space
- Communication orale et téléphonique
- Posture assise prolongée

**Diversité et inclusion**

MdM s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur.se handicapé.e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

jobs.title: Field Research and M&E Staff - Sudan
jobs.body:
**Sudan Field Research and M&E Roster - Enumerators, Monitors and Supervisors**

**About MEAL Center**

MEAL Center (MC) is a regional consulting firm specializing in monitoring, evaluation, research, assessments, third-party monitoring (TPM), learning, capacity building, and related advisory services. MC works with humanitarian and development organizations across several countries in the region, including Sudan.

MC is expanding its roster of qualified field personnel who may be engaged for upcoming research, monitoring, evaluation, and data-collection assignments across the country.

**Purpose of the Roster**

We are inviting Sudan-based professionals and experienced field personnel to register for potential short-term assignments with MC. Profiles may be considered for roles including:

- Field Researchers / Enumerators
- Field Monitors
- Field Supervisors / Team Leaders

Registration in the roster is not an offer of immediate employment or engagement. Selected candidates may be contacted when their location, experience, skills, and availability match the requirements of a specific assignment.

**Location**

Sudan - Multiple locations.

Applicants should clearly indicate their current state and locality when completing the registration form.

**Potential Assignments**

Roster members may be considered for different types of fieldwork, including:

- Household and beneficiary surveys
- Key informant interviews (KIIs)
- Focus group discussions (FGDs)
- Needs assessments
- Baseline and endline studies
- Third-party monitoring (TPM)
- Market assessments
- Direct observation and verification visits
- Impact assessments
- Resilience, conflict, peace, and other analytical studies
- Training and supervision of teams

**Sectors**

Assignments may cover a range of humanitarian and development sectors, including:

- Food Security and Livelihoods
- Health
- Nutrition
- Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH)
- Protection
- Education
- Agriculture and Irrigation
- Energy and Environment
- Governance and Social Cohesion
- Economic Development
- Entrepreneurship and Private Sector Development
- Other relevant sectors

**Candidate Profile**

We welcome applications from candidates who:

- Are currently based in Sudan and available for field assignments;
- Have experience or interest in field research, monitoring, assessments, surveys, or related data-collection activities;
- Are able to communicate effectively with communities, beneficiaries, and stakeholders;
- Can work accurately and professionally while following research protocols and ethical requirements;
- Have experience with digital data-collection tools such as KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, ODK, or similar platforms, where applicable;
- Are able to work independently as well as within field teams;
- Are willing to travel outside their current area when assignment conditions permit.

Previous humanitarian or development field experience is an advantage. Applicants with experience supervising field researchers or leading field teams are particularly encouraged to register for supervisory roles.

Knowledge of relevant Sudanese local languages is an asset.

Women and qualified applicants from all states of Sudan are strongly encouraged to register.

jobs.title: Tupande Area Coordinator - Lower Western
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## About the Role

Looking for a strategic leader to act as the entrepreneurial architect of their territory, leading a team to scale retail impact and drive revenue through data-driven execution in a rapidly growing, mission-led organization.

## Responsibilities

- Work with your manager to maximize business results in your territory.
- Recruit, train, and manage a sales team in your assigned area.
- Develop and execute sales strategies to meet or exceed sales, repayment and impact goals
- Conduct market research to identify new opportunities for growth and expansion
- Monitor and analyze sales data to identify trends and adjust sales strategies accordingly
- Collaborate with marketing and other departments to develop promotions and campaigns to drive sales
- Provide leadership and coaching to sales representatives to ensure they are meeting performance targets
- Build and maintain relationships with key customers and stakeholders in your assigned area
- Participate in target setting, sales forecasting and budgeting processes
- Continuously develop knowledge of the industry and stay up to date on market trends and competitor activity

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor's degree in business, marketing, or related field preferred
- Proven experience in sales management, preferably in a related industry

Awards, Grants and Partnership Manager - Remote in RI countries of operations
jobs.body:
**Location** Remote in RI countries of operations ( PAK, LEB, KNY, AFG, TUR, SYR, JOR)

**Travel** Frequent travel to the field (including Chad)

**Context**

**Relief International (RI) is an international non-profit organization** that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing.

Our team of more than 4,000 staff and local volunteers work in 14 countries across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, providing Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience.

We do this by working with local actors to develop safe and inclusive local programming that is evidence based, conflict sensitive, climate smart, and reaches those in need.

**Job Profile**

Relief International has been operational in Sudan since 2004 and in Chad since 2024, implementing programming focused on Health, with integrated services in Protection, WASH, Nutrition and Livelihoods both through direct implementation and with partners.

**The Awards, Grants, and Partnership Manager for Sudan and Chad plays a central role in the strategic development, management, and growth of Relief International's portfolio across both countries**. The position leads the full awards management cycle from business development and proposal design through implementation, reporting, compliance, partnership management, and close-out. The role ensures adherence to donor regulations and RI policies while strengthening organizational systems, supporting quality programming, and fostering effective partnerships.

Operating in a rapidly evolving humanitarian context, the post-holder serves as a key liaison with donors, partners, and internal stakeholders, providing strategic oversight of awards, grants, compliance, and partnerships across Sudan and Chad.

The position requires the ability to manage both strategic priorities and operational details while supporting the continued growth and quality of the country portfolio.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Accountability and Complexity**

- Accountable for balancing multiple priorities simultaneously while ensuring timely and accurate delivery of assigned tasks.
- Lead and coordinate awards, grants, and partnership management across Sudan and Chad throughout the award lifecycle.
- Ensure compliance with donor regulations, contractual obligations, RI policies, and audit requirements.
- Manage competing priorities and deadlines across a complex multi-donor portfolio.
- Provide strategic advice to senior leadership on portfolio performance, compliance risks, donor engagement, and business development opportunities.
- Serve as a principal focal point for donor communications related to award management, implementation, reporting, and modifications.
- Strengthen systems, processes, and coordination mechanisms that support effective awards and partnership management across both country programmes.

**Awards Management**

- Oversee the full award lifecycle for all grants and contracts in Sudan and Chad, ensuring compliance with donor and organizational requirements.
- Maintain accurate awards tracking systems, reporting schedules, and grant documentation.
- Lead award start-up, regular monthly reviews (Awards review Meeting), modification, and close-out processes, ensuring timely completion of all donor and organizational requirements.
- Coordinate internal award review processes and facilitate cross-departmental collaboration to address implementation challenges and compliance risks.
- Support audit readiness and ensure implementation of audit recommendations and corrective actions.
- Ensure effective records management, documentation, and archiving of all award-related files and communications.
- Provide technical guidance to program and support teams on awards management tools, procedures, and donor regulations

**Donor Compliance**

- Act as the primary resource on donor regulations, compliance requirements, and RI awards management procedures.
- Ensure proposals, budgets, reports, modifications, and implementation processes comply with donor and organizational requirements.
- Monitor compliance risks and recommend corrective actions to maintain award performance and accountability.
- Promote a strong culture of donor compliance and quality assurance across programme and support functions.

**Donor Reporting and Communication**

- Oversee donor reporting processes across Sudan and Chad, ensuring high-quality and timely submission of all deliverables.
- Coordinate and quality assure donor reporting, consolidating inputs from programme, MEAL, finance, and support teams.
- Maintain effective communication with donors regarding program progress, reporting requirements, amendments, and approvals.
- Coordinate donor visits, meetings, presentations, and briefing materials in collaboration with relevant teams.
- Ensure reporting schedules and donor communication records remain accurate and up to date.

**Proposal Development**

- Lead the development and submission of high-quality proposals, concept notes, and strategic funding opportunities for Sudan and Chad.
- Coordinate design processes involving programme, technical, operations, finance, and HQ stakeholders.
- Support donor engagement, opportunity tracking, and portfolio growth in alignment with country and organizational priorities.
- Ensure proposal packages are technically sound, operationally feasible, evidence-based, and donor compliant.
- Support value-for-money approaches and promote effective programme design and resource allocation.
- Facilitate Go/No-Go decision-making processes and contribute to strategic funding positioning efforts.

**Partnership Selection and Management**

- Lead partnership management processes across Sudan and Chad, including partner identification, mapping, selection, due diligence, contracting, monitoring, and close-out.
- Serve as the primary focal point for partnership coordination and localization efforts.
- Ensure partner agreements comply with donor and organizational requirements.
- Strengthen relationships with national and international partners, government institutions, and other stakeholders.
- Support partner performance monitoring, capacity strengthening, and organizational development initiatives.
- Ensure effective partnership documentation, compliance monitoring, and risk management throughout the partnership lifecycle.

**Capacity Building and Information Data Management**

- Strengthen staff understanding of awards, compliance, partnership, and donor management processes.
- Deliver training and mentoring to programme and support teams on key donor requirements and RI procedures.
- Support effective award monitoring, financial oversight, and information management.
- Establish and maintain robust filing, documentation, and knowledge management systems.
- Promote continuous learning and the sharing of donor guidance, tools, templates, and best practices across Sudan and Chad.

**People Management & Capacity Strengthening**

- Provide effective leadership, supervision, mentoring, and performance management for direct reports.
- Foster a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing team culture.
- Promote cross-departmental coordination and strengthen teamwork across programme and support functions.
- Support staff professional development and capacity strengthening initiatives.

**Safeguarding, Gender & Inclusion**

- Uphold and promote Relief International's safeguarding commitments and policies.
- Ensure all activities are implemented in accordance with safeguarding, protection, and Do No Harm principles.
- Maintain a safe and accountable environment for communities, partners, and staff

**Behavior and Conduct**

- Will ensure the highest standards of behavior inside and outside of work promotes the values in RI’s code of conduct and safeguarding policies
- Will be a model for ethical conduct standards for other team members
- Will ensure own actions and the actions of the teams’ members they manage do not impact on the safety of the RI team and the vulnerable communities we serve
- Will ensure external stakeholders are aware of RI conduct and reporting mechanisms
- Report any concerns

**Person Specification**

Skills, knowledge and expertise required for the role.

**Essential criteria**

- Relevant Bachelor and/or Master degree.
- Minimum five years of progressively responsible experience in awards, grants, compliance, business development, and partnership management within humanitarian or development organizations.
